S is the month when birds nest. In Gwion’s Can y Meirch (‘Song of the Horses’), a partial series of ‘I have been’s’ occurs as an interpolation. One of them is: ‘I have been a crane on a wall, a wondrous sight.’ The crane was sacred to Delian Apollo and, before Apollo, to the Sun-hero Theseus. It also appears, in triad, in a Gaulish bas-relief at Paris, and in another at Trèves, in association with the god Esus and a bull. Crane, hawk, or vulture? That is an important question because the provenience of the poem depends on the answer. The hawk, if not the royal hawk of Egyptian Horus, will have been the kite sacred to Boreas the North Wind; in Greek legend his Thracian sons Calaïs and Zetes wore kite-feathers in his honour and had the power of transforming themselves into kites. These two birds are mythologically linked in the Egyptian hieroglyph for the North Wind, which is a hawk. In Welsh the word is barcut, and in Iranian the word is barqut, which supports Pliny’s suggestion (Natural History XXX, 13) of a strong connexion between the Persian and British sun-cults. Another mark of close similarity is that Mithras, the Persian Sun-god whose birthday was celebrated at the Winter solstice, was worshipped as a bull of seven fights: his initiates having to go through seven grades before they were sealed on the brow as ‘tried soldiers of Mithras’. Mithraism was a favourite cult of the Roman legionaries in Imperial times, but they never reached Ireland, and the Song of Amergin is evidently far older than the Claudian invasion of Britain. The vulture will have been the griffon-vulture sacred to Osiris, a bird also of great importance to the Etruscan augurs and with a wider wing-span than the golden eagle. In the Song of Moses (Deuteronomy XXXII, 11) Jehovah is identified with this bird, which is a proof that its ‘uncleanness’ in the Levitical list means sanctity, not foulness. The heraldic griffin is a lion with griffon-vultures’ wings and claws and represents the Sun-god as King of the earth and air. The ordinary Welsh word for hawk is Gwalch, akin to the Latin falco, falcon, and the court-bards always likened their royal patrons to it. The mystical names Gwalchmai (‘hawk of May’); Gwalchaved (‘hawk of summer’) better known as Sir Galahad; and Gwalchgwyn (‘white hawk’) better known as Sir Gawain, are best understood in terms of this calendar formula.
S 是鸟筑巢之月。在格维翁的《马之歌》（Can y Meirch）中，有一段不完整的「我曾为」序列作为插入出现。其中一句是：「我曾为墙上之鹤，一奇观。」鹤 sacred 于提洛的阿波罗，在阿波罗之前则 sacred 于太阳英雄忒修斯。它还以三位一体的形式出现在巴黎的一幅高卢浮雕和特里尔（Trèves）的另一幅中，与神埃苏斯和一头牛相伴。鹤、鹰还是秃鹫？这是一个重要问题，因为这首诗的来源取决于答案。鹰——如果不是埃及荷鲁斯（Horus）的王鹰——将是 sacred 于北风玻璃阿斯的鸢；在希腊传说中，他的色雷斯儿子卡拉伊斯（Calaïs）和泽忒斯（Zetes）佩戴鸢羽以致敬，并有能力变为鸢。这两种鸟在埃及表示北风的象形文字中神话性地联系在一起——那是一只鹰。威尔士语中此词为 barcut，伊朗语中为 barqut，这支持了普林尼关于波斯和不列颠太阳崇拜之间密切联系的建议（《自然史》XXX, 13）。另一个相似性标志是波斯太阳神密特拉（Mithras）——其生日在冬至庆祝——被崇拜为七战之牛：其入教者须经过七个等级才被在前额上封印为「密特拉的经过考验的士兵」。密特拉教是帝国时期罗马军团兵最喜欢的崇拜，但他们从未到达爱尔兰，而阿默金之歌显然远早于克劳狄乌斯入侵不列颠。秃鹫则是 sacred 于奥西里斯的兀鹫，这种鸟对伊特鲁里亚占卜师也极为重要，翼展比金雕更宽。在摩西之歌（《申命记》XXXII, 11）中耶和华被等同于这种鸟，这证明它在利未记清单中的「不洁」意味着神圣而非肮脏。纹章中的狮鹫是长着兀鹫翅膀和爪子的狮子，代表太阳神为大地与天空之王。威尔士语中鹰的普通词是 Gwalch，类似于拉丁语 falco（隼），宫廷诗人总是将他们的王室赞助人比作它。神秘名字瓜尔奇迈（Gwalchmai，「五月之鹰」）、瓜尔查韦德（Gwalchaved，「夏天之鹰」，更广为人知的名字是加拉哈德爵士[Sir Galahad]）和瓜尔奇格温（Gwalchgwyn，「白鹰」，更广为人知的名字是高文爵士[Sir Gawain]），最好用这个历法公式来理解。

H, which starts in the second half of May, is the season of flowers, and the hawthorn, or may-tree, rules it. Olwen, the daughter of ‘Giant Hawthorn’, has already been mentioned. Her hair was yellow as the broom, her fingers pale as wood-anemones, her cheeks the colour of roses and from her footprints white trefoil sprang up – trefoil to show that she was the summer aspect of the old triple Goddess. This peculiarity gave her the name of Olwen – ‘She of the White Track’. Trefoil, by the way, was celebrated by the Welsh bards with praise out of all proportion to its beauty. Homer called it ‘the lotus’ and mentioned it as a rich fodder for horses.
H 从五月下半月开始，是花的季节，山楂即五月树统治此月。「巨人之山楂」之女奥尔温（Olwen）前面已提过。她的头发黄如金雀花，手指白如银莲花，面颊红如玫瑰，她走过之处白车轴草萌生——车轴草表明她是古老三重女神的夏季面向。这一特征赋予她奥尔温之名——「白迹之人」。顺便说一句，车轴草被威尔士吟游诗人赞颂，与其美貌不成比例地高。荷马称之为「莲花」并提及它是马的丰美饲料。

D is ruled by the midsummer oak. The meaning is, I think, that the painful smoke of green oak gives inspiration to those who dance between the twin sacrificial fires lighted on Midsummer Eve. Compare the Song of the Forest Trees:
D 由仲夏橡树主宰。我认为含义是，青橡木的呛人烟给在仲夏夜两堆祭火间舞蹈的人带来灵感。比较《树木之歌》：

Fiercest heat-giver of all timber is green oak;
Fiercest heat-giver of all timber is green oak;（所有木材中青橡木放热最猛；）



From him none may escape unhurt.
From him none may escape unhurt.（无人能从他处全身而退。）



By love of him the head is set an-aching,
By love of him the head is set an-aching,（爱他使头痛欲裂，）



By his acrid embers the eye is made sore.
By his acrid embers the eye is made sore.（他刺鼻的余烬使眼睛酸痛。）





T is the spear month, the month of the tanist; the bardic character T was shaped like a barbed spear.
T 是矛之月，替补者之月；吟游字母 T 的形状像一支倒钩矛。

C is the nut month. The salmon was, and still is, the King of the river-fish, and the difficulty of capturing him, once he is lodged in a pool, makes him a useful emblem of philosophical retirement. Thus Loki, the Norse God of cunning, disguised himself from his fellow-gods as a salmon and was drawn from his pool only with a special net of his own design. The connexion of salmon with nuts and with wisdom has already been explained.
C 是坚果之月。鲑鱼曾经是、现在仍是河鱼之王，一旦它藏入潭中，捕获之难使它成为哲学隐退的有用象征。因此北欧诡计之神洛基（Loki）伪装成鲑鱼躲避众神，只有用他自己设计的特殊网才被从潭中拖出。鲑鱼与坚果和智慧的联系前文已作解释。

M is the initial of Minerva, Latin goddess of wisdom and inventor of numbers; of Mnemosyne, the Mother of the Greek Muses; and of the Muses themselves; and of the Moirae, or Fates, who are credited by some mythographers with the first invention of the alphabet. The vine, the prime tree of Dionysus, is everywhere associated with poetic inspiration. Wine is the poets’ proper drink, as Ben Jonson knew well when he asked for his fee as Poet Laureate to be paid in sack. The base Colley Cibber asked for a cash payment in lieu of wine, and no Poet Laureate since has been poet enough to demand a return to the old system of payment.
M 是密涅瓦（Minerva，拉丁智慧女神和数字发明者）、摩涅莫绪涅（Mnemosyne，希腊缪斯之母）、缪斯本身以及莫伊赖（Moirae，即命运三女神——某些神话学家认为她们最先发明了字母表）的首字母。葡萄藤作为狄俄尼索斯的首要之树，处处与诗歌灵感联系在一起。葡萄酒是诗人的正当饮品，本·琼森（Ben Jonson）深知这一点，他要求桂冠诗人的酬金以雪利酒（sack）支付。卑鄙的科利·西伯（Colley Cibber）要求以现金替代葡萄酒支付，此后没有一位桂冠诗人足够有诗人气质去要求恢复旧有的支付制度。

G, the ivy month, is also the month of the boar. Set, the Egyptian Sun-god, disguised as a boar, kills Osiris of the ivy, the lover of the Goddess Isis. Apollo the Greek Sun-god, disguised as a boar, kills Adonis, or Tammuz, the Syrian, the lover of the Goddess Aphrodite. Finn Mac Cool, disguised as a boar, kills Diarmuid, the lover of the Irish Goddess Grainne (Greine). An unknown god disguised as a boar kills Ancaeus the Arcadian King, a devotee of Artemis, in his vineyard at Tegea and, according to the Nestorian Gannat Busamé (‘Garden of Delights’), Cretan Zeus was similarly killed. October was the boar-hunting season, as it was also the revelry season of the ivy-wreathed Bassarids. The boar is the beast of death and the ‘fall’ of the year begins in the month of the boar.
G 是常春藤之月，也是野猪之月。埃及太阳神塞特（Set）伪装为野猪杀死了常春藤的奥西里斯——女神伊西斯的情人。希腊太阳神阿波罗伪装为野猪杀死了阿多尼斯（Adonis，即坦木兹[Tammuz]）——叙利亚人，女神阿佛洛狄忒的情人。芬恩·麦库尔（Finn Mac Cool）伪装为野猪杀死了迪尔米德（Diarmuid）——爱尔兰女神格兰（Grainne/Greine）的情人。一位不知名的神伪装为野猪在特盖亚（Tegea）的葡萄园中杀死了阿尔忒弥斯的信徒、阿卡迪亚国王安凯乌斯（Ancaeus），据聂斯脱利派的《甘纳特·布萨梅》（Gannat Busamé，「欢乐之园」）记载，克里特的宙斯也以类似方式被杀。十月是猎野猪的季节，也是头戴常春藤花环的巴萨里德斯们的狂欢季节。野猪是死亡之兽，一年的「下落」从野猪之月开始。

NG is the month when the terrible roar of breakers and the snarling noise of pebbles on the Atlantic seaboard fill the heart with terror, and when the wind whistles dismally through the reed-beds of the rivers. In Ireland the roaring of the sea was held to be prophetic of a king’s death. The warning also came with the harsh cry of the scritch-owl. Owls are most vocal on moonlight nights in November and then remain silent until February. It is this habit, with their silent flight, the carrion-smell of their nests, their diet of mice, and the shining of their eyes in the dark, which makes owls messengers of the Death-goddess Hecate, or Athene, or Persephone: from whom, as the supreme source of prophecy, they derive their reputation for wisdom.
NG 是大西洋海岸上骇人的巨浪咆哮和卵石嘶吼声充满心中的恐怖之月，也是风在河床芦苇中凄厉呼啸之月。在爱尔兰，海的咆哮被视为国王驾崩的预言。警告也伴随尖啸猫头鹰的刺耳叫声而来。猫头鹰在十一月月光之夜最为活跃，此后保持沉默直到二月。正是这种习性——加上它们的静默飞行、巢穴的腐肉气味、以鼠为食以及夜间眼睛的闪光——使猫头鹰成为死亡女神赫卡忒（Hecate）、雅典娜或珀耳塞福涅（Persephone）的信使：从作为预言至高源泉的她们那里，猫头鹰获得了智慧的声名。

R is the month when the wave returns to the sea, and the end of the year to its watery beginning. A wave of the sea in Irish and Welsh poetry is a ‘sea-stag’: so that the year begins and ends with the white roebuck. In Irish legend such gods of the year as Cuchulain and Fionn fight the waves with sword and spear.
R 是波浪归于大海之月，年终回到其水之始。在爱尔兰和威尔士诗歌中，海浪是一只「海鹿」：因此一年以白色獐子开始和结束。在爱尔兰传说中，库丘林和芬恩等年之神以剑矛与波浪搏斗。

The corresponding text in the Romance of Taliesin is scattered rather than garbled.
《塔列辛传奇》中对应的文本是分散的而非篡改的。

B I have been a fierce bull and a yellow buck.
B I have been a fierce bull and a yellow buck.（我曾为猛牛和黄鹿。）

L I have been a boat on the sea.
L I have been a boat on the sea.（我曾为海上之舟。）

N I fled vehemently…on the foam of water.
N I fled vehemently…on the foam of water.（我曾猛烈地逃逸……在水之泡沫上。）

F I have been a drop in the air.
F I have been a drop in the air.（我曾为空中一滴水。）

S I journeyed as an eagle.
S I journeyed as an eagle.（我曾以鹰旅行。）

H God made me of blossom.
H God made me of blossom.（神以花造我。）

D I have been a tree-stump in a shovel.
D I have been a tree-stump in a shovel.（我曾为铲中之树桩。）

T I fled as a spear-head of woe to such as wish for woe.
T I fled as a spear-head of woe to such as wish for woe.（我曾以灾祸之矛尖逃向渴望灾祸之人。）

C I have been a blue salmon.
C I have been a blue salmon.（我曾为蓝色鲑鱼。）

M I have been a spotted snake on a hill.
M I have been a spotted snake on a hill.（我曾为山上之斑点蛇。）

G I fled as a bristly boar seen in a ravine.
G I fled as a bristly boar seen in a ravine.（我曾以刚毛野猪之形出现在峡谷中。）

NG I have been a wave breaking on the beach.
NG I have been a wave breaking on the beach.（我曾为拍岸之浪。）

R On a boundless sea I was set adrift.
R On a boundless sea I was set adrift.（在无边大海上我被放逐漂流。）





The clue to the arrangement of this alphabet is found in Amergin’s reference to the dolmen; it is an alphabet that best explains itself when built up as a dolmen of consonants with a threshold of vowels. Dolmens are closely connected with the calendar in the legend of the flight of Grainne and Diarmuid from Finn Mac Cool. The flight lasted for a year and a day, and the lovers bedded together beside a fresh dolmen every night. Numerous ‘Beds of Diarmuid and Grainne’ are shown in Cork, Kerry, Limerick, Tipperary and the West, each of them marked by a dolmen. So this alphabet dolmen will also serve as a calendar, with one post for Spring, the other for Autumn, the lintel for Summer, the threshold for New Year’s Day. Thus:
阿默金对支石墓的提及提供了排列这套字母表的线索；这是一套最好以支石墓形式来理解自身的字母表——辅音为柱、元音为门槛。支石墓与历法密切相关，这在格兰和迪尔米德逃离芬恩·麦库尔的传说中有所体现。逃亡持续了一年又一日，恋人每晚在一座新的支石墓旁同寝。科克、克里、利默里克、蒂珀雷里和西部有众多「迪尔米德与格兰之床」，每处都以支石墓为标志。因此这套字母表支石墓也可兼作历法：一根柱代表春，另一根代表秋，门楣代表夏，门槛代表新年元旦。如下：





At once one sees the reference to S as a hawk, or griffon, on the cliff; and to M as the hill of poetry or inspiration – a hill rooted in the death letters R and I and surmounted by the C of wisdom. So the text of the first part of Amergin’s song may be expanded as follows:
人们立刻看到 S 作为悬崖上的鹰或狮鹫的指涉；以及 M 作为诗歌或灵感之丘——一座扎根于死亡字母 R 和 I、以智慧之 C 为顶的丘。因此阿默金之歌第一部分的文本可以扩展如下：

God speaks and says:
神说话并说：



I am a stag of seven tines.
I am a stag of seven tines.（我是七角之鹿。）



Over the flooded world
Over the flooded world（在洪水弥漫的世界之上）



I am borne by the wind.
I am borne by the wind.（我被风承载。）



I descend in tears like dew, I lie glittering,
I descend in tears like dew, I lie glittering,（我如露珠般含泪降下，我闪烁地躺着，）



I fly aloft like a griffon to my nest on the cliff,
I fly aloft like a griffon to my nest on the cliff,（我如狮鹫般高飞至崖上之巢，）



I bloom among the loveliest flowers,
I bloom among the loveliest flowers,（我在最可爱的花丛中绽放，）



I am both the oak and the lightning that blasts it.
I am both the oak and the lightning that blasts it.（我既是橡树也是劈毁它的闪电。）





I embolden the spearman,
I embolden the spearman,（我使持矛者勇敢，）



I teach the councillors their wisdom,
I teach the councillors their wisdom,（我教议会者以智慧，）



I inspire the poets,
I inspire the poets,（我赋予诗人灵感，）



I rove the hills like a conquering boar,
I rove the hills like a conquering boar,（我如征服之野猪巡游群山，）



I roar like the winter sea,
I roar like the winter sea,（我如冬日之海咆哮，）



I return like the receding wave.
I return like the receding wave.（我如退去之浪回归。）



Who but I can unfold the secrets of the unhewn dolmen?
Who but I can unfold the secrets of the unhewn dolmen?（除我之外谁能揭开未凿支石墓[dolmen]的秘密？）





For if the poem really consists of two stanzas, each of two triads, ending with a single authoritative statement, then the first ‘Who but I?’ (which does not match the other five) is the conclusion of the second stanza, and is uttered by the New Year God. This Child is represented by the sacred threshold of the dolmen, the central triad of vowels, namely O.U.E. But one must read O.U.E. backwards, the way of the sun, to make sense of it. It is the sacred name of Dionysus, EUO, which in English is usually written ‘EVOE’.
因为如果这首诗确实由两节组成，每节含两个三联体，以一句权威性陈述结尾，那么第一个「除我之外？」（与其余五个不匹配）就是第二节结语，由新年之神说出。这位圣婴由支石墓的神圣门槛——即元音的中央三联体 O.U.E.——代表。但必须按太阳的方向倒读 O.U.E.，才能说得通。这就是狄俄尼索斯的神圣名字 EUO，英语中通常写作「EVOE」（伊沃）。

It is clear that ‘God’ is Celestial Hercules again, and that the child-poet Taliesin is a more appropriate person to utter the song than Amergin, the leader of the Milesians, unless Amergin is speaking as a mouth-piece of Hercules.
显然「神」又是天上的赫拉克勒斯，而童诗人塔列辛比米利都人的领袖阿默金更适合吟唱这首歌——除非阿默金是在作为赫拉克勒斯的代言人说话。

There is a mystery connected with the line ‘I am a shining tear of the sun’, because Deorgreine, ‘tear of the Sun’, is the name of Niamh of the Golden Hair, the lovely goddess mentioned in the myth of Laegaire mac Crimthainne. Celestial Hercules when he passes into the month F, the month of Bran’s alder, becomes a maiden. This recalls the stories of such sun-heroes as Achilles1, Hercules and Dionysus who lived for a time disguised as girls in the women’s quarters of a palace and plied the distaff. It also explains the ‘I have been a maiden’, in a series corresponding with the Amergin cycle, ascribed to Empedocles the fifth-century BC. mystical philosopher. The sense is that the Sun is still under female tutelage for half of this month – Cretan boys not yet old enough to bear arms were called Scotioi, members of the women’s quarters – then, like Achilles, he is given arms and flies off royally like a griffon or hawk to its nest.
「我是闪耀的太阳之泪」这一行有一个谜，因为 Deorgreine——「太阳之泪」——是金发尼芙的名字，即在莱盖里·麦克·克里姆坦恩（Laegaire mac Crimthainne）神话中提到的那位美丽女神。天上的赫拉克勒斯在进入 F 月，即布兰桤木之月时，变为少女。这令人想起阿喀琉斯（Achilles）¹、赫拉克勒斯和狄俄尼索斯等太阳英雄曾一度扮作少女住在王宫后宫中纺纱的故事。这也解释了归属于公元前五世纪神秘哲学家恩培多克勒（Empedocles）的一段与阿默金周期相对应的序列中的「我曾为少女」。含义是太阳在此月上半月仍处于女性监护之下——克里特尚未到持械年龄的男孩被称为 Scotioi，即后宫成员——然后像阿喀琉斯一样被授予武器，如狮鹫或鹰般威严地飞向其巢。

But why a dolmen? A dolmen is a burial chamber, a ‘womb of Earth’, consisting of a cap-stone supported on two or more uprights, in which a dead hero is buried in a crouched position like a foetus in the womb, awaiting rebirth. In spiral Castle (passage-burial), the entrance to the inner chamber is always narrow and low in representation of the entrance to the womb. But dolmens are used in Melanesia (according to Prof. W. H. R. Rivers) as sacred doors through which the totem-clan initiate crawls in a ceremony of rebirth; if, as seems likely, they were used for the same purpose in ancient Britain, Gwion is both recounting the phases of his past existence and announcing the phases of his future existence. There is a regular row of dolmens on Slieve Mis. They stand between two baetyls with Ogham markings, traditionally sacred to the Milesian Goddess Scota who is said to be buried there; alternatively, in the account preserved by Borlase in his Dolmens of Ireland, to ‘Bera a queen who came from Spain’. But Bera and Scota seem to be the same person, since the Milesians came from Spain. Bera is otherwise known as the Hag Of Beara.
但为何是支石墓？支石墓是一种墓室，一座「大地之子宫」，由一块盖石架在两根或多根立柱上构成，死去的英雄以蜷缩姿势如胎儿在子宫中般埋于其中，等待重生。在螺旋城堡（通道墓葬）中，内室入口总是窄而低，以代表子宫入口。但据里弗斯教授（Prof. W. H. R. The first two questions in the Song of Amergin, about the day of the solar month and the ages of the moon, coincide with the first two items of knowledge in the Saltair: ‘Who knows when the Sun shall set?’ means both ‘who knows the length of the hours of daylight at any given day of the year?’ – a problem worked out in exhaustive detail by the author of The Book of Enoch – and ‘Who knows on any given day how long the particular solar month in which it occurs will last?’

The third question is ‘Who brings the cattle of Tethra (the heavenly bodies) out of the ocean and puts each in his due place?’ This assumes a knowledge: of the five planets, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, which, with the Sun and Moon, had days of the week allotted to them in Babylonian astronomy, and still keep them in all European languages. Thus it corresponds with ‘the day of the week’.

The fourth question, as the glossarist explains, amounts to ‘Who is lucky in fishing?’ This corresponds with ‘the state of the sea tide’; for a fisherman who does not know what tide to expect will have no fishing luck.

The fifth question, read in the light of its gloss, amounts to: ‘Who orders the calendar from the advancing wave B to the receding wave R; from one calendar month to the next; from one season of the year to the next?’ (The three seasons of Spring, Summer and Autumn are separated by points, or angles, of the dolmen.) So it corresponds with ‘the calendar of the feasts of the perfect saints.’
