然而我应该补充，既然《启示录》第十一章预言了圣殿的保存，该书的原始版本必定写于尼禄死后、圣殿被毁之前，且当时关于他以肉身重现的谣言广为流传。此外，希伯来字母 TRJVN 加起来等于666（Tav=400；Resh=200；Yod=10；Vav=6；Nun=50），在塔木德文献中构成尼禄的常见密码伪装（trijon 意为「小兽」），而塔木德的作者们极不可能从外邦基督徒那里借用。因此，可能《启示录》的第一版是一篇犹太民族主义小册子，用亚兰语写于公元70年之前，其中666是意为「小兽」、指向尼禄的密码；但它在公元一世纪末被改写为希腊语并为基督徒读者扩充——此时不谙希伯来语的保罗派皈依者正竭力证明耶稣拒绝了摩西律法并将耶和华的祝福从犹太人转移到了他们自己身上。在这个包含许多插入和对过时材料不加批判地保留的第二版中，密码666被赋予了一个新的解答，一个任何人无需借助希伯来语就能理解的解答：即 DCLXVI。如果确实如此，那么原文从来就不是 Domitius Caesar 等等，然而我的回溯之眼正确地认出了——既然密码的原始希伯来含义是 TRIJON——多米提乌斯的兽性精神潜藏于图密善之中。

The proleptic or analeptic method of thought, though necessary to poets, physicians, historians and the rest, is so easily confused with mere guessing, or deduction from insufficient data, that few of them own to using it. However securely I buttress the argument of this book with quotations, citations and footnotes, the admission that I have made here of how it first came to me will debar it from consideration by orthodox scholars: though they cannot refute it, they dare not accept it.
超前或回溯的思维方法虽然对诗人、医生、历史学家和其他人是必要的，却很容易与单纯的猜测或从不充分数据中的推导相混淆，以至于很少有人承认使用它。无论我用多少引文、引证和脚注来加固本书的论证，我在这里承认它最初是如何降临于我的，这一事实将使正统学者拒绝考虑它：他们虽然无法反驳，却不敢接受。

1 The solution is based on the Hebrew. Nun = 50; Resh = 200; Vav = 6; Nun = 50 = Neron. Koph = 100; Samech = 60; Resh = 200 = Kesar. But Nero in Latin remains Nero when written in Hebrew, and Kaisar (which meant ‘a head of hair’ in Latin and ‘a crown’ in Hebrew – perhaps both words were borrowed from a common Aegean original) should be spelt with a Kaph (= 20), not a Koph, which makes the sum add up to only 626.
¹ 该解答基于希伯来语。Nun=50；Resh=200；Vav=6；Nun=50=Neron。Koph=100；Samech=60；Resh=200=Kesar。但拉丁语中的尼禄写为希伯来语时仍为 Nero，而 Kaisar（在拉丁语中意为「头发」，在希伯来语中意为「王冠」——也许两个词都借自共同的愛琴语原词）应该用 Kaph（=20）而非 Koph 拼写，这使得总数仅为626。





Chapter Twenty

title: 第二十章
content:
A CONVERSATION AT PAPHOS – 43 AD
帕福斯的对话——公元43年





Circling the circlings of their fish,
Circling the circlings of their fish,（环绕着她们的鱼游转，）



Nuns walk in white and pray;
Nuns walk in white and pray;（修女们着白袍行走祈祷；）



For he is chaste as they….
For he is chaste as they….（因为他如她们一般贞洁……）





These lines will serve as a text to demonstrate the peculiar workings of poetic thought. They came to me, from nowhere in particular, as the first three lines of a rhyming stanza, in the epigrammatic style of the Welsh englyn, which required two more to complete it. Their manifest meaning is that the white nuns walk in silent prayer in their convent garden, circling the fish pool and circling their rosaries in chaste prayer; the fish swims around inside. The fish, like the nuns, is proverbial for his sexual indifference, and the Mother Superior permits him as a convent pet because he cannot possibly awake any lascivious thoughts in her charges.
这几行诗将作为一个文本来展示诗性思维的独特运作方式。它们不知从何处来到我脑中，作为一首押韵诗节的前三行，采用威尔士 englyn（短诗）的格言风格，还需要两行才能完成。它们的表面含义是：白衣修女们在修道院花园中默默绕行祈祷，环绕着鱼池一圈圈走，同时一圈圈拨动念珠；鱼在池中游转。鱼如同修女一样，以其性冷淡而著称，修道院长允许它作为修院宠物，因为它不可能在她管辖的修女中唤起任何淫念。

A neat piece of observation, but not yet a poem; the truth, but not the whole truth. To tell the whole truth, I had to consider first the phenomenon of nuns, who voluntarily forgo the pleasures of carnal love and motherhood in order to become the Vestal brides of Christ, and then the phenomenon of sacred fish of all sorts and sizes, from the great fish that swallowed Jonah to the little spotted fish in wishing wells that still grant lovers or babies to peasant women in remote parishes; not forgetting the ‘mighty and stainless Fish from the Fountain whom a pure virgin grasped’ in the epitaph of the late second-century bishop Aviricius of the Phrygian Pentapolis. Only when I had asked and answered some scores of teasing questions would the fourth and fifth lines be found, to complete the poem with a simple concentration of difficult meaning.
这是一则精巧的观察，但还不是一首诗；是真相，但不是全部真相。要讲述全部真相，我必须首先考虑修女这一现象——她们自愿放弃肉欲之爱和母性的愉悦，以成为基督的维斯塔贞女新娘——然后考虑各种各样大大小小的神圣鱼，从吞下约拿的大鱼到许愿井中小小的斑点鱼——后者至今仍为偏远教区的农妇赐予情人或婴儿；还有不要忘记弗里吉亚五城主教阿维基乌斯二世后期墓志铭中「从泉源而来的大有能力且无玷的鱼，为纯洁处女所持」。只有当我提出并回答了数十个习钻问题之后，第四和第五行才会被发现，以对困难含义的简洁集中来完成这首诗。

I began by noting the strange continuance in Christianity of the original pagan title of Chief Pontiff, which the Bishop of Rome, the successor of St. Peter the Fisherman, assumed two centuries after Christianity had become the Roman state religion. For the Chief Pontiff, in Republican and early Imperial times, was personally responsible to the Capitoline Trinity (Jupiter, Juno and Minerva), for the chaste behaviour of the Vestals, as his successor now is to the Christian Trinity for that of Roman Catholic nuns. Then I threw my mind back in an analeptic trance. I found myself listening to a conversation in Latin, helped out with Greek, which I understood perfectly. Presently I began to distinguish the voices as those of Theophilus, a well-known Syrian-Greek historian and Lucius Sergius Paulus, a Roman Governor-General of Cyprus under the Emperor Claudius.
我首先注意到基督教中异教首席祭司原始称号的奇特延续——罗马主教，即渔夫圣彼得的继承者，在基督教成为罗马国教两个世纪后仍采取了这一称号。因为在共和时代和帝国早期，首席祭司个人向卡比托利欧三神（朱庇特、朱诺和密涅瓦）负责维斯塔贞女的贞洁行为，正如他的继任者现在向基督教三一神负责天主教修女的贞洁行为。然后我在回溯恍惚中把心智拉回过去。我发现自己正在听一段用拉丁语进行、以希腊语辅助的对话，我完全听得懂。不久我开始辨认出声音属于狄奥菲卢斯——一位著名的叙利亚-希腊历史学家——和卢基乌斯·塞尔吉乌斯·保卢斯——克劳狄皇帝治下的罗马塞浦路斯总督。

Paulus was saying rather heavily ‘My learned friend, a festal system of such complexity cannot have been conveyed from country to country among the bales of merchandize that traders carry in barter. It may have been imposed by conquest, yet had there ever been an Empire of Europe which included all the distant parts you mention –’
保卢斯颇为沉重地说道：「我的博学朋友，如此复杂的节日体系不可能随商人贩运的一包包货物从一国传到另一国。它可能是被征服者强加的，但可曾有过一个囊括你所提及所有遥远地区的欧洲帝国——」

‘I should also have included Portugal among them,’ interjected Theophilus.
「我还应该把葡萄牙包括在内，」狄奥菲卢斯插话道。

‘– doubtless we should have heard of it. But Alexander’s conquests were all in the East: he dared not challenge the power of Republican Rome.’
「——我们无疑应该听说过它。但亚历山大的征服全在东方：他不敢挑战共和罗马的势力。」

Theophilus said: ‘What I mean is this. I postulate a constant emigration, in ancient times, of tribes inhabiting the Southern coast of the Black Sea, a process that has indeed ceased only in the last century or two. The climate was healthy, the people vigorous and well organized, but the coastal strip narrow. Every hundred years or so, as I suppose, the land grew over-populated, and one tribe or another was necessarily sent away to seek its fortune and make room for the rest. Or it may be that they were forced to move by pressure from the East, when wandering hordes from the plains of Asia broke through the Caspian Gates of the Caucasus mountains. Of these tribes, some took the route southward across Asia Minor and ventured through Syria and as far as Egypt – we have the authority of Herodotus for this; some took the route westward across the Bosphorus and Thrace and into Greece, Italy and Gaul and even, as I say, to Spain and Portugal. Some struggled south-eastward into Chaldaea across the Taurus mountains; some moved northward up the Western shore of the Black Sea and then followed the Danube to Istria, continuing their march across Europe until they reached the north-westerly tip of Gaul; whence, it is said, some crossed over into Britain, and from Britain into Ireland. They took the festal system with them.’
狄奥菲卢斯说：「我的意思是这样的。我假设古代有一个从黑海南海岸部落持续外迁的过程，这一过程实际上直到上一两个世纪才停止。那里气候宜人，人民精壮且组织良好，但海岸狭窄。我想，大约每一百年左右，土地变得人口过剩，某个部落就必须被派出去另谋出路、为其余部落腾出空间。或者他们可能是被来自东方的压力所迫——当亚洲平原的游牧部落突破高加索山脉的里海门户时。这些部落中，有些取道南方穿越小亚细亚，冒险穿过叙利亚远至埃及——对此我们有希罗多德的权威；有些取道西行穿越博斯普鲁斯和色雷斯进入希腊、意大利和高卢，甚至如我所说到了西班牙和葡萄牙。有些东南行穿过陶鲁斯山脉进入迦勒底亚；有些北行沿黑海西岸然后沿多瑙河到伊斯特里亚，继续穿越欧洲行军直到抵达高卢的西北角；据说有些人从那里渡海到了不列颠，又从不列颠到了爱尔兰。他们带走了节日体系。」

‘Yours is a very daring theory,’ said Paulus, ‘but I can recall no authentic tradition that supports it.’
「你的理论非常大胆，」保卢斯说，「但我想不起任何可靠的传统支持它。」

Theophilus smiled. ‘Your Excellency is a true Roman – “no truth unless hallowed by a tradition.” Well, then: tell me, from what land did your hero Aeneas come?’
狄奥菲卢斯微笑道：「阁下是个真正的罗马人——『没有传统认可的就不算真理。』那么，请告诉我，你们的英雄埃涅阿斯来自哪个国家？」

‘He was a King of Dardanus on the Bosphorus before he settled in Troy.’
「他在定居特洛伊之前是博斯普鲁斯达达努斯的国王。」

‘Good: Dardanus is three-quarters of the way back from Rome to the Black Sea. And, tell me, what was the priceless possession that Aeneas brought with him from Troy? Pray forgive the dialectical method.’
「好：达达努斯从罗马回溯到黑海的路程已走了四分之三。那么，请告诉我，埃涅阿斯从特洛伊带来的无价之宝是什么？请原谅我的辩证法。」

‘You must mean the Palladium, most learned Socrates,’ answered Paulus in ironically academic tones, ‘on the safety of which the fate of Troy once depended; and the fate of Rome depends now.’
「你一定是指帕拉迪乌姆，最博学的苏格拉底，」保卢斯以反讽的学究口吻答道，「特洛伊的命运曾经取决于它的安全；现在罗马的命运也取决于它。」

‘And what, honoured Alcibiades, is the Palladium?’
「那么，尊敬的阿尔基比亚德斯，帕拉迪乌姆是什么？」

‘A venerable statue of Pallas Athene.’
「一尊古老的帕拉斯·雅典娜像。」

‘Ah, but who is she?’
「啊，但她是谁？」

‘You suggested this morning, during our visit to the wrestling-school, that she was originally a Sea-goddess like our local Cyprian deity; and mythographers record that she was born by the Lake of Triton in Libya.’
「今天早上我们在参观摔跤学校时你暗示过，她原本是一位海女神，如同我们当地的塞浦路斯神祇；神话编撰者记载她生于利比亚的特里同湖畔。」

‘So she was. And who or what is Triton, besides being the name of a once extensive lake which is now shrinking into salt marsh?’
「确实如此。那么特里同是谁或什么，除了是一个曾经广阔现在正缩成盐沼的湖泊的名称之外？」

‘Triton is a marine deity with a fish’s body who accompanies Poseidon the Sea-god and his wife Amphitrite the Sea-goddess, and blows a conch in their honour. He is said to be their son.’
「特里同是一位鱼身海神，伴随海神波塞冬及其妻子海女神安菲特里忒，并为他们吹奏海螺。据说他是他们的儿子。」

‘You give me the most helpful answers. But what does Pallas mean?’
「你给了我最有帮助的回答。但帕拉斯是什么意思？」

‘How long is this cross-examination to last? Would you send me back to school again? Pallas is one of Athene’s titles. I have never accepted Plato’s derivation of the word from pallein, to brandish; he says, you know, that she is called Pallas because she brandishes her aegis, or shield. Plato’s etymology is always suspect. What puzzles me is that Pallas is a man’s name, not a woman’s.’
「这场盘问还要持续多久？你要把我送回学校吗？帕拉斯是雅典娜的称号之一。我从不接受柏拉图将此词派生自 pallein（挥舞）的说法；他说，你知道的，她被称为帕拉斯是因为她挥舞她的羊皮盾。柏拉图的词源总是可疑的。让我困惑的是帕拉斯是男性名字，不是女性名字。」

‘I hope to be able to explain the paradox. But, first, what do you know about men called Pallas?’
「我希望能解释这个悖论。但首先，你对叫帕拉斯的人知道些什么？」

‘Pallas? Pallas? There have been many men of the name, from the legendary Pallas the Titan to our present egregious Secretary of State. The Emperor made the Senate snigger the other day by declaring that the Secretary was of the famous Pallas family that gave its name to the Palatine Hill.’
「帕拉斯？帕拉斯？叫这个名字的人很多，从传说中的提坦帕拉斯到我们当今那位显赫的国务秘书。皇帝前几天让元老院窃笑，宣称那位秘书出身于给帕拉蒂尼山得名的著名帕拉斯家族。」

‘I doubt whether the remark was as absurd as it must have sounded. Claudius, for all his eccentric habits, is no mean historian, and as Chief Pontiff has access to ancient religious records denied to others. Come, your Excellency, let us go together through the list of ancient Pallases. There was, as you say, Pallas the Titan, who was brother to Astraeus (“the Starlike”) and Perses (“the Destroyer”) and who married – whatever that means – the River Styx in Arcadia. He was the father of Zelos (“Zeal”), Cratos (“Strength”), Bia (“Force”) and Nicë (“Victory”). Does that not convey his mystical nature to you?’
「我怀疑这话并不像听起来那么荒谬。克劳狄虽然习性古怪，却是一位不差的历史学家，而且作为首席祭司他可以查阅他人无法接触的古代宗教记录。来吧，阁下，让我们一起梳理一下古代帕拉斯们的名单。如你所说，有提坦帕拉斯，他是阿斯特赖俄斯（「星辉者」）和珀耳塞斯（「毁灭者」）的兄弟，娶了——不管这意味着什么——阿卡迪亚的斯堤克斯河。他是泽洛斯（「热忱」）、克拉托斯（「力量」）、比亚（「暴力」）和尼刻（「胜利」）之父。这难道没有向你传达他的神秘本质吗？」

‘I regret to admit that it does not. Pity me as a stupid, legalistic and practical Roman.’
「很遗憾没有。请怜悯我这个愚钝的、法律至上且讲求实际的罗马人吧。」

‘If your Excellency is not careful I shall begin praising your elegiac poem on the Nymph Egeria, a copy of which was lately sent me from Rome by one of our mutual friends. Well, next comes Homer’s Pallas, whom he calls the father of the Moon. And next another Titan, the Pallas who was flayed by Athene; it was this Pallas from whom she is said to have taken her name.’
「如果阁下不小心的话，我就要开始称赞你那首关于宁芙埃格里娅的哀歌了——我们一位共同的朋友最近从罗马给我寄来了一份抄本。好吧，接下来是荷马的帕拉斯，他称之为月亮之父。再接下来是另一位提坦，被雅典娜剥皮的帕拉斯；据说雅典娜的名字就是从他那里取的。」

‘I never heard that story.’
「我从未听过这个故事。」

‘It rests on good authority. And then comes Pallas, the founder of Pallantium in Arcadia, a Pelasgian son of the Aegeus who gave his name to the Aegean Sea; now, he is of interest to us because his grandson Evander emigrated to Rome sixty years before the Trojan war and brought your sacred alphabet with him. It was he who founded a new city of Pallantium on the Palatine Hill at Rome, long since incorporated in the City. He also introduced the worship of Nicë, Neptune, (now identified with Poseidon), Pan of Lycos, Demeter and Hercules. Evander had a son named Pallas, and two daughters, Romë (“Strength”) and Dynë (“Power”). And I had almost forgotten still another Pallas, brother of Aegeus and Lycos, and therefore uncle to Evander’s grandfather Pallas.’
「这有可靠的权威依据。然后是帕拉斯，阿卡迪亚帕兰提翁的创建者，一个佩拉斯吉人，埃勾斯之子——埃勾斯给了爱琴海其名；他让我们感兴趣，因为他的孙子埃万德在特洛伊战争前六十年移民到罗马并带来了你们的神圣字母表。正是他在罗马帕拉蒂尼山建立了一座新的帕兰提翁城，早已并入罗马城中。他还引入了对尼刻、尼普顿（现已等同于波塞冬）、吕科斯来的潘、得墨忒耳和赫拉克勒斯的崇拜。埃万德有一个名叫帕拉斯的儿子，还有两个女儿，罗墨（「力量」）和狄墨（「权力」）。我差点忘了另一位帕拉斯，他是埃勾斯和吕科斯的兄弟，因此是埃万德祖父帕拉斯的叔父。」

‘A fine crop of Pallases. But I am still in the dark.’
「好一群帕拉斯。但我仍是一头雾水。」

‘Well, I do not blame your Excellency. And I hardly know where to shine the lantern. But I appeal to you for patience. Tell me, of what is the Palladium made?’
「嗯，我不怪阁下。我几乎不知道该把灯笼照向哪里。但我请你耐心。请告诉我，帕拉迪乌姆是用什么做的？」

Paulus considered. ‘I am rather rusty on mythology, my dear Theophilus, but I seem to remember that it is made of the bones of Pelops.’
保卢斯想了想。「我的神话学有些生疏了，亲爱的狄奥菲卢斯，但我似乎记得它是用珀洛普斯的骨头做的。」

Theophilus congratulated him. ‘And who was Pelops? What does his name mean?’
狄奥菲卢斯恭喜他。「那么珀洛普斯是谁？他的名字是什么意思？」

‘I was reading Apollonius Rhodius the other day. He says that Pelops came to Phrygia from Enete in Paphlagonia and that the Paphlagonians still call themselves Pelopians. Apollonius was curator of the great Alexandrian Library and his ancient history is as reliable as anyone’s. As for the name “Pelops”, it means dusky-faced. The body of Pelops was served up as a stew by Tantalus, his father, for the Gods; they discovered that it was forbidden food just in time. Only the shoulder had been eaten – by Demeter, was it not? – but some say Rhea, and restitution was made with an ivory shoulder. Pelops was brought back to life.’
「前几天我在读罗德岛的阿波罗尼乌斯。他说珀洛普斯从帕夫拉戈尼亚的埃内忒来到弗里吉亚，帕夫拉戈尼亚人至今仍自称珀洛庇亚人。阿波罗尼乌斯是亚历山大图书馆的馆长，他的古代史与任何人一样可靠。至于『珀洛普斯』这个名字，意为黝黑面孔。珀洛普斯的身体被他父亲坦塔罗斯献给众神作为炖菜；他们及时发现这是禁食。只有肩膀被吃掉了——被得墨忒耳，不是吗？——但也有人说被瑞亚，后来以象牙肩膀修复。珀洛普斯被复活了。」

‘What do you make of this cannibalistic myth?’
「你对这个食人神话怎么解释？」

‘Nothing at all, except that we now seem to have traced the Dardanians back to the Black Sea, if the sacred Palladium was made of the bones of their ancestor from Enete.’
「什么也不解释，只是我们现在似乎已经把达达尼亚人追溯到了黑海——如果神圣的帕拉迪乌姆是用他们来自埃内忒的祖先的骨头做的话。」

‘If I suggest to you that Pelops and Pallas are different titles of Kings of the same early Greek dynasty, will that help your Excellency?’
「如果我向阁下建议珀洛普斯和帕拉斯是同一个早期希腊王朝国王的不同称号，这对阁下有帮助吗？」

‘Not in the least. Pray, give me a hand out of this quaking bog.’
「一点也没有。请把我从这片颤动的沼泽中拉出来吧。」

‘Allow me to ask you a riddle: What is it with a dusky face and an ivory shoulder that comes rushing victoriously up a river, as if to a wedding, full of Zeal, Force and Strength, and whose hide is well worth the flaying?’
「请允许我问你一个谜语：什么东西有着黝黑的面孔和象牙色的肩膀，从海中冲入河流，仿佛奔赴一场婚礼，充满了热忱、暴力和力量，它的皮值得被剥下？」

‘I am good at riddles, though bad at myths. A fish of sorts. I guess the porpoise. The porpoise is not an ordinary fish, for it couples, male with female: and how royally it charges into a river-mouth from the sea! It is pale below and dark above, with a blunt, dusky muzzle. And it has a fine white shoulder-blade – broad like a paddle; and porpoise leather makes the best-wearing shoes procurable.’
「我擅长猜谜，虽然不擅神话。某种鱼吧。我猜是鼠海豚。鼠海豚不是普通的鱼，因为它是雌雄交配的：它从海中冲入河口时何等威武！它腹部苍白而背部深色，有一个钝而黝黑的吻部。它有一块漂亮的白色肩胛骨——宽如船桨；鼠海豚皮做的鞋是能买到的最耐穿的。」

‘It is not a fish at all. It is a warm-blooded creature, a cetos, a sea-beast with lungs, not an ichthus, a fish with gills and cold blood. To the sea-beast family, according to Aristotle’s system, belong all whales, seals, porpoises, grampuses and dolphins. Unfortunately in Greece we use the same word delphis indiscriminately for both the beaked dolphin and the blunt-muzzled porpoise; and though Arion’s musical mount is likely to have been a true dolphin, it is uncertain whether Delphi was originally named after the dolphin or the porpoise. “Pallas” in Greek once meant a lusty young man, and I suppose that it became the royal title of Peloponnesian kings, whose sacred beast was the lusty porpoise, when the tribe of Pelops came down into Greece from the Black Sea. Do you remember Homer’s much disputed epithet for Lacedaemon – Cetoessa, which literally means “Of the Sea-beast”?’
「它根本不是鱼。它是温血动物，是 cetos，有肺的海兽，不是 ichthus，有鳃和冷血的鱼。按亚里士多德的分类，海兽科包括所有鲸鱼、海豹、鼠海豚、虎鲸和海豚。不幸的是，在希腊我们不加区分地用同一个词 delphis 指称尖喙海豚和钝吻鼠海豚；虽然阿里翁的音乐坐骑很可能是一头真正的海豚，但德尔斐最初是以海豚还是鼠海豚命名的尚不确定。「帕拉斯」在希腊语中曾意为壮健的年轻人，我想当珀洛普斯的部落从黑海来到希腊时，它成为了伯罗奔尼撒国王的王家称号，其神圣动物就是壮健的鼠海豚。你记得荷马对拉刻代蒙那个备受争议的修饰语吗——Cetoessa，字面意为「海兽之国」？」

‘I will try to think along the lines you lay out for me,’ said Paulus. ‘The Peloponnese is, of course, sometimes called the Land of Poseidon, who is the Achaean god of all sea-beasts and fishes. Arcadia is the centre of the Peloponnese, and Pallas the Sea-beast-god reigned there, and in Lacedaemon too. Let me work this out for myself – yes – Pallas is married to the River Styx, meaning that the porpoise comes rushing up the Crathis towards the Styx in his mating season. (At the mouth of the Crathis is Aegae – I once served in that part of Greece – which explains the connexion with Aegeus. Opposite Aegae, across the Gulf of Corinth, stands Delphi, sacred to Apollo the Dolphin-god or Porpoise-god.) Later, Evander a grandson of Pallas, and with a son of the same name, is driven out of Arcadia, about the time of the great Achaean invasion, and comes to Rome. There he forms an alliance with the people of Aeneas, claiming kinship with them in virtue of a common descent from Pelops. Is that how you read the story?’
「我试着按你给我划的路线来思考，」保卢斯说。「伯罗奔尼撒有时当然被称为波塞冬之地，他是亚该亚人的所有海兽和鱼类之神。阿卡迪亚是伯罗奔尼撒的中心，海兽之神帕拉斯在那里统治，在拉刻代蒙也是如此。让我自己推演一下——是的——帕拉斯娶了斯堤克斯河，意味着鼠海豚在交配季节沿克拉西斯河冲向斯堤克斯。（克拉西斯河口是埃盖——我曾在希腊那个地区服役——这解释了与埃勾斯的联系。在埃盖对面，跨过科林斯湾，矗立着德尔斐，神圣于海豚之神或鼠海豚之神阿波罗。）后来，帕拉斯的孙子埃万德——他也有一个同名儿子——在大亚该亚入侵时期被逐出阿卡迪亚，来到罗马。在那里他与埃涅阿斯的人民结盟，以共同源于珀洛普斯的血缘关系为由。你是这样理解这个故事的吗？」

‘Exactly. And Evander was probably a Pallas too, but changed his name, after killing his father, to throw the avenging Furies off the scent.’
「完全如此。埃万德可能本来也姓帕拉斯，但在杀死父亲后改了名字，以甩掉复仇女神的追踪。」

‘Very well. He introduces the worship of the Sea-god Neptune; of Nicë, the daughter of the original Pallas; of Hercules – why Hercules?’
「很好。他引入了对海神尼普顿的崇拜；对原始帕拉斯之女尼刻的崇拜；对赫拉克勒斯的崇拜——为什么是赫拉克勒斯？」

‘His sexual lustiness commended him, and he was not only a great-grandson of Pelops but an ally of the Enetians, the original Pelopians.’
「他的性欲旺盛值得推荐，而且他不仅是珀洛普斯的曾孙，还是埃内忒人——最初的珀洛庇亚人——的盟友。」

‘And why Demeter?’
「那为什么是得墨忒耳？」

‘To rescue her from Poseidon the god of the Achaeans who, it is said, had raped her. You remember perhaps that she retreated from him up the Crathis to the Styx and there cursed the water. Demeter was old Deo, the barley-planting Mother-goddess of the Danaan Arcadians. That some mythographers call her Rhea proves her Cretan origin. Her famous mare-headed statue at Phigalia, by the River Neda in Western Arcadia, held a porpoise in one hand and in the other a sacred black dove of the sort that is used at the oak-oracle of Dodona.’
「为了从亚该亚人的神波塞冬手中解救她——据说波塞冬强暴了她。你也许记得她沿克拉西斯河退至斯堤克斯河并在那里诅咒了水。得墨忒耳就是古老的德奥，达南阿卡迪亚人的种植大麦的母神。一些神话编撰者称她为瑞亚，证明了她源于克里特。她在西阿卡迪亚涅达河畔菲伽利亚的著名马头雕像，一手持鼠海豚，另一手持一只神圣的黑鸽——就是在多多纳橡树神谕中使用的同一种。」

‘Why mare-headed?’
「为什么是马头？」

‘The horse was sacred to her, and when the Pelopians intermarried with the original Arcadians, this was recorded in myth as a marriage between Pelops and Hippodameia, “the Horse-tamer”, who is also called Danais by some mythographers. And among their children were Chrysippos, “Golden Horse”; Hippalcmos, “Bold Horse”; Nicippe, “Victorious Mare” – new clan-names.’
「马是她的神圣动物，当珀洛庇亚人与原始阿卡迪亚人通婚时，这在神话中被记录为珀洛普斯与希波达弥亚（Hippodameia，「驯马女」）的婚姻——一些神话编撰者也称她为达奈斯。他们的孩子中有克律西波斯（Chrysippos，「金马」）、希帕尔喀摩斯（Hippalcmos，「猛马」）、尼基佩（Nicippe，「胜马」）——都是新的氏族名。」

‘I see. It is not so nonsensical as it sounds. Well, now I can fill out the story. The Mother-goddess was served by the so-called Daughters of Proetus or Proteus,1 who lived in a cave at Lusi, by the headwaters of the Styx. Her priestesses had a right to the shoulder-blade of the sacred porpoise at a sacrificial feast. Porpoise beef makes very good eating, especially when it has been well hung. And Proteus, according to Homer, became herdsman to Poseidon and tended his sea-beasts. That must have been after Poseidon’s conquest of the Goddess, which he celebrated by calling himself the Mare-tamer. I take Proteus to be another name for Pallas, the Sea-beast: the Achaeans, in fact, enslaved the Pelopians, who were now also styled Danaans, and Poseidon took over the prerogatives and titles of Pallas.’
「我明白了。这并不像听起来那么荒谬。好吧，现在我可以补全故事了。母神由所谓的普罗埃图斯或普罗透斯之女¹侍奉，她们住在卢西的一个洞穴中，位于斯堤克斯河源头附近。她的女祭司在献祭宴上有权获得神圣鼠海豚的肩胛骨。鼠海豚肉非常好吃，尤其悬挂熟成后。据荷马记载，普罗透斯成为波塞冬的牧人，照管他的海兽。这必定是在波塞冬征服女神之后——他以自称驯马者来庆祝这一征服。我认为普罗透斯是海兽帕拉斯的另一个名字：亚该亚人奴役了珀洛庇亚人——后者现在也被称为达南人——波塞冬接管了帕拉斯的特权和称号。」

‘I congratulate your Excellency. You evidently agree with me in dismissing as mistaken the view that Pelops was an Achaean – unless perhaps an earlier Achaean horde had entered Greece many centuries before with the Aeolians; I suppose that the mistake arose from the knowledge that Pelops was once worshipped in the northern province of the Peloponnese now called Achaea. For the enslavement of the Pelopians by the Achaeans is confirmed in another, rather frivolous myth: Poseidon is said to have fallen in love with Pelops, as Zeus with Ganymede, and to have carried him off to be his cup-bearer. Neptune, who emigrated to Italy was, you will agree, also Pallas and must not be identified with Poseidon as the custom is. But I should guess Proteus to be a general name of the god who is the son, lover and victim of the old Mother Goddess; and assumes a variety of shapes. He is not only Pallas, the sea-beast, but Salmoneus the human oak-king, Chrysippos the golden horse, and so forth.’
「恭喜阁下。你显然同意我的看法，即珀洛普斯是亚该亚人这一观点是错误的——除非也许更早的亚该亚游群早在数百年前就随埃俄利亚人进入了希腊；我想这个错误源于人们知道珀洛普斯曾在伯罗奔尼撒北部现今称为亚该亚的地区受过崇拜。因为珀洛庇亚人被亚该亚人奴役这一点在另一个颇为轻浮的神话中得到证实：据说波塞冬爱上了珀洛普斯，如同宙斯爱上伽尼墨得斯一样，将他掳走做斟酒人。移民到意大利的尼普顿，你也会同意，同样是帕拉斯，不应如惯例那样等同于波塞冬。但我猜测普罗透斯是那位作为老母女神之子、情人和牺牲品的神的通名；他呈现各种形态。他不仅是海兽帕拉斯，还是人形橡树之王萨尔摩纽斯、金马克律西波斯等等。」

‘But Pan of Lycos? What had Evander to do with him?’
「但吕科斯来的潘呢？埃万德与他有什么关系？」

‘His ancestor Pelops probably brought him from the River Lycos, which flows into the Black Sea not far from Enete. Another lusty god. You will recall that he danced for joy when Pelops was fitted out with his new white shoulder. By the way, do you recall the various stories of Pan’s parentage?’
「他的祖先珀洛普斯大概是从吕科斯河把他带来的——那条河注入黑海，离埃内忒不远。又一位壮健之神。你大概记得，当珀洛普斯装上他新的白色肩膀时，潘高兴地跳了舞。顺便问一下，你记得关于潘出身的各种故事吗？」

‘The usual one makes him a son of the nymph Dryope by Hermes.’
「通常的说法是他是宁芙德律俄佩与赫尔墨斯之子。」

‘What does that convey to you?’
「这向你传达了什么？」

‘I have never considered. “Dryope” means a woodpecker of the sort that nests in oaks and makes an extraordinary noise with its bill in the cracks of trees, and climbs spirally up the trunk. It has a barbed tongue and portends rain, as the dolphin and porpoise portend storms by their frisking. And the nymph Dryope is connected with the cult of Hylas, a Phrygian form of Hercules who dies ceremonially every year. And Hermes – he’s the prime phallic god, and also the god of eloquence, and his erotic statues are usually carved from an oak.’
「我从未想过。德律俄佩（Dryope）意为一种啄木鸟，在橡树上筑巢，用喙在树缝中发出巨大的声响，并沿树干螺旋攀爬。它有带倒刺的舌头，预示降雨，如同海豚和鼠海豚的嬉戏预示暴风雨。宁芙德律俄佩与许拉斯的崇拜有关——许拉斯是赫拉克勒斯的弗里吉亚变体，每年仪式性死去。而赫尔墨斯——他是首要的阳具之神，也是雄辩之神，他的色情雕像通常用橡木雕刻。」

‘The tree of shepherds, the tree of Hercules, the tree of Zeus and Jupiter. But Pan, as the son of an oak-woodpecker, is hatched from an egg.’
「牧人之树，赫拉克勒斯之树，宙斯和朱庇特之树。但潘作为橡树啄木鸟之子，是从蛋中孵出来的。」

‘Hold hard,’ said Paulus. ‘I remember something to the point. Our Latin god Faunus, who is identical with Pan, the god of shepherds, is said to have been a King of Latium who entertained Evander on his arrival. And Faunus was the son of Picus, which is Latin for woodpecker. Evidently another Pelopian tribe had reached Latium from the Black Sea before either Evander or Aeneas. Faunus is worshipped in sacred groves, where he gives oracles; chiefly by voices heard in sleep while the visitant lies on a sacred fleece.’
「等一下，」保卢斯说，「我想到一些相关的。我们的拉丁神法乌努斯——与牧人之神潘同一——据说曾是拉丁姆的国王，在埃万德到达时款待了他。而法乌努斯是皮库斯之子，皮库斯在拉丁语中就是啄木鸟。显然，在埃万德或埃涅阿斯之前，另一个珀洛庇亚部落已从黑海到达拉丁姆。法乌努斯在神圣的树林中受崇拜，在那里他给予神谕——主要是访客躺在神圣羊皮上睡眠时听到的声音。」

‘Which establishes the mythical connexion between Pan, the oak, the woodpecker, and sheep. I have read another legend of his birth, too. He is said to have been the son of Penelope, Ulysses’ wife, by Hermes who visited her in the form of a ram. A ram, not a goat. This is odd, because both Arcadian Pan and his Italian counterpart Faunus have goat legs and body. I think I see how that comes about. Pallas the Titan, the royal sea-beast, was the son of Crios (the Ram). This means that the Pelopian settlers from Enete formed an alliance with the primitive Arcadians who worshipped Hermes the Ram, and acknowledged him as the father of their sea-beast King Pallas. Likewise the Aegeans – the goat-tribe – formed an alliance with the same Arcadians and acknowledged Hermes as the father of their Goat-king, Pan, whose mother was Amalthea and who became the He-goat of the Zodiac.’
「这确立了潘与橡树、啄木鸟和羊之间的神话联系。我还读过另一个关于他出生的传说。据说他是珀涅罗珀——尤利西斯之妻——与赫尔墨斯之子，赫尔墨斯以公羊之形来访她。公羊，而非山羊。这很奇怪，因为阿卡迪亚的潘和他的意大利对应者法乌努斯都有山羊的腿和身体。我想我明白这是怎么来的。提坦帕拉斯——王室海兽——是克瑞奥斯（Crios，公羊）之子。这意味着来自埃内忒的珀洛庇亚定居者与崇拜公羊神赫尔墨斯的原始阿卡迪亚人结盟，并承认赫尔墨斯为他们的海兽王帕拉斯之父。同样，埃勾斯人——山羊部落——也与同一阿卡迪亚人结盟，承认赫尔墨斯为他们的山羊王潘之父，潘的母亲是阿玛尔忒亚，他成为了黄道带的山羊。」

Paulus said smiling: ‘Neatly argued. That disposes of the other scandalous legend that Pan was the son of Penelope by all her suitors in the absence of Ulysses.’
保卢斯微笑道：「论证精巧。这也就处理了另一个丑闻性的传说——潘是珀涅罗珀在尤利西斯不在时与所有求婚者之子。」

‘Where did you get that version? It is extraordinarily interesting.’
「你从哪里得到那个版本的？它极为有趣。」

‘I cannot remember. From some grammarian or other. It makes little sense to me.’
「我记不清了。从某个语法学家那里。它对我来说没什么意义。」

‘I knew that Pan was the son of Penelope, but your version is a great improvement on it. Penelope, you see, is not really Ulysses’ wife except in a manner of speaking; she is a sacred bird, the penelops or purple-striped duck. So again, as in the Dryope version of his parentage, Pan is born from a bird – which explains the legend that he was perfectly developed from birth, as a hatched chicken is. Now to come to the suitors, by what I fear will be a longish argument. I postulate first of all that the Palladium is made from the bones of Pelops, that is to say from the ivory shoulder-blades of porpoises, a suitable and durable material, and that it is a phallic statue, not the statue of a goddess. I support my thesis by the existence, until a few years ago, of another sacred shoulder-blade of Pelops in the precinct which his great-grandson Hercules built in his honour at Olympia. Now, according to the myth, Pelops had only one sacred shoulder-blade, the right one; yet nobody has ever questioned the genuineness either of the relic at Olympia or of the Palladium. The history of the Olympian blade is this. During the siege of Troy the Greeks were told by an oracle that the only offensive counter-magic to the defensive magic of the Palladium preserved in the Citadel of Troy was the shoulder-blade of Pelops which a tribe of Pelopians had taken to Pisa in Italy. So Agamemnon sent for the thing, but the ship that was bringing it to him went down off the coast of Euboea. Generations later, a Euboean fisherman dragged it up in his net and recognized it for what it was – probably by some design carved on it. He brought it to Delphi and the Delphic Oracle awarded it to the people of Olympia, who made the fisherman its pensioned guardian. If the bone was the shoulder-blade of a sacred porpoise, not of a man, the difficulty of Pelops’s having had more than one right shoulder-blade disappears. So does the difficulty of believing that when boiled and eaten by the gods he came alive again – if the fact was that a new sacred porpoise was caught and eaten every year at Lusi by the devotees of Deo. Does all this sound reasonable?’
「我知道潘是珀涅罗珀之子，但你的版本比那好得多。你看，珀涅罗珀实际上并非尤利西斯之妻，只不过姑且这么说罢了；她是一种神圣的鸟——penelops，即紫纹鸭。所以，如同在他德律俄佩出身的版本中一样，潘是从鸟出生的——这解释了他从出生起就完美发育的传说，如同孵出的小鸡。现在说到求婚者们，恐怕要经过一段不短的论证。我首先假设帕拉迪乌姆是用珀洛普斯的骨头做的，也就是说用鼠海豚的象牙色肩胛骨做的——一种合适且耐久的材料——而且它是一尊阳具雕像，不是女神像。我以以下事实证明为支撑：直到几年前，另一块珀洛普斯的神圣肩胛骨还保存在他的曾孙赫拉克勒斯在奥林匹亚为他建造的圣域中。据神话记载，珀洛普斯只有一块神圣肩胛骨，即右肩；然而从来没有人质疑奥林匹亚圣物或帕拉迪乌姆的真伪。奥林匹亚肩胛骨的历史是这样的。在围攻特洛伊期间，希腊人得到一条神谕说，对抗保存在特洛伊卫城中帕拉迪乌姆防御魔法的唯一攻击性反魔法，是珀洛普斯的一块肩胛骨——一个珀洛庇亚部落把它带到了意大利的皮萨。于是阿伽门农派人去取，但运送它的船在埃维亚海岸外沉没了。数代之后，一个埃维亚渔民用网把它捞上来并认出了它是什么——大概是根据上面刻着的某种图案。他把它带到德尔斐，德尔斐神谕将它判给奥林匹亚的人民，他们让那个渔人做其领养老金的守护者。如果那骨头是神圣鼠海豚的肩胛骨而非人的，珀洛普斯拥有不止一块右肩胛骨的困难就消失了。同样消失的是相信他被煮熟并被众神吃掉后复活的困难——如果事实是每年在卢西由德奥的信徒捕食一头新的神圣鼠海豚。这一切听起来合理吗？」

‘More reasonable, by far, than the usual fantastic story, though cannibalism in ancient Arcadia is not incredible. And that the Palladium is a phallic statue, rather than that of a goddess, may explain why such a mystery has been made of its appearance and why it is hidden out of sight in the Penus of the Temple of Vesta. Yes, though your thesis is startling and even, at first hearing, indecent, it has much to commend it.’
「远比通常的荒诞故事合理，虽然古代阿卡迪亚的食人俗并非不可信。而帕拉迪乌姆是阳具雕像而非女神像这一观点，或许可以解释为何对其外观如此保密、为何它被藏在维斯塔神庙的至圣所中不见天日。是的，虽然你的论点令人吃惊，初听起来甚至不雅，但它颇值得考虑。」

‘Thank you. To continue: you remember that two or three of the early Kings of Rome had no discoverable father?’
「谢谢。继续：你记得早期罗马的两三位国王没有可查的父亲吗？」

‘Yes. I have often wondered how that happened.’
「是的。我常想这是怎么回事。」

‘You remember, too, that the Kingdom descended in the female line: a man was king only by virtue of marriage to a queen or of descent from a queen’s daughter. The heir to the Kingdom, in fact, was not the king’s son but the son of either his youngest daughter or his youngest sister – which explains the Latin word nepos, meaning both nephew and grandson. The focus of the community life was literally the focus, or hearth-fire, of the royal house, which was tended by the princesses of the royal line, namely the Vestal Virgins. To them the Palladium was delivered for safe-keeping as the fatale pignus imperii, the pledge granted by the Fates for the permanency of the royal line.’
「你也记得，王位沿母系传承：一个人之所以为王，仅因娶了女王或是女王之女的后裔。事实上，王位继承人不是国王之子，而是他最幼之女或最幼之妹之子——这解释了拉丁词 nepos 兼指外甥和孙子的原因。社区生活的焦点，字面上就是 focus，即王室的灶火，由王室血脉的公主们——即维斯塔贞女——照管。帕拉迪乌姆被交付给她们保管，作为 fatale pignus imperii——命运女神赐予的王室永续之信物。」

‘They still have it safe. But if you are right about the statue’s obscene nature, the Vestal Virgins seem rather an odd choice of guardians, because they are strictly forbidden to indulge in sexual intercourse!’
「她们仍安全保管着它。但如果你关于雕像猥亵性质的说法是对的，维斯塔贞女似乎是相当奇特的守护者选择，因为她们被严格禁止发生性行为！」

Theophilus laid his forefinger along his nose and said: ‘It is the commonplace paradox of religions that nothing is nefas, unlawful, that is not also fas, lawful, on particularly holy occasions. Among the Egyptians the pig is viewed with abhorrence and its very touch held to cause leprosy – indeed, the Egyptian pig as a scavenger and corpse-eater merits this abhorrence – yet the highest-born Egyptians eat its flesh with relish at their midwinter mysteries and fear no untoward consequence. The Jews, it is said, formerly did the same, if they do not do so now. Similarly, the Vestal Virgins cannot always have been debarred from the full natural privileges of their sex, for no barbarous religion enforces permanent sterility on nubile women. My view is that at midsummer during the Alban Holiday, which was a marriage feast of the Oak-queen – your Excellency’s charming nymph Egeria – with the Oak-king of the year, and the occasion of promiscuous love-making, the six Vestals, her kinswomen, coupled with six of the Oak-king’s twelve companions – you will recall Romulus’s twelve shepherds. But silently, in the darkness of a sacred cave so that nobody knew who lay with whom, nor who was the father of any child born. And did the same again with the six other companions at midwinter during the Saturnalia. Then, failing a son of the Oak-queen, the new king was chosen from a child born to a Vestal. So Penelope’s son by six suitors is explained. The Lusty God – call him Hercules or Hermes or Pan or Pallas or Pales or Mamurius or Neptune or Priapus or whatever you please – inspired the young men with erotic vigour when they had first danced around a blazing bonfire presided over by his obscene statue – the Palladium itself. Thus it happened that a king was said to be born of a virgin mother, and either to have no known father, or to be the son of the god.’
狄奥菲卢斯把食指沿鼻梁放着说：「这是宗教中常见的悖论：没有什么 nefas（不合法的）不是在特别神圣的场合也是 fas（合法的）。在埃及人那里，猪被视为可憎，接触它据说会导致麻风——确实，埃及的猪作为食腐动物和食尸者理应受到这种憎恶——然而最高贵的埃及人在冬至密仪中大快朵颐其肉，不怕任何不良后果。据说犹太人从前也如此，如果他们现在不再如此的话。同样，维斯塔贞女不可能一直被剥夺其性别的全部自然权利，因为没有哪个野蛮宗教会对成熟女性强制永久绝育。我的观点是，在仲夏的阿尔巴节日期间——那是橡树女王与当年橡树之王的婚宴，也是纵情狂欢的场合——六名维斯塔贞女作为她的女亲眷，与橡树之王的十二名同伴中的六名交媾——你会记得罗慕路斯的十二个牧人。但是默默地，在神圣洞穴的黑暗中，没人知道谁与谁同床，也没人知道所生任何孩子的父亲是谁。在仲冬的农神节期间又与其余六名同伴做同样的事。然后，如果橡树女王无子，新国王就从维斯塔贞女所生的孩子中选出。因此珀涅罗珀与六个求婚者之子得到了解释。壮健之神——无论你称他为赫拉克勒斯还是赫尔墨斯还是潘还是帕拉斯还是帕莱斯还是马穆里乌斯还是尼普顿还是普里阿波斯还是任何你喜欢的名字——在年轻男子们首先围着他的猥亵雕像——帕拉迪乌姆本身——主持的熊熊篝火跳舞之后，赋予他们色情的活力。因此，国王据说由处女母亲所生，要么没有已知父亲，要么是神之子。」

‘That is a still more startling notion than the other,’ protested Paulus, ‘and I cannot see either that you have any proof of it, or that you can explain how the Vestals ceased to be love-nymphs and became barren spinsters as now.’
「这比另一个说法更令人吃惊，」保卢斯抗议道，「我看不出你有什么证据，也无法解释维斯塔贞女如何从爱之宁芙变成了如今这样的不育老姑婆。」

‘The cessation of the royal love-orgies,’ said Theophilus, ‘follows logically on the historical course that we discussed yesterday – the extension of the kingship in ancient times from one year to four years; from four to eight; from eight to nineteen; until finally it became a life-tenure. Though popular love-orgies might continue – and at Rome continue still – to be held at midsummer and at the close of the year, they ceased to have any significance as occasions for breeding new kings. As we know, children are often born of these holiday unions and are considered lucky and cheerfully legitimized; but they have no claim to the kingship, because their mothers are no longer princesses, as formerly. It seems to have been King Tarquin the Elder who first prescribed for the Vestals what amounts to perpetual virginity, his object being to prevent them from breeding claimants to the throne. It was certainly he who introduced burying alive as a punishment for any Vestal who broke the rule; but even now the prescribed virginity is not perpetual – for after thirty years a Vestal Virgin is, I understand, entitled to unsanctify herself, if she pleases, and marry.’
「王室爱情狂欢的终止，」狄奥菲卢斯说，「逻辑上遵循我们昨天讨论的历史进程——古代王权从一年延长到四年；从四年到八年；从八年到十九年；直到最终成为终身制。虽然民间的爱情狂欢可能在仲夏和年终继续举行——在罗马至今仍在——但它们不再作为培育新国王的场合而具有任何意义。我们知道，这些节日结合所生的孩子常被视为幸运儿并被愉快地合法化；但他们无权继承王位，因为他们的母亲不再像从前那样是公主。似乎正是老塔昆王首次为维斯塔贞女规定了相当于永久童贞的规则，其目的是阻止她们生育王位觊觎者。也确实是他引入了活埋作为任何违规则维斯塔贞女的惩罚；但即便现在，规定的童贞也非永久——因为据我所知，三十年后维斯塔贞女有权——如果她愿意的话——解除圣化并出嫁。」

‘It happens very seldom; after thirty years of illustrious spinsterhood it is hard for a woman to win a husband of any worth, and she soon wearies of the world and usually dies of remorse.’
「这很少发生；在三十年的辉煌独身生活之后，一个女人很难找到任何值得的丈夫，她很快对世俗厌倦，通常死于悔恨。」

‘Now, as to the proof that the Virgins were once permitted occasional erotic delights: in the first place the novice, when initiated by the Chief Pontiff on behalf of the God, is addressed as “Amata”, beloved one, and given a head-dress bordered with pure purple,1 a white woollen fillet and a white linen vestment – the royal marriage garments of the bride of the God. In the second, we know that Silvia, the mother of Romulus and Remus, was a Vestal Virgin of Alba Longa and unexpectedly became the bride of Mamurius or Mars, then a red-faced, erotic Shepherd-god; and was not buried alive as a Vestal would now be if she became pregnant – even though she claimed that a god had forced her.’
「至于贞女曾一度被允许偶尔享受色情之乐的证据：首先，新手在由首席祭司代表神接纳时被称为「Amata」（被爱者），并被赐予镶纯紫色边的头饰¹、白色羊毛发带和白色亚麻法衣——神之新娘的王室婚服。其次，我们知道西尔维亚——罗慕路斯和瑞摩斯之母——是阿尔巴隆加的维斯塔贞女，意外地成为马穆里乌斯或马尔斯——当时一位红脸的色情牧神——的新娘；她并没有像如今怀孕的维斯塔贞女那样被活埋——尽管她声称是一位神强暴了她。」

‘They drowned Silvia in the River Anio, at all events.’
「不管怎样，他们把西尔维亚淹死在了阿尼奥河中。」

‘Only in a manner of speaking, I think. After the birth of her twins, whom she laid in the ark of osier and sedge, which is a commonplace in nativity myths of this sort, and consigned to the mercy of the waves, she took much the same baptismal bath in renewal of her virginity as the Priestess of Aphrodite yearly takes here at Paphos2 in the blue sea, and the nymph Dryope in her fountain at Pegae.’
「我想只是姑且这么说。在生下双胞胎后——她把他们放在柳条和灯心草编的方舟中，这在这类诞生神话中很常见——交托给波浪发落，她在河中接受了与阿佛洛狄忒女祭司每年在此帕福斯的²蓝色海水中、以及宁芙德律俄佩在佩盖的泉水中所接受的同样的更新贞洁的洗礼浴。」

‘The connexion between Rome and Arcadia is, I grant, very close. The Shepherd-god sends a wolf, lycos, to alarm Silvia and then overpowers her in a cave. And when the twins are born, a wolf and a woodpecker bring them food. By the way, can you explain how Pan comes to have a wolf in his service, if he is a god of shepherds?’
「罗马与阿卡迪亚的联系，我承认，非常密切。牧神派了一头狼——lycos——去惊吓西尔维亚，然后在洞穴中制服了她。当双胞胎出生后，一头狼和一只啄木鸟为他们带来食物。顺便问一下，你能解释潘如果是一位牧人之神，怎么会有狼为他效劳吗？」

‘It was probably a were-wolf. The Arcadian religious theory is that a man is sent as an envoy to the wolves. He becomes a were-wolf for eight years, and persuades the wolf-packs to leave man’s flocks and children alone during that time. Lycaon the Arcadian initiated the practice, they say, and it is likely that your ancient Guild of Lupercal priests originally provided Rome with her were-wolf too. But to speak again of Silvia. The God not only ravished her in a dark cave overshadowed by a sacred grove, but took advantage of a total eclipse of the sun. He was hiding his true shape, I suppose; which was that of a sea-beast.’
「那大概是一头狼人。阿卡迪亚的宗教理论是：一个人被派去做狼的使者。他变成狼人八年，在此期间说服狼群不要侵扰人的畜群和儿童。据说阿卡迪亚的吕卡翁开创了这一做法，你们古老的卢佩卡尔祭司公会很可能最初就为罗马提供了狼人。但再说说西尔维亚。神不仅在一座被神圣树林遮蔽的黑暗洞穴中强暴了她，还利用了日全食。我想他是在隐藏自己的真形——那是一头海兽。」

‘You seem to have the whole business worked out. Perhaps you can also explain why the hair of a Vestal is cut at marriage and never allowed to grow?’
「你似乎已经把整件事都弄清楚了。也许你还能解释为什么维斯塔贞女的头发在婚礼时被剪短且永远不允许留长？」

‘That must have been King Tarquin’s prudent regulation. Women with their hair cut cannot perform magical spells. Doubtless he feared that they would revenge themselves on him for his severity towards them. Vestal Virgins were under the king’s sole charge in those days. It was he, not the Chief Pontiff, who had the privilege of scourging any Vestal who let the sacred fire go out, and scourging to death any Vestal who took a private lover.’
「那一定是塔昆王的审慎规定。剪了头发的女人无法施展魔法咒语。他无疑是担心她们会因他对她们的严厉而报复。在那些年代，维斯塔贞女由国王独自管辖。有权鞭打任何让圣火熄灭的维斯塔贞女、以及鞭死任何私通情人的维斯塔贞女的，是他而非首席祭司。」

‘And can you also tell me why they use spring-water mixed with powdered and purified brine in their sacrifices?’
「你还能告诉我为什么她们在献祭时使用泉水混合研磨净化过的盐水吗？」

‘Tell me first what are the medical properties of water mixed with brine?’
「请先告诉我水混合盐水的药用属性是什么？」

‘It is a strong emetic and purge.’
「它是强效催吐剂和泻药。」

‘Suitable for preparing celebrants for the midsummer and midwinter feasts? I had not thought of that supplementary use. What I am suggesting is that when the twelve young shepherds – the leaping priests of Mamurius or Pallas – performed their orgiastic dance for hour after hour around the blazing bonfires they must have sweated terribly and come near to fainting.’
「适合让参与者为仲夏和仲冬宴会做准备？我没想到那个补充用途。我的意思是，当十二个年轻牧人——马穆里乌斯或帕拉斯的跳跃祭司——在熊熊篝火周围一小时又一小时地表演狂欢舞蹈时，他们必定大汗淋漓，几近晕厥。」

‘I see what you mean. In the harvest-fields countrymen always refresh themselves with brine-water in preference to plain: it restores the salt that has been lost by sweating. Brine-water fetched by Vestals at the midsummer orgy must have restored the vigour of the shepherds like a charm. Still another question, in revenge for all those that you asked me: how does Triton come to be a son of Poseidon?’
「我明白你的意思。在收获季节的田野中，农人总是用盐水而非清水来恢复体力：它补充因出汗而流失的盐分。维斯塔贞女在仲夏狂欢中取来的盐水必定像魔法一样恢复了牧人们的体力。还有一个问题，作为对你问我所有问题的报复：特里同怎么成了波塞冬之子？」

‘In the same way as Proteus comes to be his herdsman. Originally Poseidon had nothing to do with the sea. The porpoise of the Crathis, the Delphic dolphin and the Phocian seal all belong to the earlier civilization. Poseidon won them as his own when he seized the Peloponnese and the opposite shores of the Gulf of Corinth and married the Sea-goddess Amphitrite. Triton must have been her son, probably by Hermes; perhaps he ruled at “Lacedaemon of the Sea-beast”. At any rate, Poseidon becomes his foster-father by marrying the Sea-goddess Amphitrite – I take this to be one of Athene’s original titles. (By the way, the ancient Seal-king Phoceus, who gave his name to Phocis, was the son of Ornytion, which means Son of the Chicken – and the Chicken, I suppose, is Pan again who was hatched from a woodpecker’s egg or the egg of a penelope duck.) Of one thing I am sure: unless we recognize Triton and Pallas and Pelops as originally a sea-beast incarnate in a dynasty of ancient kings, we can hope to find no sense in the legends of heroes who rescued maidens from sea-beasts. The heroes are princes who challenge the sea-beast king to combat and kill him, and marry the royal heiress whom he has put under close restraint and reign in his stead by virtue of this marriage. The royal heiress is his daughter, but she is also an incarnation of the Moon; which explains why Homer’s Pallas was the Moon’s father. You find the same story in the marriage of Peleus to the Sea-goddess Thetis after his killing of Phocus, the Seal-king of Aegina. Peleus means “the muddy one” and may be a variant form of Pelops – as Pelias, the name of the king whose former territory Peleus annexed, certainly is. There was a sea-beast at Troy; Hercules, in company with the same Peleus, killed it and rescued the princess Hesionë and made himself master of the city. And clearly the many stories of princes who were saved by dolphins from drowning suggest sacred paintings of these princes riding on dolphin-back in proof of sovereignty. Arion and Icadius and Enalus…’
「与普罗透斯怎么成了他的牧人同理。波塞冬最初与海无关。克拉西斯河的鼠海豚、德尔斐的海豚和福基斯的海豹都属于更早的文明。波塞冬在夺取伯罗奔尼撒和科林斯湾对岸、并娶了海女神安菲特里忒之后，才将它们据为己有。特里同必定是她的儿子，父亲可能是赫尔墨斯；也许他统治过「海兽之拉刻代蒙」。无论如何，波塞冬通过娶海女神安菲特里忒成为他的养父——我认为这是雅典娜的原始称号之一。（顺便说一下，古老的海豹之王福凯乌斯——他给了福基斯其名——是奥尔尼提翁之子，意为鸡之子——而这只鸡，我想又是潘，从啄木鸟的蛋或紫纹鸭的蛋中孵出。）有一点我确信：除非我们把特里同、帕拉斯和珀洛普斯认作原本是化身为古代王朝的海兽，否则我们不可能在英雄从海兽手中拯救少女的传说中找到任何意义。英雄是挑战海兽国王进行战斗并杀死他、娶他所严密看管的王室继承人为妻、凭借此婚姻代之为王的王子。王室继承人是他的女儿，但她也是月亮的化身；这解释了为何荷马的帕拉斯是月亮之父。你在佩琉斯杀死埃伊纳的海豹之王福科斯后娶海女神忒提斯的故事中可以看到同样的情节。佩琉斯意为「泥泞者」，可能是珀洛普斯的变体——而佩琉斯所吞并的领土的前国王佩利亚斯之名则肯定如此。特洛伊有一头海兽；赫拉克勒斯与同一个佩琉斯一起杀死了它，救出公主赫西俄涅并使自己成为该城的主人。显然，许多王子被海豚从溺水中所救的故事暗示的是这些王子骑在海豚背上以证明王权的神圣画像。阿里翁、伊卡狄乌斯和埃纳卢斯……」

‘Theseus, of course…’
「当然还有忒修斯……」

‘And Coeranus too, and Taras and Phalanthus. The common people always prefer anecdote, however improbable, to myth, however simple: they see a prince pictured astride a dolphin and take this for literal truth and feel obliged to account for his strange choice of steed.’
「还有科厄拉努斯、塔拉斯和法兰特斯。普通人总是偏爱轶事——无论多么不可能——而非神话——无论多么简单：他们看到一位王子被描绘为骑在海豚上，便将其当作字面真实，并觉得有义务解释他为何选择如此奇特的坐骑。」

‘But what you undertook to explain at the beginning of this conversation, and have not yet explained, is why the Goddess Athene has a male name as her principal title.’
「但你在这场对话开头承诺要解释、却尚未解释的是，为何女神雅典娜有一个男性名字作为她的主要称号。」

‘She has become androgynous: there are many such deities. Sin, for example, the Moon-deity of the Semites, and the Phoenician Baalith, and the Persian Mithras. The Goddess is worshipped first and is all-powerful; presently a God enters into equal power with her, and either they become twins, as happened when Artemis agreed to share Delos with Apollo of Tempe, or else they are joined in a single bi-sexual being. Thus the Orphic hymn celebrates Zeus as both Father and Eternal Virgin. Your own Jupiter is in the same hermaphroditic tradition.’
「她已变为雌雄同体：这样的神祇很多。例如闪族人的月神辛、腓尼基的巴力特、波斯的密特拉。女神首先受崇拜且全能；随后一位神进入与她同等的权力，要么他们成为双胞胎——如阿尔忒弥斯同意与坦佩的阿波罗共享提洛斯那样——要么他们合为单一的雌雄同体存在。因此俄耳甫斯赞美诗称颂宙斯既是父亲又是永恒处女。你们自己的朱庇特也属于同一雌雄同体传统。」

‘Our own Jupiter? You surprise me.’
「我们自己的朱庇特？你让我吃惊。」

‘Yes, do you not know the couplet written by Quintus Valerius Soranus, whom Crassus praised as the most learned of all who wore the toga? No? It runs:
「是的，你难道不知道昆图斯·瓦莱里乌斯·索拉努斯——克拉苏称赞他为所有穿托加者中最博学之人——所写的对句吗？不知道？是这样的：



Jupiter Omnipotens, rerum regum-que repertor,
Jupiter Omnipotens, rerum regum-que repertor,（全能的朱庇特，万物与诸王之源，）



Progenitor genetrix-que Deum, Deus unus et idem.
Progenitor genetrix-que Deum, Deus unus et idem.（众神之父亦为母，唯一之神亦同体。）





All kings, all things, entire
All kings, all things, entire（万王万物，全部）



From Jove the Almighty came –
From Jove the Almighty came –（皆自全能朱庇特来——）



Of Gods both dam and sire
Of Gods both dam and sire（众神之母与父）



Yet God the sole and same.
Yet God the sole and same.（却是唯一同一之神。）





And Varro, his rival in learning, writing of the Capitoline Trinity, agreed that together they form a single god: Juno being Nature as matter, Jupiter being Nature as the creative impulse, and Minerva being Nature as the mind which directs the creative impulse. Minerva, as you know, often wields Jupiter’s thunderbolts; therefore if Jupiter is Eternal Virgin, Minerva is equally Eternal Father. And there we are again: Minerva is universally identified with Pallas Athene, who is the Goddess of Wisdom. Athene is to Pallas as Minerva is to Jupiter: his better half.’
而瓦罗——他在学问上与索拉努斯齐名——在写到卡比托利欧三神时同意，他们合在一起构成单一的神：朱诺是作为物质的自然，朱庇特是作为创造冲动的自然，密涅瓦是作为引导创造冲动之心灵的自然。如你所知，密涅瓦常挥舞朱庇特的雷霆；因此如果朱庇特是永恒处女，密涅瓦同样是永恒父亲。于是我们又回到了原点：密涅瓦被普遍等同于帕拉斯·雅典娜，即智慧女神。雅典娜之于帕拉斯，如同密涅瓦之于朱庇特：是他的另一半。」

‘I am getting confused in my mind between these various goddesses. Are they all the same person?’
「我在脑海里被这些不同的女神搞糊涂了。她们都是同一个人吗？」

‘Originally. She is older than all the gods. Perhaps her most archaic form is the Goddess Libya. If you read Apollonius recently you will recall that she appeared in triad by Lake Triton to Jason, wearing goatskins.’
「最初是的。她比所有神都古老。也许她最古老的形式是利比亚女神。如果你最近读过阿波罗尼乌斯，会记得她在特里同湖畔以三联体形式向伊阿宋显现，穿着羊皮。」

‘A bi-sexual deity naturally remains chaste, or so I judge from Minerva’s case,’ Paulus commented.
「雌雄同体的神自然保持贞洁，至少我从密涅瓦的情况判断如此，」保卢斯评论道。

‘Chaste as a fish.’
「贞洁如鱼。」

‘But when Jupiter began he was as unchaste as a sea-beast.’
「但朱庇特最初并不贞洁，他和海兽一样好色。」

‘Minerva reformed him.’
「密涅瓦改造了他。」

‘I daresay that is why she is called his daughter. My daughter Sergia reformed me. All daughters reform their fathers. Or try to. I was a leaping sea-beast as a young man.’
「我敢说这就是她被称为他女儿的原因。我的女儿塞尔吉娅改造了我。所有女儿都改造父亲。或者说试图改造。我年轻时也是一头跳跃的海兽。」

‘So was Apollo before his sister Artemis reformed him: he was a lusty dolphin once. But now chaste sacred fish are kept in his temples at Myra and Hierapolis.’
「阿波罗在他姐姐阿尔忒弥斯改造他之前也是如此：他曾经是一头壮健的海豚。但如今贞洁的神鱼被养在迈拉和希拉波利斯的他的神庙中。」

‘That reminds me of a question on which I am most anxious to be informed: what do you know of sea-beasts and fish in the Jewish religion? I understand that you have read their sacred books with some care.’
「这让我想起一个我非常渴望得到解答的问题：你对犹太宗教中的海兽和鱼知道些什么？我了解到你曾相当仔细地读过他们的圣书。」

‘Not recently. But I remember that there is a partial taboo on fish in the Jewish Torah, or Law; which suggests Egyptian influence. But not on scaled fish, only on the unsealed, and that would point to their having once held sea-beasts, such as the porpoise and dolphin, in reverence. Moreover, their sacred Ark – now lost – was covered with sea-beast skins; that is important. The Jews were tributary once to the Philistines, whose God was a sea-beast of many changes named Dagon – the Philistines are originally immigrants of Cretan Stock, despite their Semitic language. As I remember the story, the Philistines conquered the Jews and laid up the Ark in Dagon’s temple before his phallic statue, but the God enclosed in the Ark wrestled with Dagon and broke his statue into pieces. Yes, and the legendary hero who led the Jews into Judaea was called Jeshua, son of the Fish.’
「最近没读。但我记得犹太托拉即律法中对鱼有部分禁忌；这暗示了埃及影响。但并非对所有鱼，仅对无鳞鱼，这表明他们曾敬奉海兽如鼠海豚和海豚。此外，他们的神圣约柜——现已丢失——用海兽皮覆盖；这很重要。犹太人曾向非利士人纳贡，非利士人的神是一头多变的海兽，名叫达贡——非利士人虽然说闪族语言，但最初是克里特血统的移民。据我记得的故事，非利士人征服了犹太人并将约柜存放在达贡神庙中他的阳具雕像前，但约柜中的神与达贡搏斗并将他的雕像碎成碎片。是的，率领犹太人进入犹大的传说英雄名叫约书亚，鱼之子。」

‘Ha! That is exactly what I wanted to know. You see, a curious thing happened the other day. A written report reached me that a Jew named Barnabas was preaching some new mystical doctrine in a Jewish synagogue at the other end of the island; it was described by my informant, a Syrian Greek from Antioch with a Jewish mother, as a doctrine endangering the peace of the island. I sent for Barnabas and the other fellow and heard what both had to say. I forget his original name, but he had become a Roman citizen and asked my permission to call himself Paulus, to which I had weakly assented. I will not go into the story in detail: suffice it to say that Barnabas was preaching a new demigod, so far as I can make out a recent reincarnation of this heroic Jeshua. I did not know until you mentioned it just now that Jeshua was son of the Fish; perhaps this explains the mystery. At all events, my Oriental Secretary, a harmless little man called Manahem, took Barnabas’s part warmly, rather too warmly, and sent the other fellow about his business with a fierceness of which I should never have believed him capable.’
「哈！这正是我想知道的。你看，前几天发生了一件怪事。我收到一份书面报告，说一个名叫巴拿巴的犹太人在岛另一端的一个犹太会堂中宣讲某种新的神秘学说；我的线人——一个来自安条克的叙利亚希腊人，母亲是犹太人——将其描述为危及本岛和平的学说。我传唤了巴拿巴和另一个人，听了双方的说法。我忘了他的原名，但他已成为罗马公民并请求我允许他自称保卢斯，我勉强同意了。我不打算详述此事：只需说巴拿巴在宣讲一位新的半神，据我所能判断的，是这位英雄约书亚的近期转世。直到你刚才提到，我才知道约书亚是鱼之子；也许这解释了那个谜。无论如何，我的东方秘书——一个叫马纳姆的无害小人物——热烈地站在巴拿巴一边，甚至太热烈了，把另一个人凶狠地打发了走，我从未想到他有这样的脾气。」

‘I know Manahem; he came to you from the Court of Antipas of Galilee, did he not?’
「我认识马纳姆；他是从加利利的安提帕宫廷来你这里的，不是吗？」

‘That’s the man. He is now away on leave in Alexandria. Well, when the case was settled and Barnabas and the other fellow had both been sent out of the island with a warning never to return, I called Manahem to my private room and gave him a piece of my mind. I am not naturally observant, but long experience as a magistrate has taught me to use my eyes in court, and I had caught Manahem surreptitiously signalling to Barnabas to leave the case in his hands. He was making a secret sign with his foot, the outline of a fish traced on the pavement. I gave Manahem the fright of his life – threatened to put him to the torture unless he explained that fish to me. He confessed at once, and begged me to forgive him. The fish sign, it appears, is the pass-word of Barnabas’s society which cultivates a sort of universal pacifism under the guidance of a demi-god named Jeshua – Jesus in Greek – who has the title of the Anointed One. The pass-word is for use among Greek-speaking Jews and stands, Manahem says, for Jesus Christos Theos which are, of course, the first letters of ichthus, fish. But there is more to it than that, I believe.’
「就是他。他现在休假去了亚历山大。嗯，案子了结后，巴拿巴和另一个人都被逐出本岛并警告永不得返回，我把马纳姆叫到我的私室训斥了他一顿。我生来不善于观察，但长期做法官的经验教会了我在法庭上用眼睛，我注意到马纳姆在偷偷向巴拿巴做手势让他把案子交给他处理。他在用脚做一个暗号——在地上描画一条鱼的轮廓。我把马纳姆吓得半死——威胁要对他动刑，除非他向我解释那条鱼。他立刻招了，并请求我原谅。原来鱼形暗号是巴拿巴那个社团的接头密码——该社团在一个名叫约书亚——希腊语称耶稣——的半神指导下奉行一种普遍和平主义，约书亚拥有「受膏者」的头衔。马纳姆说这个暗号用于讲希腊语的犹太人之间，代表 Jesus Christos Theos（耶稣基督上帝），当然也就是 ichthus（鱼）的首字母。但我相信其中还有更多。」

‘I have heard of the society. They celebrate a weekly love-feast with fish, wine and bread, but tend to Pythagorean asceticism. You may be sure that Jeshua the Fish is of the chaster sort. The Jeshua who founded it was executed under Tiberius; and oddly enough his mother was a Temple Virgin at Jerusalem, and there was a mystery about his birth.’
「我听说过这个社团。他们每周以鱼、葡萄酒和面包举行爱宴，但倾向于毕达哥拉斯式的禁欲主义。你可以确信约书亚鱼属于贞洁之类。创立它的约书亚在提比略统治下被处死；而奇特的是，他的母亲是耶路撒冷的圣殿处女，他的出生有一个谜。」

‘Yes, Manahem revealed it under an oath of secrecy. You are right about this God’s chastity. Erotic religion is going out of fashion everywhere; it is inconsistent with modern social stability, except of course among the peasantry. Do you know, Theophilus, a picture rises in my mind, almost a vision. I see the white-clad Vestal Virgins in their Temple grounds offering up little prayers to chaste Jupiter, Father and Virgin, whom they serve. I see them devoutly circling the fish-pool which the sacred fish also mystically circles – the cool, pale-faced fish, as chaste as they –’
「是的，马纳姆在保密誓言下透露了。你说的这位神的贞洁没错。色情宗教到处都在过时；它与现代社会稳定不一致，当然农民除外。你知道吗，狄奥菲卢斯，我脑中浮现出一幅画面，几乎是幻象。我看到白衣维斯塔贞女在神庙庭院中向贞洁的朱庇特——父亦处女——她们所侍奉之神——献上小小的祈祷。我看到她们虔诚地环绕着鱼池，神圣的鱼也在其中神秘地游转——那清凉的、苍白面孔的鱼，如她们一般贞洁——」

Theophilus interrupted: ‘ – Who was dark-faced and hot in Silvia’s day,’ ‘And in his pool drowns each unspoken wish,’ Paulus agreed.
狄奥菲卢斯打断道：「——在西尔维亚的时代他却是黝黑面孔且滚烫的，」「他在池中淹溺每一桩未说出口的心愿，」保卢斯接道。





* * *



Theophilus was wrong to suggest that the hero rescues the chained virgin from a male sea-beast. The sea-beast is female – the Goddess Tiamat or Rahab – and the God Bel or Marduk, who wounds her mortally and usurps her authority, has himself chained her in female form to the rock to keep her from mischief. When the myth reaches Greece, Bellerophon and Hercules are more chivalrously represented as rescuing her from the monster. It has even been suggested that in the original icon, the Goddess’s chains were really necklaces, bracelets and anklets, while the sea-beast was her emanation.
狄奥菲卢斯暗示英雄从雄性海兽手中解救被锁的处女是错误的。海兽是雌性——女神提亚玛特或拉哈布——而神贝尔或马杜克致命地伤害她并篡夺其权威后，将她以雌形锁在岩石上以防她作恶。当神话传到希腊时，柏勒洛丰和赫拉克勒斯被更侠义地描绘为从怪物手中拯救她。甚至有人提出，在原始圣像中，女神的锁链实际上是项链、手镯和脚镯，而海兽是她的化身。

1 ‘Proetus’ is the earlier spelling of the word, which means ‘the early man’, formed from the adverb proi or pro.
¹ 「普罗埃图斯」是该词更早的拼写，意为「早来者」，由副词 proi 或 pro 构成。



1 Purpureus is a reduplication of purus, ‘very, very pure.’
¹ Purpureus 是 purus（「纯洁」）的重叠形式，意为「非常非常纯洁」。

2 Aphrodite persists tenaciously at Paphos. In the village of Konklia, as it is now called after the sea-shell in which she rode ashore there, a rough aniconic stone, her original neolithic image, remains on the site of the early Greek sanctuary and is still held in awe by the local people. Close by is a Frankish church, re-built about 1450 as an ordinary Greek chapel, where the saint is a golden-haired beauty called Panagia Chrisopolitissa, ‘the all-holy golden woman of the town’ – a perfect figure of Aphrodite with the infant Eros in her arms. Mr Christopher Kininmonth who gives me these particulars, says that the beach is a particularly fine one and that the Romans, who substituted their massive and tasteless Temple of Venus for the earlier Greek building, did not despise the conical image but incorporated it in their shrine.
² 阿佛洛狄忒在帕福斯顽固地存续着。在如今以她乘之登陆的海螺命名的孔克利亚村，一块粗糙的非偶像化石头——她最初的新石器时代形象——仍矗立在早期希腊圣所的原址上，至今仍被当地人敬畏。旁边是一座法兰克教堂，约1450年重建为普通希腊礼拜堂，其中的圣徒是一位金发美人，名叫 Panagia Chrisopolitissa——「全圣的金色城女」——一个完美的阿佛洛狄忒形象，怀中抱着婴儿厄洛斯。提供这些细节的克里斯托弗·金宁茅斯先生说，海滩格外美丽，罗马人——他们用自己庞大而无味的维纳斯神庙取代了更早的希腊建筑——并没有鄙视那锥形石像，而是将其纳入了他们的神殿。





Chapter Twenty-One

title: 第二十一章
content:
THE WATERS OF STYX
斯堤克斯之水





In Parry’s edition of Archbishop Ussher’s Letters – Ussher was the learned Primate of Ireland in the reign of Charles I who dated the creation of Adam in the year 4004 BC – appears a note that Langbaine the Irish antiquarian communicated to Ussher the following bardic tradition:
在帕里编辑的阿舍尔大主教书信集中——阿舍尔是查理一世时期博学的爱尔兰首席主教，他将亚当的创世年代定在公元前4004年——有一则注记说爱尔兰古物学家兰贝恩向阿舍尔传达了以下吟游诗人传统：

Nemninus being upbraided by a Saxon scholar as a Briton and therefore ignorant of the rudiments of learning, invented these letters by an improvisation, to clear his nation of the charge of dullness and ignorance.
内姆尼努斯被一位撒克逊学者斥为不列颠人，因而对学问的基础一无所知，他灵机一动发明了这些字母，以此为他民族洗脱愚钝和无知之名。





ALAP A PARTH P

BRAUT B QUITH Q

CURI C RAT R

DEXI D TRAUS T

EGIN E SUNG S

FICH F UIR U

GUIDIR G JEIL X

HUIL H OFR E

JECHUIT I ZEIRC Z

KAM K AIUN AE

LOUBER L ESTIAUL ET

MUIN M EGUI EU

NIHN N AUR AU

OR O EMC EI

KENC ELAU





This obviously was a joke at the stupid Saxon’s expense, because the British bards had used an alphabet for centuries before the arrival of the Saxons. But what do these improvised letter-names mean? Since the stupid Saxon would have used the ABC Latin order of letters and was apparently unaware that any other order existed, let us try restoring the Alap-Braut-Curi to its BLFSN Ogham order. And since we can be pretty sure that Nemninus was showing off his superior learning – probably his knowledge of Greek to tease the stupid Saxon who knew only a little monkish Latin – let us try writing out the letter-names in Greek, and see whether certain familiar combinations of words do not strike the eye. This is a difficult puzzle, because the extra words KENC, ELAU and ESTIAUL have been inserted without explanation among the letter-names and because the vowels have been mixed. (If E is OFR, OR is probably ER.) Nevertheless the DEXI-TRAUS-KAM-PARTH sequence is striking; we evidently have hit on an Egyptian Christian formula. With Clement of Alexandria’s specialized vocabulary in mind we read it as:
这显然是拿那个愚蠢的撒克逊人开的一个玩笑，因为不列颠吟游诗人在撒克逊人到来之前已使用字母表数百年了。但这些即兴的字母名是什么意思呢？既然愚蠢的撒克逊人使用的是拉丁 ABC 字母顺序，而且显然不知道还有任何其他顺序存在，让我们试着将 Alap-Braut-Curi 恢复为其 BLFSN 欧甘顺序。既然我们可以相当确定内姆尼努斯在炫耀自己更高深的学问——可能是他的希腊语知识，以取笑只懂一点修道院拉丁语的愚蠢撒克逊人——让我们试着用希腊语写出这些字母名，看看某些熟悉的词组是否不会映入眼帘。这是一个困难的谜题，因为额外的词 KENC、ELAU 和 ESTIAUL 被不加解释地插入字母名之间，而且元音被混在一起。（如果 E 是 OFR，那么 OR 可能是 ER。）尽管如此，DEXI-TRAUS-KAM-PARTH 序列令人注目；我们显然碰上了一个埃及基督教公式。带着亚历山大的克莱门特的专门词汇，我们将其读为：





DEXITERAN TRAUSEI PARTHENOMETRA KAMAX





‘The spear will wound the Virgin Mother as she stands at his right hand.’ This neatly constructed pentameter is a reminiscence of St. Luke’s Gospel (II, 35). Kamax is both a spear and a vine-prop, and therefore a most appropriate word. The weapon mentioned by Luke is a sword; but the fulfilment of the prophecy, for Christian mystics, came with the spear that pierced the side of Jesus at the Crucifixion. And as I read the eight-lettered Holy Name sequence at the end, the Lintels of Heaven (OPHREA OURANEIA) are invited to raise a shout (IACHESTHAI) of ‘Shiloh’ (JEIL) since the love-fish (EROS ALABES) has neared (EGGIKEN) the land of On (AUNAN). Aunan, or On, known to the Greeks as Heliopolis and probably the oldest city in Egypt, was the centre of the Osiris cult and probably also of the Christ-as-Osiris cult. At ‘Aun’, according to Coptic tradition, the Virgin Mary washed the Infant Jesus’s swaddling clouts in the spring Ain-esh-Shems, formerly sacred to the Sun-god Ra. From the drops that dripped from the strings, up sprang the sacred Balsam-tree. It is probable that this legend was originally told of the Goddess Isis and the Infant Horus. Gwion is, I think, referring to it in the line: ‘I have been the strings of a child’s swaddling clout’ in the Câd Goddeu and in ‘Whence is the sweetness of the balm?’ in the Angar Cyvyndawd. The Alabes was worshipped at Aun, and was a Niloticcatfish.
「长矛将刺伤站在他右手边的处女之母。」这首精心构造的五音步诗是对《路加福音》（II, 35）的回忆。Kamax 既是矛也是葡萄藤支柱，因此是一个最恰当的词。路加提到的武器是剑；但对基督教神秘主义者来说，预言的应验是在十字架上受难时刺穿耶稣侧面的那根矛。当我读到结尾的八字母神圣之名序列时，天堂的门楣（OPHREA OURANEIA）被邀请高呼（IACHESTHAI）「细罗」（JEIL），因为爱之鱼（EROS ALABES）已接近（EGGIKEN）安城之地（AUNAN）。Aunan，或安，希腊人称之为赫利奥波利斯，可能是埃及最古老的城市，是奥西里斯崇拜的中心，可能也是基督即奥西里斯崇拜的中心。据科普特传说，在「安」，童贞玛利亚在日神拉曾受崇拜的艾因-什姆斯泉中为婴儿耶稣洗涤襁褓。从拧干时滴落的水珠中，长出了神圣的香脂树。这一传说可能最初讲述的是女神伊西斯和婴儿荷鲁斯。我认为格温在《树木之战》中「我曾是一个孩子襁褓的系带」一行以及在《安加尔·齐温达德》中「香脂的甜味从何而来？」一行中正是指涉此事。Alabes 在安城受崇拜，是一种尼罗河鲶鱼。

But this is a digression, and I will leave whatever Greek scholar may be interested to work out the rest of the charm, without troubling him with my own approximate solution.
但这是离题之言，我将让任何可能感兴趣的希腊学者自己去解开这条咒语的其余部分，不以我自己的近似解答来麻烦他。

*



Of the various objectives proposed in Chapter Eight one has not yet been attained: it still remains to find out the meaning of the letter-names of the Beth-Luis-Nion. We may assume them originally to have stood for something else than trees, for the Irish tree-names, with the exception of Duir and Saille, are not formed from roots common to the Greek, Latin and Slavonic languages, as one might have expected.
在第八章提出的各项目标中，有一个尚未达成：仍然需要找出贝斯-路易斯-尼恩字母名的含义。我们可以假设它们最初代表的不是树木，因为爱尔兰树名——除了 Duir 和 Saille 之外——并非由希腊语、拉丁语和斯拉夫语共通的词根构成，如人们可能预期的那样。

The meaning of the vowels in the Boibel-Loth proved to be a sequence of stages in the life of the Spirit of the Year, incarnate in the sacred king, and the trees named in the vowels of the Beth-Luis-Nion similarly proved to form a seasonal sequence. Is it possible that the separation of the vowels from the consonants was a late development and that originally they were distributed among the consonants at regular intervals, as they are in the Greek and Latin alphabets? That A, the birth letter, rather than B, the letter of inception, really began the alphabet; and that the form ‘Ailm-Beth’ was even earlier than ‘Beth-Luis-Nion’? Since Irish legends about the alphabet particularize Greece as the place where it was invented and there is an obstinate countryside tradition in Ireland that the Tuatha de Danaan spoke Greek, why not put the Beth-Luis-Nion into ancient Greek and distribute the vowels in their seasonal order among the consonants, placing A at the winter solstice, O at the spring equinox, U at the summer solstice, E at the autumn equinox, I at the winter solstice again; and placing Straif at the beginning and Quert at the end of the summer flight of letters? Would they spell out another religious charm?
博伊贝尔-洛斯中元音的含义已被证明是年之灵——化身为神圣国王——生命中的一系列阶段，而贝斯-路易斯-尼恩元音中命名的树木同样被证明构成了一个季节序列。元音与辅音的分离是否是后来的发展，它们最初是否像希腊和拉丁字母表一样以固定间隔分布在辅音之间？A，诞生之母，而非 B，起始之母，是否才是字母表真正的开端？「Ailm-Beth」形式是否比「Beth-Luis-Nion」更早？既然关于字母表的爱尔兰传说特别指出希腊是其发明之地，而且爱尔兰有一种顽强的民间传统说达南神族说希腊语，为什么不把贝斯-路易斯-尼恩放入古希腊语中，将元音按其季节顺序分布在辅音之间——将 A 置于冬至、O 置于春分、U 置于夏至、E 置于秋分、I 再次置于冬至；并将 Straif 置于夏季字母序列的开头、Quert 置于末尾？它们会拼出另一条宗教咒语吗？

Thus:
如下：

Ailm, Beth, Luis, Nion, Onn, Fearn, Saille, Straif, Huath, Ura, Duir, Tinn, Coll, Quert, Eadha, Muin, Gort, Ngetal, Ruis, Idho.





Ailm Beth does not make a hopeful start until one recalls that Ailm (silver fir) is pronounced Alv or Alph in Irish. The root alph expresses both whiteness and produce: thus alphos is dull white leprosy (albula in Latin) and alphe is ‘gain’ and alphiton is pearl barley and Alphito is the White Grain-goddess or Pig-Demeter, alias Cerdo (which also means ‘gain’), whose connexion with Cerridwen the Welsh Pig-Demeter, alias the Old White One, has already been pointed out. The principal river in the Peloponnese is the Alpheus. Beth or Beith is the birch month and since the birch is betulus in Latin, we may transliterate it into Greek and write Baitulus. At once the words begin to make sense as an invocation. Alphito-Baitule, a compound word like Alphito-mantis (‘one who divines from pearl barley’) suggests a goddess of the same sort as ASHIMA BAETYL and ANATHA BAETYL, the two Goddess-wives of the Hebrew Jehovah in his fifth-century BC cult at Elephantine in Egypt. The meaning of Baitulos is a sacred stone in which a deity is resident; it seems to be connected with the Semitic Bethel (‘House of God’) but whether Baitulos is derived from Bethel or vice versa is not known. The Lion-goddess Anatha Baetyl was not originally Semitic, and was worshipped as Anaitis in Armenia.
Ailm Beth 最初并不构成一个有希望的开头，直到人们想起 Ailm（银杉）在爱尔兰语中读作 Alv 或 Alph。词根 alph 同时表达白色和产物：因此 alphos 是暗白色麻风（拉丁语 albula），alphe 是「收获」，alphiton 是珍珠大麦，而 Alphito 是白谷女神或猪得墨忒耳，又名 Kerdo（也意为「收获」），她与威尔士猪得墨忒耳即老白者凯丽德温的联系此前已经指出。伯罗奔尼撒的主要河流是阿尔菲奥斯河。Beth 或 Beith 是白桦月份，既然白桦在拉丁语中是 betulus，我们可以将其音译为希腊语写作 Baitulus。这些词顿时开始构成一句祈请。Alphito-Baitule，一个像 Alphito-mantis（「以珍珠大麦占卜之人」）一样的复合词，暗示一位与 ASHIMA BAETYL 和 ANATHA BAETYL 同类的女神——后者两位是公元前五世纪耶和华在埃及象岛的崇拜中的两位女神妻子。Baitulos 的含义是一块神灵寄居其中的神圣石头；它似乎与闪族语 Bethel（「神之屋」）有关，但究竟是 Baitulus 源于 Bethel 还是相反，尚不得而知。狮子女神 Anatha Baetyl 最初并非闪族神，在亚美尼亚以 Anaitis 之名受崇拜。

Luis, the next Beth-Luis-Nion letter, suggests Lusios, a divine title of many Greek deities, meaning ‘One who washes away guilt’. It is particularly applied to Dionysus, the Latin equivalent being Liber. But Dionysus in the Orphic Hymns is also called Luseios and Luseus, which suggests that the adjective is formed not directly from louein, ‘to wash’, but from the city Lusi in Arcadia famous for its connexion with Dionysus. Lusi is overshadowed by the enormous mountain Aroania, now Mount Chelmos, and lies close to the valleys of the Aroanius River, which flows into the Alpheus, and of the Styx which flows into the Crathis. The Styx (‘hateful’) was the death-river by which the Gods were said to swear, and which Demeter, the Barley Mother, cursed when Poseidon pursued her with his unwelcome attentions, presumably during the Achaean conquest of the Crathis valley.
Luis，贝斯-路易斯-尼恩的下一个字母，暗示 Lusios，许多希腊神祇的神圣称号，意为「洗涤罪咎者」。它特别用于狄俄尼索斯，拉丁语对应词为 Liber。但狄俄尼索斯在俄耳甫斯赞美诗中也被称为 Luseios 和 Luseus，这暗示该形容词并非直接源于 louein（「洗涤」），而是源于阿卡迪亚的卢西城——该城以与狄俄尼索斯的联系而闻名。卢西被巨大的阿罗尼亚山——即现在的切尔莫斯山——所遮蔽，靠近阿罗尼乌斯河谷（该河流入阿尔菲奥斯河）和斯堤克斯河谷（该河流入克拉西斯河）。斯堤克斯（「可憎的」）是众神据称以其起誓的死亡之河，当波塞冬——大概是在亚该亚人征服克拉西斯河谷期间——以不受欢迎的殷勤追逐她时，大麦之母得墨忒耳诅咒了这条河。

Melampus means ‘black foot’ and he was the son of Amythaon and the nymph Melanippe (‘black mare’). The story of how he purged the daughters of Proetus with black hellebore and pig-sacrifices, and afterwards washed away their madness in a stream, probably refers to the capture of this Danaan shrine by the Achaeans, though Melampus is reckoned as an Aeolian Minyan. He also conquered Argos, the centre of the Danaan cult. The three daughters were the Triple Goddess, the Demeter of the Styx, who must have been mare-headed, else a horse’s hoof would not have been proof against the poison of the water. But according to Philo of Heraclea and Aelian, the horn of a Scythian ass-unicorn was also proof against the poison; and Plutarch in his Life of Alexander says that an ass’s hoof makes the only safe vessel. Near by, at Stymphalus, was a triple sanctuary founded by Temenus (‘precinct’) the Pelasgian, in honour of the Goddess Hera as ‘girl, bride and widow’, a remarkable survival of the original triad. She was called ‘widow’, the Stymphalians told Pausanias, because she quarrelled with Zeus and retired to Stymphalus; this probably refers to a later revival of the primitive cult in defiance of Olympianism.
墨兰波斯意为「黑足」，他是阿密塔翁和宁芙墨拉尼佩（Melanippe，「黑马」）之子。他如何用黑嚭根草和猪祭净化普罗埃图斯之女、然后在溪流中洗去她们疯狂的故事，大概指的是亚该亚人对这座达南圣所的夺取，尽管墨兰波斯被归为埃俄利亚明尼安人。他还征服了达南崇拜的中心阿尔戈斯。三个女儿就是三联女神——斯堤克斯的得墨忒耳——她必定是马头的，否则马蹄就不会对水之毒免疫。但据赫拉克勒亚的斐洛和埃利安记载，斯基泰驴独角的角也能抵御此毒；普鲁塔克在《亚历山大传》中说驴蹄是唯一安全的器皿。附近的斯廷法罗斯有一座三重圣所，由佩拉斯吉人忒梅努斯（Temenus，「圣区」）创建，以纪念女神赫拉作为「少女、新娘和寡妇」——原始三联体的一个显著遗存。斯廷法罗斯人告诉保萨尼亚斯，她被称为「寡妇」是因为她与宙斯争吵后退居斯廷法罗斯；这可能指的是后来对原始崇拜的复兴，以对抗奥林匹克主义。

Sir James Frazer visited Lusi in 1895, and he has given a valuable account of it which allows us to read Nonacris as a name for the succession of nine precipices of Mount Aroania which overhang the gorge of the Styx. Even in the late summer there was still snow in the clefts of what he described as the most ‘awful line of precipices’ he had ever seen. The Styx is formed by the melting snow and seems to run black down the cliff-side because of the dark incrustation of the rock behind, but afterwards bright blue because of the slatey rocks over which it flows in the gorge. The whole line of precipices is vertically streaked with red and black – both death colours in ancient Greece – and Frazer accounts for Hesiod’s description of the ‘silver pillars’ of the Styx by observing that in winter immense icicles overhang the gorge. He records that a chemical analysis of Styx water shows it to contain no poisonous substance, though it is extremely cold.
詹姆斯·弗雷泽爵士于1895年访问了卢西，他对此地做了一份有价值的记述，使我们能够将诺纳克里斯读作悬挂在斯堤克斯峡谷上方的阿罗尼亚山九级连续断崖的名称。即使在夏末，他所描述的见过的最「骇人的断崖线」的裂缝中仍有积雪。斯堤克斯河由融雪形成，因背后岩石的深色外壳而沿崖壁流下时呈黑色，但随后因峡谷中流经的板岩而呈现明亮的蓝色。整条断崖线垂直地布满红色和黑色条纹——这两种在古希腊都是死亡之色——弗雷泽用冬天悬挂在峡谷上方的巨大冰柱来解释赫西俄德对斯堤克斯「银柱」的描述。他记录道，斯堤克斯水的化学分析表明它不含任何有毒物质，尽管极其寒冷。

Frazer found that the belief in the singing spotted fish still survived at Lusi – they recall the spotted poetic fish of Connla’s Well1 and so did the tradition of the snakes that Demeter set to guard the Styx water. He visited the cave of the Daughters of Proetus which overlooks the chasm of the Styx, and found that it had a natural door and window formed by the action of water.
