In English ballad-poetry the mermaid stands for the bitter-sweetness of love and for the danger run by susceptible mariners (once spelt ‘merriners’) in foreign ports: her mirror and comb stand for vanity and heartlessness.
这位玛丽安的一个常见伪装是 merry-maid（快乐少女），即 mermaid（人鱼）曾经的拼写。人鱼的标准形象——一位手持圆镜和金梳、长着鱼尾的美丽女子——表达的是「爱神从海中升起」。每一位厄琉息斯密仪——源于佩拉斯吉——的入教者在以卢·劳方式洗过锅浴后，都要与她的代表举行爱情仪式。圆镜——与梳子相配——可能是某位昔日艺术家对温柏的误置，温柏是玛丽安始终手持的爱情信物；但镜子确实也是密仪神圣陈设的一部分，可能代表「认识你自己」。梳子最初是拨弄里拉琴弦的拨片。希腊人称她为阿佛洛狄忒（Aphrodite，「从海沫中升起」），并将鲔鱼、鲟鱼、扇贝和滨螺——皆为她之神圣——用作催情剂。她最著名的神庙建于海边，因此不难理解她象征性的鱼尾。她可与月女神欧律诺墨等同——她在阿卡迪亚菲伽利亚的雕像是木雕人鱼。香桃木、骨螺和没药树也处处为她所圣；还有棕榈树（喜盐）、爱情忠贞的鸽子，以及白、绿、蓝、猩红等颜色。波提切利的《维纳斯的诞生》正是她崇拜的精确图像。高挑、金发、蓝眼、苍白面容的爱神乘着扇贝壳抵达香桃木林，大地身着鲜花长袍匆匆以猩红金穗斗篷裹住她。在英国民谣中，人鱼代表爱情的苦甜以及易感水手（曾拼作 merriners）在异国港口所冒的危险：她的镜子和梳子代表虚荣和无情。

Constantine, the first Christian Emperor, officially abolished Mary-worship, but much of the ancient ritual survived within the Church: for example among the Collyridians, an Arabian sect who used to offer the same cake and liquor at her shrine as they had formerly offered to Ashtaroth. Myrrh, too, but this was more orthodox because St. Jerome had praised the Virgin as Stilla Maris, ‘Myrrh of the Sea’. St. Jerome was punning on the name ‘Mary’, connecting it with Hebrew words marah (brine) and mor (myrrh) and recalling the gifts of the Three Wise Men.
君士坦丁——第一位基督教皇帝——正式废除了玛利亚崇拜，但大量古老仪式在教会内部存续：例如科利里迪安派——一个阿拉伯教派——曾在她的神龛前献上与从前献给阿斯塔洛特相同的饼和酒。没药也是，但这更正统，因为圣哲罗姆曾赞颂圣母为 Stilla Maris，「海之没药」。圣哲罗姆在「玛利亚」之名上做文字游戏，将其与希伯来语 marah（盐水）和 mor（没药）联系起来，并回忆三博士的礼物。

When the Crusaders invaded the Holy Land, built castles and settled down, they found a number of heretical Christian sects living there under Moslem protection, who soon seduced them from orthodoxy. This was how the cult of Mary Gipsy came to England, brought through Compostella in Spain by poor pilgrims with palm-branches in their hands, copies of the Apocryphal Gospels in their wallets and Aphrodite’s scallop-shells stitched in their caps – the palmers, celebrated in Ophelia’s song in Hamlet. The lyre-plucking, red-stockinged troubadours, of whom King Richard Lion-Heart is the best remembered in Britain, ecstatically adopted the Marian cult. From their French songs derive the lyrics by ‘Anon’ which are the chief glory of early English poetry; as the prettiest carols derive from the Apocryphal Gospels, thanks to the palmers. The most memorable result of the Crusades was to introduce into Western Europe an idea of romantic love which, expressed in terms of the ancient Welsh minstrel tales, eventually transformed the loutish robber barons and their sluttish wives to a polished society of courtly lords and ladies. From the castle and court good manners and courtesy spread to the country folk; and this explains ‘Merry England’ as the country most engrossed with Mary-worship.
当十字军入侵圣地、建城堡定居后，他们发现那里有一些在穆斯林保护下生活的异端基督教教派，这些教派很快使他们偏离正统。玛利·吉普赛的崇拜就是这样来到英格兰的——由穷苦朝圣者经西班牙孔波斯特拉带来，他们手执棕榈枝，囊中揣着《伪经福音书》的抄本，帽上缝着阿佛洛狄忒的扇贝壳——这些朝圣者在《哈姆雷特》中奥菲莉娅的歌里被歌颂。弹里拉琴、穿红袜的游吟诗人——其中狮心王理查在英国最为人记念——狂喜地采纳了玛丽安崇拜。早期英语诗歌最大的荣耀——那些署名「无名氏」的抒情诗即源自他们的法语歌曲；最美的圣诞颂歌则源自《伪经福音书》，归功于那些朝圣者。十字军最难忘的成果是将一种浪漫爱情的理念引入西欧，以古老的威尔士吟游故事表达，最终将粗野的强盗男爵和他们邋遢的妻子转变为彬彬有礼的宫廷男女社会。良好的举止和礼仪从城堡和宫廷传播到民间；这解释了「快乐的英格兰」为何成为最热衷玛利亚崇拜的国度。

In the English countryside Mary Gipsy was soon identified with the Love-goddess known to the Saxons as ‘The May Bride’ because of her ancient association with the may-tree cult brought to Britain by the Atrebates in the first century BC or AD. She paired off with Merddin, by this time Christianized as ‘Robin Hood’, apparently a variant of Merddin’s Saxon name, Rof Breoht Woden, ‘Bright Strength of Woden,’ also known euphemistically as ‘Robin Good-fellow’. In French the word Robin, which is regarded as a diminutive of Robert but is probably pre-Teutonic, means a ram and also a devil. A robinet, or water-faucet, is so called because in rustic fountains it was shaped like a ram’s head. The two senses of ram and devil are combined in the illustration to a pamphlet published in London in 1639: Robin Goodfellow, his mad pranks and merry gests. Robin is depicted as an ithyphallic god of the witches with young ram’s horns sprouting from his forehead, ram’s legs, a witches’ besom over his left shoulder, a lighted candle in his right hand. Behind him in a ring dance a coven of men and women witches in Puritan costume, a black dog adores him, a musician plays a trumpet, an owl flies overhead. It will be recalled that the Somersetshire witches called their god Robin, and ‘Robin son of Art’ was the Devil of Dame Alice Kyteler, the famous early fourteenth-century witch of Kilkenny, and used sometimes to take the form of a black dog. For the Devil as ram the classical instance is the one whom, in 1303, the Bishop of Coventry honoured with a Black Mass and saluted with a posterior kiss. In Cornwall ‘Robin’ means phallus. ‘Robin Hood’ is a country name for red campion (‘campion’ means ‘champion’), perhaps because its cloven petal suggests a ram’s hoof, and because ‘Red Champion’ was a title of the Witch-god. It may be no more than a coincidence that ‘ram’ in Sanscrit is huda. ‘Robin’, meaning ‘a ram’, has become mythologically equated with Robin (latin: rubens), meaning the red-breast.
在英格兰乡间，玛利·吉普赛很快被等同于撒克逊人所知的「五朔新娘」爱神——因为她与阿特雷巴特人在公元前一世纪或公元一世纪带入不列颠的花楸树崇拜有着古老联系。她与默丁配对，此时默丁已被基督教化为「罗宾汉」——显然是默丁的撒克逊名 Rof Breoht Woden（「沃登的光明力量」）的变体，又称委婉的「好伙计罗宾」（Robin Good-fellow）。在法语中 Robin 一词——被视为 Robert 的昵称但可能前日耳曼语——意为公羊，也意为魔鬼。robinet 或水龙头之所以如此称呼，是因为乡村喷泉的龙头被塑成公羊头形。公羊和魔鬼双重含义合并于1639年在伦敦出版的一本小册子的插图中：《好伙计罗宾的疯狂恶作剧和欢乐事迹》。罗宾被描绘为女巫的勃起神，前额生出幼公羊角，长着公羊腿，左肩扛女巫扫帚，右手执点燃的蜡烛。他身后一圈穿清教徒服装的男女女巫在环形舞蹈，一条黑狗崇拜他，一位乐师吹号，一只猫头鹰在头顶飞翔。可以回想，萨默塞特郡的女巫称她们的神为罗宾，「艺术之子罗宾」是基尔肯尼著名的十四世纪早期女巫爱丽丝·凯特勒的魔鬼，有时以黑狗之形出现。魔鬼以公羊之形的经典案例是1303年考文垂主教以黑弥撒致敬并用后吻行礼的那一位。在康沃尔「罗宾」意为阳具。「罗宾汉」是红剪秋罗的乡间名（「剪秋罗」意为「冠军」），也许因为其分裂花瓣暗示公羊蹄，又因为「红冠军」是女巫神的称号。梵语中「公羊」为 huda 也许只是巧合。「罗宾」意为「公羊」在神话上等同于 Robin（拉丁语：rubens）意为红胸鸟。

Here the story becomes complicated. The merry exploits of one Robin Hood, the famous outlaw of Sherwood Forest – whom J. W. Walker1 has now proved to have been a historical character, born at Wakefield in Yorkshire between the years 1285 and 1295, and in the service of King Edward II in the years 1323 and 1324 – became closely associated with the May Day revels. Presumably this was because the outlaw happened to have been christened Robert by his father Adam Hood the forester, and because during the twenty-two years that he spent as a bandit in the greenwood he improved on this identification of himself with Robin by renaming his wife Matilda ‘Maid Marian’. To judge from the early ballad, The Banished Man, Matilda must have cut her hair and put on male dress in order to belong to the outlaw fraternity, as in Albania to this day young women join male hunting parties, dress as men and are so treated – Atalanta of Calydon who took part in the hunt of the Calydonian Boar was the prototype. The outlaw band then formed a coven of thirteen with Marian acting as the pucelle, or maiden of the coven; presumably she wore her proper clothes in the May Day orgies as Robin’s bride. By his successful defiance of the ecclesiastics Robin became such a popular hero that he was later regarded as the founder of the Robin Hood religion, and its primitive forms are difficult to recover. However, ‘Hood’ (or Hod or Hud) meant ‘log’ – the log put at the back of the fire – and it was in this log, cut from the sacred oak, that Robin had once been believed to reside. Hence ‘Robin Hood’s steed’, the wood-louse which ran out when the Yule log was burned. In the popular superstition Robin himself escaped up the chimney in the form of a Robin and, when Yule ended, went out as Belin against his rival Bran, or Saturn – who had been ‘Lord of Misrule’ at the Yule-tide revels. Bran hid from pursuit in the ivy-bush disguised as a Gold Crest Wren; but Robin always caught and hanged him. Hence the song:
这里故事变得复杂。罗宾汉——舍伍德森林的著名绿林好汉——J. W. 沃克¹现已证明为历史人物，1285至1295年间生于约克郡韦克菲尔德，1323和1324年在爱德华二世宫廷服役——其欢乐事迹与五朔节狂欢密切相关。大概因为这位绿林好汉碰巧被父亲亚当·胡德——一名林务官——取名为罗伯特，又因为在绿林中度过的二十二年间他通过将妻子玛蒂尔达改名为「少女玛丽安」来加强自己与罗宾的认同。从早期民谣《被放逐者》判断，玛蒂尔达必然剪了头发穿上男装以加入绿林兄弟会，如同至今阿尔巴尼亚年轻女子加入男性狩猎队、穿男装并以男性相待——参加卡吕冬野猪狩猎的卡吕冬的阿塔兰塔是其原型。绿林帮随后形成十三人的巫会，玛丽安担任 pucelle 即巫会的少女；大概在五朔节狂欢中她穿回自己的女装作为罗宾的新娘。罗宾因成功对抗教会人士而成为如此受欢迎的英雄，以至于后来被视为罗宾汉宗教的创立者，其原始形式已难以恢复。然而「胡德」（Hood 或 Hod 或 Hud）意为「圆木」——放在火后面的圆木——罗宾曾被认为就住在这根取自神圣橡树的圆木中。因此「罗宾汉的坐骑」指圣诞圆木燃烧时跑出来的土鳖虫。在民间迷信中罗宾本人以知更鸟之形从烟囱逃出，圣诞季结束时以贝林之身出战他的对手布兰或萨图恩——后者曾是圣诞狂欢中的「胡闹之王」。布兰伪装成金冠鹪鹩藏在常春藤丛中；但罗宾总是抓住他并绞死他。因此有歌谣：

‘Who’ll hunt the Wren?’ cries Robin the Bobbin.
「谁来猎鹪鹩？」罗宾·波宾喊道。





Since ‘Maid Marian’ had been acting as Lady of Misrule in the Yuletide revels and deserting Robin for his rival, it is easy to see how she earned a bad name for inconstancy. Thus ‘Maud Marian’ was often written for ‘Maid Marian’: ‘Maud’ is Mary Magdalene the penitent. In Tom o’ Bedlam’s Song she is Tom’s Muse – ‘Merry Mad Maud’.
既然「少女玛丽安」在圣诞狂欢中担任胡闹女王并为了罗宾的对手而抛弃他，就不难理解她如何因善变而名声不佳。因此「Maud Marian」常被写作「Maid Marian」：「Maud」是忏悔的抹大拉的玛利亚。在《疯子汤姆之歌》中她是汤姆的缪斯——「快乐的疯莫德」（Merry Mad Maud）。

Christmas was merry in the middle ages, but May Day was still merrier. It was the time of beribboned Maypoles, of Collyridian cakes and ale, of wreaths and posies, of lovers’ gifts, of archery contests, of merritotters (see-saws) and merribowks (great vats of milk-punch). But particularly of mad-merry marriages ‘under the greenwood tree’, when the dancers from the Green went off, hand in hand, into the greenwood and built themselves little love-bowers and listened hopefully for the merry nightingale. ‘Mad Merry’ is another popular spelling of ‘Maid Marian’, and as an adjective became attached to the magician Merlin (the original ‘Old Moore’ of the popular almanacks) whose prophetic almanacks were hawked at fairs and merrimakes. Merlin was really Merddin, as Spenser explains in the Faerie Queene, but Robin Hood had taken his place as the May Bride’s lover, and he had become an old bearded prophet. The ‘merritotter’ is perhaps called after the scales (representing the Autumn equinox) in the hand of the Virgin in the Zodiac, who figured in the Mad Merry Merlin almanack: devoted readers naturally identified her with St. Mary Gipsy, for true-lovers’ fates tottered in her balance, see-sawing up and down.
中世纪的圣诞节是快乐的，但五朔节更快乐。那是饰有彩带的五朔柱、科利里迪安的饼和麦酒、花环和花束、情人礼物、射箭比赛、跷跷板（merritotters）和大桶牛奶潘趣酒（merribowks）的时节。但尤其是一年一度的疯狂欢乐的婚姻「在绿林树下」——从绿地来的舞者手牵手走进绿林，搭建小小的爱之凉棚，满怀希望地聆听快乐的夜莺。「疯快乐」（Mad Merry）是「少女玛丽安」的另一种流行拼写，作为形容词被附加到巫师默林（通俗年历中最初的「老摩尔」）身上，他的预言年历在集市和欢乐会上兜售。默林实际上是默丁，如斯宾塞在《仙后》中解释的那样，但罗宾汉已取代他成为五朔新娘的情人，而他变成了一个老长胡子的先知。「跷跷板」（merritotter）也许得名于黄道带处女手中天秤（代表秋分）——出现在《疯快乐默林》年历中：忠实的读者自然将她等同于圣玛利·吉普赛，因为真爱者的命运在她的天平上摇摆不定，上上下下。

Many of these greenwood marriages, blessed by a renegade friar styled Friar Tuck, were afterwards formally confirmed in the church-porch. But very often ‘merrybegots’ were repudiated by their fathers. It is probably because each year, by old custom, the tallest and toughest village lad was chosen to be Little John (or ‘Jenkin’) Robin’s deputy in the Merry Men masque, that Johnson, Jackson and Jenkinson are now among the commonest English names – Little John’s merrybegots. But Robin did as merrily with Robson, Hobson, Dobson (all short for Robin), Robinson, Hodson, Hudson and Hood; Greenwood and Merriman were of doubtful paternity. The Christmas ‘merrimake’ (as Sir James Frazer mentions in The Golden Bough) also produced its crop of children. Who knows how many of the Morrises and Morrisons derive their patronymics from the amorous ‘morrice-men’1, Marian’s ‘merry-weathers’? Or how many ‘Princes’, ‘Lords’ and ‘Kings’ from the Christmas King, or Prince, or Lord, of Misrule?
许多这种绿林婚姻——由被称为塔克修士的离经叛道的修士祝福——之后在教堂门廊正式确认。但「欢乐之子」（merrybegots）常常被父亲否认。大概因为每年按照旧俗选出最高最壮的村庄青年来扮演小约翰（或「詹金」）——罗宾在欢乐人化装舞会中的副手——所以约翰逊、杰克逊和詹金森如今是最常见的英国姓氏之一——小约翰的欢乐之子。但罗宾也同样留下了罗布森、霍布森、多布森（均为罗宾的缩写）、罗宾逊、霍德森、哈德森和胡德；格林伍德和梅里曼的血统则可疑。圣诞「欢乐会」（如詹姆斯·弗雷泽爵士在《金枝》中提到）也产出一茬孩子。谁知道有多少莫里斯和莫里森的姓氏源自多情的「莫里斯舞者」¹——玛丽安的「欢乐郎」？又有多少「王子」「老爷」「国王」源自圣诞的胡闹之王、王子或老爷？

The Christmas merry-night play was an important part of the English Yule-tide festivities: seven or eight versions survive. The principal incidents are the beheading and restoration to life of the Christmas King, or Christmas Fool. This is one of the clearest survivals of the pre-Christian religion, and ultimately derives from ancient Crete. Firmicus Maternus in his On the Error of Profane Religion tells how Cretan Dionysus (Zagreus) was killed at Zeus’s orders, boiled in a cauldron and eaten by the Titans. The Cretans, he says, celebrated an annual funeral feast, in which they played out the drama of the boy’s sufferings – and his shape-shifting – eating a live bull as his surrogate. Yet he did not die for, according to Epimenides, quoted by St. Paul, Minos made a panegyric over him:
圣诞狂欢夜戏剧是英格兰圣诞庆典的重要组成部分：存世有七八个版本。主要情节是圣诞王或圣诞傻瓜的被斩首和复活。这是前基督教宗教最清晰的遗存之一，最终源自古克里特。菲尔米库斯·马特努斯在《论异教之谬误》中讲述克里特的狄俄尼索斯（扎格柔斯）如何被宙斯下令杀死、在大锅中煮食并被提坦吞食。他说克里特人每年举行一次葬礼宴席，在其中演出这男孩受难——以及变形——的戏剧，以一头活公牛作为替身吞食。然而他并未死去，因为据圣保罗引用的埃庇米尼得斯记载，米诺斯为他作了颂词：

Thou diest not, but to eternity thou livest and standest.
Thou diest not, but to eternity thou livest and standest.（你不曾死去，而是永生永存。）





St. Paul quoted a similar passage from the poet Aratus:
圣保罗引用了诗人阿拉图斯的一段类似文字：

In thee we live, move, and have our being.
In thee we live, move, and have our being.（我们在你里面生活、动作、存留。）





At Athens, the same festival, called the Lenaea, (‘Festival of the Wild Women’) was held at the winter solstice, and the death and rebirth of the harvest infant Dionysus were similarly dramatized. In the original myth it was not the Titans but the wild women, the nine representatives of the Moon-goddess Hera, who tore the child in pieces and ate him. And at the Lenaea it was a yearling kid, not a bull, that was eaten; when Apollodorus says that Dionysus was transformed into a kid, Eriphos, to save him from the wrath of Hera, this means that Hera once ate him as a human child, but that when men (the Titans or tutors) were admitted to the feast a kid was substituted as victim.
在雅典，同一个节日被称为勒纳亚（Lenaea，「狂女之节」），在冬至举行，收获婴儿狄俄尼索斯的死亡和重生以类似方式被搬上舞台。在原始神话中撕裂并吞食这孩子的不是提坦，而是狂女——月女神赫拉的九位代表。在勒纳亚节上被吞食的是一岁的山羊羔而非公牛；当阿波罗多洛斯说狄俄尼索斯变形为山羊羔厄里福斯以躲避赫拉的怒火时，这意味着赫拉曾以人孩之形吞食他，但当男性（提坦或导师）被允许参加宴席时，便以山羊羔替代为牺牲。

The most ancient surviving record of European religious practice is an Aurignacian cave-painting at Cogul in North-Eastern Spain of the Old Stone Age Lenaea. A young Dionysus with huge genitals stands unarmed, alone and exhausted in the middle of a crescent of nine dancing women, who face him. He is naked, except for what appear to be a pair of close-fitting boots laced at the knee; they are fully clothed and wear small cone-shaped hats. These wild women, differentiated by their figures and details of their dress, grow progressively older as one looks clock-wise around the crescent. The row begins with three young girls, the first two in long skirts, on the right and ends with two thin dark elderly women on the left and an emaciated crone on the far side; the crone has a face like the old moon and is dancing widdershins. In between are three vigorous golden-haired women, one of them in a short, bright party-frock. They clearly represent the New Moon, Old Moon and Full Moon triads – the crone being Atropos, the senior member of the Old Moon triad.
欧洲宗教实践最古老的存世记录是西班牙东北部科古尔的一幅旧石器时代奥里尼亚克洞穴画——旧石器时代的勒纳亚。一位生殖器巨大的年轻狄俄尼索斯赤手空拳、孤身疲惫地站在九个面对他的舞蹈女子形成的新月形中央。他赤裸，只穿着似乎是系到膝盖的紧身靴；她们衣着完整，戴小锥形帽。这些狂女以身材和衣着细节区分，顺时针看去逐渐变老。队列从右侧三个少女开始——前两个穿长裙——到左侧两个瘦削黝黑的老妇结束，远端是一个骨瘦如柴的老妪；老妪有一张如残月的脸，逆向而舞。中间是三位精力充沛的金发女子，其中一位穿着明亮的短礼服。她们显然代表新月、残月和满月三联体——老妪是阿特罗波斯，残月三联体中最年长的成员。

In front of the senior member of the New Moon triad is an animal whose fore-quarters are concealed by her skirt – it seems to be a black pig. And in the foreground of the picture, bounding away behind the backs of the Full Moon triad, is the very creature that Oisin saw in his vision when being conveyed by Niamh of the Golden Hair to the Land of Youth: a hornless fawn. Balanced erect on the fawn’s neck, and facing backwards, is a boyish-looking imp or sprite, as clearly as anything the escaping soul of the doomed Dionysus. For the wild women are closing in on him and will presently tear him in bloody morsels and devour him. Though there is nothing in the painting to indicate the season, we can be sure that it was the winter solstice.
在新月三联体最年长成员前面有一只动物，前半身被她的裙子遮住——似乎是一头黑猪。在画面前景，满月三联体背后跳跃而去的正是奥伊辛在由金发妮娅薇送往青春之地时在幻象中看到的那种生物：一只无角小鹿。小鹿脖子上平衡站立、面朝后方的是一个男孩模样的精灵——那分明是注定灭亡的狄俄尼索斯逃逸的灵魂。因为狂女们正在向他逼近，即将将他撕成血淋淋的碎块吞食。虽然画中没有任何东西表明季节，但我们可以确定那是冬至。

So we get back once more to the dramatic romance of Gwion – the boy who was eaten by the wild hag Cerridwen and reborn as the miraculous child Taliesin – and to the dispute between Phylip Brydydd and the ‘vulgar rhymesters’ (see Chapter Five) as to who should first present a song to their prince on Christmas Day. The Romance of Taliesin is a sort of Christmas play, in which the sufferings of the shape-shifting child are riddlingly presented. This is the elder version, reflecting the religious theory of early European society where woman was the master of man’s destiny: pursued, was not pursued; raped, was not raped – as may be read in the faded legends of Dryope and Hylas, Venus and Adonis, Diana and Endymion, Circe and Ulysses. The danger of the various islands of women was that the male who ventured there might be sexually assaulted in the same murderous way as, according to B. Malinowski in The Sexual Life of Savages, men of North-Western Melanesia are punished for trespass against female privilege. At least one coven of nine wild women seems to have been active in South Wales during early mediaeval times: old St. Samson of Dol, travelling with a young companion, was unlucky enough to trespass in their precinct. A frightful shriek rang out suddenly and from a thicket darted a grey-haired, red-garmented hag with a bloody trident in her hand. St. Samson stood his ground; his companion fled, but was soon overtaken and stabbed to death. The hag refused to come to an accommodation with St. Samson when he reproached her, and informed him that she was one of the nine sisters who lived in those woods with their mother – apparently the Goddess Hecate. Perhaps if the younger sisters had reached the scene first, the young man would have been the victim of a concerted sexual assault. Nine murderous black-garbed women occur in the Icelandic saga of Thidrandi, who one night opened his door to a knock, though warned against the consequences, and saw them riding against him from the north. He resisted their attack with his sword for awhile, but fell mortally wounded.
于是我们再次回到格维恩的戏剧传奇——被狂老妪凯丽德温吞食后作为奇迹男童塔列辛重生的男孩——以及菲利普·布里迪德与「庸俗韵文家」之间（见第五章）关于谁应在圣诞日首先向其王子献歌的争论。塔列辛传奇是一种圣诞剧，其中变形男童的受难以谜语方式呈现。这是更古老的版本，反映了早期欧洲社会的宗教理论——女性主宰男性命运：她追逐，而非被追逐；她强暴，而非被强暴——如可在德律俄佩和许拉斯、维纳斯和阿多尼斯、狄安娜和恩底弥翁、喀耳刻和尤利西斯那些褪色的传说中所读到的。各种女子岛屿的危险在于，闯入的男性可能以与B. 马林诺夫斯基在《野人的性生活》中所记载的——美拉尼西亚西北部男子因侵犯女性特权而受惩罚——同样的凶杀方式遭受性侵犯。至少在中世纪早期南威尔士有一个九人狂女巫会在活动：老圣多尔散母的萨姆森带着一个年轻同伴旅行时，不幸闯入了她们的领地。一声可怕的尖叫突然响起，一个灰发红衣老妪手持血淋淋的三叉戟从灌木丛中冲出。圣萨姆森站住了；他的同伴逃跑但很快被追上刺死。当圣萨姆森斥责她时，老妪拒绝妥协，并告诉他她是与母亲住在那片树林中的九姐妹之一——大概是女神赫卡忒。也许如果年轻些的姐妹先到现场，那年轻人就会成为集体性侵犯的牺牲品。九个黑衣杀人女子也出现在冰岛的锡德兰迪萨迦中——他在一个夜晚不顾警告应声开门，看到她们从北方骑马向他冲来。他以剑抵抗了一阵，但终因致命伤倒下。

The transformations of Gwion run in strict seasonal order: hare in the autumn coursing season, fish in the rains of winter; bird in the spring when the migrants return, finally grain of corn in the summer harvest season. The Fury rushes after him in the form first of greyhound bitch, then of bitch-otter, then of falcon, finally overtakes him in the shape of a high-crested black hen – red comb and black feathers show her to be the Death Goddess. In this account the solar year ends in the winnowing season of early autumn, which points to an Eastern Mediterranean origin of the story. In Classical times the Cretan, Cyprian and Delphic years, and those of Asia Minor and Palestine, ended in September.
格维恩的变形严格按照季节顺序：秋季追猎季的野兔，冬季雨水中的鱼；春季候鸟归来时的鸟，最后夏季收获季的谷粒。复仇女神以灵缇牝犬、然后以水獭牝犬、然后以隼之形追赶他，最终以高冠黑牝鸡之形追上他——红冠黑羽表明她是死亡女神。在这一叙述中，太阳年结束于初秋的扬谷季节，这指向故事的地中海东部起源。在古典时代，克里特、塞浦路斯和德尔斐的年份，以及小亚细亚和巴勒斯坦的年份，都在九月结束。

However, when the victory of the patriarchal Indo-Europeans revolutionized the social system of the Eastern Mediterranean, the myth of the sexual chase was reversed. Greek and Latin mythology contains numerous anecdotes of the pursuit and rape of elusive goddesses or nymphs by gods in beast disguise: especially by the two senior gods, Zeus and Poseidon. Similarly in European folk-lore there are scores of variants on the ‘Two Magicians’ theme, in which the male magician, after a hot chase, outmagics the female and gains her maidenhead. In the English ballad of The Coal Black Smith, a convenient example of this altered form of chase, the correct seasonal order of events is broken because the original context has been forgotten. She becomes a fish, he an otter; she a hare, he a greyhound; she becomes a fly, he a spider and pulls her to his lair; finally she becomes a quilt on his bed, he a coverlet and the game is won. In a still more debased French variant, she falls sick, he becomes her doctor; she turns nun, he becomes her priest and confesses her night and day; she becomes a star, he a cloud and muffles her.
然而，当父权的印欧人的胜利革命化了东地中海的社会制度时，性追逐的神话被颠倒了。希腊和拉丁神话包含大量关于神以兽形追逐和强暴难以捉摸的女神或仙女的故事——尤其是两位最高神宙斯和波塞冬。类似地，欧洲民间传说中有无数「两个魔法师」主题的变体，其中男魔法师在一场激烈追逐后以法术胜过女魔法师并夺取她的贞操。在英国民谣《漆黑铁匠》——追逐变体的一个便利例子——中，事件的正确季节顺序被打乱了，因为原始语境已被遗忘。她变鱼，他变水獭；她变野兔，他变灵缇；她变苍蝇，他变蜘蛛将她拖入巢穴；最后她变成他床上的被子，他变成床罩，游戏结束。在一个更退化的法语变体中，她生病，他变医生；她当修女，他变神父日夜听她告解；她变星星，他变云将她遮住。

In the British witch-cult the male sorcerer was dominant – though in parts of Scotland Hecate, alias the Queen of Elfin or Faerie, still ruled – and The Coal Black Smith is likely to have been the song sung at a dramatic performance of the chase at a witches’ Sabbath; the association of smiths and horned gods is as ancient as Tubal Cain, the Kenite Goat-god. The horned Devil of the Sabbath had sexual connexion with all his witch attendants, though he seems to have used an enormous artificial member, not his own. Anne Armstrong, the Northumbrian witch already mentioned, testified in 1673 that, at a well-attended Sabbath held at Allansford, one of her companions, Ann Baites of Morpeth, successively transformed herself into cat, hare, greyhound and bee, to let the Devil – ‘a long black man, their protector, whom they call their God’ – admire her facility in changes. At first I thought that he chased Ann Baites, who was apparently the Maiden, or female leader of the coven, around the ring of witches, and that she mimicked the gait and cry of these various creatures in turn while he pursued her, adapting his changes to hers. The formula in The Coal Black Smith is ‘he became a greyhound dog’, or ‘he became an otter brown’, ‘and fetched her home again’. ‘Home again’ is used here in the technical sense of ‘to her own shape’, for Isobel Gowdie of Auldearne at her trial in 1662, quoted the witch formula for turning oneself into a hare:
在英国女巫崇拜中男性巫师占主导——虽然苏格兰部分地区赫卡忒别名精灵女王仍统治一切——《漆黑铁匠》很可能是在女巫安息日上演出追逐戏剧时所唱的歌；铁匠与角神的联系与该隐的土八·该隐——基尼特山羊神——一样古老。安息日的角魔鬼与所有女巫与会者性交，但他似乎使用的是巨大的假阳具而非自身。已提到的诺森伯兰女巫安妮·阿姆斯特朗在1673年作证说，在阿兰斯福德举行的一次盛大的安息日上，她的同伴之一莫佩斯的安·贝茨依次变身为猫、野兔、灵缇和蜜蜂，让魔鬼——「一个高大黑衣男子，他们的保护者，他们称之为他们的神」——欣赏她变形的熟练。起初我以为他追逐安·贝茨——她显然是巫会的少女或女性首领——在女巫圈中跑，而她依次模仿这些生物的步态和叫声，他追赶她时适应她的变化。《漆黑铁匠》中的公式是「他变成一只灵缇犬」或「他变成一只棕色水獭」「然后把她带回家来」。「回家来」在这里是技术意义上的「变回她自己的形状」，因为奥尔德恩的伊索贝尔·高迪在1662年受审时引用了女巫变兔的咒语：

I shall go into a hare
I shall go into a hare（我将化为野兔）



With sorrow and sighing and mickle care,
With sorrow and sighing and mickle care,（带着忧愁、叹息和无尽牵挂，）



And I shall go in the Devil’s name
And I shall go in the Devil's name（我将以魔鬼之名前往）



Aye, till I come home again.
Aye, till I come home again.（是的，直到我回来。）





It is clear from her subsequent account that there was no change of outward shape, but only of behaviour, and the verse suggests a dramatic dance. I see now that Ann Baites gave a solo performance, alternately mimicking the pursued and the pursuer, and that the Devil was content merely to applaud her. Probably the sequence was seasonal – hare and greyhound, trout and otter, bee and swallow, mouse and cat – and inherited from the earlier form of chase, with the pursuer as the black Cat-Demeter finally destroying the Sminthean mouse on the threshing-floor in the winnowing season. The whole song is easy to restore in its original version.1
从她随后的叙述中可以清楚地看到，并没有外形的改变，只是行为的改变，诗句暗示一种戏剧舞蹈。我现在明白了安·贝茨是独角表演，交替模仿被追逐者和追逐者，而魔鬼只是满意地为她鼓掌。序列大概是季节性的——野兔与灵缇、鳟鱼与水灵缇、蜜蜂与燕子、老鼠与猫——继承自更早的追逐形式，追逐者作为黑猫得墨忒耳最终在扬谷季的打谷场上消灭斯明透斯鼠。整首歌很容易恢复其原始版本。¹



An intermediate form of the ‘Two Magicians’ myth, quoted by Diodorus Siculus, Callimachus in his Hymn to Artemis and Antoninus Liberalis, the second-century AD mythographer, in his Transformations, who all refer it to different regions, is that the Goddess Artemis, alias Aphaea, Dictynna, Britomart or Atergatis, is unsuccessfully pursued and finally escapes in fish form. Callimachus makes Minos of Crete the erotic pursuer and Britomart the chaste pursued, and relates that the pursuit lasted for nine months from the early flood season to the winnowing season. The myth is intended to explain the fish-tail in the statues of the goddess at Ascalon, Phigalia, Crabos, Aegina, Cephallenia, Mount Dictynnaeum in Crete and elsewhere, and to justify her local devotees in retaining their pre-Hellenic rites and marital customs. Fishermen figure prominently in the story – Dictynna means a net – and fishermen are notoriously conservative in their beliefs. In the Philistine version from Ascalon, quoted by Athenaeus, the Goddess was Derketo and the pursuer was one Moxus or Mopsus: perhaps this should be Moschus the ancestor of King Midas’s tribe who defeated the Hittites. Cognate with this myth is the fruitless attempt by Apollo on the maidenhead of the nymph Daphne.
「两个魔法师」神话的一种中间形式——由西西里的狄奥多罗斯、卡利马科斯在《阿尔忒弥斯颂》中以及二世纪神话学家安东宁·利伯拉里斯在《变形记》中引用，他们各自将其归于不同地区——是女神阿尔忒弥斯，别名阿法亚、狄克廷娜、布里托玛特或阿特伽提斯，被追逐但未遂，最终以鱼形逃脱。卡利马科斯让克里特的米诺斯充当色情追逐者，布里托玛特为贞洁的被追逐者，并说追逐从早洪水季到扬谷季持续了九个月。这一神话旨在解释阿什凯隆、菲伽利亚、克拉博斯、埃伊纳、凯法利尼亚、克里特狄克廷娜姆山等地的女神雕像上的鱼尾，并为她的当地信徒保留其前希腊仪式和婚姻习俗提供正当理由。渔夫在故事中突出——狄克廷娜意为网——而渔夫在信仰上以保守著称。在阿什凯隆的非利士版本中——由雅典奈乌斯引用——女神是得尔凯托，追逐者是某个莫克苏斯或莫普苏斯：也许应为莫斯科斯，米达斯王部落之祖，曾击败赫梯人。与此相关的是阿波罗对仙女达芙妮贞操的徒劳企图。

The love-chase is, unexpectedly, the basis of the Coventry legend of Lady Godiva. The clue is provided by a miserere-seat in Coventry Cathedral, paralleled elsewhere in Early English grotesque woodcarving, which shows what the guide-books call ‘a figure emblematic of lechery’: a long-haired woman wrapped in a net, riding sideways on a goat and preceded by a hare. Gaster in his stories from the Jewish Targum, collected all over Europe, tells of a woman who when given a love-test by her royal lover, namely to come to him ‘neither clothed nor unclothed, neither on foot nor on horseback, neither on water nor on dry land, neither with or without a gift’ arrived dressed in a net, mounted on a goat, with one foot trailing in the ditch, and releasing a hare. The same story with slight variations, was told by Saxo Grammaticus in his late twelfth-century History of Denmark. Aslog, the last of the Volsungs, Brynhild’s daughter by Sigurd, was living on a farm at Spangerejd in Norway, disguised as a sooty-faced kitchen-maid called Krake (raven). Even so, her beauty made such an impression on the followers of the hero Ragnar Lodbrog that he thought of marrying her, and as a test of her worthiness told her to come to him neither on foot nor riding, neither dressed nor naked, neither fasting nor feasting, neither attended nor alone. She arrived on goatback, one foot trailing on the ground, clothed only in her hair and a fishing-net, holding an onion to her lips, a hound by her side.
出人意料的是，这场爱情追逐是戈黛娃夫人考文垂传说的基础。线索来自考文垂大教堂的一张misericord座椅——在早期英格兰怪诞木雕中另有类似物——导游手册称之为「象征淫欲的人物」：一个长发女子裹在网中，侧骑在山羊上，前方有一只野兔。加斯特在他从全欧洲收集的犹太 targum 故事中讲述了一个女子，当她的王室情人给她一个爱情考验——即「不穿也不脱、不行也不骑、不在水也不在陆、不带也不空」地来见他——她穿着渔网、骑着山羊、一只脚拖在沟中、释放一只野兔而来。萨克索·格拉马提库斯在其十二世纪末的《丹麦史》中讲述了几乎相同的故事，略有变化。沃尔松家族最后的传人——布伦希尔德与西格urd之女——奥斯洛格，住在挪威斯帕厄雷德的农庄上，化装成灰烬面孔的厨房女工，名叫克拉卡（乌鸦）。即便如此，她的美貌给英雄拉格纳·洛德布罗格的随从留下了如此深刻的印象，以至于他想娶她，为考验她的资格，让她「不行也不骑、不穿也不裸、不禁食也不宴飨、不随从也不独身」地来见他。她骑着山羊，一只脚拖在地上，仅以头发和渔网蔽体，唇衔洋葱，身边一条猎犬。

If the two stories are combined into a picture, the ‘figure emblematic of lechery’ has a black face, long hair, a raven flying overhead, a hare running ahead, a hound at her side, a fruit to her lips, a net over her and a goat under her. She will now be easily recognized as the May-eve aspect of the Love-and-Death goddess Freya, alias Frigg, Holda, Held, Hilde, Goda, or Ostara. In neolithic or early Bronze Age times she went North from the Mediterranean, where she was known as Dictynna (from her net), Aegea (from her goat), Coronis (from her raven), also Rhea, Britomart, Artemis and so on, and brought the Maze Dance with her.
如果将两个故事合并为一幅画面，「象征淫欲的人物」有一张黑脸、长发、头顶飞着乌鸦、前方跑着野兔、身旁一条猎犬、唇边一颗果实、身上一张网、身下一只山羊。她现在很容易被认出是爱与死女神弗蕾亚——别名弗丽嘉、霍尔达、赫尔德、希尔德、戈达或奥斯塔拉——的五朔前夕面向。在新石器时代或早期青铜时代，她从地中海北上——在那里她被称为狄克廷娜（源自她的网）、埃吉亚（源自她的山羊）、科罗尼斯（源自她的乌鸦），也称为瑞亚、布里托玛特、阿尔忒弥斯等——并将迷宫舞带到了北方。

The fruit at her lips is probably the apple of immortality and the raven denotes death and prophecy – Freya’s prophetic raven was borrowed from her by Odin, just as Bran borrowed Danu’s and Apollo Athene’s. The Goddess was established in Britain as Rhiannon, Arianrhod, Cerridwen, Blodeuwedd, Danu or Anna long before the Saxons, Angles and Danes brought very similar versions of her with them. Hilde was at home in the Milky Way, like Rhea in Crete and Blodeuwedd (Olwen) in Britain, both of whom were connected with goats; and in the Brocken May-eve ceremony a goat was sacrificed in her honour. As Holda she was mounted on a goat with a pack of twenty-four hounds, her daughters, running beside her – the twenty-four hours of May Eve – and was sometimes shown as piebald to represent her ambivalent character of black Earth-mother and corpse-like Death – Holda and Hel. As Ostara, the Saxon Goddess after whom Easter is named, she attended a May-eve Sabbath where a goat was sacrificed to her. The hare was her ritual animal: it still ‘lays’ Easter eggs. The goat spelt fertility of cattle; the hare, good hunting; the net, good fishing; the long hair, tall crops.
她唇边的果实可能是不朽之苹果，乌鸦象征死亡和预言——弗蕾亚的预言乌鸦被奥丁借走，如同布兰借走达努的、阿波罗借走雅典娜的。女神早在撒克逊人、盎格鲁人和丹麦人带来与她极其相似的版本之前，就已在英国以里安农、埃里安罗德、凯丽德温、布洛杜埃德、达努或安娜之名立足。希尔德居于银河之中，如同瑞亚在克里特、布洛杜埃德（奥尔文）在英国，她们都与山羊有关；在布罗肯山五朔前夕仪式上，一头山羊被献祭给她。作为霍尔达，她骑在山羊上，身旁跑着二十四条猎犬——她的女儿们——即五朔前夕的二十四小时——她有时被表现为花斑色，以表示她作为黑色大地母亲和尸体般死亡的双重性格——霍尔达和赫尔。作为奥斯塔拉——撒克逊的女神，复活节（Easter）因她得名——她参加一个五朔前夕安息日，一头山羊被献祭给她。野兔是她的仪式动物：它至今仍「产」复活节彩蛋。山羊意味着牛群兴旺；野兔意味着狩猎顺利；网意味着渔业丰收；长发意味着庄稼高长。

The May-eve goat, as is clear from the English witch ceremonies and from the Swedish May-play, ‘Bükkerwise’, was mated to the goddess, sacrificed and resurrected: that is to say, the Priestess had public connexion with the annual king dressed in goatskins, and either he was then killed and resurrected in the form of his successor, or else a goat was sacrificed in his stead and his reign prolonged. This fertility rite was the basis of the highly intellectualized ‘Lesser Mysteries’ of Eleusis, performed in February, representing the marriage of Goat-Dionysus to the Goddess Thyone, ‘the raving queen’, his death and resurrection.1 At Coventry, she evidently went to the ceremony riding on his back, to denote her domination of him – as Europa rode on the Minos bull, or Hera on her lion.
从英国女巫仪式和瑞典五朔剧《Bükkerwise》可以清楚地看出，五朔前夕的山羊与女神交配、被献祭并复活：也就是说，女祭司与穿着山羊皮的年度国王公开交合，然后要么他被杀死并以继任者的形式复活，要么以一头山羊代替他被献祭而延长他的统治。这一丰产仪式是高度智识化的厄琉息斯「小密仪」——在二月举行，表现山羊狄俄尼索斯与女神提俄涅（Thyone，「狂怒女王」）的婚姻、他的死亡和复活——的基础。¹在考文垂，她显然骑在他背上去参加仪式，以表示对他的支配——如同欧罗巴骑在米诺斯公牛上，或赫拉骑在她的狮子上。

The hare, as has been pointed out in Chapter Sixteen, was sacred both in Pelasgian Greece and Britain because it is swift, prolific and mates openly without embarrassment. I should have mentioned in this context that the early British tabu on hunting the hare, the penalty for a breach of which was to be struck with cowardice, was originally lifted on a single day in the year – May-eve – as the tabu on hunting the wren was lifted only on St. Stephen’s Day. (Boadicea let loose the hare during her battle with the Romans in the hope, presumably, that the Romans would strike at it with their swords and so lose courage.) The hare was ritually hunted on May-eve, and the miserere-seat ‘figure of lechery’ – which is a fair enough description of the Goddess on this occasion – is releasing the hare for her daughters to hunt. The folk-song If all those young men evidently belongs to these May-eve witch frolics:
如第十六章所述，野兔在佩拉斯吉希腊和不列颠都是神圣的，因为它迅捷、多产且毫不羞耻地公开交配。我应该在此语境中提到，早期不列颠禁猎野兔的禁忌——违者将被怯懦所击——最初在一年中仅一天——五朔前夕——解除，如同猎鹪鹩的禁忌仅在圣斯蒂芬日解除。（波阿迪西亚在与罗马人的战斗中释放野兔，大概是希望罗马人用剑砍它从而丧失勇气。）野兔在五朔前夕被仪式性地猎杀，而misericord座椅上的「淫欲人物」——在此场合这是对女神的恰当描述——正在释放野兔供她的女儿们猎杀。民歌《如果所有那些年轻人》显然属于这些五朔前夕女巫嬉戏：

If all those young men were like hares on the mountain
If all those young men were like hares on the mountain（如果所有那些年轻人像山上的野兔）



Then all those pretty maidens would get guns, go a-hunting.
Then all those pretty maidens would get guns, go a-hunting.（那么所有那些漂亮少女就会拿枪去打猎。）





‘Get guns’ is eighteenth-century; one should read ‘turn hounds’. There are other verses:
「拿枪」是十八世纪的；应读作「变灵缇」。还有其他段落：

If all those young men were like fish in the water
If all those young men were like fish in the water（如果所有那些年轻人像水中的鱼）



Then all those pretty maidens would soon follow after.
Then all those pretty maidens would soon follow after.（那么所有那些漂亮少女就会紧随其后。）





With nets? As we know from the story of Prince Elphin and Little Gwion, May-eve was the proper day for netting a weir, and the Goddess would not bring her net to the Sabbath for nothing.
用网？如我们从埃尔芬王子和小格维恩的故事中所知，五朔前夕是张网捕鱼的吉日，女神不会无缘无故把她的网带到安息日。

If all those young men were like rushes a-growing
If all those young men were like rushes a-growing（如果所有那些年轻人像生长的芦苇）



Then all those pretty maidens would get scythes go a-mowing.
Then all those pretty maidens would get scythes go a-mowing.（那么所有那些漂亮少女就会拿镰刀去割草。）





The love-chase again: the soul of the sacred king, ringed about by orgiastic women, tries to escape in the likeness of hare, or fish, or bee; but they pursue him relentlessly and in the end he is caught, torn in pieces and devoured. In one variant of the folk-song, the man is the pursuer, not the pursued:
又是爱情追逐：被狂欢女子环绕的神圣国王之灵试图以野兔、鱼或蜜蜂之形逃脱；但她们无情地追击他，最终他被抓住、撕碎并吞食。在民歌的一个变体中，男性是追逐者而非被追逐者：

Young women they run like hares on the mountain
Young women they run like hares on the mountain（年轻女子们像山上的野兔一样跑）



If I were but a young man I’d soon go a-hunting.
If I were but a young man I'd soon go a-hunting.（如果我是个年轻人我马上去打猎。）





The story of Lady Godiva, as recorded by Roger of Wendover, a St. Albans chronicler, in the thirteenth century, is that shortly before the Norman Conquest the Saxon Lady Godiva (Godgifu) asked her husband Leofric Earl of Mercia to relieve the people of Coventry from oppressive tolls. He consented on condition that she rode naked through the crowded market on a fair-day; and she did so with a knight on either side, but preserved her modesty by covering herself with her hair, so that only her ‘very white legs’ showed underneath. The story, which is also told of the Countess of Hereford and ‘King John’ in connexion with the distribution of bread and cheese at St. Briavel’s in Gloucestershire, cannot be historically true, because Coventry in Lady Godiva’s day was a village without either tolls or fairs. But it is certain that in 1040 she persuaded Leofric to build and endow a Benedictine monastery at Coventry, and what seems to have happened is that after the Conquest the monks disguised a local May-eve procession of the Goddess Goda, during which all pious Christians were at first required to keep indoors, with an edifying anecdote about their benefactress Lady Godiva, modelling the story on Saxo’s. The fraud is given away by the ‘Lady Godiva’ procession of Southam (twelve miles south of Coventry and included in Leofric’s earldom), where two figures were carried, one white and one black – the Goddess as Holda and Hel, Love and Death. The story of Peeping Tom the Tailor is not mentioned by Roger of Wendover, but may be a genuine early tradition. The St. Briavel’s ceremony which took place, like the Southam and Coventry processions, on Corpus Christi, a date associated both at York and Coventry with mystery plays, is said to have commemorated the freeing of the people from a tax on the gathering of fire-wood in the neighbouring forest; Corpus Christi always falls on a Friday, the Goddess’s own day, and corresponds roughly with May Eve; thus, it seems that the mystery-play has its origin in the May Eve festivities, Bükkerwise, in honour of Goda, the Bona Dea. If there was a prohibition against men witnessing the procession, as there was at Rome in the Bona Dea ceremonies, and as there was in Celtic Germany according to Tacitus (Germania, chap. 40) against any man witnessing Hertha’s annual bath after her progress back to her sacred grove, and as there was in Greece in the days of Actaeon, when Diana took her woodland bath, Peeping Tom may record the memory of this.

There is an unconscious hankering in Britain after goddesses, if not for a goddess so dominant as the aboriginal Triple Goddess, at least for a female softening of the all-maleness of the Christian Trinity. The male Trinity corresponds increasingly less with the British social system, in which woman, now that she has become a property owner and a voter, has nearly regained the position of respect which she enjoyed before the Puritan revolution. True, the male Trinity antedated the Puritan revolution but it was a theological not an emotional concept: as has been shown, the Queen of Heaven with her retinue of female saints had a far greater hold in the popular imagination between the Crusades and the Civil War than either the Father or the Son. And one of the results of Henry VIII’s breach with Rome was that when his daughter Queen Elizabeth became head of the Anglican Church she was popularly regarded as a sort of deity: poets not only made her their Muse but gave her titles – Phoebe, Virginia, Gloriana – which identified her with the Moon-goddess, and the extraordinary hold that she gained on the affections of her subjects was largely due to this cult.

The temporary reinstatement of the Thunder-god in effective religious sovereignty during the Commonwealth is the most remarkable event in modern British history: the cause was a mental ferment induced by the King James Bible among the mercantile classes of the great towns and in parts of Scotland and England where Celtic blood ran thinnest. The first Civil War was fought largely between the chivalrous nobility with their retainers and the anti-chivalrous mercantile classes with their artisan supporters. The Anglo-Saxon-Danish south-east was solidly Parliamentarian and the Celtic north-west as solidly Royalist. It was therefore appropriate that at the Battle of Naseby, which decided the war, the rival battle cries were, for the Parliamentary army, ‘God our Strength’ and for the Royalist army ‘Queen Marie’. Queen Marie was a Catholic and her name evoked the Queen of Heaven and of Love. The Thunder-god won the day, and vented his spite not only on the Virgin and her retinue of saints, but on Maid Marian and her maypole retinue, and on the other Triple Goddess cult which still survived secretly in many parts of the British Isles – the witch cult. But his triumph was short-lived because after gaining the victory he had removed the King,1 his chief representative. He was therefore temporarily ousted at the Restoration and when he returned in 1688 with a Protestant King as his representative, his thunderous fury had been curbed. He gained a second access of strength in the enthusiastic religious revival, fostered by the merchant class, which accompanied the Industrial Revolution; but lost ground again at the beginning of the present century.

1 In the corresponding ancient British mysteries there seems to have been a formula in which the Goddess teasingly promised the initiate who performed a sacred marriage with her that he would not die ‘either on foot or on horseback, on water or on land, on the ground or in the air, outside a house or inside, shod or unshod, clothed or unclothed,’ and then, as a demonstration of her power, manoeuvred him into a position where the promise was no longer valid – as in the legend of Llew Llaw and Blodeuwedd, where a goat figures in the murder scene. Part of the formula survives in the Masonic initiation ritual. The apprentice ‘neither naked nor clothed, barefoot nor shod, deprived of all metals, hood winked, with a cable-tow about his neck is led to the door of the lodge in a halting moving posture.’
¹ 在对应的古不列颠密仪中，似乎有一则公式：女神调戏性地向与她举行神圣婚姻的入教者承诺他不会死「不行也不骑、不在水也不在陆、不在地上也不在空中、不在屋外也不在屋内、不穿鞋也不赤脚、不穿也不脱」，然后，为展示她的权力，将他操纵到一个承诺不再有效的位置——如卢·劳与布洛杜埃德的传说中山羊出现在谋杀场景中。部分公式存留于共济会入教仪式中。学徒「不裸也不穿、不赤足也不穿鞋，被剥夺一切金属，蒙眼，脖套缆绳，以跛行的姿态被引向会堂大门。」



1 It is a strange paradox that Milton, though he had been the first Parliamentary author to defend the execution of Charles I and was the Thunder-god’s own Laureate, fell later under the spell of ‘the Northern Muse’, Christina of Sweden, and in his Second Defense of the English People his flattery of her is not only as extravagant as anything that the Elizabethans wrote about Elizabeth, but seems wholly sincere.
¹ 一个奇怪的悖论是，弥尔顿虽然曾是第一位为处决查理一世辩护的议会派作家，是雷神自己的桂冠诗人，后来却落入「北方缪斯」——瑞典的克里斯蒂娜——的魔咒。他在《为英国人民的第二次辩护》中对她的颂扬不仅如伊丽莎白时代人对伊丽莎白的任何赞词一样奢华，而且似乎完全真诚。





Chapter Twenty-Three

title: 第二十三章
content:
FABULOUS BEASTS
幻兽





Indian mystics hold that to think with perfect clarity in a religious sense one must first eliminate all physical desire, even the desire to continue living; but this is not at all the case with poetic thinking, since poetry is rooted in love, and love in desire, and desire in hope of continued existence. However, to think with perfect clarity in a poetic sense one must first rid oneself of a great deal of intellectual encumbrance, including all dogmatic doctrinal prepossessions: membership of any political party or religious sect or literary school deforms the poetic sense – as it were, introduces something irrelevant and destructive into the magic circle, drawn with a rowan, hazel or willow rod, within which the poet insulates himself for the poetic act. He must achieve social and spiritual independence at whatever cost, learn to think mythically as well as rationally, and never be surprised at the weirdly azoölogical beasts which walk into the circle; they come to be questioned, not to alarm.
印度神秘主义者认为，要以宗教意义上的完美清晰来思考，人必须首先消除一切肉体欲望，甚至继续活下去的欲望；但诗性思考绝非如此，因为诗歌植根于爱，爱植根于欲望，欲望植根于对继续存在的希望。然而，要以诗性意义上的完美清晰来思考，人必须首先摆脱大量智识负担，包括一切教条式的先入之见：隶属于任何政党、宗派或文学流派都会扭曲诗性感觉——仿佛在用花楸、榛树或柳条魔杖画出的魔法圈中引入了某种无关且具破坏性的东西——诗人正是在这个圈内将自己隔绝以进行诗性活动。他必须不惜一切代价实现社会和精神上的独立，学会以神话的方式也以理性的方式思考，且永远不要对走入圈内的怪异非动物学野兽感到惊讶；它们是来被质询的，不是来惊吓的。

If the visitant is a Chimaera (‘She-goat’) for example, the poet will recognize her by the lion-head, goat-body and serpent-tail as a Carian Calendar-beast – another form of the winged goat, on which, according to Clement of Alexandria, Zeus flew up to Heaven. The Chimaera was a daughter of Typhon, the destructive storm god, and of Echidne, a winter Snake-goddess; the Hittites borrowed her from the Carians and carved her likeness on a temple at Carchemish on the Euphrates. Cerberus, a bitch miscalled a dog, is also likely to appear in the circle: a cognate beast, with the usual triad of heads – lioness, lynx and sow. The lynx is an autumn beast, apparently mentioned by Gwion in his Can Y Meirch, though he may be referring to the Palug Cat, the Anglesey Cat-Demeter: ‘I have been a spotted-headed cat on a forked tree.’
如果访客是喀迈拉（Chimaera，「牝山羊」），诗人会从她的狮首、山羊身和蛇尾认出她是一头卡里亚历法兽——飞山羊的另一种形式，据克莱门特·亚历山大记载，宙斯骑着它飞上天堂。喀迈拉是暴风神堤丰与冬蛇女神厄喀德涅之女；赫梯人从卡里亚人那里借走她，将其形象雕刻在幼发拉底河上卡尔基米什的一座神庙上。刻耳柏洛斯——一头被误称为犬的牝犬——也可能出现在圈内：一头同族野兽，有通常的三首——狮、猞猁和牝猪。猞猁是秋季之兽，大概被格维恩在《马之歌》中提及，虽然他可能指的是帕卢格猫——安格尔西的猫得墨忒耳：「我曾是一只在分叉树上的斑点头猫。」

The unicorn may puzzle the poet. But the unicorn of Pliny’s description – which is embodied in the heraldic unicorn of the British Royal Arms, except that the horn is a straight white spiral – makes good calendar sense: it stands for the five-season solar year of the Boibel-Loth alphabet. The horn is centred in the Dog-days, and is the symbol of power: ‘I will exalt your horn.’ It stands for the E season, then beginning; as the head of the deer stands for the I season, in which deer were hunted; the body of the horse for the A season, at the beginning of which the October Horse was sacrificed at Rome; the feet of the elephant for the O season, in which the earth puts out her greatest strength; the tail (Ura) of the lion for the U season. The beast of the horn was originally, it seems, the rhinoceros, which is the most formidable beast in the world – ‘and who would cross Tom Rhinoceros does what the Panther dares not’ – but owing to the difficulty of obtaining rhinoceros horn the long curved black horns of the oryx were in Pliny’s time fraudulently supplied by traders as ‘unicorn’s horn’. Pliny, who had the usual Roman dislike and mistrust of fabulous beasts and mentioned the unicorn as a genuine zoölogical specimen, must have seen such a horn. In Britain, however, the narwhal horn became the accepted type, because of its white colour and superior hardness and because it is curved in the spiral of immortality, and because the variously named God of the Year always came out of the sea – as Gwion puts it in his Angar Cyvyndawd: ‘From the Deep he came in the flesh.’ The narwhal is called the ‘sea-unicorn’ in consequence. However, a few British mythographers, such as the early seventeenth-century Thomas Boreman, accepted Pliny’s view, recording: ‘His horn is as hard as iron and as rough as any file, twisted and curled like a flaming sword; very straight, sharp and everywhere black, excepting the point.’ An interesting variety of the unicorn is the wild-ass unicorn, which Herodotus accepted as genuinely zoological; the wild ass is the beast of Set, whose fifth part of the year centres at midsummer and whose horn is thus exalted. But it must not be forgotten that the fifth-century BC historian, Ctesias, the first Greek to write about the unicorn, describes its horn, in his Indica, as being coloured white, red and black. These are the colours of the Triple Moon-goddess, as has been shown in the mulberry-and-calf riddle quoted from Suidas near the close of Chapter Four, to whom the God of the Year was subject.
独角兽可能让诗人困惑。但老普林尼描述的独角兽——体现在英国皇家纹章的纹章独角兽中，只是角是直的白色螺旋——在历法上说得通：它代表博伊贝尔-洛斯字母表的五季太阳年。角以犬日为中心，是权力的象征：「我将高举你的角。」它代表当时开始的 E 季；如鹿头代表猎鹿的 I 季；马体代表以罗马十月马献祭开始的 A 季；象足代表大地展现最大力量的 O 季；狮尾（Ura）代表 U 季。有角之兽最初似乎是犀牛——世上最可怕的野兽——「谁敢招惹犀牛汤姆，便做了豹子不敢做的事」——但由于获取犀牛角的困难，普林尼时代商人欺诈性地以角马的长弯黑角充当「独角兽角」。普林尼通常像罗马人一样厌恶和不信任幻兽，将独角兽视为真正的动物学标本，他必然见过这样的角。然而在英国，独角鲸角成为公认的标准，因为其白色和 superior硬度，因为它以不朽的螺旋弯曲，也因为名称各异的车之神总是从海中来——如格维恩在《安加尔·基温达德》中所言：「他从深渊中以肉身而来。」独角鲸因此被称为「海独角兽」。然而，少数英国神话学家——如十七世纪早期的托马斯·博尔曼——接受普林尼的观点，记载道：「他的角硬如铁、粗如锉，扭曲卷曲如烈焰之剑；极直、尖锐、通体黑色，唯尖端除外。」独角兽的一个有趣变种是野驴独角兽，希罗多德接受其为真正的动物；野驴是塞特之兽，其一年的第五部分以仲夏为中心，因此其角被高举。但不可忘记的是，公元前五世纪的历史学家克特西亚斯——第一个写到独角兽的希腊人——在其《印度志》中描述其角为白、红、黑三色。如第四章末尾引用的苏伊达斯桑椹与牛犊谜语所示，这是三重月女神的颜色，年之神受其统辖。

The unicorn probably had a spatial as well as a temporal meaning, though space has always been divided by four quarters of the horizon, not by five fifths. The square cross, whether plain or converted into a swastika or cross-crosslet, has from time immemorial represented the fullest extent of sovereignty; it was a prime symbol in Minoan Crete, either alone or enclosed in a circle, and was reserved for the Goddess and her royal son, the King. In parts of India where Kali is worshipped, with rites closely resembling those of the Cretan and Pelasgian Great Goddess, as the most potent of a Pentad of deities, namely Siva, Kali, Vishnu, Surya and the elephant-god Ganesa – roughly corresponding with the Egyptian pentad, namely Osiris, Horus, Isis, Set and Nephthys – five has a definite spatial sense. In the coronation ritual of an Indian king, the officiating priest as he invests the king with a sacred mantle called ‘the Womb’ in a ceremony of rebirth, gives him five dice and says: ‘Thou art the master; may these five regions of thine fall to thy lot.’ The five regions are the four quarters of the earth, and the zenith.
独角兽大概有空间意义也有时间意义，虽然空间历来由地平线的四象限划分，而非五等分。方形十字——无论是简单的还是变为卍字或十字十字架——自远古以来代表最完整的主权范围；它是弥诺斯克里特的一个主要符号，单独出现或包含在圆圈内，专属女神及其王室之子——国王。在印度崇拜迦梨的地区——其仪式与克里特和佩拉斯吉大女神的仪式极为相似——迦梨作为五神组——湿婆、迦梨、毗湿奴、苏利耶和象神伽涅沙——中最强大者被崇拜——大致对应埃及五神组：奥西里斯、荷鲁斯、伊西斯、塞特和奈芙蒂斯——五有明确的空间意义。在印度国王的加冕仪式中，主持祭司在以称为「子宫」的神圣斗篷为国王举行重生仪式时，给他五枚骰子并说：「你是主人；愿你的这五个区域归于你名下。」五个区域是大地四象限和天顶。

Thus the unicorn’s single exalted horn represents ‘the upper pole’ which reaches from the king directly up to the zenith, to the hottest point attained by the sun. The unicorn’s horn in Egyptian architecture is the obelisk; which has a square base tapering to a pyramidical point: it expresses dominion over the four quarters of the world and the zenith. In squatter form it is the pyramid, and the dominion originally expressed was not that of the Sun-god, who never shines from the north, but that of the Triple Goddess whose white marble triangle encloses her royal son’s tomb from every side.
因此独角兽单一高举的角代表「上极」——从国王直达天顶，即太阳达到的最热点。独角兽的角在埃及建筑中是方尖碑；它有方形底座逐渐收窄至锥形尖顶：它表达了对世界四象限和天顶的统治。在更矮的形式中它是金字塔，最初表达的统治不是太阳神的——太阳从不从北方照耀——而是三重女神的，她的白色大理石三角形从四面围住她王室之子的墓。

Kali, like her counterpart Minerva, has five as her sacred numeral. Thus her mystic, the poet Ram Prasad, addresses her as she dances madly on Siva’s prostrate body:
迦梨如同她的对应者密涅瓦，以五为神圣数字。因此她的神秘主义者——诗人拉姆·普拉萨德——在她狂舞于湿婆俯卧之身时如此向她致辞：

My heart is five lotuses. You building these five into one, dance and swell in my mind.
My heart is five lotuses. You building these five into one, dance and swell in my mind.（我的心是五朵莲花。你将这五朵合而为一，在我心中舞蹈膨胀。）





He is referring to the cults of the five deities, all of which are really cults of Kali. It will be recalled that both Dionysus and the sacred white cow, Io of Argos, who ultimately became the goddess Isis, are recorded to have paid visits to India.
他指的是五位神祇的崇拜，其实都是迦梨的崇拜。可以回想，狄俄尼索斯和阿尔戈斯的白色神牛伊俄——她最终成为女神伊西斯——据记载都曾访问印度。

In the Dionysian Mysteries the hirco-cervus, goat-stag, was the symbol of resurrection, of man’s hope of immortality, and it seems that when the Hyperborean Druids visited Thessaly they recognized the goat stag, associated with apples, as their own immortal white hart or hind, which also was associated with apples. For the apple tree, ut dicitur, is the shelter of the white hind. It is from the goat-stag that the unicorn of heraldry and of mediaeval art derives its occasional beard; but among Christian mystics the Greek goat-unicorn of Daniel’s vision has contributed bellicosity to this once pacific beast.
在狄俄尼索斯密仪中，山羊鹿（hirco-cervus）是复活——人类不朽希望的象征，当极北的德鲁伊访问色萨利时，他们似乎认出了与苹果相关联的山羊鹿就是自己的不朽白牡鹿或牝鹿——后者也与苹果相关。因为苹果树，据说，是白牝鹿的庇护所。纹章和中世纪艺术中的独角兽偶有胡须即源自山羊鹿；但在基督教神秘主义者中，但以理异象中的希腊山羊独角兽为这只曾经平和的野兽增添了好斗性。

In Britain and France, the white hart or hind was not ousted by the unicorn; it persisted in popular tradition and figured in the mediaeval romances as an emblem of mystery. King Richard II adopted ‘a white hart lodged’ as his personal badge; which is how the beast found its way to the sign-boards of British inns. It sometimes wore a cross between its antlers as it had appeared to St. Hubert, patron of huntsmen, who had been chasing it through the dense forest for weeks without rest and to St. Julian the Hospitaler. Thus the Unicorn of the desert and the White Hart of the forest have the same mystical sense; but during the Hermetic vogue of the early seventeenth century were distinguished as meaning respectively the spirit and the soul. The Hermetics were neo-Platonists who patched their philosophic cloaks with shreds of half-forgotten bardic lore. In the Book of Lambspring‚ a rare Hermetic tract, an engraving shows a deer and a unicorn standing together in a forest. The text is:
在英国和法国，白牡鹿或牝鹿并未被独角兽取代；它在民间传统中存续，在中世纪传奇中作为神秘象征出现。理查德二世采用「一只卧伏的白牡鹿」作为个人徽章；这便是此兽如何出现在英国酒馆招牌上的。它有时在角间戴着十字架——如同它曾出现在猎人的主保圣人圣休伯特面前，后者已在密林中追逐它数周无歇——以及圣朱利安·医院院面前。因此沙漠中的独角兽和森林中的白牡鹿具有同样的神秘含义；但在十七世纪早期赫尔墨斯主义风潮中被区分为分别代表精神和灵魂。赫尔墨斯主义者是新柏拉图主义者，他们用半被遗忘的吟游诗学碎片缝补哲学外衣。在《拉姆普林之书》——一部罕见的赫尔墨斯主义小册子——中，一幅版画显示一头鹿和一只独角兽并肩立于森林中。文本如下：

The Sages say truly that two animals are in this forest: one glorious, beautiful and swift, a great and strong deer; the other an unicorn….If we apply the parable of our art, we shall call the forest the body….The Unicorn will be the spirit at all times. The deer desires no other name but that of the soul….He that knows how to tame and master them by art, to couple them together, and to lead them in and out of the forest, may justly be called a Master.
The Sages say truly that two animals are in this forest: one glorious, beautiful and swift, a great and strong deer; the other an unicorn….If we apply the parable of our art, we shall call the forest the body….The Unicorn will be the spirit at all times. The deer desires no other name but that of the soul….He that knows how to tame and master them by art, to couple them together, and to lead them in and out of the forest, may justly be called a Master.（智者们说得对，这片森林中有两只动物：一只辉煌、美丽而敏捷，是一头高大强壮的鹿；另一只是独角兽……如果我们将我们技艺的寓言加以应用，我们应称森林为身体……独角兽永远是精神。鹿只渴望一个名字，那就是灵魂……懂得以法术驯服和掌控它们、将它们配对、并引领它们进出森林的人，可以正当地被称为大师。）





An anonymous beast may appear to the poet with deer’s head crowned with gold, horse’s body and serpent’s tail. He will be out of a Gaelic poem published by Carmichael in Carmina Gadelica, a dialogue between Bride and her unnamed son.
一只无名的野兽可能以戴金冠的鹿头、马体和蛇尾出现在诗人面前。它出自卡迈克尔在《盖尔赞歌》中发表的一首盖尔语诗——新娘与她无名之子之间的对话。

BRIDE: Black the town yonder,
BRIDE: Black the town yonder,（新娘：那边的城镇是黑的，）



Black those that are in it;
Black those that are in it;（里面的人也是黑的；）



I am the White Swan,
I am the White Swan,（我是白天鹅，）



Queen of them all.
Queen of them all.（她们所有人的女王。）





SON: I will voyage in God’s name
SON: I will voyage in God's name（儿子：我将以神之名航行）



In likeness of deer,
In likeness of deer,（以鹿之形，）



In likeness of horse,
In likeness of horse,（以马之形，）



In likeness of serpent, in likeness of king.
In likeness of serpent, in likeness of king.（以蛇之形，以王之形。）



More powerful will it be with me than with all others.
More powerful will it be with me than with all others.（它在我身上将比在所有其他人身上更为强大。）





The son is evidently a god of the waning year, as the sequence of deer, horse and serpent shows.
这个儿子显然是渐消年之神，正如鹿、马和蛇的序列所示。

Or a phoenix may fly into the circle. The phoenix, though literally believed in by the Romans – I suppose because its visits to On-Heliopolis were said to be so brief and far between that nobody could disprove its existence – was also a calendar beast. For the Egyptians had no leap-year: every year the fragment of a day which was left over at New Year was saved up, until finally after 1460 years, called a Sothic Year, the fragments amounted to a whole year; and the fixed festivals which had become more and more displaced as the centuries went by (with the same sort of attendant inconveniences as New Zealanders experience from their midsummer Christmas) fetched up again where they had originally stood; and a whole year could be intercalated in the annals. This was the occasion of much rejoicing, and at On-Heliopolis, the chief Sun Temple of Egypt, an eagle with painted wings was, it seems, burned alive with spices in a nest of palm branches to celebrate the event.
或者一只凤凰可能飞入圈内。凤凰虽然被罗马人字面地相信——我想是因为据说它访问昂-赫利奥波利斯的间隔如此短暂而稀少以至于无人能反驳其存在——也是一种历法兽。因为埃及人没有闰年：每年新年结束时剩下的一天碎片被积攒起来，直到1460年后——称为一个索提斯年——碎片总计一整年；随着世纪推移而越来越偏移的固定节日（带着新西兰人因仲夏圣诞节所经历的同样不便）重新回到了它们最初的位置；于是可以闰入一整年。这是一个盛大庆祝的时刻，在昂-赫利奥波利斯——埃及最重要的太阳神庙——一只翅膀涂彩的鹰似乎被连同香料在一个棕榈枝巢中活活烧死以庆祝这一事件。

This eagle represented the Sun-god, and the palm was sacred to the Great Goddess his mother; the Sun had completed his great revolution and the old Sun-eagle was therefore returned to the nest for the inauguration of a new Phoenix Age. The legend was that from the ashes of the Phoenix a little worm was born which presently turned into a real Phoenix. This worm was the six hours and the few odd minutes which were left over at the end of the Phoenix Year: in four years they would add up to a whole day, a Phoenix chick. From Herodotus’s muddled account of the Phoenix it seems that there was always a sacred eagle kept at On-Heliopolis, and that when it died it was embalmed in a round egg of myrrh, which would preserve it indefinitely; then another eagle was consecrated. Presumably these eggs of myrrh were included in the final holocaust. That the Phoenix came flying from Arabia need mean no more than that, for the Egyptians, the sun rose from the Sinai desert. It is ironical that the early Christians continued to believe in a literal Phoenix, which they made a type of the resurrected Christ, long after the Phoenix had been killed. The Emperor Augustus unwittingly killed it in 30 BC when he stabilized the Egyptian calendar.1
这只鹰代表太阳神，棕榈是伟大女神——他母亲——的神圣之树；太阳完成了他的大循环，因此旧太阳之鹰被送回巢中以开启新的凤凰纪元。传说凤凰的灰烬中诞生了一条小虫，不久变成真正的凤凰。这条虫子是凤凰年结束后剩余的六小时零几分：四年后它们将合计一整天，一只凤凰幼崽。从希罗多德对凤凰的混乱叙述来看，昂-赫利奥波利斯似乎一直养着一只神圣的鹰，当它死去时被包在一个圆形没药蛋中防腐保存，可以无限期保存；然后另一只鹰被祝圣。大概这些没药蛋被包含在最终的焚烧中。凤凰从阿拉伯飞来的说法不过意味着对埃及人来说太阳从西奈沙漠升起。讽刺的是，早期基督徒在凤凰被杀死很久之后仍继续字面地相信凤凰，将其作为复活基督的预表。奥古斯都皇帝在公元前30年稳定埃及历法时无意中杀死了凤凰。¹

Or a pack of tall, white Gabriel Hounds with red ears and pink noses may come streaming into view in pursuit of an unbaptised soul. Despite their spectral appearance and their sinister reputation in British myth, these animals are decently zoölogical. They are the ancient Egyptian hunting dogs, pictured in tomb paintings, which though extinct in Egypt are still bred in the Island of Ibiza, where they were originally brought by Carthaginian colonists. The breed may also have been introduced into Britain towards the close of the second millennium BC along with the blue Egyptian beads found in Salisbury Plain burials. They are larger and faster than greyhounds and hunt by smell as well as by sight; when in view of game they make the same yelping noise that migrating wild geese – especially the barnacle-goose – make when they fly far overhead at night: a sound taken in the North and West of England as an omen of approaching death. Anubis, the embalmer-god who conveyed the soul of Osiris to the Underworld, was originally a prowling jackal but came to be pictured as a noble-hearted hunting dog, only his bushy tail remaining as evidence of his jackal days.
或者一群高大白色的加百列猎犬——红耳粉鼻——可能涌现在视野中，追逐一个未受洗的灵魂。尽管它们幽灵般的外表和英国神话中的恶名，这些动物是正正经经的动物学物种。它们是古埃及猎犬——见于墓画——虽已在埃及灭绝但仍在于伊维萨岛繁殖，由迦太基殖民者最初带到那里。这一品种也可能在公元前二千纪末与在索尔兹伯里平原墓葬中发现的蓝色埃及珠一起被引入英国。它们比灵缇更大更快，凭嗅觉和视觉狩猎；当发现猎物时发出与迁徙的雁群——尤其是白颊雁——夜间在高空飞过时相同的吠叫声：这声音在英格兰北部和西部被视为死亡的预兆。阿努比斯——运送奥西里斯灵魂到冥界的防腐神——最初是一只潜行的豺，但后来被描绘为高贵心的猎犬，只有蓬松的尾巴保留了豺的痕迹。

Or the visitant may be a Cherub. The Cherub mentioned in the first chapter of Ezekiel is also clearly a beast of the calendar sort. It has four parts which represent the ‘four New Years’ of Jewish tradition: Lion for Spring; Eagle for Summer; Man for Autumn, the principal New Year; and Ox for Winter, the Judaean ploughing season. This Cherub is identified by Ezekiel with a fiery wheel, which is as plainly the wheel of the solar year as the God whom it serves is plainly the Sun of Righteousness, an emanation of the Ancient of Days. Moreover, each Cherub – there are four of them – is a wheel of this God’s chariot and rolls straight forward, without deflexion. Ezekiel’s summary: ‘And their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel’ has become proverbial for its unintelligibility. But it makes simple calendar sense. Each wheel of God’s chariot is the annual cycle, or wheel, of the four seasons; and the chariot’s arrival inaugurated a cycle, or wheel, of four years. Every year, in fact, wheels within a four-year wheel from the beginning to he end of time: and the Eternal Charioteer is the God of Israel. By making the Cherub-wheels themselves provide the motive power of the chariot, Ezekiel avoided having to put an angelic horse between the shafts: he remembered that horse-drawn votive chariots set up by King Manasseh in the Temple of Jerusalem had been removed as idolatrous by Good King Josiah. But Ezekiel’s Eagle should really be a Ram or a Goat, and his Man a man-faced fiery Serpent; with eagle’s wings for each of the four beasts. His reasons for this misrepresentation will appear in my last chapter.
或者访客可能是一头基路伯。以西结第一章提到的基路伯显然也是一种历法兽。它有四个部分代表犹太传统中的「四个新年」：狮子代表春季；鹰代表夏季；人代表秋季——主要的新年；牛代表冬季——犹地亚的犁地季节。以西结将这基路伯等同于一轮火轮，它如同太阳年之轮一样明显，而它所侍奉的神也如同「公义的太阳」——亘古常在者的流出一样明显。而且，每头基路伯——共有四头——是这位神战车的一个轮子，笔直向前滚动不偏转。以西结的总结「它们的形状和功用如同轮中套轮」已因其不可理解性成为谚语。但它有简单的历法意义。神战车的每个轮子是四季的年度循环，即轮；战车的到达开启了一个四年的循环，即轮。实际上每年都是从时间之始到时间之终在四年一轮中的轮中之轮：而永恒的御者是以色列的神。通过让基路伯轮本身提供战车的动力，以西结避免了在辕间放一匹天使马：他记得玛拿西王在耶路撒冷圣殿中设立的马拉还愿战车已被好王约西亚作为偶像崇拜拆除。但以西结的鹰实际上应为公羊或山羊，他的人面应为人面火蛇；四兽各带鹰翅。他如此误饰的原因将在我的最后一章中揭示。

The colour of these bright cloud-borne Cherubim was Apollonian amber, like that of the Man whom they served. They might well be ministers of Hyperborean Apollo the Sun-god, whose sacred jewel was amber. What is more, each golden spoke of the wheel ended in the leg of a calf; and the golden calf was the sacred beast of the god who, according to King Jeroboam, had brought Israel out of Egypt, as it also was of the God Dionysus, the changing part of the unchanging Apollo.
这些明亮的云载基路伯的颜色是阿波罗式的琥珀色，如同它们所侍奉之人。它们很可能是极北太阳神阿波罗的使者——琥珀是他的神圣宝石。更重要的是，轮的每根金辐都以一条牛犊的腿结束；而金牛犊是——据耶罗波安王说——带领以色列出埃及的神的神圣之兽，也是狄俄尼索斯——不变的阿波罗的变化部分——的神圣之兽。

This apparent identification of Jehovah with Apollo seems to have alarmed the Pharisees, though they did not dare reject the vision. It is recorded that a student who recognized the meaning of hashmal (amber -‘hashmal’ is modern Hebrew for electricity; ‘electricity’ is derived from the Greek word for amber) and discussed it imprudently was blasted by lightning (Haggada, 13.B). For this reason, according to the Mishnah, the Ma’aseh Merkabah (‘Work of the Chariot’) might not be taught to anyone unless he were not only wise but able to deduce knowledge through wisdom (‘gnosis’) of his own, and no one else might be present during the teaching. And ‘he who speaks of the things which are before, behind, above and below, it were better that he had never been born’. On the whole it was considered safest to leave the Merkabah alone, especially as it was prophesied that ‘in the fullness of time Ezekiel will come again and unlock for Israel the chambers of the Merkabah.’ (Cant. Rabbah, I, 4.) Thus only a few known Rabbis taught the mystery and only to the most select of their pupils; among them Rabbi Johanan ben Zadkai, Rabbi Joshua (Vice-President of the Sanhedrin under Gamaliel), Rabbi Akiba and Rabbi Nehunia. Rabbi Zera said that even chapter headings of the Merkabah must not be communicated except to a person who was the head of an academy and was cautious in temperament. Rabbi Ammi said the doctrine might be entrusted only to one who possessed all the five qualities enumerated in Isaiah, III, 3: the captain of fifty, the honourable man, the counsellor, the skilled craftsman, the eloquent orator. The belief grew that expositions of the Merkabah mystery would cause Jehovah to appear. ‘Rabbi Johanan ben Zadkai was riding along the road upon his ass, while his pupil Eleazar ben Arak walked behind him. Said Rabbi Eleazar: “Master, teach me about the Work of the Chariot.” Rabbi Johanan declined. Rabbi Eleazar said again: “Am I permitted to repeat in your presence one thing which you have already taught me?” Rabbi Johanan assented, but dismounted from his ass, wrapped himself in his gown and seated himself upon a stone under an olive-tree. He declared that it was unseemly that he should be riding while his pupil was discoursing on so awful a mystery, and while the Shekinah (‘the Brightness’) and the Malache ha-Shareth (‘the Angels-in-Waiting’) were accompanying them. Immediately Rabbi Eleazar began his exposition, fire came down from Heaven and encircled them and the whole field. The angels assembled to listen, as the sons of man assemble to witness the festivities of a marriage; and there was a singing in the terebinth-trees: “Praise the Lord from the earth, ye dragons and all deeps, fruitful trees and all cedars, praise ye the Lord!” To which an angel answered from the fire, saying: “This is the Work of the Chariot!” When Eleazar had finished, Rabbi Johanan stood up and kissed him on the head. He said: “Praised be the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, for He has given our father Abraham a wise son who knows how to discourse on the glory of our Father in Heaven.”’
这种将耶和华与阿波罗等同的表面迹象似乎使法利赛人警恐，尽管他们不敢拒绝这个异象。据记载，一个理解了 hashmal（琥珀——「hashmal」是现代希伯来语中的「电」；「electricity」派生自希腊语的琥珀一词）的含义并轻率讨论的学生被闪电击毙（Haggada, 13.B）。因此，据《密西拿》记载，Ma'aseh Merkabah（「战车之工」）不可教给任何人，除非他不仅明智而且能通过自己的智慧（「灵知」）推导知识，且教学期间不得有其他人在场。「谁谈论前、后、上、下之事，还不如从未出生。」总的来说，人们认为最安全的做法是不碰战车之工，尤其因为有预言说「时机成熟时以西结将再次来临并为以色列开启战车之室。」（Cant. Rabbah, I, 4.）因此只有少数知名拉比教授这一密仪，且只教给他们最精选的学生；其中包括拉比约哈南·本·扎德凯、拉比约书亚（迦玛列治下的大议会副主席）、拉比阿基巴和拉比内胡尼亚。拉比泽拉说，即使是战车之工的章节标题也不可传授给非学院院长且性情不慎之人。拉比阿米说，这一教义只能托付给具备《以赛亚书》III, 3 所列全部五种品质的人：五十夫长、尊贵人、谋士、巧匠、善辩的演说家。人们逐渐相信阐述战车之工密仪会令耶和华显现。「拉比约哈南·本·扎德凯骑驴走在路上，他的学生以利亚撒·本·阿拉克跟在后面。以利亚撒说：『老师，请教我战车之工。』拉比约哈南拒绝了。以利亚撒又说：『我可以在您面前复述您已经教过我的一件事吗？』拉比约哈南同意了，但从驴上下来，裹上长袍，在一棵橄榄树下的石头上坐下。他声称在学生论述如此可怕的密仪、且舍金纳（「光辉」）和 Malache ha-Shareth（「侍候天使」）随行之际他骑驴是不合适的。以利亚撒立刻开始阐述，火从天降环绕他们和整片田野。天使们聚集来听，如同人之子聚集观看婚宴的庆典；笃耨香树中有歌声响起：「主啊，从地上赞美主，你们这些龙和一切深渊，果树和一切香柏树，赞美主！」一位天使从火中回答说：「这就是战车之工！」以利亚撒讲完后，拉比约哈南站起来亲吻他的额头。他说：「赞美亚伯拉罕、以撒和雅各的神，因为他赐予我们的祖先亚伯拉罕一个明智之子，知道如何论述我们天上之父的荣耀。」」

Rabbi Jose ha-Kohen and Rabbi Joshua had similar experiences. And once Rabbi Ben Azzai was sitting in meditation on the Scriptures when suddenly a flame encircled him. His pupils ran to Rabbi Akiba, who came up and said to Azzai: ‘Art thou studying the mysteries of the Merkabah?’ The mystery was not monopolized by the Jews. According to Macrobius, the oracle of Colophon, one of the twelve Ionian cities of Asia Minor, gave the nature of the transcendent God Iao as fourfold. In the Winter he was Hades, or Cronos; in the Spring, Zeus; in the Summer, Helios (the Sun); in the Autumn Iao, or Dionysus. This lore must have been part of the instruction, mentioned in Chapter Fifteen, that was given to Cyprian of Antioch on Mount Olympus by his seven mystagogues. Iao in the Orphic religion was also known as the four-eyed Phanes (from phaino, ‘I appear’) first-born of the Gods. In the Orphic fragment 63, he is described as having golden wings, and the heads of ram, bull, snake and lion. Bull’s heads were fastened to his side to denote his principal nature and he wore a great snake as a head-dress, which ‘resembled every sort of wild beast’.
拉比约西·哈科恩和拉比约书亚有类似经历。还有一次拉比本·阿扎伊正在冥想经文时，突然一团火焰包围了他。他的学生们跑去找拉比阿基巴，阿基巴过来对阿扎伊说：「你在研究战车之工的密仪吗？」这一密仪并非犹太人独占。据马克罗比乌斯记载，小亚细亚十二个爱奥尼亚城市之一科洛丰的神谕将超越神 Iao 的性质描述为四重。冬季他是哈得斯或克罗诺斯；春季是宙斯；夏季是赫利俄斯（太阳）；秋季是 Iao 或狄俄尼索斯。这些学说必然是第十五章提到的七位秘仪引导者在奥林匹斯山上给予安条克的居普良的教导的一部分。Iao 在俄耳甫斯教中也被称为四眼的法涅斯（源自 phaino，「我显现」）——诸神的长子。在俄耳甫斯残篇63中，他被描述为拥有金翼和公羊、公牛、蛇和狮子的头。公牛头被固定在他身体两侧以表示他的主要性质，他戴了一条大蛇作为头饰，「形似各种野兽」。

Here we can make a bold identification of the Cherub with the turning wheel that guards the Paradises of Celtic legend: for according to Genesis, III, 24, Cherubs were stationed at the East Gate of Eden. They were armed with ‘the whirling sword of Jehovah’ – the one with which (according to Isaiah, XXVII, 1) he killed the Dragon, as Marduk had killed Tiamat – to prevent anyone from entering. The paradise of Ezekiel’s tradition (Chapter XXXVIII, 13–16) is a well-watered garden at the base of a hill which heroes, such as the King of Tyre, occasionally visit. It glitters with precious stones and is a place of drum and pipe. We have seen that Gwion placed it in the valley of Hebron. The Seraphs, or ‘fiery serpents’, associated with the Cherubs in their guardian duties, are evidently another way of expressing the sacred spirals carved as a warning on the gate of the sacred enclosure; the Cherubs, because distinguished from them, are likely to have been swastikas, or fire-wheels.
这里我们可以大胆地将基路伯等同于守卫凯尔特传奇中乐园的旋转之轮：因为据《创世记》III, 24 记载，基路伯被驻守在伊甸园东门。他们配备了「耶和华的旋转火剑」——即他（据《以赛亚书》XXVII, 1）用来杀死龙的剑，如同马尔杜克杀死了提阿玛特——以阻止任何人进入。以西结传统中的乐园（第三十八章13-16节）是山脚下的一座水草丰美的花园，英雄如图尔王偶尔造访。它闪烁着宝石，是鼓和笛的地方。我们已看到格维恩将其置于希伯仑谷。与基路伯共同承担守护职责的撒拉弗——即「火蛇」——显然是另一种表达刻在神圣围场大门上作为警告的神圣螺旋的方式；基路伯因为与它们区分开来，可能是卍字或火轮。

The King of Tyre in Ezekiel’s account is easily recognized as the Canopic Hercules, originally an Aegean sun-hero, who became Semitized as Melkarth the chief god of Tyre. The islet off Tyre is thought to have been the chief station used by the Peoples of the Sea during the second millennium BC in their trade with Syria; as Pharos was in their trade with Egypt. Ezekiel, cognisant of the original closeness of the cults of Jehovah and Melkarth, declares that no further religious understanding is possible between Jerusalem and Tyre, as in the time of Solomon and Hiram. King Hiram of Tyre, like Solomon whom he equalled and even surpassed in wisdom, was a priest of Melkarth, and Jehovah now admits through the mouth of Ezekiel: ‘Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.’ However, he charges the present King of Tyre with having committed the sin of claiming to be a god, Melkarth as an Immortal, and the punishment for his presumption is death. This is an indirect warning to Ezekiel’s own King, Zedekiah of Judah, a descendant of Solomon, not to be seduced by the Tyrian into similarly presuming to be Jehovah. (Zedekiah did not listen to the warning and ‘the profane, wicked Prince’ died blind and in chains at Riblah, the capital of his Cushite foes. He was the last King of Judah.) So Ezekiel utters a lament for Melkarth that, like Adam, he has been ousted from the Paradise by the Cherub, despite his original holiness and wisdom, and must now be burned to ashes. This was, of course, no more than Melkarth’s destiny: in the Greek account he went to the apple-grove of the West – the Garden of the Hesperides – but had to obey the herald Copreus and return from its delights; and ended in ashes on Mount Oeta.
以西结记述中的图尔王很容易被认出是卡诺皮克的赫拉克勒斯——最初是一位爱琴太阳英雄，后闪米特化为梅尔卡什——图尔的主神。图尔附近的小岛被认为是公元前二千纪海上民族与叙利亚贸易时使用的主要站点；如同法罗斯是她们与埃及贸易时的站点。以西结知道耶和华与梅尔卡什崇拜最初密切的关系，宣称耶路撒冷和图尔之间不可能再有宗教理解，如同所罗门和希兰时代那样。图尔的希兰王如同所罗门——在智慧上与所罗门匹敌甚至超越——是梅尔卡什的祭司，而耶和华如今借以西结之口承认：「你圆满无缺，充满智慧，完美无瑕。」然而，他控告现任图尔王犯下了声称自己是神——梅尔卡什作为不朽者——的罪，对其傲慢的惩罚是死亡。这是对以西结自己的王——犹大的西底家，所罗门的后裔——的间接警告，不要被图尔人引诱而同样妄称耶和华。（西底家未听从警告，「这亵渎的恶王」在利比拉——他的古实敌人的首都——瞎眼戴着锁链死去。他是犹大最后的国王。）因此以西结为梅尔卡什发出哀叹——如同亚当一样，他被基路伯逐出乐园，尽管他原本的神圣和智慧，如今必须被烧成灰烬。这当然不过是梅尔卡什的命运：在希腊记载中他去了西方的苹果园——赫斯珀里得斯之园——但必须听从传令官科普柔斯之命离开其乐；最终在俄塔山的灰烬中终结。

The poetic connexion of the Cherub with the burning to death of Hercules-Melkarth is that the pyre was kindled by a Cherub, that is to say, by a whirling round of the swastika-shaped fire-wheel, attached to a drill. This method of making fire by the drilling of an oak-plank survived until the eighteenth century in the Scottish highlands, but only in the kindling of the Beltane need-fire, to which miraculous virtue was ascribed. Hawthorn, the wood of chastity, was often used for the drilling. Sir James Frazer describes the need-fire ceremony at length in The Golden Bough and shows that it originally culminated in the sacrifice of a man representing the Oak-god. In some Scottish parishes the victim was even called ‘Baal’, which was Melkarth’s usual title.
基路伯与赫拉克勒斯-梅尔卡什被烧死之间的诗性联系在于：柴堆是由基路伯点燃的，即由一个卍字形火轮的旋转——附在钻上——所点燃。这种通过钻木取火（橡木板）的方法在苏格兰高地一直存续到十八世纪，但仅用于点燃五朔节的救命火——人们赋予其奇迹般的力量。山楂木——贞洁之木——常被用于钻木。詹姆斯·弗雷泽爵士在《金枝》中详细描述了救命火仪式，并表明它最初以代表橡树之神的人为牺牲而达到高潮。在苏格兰一些教区，牺牲者甚至被称为「巴力」——这是梅尔卡什的常用称号。

So we see that Ezekiel is a master of ambivalent statement. He has made the fate of Hercules a symbol of the approaching destruction of Tyre by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon; in punishment for the vice of pride which since the city rose to commercial prosperity (‘the multitude of thy merchandize, the iniquity of thy traffic’) has corrupted its rulers.
