This fourfold blessing, which was certainly not composed earlier than the time of Ezekiel, is explained in the last verse of the chapter as a formula embodying the Tetragrammaton:
这一四重祝福——其编撰时间肯定不早于以西结时代——在该章最后一节中被解释为体现四字神名的公式：

And they [Aaron and his sons] shall put my Name upon the Children of Israel, and I shall bless them.
And they [Aaron and his sons] shall put my Name upon the Children of Israel, and I shall bless them.（他们〔亚伦和他的儿子们〕要将我的名放在以色列人身上，我要赐福给他们。）





The first two blessings are really one, together representing the Third Person, Life and the Brightness, J H; the third blessing represents the First person, Light, H; the fourth blessing represents the Second Person, Peace, W. This Trinity is one indivisible God, because if a single letter is omitted the Name loses its power, and because the three concepts are interdependent. The Second Person is ‘begotten by the Father before all the world’ in the sense that ‘the World’ is a false Creation which he preceded. This interpretation of J H W H as ‘Light and the Glory, Life and Peace’ further explains why the priests sometimes enlarged it to 42 letters. In the Pythagorean system, 7, written as H aspirate, was the numeral of Light and 6, written as Digamma F (W in Hebrew), was that of Life. But 6 also stood for the Glory, and 7 for Peace as the seventh day of the week; so six times seven, namely 42, expressed Light, the Glory and Peace multiplied by Life. Though the Jews used the Phoenician notation of numeral letters for public purposes, it is likely that they used the early Greek in their mysteries, just as they used the Greek ‘Boibalos’ calendar-alphabet.
前两福实为一福，共同代表第三位——生命与荣耀，J H；第三福代表第一位——光，H；第四福代表第二位——和平，W。这三一是一个不可分割的神，因为若遗漏任何一个字母，名字便失去力量，且三个概念相互依存。第二位「在创世之前由父所生」，意即「世界」是一个他所先于的虚假创世。将 JHWH 解释为「光与荣耀、生命与和平」进一步解释了为何祭司有时将其扩展为 42 个字母。在毕达哥拉斯体系中，7（写作送气 H）是光的数字，6（写作双伽马 F，即希伯来语中的 W）是生命的数字。但 6 也代表荣耀，7 也代表和平即一周的第七日；因此六乘七即 42，表达的是光、荣耀与和平乘以生命。虽然犹太人公开使用腓尼基的字母数字记法，但很可能在密仪中使用早期希腊记法，正如他们使用希腊语「Boibalos」日历字母表。

The Menorah symbolized the fullness of Jehovah’s Creation, yet it did not contain the first of the four letters of the Tetragrammaton; and its lights recalled his seven-letter Name, but not the eight-letter one. However, at the Feast of Illumination, or ‘The Feast of Lights’, (mentioned in John, X, 22 and Josephus’s Antiquities, XII, 7.7), the ancient Hebrew Winter Solstice Feast, an eight-branched candlestick was used, as it still is in Jewish synagogues, known as the Chanukah candlestick. The rabbinical account is that this eight-day festival which begins on the twenty-fifth day of the month Kislev, was instituted by Judas Maccabeus and that it celebrates a miracle: at the Maccabean consecration of the Temple a small cruse of sacred oil was found, hidden by a former High Priest, which lasted for eight days. By this legend the authors of the Talmud hoped to conceal the antiquity of the feast, which was originally Jehovah’s birthday as the Sun-god and had been celebrated at least as early as the time of Nehemiah (II Maccabees, I, 18). Antiochus Epiphanes had sacrificed to Olympian Zeus, three years before Judas’s re-institution of the festival, at the same place and on the same day: Zeus’s birthday fell at the winter solstice too – as did that of Mithras the Persian Sun-god whose cult had greatly impressed the Jews in the time of their protector Cyrus. According to rabbinical custom one light of the candlestick was kindled each day of the festival until all eight were alight; the earlier tradition had been to begin with eight lights and extinguish one each day until all were out.
七灯台象征耶和华创世的全备，但它不包含四字神名的第一个字母；它的灯光让人想起他的七字母名，而非八字母名。然而，在光明节即「灯节」（见于《约翰福音》X, 22 和约瑟夫《犹太古事记》XII, 7.7）——古老的希伯来冬至节——中，使用的是一座八枝烛台，如今天犹太会堂中仍然如此，称为修殿节烛台。拉比的说法是，这个从基斯流月二十五日开始的八日节期由犹大·马加比设立，庆祝一个奇迹：马加比献殿时发现了一小瓶由前任大祭司藏匿的圣油，足够燃烧八天。通过这一传说，《塔木德》的作者希望掩盖此节的古老性——它最初是耶和华作为太阳神的生日，至少早在尼希米时代就已庆祝（《马加比二书》I, 18）。安条克四世在犹大重新设立此节前三年，于同一地点同一天向奥林匹斯宙斯献祭：宙斯的生日也在冬至——波斯太阳神密特拉的生日也是如此，密特拉崇拜在居鲁士保护犹太人时期对犹太人影响极大。按拉比习俗，烛台的灯每天点燃一盏，直到八盏全亮；更早的传统是从八盏开始，每天熄灭一盏，直到全灭。

In the Chanukah candlestick which, among the Moroccan Jews (whose tradition is the oldest and purest) is surmounted by a small pomegranate, the eight lights are set in a row, each on a separate branch, as in the Menorah; and an arm projects from the pedestal with a separate light in its socket from which all the rest are kindled. The eighth light in the row must stand for the extra day of the year, the day of the letter J, which is intercalated at the winter solstice: for the pomegranate, the emblem not only of the seventh day of the week but of the planet Ninib, ruler of the winter solstice, shows that this candlestick is a Menorah enlarged to contain all the letters of the Tetragrammaton, that it is, in fact, the ‘Eightfold City of Light’ in which the Word dwelt. The number Eight, the Sungod’s number of increase, recalled Jehovah’s creative order to increase and multiply; and the eight lights could further be understood (it will be shown) as symbolizing the eight essential Commandments.
在修殿节烛台中——摩洛哥犹太人（其传统最为古老纯粹）的烛台顶部有一个小石榴——八盏灯排成一行，每盏在独立的枝上，如七灯台一样；另有一臂从底座伸出，其插座中有一盏独立的灯，用于点燃其余所有灯。排中的第八盏灯必定代表年的额外日，即字母 J 之日，在冬至时插入：因为石榴——不仅是每周第七日的象征，也是冬至主宰行星尼尼伯的象征——表明这座烛台是一座扩展的七灯台，包含四字神名的所有字母，实际上就是「光之八重城」，道寓其中。数字八，太阳神的增长之数，让人想起耶和华「生养众多」的创世命令；八盏灯还可被理解为（将如下所示）象征八条核心诫命。

The Chanukah candlestick was the only one ritually used in the synagogues of the Dispersion, because of the Sanhedrin law forbidding the reproduction of the Menorah or of any other object housed in the Holy of Holies. This law was designed to prevent the foundation of a rival Temple to that of Jerusalem, but aimed also, it seems, at the Ophites, who justified their heretical religious views by the centrality of the fourth light (that of the Wise Serpent Nabu) in the seven-branched candlestick; they would find no central light in this one. The separate light probably stood for the oneness of Jehovah as contrasted with the diversity of his works and brought the total number of lights up to nine, symbolizing the thrice-holy Trinity. The meaning of the pomegranate at the top has been forgotten by the Moroccan Jews, who regard it as a mere decoration though agreeing that it is of high antiquity; Central European Jews have substituted for it a knob surmounted by a Star of David. Among the Moroccan Jews a pomegranate is also placed on the sticks around which the sacred scroll of the Torah is wound, the sticks being called Es Chajim, ‘the tree of life’; Central European Jews have reduced this pomegranate to the crown formed by its withered calyx. The common-sense Rabbinical explanation of the sanctity of the pomegranate is that it is the only fruit which worms do not corrupt.
修殿节烛台是散居会堂中唯一被仪式使用的烛台，因为公会法律禁止复制七灯台或至圣所中的任何其他器物。这一法律旨在防止建立与耶路撒冷圣殿竞争的圣殿，但似乎也针对蛇派——他们以七枝烛台中第四盏灯（智慧之蛇纳布的灯）的中心地位来为其异端宗教观点辩护；在这座烛台中他们找不到中心灯。那盏独立的灯可能代表耶和华的唯一性，与其作品的多样性形成对比，并将灯的总数提升至九，象征三重圣洁的三一。石榴在顶部的含义已被摩洛哥犹太人遗忘，他们将其视为纯粹的装饰，尽管同意它具有高度古旧性；中欧犹太人用一个大卫之星顶替的圆球代替了它。在摩洛哥犹太人中，石榴也放在托拉圣卷缠绕的杖的顶端，这些杖称为 Es Chajim，即「生命之树」；中欧犹太人将这个石榴缩减为其干枯花萼形成的冠。拉比对石榴神圣性的常识解释是：它是唯一不被虫蛀的水果。

The Ten Commandments, which are among the latest additions to the Pentateuch, are designed as glosses on the same mystery. The oddness of their choice seems to have struck Jesus when he quoted the ‘Love thy God’ and ‘Love thy neighbour’ commandments, from elsewhere in the Pentateuch, as transcending them in spiritual value. But it is a more carefully considered choice than appears at first sight. The Commandments, which are really eight, not ten, to match the numbers of letters in the Name, fall into two groups: one of three ‘Thou shalts’ concerned with the True Creation, and the other of five ‘Thou shalt nots’ concerned with the False Creation: each group is prefaced by a warning. The order is purposely ‘pied’, as one would expect.

This mystical god differed not only from the Babylonian Bel or Marduk but from Ormazd, the Supreme God of the Persian Zoroastrians, with whom some Jewish syncretists identified him, in having separated himself from the erroneous material universe to live securely cloistered in his abstract city of light. Ormazd was a sort of three-bodied Geryon, the usual Aryan male trinity that first married the Triple Goddess, then dispossessed her and went about clothed in her three colours – white, red and dark blue, like the heifer calf in Suidas’s riddle, performing her ancient functions. Thus Ormazd appeared in priestly white to create (or recreate) the world; in warrior red to combat evil; in husbandman’s dark blue to ‘bring forth fecundity’.
这位神秘的神不仅不同于巴比伦的贝尔或马尔杜克，也不同于波斯琐罗亚斯德教的至高神奥尔穆兹德——一些犹太混合主义者将他与奥尔穆兹德等同——其区别在于他已将自己从错误的物质宇宙中分离出来，安全地隐居于他的抽象光之城。奥尔穆兹德是一种三体革律翁，即通常的雅利安男性三联神——先娶三联女神，继而夺其位，穿着她的三色——白、红、深蓝，如苏伊达斯谜语中的牝犊，履行她古老的职能。因此奥尔穆兹德以祭司白出现以创造（或再造）世界；以战士红出现以对抗邪恶；以农人深蓝出现以「带来丰祚」。

The pre-Christian Jewish apocalyptics, probably influenced by religious theory brought from India, along with the ethrog, by Jewish merchants, expected the birth of a divine child: the Child, prophesied by the Sibyl, who would free the world from sin. This implied that Michael and the archangels to whom the new Idealistic God had delegated the immediate care of mankind had proved no match for the World, Flesh and Devil – the grosser powers which he had repudiated. The only solution was for the Prince of Peace, namely the Second Person, the Son of Man, who had hitherto had no independent existence,1 to become incarnate as perfect man – the human Messiah born of Judah, Benjamin and Levi. By exposing the vanity of the material Creation he would bring all Israel to repentance and thus initiate the deathless millennary kingdom of God on earth, to which the Gentile nations would ultimately be admitted. This was the faith of Jesus, who was of Judah, Benjamin and Levi and had been ritually rebegotten by God at his Coronation: he expected the actual historical appearance of the Son of Man on the Mount of Olives to follow his own prophesied death by the sword, and assured his disciples that many then living would never die but enter directly into the kingdom of God. The prophecy was not fulfilled because it was founded on a confusion between poetic myth and historical event, and everyone’s hopes of the millennium were dashed.
基督教之前的犹太启示录者——可能受到随同香橼一起由犹太商人从印度带来的宗教理论的影响——期待一位圣童的诞生：西彼拉预言的那位将使世界从罪恶中解脱的圣童。这意味着新的唯心之神所委派直接照管人类的天使长米迦勒等人不是世界、肉体和魔鬼——他所摈弃的粗鄙力量——的对手。唯一的解决办法是让和平之君即第二位、人子——此前没有独立存在¹——成为完美之人即人化肉身——由犹大、便雅悯和利未而生的人间弥赛亚。通过揭露物质创世的虚妄，他将使全以色列悔改，从而在地上开启上帝不死千年王国，外邦民族最终也将被接纳。这是那稣的信仰——他出身犹大、便雅悯和利未，在加冕礼上被上帝仪式性地重生：他预期人子在橄榄山的实际历史显现将紧随他自己预言中的死于刀剑之后，并向门徒保证当时许多活着的人将永不死去，而是直接进入上帝之国。这一预言未能实现，因为它基于诗性神话与历史事件的混淆，每个人对千年的希望都破灭了。

The Grecians then claimed that those hopes had not after all been premature, that Jesus had indeed been the Second Person of the Trinity, and that the Kingdom of God was at hand, the dreadful signs which would portend its coming, the so-called Pangs of the Messiah, being apparent to everyone. But when the Gentile Church had wholly separated itself from the Judaistic Church and Jesus as King of Israel was an embarrassing concept to Christians who wished to escape all suspicion of being Jewish nationalists, it was decided that he had been born as the Second Person not at his coronation but at his physical birth; though spiritually begotten before all the world. This made Mary the Mother of Jesus into the immaculate human receptacle of the Life and Brightness of God, the Third Person of the Trinity; so that it had to be presumed that she was herself immaculately conceived by her mother St. Ann. Here was a fine breeding-ground for all sorts of heresy, and soon we return in our argument to the point where the Theme reasserted itself popularly with the Virgin as the White Goddess, Jesus as the Waxing Sun, the Devil as the Waning Sun. There was no room here for the Father God, except as a mystical adjunct of Jesus (‘I and the Father are One’).
希腊派随后声称那些希望终究不是过早的，那稣确实是三一之第二位，上帝之国即将来临，预示其到来的可畏迹象即所谓的弥赛亚之痛已为所有人所见。但当外邦教会完全脱离犹太教会，且作为以色列王的那稣对希望摆脱一切犹太民族主义者嫌疑的基督徒而言是一个尴尬概念时，他们决定他不是在加冕礼上而是在肉身出生时作为第二位诞生；尽管在灵性上在创世之前受生。这使得马利亚作为那稣之母成为上帝生命与荣耀即三一第三位的无玷人间受体；因此必须推定她本人由其母亲圣安娜无玷受孕。这成了各种异端的温床，很快我们的论证回到了诗性主题以流行方式重新抬头之处：童贞女作为白女神，那稣作为上弦日，魔鬼作为下弦日。这里没有父神的位置，除了作为那稣的神秘附属（「我与父原为一」）。

1 There are only a few recorded references in English Literature to a male Muse, and most of these occur in poems written by homosexuals and belong to morbid pathology. However, George Sandys in A Relation of a Journey Begun (1615), calls James I a ‘Crowned Muse’ perhaps because James behaved more like a Queen than a King towards his favourites at Court and because he published an elementary treatise on versification. And Milton writes in Lycidas:
¹ 在英语文学中只有少数几处记录提到男性缪斯，其中大部分出现在同性恋者所写的诗中，属于病态病理学。然而乔治·桑迪斯在《旅行记》（1615）中称詹姆斯一世为「加冕的缪斯」，也许因为詹姆斯在宫廷中对其宠臣的表现更像女王而非国王，且他出版了一部基础的格律论著。弥尔顿在《利西达斯》中写道：



1 Vulcan is another example of a god who ‘went the way of all flesh’ before his final extinction. The last addition to the Vulcan legend was made by Apuleius in The Golden Ass where Vulcan cooks the wedding breakfast for Cupid and Psyche.
¹ 伏尔甘是另一位「走了一切血肉之路」然后最终消亡的神。伏尔甘传说的最后一次增补由阿普列乌斯在《金驴记》中完成，其中伏尔甘为丘比特和普赛克准备婚宴。



1 Gordium was in Eastern Phrygia, and according to local tradition whoever untied the knot would become master of Asia. Alexander, who had not the learning, patience or ingenuity to perform the task decently, used his sword. It was a raw-hide knot on the ox-yoke which had belonged to a Phrygian peasant named Gordius, and Gordius had been divinely marked out for royalty when an eagle settled on the yoke; by marriage with the priestess of Telmissus he became a petty king and presently extended his dominion over all Phrygia. When he built the fortress of Gordium he dedicated the yoke to King Zeus, it is said, and laid it up in the citadel. Gordium commanded the main trade route across Asia Minor from the Bosphorus to Antioch, so that the manifest meaning of the prophecy was that nobody could rule Asia Minor who did not hold Gordium; and it was from Gordium that Alexander began his second Eastern campaign which culminated in the defeat of Darius at Issus. Now, Gordius was the father of Midas, who has already been mentioned as a devotee of the Orphic Dionysus, so the yoke must originally have been dedicated to King Dionysus, not to Father Zeus. And the secret of the knot must have been a religious one, for another widespread early means of recording messages, besides notching sticks and scratching letters on clay, was to tie knots in string or strips of raw-hide. The Gordian knot, in fact, should have been ‘untied’ by reading the message it contained, which was perhaps a divine name of Dionysus, the one contained in the vowels of the Beth-Luis-Nion. By cutting the knot Alexander ended an ancient religious dispensation, and since his act seemed to go unpunished – for he afterwards conquered the whole East as far as the Indus valley – it became a precedent for rating military power above religion or learning; just as the sword of Brennus the Gaul, thrown into the scales that measured out the agreed tribute of Roman gold, provided a precedent for rating military power above justice or honour.
¹ 戈尔迪乌姆位于东弗里吉亚，据当地传统，能解开此结的人将成为亚洲之主。亚历山大没有学问、耐心或技巧来完成这一任务，便用了他的剑。那是一个生牛皮结，在一辆牛轭上，属于一个名叫戈尔迪乌斯的弗里吉亚农民；当一只鹰落在轭上时，戈尔迪乌斯被神标记为王；通过与特尔弥苏斯的女祭司结婚，他成为小国之王，不久将其统治扩展到整个弗里吉亚。当他建造戈尔迪乌姆要塞时，据说他将牛轭献给了王神宙斯，并将其存放在卫城中。戈尔迪乌姆控制着从博斯普鲁斯到安条克的跨小亚细亚主要贸易路线，因此这一预言的明显含义是：不占据戈尔迪乌姆便不能统治小亚细亚；亚历山大正是从戈尔迪乌姆开始了他的第二次东方战役，最终在伊苏斯击败大流士。戈尔迪乌斯是迈达斯的父亲，后者已作为俄耳甫斯狄俄尼索斯的信徒被提及，因此牛轭最初必定是献给王神狄俄尼索斯而非父神宙斯的。此结的秘密必定是宗教性的，因为除了在棍上刻痕和在粘土上划字母外，另一种早期广泛使用的记录信息的方法是在绳子或生牛皮条上打结。事实上，戈尔迪乌斯之结本应通过解读其所含信息来「解开」——那也许是狄俄尼索斯的一个神名，即贝斯-路易斯-尼恩字母表元音中所含的那个。亚历山大斩断此结结束了古代宗教秩序，由于他的行为似乎未受惩罚——因为他之后征服了整个东方直到印度河流域——它成了将军事权力凌驾于宗教或学问之上的先例；正如高卢人布伦努斯将剑掷入衡量约定罗马黄金贡赋的天平中，成了将军事权力凌驾于正义或荣誉之上的先例。



1 In the Babylonian Epic it was Ishtar, not any male God, who caused the Deluge. Gilgamesh (Noah) stocked an ark with beasts of every kind and gave a New Year’s feast to the builders with great outpouring of new wine; the New Year’s Feast being an autumnal one. The myth seems to be iconotropic, for the account of the great wine-drinking, which appears in the Genesis version as a moral story of Noah’s drunkenness and the bad behaviour of his son Canaan (Ham), recalls the myth of the wine-god Dionysus. When captured by Tyrrhenian pirates, Dionysus changed the masts of their ship into serpents, himself into a lion and the sailors into dolphins, and wreathed everything with ivy. The original Asianic icon from which both myths are presumably derived must have shown the god in a moon-ship at the Vintage Feast, going through his habitual New Year changes – bull, lion, snake and so on – which gave rise to the Babylonian story of the cargo of animals. The pirates’ ship is probably described as Tyrrhenian because it had a figure-head in the shape of a Telchin, or dog with fins for feet, an attendant of the Moon-goddess.
¹ 在巴比伦史诗中，引发洪水的不是任何男性神，而是伊什塔尔。吉尔伽美什（诺亚）在方舟中装载了各种野兽，并向建造者大摔新酒地举行新年宴；新年宴是秋季的。这个神话似乎是误释性的，因为大量饮酒的记载——在《创世记》版本中作为诺亚醉酒和其子迦南（含）恶行的道德故事出现——让人想起酒神狄俄尼索斯的神话。当被第勒尼安海盗捕获时，狄俄尼索斯将船桅变为蛇，自己变为狮子，水手变为海豚，并用常春藤缠绕一切。两个神话大概都源于的原始亚细亚图像，必定展示了神在采摘节的月船中经历他惯常的新年变化——牝牛、雄狮、蛇等——这产生了巴比伦故事中装载动物的情节。海盗船被描述为第勒尼安的，大概是因为它有一个忒尔钦形状的船首像——一种足有鳍的犬，月女神的随从。



1 This was denounced as the Beryllian heresy at Bostia in AD 244.
¹ 这一观点于公元244年在博斯提亚被谴责为贝里利安异端。





Chapter Twenty-Six

title: 第二十六章
content:
RETURN OF THE GODDESS





What, then, is to be the future of religion in the West? Sir James Frazer attributed the defects of European civilization to ‘the selfish and immoral doctrine of Oriental religions which inculcated the communion of the soul with God, and its eternal salvation, as the only objects worth living for’. This, he argued, undermined the unselfish ideal of Greek and Roman society which subordinated the individual to the welfare of the State. Adolf Hitler said later, more succinctly: ‘The Jews are to blame for all our troubles.’ Both statements, however, were historically untrue.
那么，西方宗教的未来将如何？詹姆斯·弗雷泽爵士将欧洲文明的缺陷归咎于「东方宗教的自私和不道德的教义，它们灌输灵魂与上帝的合一及其永恒救赎为唯一值得为之而活的目标」。他论证说，这破坏了将个人从属于国家福祉的希腊和罗马社会的无私理想。阿道夫·希特勒后来更简洁地说：「犹太人要为我们所有的麻烦负责。」然而两种说法在历史上都不真实。

Frazer, an authority on Greek religion, must have known that the Salvationist obsession of the Greek Orphics was Thraco-Libyan, not Oriental, and that long before the Jews of the Dispersal had introduced to the Greek world their Pharisaic doctrine of oneness with God, city-state idealism had been destroyed from within. Once speculative philosophy had made sceptics of all educated Greeks who were not Orphics or members of some other mystical fraternity, public as well as private faith was undermined and, despite the prodigious conquests of Alexander, Greece was easily defeated by the semi-barbarous Romans, who combined religious conservatism with national esprit de corps. The Roman nobles then put themselves to school under the Greeks, and caught the philosophical infection; their own idealism crumbled and only the regimental esprit de corps of the untutored legions, combined with Emperor-worship on the Oriental model, staved off political collapse. Finally, in the fourth century AD, they found the pressure of the barbarians against their frontiers so strong that it was only by recourse to the still vigorous faith of Christianity that they could save what remained of the Empire.
弗雷泽是希腊宗教权威，他一定知道希腊俄耳甫斯教徒的救赎执念是色雷斯-利比亚的，而非东方的；而且在散居犹太人向希腊世界引入其法利赛式的与上帝合一教义之前很久，城邦理想主义已从内部被摧毁。一旦思辨哲学使所有非俄耳甫斯教徒或非其他神秘兄弟会成员的受过教育的希腊人成为怀疑论者，公共和私人信仰均被动摇，尽管亚历山大取得了惊人的征服，希腊还是轻易被半野蛮的罗马人击败——后者将宗教保守主义与民族团队精神结合在一起。罗马贵族随后向希腊人学习，染上了哲学感染；他们自身的理想主义崩塌，只有未受教育的军团的团队精神，加上东方模式的皇帝崇拜，才推迟了政治崩溃。最终在公元四世纪，他们发现蛮族对边境的压力如此强大，以至于只有求助于仍然旺盛的基督教信仰才能拯救帝国剩余的部分。

Hitler’s remark, which was not original, referred to the alleged economic oppression of Europe by the Jews. He was being unfair: under Christianity the Jews had for centuries been forbidden to hold land or become members of ordinary craft-guilds, and obliged to live on their wits. They became jewellers, physicians, money-lenders and bankers, and started such new, highly skilled industries as the manufacture of optical glass and drugs; England’s sudden commercial expansion in the seventeenth century was caused by Cromwell’s welcome to the Dutch Jews, who brought their modern banking-system to London. If Europeans dislike the results of unlimited capitalism and industrial progress, they have only themselves to blame: the Jews originally invoked the power of money as a bulwark against Gentile oppression. They were forbidden by the Mosaic Law either to lend money at interest among themselves or to let loans run on indefinitely – every seventh year the debtor had to be released from his bond – and it is not their fault that money, ceasing to be a practical means of exchanging goods and services, has achieved irresponsible divinity in the Gentile world.
希特勒的话——并非原创——指的是所谓犹太人对欧洲的经济压迫。他不够公正：在基督教统治下，犹太人数百年来被禁止拥有土地或成为普通手工业行会的成员，被迫以智慧谋生。他们成为珠宝商、医生、放贷者和银行家，并开创了光学玻璃和药品制造等新的高技能产业；英国十七世纪突然的商业扩张源于克伦威尔欢迎荷兰犹太人，他们将现代银行系统带到了伦敦。如果欧洲人不喜欢无限资本主义和工业进步的后果，他们只能怪自己：犹太人最初是作为抵御外邦人压迫的屏障才唤起金钱的力量。摩西律法禁止他们在自己人中放贷取息，也禁止贷款无限期延续——每第七年债务人必须被解除债务——金钱不再是交换商品和服务的实际手段，而在外邦人世界中获得了不负责任的神格，这不是他们的过错。

Yet neither Fraser nor Hitler were far from the truth, which was that the early Gentile Christian borrowed from the Hebrew prophets the two religious concepts, hitherto unknown in the West, which have become the prime causes of our unrest: that of a patriarchal God, who refuses to have any truck with Goddesses and claims to be self-sufficient and all-wise; and that of a theocratic society, disdainful of the pomps and glories of the world, in which everyone who rightly performs his civic duties is a ‘son of God’ and entitled to salvation, whatever his rank or fortune, by virtue of direct communion with the Father.
然而弗雷泽和希特勒都离真相不远，真相是：早期外邦基督徒从希伯来先知那里借来了两个此前在西方不为人知的宗教概念，它们已成为我们动荡的首要原因：一是父权神的概念，他拒绝与任何女神打交道，自称自足且全知；二是神权社会的概念，藐视世俗的浮华与荣耀，其中每个正确履行公民义务的人都是「上帝之子」，无论其地位或财富如何，都因与父神的直接交流而有权获得救赎。

Both these concepts have since been vigorously contested within the Church itself. However deeply Westerners may admire Jesus’s single-minded devotion to the remote, all-holy, Universal God of the Hebrew prophets, few of them have ever accepted whole-heartedly the antagonism between flesh and spirit implied in his cult. And though the new God-head seemed philosophically incontrovertible, once the warlike and petulant Zeus-Jupiter, with his indiscreet amours and quarrelsome Olympian family, had ceased to command the respect of intelligent people, the early Church Fathers soon found that man was not yet ready for ideal anarchy: the All-Father, a purely meditative patriarch who did not intervene personally in mundane affairs, had to resume his thunderbolt in order to command respect. Even the communistic principle, for a breach of which Ananias and Sapphira had been struck dead, was abandoned as unpractical. As soon as the Papal power was acknowledged superior to that of kings, the Popes assumed magnificent temporal pomp, took part in power-politics, waged wars, rewarded the rich and well-born with indulgences for sin in this world and promises of preferential treatment in the next, and anathematized the equalitarian principles of their simple predecessors. And not only has Hebrew monotheism been modified at Rome by the gradual introduction of Virgin-worship, but the ordinary Catholic layman has long been cut off from direct communication with God: he must confess his sins and acquaint himself with the meaning of God’s word, only through the mediation of a priest.
这两个概念此后在教会内部受到激烈的质疑。无论西方人多么钦佩那稣对希伯来先知的遥远、全圣、万有之神的专注奉献，他们中很少有人全心全意接受其崇拜中所暗示的肉与灵的对立。虽然新的神格在哲学上似乎无可辩驳——一旦好战而易怒的宙斯-朱庇特以其不检点的风流和好斗的奥林匹斯家族不再能赢得智者的尊重——早期教父很快发现人类尚未准备好迎接理想的无政府状态：万有之父，一位纯粹冥想的族长，不亲自干预世俗事务，不得不重新拿起雷锤以赢得尊重。甚至共产主义原则——亚拿尼亚和撒非拉因违反此原则而被击毙——也作为不切实际而被放弃。一旦教皇权力被承认高于国王，教皇们便承担起辉煌的世俗排场，参与权力政治，发动战争，以今世的赎罪券和来世的优待承诺奖赏富人和贵胄，并诅咒其朴素前辈的平等主义原则。不仅希伯来一神教在罗马因逐渐引入童贞女崇拜而被修正，而且普通天主教平信徒早已被切断与上帝的直接交流：他必须通过祭司的中介才能认罪和了解上帝之言的含义。

Protestantism was a vigorous reassertion of the two rejected concepts, which the Jews themselves had never abandoned, and to which the Mohammedans had been almost equally faithful. The Civil Wars in England were won by the fighting qualities of the Virgin-hating Puritan Independents, who envisaged an ideal theocratic society in which all priestly and episcopal pomp should be abolished, and every man should be entitled to read and interpret the Scriptures as he pleased, with direct access to God the Father. Puritanism took root and flourished in America, and the doctrine of religious equalitarianism, which carried with it the right to independent thinking, turned into social equalitarianism, or democracy, a theory which has since dominated Western civilization. We are now at the stage where the common people of Christendom, spurred on by their demagogues, have grown so proud that they are no longer content to be the hands and feet and trunk of the body politic, but demand to be the intellect as well – or, as much intellect as is needed to satisfy their simple appetites. As a result, all but a very few have discarded their religious idealism, Roman Catholics as well as Protestants, and come to the private conclusion that money, though the root of all evil, is the sole practical means of expressing value or of determining social precedence; that science is the only accurate means of describing phenomena; and that a morality of common honesty is not relevant either to love, war, business or politics. Yet they feel guilty about their backsliding, send their children to Sunday School, maintain the Churches, and look with alarm towards the East, where a younger and more fanatic faith threatens.
新教是对这两个被拒绝的概念的强烈重申——犹太人自己从未放弃这些概念，穆罕默德教徒也几乎同样忠诚。英国内战由仇恨童贞女的清教独立派的战斗品质赢得，他们设想一个理想的theocratic社会，其中一切祭司和主教排场都应废除，每个人都有权随心阅读和诠释经文，直接接触父神。清教主义在美国扎根繁荣，宗教平等主义教义——附带独立思考的权利——转变为社会平等主义即民主，这一理论此后主导了西方文明。我们现在处于这样一个阶段：基督教世界的平民在其煽动者的驱使下变得如此骄傲，不再满足于做政治体的手脚和躯干，而要求也做大脑——或者说，满足其简单食欲所需的那点大脑。结果是，除了极少数人外，所有人都抛弃了他们的宗教理想主义，无论天主教徒还是新教徒，私下得出结论：金钱虽然是一切恶的根源，却是表达价值或确定社会地位的唯一实际手段；科学是描述现象的唯一准确手段；诚实信用道德与爱情、战争、商业或政治无关。然而他们对自己的堕落感到内疚，送孩子上主日学，维持教会，并惊恐地望向东方——那里一个更年轻、更狂热的信仰正在威胁。

What ails Christianity today is that it is not a religion squarely based on a single myth; it is a complex of juridical decisions made under political pressure in an ancient law-suit about religious rights between adherents of the Mother-goddess who was once supreme in the West, and those of the usurping Father-god. Different ecclesiastical courts have given different decisions, and there is no longer a supreme judicature. Now that even the Jews have been seduced into evading the Mosaic Law and whoring after false gods, the Christians have drifted farther away than ever from the ascetic holiness to which Ezekiel, his Essene successors, and Jesus, the last of the Hebrew prophets, hoped to draw the world. Though the West is still nominally Christian, we have come to be governed, in practice, by the unholy triumdivate of Pluto god of wealth, Apollo god of science, and Mercury god of thieves. To make matters worse, dissension and jealousy rage openly between these three, with Mercury and Pluto blackguarding each other, while Apollo wields the atomic bomb as if it were a thunderbolt; for since the Age of Reason was heralded by his eighteenth-century philosophers, he has seated himself on the vacant throne of Zeus (temporarily indisposed) as Triumdival Regent.
基督教今天的问题是它并非稳固地建立在单一神话之上的宗教；它是一个由政治压力下在一场古老诉讼中做出的司法判决的复合体——那场诉讼是关于曾经至高无上的母神与篡位的父神之间宗教权利的争端。不同的教会法庭给出了不同的判决，不再有最高司法机构。如今连犹太人也被引诱着规避摩西律法、追从假神，基督徒比以往任何时候都更远离以西结及其艾赛尼继承者和最后一位希伯来先知那稣希望将世界引向的禁欲圣洁。虽然西方名义上仍是基督教的，但实际上我们已由不神圣的三执政统治：冥王普路同即财富之神、阿波罗即科学之神、墨丘利即盗贼之神。更糟糕的是，这三位之间公然爆发了纷争和嫉妒，墨丘利和普路同互相谩骂，而阿波罗挥舞原子弹仿佛那是雷锤；因为自理性时代由他十八世纪的哲学家宣告以来，他已坐在空出的宙斯宝座上（宙斯暂时告假）担任三执政摄政。

The propaganda services of the West perpetually announce that the only way out of our present troubles is a return to religion, but assume that religion ought not to be defined in any precise sense: that no good can come from publicizing either the contradictions between the main revealed religions and their mutually hostile sects, or the factual mis-statements contained in their doctrines, or the shameful actions which they have all, at one time or another, been used to cloak. What is really being urged is an improvement in national and international ethics, not everyone’s sudden return to the beliefs of his childhood – which, if undertaken with true religious enthusiasm, would obviously lead to a renewal of religious wars: only since belief weakened all round have the priests of rival religions consented to adopt a good-neighbourly policy. Then why not say ethics, since it is apparent that the writers and speakers, with few exceptions, have no strong religious convictions themselves? Because ethics are held to derive from revealed religion, notably the Ten Commandments, and therefore the seemingly unethical behaviour of communists is attributed to their total repudiation of religion; and because the co-existence of contradictory confessions within a State is held by non-communists to be a proof of political health; and because a crusade against Communism can be launched only in the name of religion.
西方的宣传机构不断宣布摆脱当前困境的唯一出路是回归宗教，但假定宗教不应以任何精确意义来定义：公开主要启示宗教之间的矛盾及其互相敌对的教派、其教义中包含的事实性错误陈述、以及它们都曾在某个时期被用来掩盖的可耻行为，都不会带来好处。真正被敦促的是改善国家和国际伦理，而非每个人突然回归童年信仰——如果以真正的宗教热忱来做，显然会导致宗教战争的重新爆发：只有各方信仰普遍减弱之后，对立宗教的祭司们才同意采取睦邻政策。那为什么不直说伦理，因为显然写作者和演讲者中除了极少数例外自己并没有强烈的宗教信念？因为伦理被认为源自启示宗教，尤其是十诫，因此共产主义者看似不道德的行为被归因于他们对宗教的彻底否定；又因为一个国家内部矛盾信条的共存被非共产主义者视为政治健康的证明；又因为反共产主义的十字军只能以宗教的名义发动。

Communism is a faith, not a religion. It is simple, social equalitarianism, generous and unnationalistic in original intention, the exponents of which, however, have been forced, as the early Christians were, to postpone their hopes of an immediate millennium and adopt a pragmatic policy that will at least guarantee their own survival in a hostile world.
共产主义是一种信仰，而非宗教。它最初是简单的社会平等主义，慷慨且非民族主义，但其倡导者被迫像早期基督徒一样推迟了对立即千年的希望，采取了至少能保证自己在敌对世界中生存的务实政策。

Since, then, the Communistic faith, however fanatically held, is not a religion, and since all contemporary religions contradict one another, however politely, in their articles of faith, can any definition of the word religion be made that is practically relevant to a solution of the present political problems?
既然共产主义信仰——无论被多么狂热地持有——不是宗教，且所有当代宗教在信仰条款上无论如何礼貌地都互相矛盾，那么能否给出一个与解决当前政治问题实际相关的「宗教」定义？

The dictionaries give its etymology as ‘doubtful’. Cicero connected it with relegere, ‘to read duly’ – hence ‘to pore upon, or study’ divine lore. Some four-and-a-half centuries later, Saint Augustine derived it from religare, ‘to bind back’ and supposed that it implied a pious obligation to obey divine law; and this is the sense in which religion has been understood ever since. Augustine’s guess, like Cicero’s (though Cicero came nearer the truth), did not take into account the length of the first syllable of religio in Lucretius’s early De Rerum Natura, or the alternative spelling relligio. Relligio can be formed only from the phrase rem legere, ‘to choose, or pick, the right thing’, and religion for the primitive Greeks and Romans was not obedience to laws but a means of protecting the tribe against evil by active counter-measures of good. It was in the hands of a magically-minded priesthood, whose duty was to suggest what action would please the gods on peculiarly auspicious or inauspicious occasions. When, for example, a bottomless chasm suddenly opened in the Roman Forum, they read it as a sign that the gods demanded a sacrifice of Rome’s best; one Mettus Curtius felt called upon to save the situation by choosing the right thing, and leaped into the chasm on horseback, fully armed. On another occasion a woodpecker appeared in the Forum where the City Praetor, Aelius Tubero, was dispensing justice, perched on his head and allowed him to take it in his hand. Since the woodpecker was sacred to Mars, its unnatural tameness alarmed the augurs, who pronounced that, if it were released, disaster would overcome Rome; if killed, the Praetor would die for his act of sacrilege. Aelius Tubero patriotically wrung its neck, and afterwards came to a violent end. These unhistorical anecdotes seem to have been invented by the College of Augurs as examples of how signs should be read and how Romans should act in response to them.
词典给出的词源为「可疑」。西塞罗将其与 relegere「正当阅读」联系——即「研读、钻研」神圣学问。约四个半世纪后，圣奥古斯丁将其源自 religare「绑回」，意指服从神法的虔诚义务；此后宗教便被如此理解。奥古斯丁的猜测如西塞罗的（虽然西塞罗更接近真相）未考虑卢克莱修早期《物性论》中 religio 第一音节的长度，或其替代拼写 relligio。relligio 只能来自短语 rem legere「选择，拣选正确之物」，而对于原始的希腊人和罗马人来说，宗教不是对法律的服从，而是通过积极的善行反制来保护部落免受邪恶之害的手段。它在具有魔法思维的祭司团手中，其职责是建议在特别吉或不幸的场合采取什么行动取悦诸神。例如，当罗马广场突然裂开一个无底深渊时，他们将其解读为诸神要求以罗马最精锐之物献祭的征兆；一位名叫梅图斯·库尔提乌斯的人感到有责任通过选择正确之物来挽救局面，全副武装地骑马跃入深渊。另一次，一只啄木鸟出现在广场上城市裁判官埃利乌斯·图贝罗正在执法之处，栖在他头上，让他可以用手捉住。由于啄木鸟是马尔斯的圣鸟，其反常的温顺令占卜官警恐，他们宣告：如果放走它，灾难将降于罗马；如果杀死它，裁判官将因亵渎之罪而死。埃利乌斯·图贝罗爱国地拧断了它的脖子，后来果然死于非命。这些非历史性轶事似乎是占卜官学院为了举例说明征兆应如何解读以及罗马人应如何应对而编造的。

The case of Aelius Tubero is a useful illustration not only of relligio but of the difference between taboo and law. The theory of taboo is that certain things are prophetically announced by a priest or priestess to be harmful to certain people at certain times – though not necessarily to other people at the same time, or to the same people at other times; and the primitive punishment for the breach of a taboo is ordained not by the judges of the tribe but by the transgressor himself, who realizes his error and either dies of shame and grief or flees to another tribe and changes his identity. It was understood at Rome that a woodpecker, as the bird of Mars, might not be killed by anybody except the King, or his ritual successor under the Republic, and only on a single occasion in the year, as an expiatory sacrifice to the Goddess. In a less primitive society Tubero would have been publicly tried, under such-and-such a law, for killing a protected sacred bird, and either executed, fined or imprisoned; as it was, his breach of taboo was left to his own sense of divine vengeance.
埃利乌斯·图贝罗的案例不仅说明了 relligio，也说明了禁忌与法律的区别。禁忌的理论是：某些事物由祭司或女祭司预言性地宣布对某些人在某些时候有害——但未必对其他人在同时有害，或对同样的人在其他时候有害；违反禁忌的原始惩罚不是由部落的法官裁定，而是由违反者自己承担——他意识到自己的错误，要么死于羞愧和悲伤，要么逃到另一个部落改变身份。在罗马，众所周知啄木鸟作为马尔斯之鸟不得被任何人杀死，除非是国王或共和国时期其仪式继承者，且一年中只有一次，作为对女神的赎罪祭。在较不原始的社会中，图贝罗将根据某条法律因杀死受保护的圣鸟而受公审，要么被处死、罚款或监禁；但实际上，他的禁忌违犯被留给他自己对神罚的感知。

Primitive religion at Rome was bound up with the sacred monarchy: the King was restrained by a great number of taboos designed to please the various-titled Goddess of Wisdom whom he served, and the members of her divine family. It seems that the duty of his twelve priestly companions, one for every month of the year, called the lictores, or ‘choosers’, was to protect him against ill-luck or profanation and pay careful attention to his needs. Among their tasks must have been the relictio, or ‘careful reading’, of signs, omens, prodigies and auguries; and the selectio of his weapons, his clothes, his food and the grasses and leaves of his lectum or bed.1 On the extinction of the monarchy, the purely religious functions of the King were invested in the Priest of Jove, and the executive functions passed to the Consuls; the lictors became their guard of honour. The word lictor then became popularly connected with the word religare, ‘to bind’, because it was a lictorial function to bind those who rebelled against the power of the Consuls. Originally there had been no Twelve Tables, nor any other Roman code of laws; there had only been oral tradition, based on instinctive good principles and particular magical announcements. Mettus Curtius and Aelius Tubero are not represented as having been under any legal obligation to do what they did; they made an individual choice for moral reasons.
罗马的原始宗教与神圣王权紧密相连：国王受到大量旨在取悦他所侍奉的多名号智慧女神及其神圣家族成员的禁忌约束。他的十二位祭司同伴——每年每月一位——称为 lictores 即「选择者」——的职责似乎是保护他免遭厄运或亵渎，并仔细照顾他的需求。他们的任务包括对征兆、预兆、异象和鸟占的 relictio 即「仔细阅读」；以及对他的武器、衣物、食物和他的 lectum 即床榻上的草和叶的 selectio。¹ 王权消亡后，国王的纯宗教职能被赋予朱庇特祭司，行政职能转给执政官；lictor 成为他们的仪仗卫队。lictor 一词随后被俗众与 religare「绑缚」联系起来，因为绑缚反抗执政官权力之人是 lictor 的职能。最初没有《十二铜表法》，也没有任何其他罗马法典；只有基于本能的善良原则和特定的魔法宣告的口传传统。梅图斯·库尔提乌斯和埃利乌斯·图贝罗并未被表现为有任何法律义务去做他们所做的事；他们是出于道德原因做出的个人选择。

It must be explained that the word lex, ‘law’, began with the sense of a ‘chosen word’, or magical pronouncement, and that, like lictor, it was later given a false derivation from ligare. Law in Rome grew out of religion: occasional pronouncements developed proverbial force and became legal principles. But as soon as religion in its primitive sense is interpreted as social obligation and defined by tabulated laws – as soon as Apollo the Organizer, God of Science, usurps the power of his Mother the Goddess of inspired truth, wisdom and poetry, and tries to bind her devotees by laws – inspired magic goes, and what remains is theology, ecclesiastical ritual, and negatively ethical behaviour.
必须解释的是，lex「法律」一词最初意为「被选择之词」即魔法宣告，且像 lictor 一样后来被赋予了一个来自 ligare 的虚假词源。罗马的法律从宗教中生长出来：偶尔的宣告获得了谚语般的力量并成为法律原则。但一旦宗教在其原始意义上被解释为社会义务并以成文法界定——一旦组织者阿波罗即科学之神篡夺了其母即灵感真理、智慧和诗歌女神的权力，试图以法律约束她的信徒——灵感魔法便消失了，留下的是神学、教会仪式和消极的伦理行为。

If, therefore, it is wished to avoid disharmony, dullness and oppression in all social (and all literary) contexts, each problem must be regarded as unique, to be settled by right choice based on instinctive good principle, not by reference to a code or summary of precedents; and, granted that the only way out of our political troubles is a return to religion, this must somehow be freed of its theological accretions. Positive right choosing based on moral principle must supersede negative respect for the Law which, though backed by force, has grown so hopelessly inflated and complex that not even a trained lawyer can hope to be conversant with more than a single branch of it. Willingness to do right can be inculcated in most people if they are caught early enough, but so few have the capacity to make a proper moral choice between circumstances or actions which at first sight are equally valid, that the main religious problem of the Western world, is briefly, how to exchange demagogracy, disguised as democracy, for a non-hereditary aristocracy whose leaders will be inspired to choose rightly on every occasion, instead of blindly following authoritarian procedure. The Russian Communist Party has confused the issue by presenting itself as such an aristocracy and claiming to be inspired in its choice of policy.
因此，如果希望避免一切社会（和一切文学）语境中的不和、沉闷和压迫，每个问题都必须被视为独特的，应通过基于本能善良原则的正确选择来解决，而非参照法典或判例汇编；且鉴于摆脱政治困境的唯一出路是回归宗教，这必须以某种方式摆脱其神学附吸。基于道德原则的积极正确选择必须取代对法律的消极尊重——法律虽有武力支撑，却已膨胀得如此无可救药地复杂，以至于即使是受过训练的律师也只敢期望精通其中一个分支。向善的意愿可以在大多数人身上及早培养，但很少有人具备在初看同样有效的情况或行动之间做出正确道德选择的能力，因此西方世界的主要宗教问题简言之是：如何将伪装成民主的煽动政治交换为一种非世袭的贵族制，其领袖将被激发在每次场合中做出正确选择，而非盲目遵循权威程序。俄国共产党混淆了这一议题，它以这种贵族制自居，声称其政策选择是被激发的。

* * *



There are two distinct and complementary languages: the ancient, intuitive language of poetry, and the more modern, rational language or prose, universally current. Myth and religion are clothed in poetic language; science, ethics, philosophy and statistics in prose. A stage in history has now been reached when it is generally conceded that the two languages should not be combined into a single formula, though Dr. Barnes, the liberal Bishop of Birmingham, complains1 that a majority of reactionary bishops would like to insist on a literal belief even in the stories of Noah’s Ark and Jonah’s Whale. The Bishop is right to deplore the way in which these venerable religious symbols have been misinterpreted for didactic reasons; and to deplore still more the Church’s perpetuation of fables as literal truth. The story of the Ark is probably derived from an Asianic icon in which the Spirit of the Solar Year is shown in a moon-ship, going through his habitual New Year changes – bull, lion, snake and so on; and the story of the Whale from a similar icon showing the same Spirit being swallowed at the end of the year by the Moon-and-Sea-goddess, represented as a sea-monster, to be presently re-born as a New Year fish, or finned goat. The she-monster Tiamat who, in early Babylonian mythology, swallowed the Sun-god Marduk (but whom he later claimed to have killed with his sword) was used by the author of the Book of Jonah to symbolize the power of the wicked city, mother of harlots, that swallowed and then spewed up the Jews. The icon, a familiar one on the Eastern Mediterranean, survived in Orphic art, where it represented a ritual ceremony of initiation: the initiate was swallowed by the Universal Mother, the sea-monster, and re-born as an incarnation of the Sun-god. (On one Greek vase the Jonah-like figure is named Jason, because the history of his voyage in the Argo had by that time been attached to the signs of the Zodiac around which the Sun makes its annual voyage.) The Hebrew prophets knew Tiamat as the Moon-and-Sea-goddess Rahab, but rejected her as the mistress of all fleshly corruptions; which is why in the ascetic Apocalypse the faithful are promised ‘No more sea’.
存在两种截然不同且互补的语言：古老的、直觉的诗歌语言，以及更现代的、理性的散文语言——后者通行全球。神话和宗教以诗歌语言为衣；科学、伦理、哲学和统计以散文为衣。历史已达到这样一个阶段：人们普遍承认这两种语言不应合为单一公式，尽管伯明翰的自由派主教巴恩斯博士抱怨¹ 反动主教多数派试图坚持对诺亚方舟和约拿鲸鱼故事甚至进行字面信仰。主教痛惜这些古老宗教象征因教诲原因而被误解的方式是正确的；更应痛惜的是教会将寓言当作字面真相来延续。方舟故事大概源自一幅亚细亚图像，其中太阳年之灵在月船中经历他惯常的新年变化——牝牛、雄狮、蛇等；鲸鱼故事则来自类似的图像，表现同一个灵在年末被以海怪形象出现的月与海女神吞噬，随后作为新年鱼或有鳍山羊重生。早期巴比伦神话中吞噬太阳神马尔杜克（但他后来声称用剑杀死了她）的雌怪提亚马特，被《约拿书》作者用来象征邪恶之城即淫乱之母的权力——它吞噬然后吐出犹太人。这一在地中海东部常见的图像在俄耳甫斯艺术中存留，代表一种入教仪式：入教者被万有之母即海怪吞噬，然后作为太阳神的化身重生。（在一尊希腊花瓶上，约拿式人物被命名为伊阿宋，因为那时他的阿尔戈号航海史已被附会于太阳年度航行的黄道宫。）希伯来先知知道提亚马特即月与海女神拉哈伯，但拒绝她为一切肉体腐败的女主人；这就是为什么在禁欲的《启示录》中，忠信者被许诺「海也不再有了」。

Dr. Barnes was quoting the stories of the Whale and Ark as obvious absurdities, but at the same time warning his fellow-bishops that few educated persons believe literally even in Jesus’s miracles. The merely agnostic attitude, ‘He may have risen to Heaven; we have no evidence for or against this claim’, has now given place in the back-rooms to the positively hostile: ‘Scientifically, it does not add up.’ A New Zealand atomic scientist assured me the other day that Christianity had received its heaviest blow in 1945: a fundamental tenet of the Church, namely that Jesus’s material body was immaterialized at the Ascension had, he said, been spectacularly disproved at Hiroshima and Nagasaki – anyone with the least scientific perception must realize that any such break-down of matter would have caused an explosion large enough to wreck the entire Middle East.
巴恩斯博士引用鲸鱼和方舟故事作为明显的荒谬之谈，但同时也警告同僚主教，很少有受过教育的人甚至字面相信那稣的奇迹。纯粹不可知的态度——「他可能升天了；我们没有支持或反对这一说法的证据」——如今在后室中已被积极敌对的态度取代：「科学上说不通。」一位新西兰原子科学家前几天向我保证，基督教在1945年受到了最沉重的打击：教会的一个基本信条，即那稣的物质身体在升天时被非物质化了，他说，在广岛和长崎已被壮观地反驳——任何稍有科学感知力的人都必须意识到，任何此类物质崩溃都将引发足以摧毁整个中东的爆炸。

Now that scientists are talking in this strain, Christianity has little chance of maintaining its hold on the governing classes unless the historical part of ecclesiastical doctrine can be separated from the mythical: that is to say, unless a distinction can be drawn between the historical concept ‘Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews’, and the equally valid mythical concepts ‘Christ’ and ‘Son of Man’ in terms of which alone the Virgin Birth, the Ascension and the miracles make unchallengeable sense. If this were to happen, Christianity would develop into a pure mystery-cult, with a Christ, divorced from his temporal history, paying the Virgin-Queen of Heaven a filial obedience that Jesus of Nazareth reserved for his Incomprehensible Father. Scientists would perhaps welcome the change as meeting the psychological needs of the masses, involving no anti-scientific absurdities, and having a settling effect on civilization; one of the reasons for the restlessness of Christendom has always been that the Gospel postulates an immediate end of time and therefore denies mankind a sense of spiritual security. Confusing the languages of prose and myth, its authors claimed that a final revelation had at last been delivered: everyone must repent, despise the world, and humble himself before God in expectation of the imminent Universal Judgement. A mystical Virgin-born Christ, detached from Jewish eschatology and unlocalized in first-century Palestine, might restore religion to contemporary self-respect.
既然科学家开始以这种方式说话，除非教会教义的历史部分能够与神话部分分离——也就是说，除非能在历史概念「拿撒勒人那稣，犹太人之王」与同样有效的神话概念「基督」和「人子」之间划定区分——基督教几乎没有机会维持其对统治阶层的掌控，而只有以后者来理解童贞女生子、升天和奇迹才无可辩驳。如果这成为现实，基督教将发展成一种纯粹的密仪宗教，一个脱离其世俗历史的基督向天上的童贞女王致以孝敬的服从，正如拿撒勒人那稣为其不可理解的父神所保留的那样。科学家也许会欢迎这一改变，认为它满足了大众的心理需求，不涉及反科学的荒谬，且对文明有稳定作用；基督教世界不安的原因之一一直是福音书假设时间即将终结，因此否认人类以灵性安全感。一个神秘的、由童贞女所生的基督，脱离犹太末世论、不被定位于一世纪巴勒斯坦，或许能恢复宗教的当代自尊。

However, such a religious change is impossible under present conditions: any neo-Arian attempt to degrade Jesus from God to man would be opposed as lessening the authority of his ethical message of love and peace. Also, the Mother-and-Son myth is so closely linked with the natural year and its cycle of ever-recurring observed events in the vegetable and animal queendoms that it makes little emotional appeal to the confirmed townsman, who is informed of the passage of the seasons only by the fluctuations of his gas and electricity bills or by the weight of his underclothes. He is chivalrous to women but thinks only in prose; the one variety of religion acceptable to him is a logical, ethical, highly abstract sort which appeals to his intellectual pride and sense of detachment from wild nature. The Goddess is no towns woman: she is the Lady of the Wild Things, haunting the wooded hill-tops – Venus Cluacina, ‘she who purifies with myrtle’, not Venus Cloacina, ‘Patroness of the Sewage System’, as she first became at Rome; and though the townsman has now begun to insist that built-up areas should have a limit, and to discuss decentralization (the decanting of the big towns into small, independent communities, well spaced out), his intention is only to urbanize the country, not to ruralize the town. Agricultural life is rapidly becoming industrialized and in England, the world’s soberest social laboratory, the last vestiges of the ancient pagan celebrations of the Mother and Son are being obliterated, despite a loving insistence on Green Belts and parks and private gardens. It is only in backward parts of Southern and Western Europe that a lively sense still survives in the countryside of their continued worship.
然而，这样的宗教变革在当前条件下是不可能的：任何新阿里乌主义试图将那稣从神降格为人都会遭到反对，被认为削弱了他爱与和平的伦理信息的权威。此外，母子神话与自然年及其动植物王国中反复观察到的循环事件如此紧密相连，以至于对坚定的城市人几乎没有情感吸引力——他仅通过煤气费和电费的波动或内衣的重量来感知季节的推移。他对女性彬彬有礼但只用散文思考；他能接受的唯一宗教是一种逻辑的、伦理的、高度抽象的种类，诉诸他的智识骄傲和与野性自然的疏离感。女神不是城市女子：她是野生之物的女主人，出没于林木葱郁的山顶——是维纳斯·克卢阿基纳即「以桃金娘净化者」，而非维纳斯·克洛阿基纳即「下水道系统主保」，如她最初在罗马所变成的那样；虽然城市人现在开始坚持建成区应有界限，并讨论去中心化（将大城市倒入小而独立、间隔良好的社区），他的意图只是将乡村城市化，而非将城市乡村化。农业生活正在迅速工业化，在英国——世界上最审慎的社会实验室——母与子的古老异教庆祝活动的最后痕迹正在被抹去，尽管对绿带和公园及私人花园有深情的坚持。只有在南欧和西欧的落后地区，乡村中对他们持续崇拜的活跃意识仍然存活。

No: there seems no escape from our difficulties until the industrial system breaks down for some reason or other, as it nearly did in Europe during the Second World War, and nature reasserts herself with grass and trees among the ruins.
不：似乎在我们走出困境之前，工业系统因某种原因崩溃——如二战期间在欧洲几乎发生的那样——大自然以草和树在废墟中重新宣告自己的存在。

The Protestant Churches are divided between liberal theology and fundamentalism, but the Vatican authorities have made up their minds how to face the problems of the day. They encourage two antinomous trends of thought to co-exist within the Church: the authoritarian, or paternal, or logical, as a means of securing the priest’s hold on his congregation and keeping them from free-thinking; the mythical, or maternal, or supralogical, as a concession to the Goddess, without whom the Protestant religion has lost its romantic glow. They recognize her as a lively, various, immemorial obsession, deeply fixed in the racial memory of the European countryman and impossible to exorcize; but are equally aware that this is an essentially urban civilization, therefore authoritarian, and therefore patriarchal. It is true that woman has of late become virtual head of the household in most parts of the Western world, and holds the purse-strings, and can take up almost any career or position she pleases; but she is unlikely to repudiate the present system, despite its patriarchal framework. With all its disadvantages, she enjoys greater liberty of action under it than man has retained for himself; and though she may know, intuitively, that the system is due for a revolutionary change, she does not care to hasten or anticipate this. It is easier for her to play man’s game a little while longer, until the situation grows too absurd and uncomfortable for complaisance. The Vatican waits watchfully.
新教教会分裂为自由神学和基要主义，但梵蒂冈当局已下定决心如何面对当代问题。他们鼓励两种对立的思想趋势在教会中共存：权威主义的即父权的即逻辑的，作为确保祭司对其会众掌控并防止自由思考的手段；神话的即母性的即超逻辑的，作为对女神的让步——没有她，新教便失去了浪漫的光辉。他们承认她是一种活泼的、多样的、古已有之的执念，深深固定在欧洲乡民的种族记忆中，无法驱除；但也同样意识到这是一个本质上的城市文明，因此是权威主义的，因此是父权的。诚然，近来女性在西方世界大部分地区已成为家庭的实际户主，掌握财政大权，可以从事她喜欢的几乎任何职业或职位；但她不太可能否定现行制度，尽管其框架是父权的。尽管有其不利之处，她在其下享有的行动自由比男人为自己保留的还要大；虽然她可能直觉地知道这一制度注定要发生革命性变化，但她不急于加速或预判之。对她来说，再多玩一阵男人的游戏更容易，直到局势变得太荒谬和太不舒服以至于无法迁就。梵蒂冈警惕地等待着。

Meanwhile, Science itself is in difficulties. Scientific research has become so complicated and demands such enormous apparatus that only the State or immensely rich patrons can pay for it, which in practice means that a disinterested search for knowledge is cramped by the demand for results that will justify the expense: the scientist must turn showman. Also, a huge body of technical administrators is needed to implement his ideas, and these too rank as scientists; yet, as Professor Lancelot Hogben points out,1 (and he is exceptional in being an F.R.S. with sufficient knowledge of history and the humanities to be able to view science objectively) they are no more than ‘fellow-travellers’ – careerists, opportunists, and civil-service-minded authoritarians. A non-commercial benevolent institution like the Nuffield Foundation, he says, is as high-handed in its treatment of scientists as a Treasury-controlled Government department. In consequence, pure mathematics is almost the only free field of science left. Moreover, the corpus of scientific knowledge, like that of law, has grown so unwieldy that not only are most scientists ignorant of even the rudiments of more than one specialized study, but they cannot keep up with the publications in their own field, and are forced to take on trust findings which they should properly test by personal experiment. Apollo the Organizer, in fact, seated on Zeus’s throne, is beginning to find his ministers obstructive, his courtiers boring, his regalia tawdry, his quasi-royal responsibilities irksome, and the system of government breaking down from over-organization: he regrets having enlarged the realm to such absurd proportions and given his uncle Pluto and his half-brother Mercury a share in the Regency, yet dares not quarrel with these unreliable wretches for fear of worse to come, or even attempt to re-write the constitution with their help. The Goddess smiles grimly at his predicament.
与此同时，科学本身也陷入困境。科学研究变得如此复杂，需要如此庞大的设备，以至于只有国家或极富有的赞助人才能负担，这在实践中意味着无私的知识探索被要求产生能证明开销合理的结果所束缚：科学家必须变成表演者。此外，需要一个庞大的技术行政人员队伍来实施他的想法，这些人也算科学家；然而正如兰斯洛特·霍格本教授所指出的，¹（他是少有的兼具足够历史和人文学科知识以客观审视科学的皇家学会会员）他们不过是「同路人」——野心家、机会主义者和具有公务员心态的威权主义者。他说，一个像纳菲尔德基金会这样的非商业慈善机构，在对待科学家的态度上与财政部控制的政府部门一样专横。结果是，纯数学几乎是仅存的自由科学领域。此外，科学知识体系如同法律一样变得如此臃肿，以至于大多数科学家不仅对不止一门专业研究的入门知识一无所知，而且无法跟上自己领域的出版物，被迫凭信任接受本应由个人实验验证的发现。组织者阿波罗事实上坐在宙斯的宝座上，正开始发现他的大臣们碍事，他的朝臣们无趣，他的徽饰俗气，他的准皇家责任令人厌烦，政府系统因过度组织而崩溃：他后悔将王国扩大到如此荒谬的规模，并让他的叔叔普路同和异母兄弟墨丘利分享摄政权，却不敢与这些不可靠的恶棍争吵以免更糟的事情发生，甚至不敢尝试在他们的帮助下重写宪法。女神阴沉地对他的困境微笑。

This is the ‘brave new world’ satirized by Aldous Huxley, an ex-poet turned philosopher. What has he to offer in its place? In his Perennial Philosophy he recommends a saintly mysticism of not-being in which woman figures only as an emblem of the soul’s surrender to the creative lust of God. The West, he says in effect, has failed because its religious feelings have been too long linked with political idealism or the pursuit of pleasure; it must now look to India for guidance in the rigorous discipline of asceticism. Little or nothing is, of course, known to the Indian mystics that was unknown to Honi the Circle-drawer and the other Essene therapeutics with whom Jesus had so close an affinity, or to the Mohammedan mystics; but talk of political reconciliation between Far East and Far West is in fashion and Mr. Huxley therefore prefers to style himself a devotee of Ramakrishna, the most famous Indian mystic of modern times.
这就是奥尔德斯·赫胥黎——一位从诗人转变为哲学家的人——所讽刺的「美丽新世界」。他能拿什么来取代它？在《长青哲学》中他推荐一种圣洁的「无存」神秘主义，其中女性仅作为灵魂向上帝创造性欲望投降的象征出现。他实际上是说，西方失败了，因为其宗教情感太长时间与政治理想主义或追求快乐联系在一起；它现在必须向印度寻求苦行严格修行的指导。当然，印度神秘主义者所知甚少的东西，圈地者霍尼及其他与那稣关系密切的艾赛尼治疗者或穆罕默德神秘主义者并非不知；但远东与远西之间政治和解的谈论正当时髦，因此赫胥黎先生宁愿自称现代最著名的印度神秘主义者罗摩克里希纳的信徒。

Ramakrishna’s case is an interesting one. He lived all his life in the grounds of the White Goddess Kali’s temple at Dakshineswar on the Ganges, and in 1842, at the age of six, had fallen in a faint at the beauty of a flock of cranes, her birds, flying across a background of storm clouds. At first he devoted himself to Kali-worship with true poetic ecstacy like his predecessor Ramprasad Sen (1718–1775); but, when he grew to manhood, allowed himself to be seduced: he was unexpectedly acclaimed by Hindu pundits as a re-incarnation of Krishna and Buddha, and persuaded by them into orthodox techniques of devotion. He became an ascetic saint of the familiar type with devoted disciples and a Gospel of ethics posthumously published, and was fortunate enough to marry a woman of the same mystic capacities as himself who, by agreeing to forgo physical consummation, helped him to illustrate the possibility of a purely spiritual union of the sexes. Though he did not need to declare war on the Female, as Jesus had done, he set himself painfully to ‘dissolve his vision of the Goddess’ in order to achieve the ultimate bliss of samadhi, or communion with the Absolute; holding that the Goddess, who was both the entangler and the liberator of physical man, has no place in that remote esoteric Heaven. In later life he claimed to have proved by experiment that Christians and Mohammedans could also achieve the same bliss as himself; first, by turning Christian and devoting himself to the Catholic liturgy until he achieved a vision of Jesus Christ, and then Moslem until he achieved a vision of Mohammed – after each experience resuming samadhi.
罗摩克里希纳的案例很有趣。他一生居住在恒河上达克希涅斯瓦尔的白女神迦梨寺庙的庭院中，1842年六岁时因一群白鹤——她的鸟——飞过暴风云背景的美丽而晕倒。最初他像前辈拉姆普拉萨德·森（1718-1775）一样以真正的诗意狂喜投身迦梨崇拜；但成年后被引诱：他意外地被印度教祭司们赞誉为克里希纳和佛的化身，并被说服接受正统的修行技术。他成为了一种常见的禁欲圣徒，有虔诚的门徒和死后出版的福音书，并有幸娶了一位与自己有同等神秘能力的女子——她同意放弃肉体圆满，帮助他证明两性之间纯粹灵性结合的可能性。虽然他不需要像那稣那样向女性宣战，但他痛苦地着手「消解他对女神的幻象」以达到三昧即与绝对者合一的终极极乐；他认为女神——既是肉体之人的缠绊者又是解脱者——在那个遥远的秘传天国中没有位置。晚年他声称通过实验证明了基督徒和穆罕默德教徒也能达到与他相同的极乐：首先他变成基督徒投身天主教礼拜直到见到耶稣基督的异象，然后变成穆罕默德教徒直到见到穆罕默德的异象——每次体验后都恢复三昧。

What, then, is samadhi? It is a psychopathic condition, a spiritual orgasm, indistinguishable from the ineffably beautiful moment, described by Dostoievsky, which precedes an epileptic fit. Indian mystics induce it at will by fasting and meditation, as the Essenes and early Christian and Mohammedan saints also did. Ramakrishna had, in fact, ceased to be a poet and become a morbid-psychologist and religious politician addicted to the most refined form of solitary vice imaginable. Ramprasad had never allowed himself to be thus tempted from his devotion to the Goddess by spiritual ambition. He had even rejected the orthodox hope of ‘not-being’, through mystic absorption in the Absolute, as irreconcilable with his sense of individual uniqueness as the Goddess’s child and lover:
那么，三昧是什么？它是一种精神变态状态，一种灵性高潮，与陀思妥耶夫斯基所描述的癫痫发作前那不可言喻的美丽时刻无异。印度神秘主义者通过禁食和冥想随意引发之，正如艾赛尼派和早期基督教及穆罕默德圣徒所做的那样。事实上罗摩克里希纳已不再是诗人，而成为病态心理学家和宗教政客，沉迷于可以想象的最精致的孤独恶习。拉姆普拉萨德从未允许自己被灵性野心如此诱离对女神的虔诚。他甚至拒绝了通过神秘地消融于绝对者中而达到「无存」的正统希望，认为这与他对自身作为女神之子和情人的独特个体性的感知不可调和：

Sugar I like, yet I have no desire
Sugar I like, yet I have no desire（糖我喜欢，但我无意）



To become sugar,
To become sugar,（变成糖，）





and faced the prospect of death with poetic pride:
并以诗性的骄傲面对死亡的前景：

How can yon shrink from death,
How can yon shrink from death,（你怎能畏惧死亡，）



Child of the Mother of All Living?
Child of the Mother of All Living?（众生之母的孩子？）



A snake, and you fear frogs?
A snake, and you fear frogs?（身为蛇，你怕青蛙？）





One Kalipuja Day he followed Kali’s image into the Ganges until the waters closed over his head.
一个迦梨祭日，他追随迦梨的神像走入恒河，直到河水没过他的头顶。

The story of Ramprasad’s devotion to Kali reads familiarly to the Western romantic; samadhi, the unchivalrous rejection of the Goddess, will not appeal even to the Western townsman. Nor are any other revivals of Father-god worship, whether ascetic or epicurean, autocratic or communist, liberal or fundamentalist, likely to solve our troubles; I foresee no change for the better until everything gets far worse. Only after a period of complete political and religious disorganization can the suppressed desire of the Western races, which is for some practical form of Goddess-worship, with her love not limited to maternal benevolence and her after-world not deprived of a sea, find satisfaction at last.
拉姆普拉萨德对迦梨的虔诚故事对西方浪漫主义者而言读来似曾相识；三昧即对女神的不侠排斥，即使对西方城市人也不会有吸引力。其他任何形式的父神崇拜复兴——无论禁欲的还是享乐的、专制的还是共产主义的、自由派的还是基要派的——也不可能解决我们的困境；我预见不到任何好转，除非一切都变得更糟。只有在一段完全的政治和宗教瓦解时期之后，西方种族被压抑的渴望——即某种实际形式的女神崇拜，她的爱不限于母性的仁慈，她的来世也不缺少海洋——才能最终得到满足。

How should she then be worshipped? Donne anticipated the problem in his early poem The Primrose. He knew that the primrose is sacred to the Muse and that the ‘mysterious number’ of its petals stands for women. Should he adore a six-petalled or a four-petalled freak, a Goddess that is either more, or less, than true woman? He chose five petals and proved by the science of numbers that woman, if she pleases, has complete domination of man. But it was said of the lotus-crowned Goddess in the Corinthian Mysteries, long before the phrase was applied to the ideally benign Father-god, ‘Her service is perfect freedom’;1 and, indeed, her habit has never been to coerce, but always to grant or withhold her favours according as her sons and lovers came to her with exactly the right gifts in their hands – gifts of their own choosing, not her dictation. She must be worshipped in her ancient quintuple person, whether by counting the petals of lotus or primrose: as Birth, Initiation, Consummation, Repose and Death.
那么她应如何被崇拜？多恩在其早期诗作《报春花》中预见到了这一问题。他知道报春花是献给缪斯的圣花，其花瓣的「神秘数字」代表女性。他应该崇拜六瓣或四瓣的变异体——一种多于或少于真正女人的女神吗？他选择了五瓣，并以数字科学证明女人如果愿意，可以完全支配男人。但早在这一短语被用于理想仁慈的父神之前，科林斯密仪中头戴莲花的女神就被如此说：「侍奉她即是完美的自由」；¹ 确实，她的习惯从来不是强迫，而是根据她的儿子和情人们是否手中带着恰好正确的礼物来赐予或拒绝她的恩宠——礼物由他们自己选择，而非她指定。她必须以其古老的五重身份被崇拜——无论通过数莲花还是报春花的花瓣：诞生、入教、圆满、安息和死亡。

It will be objected that man has as valid a claim to divinity as woman. That is true only in a sense; he is divine not in his single person, but only in his twinhood. As Osiris, the Spirit of the Waxing Year he is always jealous of his weird, Set, the Spirit of the Waning Year, and vice-versa; he cannot be both of them at once except by an intellectual effort that destroys his humanity, and this is the fundamental defect of the Apollonian or Jehovistic cult. Man is a demi-god: he always has either one foot or the other in the grave; woman is divine because she can keep both her feet always in the same place, whether in the sky, in the underworld, or on this earth. Man envies her and tells himself lies about his own completeness, and thereby makes himself miserable; because if he is divine she is not even a demi-goddess – she is a mere nymph and his love for her turns to scorn and hate.
会有人反对说男人与女人一样有资格获得神性。这仅在某种意义上为真；他的神性不在于他单独的人身，而仅在于他的孪生性。作为奥西里斯即上弦年之灵，他总是嫉妒他的命运对偶塞特即下弦年之灵，反之亦然；他不能同时成为两者，除非以一种摧毁其人性的智识努力，而这正是阿波罗式或耶和华崇拜的根本缺陷。男人是半神：他总是一只脚或另一只脚在坟墓中；女人是神圣的，因为她可以始终双脚站在同一处——无论在天上、在冥间还是在地上。男人嫉妒她，对自己自身的完整性撒谎，因此使自己痛苦；因为如果他是神圣的，她便连半女神都不是——她不过是一个宁芙，他对她的爱便转为蔑视和仇恨。

Woman worships the male infant, not the grown man: it is evidence of her deity, of man’s dependence on her for life. She is passionately interested in grown men, however, because the love-hate that Osiris and Set feel for each other on her account is a tribute to her divinity. She tries to satisfy both, but can only do so by alternate murder, and man tries to regard this as evidence of her fundamental falsity, not of his own irreconcilable demands on her.
女人崇拜男婴，而非成年男人：这是她神性的证据，是男人对她的生命依赖的证明。然而她对成年男人充满激情地关注，因为奥西里斯和塞特因她而彼此感受到的爱恨是对她神性的贡品。她试图满足两者，但只能通过交替的谋杀来实现，而男人试图将此视为她根本虚伪的证据，而非他自己对她不可调和的要求。

There are frequent denials of her power, for example Allan Ramsay’s Goddess of the Slothful (from The Gentle Shepherd, 1725):
她的权力经常被否认，例如艾伦·拉姆齐的《懒惰者的女神》（选自《温柔的牧羊人》，1725）：

O Godless of the Slothful, blind and vain,
O Godless of the Slothful, blind and vain,（啊懒惰者的女神，盲目而虚荣，）



Who with foul hearts. Rites, foolish and profane,
Who with foul hearts. Rites, foolish and profane,（怀着肮脏的心，举行愚蠡而亵渎的仪式，）



Altars and Temples hallowst to thy name!
Altars and Temples hallowst to thy name!（祭坛与圣殿以你的名为圣！）





Temples? or Sanctuaries vile, said I?
Temples? or Sanctuaries vile, said I?（圣殿？抑或我说的是卑劣的圣所？）



To protect Lewdness and Impiety,
To protect Lewdness and Impiety,（为保护淫荡与不敬，）



Under the Robe of the Divinity?
Under the Robe of the Divinity?（在神明的袍服之下？）





And thou Base Goddess! that thy wickedness,
And thou Base Goddess! that thy wickedness,（而你卑贱的女神！你的恶行，）



When others do as bad, may seem the less,
When others do as bad, may seem the less,（当旁人作恶同样，便显得你不过如此，）



Givest them the reins to all lasciviousness.
Givest them the reins to all lasciviousness.（你给他们纵情淫欲的缰绳。）





Rotter of soul and body, enemy
Rotter of soul and body, enemy（灵魂与肉体的腐蚀者，仇敌）



Of reason, plotter of sweet thievery,
Of reason, plotter of sweet thievery,（理性的敌人，甜蜜窃盗的策划者，）



The little and great world’s calamity.
The little and great world's calamity.（小世界与大世界的灾祸。）





Reputed worthily the Ocean’s daughter:
Reputed worthily the Ocean's daughter:（被恰如其分地称为海洋之女：）



That treacherous monster, which with even water
That treacherous monster, which with even water（那诡诈的怪物，以平静的水面）





First soothes, but ruffles into storms soon after.
First soothes, but ruffles into storms soon after.（先予抚慰，旋即搅起暴风。）





Such minds of sighs, such Cataracts of tears,
Such minds of sighs, such Cataracts of tears,（如此叹息之雾，如此泪之瀑布，）



Such breaking waves of hopes, such gulfs of fears,
Such breaking waves of hopes, such gulfs of fears,（如此希望之碎浪，如此恐惧之深渊，）



Thou makest of men, such rocks of cold despairs.
Thou makest of men, such rocks of cold despairs.（你使男人成为，如此冰冷绝望的礁石。）





Tides of desire so headstrong, as would move
Tides of desire so headstrong, as would move（欲望的潮水如此倔强，足以动摇）



The world to change thy name, when thou shalt prove
The world to change thy name, when thou shalt prove（世界更改你的名字，当你被证明）



Mother of Rage and Tempests, not of Love.
Mother of Rage and Tempests, not of Love.（是狂怒与暴风之母，而非爱之母。）





Behold what sorrow now and discontent
Behold what sorrow now and discontent（看啊，你加诸于）



On a poor pair of Lovers thou hast sent!
On a poor pair of Lovers thou hast sent!（一对可怜恋人身上的愁苦与不满！）



Go thou, that vaunt’st thyself Omnipotent.
Go thou, that vaunt'st thyself Omnipotent.（去吧，你那自夸全能的。）





But the longer her hour is postponed, and therefore the more exhausted by man’s irreligious improvidence the natural resources of the soil and sea become, the less merciful will her five-fold mask be, and the narrower the scope of action that she grants to whichever demi-god she chooses to take as her temporary consort in godhead. Let us placate her in advance by assuming the cannibalistic worst:
但她的时辰被推迟得越久，土壤和海洋的自然资源因人类的不虔诚的短视而消耗得越甚，她五重面具的慈悲便越少，她赐予她所选择作为神格之临时配偶的任何半神的行动范围也越窄。让我们以最坏的同类相食之假设来预先安抚她：

Under your Milky Way
Under your Milky Way（在你的银河之下）



And slow-revolving Bear,
And slow-revolving Bear,（与缓缓旋转的熊座，）



Frogs from the alder-thicket pray
Frogs from the alder-thicket pray（赤杨灌木丛中的青蛙祈祷）



In terror of the judgement day,
In terror of the judgement day,（在审判日的恐惧中，）



Loud with repentance there.
Loud with repentance there.（在那儿响亮地忏悔。）





The log they crowned as king
The log they crowned as king（他们加冕为王的圆木）



Grew sodden, lurched and sank.
Grew sodden, lurched and sank.（浸透水发软，摇晃着沉没。）



Dark waters bubble from the spring,
Dark waters bubble from the spring,（幽暗的水从泉眼冒泡，）



An owl floats by on silent wing,
An owl floats by on silent wing,（一只鸮以无声之翼飘过，）



They invoke you from each bank.
They invoke you from each bank.（他们在两岸呼唤你。）





At dawn you shall appear,
At dawn you shall appear,（黎明时你将现身，）



A gaunt, red-wattled crane,
A gaunt, red-wattled crane,（一只瘦削、红肉垂的鹤，）



She whom they know too well for fear,
She whom they know too well for fear,（她令他们太熟悉以至于不惧，）



Lunging your beak down like a spear
Lunging your beak down like a spear（喙如长矛般猛刺而下）



To fetch them home again.
To fetch them home again.（将他们重新带回家园。）





And we owe her a satire on the memory of the man who first tilted European civilization off balance, by enthroning the restless and arbitrary male will under the name of Zeus and dethroning the female sense of orderliness, Themis. The Greeks knew him as Pterseus the Destroyer, the Gorgon-slaying warrior-prince from Asia, remote ancestor of the destroyers Alexander, Pompey and Napoleon.
我们还欠她一首讽刺诗，纪念那个最初使欧洲文明失去平衡的人——他将以宙斯之名登基的躁动而专横的男性意志置于王座，废黜了女性的秩序感即忒弥斯（Themis）。希腊人称他为毁灭者普特修斯（Pterseus the Destroyer），那个来自亚细亚的屠戮戈耳工的武士王子，是亚历山大、庞培和拿破仑等毁灭者的远祖。

Swordsman of the narrow lips,
Swordsman of the narrow lips,（薄唇的剑客，）



Narrow hips and murderous mind
Narrow hips and murderous mind（窄臀与杀伐之心）





Fenced with chariots and ships,
Fenced with chariots and ships,（以战车与船只设障，）



By your joculators hailed
By your joculators hailed（被你的弄臣称颂）



The mailed wonder of mankind,
The mailed wonder of mankind,（披甲的人类奇观，）



Far to westward you have sailed.
Far to westward you have sailed.（你已航向遥远的西方。）





You it was dared seize the throne
You it was dared seize the throne（是你胆敢篡夺王座）



Of a blown and amorous prince
Of a blown and amorous prince（属于一个骄纵好色的王子）



Destined to the Moon alone,
Destined to the Moon alone,（命定只属于月亮，）



A lame, golden-heeled decoy,
A lame, golden-heeled decoy,（一个跛脚、金踵的诱饵，）



Joy of hens that gape and wince
Joy of hens that gape and wince（张嘴喘息畏缩的母鸡之乐）



Inarticulately coy.
Inarticulately coy.（语无伦次地扭捏。）





You who, capped with lunar gold
You who, capped with lunar gold（你，头戴月之金冠）



Like an old and savage dunce,
Like an old and savage dunce,（如一个古老而蛮荒的蠢汉，）



Let the central hearth go cold,
Let the central hearth go cold,（任中央炉火熄灭，）



Grinned, and left us here your sword
Grinned, and left us here your sword（咧嘴一笑，留下你的剑）



Warden of sick fields that once
Warden of sick fields that once（曾经自发生长的）



Sprouted of their own accord.
Sprouted of their own accord.（病田的看守人。）





Gusts of laughter the Moon stir
Gusts of laughter the Moon stir（月亮激起阵阵笑声）



That her Bassarids now bed
That her Bassarids now bed（因她的巴萨里德们如今与）



With the unnoble usurer,
With the unnoble usurer,（卑劣的放贷者同床，）



While an ignorant pale priest
While an ignorant pale priest（而一个无知的苍白祭司）



Rides the beast with a man’s head
Rides the beast with a man's head（骑乘人首之兽）



To her long-omitted feast.
To her long-omitted feast.（赴她久已缺席的盛宴。）





1 The English word litter, derived from lectum, has the double sense of bed and bedding; and the Lord of the Manor of Oterarsee in Angevin times held his fief ‘by the service of finding litter for the King’s bed: in summer grass and herbs, and in winter straw’.
¹ 英文词 litter（草垫/卧具）源自 lectum，兼有床和铺卧之物的双重含义；安茹时代的奥特拉斯庄园领主以其封地义务「为国王的卧榻准备铺草：夏季用青草和香草，冬季用稻草」持有其采邑。



1 February, 1949.
1949年2月。



1 The New Authoritarianism, Conway Memorial Lecture, 1949.
¹ 《新威权主义》，康威纪念讲座，1949年。



1 Borrowed by St. Augustine from Lucius’s address to Isis in Apuleius’s Golden Ass, and now part of the Protestant liturgy.
¹ 圣奥古斯丁从阿普列尤斯《金驴记》中路修斯对伊西斯的致辞中借用，如今是新教礼拜仪式的一部分。





Chapter Twenty-Seven

title: 第二十七章
content:
POSTSCRIPT 1960
1960年后记





People often ask me how I came to write The White Goddess. Here is the story.
人们常问我为何会写《白女神》。事情是这样的。

Though a poet by calling, I make my livelihood by prose – biographies, novels, translations from various languages, and so forth. My home has been in Majorca since 1929. Temporarily exiled because of the Spanish Civil War, I wandered around Europe and the United States; and the Second World War caught me in England, where I stayed until it ended and I could return to Majorca. In 1944, at the Devonshire village of Galmpton, I was working against time on a historical novel about the Argonauts, when a sudden overwhelming obsession interrupted me. It took the form of an unsolicited enlightenment on a subject which had meant little enough to me. I stopped marking across my big Admiralty chart of the Black Sea the course taken (the mythographers said) by the Argo from the Bosphorus to Baku and back. Instead, I began speculating on a mysterious ‘Battle of the Trees’, fought in pre-historic Britain, and my mind ran at such a furious rate all night, as well as all the next day, that it was difficult for my pen to keep pace with it. Three weeks later, I had written a seventy-thousand-word book, called The Roebuck in the Thicket.
我虽以诗人为天职，却以散文谋生——传记、小说、各种语言的翻译等等。自1929年起我的家在马略卡（Majorca）。因西班牙内战暂时流亡，我辗转于欧洲和美国各地；二战爆发时我在英国，一直待到战争结束才得以返回马略卡。1944年，在德文郡的加姆普顿村，我正争分夺秒地写一部关于阿尔戈英雄的历史小说，突然一阵排山倒海般的痴迷打断了我。它以一种不请自来的顿悟形式出现，主题对我而言此前几乎无足轻重。我停止了在黑海大海军图上标注阿尔戈号从博斯普鲁斯到巴库再返航的航线（据神话编纂者所言），转而开始思索一场史前不列颠的神秘「树木之战」，我的思维整夜及次日全天以如此狂暴的速度运转，以至于笔很难跟上它。三周后，我写完了七万字的书稿，名为《灌木丛中的獐鹿》（The Roebuck in the Thicket）。

I am no mystic: I avoid participation in witchcraft, spiritualism, yoga, fortune-telling, automatic writing, and the like. I live a simple, normal, rustic life with my family and a wide circle of sane and intelligent friends. I belong to no religious cult, no secret society, no philosophical sect; nor do I trust my historical intuition any further than it can be factually checked.
我不是神秘主义者：我避免参与巫术、招魂术、瑜伽、算命、自动书写及诸如此类。我与家人和一大群理智聪慧的朋友过着简单正常的田园生活。我不属于任何宗教教派、秘密社团或哲学流派；也不信任我的历史直觉超出可被事实验证的范围。

While engaged on my Argonaut book, I found the White Goddess of Pelion growing daily more important to the narrative. Now, I had in my work-room several small West African brass objects – bought from a London dealer – gold-dust weights, mostly in the shape of animals, among them a humpback playing a flute. I also had a small brass-box, with a lid, intended (so the dealer told me) to contain gold dust. I kept the humpback seated on the box. In fact, he is still seated there; but I knew nothing about him, or about the design on the box-lid, until ten years had gone by. Then I learned that the humpback was a herald in the service of the Queen-mother of some Akan State; and that every Akan Queen-mother (there are a few reigning even today) claims to be an incarnation of the Triple Moon-goddess Ngame. The design on the box-lid, a spiral, connected by a single stroke to the rectangular frame enclosing it – the frame having nine teeth on either side – means: ‘None greater in the universe than the Triple Goddess Ngame!’ These gold weights and the box were made before the British seizure of the Gold Coast, by craftsmen subservient to the Goddess, and regarded as highly magical.
在写阿尔戈英雄那本书时，我发现佩利翁山的白女神在叙事中日益重要。当时我的工作室里有几件西非小铜器——从伦敦一位商人处购得——多为动物形状的黄金粉尘砝码，其中有一个吹笛的驼背人。还有一个小铜盒，带盖子，据商人说是用来装金粉的。我把驼背人坐在盒子上。事实上他至今仍坐在那里；但直到十年过去了，我才对他或盒盖上的图案有所了解。后来我得知驼背人是某阿坎（Akan）邦国王母麾下的传令官；而每一位阿坎王母（至今仍有几位在位）都声称是三月神恩加梅（Ngame）的化身。盒盖上的图案——一条螺旋线，由一道笔划连接到包围它的矩形框，框的两侧各有九齿——意思是：「宇宙间无大于三月神恩加梅者！」这些金砝码和铜盒制作于英国夺取黄金海岸之前，由侍奉女神的工匠所造，被视为具有强大魔力。

Very well: put it down to coincidence. Deny any connexion between the hump-backed herald on the box (proclaiming the sovereignty of the Akan Triple Moon-goddess, and set in a ring of brass animals representing Akan clan totems) and myself, who suddenly became obsessed by the European White Goddess, wrote about her clan totems in the Argonaut context, and now had thrust upon me ancient secrets of her cult in Wales, Ireland and elsewhere. I was altogether unaware that the box celebrated the Goddess Ngame, that the Helladic Greeks, including the primitive Athenians, were racially linked with Ngame’s people – Libyan Berbers, known as the Garamantians, who moved south from the Sahara to the Niger in the eleventh century AD, and there intermarried with negroes. Or that Ngame herself was a Moon-goddess, and that the White Goddess of Greece and Western Europe shared her attributes. I knew only that Herodotus recognized the Libyan Neith as Athene.
好吧：把这归于巧合。否认铜盒上的驼背传令官（宣示阿坎三月女神之主权，置于一圈代表阿坎氏族图腾的铜动物中间）与我之间有任何联系——我突然被欧洲白女神所困，在阿尔戈英雄的语境中写了她的氏族图腾，如今又被强加了她在威尔士、爱尔兰及其他地方的古老密仪秘密。我完全不知道铜盒颂扬的是恩加梅女神，不知道希腊本土人（包括原始雅典人）与恩加梅的族人——利比亚柏柏尔人，即加拉曼特人（Garamantians）——有种族联系，他们在公元十一世纪从撒哈拉南迁至尼日尔河，与黑人通婚。也不知道恩加梅本人就是月神，而希腊和西欧的白女神与她共享属性。我只知道希罗多德将利比亚的奈特（Neith）认作雅典娜。

On returning to Majorca soon after the War, I worked again at The Roebuck in the Thicket, now called The White Goddess, and wrote more particularly about the Sacred King as the Moon-goddess’s divine victim; holding that every Muse-poet must, in a sense, die for the Goddess whom he adores, just as the King died. Old Georg Schwarz, a German-Jewish collector, had bequeathed me five or six more Akan gold-weights, among them a mummy-like figurine with one large eye. It has since been identified by experts on West African art as the Akan King’s okrafo priest. I had suggested in my book that, in early Mediterranean society, the King fell a sacrifice at the end of his term. But later (to judge from Greek and Latin myths) he won executive power as the Queen’s chief minister and the privilege of sacrificing a surrogate. The same governmental change, I have since learned, took place after the matriarchal Akan arrived at the Gold Coast. In Bono, Asante, and other near-by states, the King’s surrogate victim was called the ‘okrafo priest’. Kjersmeier, the famous Danish expert on African art, who has handled ten thousand of these gold-weights, tells me that he never saw another like mine. Dismiss it as a coincidence, if you please, that the okrafo figurine lay beside the herald on the gold box, while I wrote about the Goddess’s victims.
战后不久回到马略卡后，我重新着手《灌木丛中的獐鹿》——现改名为《白女神》——更着重地写了神圣国王作为月女神的神圣牺牲者；主张每一位缪斯诗人在某种意义上都必须为他所崇拜的女神而死，正如国王死去一样。老乔治·施瓦茨（Georg Schwarz），一位德裔犹太收藏家，遗赠给我五六件阿坎金砝码，其中有一尊独眼的木乃伊式小人像。后来经西非艺术专家鉴定为阿坎国王的奥克拉福祭司（okrafo priest）。我在书中曾提出，在早期地中海社会中，国王在任期结束时被献祭。但后来（从希腊和拉丁神话判断）他赢得了行政权力，成为王后的首席大臣，并获得了献祭替身的特权。我后来得知，母系阿坎人到达黄金海岸后也发生了同样的政体变化。在博诺（Bono）、阿散蒂（Asante）及其他邻近邦国，国王的替身牺牲被称为「奥克拉福祭司」。著名的丹麦非洲艺术专家谢尔斯迈尔（Kjersmeier），经手过上万件金砝码，告诉我他从未见过与我这件相同的。如果你愿意，就把奥克拉福小人像放在金盒上的传令官旁边、而我在书写女神的牺牲者这一事实当作巧合吧。

After The White Goddess had been published, a Barcelona antiquary read my Claudius novels and invited me to choose myself a stone for a seal-ring from a collection of Roman gems recently bought. Among them was a stranger, a banded carnelian seal of the Argonaut period, engraved with a royal stag galloping towards a thicket, and a crescent moon on its flank! Dismiss that as a coincidence, too, if you please.
《白女神》出版后，巴塞罗那一位古董商读了我的克劳狄乌斯小说，邀请我从他新购入的一批罗马宝石中自选一枚做印章戒指。其中有一枚异品——阿尔戈英雄时代的条纹红玉髓印章，刻着一头雄鹿奔向灌木丛，鹿侧有一弯新月！如果你愿意，也把这件事当作巧合吧。

Chains of more-than-coincidence occur so often in my life that, if I am forbidden to call them supernatural hauntings, let me call them a habit. Not that I like the word ‘supernatural’; I find these happenings natural enough, though superlatively unscientific.
超过巧合的连锁在我生命中如此频繁地发生，以至于如果我被禁止称之为超自然作祟，那就让我称之为习惯吧。并非我喜欢「超自然」一词；我觉得这些事件足够自然，尽管极不科学。

In scientific terms, no god at all can be proved to exist, but only beliefs in gods, and the effects of such beliefs on worshippers. The concept of a creative goddess was banned by Christian theologians almost two thousand years ago, and by Jewish theologians long before that. Most scientists, for social convenience, are God-worshippers; though I cannot make out why a belief in a Father-god’s authorship of the universe, and its laws, seems any less unscientific than a belief in a Mother-goddess’s inspiration of this artificial system. Granted the first metaphor, the second follows logically – if these are no better than metaphors….
以科学术语而言，任何神的存在都无法被证明，只能证明对神的信仰及此类信仰对崇拜者的影响。创造性女神的概念几乎在两千年前被基督教神学家取缔，而在此之前更久就被犹太神学家取缔了。大多数科学家出于社会便利而崇拜上帝；尽管我不明白，信仰父神创造宇宙及其法则，为何似乎比信仰母神启发这一人造体系更不科学。若承认第一个隐喻，第二个便在逻辑上成立——如果这些不过是隐喻的话……

True poetic practice implies a mind so miraculously attuned and illuminated that it can form words, by a chain of more-than-coincidences, into a living entity – a poem that goes about on its own (for centuries after the author’s death, perhaps) affecting readers with its stored magic. Since the source of poetry’s creative power is not scientific intelligence, but inspiration – however this may be explained by scientists – one may surely attribute inspiration to the Lunar Muse, the oldest and most convenient European term for this source? By ancient tradition, the White Goddess becomes one with her human representative – a priestess, a prophetess, a queen-mother. No Muse-poet grows conscious of the Muse except by experience of a woman in whom the Goddess is to some degree resident; just as no Apollonian poet can perform his proper function unless he lives under a monarchy or a quasi-monarchy. A Muse-poet falls in love, absolutely, and his true love is for him the embodiment of the Muse. As a rule, the power of absolutely falling in love soon vanishes; and, as a rule, because the woman feels embarrassed by the spell she exercises over her poet-lover and repudiates it; he, in disillusion, turns to Apollo who, at least, can provide him with a livelihood and intelligent entertainment, and reneges before his middle ’twenties. But the real, perpetually obsessed Muse-poet distinguishes between the Goddess as manifest in the supreme power, glory, wisdom and love of woman, and the individual woman whom the Goddess may make her instrument for a month, a year, seven years, or even more. The Goddess abides; and perhaps he will again have knowledge of her through his experience of another woman.
真正的诗歌实践意味着一种如此奇迹般调谐和照亮的头脑，以至于它能通过一连串超过巧合的事件，将词语塑造为一个活的实体——一首在作者死后数世纪也许仍在自行游走的诗，以其储存的魔力影响读者。既然诗歌创造力的源泉不是科学智识而是灵感——无论科学家如何解释——人们难道不能将灵感归于月亮缪斯，这一最古老、最便利的欧洲术语？按照古老传统，白女神与她在人间的代表——女祭司、女先知、王母——合为一体。没有缪斯诗人能意识到缪斯，除非通过在一个女人身上体验到女神的某种程度驻在；正如没有阿波罗式诗人能履行其正当职能，除非他生活在一个君主制或准君主制之下。缪斯诗人会绝对地坠入爱河，他的真爱对他而言便是缪斯的化身。通常，绝对坠入爱河的力量很快消失；且通常是因为女人对她施加于诗人情人的法力感到尴尬而拒绝它；他在幻灭中转向阿波罗——后者至少能给他提供生计和智识娱乐——在二十五六岁之前叛逃。但真正的、永远被困扰的缪斯诗人区分女神（显现为女人的至高权力、荣耀、智慧与爱）与女神可能作为其工具一个月、一年、七年甚至更久的个别女人。女神永存；也许他还会通过另一个女人的经验再次认识她。

Being in love does not, and should not, blind the poet to the cruel side of woman’s nature – and many Muse-poems are written in helpless attestation of this by men whose love is no longer returned:
恋爱并不会也不应该使诗人对女人天性中残酷的一面视而不见——许多缪斯诗作是那些爱已不再被回报的男人在无助中写下的证明：

‘As ye came from the holy land
‘As ye came from the holy land（「你们从圣地来，）



Of Walsinghame,
Of Walsinghame,（沃尔辛厄姆的圣地，）



Met you not with my true love
Met you not with my true love（你们可曾遇见我的真爱）



By the way as ye came?’
By the way as ye came?’（在你们来的路上？」）





‘How should I know your true love,
‘How should I know your true love,（「我怎能认出你的真爱，）



That have met many a one
That have met many a one（我遇见过许许多多的人）



As I came from the holy land,
As I came from the holy land,（当我从圣地来，）



That have come, that have gone?’
That have come, that have gone?’（来了又走了的人？」）





‘She is neither white nor brown,
‘She is neither white nor brown,（「她既不白也不褐，）



But as the heavens fair;
But as the heavens fair;（而是如天空般明媚；）

There is none hath her divine form（地上空中无人拥有）



In the earth, in the air.’
In the earth, in the air.’（她那神圣的身形。」）

‘Such a one did I meet, good sir,（「我确实遇见了这样一位，好先生，）



Such an angelic face,

Who like a nymph, like a queen, did appear（她如宁芙、如女王般现身）



In her gait, in her grace.’
In her gait, in her grace.’（在她的步态中，在她的优雅中。」）
