Stage 3: Separation of the spirit-body for independent existence
第三阶段：灵体分离以独立存在



Stage 4: The centre in the midst of conditions
第四阶段：条件之中的中心

[48] Psychiatrists are always ready to believe in toxins and the like, and even to explain schizophrenia in these terms, putting next to no emphasis on the psychic contents as such. On the other hand, in psychogenic disturbances (hysteria, obsessional neurosis, etc.), where toxic effects and cell degeneration are out of the question, split-off complexes are to be found similar to those occurring in somnambulistic states. Freud would like to explain these spontaneous split-offs as due to unconscious repression of sexuality, but this explanation is by no means valid in all cases, because contents that the conscious mind cannot assimilate can emerge just as spontaneously out of the unconscious, and in these cases the repression theory is inadequate. Moreover, their autonomy can be observed in daily life, in affects that obstinately obtrude themselves against our will and, in spite of the most strenuous efforts to repress them, overwhelm the ego and force it under their control. No wonder the primitive sees in these moods a state of possession or sets them down to a loss of soul. Our colloquial speech reflects the same thing when we say: “I don’t know what has got into him today,” “he is possessed of the devil,” “he is beside himself,” etc. Even legal practice recognizes a degree of diminished responsibility in a state of affect. Autonomous psychic contents are thus quite common experiences for us. Such contents have a disintegrating effect upon consciousness.
[48] 精神科医生总是乐于相信毒素之类的东西，甚至以此来解释精神分裂症，几乎不强调心理内容本身。另一方面，在心因性障碍（癔症、强迫症等）中，当毒效和细胞退化不可能是问题时，同样可以发现类似于梦游状态中出现的分裂情结。弗洛伊德想将这些自发分裂解释为性冲动的无意识压抑所致，但这一解释并非在所有案例中都成立，因为意识无法同化的内容同样可以自发地从无意识中涌出，在这些案例中压抑理论是不够的。而且，它们的自主性可以在日常生活中观察到——在那些顽固地违背我们意志而强入的情感中，在尽管最极力压制仍压制不住、压倒自我并迫使其受控于其下的情感中。难怪原始人在这些情绪中看到附体状态，或将其归因于失魂。我们的俗语也反映了同样的事："我不知道他今天怎么了"、"他被魔鬼附身了"、"他己不由己"等等。甚至法律实践也在情感状态下承认一定程度的责任能力减弱。因此，自主的心理内容对我们来说是相当常见的经验。这类内容对意识有瓦解作用。

[49] But besides the ordinary, familiar affects there are subtler, more complex emotional states that can no longer be described as affects pure and simple but are fragmentary psychic systems. The more complicated they are, the more they have the character of personalities. As constituents of the psychic personality, they necessarily have the character of “persons.” Such fragmentary systems are to be found especially in mental diseases, in cases of psychogenic splitting of the personality (double personality), and of course in mediumistic phenomena. They are also encountered in the phenomenology of religion. Many of the earlier gods developed from “persons” into personified ideas, and finally into abstract ideas. Activated unconscious contents always appear at first as projections upon the outside world, but in the course of mental development they are gradually assimilated by consciousness and reshaped into conscious ideas that then forfeit their originally autonomous and personal character. As we know, some of the old gods have become, via astrology, nothing more than descriptive attributes (martial, jovial, saturnine, erotic, logical, lunatic, and so on).
[49] 但除了普通的、熟悉的情感之外，还有更微妙、更复杂的情绪状态，它们已不能再被描述为纯粹的情感，而是碎片式的心理系统。它们越复杂，就越具有人格特征。作为心理人格的组成部分，它们必然具有"人"的特征。这类碎片系统尤其在精神疾病、人格的心因性分裂（双重人格）案例中，当然也在灵媒现象中被发现。它们也出现在宗教现象学中。许多早期的神从"人"发展为人格化观念，最终成为抽象观念。被激活的无意识内容起初总是作为对外部世界的投射而出现，但在心理发展过程中逐渐被意识同化，并被重塑为意识观念，从而丧失其原初的自主性和人格特征。如我们所知，一些旧神通过占星学变成了不过是描述性的属性（威武的、欢乐的、阴都的、色情的、逻辑的、疯癫的等等）。

[50] The instructions of The Tibetan Book of the Dead in particular help us to see how great is the danger that consciousness will be disintegrated by these figures. Again and again the dead are instructed not to take these shapes for truth, not to confuse their murky appearance with the pure white light of Dharmakaya (the divine body of truth). That is to say, they are not to project the one light of highest consciousness into concretized figures and dissolve it into a plurality of autonomous fragmentary systems. If there were no danger of this, and if these systems did not represent menacingly autonomous and disintegrative tendencies, such urgent instructions would not be necessary. Allowing for the simpler, polytheistic attitude of the Eastern mind, these instructions would be almost the equivalent of warning a Christian not to let himself be blinded by the illusion of a personal God, let alone by the Trinity and the host of angels and saints.
[50] 《西藏度亡经》的指导特别有助于我们看到意识被这些形象瓦解的危险有多大。亡者一再被告诫不要将这些形体当作真实，不要将其浑浊的面貌与法身（神圣真理之体）的纯白光相混淆。也就是说，不要将最高意识的光投射到具象化的形象中并将其消解为多数自主的碎片系统。如果不存在这种危险，如果这些系统不代表令人威胁的自主和瓦解趋势，这样的迫切指导就不是必要的。考虑到东方心灵的更简单的多神论态度，这些指导几乎等同于警告基督徒不要被人格神的幻象所蒙蔽，更不用说三一神和众天使圣徒了。

[51] If tendencies towards dissociation were not inherent in the human psyche, fragmentary psychic systems would never have been split off; in other words, neither spirits nor gods would ever have come into existence. That is also the reason why our time has become so utterly godless and profane: we lack all knowledge of the unconscious psyche and pursue the cult of consciousness to the exclusion of all else. Our true religion is a monotheism of consciousness, a possession by it, coupled with a fanatical denial of the existence of fragmentary autonomous systems. But we differ from the Buddhist yoga doctrines in that we even deny that these systems are experienceable. This entails a great psychic danger, because the autonomous systems then behave like any other repressed contents: they necessarily induce wrong attitudes since the repressed material reappears in consciousness in a spurious form. This is strikingly evident in every case of neurosis and also holds true for the collective psychic phenomena. Our time has committed a fatal error; we believe we can criticize the facts of religion intellectually. Like Laplace, we think God is a hypothesis that can be subjected to intellectual treatment, to be affirmed or denied. We completely forget that the reason mankind believes in the “daemon” has nothing whatever to do with external factors, but is simply due to a naïve awareness of the tremendous inner effect of autonomous fragmentary systems. This effect is not abolished by criticizing it—or rather, the name we have given it—or by describing the name as false. The effect is collectively present all the time; the autonomous systems are always at work, for the fundamental structure of the unconscious is not affected by the deviations of our ephemeral consciousness.
[51] 如果解离趋势不是人性中固有的，碎片式心理系统就永远不会被分裂出来；换言之，既不会有灵也不会有神出现。这也是为什么我们这个时代变得如此彻底无神和亵渎的原因：我们缺乏对无意识心灵的一切知识，一味追求意识崇拜而排斥一切其他。我们真正的宗教是意识的一种一神论——被它所附体，同时狂热地否认碎片式自主系统的存在。但我们与佛教瑜伽教义的不同在于我们甚至否认这些系统是可以被经验的。这带来一种巨大的心理危险，因为自主系统随后就像其他被压抑的内容一样行事：它们必然引入错误的态度，因为被压抑的材料以虚假的形式重新出现在意识中。这在每个神经症案例中都是明显可见的，对集体心理现象也同样成立。我们这个时代犯了一个致命的错误：我们以为可以从理智上批判宗教事实。像拉普拉斯一样，我们认为上帝是一个可以受理智处理、被肯定或否定的假设。我们完全忘记了人类之所以信仰"精灵"与外部因素毫无关系，而仅仅是因为对自主碎片系统之巨大内在效果的一种朴素意识。这一效果不会因对它的批判——或者更确切地说对我们给它取的名字的批判——或因宣称这个名字是假的而被取消。效果始终集体性地存在；自主系统一直在运作，因为无意识的基本结构不受我们瞬息意识偏向的影响。

[52] If we deny the existence of the autonomous systems, imagining that we have got rid of them by a mere critique of the name, then the effect which they still continue to exert can no longer be understood, nor can they be assimilated to consciousness. They become an inexplicable source of disturbance which we finally assume must exist somewhere outside ourselves. The resultant projection creates a dangerous situation in that the disturbing effects are now attributed to a wicked will outside ourselves, which is naturally not to be found anywhere but with our neighbour de l’autre côté de la rivière. This leads to collective delusions, “incidents,” revolutions, war—in a word, to destructive mass psychoses.
[52] 如果我们否认自主系统的存在，以为仅仅通过批判名字就能摆脱它们，那么它们仍在施加的效果就无法被理解，也无法被同化到意识中。它们成为一个不可解释的干扰之源，我们最终假设它一定存在于我们之外的某处。由此产生的投射创造了一种危险局面：干扰效果现在被归因于我们之外的某个邪恶意志——这个意志自然在任何地方都找不到，除了在我们河对岸的邻人那里。这导致集体妄想、"事件"、革命、战争——总之，导致破坏性的大众精神病。

[53] Insanity is possession by an unconscious content that, as such, is not assimilated to consciousness, nor can it be assimilated since the very existence of such contents is denied. This attitude is equivalent to saying: “We no longer have any fear of God and believe that everything is to be judged by human standards.” This hybris or narrowness of consciousness is always the shortest way to the insane asylum. I recommend the excellent account of this problem in H. G. Wells’s novel Christina Alberta’s Father, and Schreber’s Memoirs of My Nervous Illness.
[53] 疯狂是被一个无意识内容所附体——这内容作为未被同化到意识中的东西，也无法被同化，因为这类内容的存在本身被否认了。这种态度等同于说："我们不再敬畏上帝，认为一切都应以人的标准来评判。"这种傲慢或意识的狭隘总是通往疯人院的最短路。我推荐 H. G. 威尔斯的小说《克里斯蒂娜·阿尔伯塔的父亲》和施雷伯的《我的神经疾病回忆录》中对这一问题的出色描述。

[54] It must stir a sympathetic chord in the enlightened European when it is said in the Hui Ming Ching that the “shapes formed by the spirit-fire are only empty colours and forms.” That sounds thoroughly European and seems to suit our reason to a T. We think we can congratulate ourselves on having already reached such a pinnacle of clarity, imagining that we have left all these phantasmal gods far behind. But what we have left behind are only verbal spectres, not the psychic facts that were responsible for the birth of the gods. We are still as much possessed by autonomous psychic contents as if they were Olympians. Today they are called phobias, obsessions, and so forth; in a word, neurotic symptoms. The gods have become diseases; Zeus no longer rules Olympus but rather the solar plexus, and produces curious specimens for the doctor’s consulting room, or disorders the brains of politicians and journalists who unwittingly let loose psychic epidemics on the world.
[54] 当《慧命经》说"精神之火所成之形不过空色空相"时，必定会拨动开明的欧洲人的同情之弦。这听起来彻底是欧洲式的，似乎完全合乎我们的理性。我们以为自己已经达到了如此清晰的高峰，以为已将所有这些幻影般之神远远抛在身后。但我们抛在身后的只是词语的幽灵，而非导致诸神诞生的心理事实。我们仍然像被奥林匹斯神祇附体一样被自主心理内容所附。今天它们被称为恐惧症、强迫症等等；总之，神经症症状。诸神已变成了疾病；宙斯不再统治奥林匹斯，而是统治太阳神经丛，为医生的诊室制造奇特的标本，或搅乱政客和记者的大脑——他们不知不觉地向世界释放心理流行病。

[55] So it is better for Western man if he does not know too much about the secret insights of the Oriental sages to begin with, for, as I have said, it would be a case of the “right means in the hands of the wrong man.” Instead of allowing himself to be convinced once more that the daemon is an illusion, he ought to experience once more the reality of this illusion. He should learn to acknowledge these psychic forces anew, and not wait until his moods, nervous states, and delusions make it clear in the most painful way that he is not the only master in his house. His dissociative tendencies are actual psychic personalities possessing a differential reality. They are “real” when they are not recognized as real and consequently projected; they are relatively real when they are brought into relationship with consciousness (in religious terms, when a cult exists); but they are unreal to the extent that consciousness detaches itself from its contents. This last stage, however, is reached only when life has been lived so exhaustively and with such devotion that no obligations remain unfulfilled, when no desires that cannot safely be sacrificed stand in the way of inner detachment from the world. It is futile to lie to ourselves about this. Wherever we are still attached, we are still possessed; and when we are possessed, there is one stronger than us who possesses us. (“Verily I say unto thee, thou shalt by no means come out thence, until thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.”) It is not a matter of indifference whether one calls something a “mania” or a “god.” To serve a mania is detestable and undignified, but to serve a god is full of meaning and promise because it is an act of submission to a higher, invisible, and spiritual being. The personification enables us to see the relative reality of the autonomous system, and not only makes its assimilation possible but also depotentiates the daemonic forces of life. When the god is not acknowledged, egomania develops, and out of this mania comes sickness.
[55] 因此，西方人最好不要一开始就知道太多东方圣贤的秘密洞见，因为正如我所说，那会是"正确的方法落入错误之人手中"的情况。他不应再次被说服精灵是幻觉，而应当再次经验这一幻觉的现实性。他应当学会重新承认这些心理力量，而不是等到他的情绪、神经状态和妄想以最痛苦的方式表明他不是自己家中唯一的主人。他的解离趋势是具有微差现实性的实际心理人格。当它们不被承认为真实并因而被投射时，它们是"真实的"；当它们被带入与意识的关系中时（用宗教术语说，当存在崇拜时），它们是相对真实的；但当意识从其内容中超脱出来时，它们就是不真实的。然而，这最后一个阶段只有当生命被如此充分且如此奉献地生活过——以至没有未尽的义务，没有不能安全牺牲的欲望阻挡内在超世——才能达到。在这一点上对自己撒谎是徒劳的。只要我们还有执着，我们就还被附体；当我们被附体时，就有一个比我们更强者在附着我们。（"我实在告诉你，若还不还清最后一文钱，你绝不能从那里出来。"）将某物称为"狂躁"还是"神"并非无关紧要。服务于狂躁是可憎和不体面的，但服务于神则充满意义和希望，因为这是对一个更高的、不可见的、灵性之物的顺服行为。人格化使我们能够看到自主系统的相对现实性，不仅使其同化成为可能，而且贬低了生命的精灵力量。当神不被承认时，自我狂躁便发展起来，从这种狂躁中产生疾病。

[56] Yoga takes acknowledgment of the gods as something self-evident. Its secret instruction is intended only for those whose consciousness is struggling to disentangle itself from the daemonic forces of life in order to enter into the ultimate undivided unity, the “centre of emptiness,” where “dwells the god of utmost emptiness and life,” as our text says.3 “To hear such a teaching is difficult to attain in thousands of aeons.” Evidently the veil of Maya cannot be lifted by a merely rational resolve; it requires a most thorough going and persevering preparation consisting in the full payment of all debts to life. For as long as unconditional attachment through cupiditas exists, the veil is not lifted and the heights of a consciousness free of contents and free of illusion are not attained; nor can any trick nor any deceit bring this about. It is an ideal that can ultimately be realized only in death. Until then there are the real and relatively real figures of the unconscious.
[56] 瑜伽将对诸神的承认视为理所当然之事。其秘密指导只面向那些其意识正在挣扎着从生命的精灵力量中解脱出来以进入最终不可分割的统一、"空之中心"的人——"在那里住着至空与生命之神"，如我们的文本所说。3"得闻此法，千万劫中难遇。"显然，摩耶之幕不能仅仅通过理性的决心来掀开；它需要一种最彻底、最坚持的准备——包括向生命偿还一切债务。只要通过食欲而存在的无条件执着还在，幕就不被掀开，那无内容的、无幻象的意识的顶峰就达不到；任何诡计或任何欺编也无法实现这一点。这是一个最终只能在死亡中实现的理想。在那之前，存在着无意识的真实和相对真实的形象。





B. ANIMUS AND ANIMA
B. 阿尼玛斯与阿尼玛


[57] According to our text, among the figures of the unconscious there are not only the gods but also the animus and anima. The word hun is translated by Wilhelm as animus. And indeed, the term “animus” seems appropriate for hun, the character for which is made up of the sign for “clouds” and that for “demon.” Thus hun means “cloud-demon,” a higher breath-soul belonging to the yang principle and therefore masculine. After death, hun rises upward and becomes shen, the “expanding and self-revealing” spirit or god. “Anima,” called p’o, and written with the characters for “white” and “demon,” that is, “white ghost,” belongs to the lower, earthbound, bodily soul, the yin principle, and is therefore feminine. After death, it sinks downward and becomes kuei (demon), often explained as “the one who returns” (i.e., to earth), a revenant, a ghost. The fact that the animus and anima part after death and go their ways independently shows that, for the Chinese consciousness, they are distinguishable psychic factors; originally they were united in “the one effective, true human nature,” but in the “house of the Creative” they are two. “The animus is in the heavenly heart.” “By day it lives in the eyes [i.e., in consciousness]; at night it houses in the liver.” It is “that which we have received from the great emptiness, that which is identical in form with the primal beginning.” The anima, on the other hand, is the “energy of the heavy and the turbid”; it clings to the bodily, fleshly heart. Its effects are “sensuous desires and impulses to anger.” “Whoever is sombre and moody on waking . . . is fettered to the anima.”4
[57] 根据我们的文本，在无意识的形象中不仅有诸神，还有阿尼玛斯和阿尼玛。"魂"字被威廉译为 animus（阿尼玛斯）。确实，"animus"一词似乎适用于魂——其字形由"云"和"鬼"两个符号组成。因此魂意为"云鬼"，是一种属于阳原则的更高气息之魂，因而是男性的。死后，魂上升成为神——"舒展而自显"的灵或神明。"阿尼玛"称为魄，字形由"白"和"鬼"组成，即"白鬼"，属于低等的、扎根大地的身体之魂，即阴原则，因而是女性的。死后，它下沉成为鬼（"归"者，即归于大地者），一种亡魂、鬼。阿尼玛斯和阿尼玛在死后分离并各自独立行走这一事实表明，对于中国意识来说，它们是可区分的心理因素；它们原本统一于"一灵真性"之中，但在"干之家中"则是二者。"魂在天心。""昼居于目【即在意识中】；夜宿于肝。"它是"我们从太虚中所得之物，与太初同形者"。另一方面，阿尼玛是"重浊之气"；它依附着肉体的、有形的心。其效果是"情欲与忿怒之冲动"。"醒时闷闷不乐者……被魄所缚。"4

[58] Many years ago, before Wilhelm acquainted me with this text, I used the term “anima”5 in a way quite analogous to the Chinese definition of p’o, and of course entirely apart from any metaphysical premise. To the psychologist, the anima is not a transcendental being but something quite within the range of experience, as the Chinese definition makes clear: affective states are immediate experiences. Why, then, speak of the anima and not simply of moods? The reason is that affects have an autonomous character, and therefore most people are under their power. But affects are delimitable contents of consciousness, parts of the personality. As such, they partake of its character and can easily be personified—a process that still continues today, as I have shown. The personification is not an idle invention, since a person roused by affect does not show a neutral character but a quite distinct one, entirely different from his ordinary character. Careful investigation has shown that the affective character of a man has feminine traits. From this psychological fact derives the Chinese doctrine of the p’o soul as well as my own concept of the anima. Deeper introspection or ecstatic experience reveals the existence of a feminine figure in the unconscious, hence the feminine name: anima, psyche, Seele. The anima can be defined as the image or archetype or deposit of all the experiences of man with woman. As we know, the poets have often sung the anima’s praises.6 The connection of anima with ghost in the Chinese concept is of interest to parapsychologists inasmuch as mediumistic “controls” are very often of the opposite sex.
[58] 多年前，在威廉让我熟悉这一文本之前，我就以一种与中国对魄的定义完全类似的方式使用了"阿尼玛"5这一术语——当然完全独立于任何形而上学前提。对心理学家来说，阿尼玛不是一个超验存在，而是完全在经验范围之内的事物——正如中国的定义所表明的：情感状态是直接的经验。那么，为什么说阿尼玛而不简单地说情绪呢？原因是情感具有自主特征，因此大多数人处于其权力之下。但情感是意识的可界定内容，是人格的组成部分。作为这样的东西，它们参与人格的特征，可以很容易地被人格化——这一过程至今仍在继续，正如我所表明的。人格化并非无用的发明，因为被情感激起的人并不表现出中性性格，而是一个相当独特的、与其平常性格完全不同的性格。仔细的研究表明，男性的情感性格具有女性特征。从这一心理事实中产生了中国关于魄的学说以及我自己的阿尼玛概念。更深入的内省或出神经验揭示无意识中存在一个女性形象，因此有了女性化的名称：阿尼玛、psyche、Seele。阿尼玛可以定义为男性与女性一切经验的形象或原型或沉积。如我们所知，诗人们常常赞颂阿尼玛。6阿尼玛在中国概念中与鬼的联系引起超心理学家的兴趣，因为灵媒的"控制灵"往往为异性。

[59] Although Wilhelm’s translation of hun as “animus” seems justified to me, nonetheless I had important reasons for choosing the term “Logos” for a man’s “spirit,” for his clarity of consciousness and his rationality, rather than the otherwise appropriate expression “animus.” Chinese philosophers are spared certain difficulties that aggravate the task of the Western psychologist. Like all mental and spiritual activity in ancient times, Chinese philosophy was exclusively a component of the masculine world. Its concepts were never understood psychologically, and therefore were never examined as to how far they also apply to the feminine psyche. But the psychologist cannot possibly ignore the existence of woman and her special psychology. For these reasons I would prefer to translate hun as it appears in man by “Logos.” Wilhelm in his translation uses Logos for hsing, which can also be translated as “essence of human nature” or “creative consciousness.” After death, hun becomes shen, “spirit,” which is very close, in the philosophical sense, to hsing. Since the Chinese concepts are not logical in our sense of the word, but are intuitive ideas, their meanings can only be elicited from the ways in which they are used and from the constitution of the written characters, or from such relationships as obtain between hun and shen. Hun, then, would be the light of consciousness and reason in man, originally coming from the logos spermatikos of hsing, and returning after death through shen to the Tao. Used in this sense the expression “Logos” would be especially appropriate, since it includes the idea of a universal being, and thus covers the fact that man’s clarity of consciousness and rationality are something universal rather than individually unique. The Logos principle is nothing personal, but is in the deepest sense impersonal, and thus in sharp contrast to the anima, which is a personal demon expressing itself in thoroughly personal moods (“animosity”!).
[59] 尽管威廉将魂译为"animus"在我看来是合理的，但我仍有重要理由选择"逻各斯"一词来表示男性的"灵"——他的意识清晰度和理性——而不是用原本也合适的"animus"一词。中国哲学家避免了某些加重西方心理学家任务的困难。像古代一切精神活动一样，中国哲学完全是男性世界的组成部分。其概念从未被从心理学上理解，因此从未被检验它们在多大程度上也适用于女性心灵。但心理学家不可能忽视女性的存在及其特殊心理学。出于这些原因，我更倾向于将魂在男性中的表现译为"逻各斯"。威廉在其译本中用逻各斯来翻译性——性也可以译为"人性之本质"或"创造意识"。死后，魂成为神——"灵"，在哲学意义上与性非常接近。由于中国概念不是我们意义上的逻辑概念，而是直觉观念，其含义只能从其使用方式和字形构造中，或从魂与神之间的关系中加以提取。那么，魂便是男性中的意识之光和理性之光，原初来自性的逻各斯·斯佩玛提克斯（logos spermatikos），死后通过神回归于道。在这个意义上使用，"逻各斯"这一表达将特别合适，因为它包含了一种普遍存在的观念，从而涵盖了以下事实：男性的意识清晰度和理性是某种普遍之物而非个人独特之物。逻各斯原理不是个人的，而是在最深层意义上的非个人之物，因此与阿尼玛形成鲜明对比——后者是一个以彻底个人的情绪表达自身的个人精灵（"敌意"！）。

[60] In view of these psychological facts, I have reserved the term “animus” strictly for women, because, to answer a famous question, mulier non habet animam, sed animum. Feminine psychology exhibits an element that is the counterpart of a man’s anima. Primarily, it is not of an affective nature but is a quasi-intellectual factor best described by the word “prejudice.” The conscious side of woman corresponds to the emotional side of man, not to his “mind.” Mind makes up the “soul,” or better, the “animus” of woman, and just as the anima of a man consists of inferior relatedness, full of affect, so the animus of woman consists of inferior judgments, or better, opinions. As it is made up of a plurality of preconceived opinions, the animus is far less susceptible of personification by a single figure, but appears more often as a group or crowd. (A good example of this from parapsychology is the “Imperator” group in the case of Mrs. Piper.7) On a low level the animus is an inferior Logos, a caricature of the differentiated masculine mind, just as on a low level the anima is a caricature of the feminine Eros. To pursue the parallel further, we could say that just as hun corresponds to hsing, translated by Wilhelm as Logos, so the Eros of woman corresponds to ming, “fate” or “destiny,” interpreted by Wilhelm as Eros. Eros is an interweaving; Logos is differentiating knowledge, clarifying light. Eros is relatedness, Logos is discrimination and detachment. Hence the inferior Logos of woman’s animus appears as something quite unrelated, as an inaccessible prejudice, or as an opinion which, irritatingly enough, has nothing to do with the essential nature of the object.
[60] 鉴于这些心理事实，我将"animus"（阿尼玛斯）一词严格保留给女性使用，因为，回答一个著名的问题，女人没有anima（阿尼玛），而有animus（阿尼玛斯）。女性心理学展示了一种与男性阿尼玛相对应的元素。它主要不是情感性质的，而是一种准理智因素，最好用"偏见"一词来描述。女性的意识面对应于男性的情感面，而非其"理智"。理智构成了女性的"灵魂"，或更确切地说"阿尼玛斯"——正如男性的阿尼玛由低劣的、充满情感的关系性构成一样，女性的阿尼玛斯由低劣的判断，或更确切说由意见构成。由于它由众多先入之见构成，阿尼玛斯远不像单一形象那样容易被人格化，而是更常以群体或人群的形式出现。（超心理学中的一个好例子是派珀夫人案例中的"Imperator"群体。7）在低层次上，阿尼玛斯是一种低劣的逻各斯，是分化了的男性理智的滑稽模仿，正如在低层次上阿尼玛是女性爱洛斯的滑稽模仿。进一步推进这一类比，我们可以说：正如魂对应于性——威廉将其译为逻各斯——女性的爱洛斯则对应于命——"命运"或"定数"，威廉将其解释为爱洛斯。爱洛斯是交织；逻各斯是分化的知识、澄清之光。爱洛斯是关联，逻各斯是辨别和超脱。因此，女性阿尼玛斯的低劣逻各斯表现为某种完全不相关的东西——一种不可接近的偏见，或一种与客体本质无关的意见——这令人恼火。

[61] I have often been accused of personifying the anima and animus as mythology does, but this accusation would be justified only if it could be proved that I concretize these concepts in a mythological manner for psychological use. I must declare once and for all that the personification is not an invention of mine, but is inherent in the nature of the phenomena. It would be unscientific to overlook the fact that the anima is a psychic, and therefore a personal, autonomous system. None of the people who make the charge against me would hesitate for a second to say, “I dreamed of Mr. X,” whereas, strictly speaking, he dreamed only of a representation of Mr. X. The anima is nothing but a representation of the personal nature of the autonomous system in question. What the nature of this system is in a transcendental sense, that is, beyond the bounds of experience, we cannot know.
[61] 我常被指责像神话那样将阿尼玛和阿尼玛斯人格化，但这一指责只有在能够证明我以神话方式将这些概念具象化用于心理目的时才能成立。我必须一劳永逸地声明：人格化不是我的发明，而是现象本质所固有的。忽视阿尼玛是一个心理的、因此是个人的自主系统这一事实，将是不科学的。指控我的人中没有一个会犹豫一秒钟说"我梦见了某先生"，而严格说来他只是梦见了一个某先生的表象。阿尼玛不过是上述自主系统之个人性质的表象。这一系统在超验意义上——即超越经验范围——的本质是什么，我们无法知道。

[62] I have defined the anima as a personification of the unconscious in general, and have taken it as a bridge to the unconscious, in other words, as a function of relationship to the unconscious. There is an interesting point in our text in this connection. The text says that consciousness (that is, the personal consciousness) comes from the anima. Since the Western mind is based wholly on the standpoint of consciousness, it must define the anima in the way I have done. But the East, based as it is on the standpoint of the unconscious, sees consciousness as an effect of the anima. And there can be no doubt that consciousness does originate in the unconscious. This is something we are apt to forget, and therefore we are always attempting to identify the psyche with consciousness, or at least to represent the unconscious as a derivative or an effect of consciousness (as in the Freudian repression theory). But, for the reasons given above, it is essential that we do not detract from the reality of the unconscious, and that the figures of the unconscious be understood as real and effective factors. The person who has understood what is meant by psychic reality need have no fear that he has fallen back into primitive demonology. If the unconscious figures are not acknowledged as spontaneous agents, we become victims of a one-sided belief in the power of consciousness, leading finally to acute tension. A catastrophe is then bound to happen because, for all our consciousness, the dark powers of the psyche have been overlooked. It is not we who personify them; they have a personal nature from the very beginning. Only when this is thoroughly recognized can we think of depersonalizing them, of “subjugating the anima,” as our text expresses it.
[62] 我将阿尼玛定义为无意识一般的人格化，并将其作为通往无意识的桥梁，换言之，作为与无意识的关联功能。在这一方面我们的文本中有一个有趣的点。文本说意识（即个人意识）来自阿尼玛。由于西方心灵完全基于意识的立场，它必须以我所做的方式来定义阿尼玛。但东方基于无意识的立场，将意识视为阿尼玛的效果。而毫无疑问，意识确实源于无意识。这是我们容易忘记的，因此我们总是试图将心灵等同于意识，或至少将无意识表述为意识的派生物或效果（如弗洛伊德的压抑理论）。但出于上述原因，我们不应减损无意识的现实性，无意识的形象应被理解为真实的、有效的因素。理解了心理现实之含义的人不必担心自己退回到了原始的魔鬼学。如果无意识形象不被承认为自发行动者，我们就会成为片面相信意识力量之下的受害者，最终导致尖锐的紧张。灾难必然会发生，因为尽管我们有意识，心灵中的黑暗力量却被忽视了。不是我们将它们人格化；它们从一开始就具有个人性质。只有当这一点被彻底认识到，我们才能考虑去人格化它们，即如我们的文本所说的"降伏魄"。

[63] Here again we find an enormous difference between Buddhism and the Western attitude of mind, and again there is a dangerous semblance of agreement. Yoga teaching rejects all fantasy products and we do the same, but the East does so for entirely different reasons. In the East there is an abundance of conceptions and teachings that give full expression to the creative fantasy; in fact, protection is needed against an excess of it. We, on the other hand, regard fantasy as worthless subjective day-dreaming. Naturally the figures of the unconscious do not appear in the form of abstractions stripped of all imaginative trappings; on the contrary, they are embedded in a web of fantasies of extraordinary variety and bewildering profusion. The East can reject these fantasies because it has long since extracted their essence and condensed it in profound teachings. But we have never even experienced these fantasies, much less extracted their quintessence. We still have a large stretch of experience to catch up with, and only when we have found the sense in apparent nonsense can we separate the valuable from the worthless. We can be sure that the essence we extract from our experience will be quite different from what the East offers us today. The East came to its knowledge of inner things in childlike ignorance of the external world. We, on the other hand, shall explore the psyche and its depths supported by an immense knowledge of history and science. At present our knowledge of the external world is the greatest obstacle to introspection, but the psychological need will overcome all obstructions. We are already building up a psychology, a science that gives us the key to the very things that the East discovered—and discovered only through abnormal psychic states.
[63] 在这里我们再次发现佛教与西方心态之间的巨大差异，同时又存在一种危险的一致假象。瑜伽教义排斥一切幻想产物，我们也这样做，但东方出于完全不同的理由。在东方，有大量的概念和教义充分表达了创造性幻想；实际上，需要保护以免其过度。我们则将幻想视为无价值的主观白日梦。自然，无意识的形象不会以剧除一切想象装饰的抽象形式出现；相反，它们嵌入在变化万千、令人困惑的幻想之网中。东方可以排斥这些幻想，因为它早已提取了其精华并凝结为深刻的教义。但我们从未经验过这些幻想，更不用说提取其精精了。我们还有一大段经验需要追赶，只有当我们在表面的无意义中找到了意义，才能将有价值的与无价值的分开。我们可以确信，我们从自己的经验中提取出的精华将与东方今天提供给我们的截然不同。东方是在对客观世界幼稚无知的状态下获得对内在事物的认识的。而我们则将在庞大的历史和科学知识的支撑下探索心灵及其深处。目前我们对客观世界的知识是内省的最大障碍，但心理需要将克服一切阻爵。我们已经在建立一种心理学——一门科学，它为我们提供了通往东方所发现之物——且仅仅通过异常心理状态才发现之物——的钥匙。





5. THE DETACHMENT OF CONSCIOUSNESS FROM THE OBJECT
5. 意识从客体中脱离


[64] By understanding the unconscious we free ourselves from its domination. That is really also the purpose of the instructions in our text. The pupil is taught to concentrate on the light of the innermost region and, at the same time, to free himself from all outer and inner entanglements. His vital impulses are guided towards a consciousness void of content, which nevertheless permits all contents to exist. The Hui Ming Ching1 says of this detachment:
[64] 通过理解无意识，我们从其支配中解放出来。这也正是我们文本中指导的真正目的。学习者被教导集中于最内在区域的光，同时从一切外在和内在的纠葛中解脱出来。他的生命冲动被引向一种空无内容的意识——这意识却允许一切内容存在。《慧命经》1对这种超脱说：

A halo of light surrounds the world of the law.
法界之光轮环绕，

We forget one another, quiet and pure, all-powerful and empty.
相忘于寂静清净，无量而空。

The emptiness is irradiated by the light of the heart of heaven.
虚空为天心之光所照耀。

The water of the sea is smooth and mirrors the moon in its surface.
海面平静如镜，映月于其上。

The clouds disappear in blue space; the mountains shine clear.
云消于碧空；山峦清明。

Consciousness reverts to contemplation; the moon-disk rests alone.
意识归于静观；月轮独圆。

[65] This description of fulfilment depicts a psychic state that can best be characterized as a detachment of consciousness from the world and a withdrawal to a point outside it, so to speak. Thus consciousness is at the same time empty and not empty. It is no longer preoccupied with the images of things but merely contains them. The fullness of the world which hitherto pressed upon it has lost none of its richness and beauty, but it no longer dominates. The magical claim of things has ceased because the interweaving of consciousness with world has come to an end. The unconscious is not projected any more, and so the primordial participation mystique with things is abolished. Consciousness is no longer preoccupied with compulsive plans but dissolves in contemplative vision.
[65] 这一圆满描述描绘了一种心理状态，可以最好地将其特征为意识从世界中超脱并退至世界之外的某一点。因此意识同时是空的又不是空的。它不再被事物的形象所占据，而只是包含它们。迄今为止压迫着它的世界之丰满并未失去其丰富和美丽，但它不再主导。事物的魔力要求已经停止，因为意识与世界的交织已经终结。无意识不再被投射，因此与事物的原始神秘参与被取消了。意识不再被强迫性的计划所占据，而是消融于静观的视野中。

[66] How did this effect come about? (We assume, of course, that the Chinese author was first of all not a liar; secondly, that he was of sound mind; and thirdly, that he was an unusually intelligent man.) To understand and explain this detachment, we must proceed by a roundabout way. It is an effect that cannot be simulated; nothing would be more childish than to make such a psychic state an object of aesthetic experiment. I know this effect very well from my practice; it is the therapeutic effect par excellence, for which I labour with my students and patients, and it consists in the dissolution of participation mystique. By a stroke of genius, Lévy-Bruhl singled out what he called participation mystique as being the hallmark of the primitive mentality.2 What he meant by it is simply the indefinitely large remnant of non-differentiation between subject and object, which is still so great among primitives that it cannot fail to strike our European consciousness very forcibly. When there is no consciousness of the difference between subject and object, an unconscious identity prevails. The unconscious is then projected into the object, and the object is introjected into the subject, becoming part of his psychology. Then plants and animals behave like human beings, human beings are at the same time animals, and everything is alive with ghosts and gods. Civilized man naturally thinks he is miles above these things. Instead of that, he is often identified with his parents throughout his life, or with his affects and prejudices, and shamelessly accuses others of the things he will not see in himself. He too has a remnant of primitive unconsciousness, of non-differentiation between subject and object. Because of this, he is magically affected by all manner of people, things, and circumstances, he is beset by disturbing influences nearly as much as the primitive and therefore needs just as many apotropaic charms. He no longer works magic with medicine bags, amulets, and animal sacrifices, but with tranquillizers, neuroses, rationalism, cult of the will, etc.
[66] 这一效果是如何产生的？（我们当然假定中国作者首先不是骗子；其次，他精神健全；第三，他是一个异常聪明的人。）要理解并解释这种超脱，我们必须走一条弯路。这是一种无法模拟的效果；将这样的心理状态作为美学实验的对象再幼稚不过了。我从实践中非常了解这一效果；它是我与学生和患者一同努力追求的治疗效果 par excellence，它在于神秘参与的消解。列维-布吕尔以其天才之笔将他所谓的神秘参与标示为原始心态的标志。2他所说的不过是主体与客体之间尚未分化的不确定大块残余——这在原始人中如此之大以至于不可能不给我们欧洲意识以强烈冲击。当对主体与客体之间的差异没有意识时，一种无意识的同一性便占主导。无意识被投射到客体中，客体被内摄到主体中，成为其心理学的一部分。于是植物和动物像人一样行为，人同时也是动物，一切都被鬼和神所赋予生命。文明人自然以为自己远远高于这些事物。然而，他一生常常与父母同一，或与其情感和偏见同一，并恬不知耻地指责别人那些他不愿在自己身上看到的东西。他也有原始无意识的残余，即主体与客体之间的未分化。正因如此，他被各种各样的人、事和环境以魔法方式所影响，他被干扰性影响所困扰几乎不亚于原始人，因此同样需要许多驱邪符咒。他不再用药袋、护符和动物牺牲来施法，而是用镇静剂、神经症、理性主义、意志崇拜等等。

[67] But if the unconscious can be recognized as a co-determining factor along with consciousness, and if we can live in such a way that conscious and unconscious demands are taken into account as far as possible, then the centre of gravity of the total personality shifts its position. It is then no longer in the ego, which is merely the centre of consciousness, but in the hypothetical point between conscious and unconscious. This new centre might be called the self. If the transposition is successful, it does away with the participation mystique and results in a personality that suffers only in the lower storeys, as it were, but in its upper storeys is singularly detached from painful as well as from joyful happenings.
[67] 但如果无意识可以被承认为与意识并列的共定因素，如果我们能以一种尽可能顾及意识和无意识要求的方式生活，那么整体人格的重心便会转移其位置。它不再在自我之中——自我不过是意识的中心——而在意识与无意识之间的假想点。这个新中心可以称为自性。如果这一移置成功，它便消除了神秘参与，产生出一种人格——这种人格仿佛只在底层受苦，而在其上层则异常超脱于痛苦和欢乐的事件。

[68] The production and birth of this superior personality is what is meant when our text speaks of the “holy fruit,” the “diamond body,” or any other kind of incorruptible body. Psychologically, these expressions symbolize an attitude that is beyond the reach of emotional entanglements and violent shocks—a consciousness detached from the world. I have reasons for believing that this attitude sets in after middle life and is a natural preparation for death. Death is psychologically as important as birth and, like it, is an integral part of life. What happens to the detached consciousness in the end is a question the psychologist cannot be expected to answer. Whatever his theoretical position he would hopelessly overstep the bounds of his scientific competence. He can only point out that the views of our text in regard to the timelessness of the detached consciousness are in harmony with the religious thought of all ages and with that of the overwhelming majority of mankind. Anyone who thought differently would be standing outside the human order and would, therefore, be suffering from a disturbed psychic equilibrium. As a doctor, I make every effort to strengthen the belief in immortality, especially with older patients when such questions come threateningly close. For, seen in correct psychological perspective, death is not an end but a goal, and life’s inclination towards death begins as soon as the meridian is passed.
[68] 这一超凡人格的产生和诞生正是我们文本在谈及"圣果"、"金刚身"或任何其他不朽之体时所意味的。在心理学上，这些表达象征一种超越情感纠葛和猛烈冲击之范围的态度——一种从世界中超脱的意识。我有理由相信这种态度在人生中期之后出现，是对死亡的自然准备。死亡在心理学上与出生同样重要，并且与出生一样是生命不可或缺的一部分。超脱的意识最终会遭遇什么，这是一个不能期望心理学家回答的问题。无论他的理论立场如何，他都会绝望地超越其科学能力的界限。他只能指出：我们文本关于超脱意识之永恒性的观点与一切时代的宗教思想以及绝大多数人类的思想是一致的。任何持不同看法的人都站在人类秩序之外，因此会遭受心理平衡的失调。作为一名医生，我竭力加强不朽的信仰，特别是对老年患者——当这些问题咄咄逼人地逼近时。因为从正确的心理学角度来看，死亡不是终点而是目标，而生命对死亡的倾斜自正午一过便开始了。

[69] Chinese yoga philosophy is based upon this instinctive preparation for death as a goal. In analogy with the goal of the first half of life—procreation and reproduction, the means of perpetuating one’s physical existence—it takes as the goal of spiritual existence the symbolic begetting and birth of a “spirit-body,” or “breath-body,” which ensures the continuity of detached consciousness. It is the birth of the pneumatic man, known to the European from antiquity, but which he seeks to produce by quite other symbols and magical practices, by faith and a Christian way of life. Here again we stand on a foundation quite different from that of the East. Again the text sounds as though it were not so very far from Christian ascetic morality, but nothing could be more mistaken than to assume that it actually means the same thing. Behind our text is a civilization thousands of years old, one which is built up organically on primitive instincts and knows nothing of that brutal morality so suited to us as recently civilized Teutonic barbarians. For this reason the Chinese are without the impulse towards violent repression of the instincts that poisons our spirituality and makes it hysterically exaggerated. The man who lives with his instincts can also detach from them, and in just as natural a way as he lived with them. Any idea of heroic self-conquest would be entirely foreign to the spirit of our text, but that is what it would infallibly amount to if we followed the instructions literally.
[69] 中国瑜伽哲学正是建立在这种对死亡作为目标的直觉准备之上。与生命前半程的目标——生育和繁殖，即延续肉身存在的手段——类比，它将以灵性存在为目标的象征性孕育和诞生——"灵体"或"息体"——视为确保超脱意识之连续性的手段。这是灵性之人的诞生，欧洲人从古代就知晓，但他试图以完全不同的象征和魔法实践、以信仰和基督徒的生活方式来产生它。在这里我们再次站在与东方完全不同的基础上。文本再次听起来似乎与基督教禁欲道德相差不远，但假定它实际上意味着同样的事情再错误不过了。在我们文本背后是一个有数千年历史的文明——它有机地建立在原始本能之上，对那种适合我们这些刚刚文明的日耳曼蛮族的残酷道德一无所知。因此，中国人没有那种毒害我们灵性并使其歇斯底里地夸张的对本能的暴力压抑冲动。与本能共存的人也能与之超脱，其方式恰如他与本能共存一样自然。英雄式自我征服的观念对于我们文本的精神来说将完全陌生，但如果我们照字面遵循指导，那必然会走向这一步。

[70] We must never forget our historical antecedents. Only a little more than a thousand years ago we stumbled out of the crudest beginnings of polytheism into a highly developed Oriental religion which lifted the imaginative minds of half-savages to a height that in no way corresponded to their spiritual development. In order to keep to this height in some fashion or other, it was inevitable that the instinctual sphere should be largely repressed. Thus religious practice and morality took on a decidedly brutal, almost malignant, character. The repressed elements naturally did not develop, but went on vegetating in the unconscious, in their original barbarism. We would like to scale the heights of a philosophical religion, but in fact are incapable of it. To grow up to it is the most we can hope for. The Amfortas wound and the Faustian split in the Germanic man are still not healed; his unconscious is still loaded with contents that must first be made conscious before he can be free of them. Recently I received a letter from a former patient which describes the necessary transformation in simple but trenchant words. She writes:
[70] 我们绝不能忘记我们的历史前因。就在一千多年前，我们从最粗暴的多神教开端跌跌撞撞地进入一种高度发展的东方宗教——它将半野蛮人的想象力提升到一种与其灵性发展完全不相应的高度。为了以某种方式保持在这一高度，本能领域的很大一部分必然被压抑。因此宗教实践和道德呈现出一种明确的粗暴、几乎恶性的特征。被压抑的元素自然没有发展，而是在无意识中以原始的野蛮状态继续苟存。我们想要攀登哲学宗教的高峰，但实际上做不到。成长到那一步是我们所能期望的极限。安佛塔斯之伤和浮士德式的分裂在日耳曼人身上至今未愈；他的无意识仍然负载着那些内容——这些内容必须首先被带入意识，然后他才能从中解脱。最近我收到一封前患者的来信，她以简洁而有力的语言描述了必要的转变。她写道：

Out of evil, much good has come to me. By keeping quiet, repressing nothing, remaining attentive, and by accepting reality—taking things as they are, and not as I wanted them to be—by doing all this, unusual knowledge has come to me, and unusual powers as well, such as I could never have imagined before. I always thought that when we accepted things they overpowered us in some way or other. This turns out not to be true at all, and it is only by accepting them that one can assume an attitude towards them.3 So now I intend to play the game of life, being receptive to whatever comes to me, good and bad, sun and shadow forever alternating, and, in this way, also accepting my own nature with its positive and negative sides. Thus everything becomes more alive to me. What a fool I was! How I tried to force everything to go according to the way I thought it ought to!
从恶中，许多善来到了我身边。通过保持安静，不压抑任何东西，保持留心，以及接受现实——按事物的本来面目接受它们，而非按我希望它们成为的样子——通过做这一切，非凡的知识来到了我身边，非凡的力量也如此，这些都是我以前从未想象过的。我总以为当我们接受事物时，它们会以某种方式压倒我们。事实证明完全不是如此，只有接受它们，人才能对它们采取一种态度。3所以现在我打算玩生命的游戏，对来到我面前的一切——好的和坏的，永远交替的阳光和阴影——保持接受，并以此方式也接受我自己的本性及其正面和负面。于是对我来说一切都变得更加有生命力了。我曾经多傻啊！我怎么试图强迫一切按照我认为它应该的方式去走！

[71] Only on the basis of such an attitude, which renounces none of the Christian values won in the course of Christian development, but which, on the contrary, tries with Christian charity and forbearance to accept even the humblest things in one’s own nature, will a higher level of consciousness and culture become possible. This attitude is religious in the truest sense, and therefore therapeutic, for all religions are therapies for the sorrows and disorders of the soul. The development of the Western intellect and will has given us an almost fiendish capacity for aping such an attitude, with apparent success, despite the protests of the unconscious. But it is only a matter of time before the counterposition asserts itself all the more harshly. Aping an attitude always produces an unstable situation that can be overthrown by the unconscious at any time. A safe foundation is found only when the instinctive premises of the unconscious win the same respect as the views of the conscious mind. No one should blind himself to the fact that this necessity of giving due consideration to the unconscious runs violently counter to our Western, and in particular the Protestant, cult of consciousness. Yet, though the new always seems to be the enemy of the old, anyone with a more than superficial desire to understand cannot fail to discover that without the most serious application of the Christian values we have acquired, the new integration can never take place.
[71] 只有在这样一种态度的基础上——它不放弃在基督教发展过程中赢得的任何基督教价值，相反，以基督教的仁爱和宽容去接受自己本性中哪怕是最卑微的东西——更高的意识和文化才有可能。这种态度在最真正意义上是宗教的，因此是治疗性的，因为一切宗教都是对灵魂之悲伤和紊乱的治疗。西方理智和意志的发展赋予了我们一种几乎恶魔般的模仿这种态度的能力，表面上很成功，尽管无意识在抗议。但这只是时间问题，反位态将以更严厉的方式坚持自己。模仿的态度总是产生一种不稳定的状态，可以随时被无意识推翻。只有当无意识的本能前提获得与意识观点同等的尊重时，才能找到安全的基础。任何人都不应自欺地忽视：这一给予无意识应有考虑的必要性与我们的西方——尤其是新教——意识崇拜激烈相抵触。然而，尽管新事物总是似乎是旧事物的敌人，但任何有超越表面之理解欲望的人都不能不发现：没有我们所获得的基督教价值的最认真运用，新的整合永远不可能发生。





6. THE FULFILMENT
6. 圆满


[72] A growing familiarity with the spirit of the East should be taken merely as a sign that we are beginning to relate to the alien elements within ourselves. Denial of our historical foundations would be sheer folly and would be the best way to bring about another uprooting of consciousness. Only by standing firmly on our own soil can we assimilate the spirit of the East.
[72] 对东方精神日益熟悉只不过应被视为我们开始与自身内部的异己元素建立关系的一个标志。否认我们的历史根基将是纯然的愚蠢，是造成意识另一次拔根的最佳方式。只有牢牢站在自己的土地上，我们才能吸收东方的精神。

[73] Speaking of those who do not know where the true springs of secret power lie, an ancient adept says, “Worldly people lose their roots and cling to the treetops.” The spirit of the East has grown out of the yellow earth, and our spirit can, and should, grow only out of our own earth. That is why I approach these problems in a way that has often been charged with “psychologism.” If “psychology” were meant, I should indeed be flattered, for my aim as a psychologist is to dismiss without mercy the metaphysical claims of all esoteric teachings. The unavowed purpose of gaining power through words, inherent in all secret doctrines, ill accords with our profound ignorance, which we should have the modesty to admit. I quite deliberately bring everything that purports to be metaphysical into the daylight of psychological understanding, and do my best to prevent people from believing in nebulous power-words. Let the convinced Christian believe, by all means, for that is the duty he has taken upon himself; but whoever is not a Christian has forfeited the charisma of faith. (Perhaps he was cursed from birth with not being able to believe, but merely to know.) Therefore, he has no right to put his faith elsewhere. One cannot grasp anything metaphysically, one only can do so psychologically. Therefore I strip things of their metaphysical wrappings in order to make them objects of psychology. In that way I can at least extract something understandable from them and avail myself of it, and I also discover psychological facts and processes that before were veiled in symbols and beyond my comprehension. In doing so I may perhaps be following in the footsteps of the faithful, and may possibly have similar experiences; and if in the end there should be something ineffably metaphysical behind it all, it would then have the best opportunity of showing itself.
[73] 谈到那些不知道秘密力量之真正源泉何在的人，古代一位大师说："世人失其根而附于枝。"东方的精神从黄土地中生长出来，而我们的精神只能也只应该从我们自己的土地中生长。这就是为什么我以一种常常被指责为"心理学主义"的方式来处理这些问题。如果真的是"心理学"，我确实应当感到荣幸，因为我作为心理学家的目标是无情地摒弃一切秘传教义的形而上学主张。通过言辞获取权力这一未言明的目的——一切秘密教义中固有的——与我们深刻的无知不相称，我们应该有勇气承认这种无知。我完全有意识地将一切自称形而上学的东西带入心理学理解的日光之下，并竭力阻止人们相信含糊的权力词汇。让坚定的基督徒去信仰吧，因为这是他承担的责任；但不是基督徒的人已丧失了信仰的超凡魅力。（也许他从出生起就被诅咒为不能信仰，只能知道。）因此，他没有权利在别处投放他的信仰。人不能从形而上学上把握任何东西，只能从心理学上把握。因此我剥去事物的形而上学包装，使其成为心理学的对象。这样我至少能从中提取出可理解的东西并加以利用，我还发现了以前被象征所遮蔽、超出我理解范围的心理事实和过程。在这样做时，我也许正追随着信徒的脚步，也许可能有类似的经验；如果最终这一切背后确实存在某种不可言说的形而上学之物，那时它将有最好的机会显示自己。

[74] My admiration for the great philosophers of the East is as genuine as my attitude towards their metaphysics is irreverent.1 I suspect them of being symbolical psychologists, to whom no greater wrong could be done than to take them literally. If it were really metaphysics that they mean, it would be useless to try to understand them. But if it is psychology, we can not only understand them but can profit greatly by them, for then the so-called “metaphysical” comes within the range of experience. If I assume that God is absolute and beyond all human experience, he leaves me cold. I do not affect him, nor does he affect me. But if I know that he is a powerful impulse of my soul, at once I must concern myself with him, for then he can become important, even unpleasantly so, and can affect me in practical ways—which sounds horribly banal, like everything else that is real.
[74] 我对东方伟大哲学家的钦佩是真诚的，正如我对他们的形而上学态度是不恭的一样。1我怀疑他们是象征性的心理学家，对他们最大的不公正莫过于照字面理解他们。如果他们真的意指形而上学，那么试图理解他们就是徒劳的。但如果那是心理学，我们不仅能够理解他们，而且能从中受益甚多，因为那时所谓的"形而上学"就落入了经验的范围。如果我假定上帝是绝对的、超越一切人类经验的，他就让我感到冷漠。我不影响他，他也不影响我。但如果我知道他是我灵魂的一个强大冲动，我就必须立刻关注他，因为那时他可以变得重要——甚至令人不快地重要——并能在实践中影响我——这听起来可怕地平庸，像一切其他真实之物一样。

[75] The epithet “psychologism” applies only to a fool who thinks he has his soul in his pocket. There are certainly more than enough such fools, for although we know how to talk big about the “soul,” the depreciation of everything psychic is a typically Western prejudice. If I make use of the concept “autonomous psychic complex,” my reader immediately comes up with the ready-made prejudice that it is “nothing but a psychic complex.” How can we be so sure that the soul is “nothing but”? It is as if we did not know, or else continually forgot, that everything of which we are conscious is an image, and that image is psyche. The same people who think that God is depreciated if he is understood as something moved in the psyche, as well as the moving force of the psyche—i.e., as an autonomous complex—can be so plagued by uncontrollable affects and neurotic states that their wills and their whole philosophy of life fail them miserably. Is that a proof of the impotence of the psyche? Should Meister Eckhart be accused of “psychologism” when he says, “God must be born in the soul again and again”? I think the accusation of “psychologism” can be levelled only at an intellect that denies the genuine nature of the autonomous complex and seeks to explain it rationalistically as the consequence of known causes, i.e., as something secondary and unreal. This is just as arrogant as the metaphysical assertion that seeks to make a God outside the range of our experience responsible for our psychic states. Psychologism is simply the counterpart of this metaphysical presumption, and is just as childish. Therefore it seems to me far more reasonable to accord the psyche the same validity as the empirical world, and to admit that the former has just as much “reality” as the latter. As I see it, the psyche is a world in which the ego is contained. Maybe there are fishes who believe that they contain the sea. We must rid ourselves of this habitual illusion of ours if we wish to consider metaphysical assertions from the standpoint of psychology.
[75] "心理学主义"这一称谓只适用于那些以为自己的灵魂装在口袋里的蠢人。这样的蠢人当然够多，因为虽然我们懂得如何高谈阔论"灵魂"，但对一切心理之物的贬低是典型的西方偏见。如果我使用"自主心理情结"这一概念，我的读者立刻就拿出现成的偏见说那"不过是一个心理情结"。我们怎么如此确信灵魂"不过是"什么呢？这好像我们不知道或不断忘记：我们所意识的一切都是一个形象，而那形象就是心理。那些认为如果上帝被理解为在心理中活动的东西以及心理的推动力——即自主情结——就被贬低了的人，同时可能被不可控制的情感和神经状态所折磨，以至于他们的意志和整个人生哲学悲惨地失效。这是心理无能的证明吗？艾克哈特大师说"上帝必须一次又一次地在灵魂中诞生"时，难道应当被控以"心理学主义"吗？我认为"心理学主义"的指控只能指向一种否定自主情结之真正本质、试图以理性主义将其解释为已知原因之结果的理智——即某种次要的和不真实的东西。这与试图以我们经验范围之外的上帝来为我们的心理状态负责的形而上学主张同样傲慢。心理学主义不过是这种形而上学偭妄的对应物，同样幼稚。因此，在我看来，赋予心理与经验世界同样的有效性，承认前者与后者同样具有"现实性"，远更为合理。在我看来，心理是一个世界，自我被包含其中。也许有鱼相信它们包含着大海。我们必须摆脱我们的这种习惯性幻觉，如果我们要从心理学的立场考虑形而上学主张的话。

[76] A metaphysical assertion of this kind is the idea of the “diamond body,” the incorruptible breath-body which grows in the golden flower or in the “field of the square inch.”2 This body is a symbol for a remarkable psychological fact which, precisely because it is objective, first appears in forms dictated by the experience of biological life—that is, as fruit, embryo, child, living body, and so on. This fact could be best expressed by the words “It is not I who live, it lives me.” The illusion of the supremacy of consciousness makes us say, “I live.” Once this illusion is shattered by a recognition of the unconscious, the unconscious will appear as something objective in which the ego is included. The attitude towards the unconscious is then analogous to the feeling of the primitive to whom the existence of a son guarantees continuation of life—a feeling that can assume grotesque forms, as when the old Negro, angered at his son’s disobedience, cried out, “There he stands with my body, but does not even obey me!”
[76] 这种形而上学主张之一就是"金刚身"的观念——在金花或"方寸之田"中生长的不腐息体。2这个身体是一个非凡心理事实的象征——正因为它是客观的，它首先以由生物生命经验所规定的形式出现——即作为果实、胚胎、婴儿、活体等等。这一事实最好用以下话语来表达："不是我活着，而是它活着我。"意识至上性的幻觉使我们说"我活着"。一旦这一幻觉通过认识到无意识而被打破，无意识便作为某种客观之物出现——自我被包含其中。对无意识的态度于是类似于原始人的感觉——对他来说，儿子的存在保证了生命的延续——这种感觉可以采取荒唐的形式，比如那个老黑奴因儿子不听话而怒喊："他站在那里带着我的身体，却不听我的话！"

[77] It is, in fact, a change of feeling similar to that experienced by a father to whom a son has been born, a change known to us from the testimony of St. Paul: “Yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.” The symbol “Christ” as “son of man” is an analogous psychic experience of a higher spiritual being who is invisibly born in the individual, a pneumatic body which is to serve us as a future dwelling, a body which, as Paul says, is put on like a garment (“For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ”). It is always a difficult thing to express, in intellectual terms, subtle feelings that are nevertheless infinitely important for the individual’s life and well-being. It is, in a sense, the feeling that we have been “replaced.” but without the connotation of having been “deposed.” It is as if the guidance of life had passed over to an invisible centre. Nietzsche’s metaphor, “in most loving bondage, free,” would be appropriate here. Religious language is full of imagery depicting this feeling of free dependence, of calm acceptance.
[77] 实际上，这是一种感受的变化，类似于一个父亲得子时所经验的变化——我们从保罗的见证中知道这种变化："现在活着的不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着。""基督"这一象征作为"人子"是一种类似的更高灵性存在的心理经验——这个存在不可见地在个人中诞生，一个灵性之体，它将作为我们未来的居所，一个如保罗所说可以像衣服一样穿上的身体（"你们受洗归入基督的都是披戴基督了"）。用理智的术语来表达那些微妙的感觉总是困难的，但这些感觉对于个人的生命和福祉却是无限重要的。在某种意义上，这是一种我们被"取代"了的感受，但不含有被"罢黜"的意味。仿佛生命的指导已经转移到了一个不可见的中心。尼采的比喻"在最慈爱的束缚中，自由"在此处是恰当的。宗教语言充满了描绘这种自由依存、平静接受之感受的意象。

[78] This remarkable experience seems to me a consequence of the detachment of consciousness, thanks to which the subjective “I live” becomes the objective “It lives me.” This state is felt to be higher than the previous one; it is really like a sort of release from the compulsion and impossible responsibility that are the inevitable results of participation mystique. This feeling of liberation fills Paul completely; the consciousness of being a child of God delivers one from the bondage of the blood. It is also a feeling of reconciliation with all that happens, for which reason, according to the Hui Ming Ching, the gaze of one who has attained fulfilment turns back to the beauty of nature.
[78] 这一非凡的经验在我看来是意识超脱的结果——由于这种超脱，主观的"我活着"变成了客观的"它活着我"。这一状态被感受为高于前一状态；它确实像是从强制和不可能的责任中的一种解放——这些强制和责任是神秘参与的不可避免结果。这种解脱感完全充满了保罗；作为上帝之儿女的意识使人脱离了血缘的奴役。它也是一种与一切发生之事和解的感觉，正因如此，根据《慧命经》，达到圆满者的目光会回转到大自然之美。

[79] In the Pauline Christ symbol the supreme religious experiences of West and East confront one another: Christ the sorrow-laden hero, and the Golden Flower that blooms in the purple hall of the city of jade. What a contrast, what an unfathomable difference, what an abyss of history! A problem fit for the crowning work of a future psychologist!
[79] 在保罗的基督象征中，西方与东方的最高宗教经验面对面：负载悲伤的英雄基督，与在玉城紫殿中绽放的金花。多么大的反差，多么不可测的差异，多么深的历史鸿沟！一个适合未来心理学家的收官之作的问题！

[80] Among the great religious problems of the present is one which has received scant attention, but which is in fact the main problem of our day: the evolution of the religious spirit. If we are to discuss it, we must emphasize the difference between East and West in their treatment of the “jewel,” the central symbol. The West lays stress on the human incarnation, and even on the personality and historicity of Christ, whereas the East says: “Without beginning, without end, without past, without future.”3 The Christian subordinates himself to the superior divine person in expectation of his grace; but the Oriental knows that redemption depends on the work he does on himself. The Tao grows out of the individual. The imitatio Christi has this disadvantage: in the long run we worship as a divine example a man who embodied the deepest meaning of life, and then, out of sheer imitation, we forget to make real our own deepest meaning—self-realization. As a matter of fact, it is not altogether inconvenient to renounce one’s own meaning. Had Jesus done so, he would probably have become a respectable carpenter and not a religious rebel to whom the same thing would naturally happen today as happened then.
[80] 在当今的重大宗教问题中，有一个几乎未受关注，但实际上是我们这个时代的主要问题：宗教精神的进化。如果我们要讨论它，就必须强调东西方在对待"宝石"——中心象征——方面的差异。西方强调人的化身，甚至强调基督的人格性和历史性，而东方说："无始无终，无过去无未来。"3基督徒使自己从属于优越的神圣位格，期待其恩典；但东方人知道救赎取决于他对自己所做的工作。道从个体中生长出来。效法基督有这样一个缺点：从长远来看，我们将一个体现了生命最深意义的人作为神圣榜样来崇拜，然后出于纯粹的模仿，我们忘记了实现我们自己的最深意义——自我实现。事实上，放弃自己的意义并非完全不便利。如果耶稣这样做了，他可能会成为一个体面的木匠，而不是一个宗教叛逆者——今天同样的事情自然也会发生在他身上，正如当时发生的那样。

[81] The imitation of Christ might well be understood in a deeper sense. It could be taken as the duty to realize one’s deepest conviction with the same courage and the same self-sacrifice shown by Jesus. Happily not everyone has the task of being a leader of humanity, or a great rebel; and so, after all, it might be possible for each to realize himself in his own way. This honesty might even become an ideal. Since great innovations always begin in the most unlikely places, the fact that people today are not nearly as ashamed of their nakedness as they used to be might be the beginning of a recognition of themselves as they really are. Hard upon this will follow an increasing recognition of many things that formerly were strictly taboo, for the reality of the earth will not forever remain veiled like the virgines velandae of Tertullian. Moral unmasking is but a step further in the same direction, and behold, there stands man as he is, and admits to himself that he is as he is. If he does this in a meaningless way he is just a muddled fool; but if he knows the significance of what he is doing he could belong to a higher order of man who makes real the Christ symbol, regardless of the suffering involved. It has often been observed that purely concrete taboos or magical rites in an early stage of a religion become in the next stage something psychic, or even purely spiritual symbols. An outward law becomes in the course of time an inward conviction. Thus it might easily happen to contemporary man, especially Protestants, that the person Jesus, now existing outside in the realm of history, might become the higher man within himself. Then we would have attained, in a European way, the psychological state corresponding to Eastern enlightenment.
[81] 效法基督也许可以被理解为一种更深层的意义。它可以被理解为以耶稣所表现的同样勇气和同样自我牺牲来实现自己最深信念的职责。幸好不是每个人都有做人类领袖或伟大叛逆者的任务；因此，毕竟每个人都有可能以自己的方式实现自我。这种诚实甚至可以成为一种理想。既然伟大的创新总是从最不可能的地方开始，那么今天人们不再像从前那样为自己的赤裸感到羞耻这一事实，可能是他们开始按自己的真实面目认识自己的开端。紧接着将是对许多以前严格禁忌之事的越来越多认识，因为大地的现实不会永远像德尔图良的"需蒙面之处女"那样被遮蔽。道德上的揭面不过是同一方向的再进一步，看哪，人就站在那里，以本来的面目，向自己承认自己就是如此。如果他以无意义的方式做这件事，他不过是一个糊涂的蠢人；但如果他知道他所做之事的意义，他可能属于一个更高层次的人——他不顾所涉及的苦难而实现了基督象征。人们常常观察到，一种宗教早期阶段中纯粹具体的禁忌或魔法仪式在下一阶段变成了某种心理的甚至纯粹灵性的象征。外在法则随着时间的推移变成内在信念。因此，当代人——尤其是新教徒——可能会发现，现在存在于历史领域之外的耶稣这个人，可能成为他自己内部的更高之人。那样我们就以一种欧洲的方式达到了与东方启蒙相应的心理状态。

[82] All this is a step in the evolution of a higher consciousness on its way to unknown goals, and is not metaphysics as ordinarily understood. To that extent it is only “psychology,” but to that extent, too, it is experienceable, understandable and—thank God—real, a reality we can do something with, a living reality full of possibilities. The fact that I am content with what can be experienced psychically, and reject the metaphysical, does not amount, as any intelligent person can see, to a gesture of scepticism or agnosticism aimed at faith and trust in higher powers, but means approximately the same as what Kant meant when he called the thing-in-itself a “merely negative borderline concept.” Every statement about the transcendental is to be avoided because it is only a laughable presumption on the part of a human mind unconscious of its limitations. Therefore, when God or the Tao is named an impulse of the soul, or a psychic state, something has been said about the knowable only, but nothing about the unknowable, about which nothing can be determined.
[82] 所有这一切都是更高意识向未知目标进化的一步，不是通常所理解的形而上学。在这一范围内它只是"心理学"，但在这一范围内它也是可经验的、可理解的——谢天谢地——是真实的，一种我们可以有所作为的现实，一种充满可能性的活生生的现实。我满足于心理上可经验之物而摒弃形而上学，这并不构成——如任何聪明人所能看出的——一种针对对更高力量的信仰和信任的怀疑主义或不可知论的姿态，而是大致意味着康德将物自体称为"纯然否定的界限概念"时所意味的东西。一切关于超验的陈述都应避免，因为它不过是一个未意识到自身界限的人类心智的可笑偭妄。因此，当上帝或道被称为灵魂的冲动或一种心理状态时，所说的只是关于可知者的，而关于不可知者——关于不可知者什么也不能确定——则什么也没说。





7. CONCLUSION
7. 结论


[83] The purpose of my commentary is to attempt to build a bridge of psychological understanding between East and West. The basis of every real understanding is man, and therefore I had to speak of human beings. This must be my excuse for having dealt only with general aspects, and for not having entered into technical details. Technical directions are valuable for those who know, for example, what a camera is, or a combustion engine, but they are useless for anyone who has no idea of such apparatus. Western man for whom I write is in an analogous position. Therefore it seemed to me important above all to emphasize the agreement between the psychic states and symbolisms of East and West. These analogies open a way to the inner chambers of the Eastern mind, a way that does not require the sacrifice of our own nature and does not confront us with the threat of being torn from our roots. Nor is it an intellectual telescope or microscope offering a view of no fundamental concern to us because it does not touch us. It is the way of suffering, seeking, and striving common to all civilized peoples; it is the tremendous experiment of becoming conscious, which nature has laid upon mankind, and which unites the most diverse cultures in a common task.
[83] 我的评注的目的是试图在东西方之间架起一座心理学理解的桥梁。一切真正理解的基础是人，因此我不得不谈论人类。这必须成为我只涉及一般方面、未深入技术细节的借口。技术指导对那些已经知道照相机或内燃机是什么的人是有价值的，但对对这些装置一无所知的人则毫无用处。我为之写作的西方人处于类似的境地。因此，在我看来最重要的是强调东西方心理状态和象征体系之间的一致性。这些类比开辟了一条通往东方心灵内室的道路，一条不需要牺牲我们自身本性、不面对被拔根之威胁的道路。它也不是一架智识望远镜或显微镜——提供一种与我们根本无关因为它不触及我们的景观。这是一条一切文明民族共有的受苦、寻找和奋斗之路；它是成为意识的巨大实验——自然将这一实验赋予人类，它将最多元的文化联合在一项共同任务中。

[84] Western consciousness is by no means the only kind of consciousness there is; it is historically conditioned and geographically limited, and representative of only one part of mankind. The widening of our consciousness ought not to proceed at the expense of other kinds of consciousness; it should come about through the development of those elements of our psyche which are analogous to those of the alien psyche, just as the East cannot do without our technology, science, and industry. The European invasion of the East was an act of violence on a grand scale, and it has left us with the duty—noblesse oblige—of understanding the mind of the East. This is perhaps more necessary than we realize at present.
[84] 西方意识绝非唯一的意识类型；它受历史条件制约，受地理范围限制，只代表人类的一部分。我们意识的拓展不应以牺牲其他类型的意识为代价；它应通过发展我们心理中与异己心理相类似的元素来实现——正如东方也不能缺少我们的技术、科学和工业。欧洲对东方的入侵是一场大规模的暴力行为，它留给我们一项责任——贵族的责任——理解东方的心灵。这也许比我们目前意识到的更为必要。

I



THE TEXTS
文本


[85] I must make clear at once that the following observations on the visions of Zosimos of Panopolis, an important alchemist and Gnostic of the third century A.D., are not intended as a final explanation of this extraordinarily difficult material. My psychological contribution is no more than an attempt to shed a little light on it and to answer some of the questions raised by the visions.
[85] 我必须立刻声明，以下关于帕诺波利斯的佐西莫斯（公元三世纪重要的炼金术士和诺斯底主义者）异象的观察，并不打算作为对这份极其艰深材料的最终解释。我的心理学贡献不过是试图为其提供一点微光，并回答这些异象所引发的一些问题。

[86] The first vision occurs at the beginning of “The Treatise of Zosimos the Divine concerning the Art.”1 Zosimos introduces the treatise with some general remarks on the processes of nature and, in particular, on the “composition of the waters” (θέσιςủδάτων) and various other operations, and closes with the words: “… and upon this simple system of many colours is based the manifold and infinitely varied investigation of all things.” Thereupon the text begins:2
[86] 第一个异象出现在《神圣的佐西莫斯关于技艺的论著》的开头。1 佐西莫斯在论著的引言中对自然过程，特别是“水之组合”（composition of the waters，θέσιςủδάτων）及其他各种操作进行了一些总体论述，并以这样的话结尾：“……对于万物那繁复且无限多样的探索，正是基于这个由多种颜色构成的简单系统。”紧接着，正文开始了：2

(III, i, 2.) And as I spoke thus I fell asleep, and I saw a sacrificer3 standing before me, high up on an altar, which was in the shape of a bowl. There were fifteen steps leading up to the altar. And the priest stood there, and I heard a voice from above saying to me: “I have performed the act of descending the fifteen steps into the darkness, and of ascending the steps into the light. And he who renews me is the sacrificer, by casting away the grossness of the body; and by compelling necessity I am sanctified as a priest and now stand in perfection as a spirit.” And on hearing the voice of him who stood upon the altar, I inquired of him who he was. And he answered me in a fine voice, saying: “I am Ion,4 the priest of the inner sanctuaries, and I submit myself to an unendurable torment.5 For there came one in haste at early morning, who overpowered me, and pierced me through with the sword, and dismembered me in accordance with the rule of harmony.6 And he drew off the skin of my head with the sword, which he wielded with strength, and mingled the bones with the pieces of flesh, and caused them to be burned upon the fire of the art, till I perceived by the transformation of the body that I had become spirit. And that is my unendurable torment.” And even as he spoke thus, and I held him by force to converse with me, his eyes became as blood. And he spewed forth all his own flesh. And I saw how he changed into the opposite of himself, into a mutilated anthroparion,7 and he tore his flesh with his own teeth, and sank into himself.
（III, i, 2.）我正这么说着，便陷入了沉睡。我看见一个献祭者3站在我面前，高高地站在一个碗状的祭坛上。有十五级台阶通向祭坛。祭司站在那里，我听到从上方传来一个声音对我说：“我已经完成了走下十五级台阶进入黑暗，以及走上台阶进入光明的仪式。而那个通过褪去肉身的粗糙来更新我的人，就是这个献祭者；受必然性所迫，我被圣化为祭司，现在作为纯粹的精神完美地站在这里。”听到站在祭坛上那人的声音，我问他是谁。他用优美的声音回答我说：“我是伊恩（Ion），4内殿的祭司，我正经受着难以忍受的折磨。5因为清晨时分，有人匆匆赶来，制服了我，用剑将我刺穿，并按照和谐的法则将我肢解。6他挥舞着强有力的剑，剥下了我头上的皮，将骨头和肉块混合在一起，放在技艺之火上焚烧，直到我通过肉身的转化意识到我已经成为了精神。而这就是我那难以忍受的折磨。”就在他这样说着，而我强行拉住他与我交谈时，他的眼睛变得像血一样红。他吐出了自己所有的肉。我看着他变成了与自己截然相反的东西，变成了一个残缺不全的小人（anthroparion），7他用自己的牙齿撕咬自己的肉，并深深陷入自身之中。

(III, i, 3.) Full of fear I awoke from sleep, and I thought to myself: “Is not this the composition of the waters?” And I was assured that I had well understood, and again I fell asleep. I saw the same bowl-shaped altar and, on the upper part, boiling water, and a numberless multitude of people in it. And there was no one near the altar whom I could question. Then I went up to the altar to see this sight. And I perceived an anthroparion, a barber8 grown grey with age, who said to me: “What are you looking at?” I replied that I was astonished to see the seething of the water, and the men burning and yet alive. He answered me thus: “The sight that you see is the entrance, and the exit, and the transformation.” I asked him: “What transformation?” and he answered: “This is the place of the operation called embalming. Those who seek to obtain the art9 enter here, and become spirits by escaping from the body.” Then I said to him: “And you, are you a spirit?” And he answered: “Yes, a spirit and a guardian of spirits.” As we spoke, while the boiling continued and the people uttered distressful cries, I saw a brazen man holding a leaden tablet in his hand. And he spoke with a loud voice, looking upon the tablet: “I command all those who are undergoing the punishment to be calm, to take each of them a leaden tablet, to write with their own hand, and to keep their eyes upraised in the air and their mouths open, until their uvula swell.”10 The deed followed the word, and the master of the house said to me: “You have beheld, you have stretched your neck upward and have seen what is done.” I replied that I had seen, and he continued: “This brazen man whom you see is the priest who sacrifices and is sacrificed, and spews forth his own flesh. Power is given him over this water and over the people who are punished.”11
（III, i, 3.）我满怀恐惧地从睡梦中惊醒，我心里想：“这难道不是水之组合吗？”我确信自己已经很好地理解了，于是再次入睡。我看到了同一个碗状的祭坛，而在它的上方，是沸腾的水，里面有无数的人。祭坛附近没有一个人可以让我询问。于是我走上祭坛去观看这番景象。我看到一个小人（anthroparion），一个因为年迈而头发花白的理发师，8他对我说：“你在看什么？”我回答说，看到沸水翻滚，而人们在其中燃烧却依然活着，我感到十分震惊。他这样回答我：“你所看到的这番景象，就是进入、退出以及转化。”我问他：“什么转化？”他回答：“这里是进行被称为‘防腐处理’（embalming）操作的地方。那些寻求获得这门技艺9的人进入这里，通过逃离肉身而成为精神。”然后我对他说：“那么你呢，你是一个精神吗？”他回答说：“是的，一个精神，同时也是精神的守护者。”就在我们说话的时候，沸腾还在继续，人们发出痛苦的呼号，这时我看到一个铜人，手里拿着一块铅板。他看着铅板，大声说道：“我命令所有正在经受惩罚的人保持安静，每人拿一块铅板，亲手写字，并保持眼睛向上仰望天空，张开嘴巴，直到你们的小舌肿胀。”10言出必行，这房子的主人对我说：“你已经看到了，你已经伸长脖子向上看，并看到了所发生的事情。”我回答说我看到了，他继续说道：“你所看到的这个铜人，就是那位既献祭又被献祭，并且吐出自己血肉的祭司。大能已赐予他，使他统辖这水以及受惩罚的人。”11

(III, v, 1.) At last I was overcome with the desire to mount the seven steps and to see the seven punishments, and, as was suitable, in a single day; so I went back in order to complete the ascent. Passing it several times, I at length came upon the path. But as I was about to ascend, I lost my way again; greatly discouraged, and not seeing in which direction I should go, I fell asleep. And while I was sleeping, I saw an anthroparion, a barber clad in a robe of royal purple, who stood outside the place of punishments. He said to me: “Man, what are you doing?” and I replied: “I have stopped here because, having turned aside from the road, I have lost my way.” And he said: “Follow me.” And I turned and followed him. When we came near to the place of punishments, I saw my guide, this little barber, enter that place, and his whole body was consumed by the fire.
（III, v, 1.）最后，我被想要登上七级台阶并在一天内看完七重惩罚（这似乎是合适的）的渴望所克服；所以我原路返回以完成登顶。我路过那里好几次，终于找到了那条路。但正当我要攀登时，我又迷路了；我非常沮丧，不知道该往哪个方向走，于是就睡着了。在睡梦中，我看到一个小人，一个穿着皇家紫袍的理发师，站在惩罚之地外面。他对我说：“人啊，你在做什么？”我回答说：“我停在这里，是因为我偏离了道路，迷失了方向。”他说：“跟我来。”我转身跟着他。当我们靠近惩罚之地时，我看到我的向导，这个理发师小人进入了那个地方，他的整个身体都被火吞噬了。

(III, v, 2.) On seeing this, I stepped aside, trembling with fear; then I awoke, and said within myself: “What means this vision?” And again I clarified my understanding, and knew that this barber was the brazen man, clad in a purple garment. And I said to myself: “I have well understood, this is the brazen man. It is needful that first he must enter the place of punishments.”
（III, v, 2.）看到这一幕，我吓得浑身发抖，退到一旁；然后我醒了过来，心里想：“这个异象是什么意思？”我再次理清了思路，知道这个理发师就是那个穿着紫衣的铜人。我对自己说：“我完全明白了，这就是那个铜人。首先，他必须进入惩罚之地，这是不可避免的。”

(III, v, 3.) Again my soul desired to mount the third step also. And again I followed the road alone, and when I was near the place of punishments, I again went astray, not knowing my way, and I stopped in despair. And again, as it seemed, I saw an old man whitened by years, who had become wholly white, with a blinding whiteness. His name was Agathodaimon. Turning himself about, the old man with white hair gazed upon me for a full hour. And I urged him: “Show me the right way.” He did not come towards me, but hastened on his way. But I, running hither and thither, at length came to the altar. And when I stood at the top of the altar, I saw the white-haired old man enter the place of punishments. O ye demiurges of celestial nature! Immediately he was transformed by the flame into a pillar of fire. What a terrible story, my brethren! For, on account of the violence of the punishment, his eyes filled with blood. I spoke to him, and asked: “Why are you stretched out there?” But he could barely open his mouth, and groaned: “I am the leaden man, and I submit myself to an unendurable torment.” Thereupon, seized with great fear, I awoke and sought within myself the reason for what I had seen. And again I considered and said to myself: “I have well understood, for it means that the lead is to be rejected, and in truth the vision refers to the composition of the liquids.”
（III, v, 3.）我的灵魂再次渴望登上第三级台阶。我又一次独自顺着这条路走，当接近惩罚之地时，我又迷路了，不知该如何走，绝望地停了下来。就在这时，我又看到了一个被岁月染白了头发的老人，他全身洁白，白得刺眼。他的名字叫阿加索代蒙（Agathodaimon）。这位白发老人转过身来，盯着我看了足足一个小时。我催促他：“请给我指明正确的道路。”他没有朝我走来，而是继续匆匆赶路。而我四处乱跑，终于来到了祭坛前。当我站在祭坛顶端时，我看到那位白发老人进入了惩罚之地。哦，天性的造物主们啊！他立刻被火焰变成了一根火柱。我的兄弟们，这是多么可怕的故事啊！因为惩罚太过猛烈，他的双眼充血。我对他说话，问道：“你为什么躺在那里？”但他几乎无法张开嘴，呻吟着说：“我是铅人，我正经受着难以忍受的折磨。”于是，我怀着巨大的恐惧醒来，在心里寻找我所见景象的原因。我再次思考，并对自己说：“我完全明白了，因为这意味着要拒斥铅，实际上，这个异象指的是液体之组合。”

(III, vbis.) Again I beheld the divine and holy bowl-shaped altar, and I saw a priest clothed in a white robe reaching to his feet, who was celebrating these terrible mysteries, and I said: “Who is this?” And the answer came: “This is the priest of the inner sanctuaries. It is he who changes the bodies into blood, makes the eyes clairvoyant, and raises the dead.” Then, falling again to earth, I again fell asleep. And as I was ascending the fourth step, I saw, to the east, one approaching, holding a sword in his hand. And another [came] behind him, bringing one adorned round about with signs, clad in white and comely to see, who was named the Meridian of the Sun.12 And as they drew near to the place of punishments, he who held the sword in his hand [said]: “Cut off his head, immolate his body, and cut his flesh into pieces, that it may first be boiled according to the method,13 and then delivered to the place of punishments.” Thereupon I awoke and said: “I have well understood, this concerns the liquids in the art of the metals.” And he who bore the sword in his hand said again: “You have completed the descent of the seven steps.” And the other answered, as he caused the waters to gush forth from all the moist places: “The procedure is completed.”
（III, vbis.）我又一次看到了那神圣纯洁的碗状祭坛，我看到一位身穿及足白袍的祭司，正在主持这些可怕的奥秘，我问道：“这是谁？”回答传来：“这是内殿的祭司。正是他将身体变成血液，使眼睛获得透视力，并让死者复活。”然后，我又一次倒在地上，沉沉睡去。当我登上第四级台阶时，我看到东边走来一个人，手里拿着一把剑。另一个人跟在他后面，带来了一个全身装饰着符号、穿着白衣、相貌英俊的人，他被称为“太阳的子午线”（Meridian of the Sun）。12当他们靠近惩罚之地时，手里拿着剑的人[说]：“砍下他的头，献祭他的身体，将他的肉切成碎片，以便首先按照方法将其煮沸，13然后再将其送到惩罚之地。”于是我醒了过来，说道：“我完全明白了，这关系到金属技艺中的液体。”那个手里拿着剑的人又说：“你已经完成了走下七级台阶的仪式。”另一个人一边使水从所有潮湿的地方涌出，一边回答说：“程序已完成。”

(III, vi, 1.) And I saw an altar which was in the shape of a bowl, and a fiery spirit stood upon the altar, and tended the fire for the seething and the boiling and the burning of the men who rose up from it. And I inquired about the people who stood there, and I said: “I see with astonishment the seething and the boiling of the water, and the men burning and yet alive!” And he answered me, saying: “This boiling that you see is the place of the operation called embalming. Those who seek to obtain the art enter here, and they cast their bodies from them and become spirits. The practice [of the art] is explained by this procedure; for whatever casts off the grossness of the body becomes spirit.”
（III, vi, 1.）我看到一个碗状的祭坛，祭坛上站着一个火之灵，他看管着炉火，以便让那些从水中升起的人沸腾、翻滚并燃烧。我询问了站在那里的人，我说：“我惊奇地看到水在沸腾翻滚，而人在燃烧却依然活着！”他回答我说：“你看到的这种沸腾，就是进行所谓的‘防腐处理’操作的地方。那些寻求获得这门技艺的人进入这里，褪去肉身，成为精神。[技艺的]实践就是通过这个程序来解释的；因为任何褪去了肉身粗糙的东西都会成为精神。”

[87] The Zosimos texts are in a disordered state. At III, i, 5 there is a misplaced but obviously authentic résumé or amplification of the visions, and at III, i, 4 a philosophical interpretation of them. Zosimos calls this whole passage an “introduction to the discourse that is to follow” (III, i, 6).
[87] 佐西莫斯的文本处于一种混乱的状态。在 III, i, 5 处有一段位置错乱但显然是真实的异象摘要或扩展，而在 III, i, 4 处则是对它们的哲学解释。佐西莫斯将这整个段落称为“接下来论述的引言”（III, i, 6）。

(III, i, 5.) In short, my friend, build a temple from a single stone, like to white lead, to alabaster, to Proconnesian marble,14 with neither end nor beginning in its construction.15 Let it have within it a spring of the purest water, sparkling like the sun. Note carefully on what side is the entrance to the temple, and take a sword in your hand; then seek the entrance, for narrow is the place where the opening is. A dragon lies at the entrance, guarding the temple. Lay hold upon him; immolate him first; strip him of his skin, and taking his flesh with the bones, separate the limbs; then, laying [the flesh of] the limbs16 together with the bones at the entrance of the temple, make a step of them, mount thereon, and enter, and you will find what you seek.17 The priest, that brazen man, whom you see seated in the spring and composing the substance, [look on] him not as the brazen man, for he has changed the colour of his nature and has become the silver man; and if you will, you will soon have him [as] the golden man.
（III, i, 5.）简而言之，我的朋友，用一块整石建造一座神庙，这块石头要像白铅、雪花石膏、普罗孔内苏斯（Proconnesian）大理石，14在它的建造中既没有终点也没有起点。15让它内部有一眼最纯净的泉水，像太阳一样闪耀。仔细注意神庙的入口在哪一边，手里拿一把剑；然后寻找入口，因为入口所在的地方很狭窄。一条龙躺在入口处，守护着神庙。抓住他；首先献祭他；剥去他的皮，将他的肉连同骨头一起取下，分开四肢；然后，将四肢[的肉]16连同骨头一起放在神庙的入口处，把它们做成台阶，踩在上面，走进去，你就会找到你所寻找的。17那位祭司，那个你看到坐在泉水中调配物质的铜人，不要[把]他当成铜人，因为他已经改变了自己本性的颜色，变成了银人；如果你愿意，你很快就会让他[变成]金人。

(III, i, 4.) And after I had seen this apparition, I awoke, and I said to myself: “What is the cause of this vision? Is not that boiling white and yellow water the divine water?” And I found that I had well understood. And I said: “Beautiful it is to speak and beautiful to hear, beautiful to give and beautiful to receive, beautiful to be poor and beautiful to be rich. How does nature teach giving and receiving? The brazen man gives and the hydrolith receives; the metal gives and the plant receives; the stars give and the flowers receive; the heavens give and the earth receives; the thunderclaps give forth darting fire. And all things are woven together and all things are undone again; all things are mingled together and all things combine; and all things unite and all things separate; all things are moistened and all things are dried; and all things flourish and all things fade in the bowl of the altar. For each thing comes to pass with method and in fixed measure and by exact18 weighing of the four elements. The weaving together of all things and the undoing of all things and the whole fabric of things cannot come to pass without method. The method is a natural one, preserving due order in its inhaling and its exhaling; it brings increase and it brings decrease. And to sum up: through the harmonies of separating and combining, and if nothing of the method be neglected, all things bring forth nature. For nature applied to nature transforms nature. Such is the order of natural law throughout the whole cosmos, and thus all things hang together.”
（III, i, 4.）我看到这个幻影后醒了过来，我对自己说：“这个异象的原因是什么？那沸腾的白色和黄色水难道不就是神圣之水吗？”我发现我已经很好地理解了。我说：“言说固然美好，倾听亦然；给予固然美好，接受亦然；贫穷固然美好，富有亦然。大自然是如何教导给予和接受的呢？铜人给予，而水石（hydrolith）接受；金属给予，而植物接受；星辰给予，而花朵接受；天空给予，而大地接受；雷霆万钧释放出飞射的火焰。万物交织在一起，万物又再次解开；万物混合在一起，万物又相互结合；万物结合，万物又分离；万物被浸润，万物又被烘干；在祭坛的碗里，万物繁荣，万物又枯萎。因为每一件事的发生都遵循着方法、固定的尺度，以及对四大元素的精确18称量。万物的交织、万物的解开以及事物的整个结构，都离不开方法。这个方法是自然的，在它的吸气和呼气中保持着应有的秩序；它带来增长，也带来减少。总而言之：通过分离和结合的和谐，如果不忽视方法中的任何细节，万物就能孕育出自然。因为将自然运用于自然，就会转化自然。这就是整个宇宙中自然法则的秩序，万物因此而紧密相连。”

(III, i, 6.) This introduction is the key which shall open to you the flowers of the discourse that is to follow, namely, the investigation of the arts, of wisdom, of reason and understanding, the efficacious methods and revelations which throw light upon the secret words.
（III, i, 6.）这段引言是一把钥匙，将为你开启后续论述的花朵，即对各种技艺、智慧、理性和理解的探索，以及那些能照亮秘密话语的有效方法和启示。





II



COMMENTARY
评注



1. GENERAL REMARKS ON THE INTERPRETATION
1. 关于解释的一般性评论


[88] Although it looks as if this were a series of visions following one after the other, the frequent repetitions and striking similarities suggest rather that it was essentially a single vision which is presented as a set of variations on the themes it contains. Psychologically at least, there is no ground for supposing that it is an allegorical invention. Its salient features seem to indicate that for Zosimos it was a highly significant experience which he wished to communicate to others. Although alchemical literature contains a number of allegories which without doubt are merely didactic fables and are not based on direct experience,1 the vision of Zosimos may well have been an actual happening. This seems to be borne out by the manner in which Zosimos himself interprets it as a confirmation of his own preoccupation: “Is not this the composition of the waters?” Such an interpretation seems—to us at any rate—to leave out of account the most impressive images in the vision, and to reduce a far more significant complex of facts to an all too simple common denominator. If the vision were an allegory, the most conspicuous images would also be the ones that have the greatest significance. But it is characteristic of any subjective dream interpretation that it is satisfied with pointing out superficial relationships which take no account of the essentials. Another thing to be considered is that the alchemists themselves testify to the occurrence of dreams and visions during the opus.2 I am inclined to think that the vision or visions of Zosimos were experiences of this kind, which took place during the work and revealed the nature of the psychic processes in the background.3 In these visions all those contents emerge which the alchemists unconsciously projected into the chemical process and which were then perceived there, as though they were qualities of matter. The extent to which this projection was fostered by the conscious attitude is shown by the somewhat overhasty interpretation given by Zosimos himself.
[88] 尽管这看起来像是一系列接连发生的异象，但频繁的重复和惊人的相似性反而表明，它本质上是一个单一的异象，只是以其所包含主题的变奏形式呈现出来。至少从心理学角度来看，没有理由认为这是一种寓言式的虚构。其显著特征似乎表明，对佐西莫斯而言，这是一次极其重要的经历，他希望将其传达给他人。虽然炼金术文献中包含许多寓言，这些寓言毫无疑问只是纯粹的说教故事，并非基于直接经验，1 但佐西莫斯的异象很可能是一次真实发生的事件。佐西莫斯本人将其解释为对自己所全神贯注之事（“这难道不是水之组合吗？”）的确认，这似乎证实了这一点。这种解释——至少对我们而言——似乎忽略了异象中最令人印象深刻的图像，并将一个重要得多的复杂事实简化为了一个过于简单的共同分母。如果这个异象是一个寓言，那么最显眼的图像也必然是具有最重要意义的图像。但任何主观的梦境解释的特征就是，它满足于指出那些不考虑本质的表面联系。另一件需要考虑的事情是，炼金术士们自己也证明了在炼金工作（opus）期间会发生梦境和异象。2 我倾向于认为，佐西莫斯的一个或多个异象就是这种类型的体验，它们发生在工作期间，并揭示了背景中心理过程的本质。3 在这些异象中，所有那些炼金术士无意识地投射到化学过程中的内容都显现出来了，并在那里被感知到，仿佛它们是物质的属性。这种投射在多大程度上受到意识态度的助长，从佐西莫斯本人给出的有些过于草率的解释中可见一斑。

[89] Even though his interpretation strikes us at first as somewhat forced, indeed as far-fetched and arbitrary, we should nevertheless not forget that while the conception of the “waters” is a strange one to us, for Zosimos and for the alchemists in general it had a significance we would never suspect.
