The treatise is one of the few that were written in Latin; the style is exceedingly strange, but all the same it contains so many significant hints that it is worth investigating more closely. Adam von Bodenstein, who edited it, says in a dedicatory letter2 to Ludwig Wolfgang von Hapsberg, governor of Badenweiler, that it was “taken down from the mouth of Paracelsus and carefully revised.” The obvious inference is that the treatise is based on notes of Paracelsus’s lectures and is not an original text. As Bodenstein himself wrote fluent and easily understandable Latin, quite unlike that of the treatise, one must assume that he did not devote any particular attention to it and made no effort to put it into more intelligible form, otherwise much more of his own style would have crept in. Probably he left the lectures more or less in their original state, as is particularly apparent towards the end. It is also likely that he had no very clear understanding of what they were about, any more than had the supposed translator Oporin. This is not surprising, as the Master himself all too often lacks the necessary clarity when discussing these complicated matters. Under these circumstances it is difficult to say how much should be put down to incomprehension and how much to undisciplined thinking. Nor is the possibility of actual errors in transcription excluded.3 In our interpretation, therefore, we are on uncertain ground from the start, and much must remain conjecture. But as Paracelsus, for all his originality, was strongly influenced by alchemical thinking, a knowledge of the earlier and contemporary alchemical treatises, and of the writings of his pupils and followers, is of considerable help in interpreting some of the concepts and in filling out certain gaps. An attempt to comment on and to interpret the treatise, therefore, is not entirely hopeless, despite the admitted difficulties.
[169] 《论长生》这篇论著虽然部分内容难以理解，但在这方面给了我们一些信息，尽管我们必须费力地将其从其所嵌入的秘术语语中剕离出来。该论著是少数几部用拉丁文写成的作品之一；文风极为奇特，但仍然包含许多重要暗示，值得更仔细地加以考察。编辑此书的亚当·冯·博登施泰因在致巴登魏勒总督路德维希·沃尔夫冈·冯·哈普斯贝格2 的献辞信中说，它是"从帕拉塞尔苏斯口述中记录下来并仔细修订的"。显而易见的推论是，该论著基于帕拉塞尔苏斯讲座的笔记，并非原始文本。由于博登施泰因本人写的拉丁文流畅易懂，与该论著的拉丁文截然不同，因此必须假定他对此并未特别用心，也没有努力将其整理成更易懂的形式，否则他的个人风格会更多地渗入其中。他可能基本上将讲座保持了原样，这一点在接近结尾处尤为明显。他很可能对其内容也没有很清楚的理解，正如假定的译者奥珀林一样。这并不令人惊讶，因为大师本人在讨论这些复杂问题时也常常缺乏必要的清晰性。在这种情况下，很难说有多少应归因于不理解，有多少应归因于不严谨的思考。也不能排除实际抄写错误的可能性。3 因此，在我们的诠释中，从一开始就处于不确定的地基上，许多东西只能是推测。但由于帕拉塞尔苏斯尽管富有独创性，却深受炼金术思维的影响，因此了解之前和同时代的炼金术论著以及他的学生和追随者的著作，对于诠释某些概念和填补某些空白有相当大的帮助。因此，尽管存在上述困难，试图对该论著进行注释和诠释并非完全没有希望。





A. THE ILIASTER
A. 伊利亚斯特


[170] The treatise is mainly concerned with the conditions under which longevity, which in Paracelsus’s opinion extends up to a thousand years or more, can be attained. In what follows I shall give chiefly the passages that relate to the secret doctrine and are of help in explaining it.4 Paracelsus starts by giving a definition of life, as follows: “Life, by Hercules, is nothing other than a certain embalsamed Mumia, which preserves the mortal body from the mortal worms and from corruption5 by means of a mixed saline solution.” Mumia was well known in the Middle Ages as a medicament, and it consisted of the pulverized parts of real Egyptian mummies, in which there was a flourishing trade. Paracelsus attributes incorruptibility to a special virtue or agent named “balsam.” This was something like a natural elixir, by means of which the body was kept alive or, if dead, incorruptible.6 By the same logic, a scorpion or venomous snake necessarily had in it an alexipharmic, i.e., an antidote, otherwise it would die of its own poison.
[170] 该论著主要讨论在何种条件下可以达到长寿——在帕拉塞尔苏斯看来，长寿可长达千年以上。在下文中，我将主要给出与秘术教义相关并有助于解释它的段落。4 帕拉塞尔苏斯首先给出了生命的定义，如下："以赫拉克勒斯之名发誓，生命不过是一种经过防腐处理的穆米亚（Mumia），它通过一种混合盐液保存必死之体，使之免受必死之虫和腐败5 的侵害。"穆米亚在中世纪作为一种药物广为人知，它由真正的埃及木乃伊的粉末状部分组成，对此有着繁荣的贸易。帕拉塞尔苏斯将不可腐朽性归因于一种名为"香脂"（balsam）的特殊德性或媒介。这类似于一种天然的灵药，借助于它，身体得以保持存活，或者如果已经死亡则保持不腐。6 按同样的逻辑，蝎子或毒蛇必然体内含有一种解毒剂（alexipharmic），即抗毒药，否则它将死于自身的毒液。

[171] Paracelsus goes on to discuss a great many arcane remedies, since diseases shorten life and have above all to be cured. The chief among these remedies are gold and pearls, which latter can be transformed into the quinta essentia. A peculiar potency is attributed to Cheyri,7 which fortifies the microcosmic body so much that it “must necessarily continue in its conservation through the universal anatomy of the four elements.”8 Therefore the physician should see to it that the “anatomy” (= structure) of the four elements “be contracted into the one anatomy of the microcosm, not out of the corporeal, but out of that which preserves the corporeal.” This is the balsam, which stands even higher than the quinta essentia, the thing that ordinarily holds the four elements together. It “excels even nature herself” because it is produced by a “bodily operation.”9 The idea that the art can make something higher than nature is typically alchemical. The balsam is the life principle, the spiritus mercurii, and it more or less coincides with the Paracelsan concept of the Iliaster. The latter is higher than the four elements and determines the length of life. It is therefore roughly the same as the balsam, or one could say that the balsam is the pharmacological or chemical aspect of the Iliaster.10 The Iliaster has three forms: Iliaster sanctitus,11 paratetus,12 and magnus. They are subordinate to man (“microcosmo subditi”) and can be brought “into one gamonymus.” Since Paracelsus attributes a special “vis ac potestas coniunctionis” to the Iliaster, this enigmatic “gamonymus” (γάμος = marriage, ὄνομα = name) must be interpreted as a kind of chymical wedding, in other words as an indissoluble, hermaphroditic union.13 There are as many Iliastri as there are men; that is to say in every man there is an Iliaster that holds together each individual’s peculiar combination of qualities.14 It therefore seems to be a kind of universal formative principle and principle of individuation.
[171] 帕拉塞尔苏斯接着讨论了大量的秘药，因为疾病缩短寿命，所以首先必须治愈疾病。这些药物中首要是金和珍珠，后者可以转化为第五精华（quinta essentia）。切伊里（Cheyri）7 被赋予了特殊的功效，它极大地强化微宇宙之体，使其"必然能够通过四元素之普遍解剖而保持其存续"。8 因此医师应确保四元素的"解剖"（＝结构）"被收缩为微宇宙的一个解剖，不是出自形体之物，而是出自保存形体之物"。这就是香脂，它甚至高于第五精华——即通常将四元素维系在一起的东西。它"甚至超越了自然本身"，因为它是由一种"身体运作"产生的。9 艺术能制造出高于自然之物，这一思想是典型的炼金术思想。香脂是生命原则，即水银之灵（spiritus mercurii），它或多或少与帕拉塞尔苏斯的伊利亚斯特概念相吻合。后者高于四元素，并决定寿命的长短。因此它大致等同于香脂，或者可以说香脂是伊利亚斯特的药理学或化学层面。10 伊利亚斯特有三种形式：圣化伊利亚斯特（Iliaster sanctitus），11 准备态（paratetus），12 和大伊利亚斯特（magnus）。它们从属于人（"microcosmo subditi"），可以被带入"一个 gamonymus"。由于帕拉塞尔苏斯赋予伊利亚斯特一种特殊的"结合之力与权"（vis ac potestas coniunctionis），这个谜一般的"gamonymus"（γάμος ＝ 婚姻，ὄνομα ＝ 名字）必须被解释为一种化学婚礼，换言之，一种不可分解的、雌雄同体的结合。13 伊利亚斯特的数量与人一样多；也就是说，每个人体内都有一个伊利亚斯特，维系着每个人独特的品质组合。14 因此，它似乎是一种普遍的形成原则和个体化原则。





B. THE AQUASTER
B. 阿夸斯特


[172] The Iliaster forms the starting point for the arcane preparation of longevity. “We will explain what is most needful in this process regarding the Iliaster. In the first place, the impure animate body must be purified through the separation of the elements, which is done by your meditating upon it; this consists in the confirmation of your mind beyond all bodily and mechanic work.”15 In this way a “new form is impressed” on the impure body.
[172] 伊利亚斯特构成了长生秘术制备的出发点。"我们将解释在此过程中关于伊利亚斯特最需要的事项。首先，不洁的有生之体必须通过元素的分离来净化，这是通过你对它的冥想来完成的；这在于你的心智超越一切身体和机械工作的确认。"15 通过这种方式，一种"新形式"被印在不洁之体上。

[173] I have translated imaginatio here by “meditating.” In the Paracelsist tradition imaginatio is the active power of the astrum (star) or corpus coeleste sive supracoeleste (Ruland), that is, of the higher man within. Here we encounter the psychic factor in alchemy: the artifex accompanies his chemical work with a simultaneous mental operation which is performed by means of the imagination. Its purpose is to cleanse away the impure admixture and at the same time to bring about the “confirmation” of the mind. The Paracelsan neologism confirmamentum is probably not without reference to the “firmament.” During this work man is “raised up in his mind, so that he is made equal to the Enochdiani” (those who enjoy an unusually long life, like Enoch).16 Hence his “interior anatomy” must be heated to the highest degree.17 In this way the impurities are consumed and only the solid is left, “without rust.” While the artifex heats the chemical substance in the furnace he himself is morally undergoing the same fiery torment and purification.18 By projecting himself into the substance he has become unconsciously identical with it and suffers the same process. Paracelsus does not fail to point out to his reader that this fire is not the same as the fire in the furnace. This fire, he says, contains nothing more of the “Salamandrine Essence or Melusinian Ares,” but is rather a “retorta distillatio from the midst of the centre, beyond all coal fire.” Since Melusina is a watery creature, the “Melusinian Ares”19 refers to the so-called “Aquaster,”20 which stands for the watery aspect of the Iliaster, i.e., the Iliaster which animates and preserves the liquids in the body. The Iliaster is without doubt a spiritual, invisible principle although it is also something like the prima materia, which, however, in alchemical usage by no means corresponds to what we understand by matter. For the alchemists the prima materia was the humidum radicale (radical moisture),21 the water,22 the spiritus aquae,23 and vapor terrae;24 it was also called the “soul” of the substances,25 the sperma mundi,26 Adam’s tree of paradise with its many flowers, which grows on the sea,27 the round body from the centre,28 Adam and the accursed man,29 the hermaphroditic monster,30 the One and the root of itself,31 the All,32 and so on. The symbolical names of the prima materia all point to the anima mundi, Plato’s Primordial Man, the Anthropos and mystic Adam, who is described as a sphere (= wholeness), consisting of four parts (uniting different aspects in itself), hermaphroditic (beyond division by sex), and damp (i.e., psychic). This paints a picture of the self, the indescribable totality of man.
[173] 我在此将 imaginatio 译为"冥想"。在帕拉塞尔苏斯主义传统中，imaginatio 是星辰（astrum）或天体或超天体（corpus coeleste sive supracoeleste，鲁兰德语）的主动力量，即内在之更高人的力量。在这里我们遇到了炼金术中的心理因素：工匠在进行化学工作的同时，伴随着一项通过想象来进行的心理运作。其目的是清除不洁的混合物，同时实现心智的"确认"。帕拉塞尔苏斯的新造词 confirmamentum（确认）大概并非与"苍穹"（firmament）无关。在这项工作期间，人"在心智中被提升，以至被等同于以诺式之人"（Enochdiani，即像以诺一样享有异常长寿的人）。16 因此他的"内在解剖"必须被加热到最高程度。17 这样不洁之物被消耗，只留下坚实的，"无锈"。当工匠在炉中加热化学物质时，他自己也在道德上经历同样的烈火煎熬和净化。18 通过将自身投射到物质中，他已无意识地与之同一，并遭受同样的过程。帕拉塞尔苏斯不忘向读者指出，这种火不同于炉中之火。他说，这火不再包含任何"火螄蜥精华或美露辛之阿瑞斯"（Melusinian Ares），而是一种"从中心之中央进行的回流蒸馏，超越一切炭火"。由于美露辛是水生之物，"美露辛之阿瑞斯"19 指的是所谓的"阿夸斯特"（Aquaster），20 它代表伊利亚斯特的水之面向，即赋予身体中的液体以活力并加以保存的伊利亚斯特。伊利亚斯特无疑是一个灵性的、不可见的原则，尽管它也类似于原初物质（prima materia），但在炼金术用法中，后者绝非我们所理解的"物质"。对炼金术士来说，原初物质是根本湿气（humidum radicale），21 水，22 水之灵（spiritus aquae），23 和地之蒸气（vapor terrae）；24 它也被称为物质的"灵魂"，25 世界之精（sperma mundi），26 亚当的乐园之树及其繁花，生长在海上的，27 来自中心的圆体，28 亚当和受诅咒之人，29 雌雄同体的怪物，30 自身即一且为自身之根，31 万物，32 等等。原初物质的象征名称全都指向世界灵魂（anima mundi）、柏拉图的原人、人和神秘亚当——他被描述为一个球体（＝整体），由四部分组成（在自身中统合不同面向），雌雄同体（超越性别之分），且湿润（即心理的）。这描绘了一幅自性——人那不可描述的整体——的图景。

[174] The Aquaster, too, is a spiritual principle; for instance, it shows the adept the “way by which he can search out divine magic.” The adept himself is an “aquastric magician.” The “scayolic33 Aquaster” shows him the “great cause” with the help of the Trarames (ghostly spirits). Christ took his body from the celestial Aquaster, and the body of Mary was “necrocomic”34 and “aquastric.” Mary “came from the iliastric Aquaster.” There, Paracelsus emphasizes, she stood on the moon (the moon is always related to water). Christ was born in the celestial Aquaster. In the human skull there is an “aquastric fissure,” in men on the forehead, in women at the back of the head. Through this fissure women are liable to be invaded in their “cagastric” Aquaster by a crowd of diabolical spirits; but men, through their fissure, give birth, “not cagastrically but necrocomically, to the necrocomic Animam vel spiritum vitae microcosmi, the iliastric spirit of life in the heart.” In the “centre of the heart dwells the true soul, the breath of God.”35
[174] 阿夸斯特同样是一个灵性原则；例如，它向修炼者展示"他可以借此探求神圣魔法的道路"。修炼者本人就是一个"阿夸斯特魔法师"。"斯卡约利克33 阿夸斯特"在特拉拉梅斯（幽灵之灵）的帮助下向他展示"伟大的因"。基督从天上的阿夸斯特获取了他的身体，而玛利亚的身体是"死灵体的"34 和"阿夸斯特的"。玛利亚"来自伊利亚斯特的阿夸斯特"。帕拉塞尔苏斯强调，在那里她站在月亮上（月亮总是与水相关）。基督诞生于天上的阿夸斯特。在人的头骨中有一个"阿夸斯特裂缝"，男性在额头，女性在后脑。通过这个裂缝，女性的"卡加斯特"阿夸斯特可能被一群魔鬼之灵侵入；而男性通过他们的裂缝，"不是以卡加斯特的方式而是以死灵体的方式"，生产出"微宇宙的死灵体生命灵魂或精神（Animam vel spiritum vitae microcosmi），即心中的伊利亚斯特生命之灵"。"在心的中央居住着真正的灵魂，上帝的气息。"35

[175] From these quotations it is easy to see what the Aquaster means. Whereas the Iliaster seems to be a dynamic spiritual principle, capable of both good and evil, the Aquaster, because of its watery nature, is more a “psychic” principle with quasimaterial attributes (since the bodies of Christ and Mary partook of it). But it functions psychically as a “necrocomic” (i.e., telepathic) agent related to the spiritual world, and as the birthplace of the spiritus vitae. Of all the Paracelsan concepts, therefore, the Aquaster comes closest to the modern concept of the unconscious. So we can see why Paracelsus personifies it as the homunculus and describes the soul as the celestial Aquaster. Like a true alchemist, he thought of the Aquaster and Iliaster as extending both upwards and downwards: they assume a spiritual or heavenly form as well as a quasi-material or earthly one. This is in keeping with the axiom from “Tabula smaragdina”: “What is below is like what is above, that the miracle of the one thing may be accomplished.” This one thing is the lapis or filius philosophorum.36 As the definitions and names of the prima materia make abundantly plain, matter in alchemy is material and spiritual, and spirit spiritual and material. Only, in the first case matter is cruda, confusa, grossa, crassa, densa, and in the second it is subtilis. Such, too, is the opinion of Paracelsus.
[175] 从这些引文中不难看出阿夸斯特意味着什么。如果说伊利亚斯特似乎是一个能动的灵性原则，兼具善与恶的能力，那么阿夸斯特由于其水性，更像是一个具有准物质属性的"心理"原则（因为基督和玛利亚的身体都参与了它）。但它在心理上作为一个与灵性世界相关的"死灵体的"（即心灵感应的）媒介发挥作用，同时也是生命之灵（spiritus vitae）的诞生地。因此，在所有帕拉塞尔苏斯的概念中，阿夸斯特最接近现代的无意识概念。由此我们可以理解为什么帕拉塞尔苏斯将它拟人化为人造人（homunculus），并将灵魂描述为天上的阿夸斯特。作为一个真正的炼金术士，他认为阿夸斯特和伊利亚斯特既向上也向下延伸：它们既有灵性的或天上的形态，也有准物质的或地上的形态。这与《翡翠石板》（Tabula smaragdina）中的格言一致："下如上，上如下，以成太一之奇迹。"这太一就是哲学家之石（lapis）或哲学家之子（filius philosophorum）。36 正如原初物质的定义和名称充分表明的那样，在炼金术中，物质既是物质的也是灵性的，精神既是灵性的也是物质的。只是在前一种情况下物质是粗的（cruda）、混乱的（confusa）、粗大的（grossa）、厚重的（crassa）、致密的（densa），而在后一种情况下则是精微的（subtilis）。帕拉塞尔苏斯的观点也是如此。





C. ARES
C. 阿瑞斯


[176] Rather superficially, Adam von Bodenstein conceives “Ares” to be the “prime nature of things, determining their form and species.”37 Ruland lumps it together with the Iliaster and Archeus. But whereas the Iliaster is the hypostasis of being in general (“generis generalissimi substantia”), Archeus is given the role of a “dispenser of nature” (naturae dispensator) and “initiator.” Ares, however, is the “assigner, who extends the peculiar nature to each species, and gives individual form.”38 It can therefore be taken as the principle of individuation in the strict sense. It proceeds from the supracelestial bodies, for “such is the property and nature of supracelestial bodies that they straightway produce out of nothing a corporeal imagination [imaginationem corporalem], so as to be thought a solid body. Of this kind is Ares, so that when one thinks of a wolf, a wolf appears.39 This world is like the creatures composed of the four elements. From the elements arise things which are in no way like their origins, but nonetheless Ares bears them all in himself.”40
[176] 亚当·冯·博登施泰因相当表面地将"阿瑞斯"（Ares）理解为"事物的初始本性，决定其形式和种类"。37 鲁兰德将其与伊利亚斯特和 Archeus 混为一谈。但如果说伊利亚斯特是一般存在之本质（"generis generalissimi substantia"，最普遍类属之实体），那么 Archeus 则被赋予"自然分配者"（naturae dispensator）和"开创者"的角色。然而阿瑞斯是"分配者，将独特的本性赋予每个种类，并给予个体形式"。38 因此，它可以被视为严格意义上的个体化原则。它源自超天体，因为"超天体的特性与本性便是如此：它们直接从虚无中产生出有形的想象〔imaginationem corporalem〕，以至于被认为是坚固之体。阿瑞斯便是此类，因此当一个人想到狼时，狼便出现。39 这个世界如同由四元素组成的造物。从元素中产生的事物与其起源毫不相似，但阿瑞斯将它们全部承载于自身之中。"40

[177] Ares, accordingly, is an intuitive concept for a preconscious, creative, and formative principle which is capable of giving life to individual creatures. It is thus a more specific principle of individuation than the Iliaster, and as such it plays an important role in the purification of the natural man by fire and his transformation into an “Enochdianus.” The fire he is heated with is, as we have seen, no ordinary fire, since it does not contain either the “Melusinian Ares” or the “Salamandrine Essence.” The salamander symbolizes the fire of the alchemists. It is itself of the nature of fire, a fiery essence. According to Paracelsus, Salamandrini and Saldini are men or spirits of fire, fiery beings. It is an old tradition that, because they have proved their incorruptibility in the fire, such creatures enjoy a particularly long life. The salamander is also the “incombustible sulphur”—another name for the arcane substance from which the lapis or filius is produced. The fire for heating the artifex contains nothing more of the nature of the salamander, which is an immature, transitional form of the filius, that incorruptible being whose symbols indicate the self.
[177] 因此，阿瑞斯是对一个前意识的、创造性的和形成性原则的直觉概念，该原则能够赋予个体造物以生命。因此，它是一个比伊利亚斯特更为具体的个体化原则，作为这样的原则，它在用火净化自然人并将其转化为"以诺式之人"（Enochdianus）的过程中发挥着重要作用。如我们所见，用来加热他的火并非寻常之火，因为它既不包含"美露辛之阿瑞斯"也不包含"火螄蜥精华"。火螄蜥象征着炼金术士的火。它本身具有火的性质，是一种火之精华。根据帕拉塞尔苏斯的说法，Salamandrini 和 Saldini 是火之人或火之灵，是火焰之 beings。一个古老的传统认为，因为这些造物在火中证明了其不可腐朽性，所以享有特别长寿。火螄蜥也是"不可燃硫磺"——即产生哲学家之石或子之秘术物质的另一个名称。用来加热工匠的火不再包含火螄蜥的性质，后者是子的一个不成熟的过渡形态——那个不可腐朽之存在，其象征指向自性。

[178] Paracelsus endows Ares with the attribute “Melusinian.” Since Melusina undoubtedly belongs to the watery realm, the realm of the nymphs, this attribute imports a watery character into the concept of Ares, which in itself is spiritual. Ares is thus brought into relationship with the lower, denser region and is intimately connected with the body. As a result, Ares becomes so like the Aquaster that it is scarcely possible to distinguish them conceptually. It is characteristic of Paracelsan thinking, and of alchemy in general, that there are no clear-cut concepts, so that one concept can take the place of another ad infinitum. At the same time every concept behaves hypostatically, as though it were a substance that could not at the same time be another substance. This typical primitive phenomenon is found also in Indian philosophy, which swarms with hypostases. Examples of this are the myths of the gods, which, as in Greek and Egyptian mythology, make utterly contradictory statements about the same god. Despite their contradictions, however, the myths continue to exist side by side without disturbing one another.
[178] 帕拉塞尔苏斯赋予阿瑞斯以"美露辛的"属性。由于美露辛无疑属于水的领域——宁芙的领域——这一属性将水的特征引入了本身是灵性的阿瑞斯概念中。由此，阿瑞斯与较低的、较致密的领域产生了关联，并与身体紧密相连。结果，阿瑞斯变得如此类似于阿夸斯特，以至于在概念上几乎不可能区分它们。帕拉塞尔苏斯思维——以及一般炼金术——的特征在于没有清晰界定概念，因此一个概念可以无限地替代另一个概念。同时，每个概念都以实体的方式行事，仿佛它是一种不能同时是另一种实体的实体。这种典型的原始现象也见于印度哲学，后者充满了实体化。诸神神话便是例证，如同在希腊和埃及神话中一样，它们对同一位神做出完全矛盾的陈述。然而，尽管存在矛盾，这些神话却继续并存而不相互干扰。





D. MELUSINA
D. 美露辛


[179] As we shall meet with Melusina several times more in the course of our interpretation, we must examine more closely the nature of this fabulous creature, and in particular the role she plays in Paracelsus. As we know, she belongs to the realm of the Aquaster, and is a water-nymph with the tail of a fish or snake. In the original old French legend she appears as “mère Lusine,” the ancestress of the counts of Lusignan. When her husband once surprised her in her fish-tail, which she had to wear only on Saturdays, her secret was out and she was forced to disappear again into the watery realm. She reappeared only from time to time, as a presage of disaster.
[179] 由于我们在诠释过程中还会多次遇到美露辛，因此必须更仔细地审视这一传说生物的本性，尤其是她在帕拉塞尔苏斯中所扮演的角色。如我们所知，她属于阿夸斯特的领域，是一个长着鱼尾或蛇尾的水中宁芙。在最初的古法语传说中，她以"mère Lusine"（露西娜之母）的形象出现，是吕西尼昂伯爵家族的女祖先。当她的丈夫有一次撞见她长着鱼尾——这只在星期六才会出现——她的秘密便暴露了，她被迫再次消失在水之领域中。她只是不时重新出现，作为灾难的预兆。

[180] Melusina comes into the same category as the nymphs and sirens who dwell in the “Nymphidida,” the watery realm.41 In the treatise “De sanguine,”42 the nymph is specified as a Schröttli, ‘nightmare.’ Melusines, on the other hand, dwell in the blood.43 Paracelsus tells us in “De pygmaeis”44 that Melusina was originally a nymph who was seduced by Beelzebub into practising witchcraft. She was descended from the whale in whose belly the prophet Jonah beheld great mysteries. This derivation is very important: the birthplace of Melusina is the womb of the mysteries, obviously what we today would call the unconscious. Melusines have no genitals,45 a fact that characterizes them as paradisal beings, since Adam and Eve in paradise had no genitals either.46’ Moreover paradise was then beneath the water “and still is.”47 When the devil glided into the tree of paradise the tree was “saddened,” and Eve was seduced by the “infernal basilisk.”48 Adam and Eve “fell for” the serpent and became “monstrous,” that is, as a result of their slip-up with the snake they acquired genitals.49 But the Melusines remained in the paradisal state as water creatures and went on living in the human blood. Since blood is a primitive symbol for the soul,50 Melusina can be interpreted as a spirit, or at any rate as some kind of psychic phenomenon. Gerard Dorn confirms this in his commentary on De vita longa, where he says that Melusina is a “vision appearing in the mind.”51 For anyone familiar with the subliminal processes of psychic transformation, Melusina is clearly an anima figure. She appears as a variant of the mercurial serpent, which was sometimes represented in the form of a snake-woman52 by way of expressing the monstrous, double nature of Mercurius. The redemption of this monstrosity was depicted as the assumption and coronation of the Virgin Mary.53
[180] 美露辛与居住在"宁芙之域"（Nymphidida）即水之领域中的宁芙和海妖塞壬属于同一类别。41 在《论血》论著中，42 宁芙被具体指定为 Schröttli，即'梦魇'。而美露辛则居住在血液中。43 帕拉塞尔苏斯在《论矮人》中44 告诉我们，美露辛原本是一位被别西卜引诱去行巫术的宁芙。她源自在其腹中先知约拿看到伟大奥秘的鲸鱼。这一渊源非常重要：美露辛的诞生地是奥秘的子宫——显然就是我们今天所说的无意识。美露辛没有生殖器，45 这一事实将她们特征化为乐园之 beings，因为亚当和夏娃在乐园中也没有生殖器。46' 此外乐园当时在水下，"现在仍然如此"。47 当魔鬼滑入乐园之树时，树"悲伤了"，夏娃被"地狱蛇怪"诱惑。48 亚当和夏娃"堕入"蛇的圈套并变得"怪异"——也就是说，由于与蛇的差错，他们获得了生殖器。49 但美露辛作为水之 beings 保持了乐园状态，继续生活在人的血液中。由于血液是灵魂的原始象征，50 美露辛可以被解释为一个精灵，或无论如何是某种心理现象。杰拉德·多恩在他对《论长生》的注释中证实了这一点，他说美露辛是"出现在心智中的幻象"。51 对于任何熟悉心理转化的阈下过程的人来说，美露辛显然是一个阿尼玛形象。她以水银蛇的一个变体出现，后者有时以蛇女的形式52 来表现墨丘利乌斯怪异的双重本性。这种怪异的救赎被描绘为圣母玛利亚的升天和加冕。53





E. THE FILIUS REGIUS AS THE ARCANE SUBSTANCE (MICHAEL MAIER)
E. 作为秘术物质的王者之子（迈克尔·迈尔）


[181] It is not my intention to enter more closely into the relations between the Paracelsan Melusines and the mercurial serpent. I only wish to point out the alchemical prototypes that may have had an influence on Paracelsus, and to suggest that the longing of Melusina for a soul and for redemption has a parallel in that kingly substance which is hidden in the sea and cries out for deliverance. Of this filius regius Michael Maier says:54 “He lives and calls from the depths:55 Who shall deliver me from the waters and lead me to dry land? Even though this cry be heard of many, yet none takes it upon himself, moved by pity, to seek the king. For who, they say, will plunge into the waters? Who will imperil his life by taking away the peril of another? Only a few believe his lament, and think rather that they hear the crashing and roaring of Scylla and Charybdis. Therefore they remain sitting indolently at home, and give no thought to the kingly treasure, nor to their own salvation.”
[181] 我并不打算更深入地探讨帕拉塞尔苏斯的美露辛与水银蛇之间的关系。我只想指出可能对帕拉塞尔苏斯产生影响的炼金术原型，并提示美露辛对灵魂和救赎的渴望与那隐藏在海中、呼喊求解放的王者物质有着平行关系。关于这王者之子（filius regius），迈克尔·迈尔说：54 "他活着并从深处呼唤：55 谁将把我从水中救出，引我到干地？尽管许多人听到了这呼声，却无人出于怜悯而承担起寻找国王的责任。因为谁，他们说，会跳入水中？谁会冒着生命危险去解除他人的危险？只有少数人相信他的哀叹，更多地以为他们听到的是斯库拉和卡律布狄斯的轰鸣和咆哮。因此他们懒散地坐在家中，既不关心王者宝藏，也不关心自己的救赎。"

[182] We know that Maier can have had no access to the Philosophumena of Hippolytus, long believed lost, and yet it might well have served him as a model for the king’s lament. Treating of the mysteries of the Naassenes, Hippolytus says: “But what that form is which comes down from above, from the Uncharacterized [ἀχαρακτηρἰστου], no man knows. It is found in earthly clay, and yet none recognize it. But that is the god who dwells in the great flood.58 In the Psalter he calls and cries out from many waters.57 The many waters, they say, are the multitude of mortal men, whence he calls and cries aloud to the uncharacterized Man:58 Save mine Only-Begotten59 from the lions.”60 And he receives the reply [Isaiah 43 : 1ff.]: “And now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and formed thee, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name. Thou art mine. When thou shalt pass through the waters, I will be with thee, and the rivers shall not cover thee. When thou shalt walk through the fire, thou shalt not be burnt, and the flames shall not burn in thee.” Hippolytus goes on to quote Psalm 23 : 7ff., (DV), referring it to the ascent (ἄνοδος) or regeneration (ἀναγέννησις) of Adam: “Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates, and the King of Glory shall enter in. Who is this King of Glory? The Lord who is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. . . . But who, say the Naassenes, is this King of Glory? A worm and no man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people.”61
[182] 我们知道迈尔不可能接触到希波吕托斯的《哲学述评》——该书长期被认为已经佚失——但它很可能为他提供了国王哀叹的范本。在论述拿撒尼派奥秘时，希波吕托斯说："但从上面、从那不可名状者〔ἀχαρακτηριστου〕降下来的那个形式是什么样的，无人知晓。它被发现于尘世泥土中，却无人认出它。但那就是寓居于大洪水中的神。56 在《诗篇》中，他从众水中呼唤呐喊。57 众水，他们说，即是必死之人的群多，他从其中向那不可名状之人呼喊：58 从狮子中救出我的独生子。"60 他得到的回答是〔以赛亚书43:1以下〕："如今创造你的主、塑造你的以色列的雅各如此说：不要害怕，因为我已救赎了你，以你的名呼召了你。你是属我的。你从水中经过，我必与你同在；江河不能漫过你。你从火中行过，必不被烧，火焰不会在你身上燃烧。"希波吕托斯接着引用《诗篇》23:7以下（杜艾版），将其与亚当的上升（ἄνοδος）或重生（ἀναγέννησις）联系起来："众城门啊，抬起你们的门楣，永久的门户啊，被举起，荣耀之王将要进来。这荣耀之王是谁？是有力有能的主，在战场上大有能力的主。……但拿撒尼派说，这荣耀之王是谁？是一条虫，不是人，是人的耻辱，是被百姓弃绝的。"61

[183] It is not difficult to see what Michael Maier means. For him the filius regius or Rex marinus, as is evident from a passage in the text not quoted here, means antimony,62 though in his usage it has only the name in common with the chemical element. In reality it is the secret transformative substance, which fell from the highest place into the darkest depths of matter where it awaits deliverance. But no one will plunge into these depths in order, by his own transformation in the darkness and by the torment of fire, to rescue his king. They cannot hear the voice of the king and think it is the chaotic roar of destruction. The sea (mare nostrum) of the alchemists is their own darkness, the unconscious. In his way, Epiphanius63 correctly interpreted the “mire of the deep” (limus profundi) as “matter born of the mind, smutty reflections and muddy thoughts of sin.” Therefore David in his affliction had said (Psalm 68 : 3, DV): “I stick fast in the mire of the deep.” For the Church Father these dark depths could only be evil itself, and if a king got stuck in them it was on account of his own sinfulness. The alchemists took a more optimistic view: the dark background of the soul contains not only evil but a king in need of, and capable of, redemption, of whom the Rosarium says: “At the end of the work the king will go forth for thee, crowned with his diadem, radiant as the sun, shining like the carbuncle . . . constant in the fire.”64 And of the worthless prima materia they say: “Despise not the ash, for it is the diadem of thy heart, and the ash of things that endure.”65
[183] 不难看出迈克尔·迈尔的意图。对他来说，王者之子或海中之王（Rex marinus），正如文中未引用的一段所表明的那样，指的是锡，62 但在他的用法中，它与化学元素仅仅共有名称而已。实际上，它是秘密的转化物质，从最高处坠入物质最黑暗的深渊，在那里等待解放。但没有人愿意潜入这些深处，通过自身在黑暗中的转化和火的煎熬来拯救他的国王。他们听不到国王的声音，以为那是毁灭的混沌咆哮。炼金术士的海洋（mare nostrum）就是他们自身的黑暗，即无意识。以他自己的方式，埃皮法尼乌斯63 正确地将"深渊之泥"（limus profundi）解释为"生于心智的物质，肮脏的反思和罪恶的浑浊思想"。因此大卫在苦难中说（《诗篇》68:3，杜艾版）："我陷在深渊之泥中。"对教父来说，这些黑暗深处只能是邪恶本身，如果一个国王陷在其中，那是由于他自身的罪。炼金术士则持更为乐观的看法：灵魂的黑暗背景不仅包含邪恶，还包含一个需要且能够被救赎的国王——《玫瑰园》（Rosarium）说："在工作的末了，国王将为你而出，头戴王冠，如太阳般光辉，如红宝石般闪耀……在火中恒定不变。"64 而对于无价值的原初物质，他们说："不要轻视灰烬，因为它是你心的王冠，是持久之物的灰烬。"65

[184] These quotations give one an idea of the mystic aura that surrounded the figure of the filius regius, and I do not think it superfluous to have drawn attention to that distant period when the central ideas of philosophical alchemy were being freely discussed by the Gnostics. Hippolytus gives us perhaps the most complete insight into their analogical thinking, which is akin to that of the alchemists. Anyone who came into contact with alchemy during the first half of the sixteenth century could not fail to feel the fascination of these Gnostic ideas. Although Maier lived and wrote more than seventy years after Paracelsus, and we have no reason to suppose that Paracelsus was acquainted with the heresiologists, his knowledge of the alchemical treatises, and particularly of Hermes [Fig. B6] which he so often quotes, would have sufficed to impress upon him the figure of the filius regius and also that of the much lauded Mater Natura—a figure not entirely in accord with the views of Christianity. Thus the “Tractatus aureus Hermetis” says: “O mightiest nature of the natures, who containest and separatest the midmost of the natures, who comest with the light and art born with the light, who hast given birth to the misty darkness, who art the mother of all beings!”66 This invocation echoes the classical feeling for nature, and its style is reminiscent of the oldest alchemical treatises, such as those of pseudo-Democritus, and of the Greek Magic Papyri. In this same treatise we encounter the Rex coronatus and filius noster rex genitus, of whom it is said: “For the son is a blessing and possesses wisdom. Come hither, ye sons of the wise, and let us be glad and rejoice, for death is overcome, and the son reigns; he is clothed with the red garment, and the purple [chermes] is put on.” He lives from “our fire,” and nature “nourishes him who shall endure for ever” with a “small fire.” When the son is brought to life by the opus, he becomes a “warrior fire” or a “fighter of fire.”67
[184] 这些引文让人领略到王者之子形象周围的神秘光环，我认为注意到那个遥远的时代——当时哲学炼金术的核心思想正被诺斯替教派自由讨论——并非多余。希波吕托斯也许为我们提供了对他们的类比思维——与炼金术士的思维相通——最完整的洞见。任何在十六世纪上半叶接触炼金术的人，都不可能不感受到这些诺斯替思想的魅力。虽然迈尔生活和写作的时间比帕拉塞尔苏斯晚了七十多年，我们也没有理由假定帕拉塞尔苏斯了解那些异端学家，但他对炼金术论著的了解——尤其是他经常引用的赫尔墨斯文献〔图B6〕——足以使王者之子的形象以及备受赞颂的自然之母（Mater Natura）的形象——一个与基督教观点不完全一致的形象——深深印在他心中。因此《赫尔墨斯金色论著》说："啊，众自然之中最强有力的自然，你包含并分离众自然之核心，你随光而来，与光同生，你生出了朦胧的黑暗，你是万物之母！"66 这一祈唤回响着古典的自然感情，其风格令人想起最古老的炼金术论著，如伪德谟克利特的论著，以及希腊魔法纸草文献。在同一部论著中，我们遇到了加冕之王（Rex coronatus）和我们生出的王者之子（filius noster rex genitus），关于他说："因为子是祝福，拥有智慧。来吧，智慧之子们，让我们欢欣喜悦，因为死亡已被克服，子已为王；他穿上红色衣袍，披上紫色〔chermes〕。"他以"我们的火"为生，自然用"小火""滋养那将永存者"。当子通过炼金术操作被赋予生命时，他成为"战士之火"或"火之斗士"。67





F. THE PRODUCTION OF THE ONE, OR CENTRE, BY DISTILLATION
F. 通过蒸馏产出太一或中心


[185] After this discussion of some of the basic concepts of alchemy, let us come back to the Paracelsan process of transforming the Iliaster. Paracelsus calls this process a retorta distillatio. The purpose of distillation in alchemy was to extract the volatile substance, or spirit, from the impure body. This process was a psychic as well as a physical experience. The retorta distillatio is not a known technical term, but presumably it meant a distillation that was in some way turned back upon itself. It might have taken place in the vessel called the Pelican [Fig. B7], where the distillate runs back into the belly of the retort. This was the “circulatory distillation,” much favoured by the alchemists. By means of the “thousandfold distillation” they hoped to achieve a particularly “refined” result.68 It is not unlikely that Paracelsus had something like this in mind, for his aim was to purify the human body to such a degree that it would finally unite with the maior homo, the inner spiritual man, and partake of his longevity. As we have remarked, this was not an ordinary chemical operation, it was essentially a psychological procedure. The fire to be used was a symbolical fire, and the distillation had to start “from the midst of the centre” (ex medio centri).
[185] 在讨论了炼金术的一些基本概念之后，让我们回到帕拉塞尔苏斯转化伊利亚斯特的过程。帕拉塞尔苏斯将这一过程称为回流蒸馏（retorta distillatio）。在炼金术中，蒸馏的目的是从不洁之体中提取挥发性物质即精神。这一过程既是物理体验也是心理体验。回流蒸馏并非一个已知的技术术语，但大概意味着一种以某种方式回转自身的蒸馏。它可能发生在被称为鹈鹱瓶〔图B7〕的容器中，在那里馏出物流回蒸馏瓶的腹部。这就是炼金术士极为钟爱的"循环蒸馏"。通过"千次蒸馏"，他们希望获得特别"精炼"的结果。68 帕拉塞尔苏斯心中很可能想的正是类似的东西，因为他的目标是将人体净化到如此程度，使之最终与更大之人（maior homo）——内在的灵性之人——合一，并分享其长寿。如前所述，这不是一次普通的化学操作，它在本质上是一个心理过程。所使用的火是象征性的火，蒸馏必须"从中心之中央"（ex medio centri）开始。

[186] The accentuation of the centre is again a fundamental idea in alchemy. According to Michael Maier, the centre contains the “indivisible point,” which is simple, indestructible, and eternal. Its physical counterpart is gold, which is therefore a symbol of eternity.69 In Christianos the centre is compared to paradise and its four rivers. These symbolize the philosophical fluids (ὑγρά), which are emanations from the centre.70 “In the centre of the earth the seven planets took root, and left their virtues there, wherefore in the earth is a germinating water,” says Aurora consurgens.71 Benedictus Figulus72 writes:
[186] 对中心的强调同样是炼金术的一个基本思想。根据迈克尔·迈尔的说法，中心包含"不可分割之点"，它是简单的、不可毁灭的和永恒的。其物理对应物是金，金因此是永恒的象征。69 在克里斯蒂亚诺斯那里，中心被比作乐园及其四条河流。这些象征着哲学流体（ὑγρά），是从中心流出的流溢。70 "在地之中心，七行星扎下了根，将它们的德性留在了那里，因此地中有一萌发之水，"《升腾之曙光》说。71 本尼迪克图斯·菲古鲁斯72 写道：

Visit the centre of the earth,
"探访大地之中心，"

There you will find the global fire.
"在那里你将找到全球之火。"

Rectify it of all dirt,
"将一切污秽从中净化，"

Drive it out with love and ire. . . .
"以爱与怒将其驱出。……"

He calls this centre the “house of fire” or “Enoch,” obviously borrowing the latter term from Paracelsus. Dorn says that nothing is more like God than the centre, for it occupies no space, and cannot be grasped, seen, or measured. Such, too, is the nature of God and the spirits. Therefore the centre is “an infinite abyss of mysteries.”73 The fire that originates in the centre carries everything upward, but when it cools everything falls back again to the centre. “The physiochemists call this movement circular, and they imitate it in their operations.” At the moment of culmination, just before the descent, the elements “conceive the male seeds of the stars,” which enter into the elemental matrices (i.e., the non-sublimated elements) during the descent. Thus all created things have four fathers and four mothers. The conception of the seeds results from the “influxum et impressionem” of Sol and Luna, who thus function as nature gods, though Dorn does not say this quite as clearly.74
他将这一中心称为"火之屋"或"以诺"，后者显然借自帕拉塞尔苏斯。多恩说，没有什么比中心更像上帝，因为它不占据空间，不能被把握、看见或测量。上帝和诸灵的本性也是如此。因此中心是"奥秘的无尽深渊"。73 起源于中心的火将一切向上携带，但当它冷却时，一切又回落到中心。"物理化学家称这种运动为圆形运动，他们在操作中模仿它。"在达到顶点的那一刻，就在下降之前，元素们"受孕了星辰的雄性种子"，这些种子在下降过程中进入元素的母体（即未升华的元素）。因此一切受造物有四个父亲和四个母亲。种子的受孕源自太阳和月亮的"流入与印象"（influxum et impressionem），它们因此作为自然之神发挥作用，尽管多恩没有说得那么清楚。74

[187] The creation of the elements and their ascent to heaven through the force of the fire serve as a model for the spagyric process. The lower waters, cleansed of their darkness, must be separated from the celestial waters by a carefully regulated fire. “In the end it will come to pass that this earthly, spagyric foetus clothes itself with heavenly nature by its ascent, and then by its descent visibly puts on the nature of the centre of the earth, but nonetheless the nature of the heavenly centre which it acquired by the ascent is secretly preserved.”75 The spagyric birth (spagirica foetura) is nothing other than the filius philosophorum, the inner, eternal man in the shell of the outer, mortal man. The filius is not only a panacea for all bodily defects, it also conquers the “subtle and spiritual sickness in the human mind.” “For in the One,” says Dorn,76 “is the One and yet not the One; it is simple and consists of the number four. When this is purified by the fire in the sun,77 the pure water78 comes forth, and, having returned to simplicity,79 it [the quaternity as unity] will show the adept the fulfilment of the mysteries. This is the centre of the natural wisdom, whose circumference, closed in itself, forms a circle: an immeasurable order reaching to infinity.” “Here is the number four, within whose bounds the number three, together with the number two combined into One, fulfils all things, which it does in miraculous wise.” In these relations between four, three, two, and one is found, says Dorn, the “culmination of all knowledge and of the mystic art, and the infallible midpoint of the centre (infallibile medii centrum).”80 The One is the midpoint of the circle, the centre of the triad, and it is also the “novenary foetus” (foetus novenarius), i.e., it is as the number nine to the ogdoad, or as the quintessence to the quaternity.31
[187] 元素的创造及其通过火力升入天界，为斯帕吉里克过程提供了模型。下层之水在洗去其黑暗之后，必须通过精心调控的火与天上的水分离开来。"最终将发生的是，这一尘世的、斯帕吉里克胎儿在其上升时为自己穿上天的本性，然后在其下降时可见地穿上地之中心的本性，但尽管如此，它在上升时获得的天之中心的本性却被秘密地保存着。"75 斯帕吉里克之生（spagirica foetura）不是别的，正是哲学家之子——外在必死之人的外壳中的内在永恒之人。哲学家之子不仅是所有身体缺陷的万灵药，它还征服了"人心中的精微和灵性之病"。"因为太一中，"多恩说，76 "有太一而非太一；它是简单的，由数字四组成。当这被太阳中的火净化时，77 纯水78 出现，在回归简单之后，79 它〔作为统一的四元〕将向修炼者展示奥秘的圆满。这是自然智慧的中心，其周围自我封闭形成一个圆：一个延伸至无限的不可度量之秩序。""这里是数字四，在其范围内数字三连同数字二合为太一，成就万物，以奇迹般的方式做到。"多恩说，在四、三、二、一的这些关系中，找到了"一切知识和秘术的顶峰，以及中心的无误中点（infallibile medii centrum）"。80 太一是圆的中点，三元之中心，它也是"九数胎儿"（foetus novenarius），即它对于八元而言如数字九，或如第五精华对于四元。31

[188] The midpoint of the centre is fire. On it is modelled the simplest and most perfect form, which is the circle. The point is most akin to the nature of light,82 and light is a simulacrum Dei.83 Just as the firmament was created in the midst of the waters above and below the heavens, so in man there is a shining body, the radical moisture, which comes from the sphere of the heavenly waters.84 This body is the “sidereal balsam,” which maintains the animal heat. The spirit of the supracelestial waters has its seat in the brain, where it controls the sense organs. In the microcosm the balsam dwells in the heart,85 like the sun in the macrocosm. The shining body is the corpus astrale, the “firmament” or “star” in man. Like the sun in the heavens, the balsam in the heart is a fiery, radiant centre. We meet this solar point in the Turba,86 where it signifies the “germ of the egg, which is in the yolk, and that germ is set in motion by the hen’s warmth.” The “Consilium coniugii” says that in the egg are the four elements and the “red sun-point in the centre, and this is the young chick.”87 Mylius interprets this chick as the bird of Hermes,88 which is another synonym for the mercurial serpent.
[188] 中心的中点是火。在其上塑造了最简单也最完美的形式，即圆。点最接近光的性质，82 而光是上帝的肖像（simulacrum Dei）。83 正如穹苍被创造在诸天之上和之下的众水之中，人之中也有一个发光之体——根本湿气——它来自天上众水的领域。84 这一体是"星辰香脂"，它维持着体温。超天体之水的灵居于大脑，在那里它控制着感官器官。在微宇宙中，香脂寓居在心中，85 如同太阳在宏观宇宙中。发光之体是星辰之体（corpus astrale），人中的"穹苍"或"星"。如同太阳在天上，心中的香脂是一个火的、辐射的中心。我们在《集会》中遇到这个太阳之点，86 在那里它意味着"蛋中的胚芽，位于蛋黄之中，而那胚芽被母鸡的温暖所推动"。《婚配之议》说蛋中有四元素和"中心的红色太阳之点，这就是小鸡。"87 米利乌斯将这只小鸡解释为赫尔墨斯之鸟，88 这是水银蛇的另一个同义词。

[189] From this context we can see that the retorta distillatio ex medio centri results in the activation and development of a psychic centre, a concept that coincides psychologically with that of the self.
[189] 从这一上下文中我们可以看出，从中心之中央进行的回流蒸馏（retorta distillatio ex medio centri）导致一个心理中心的激活和发展——这一概念在心理学上与自性的概念相吻合。





G. THE CONIUNCTIO IN THE SPRING
G. 春季的结合


[190] At the end of the process, says Paracelsus, a “physical lightning” will appear, the “lightning of Saturn” will separate from the lightning of Sol, and what appears in this lightning pertains “to longevity, to that undoubtedly great Iliaster.”89 This process does not take anything away from the body’s weight but only from its “turbulence,” and that “by virtue of the translucent colours.”80 “Tranquillity of mind”91 as a goal of the opus is stressed also by other alchemists. Paracelsus has nothing good to say about the body. It is “bad and putrid.” When it is alive, it lives only from the “Mumia.” Its “continual endeavour” is to rot and turn back into filth. By means of the Mumia the “peregrinus microcosmus” (wandering microcosm) controls the physical body, and for this the arcana are needed.92 Here Paracelsus lays particular stress on Thereniabin93 and Nostoch94 (as before on Cheyri) and on the “tremendous powers” of Melissa. Melissa is singled out for special honour because in ancient medicine it was considered to be a means of inducing happiness, and was used as a remedy for melancholia and for purging the body of “black, burnt-out blood.”95 It unites in itself the powers of the “supracelestial coniunctio,” and that is “Iloch, which comes from the true Aniadus.” As Paracelsus had spoken just before of Nostoch, the Iliaster has changed under his eyes into Iloch. The Aniadus that now makes its appearance constitutes the essence of Iloch, i.e., of the coniunctio. But to what does the coniunctio refer? Before this Paracelsus had been speaking of a separation of Saturn and Sol. Saturn is the cold, dark, heavy, impure element, Sol is the opposite. When this separation is completed and the body has been purified by Melissa and freed from Saturnine melancholy, then the coniunctio can take place with the long-living inner, or astral, man,96 and from this conjunction arises the “Enochdianus.” Iloch or Aniadus appears to be something like the virtue or power of the everlasting man. This “Magnale” comes about by the “exaltation of both worlds,” and “in the true May, when the exaltations of Aniada begin, these should be gathered.” Here again Paracelsus outdoes himself in obscurity, but this much at least is evident, that Aniadus denotes a springtime condition, the “efficacity of things,” as Dorn defines it.
[190] 帕拉塞尔苏斯说，在过程的末了，将出现一种"物理闪电"，"土星之闪电"将与太阳之闪电分离，而这闪电中所出现的事物属于"长寿，属于那无疑伟大的伊利亚斯特"。89 这一过程不从身体的重量中取走任何东西，只取走其"骚动"，而且是"凭借半透明的颜色"。80 "心灵之宁静"91 作为炼金术的目标也受到其他炼金术士的强调。帕拉塞尔苏斯对身体没有好话。它是"坏的、腐臭的"。活着时，它仅靠"穆米亚"存活。它"持续不断的努力"就是腐烂并变回污秽。通过穆米亚，"流浪微宇宙"（peregrinus microcosmus）控制着身体，为此需要秘药。92 这里帕拉塞尔苏斯特别强调特雷尼亚宾93 和诺斯托克94（如同之前强调切伊里一样）以及蜜蜂花（Melissa）的"巨大力量"。蜜蜂花被单独给予特别荣誉，因为在古代医学中它被认为是引发快乐的手段，被用作治疗忧郁症和清除身体中"黑色、烧尽的血液"的药物。95 它在自身中统一了"超天体结合"的力量，那就是"伊洛赫（Iloch），来自真正的阿尼亚杜斯（Aniadus）"。由于帕拉塞尔苏斯在此之前刚谈到诺斯托克，伊利亚斯特在他眼下变成了伊洛赫。现在出现的阿尼亚杜斯构成了伊洛赫即结合的本质。但结合指的是什么？在此之前帕拉塞尔苏斯谈到了土星和太阳的分离。土星是冷的、暗的、重的、不洁的元素，太阳则相反。当这一分离完成、身体被蜜蜂花净化并从土星式忧郁中解放出来之后，结合就可以与长寿的内在之人即星辰之人96 发生，从这一结合中产生出"以诺式之人"。伊洛赫或阿尼亚杜斯似乎是某种类似永恒之人的德性或力量的东西。这一"伟业"（Magnale）通过"两个世界的提升"而产生，"在真正的五月，当阿尼亚达的提升开始时，应采集它们。"帕拉塞尔苏斯在这里再次在晦涩方面超越了自己，但至少有一点是清楚的，即阿尼亚杜斯表示一种春季状态——多恩所定义的"事物的效力"。
