Harum tempora prima, i.e. initia annuit, i.e. admittit, sed ad finem seipsum immutat, intellige propter intervenientes ac impedientes distractiones, quo minus consequantur effectum inchoatae, scl. operationes. Ex quibus [Paracelsus] colligit supermonica1 figmenta, hoc est, speculationes aenigmaticas, in cyphantis [vas stillatorium], i.e. separationum vel praeparationum operationibus, aperire fenestram, hoc est, intellectum, sed ut figantur, i.e. ad finem perducantur, recusant gesta Melosines, hoc est, visionum varietates, et observationes, quae cuius modi sunt (ait) missa facimus.
[帕拉塞尔苏斯]说美露辛，即出现在心智中的幻象……从宁芙之性离去，进入另一种转化，在其中她将留存——只要那困难的阿德赫，即内在之人，允许，即赞许：他确实产生两者，即斯卡约拉——即心智操作——的死与生。它们的最初时光，即开端，他允许，即赞许；但在最终他改变了自身，理解为由于介入和妨碍的干扰，使已开始的事物——即操作——无法达到效果。由此[帕拉塞尔苏斯]推断，超凡的1 构想，即谜一般的思辨，在蒸馏器[vas stillatorium]中——即分离或制备的操作中——打开一扇窗，即理智；但为了使之固定，即达到终点，必须拒绝美露辛的作为，即幻象的多样性和观察，不管是什么样的（他说），我们将其搁置。（拉丁原文保留不译）

[Paracelsus] says that Melusina, i.e., the vision appearing in the mind, departs from her nymphididic nature into another transmutation, in which she will remain if only that difficult Adech, that is, the inner man, permit, that is, approve: who brings about both, that is, death and life, of the Scaiolae, that is, the mental operations. The first times, that is, the beginnings, of these he permits, that is, favours; but at the end he changes himself, namely because of the distractions that intervene and impede, so that the things begun, that is, the operations, do not obtain their effect.
[帕拉塞尔苏斯]说美露辛——即出现在心智中的幻象——从宁芙之性离去，进入另一种转化，在其中她将留存——只要那困难的阿德赫，即内在之人允许，即赞许：他产生两者，即斯卡约拉——即心智操作——的死与生。它们的最初时光，即开端，他允许，即赞许；但在最终他改变了自身，即因为介入和妨碍的干扰，使已开始的事物——即操作——无法达到效果。



Ad naturam nymphididicam rediens, ut in animis nostris concipiatur, inquit atque hac via ad annum aniadin2 perveniamus, hoc est, ad vitam longam per imaginationem, arripimus characteres Veneris, i.e. amoris scutum et loricam ad viriliter adversis resistendum obstaculis: amor enim omnem difficultatem superat: quos et si vos una cum aliis cognoscitis, putato characteres, minime tamen usurpatis. Absolvit itaque iam Paracelsus ea, quae prioribus capitibus indicavit in vitam hanc secure consequendam, in qua dominatur et regnat aniadus, i.e. rerum efficicia et cum ea is, cui sine fine assistimus, permanet, aniadus nempe coelestis: Haec atque alia arcana nulla re prorsus indigent.3
回到宁芙之性，为了使她能被构想于我们的心智中，他说，并通过这条道路到达阿尼亚丁2 之年，即通过想象达到长生，我们取维纳斯之符，即爱之盾与胄，以雄壮地抵抗逆境中的障碍：因为爱克服一切困难：即使你们与他人一起认识这些符，却几乎没有使用过。帕拉塞尔苏斯以此完成了在前几章中所指出的，以便我们安全地获得那阿尼亚杜斯——即事物的效力——统治和主宰的生命，并永远与那天上的阿尼亚杜斯同在——在他之中我们无尽地存在：这以及其他奥秘绝对不需要任何事物。3（拉丁原文保留不译）

From which [Paracelsus] concludes that the supermonic1 figments, that is, enigmatical speculations, in the Cyphanta [distilling vessel], open a window, that is, the understanding, by means of the operations of separation or preparation; but in order to become fixed, that is, brought to an end, they have to oppose the acts of Melusina, that is, divers visions and observations, which of whatever kind they may be, he says, we dismiss. Returning to the nymphididic realm, in order that [she] may be conceived in our minds, and that in this way we may attain to the year Aniadin,2 that is, to a long life by imagination, we take the characters, of Venus, that is, the shield and buckler of love, to resist manfully the obstacles that confront us, for love overcomes all difficulties; which characters, even if you know yourselves one with others, you have nevertheless put to little use. And thus Paracelsus brings to an end those things which he treated of in the earlier chapters, that we may safely obtain that life over which Aniadus, that is, the efficacity of things, dominates and reigns, and which endures for ever with him, namely the heavenly Aniadus, in whom we are present without end: this and other mysteries are in need of nothing whatever.3
由此[帕拉塞尔苏斯]推断，超凡的1 构想，即谜一般的思辨，在蒸馏器中——即通过分离或制备的操作——打开一扇窗，即理智；但为了使之固定，即达到终点，必须拒绝美露辛的作为，即多样的幻象和观察，不管是什么样的（他说），我们将其搁置。回到宁芙之性，为了使她能被构想于我们的心智中，并通过这条道路到达阿尼亚丁2 之年——即通过想象达到长生——我们取维纳斯之符，即爱之盾与胄，以雄壮地抵抗我们面前的障碍，因为爱克服一切困难；这些符即使你们与他人一起认识，却几乎没有使用过。帕拉塞尔苏斯以此完成了在前几章中所指出的，以便我们安全地获得那阿尼亚杜斯——即事物的效力——统治和主宰的生命，并永远与那天上的阿尼亚杜斯同在——在他之中我们无尽地存在：这以及其他奥秘绝对不需要任何事物。3





A. MELUSINA AND THE PROCESS OF INDIVIDUATION
A. 美露辛与个体化过程


[215] The text certainly needs a commentary! The Scaiolae, as the four parts, limbs, or emanations of the Anthropos,4 are the organs with which he actively intervenes in the world of appearances or by which he is connected with it, just as the invisible quinta essentia, or aether, appears in this world as the four elements or, conversely, is composed out of them. Since the Scaiolae, as we have seen, are also psychic functions, these must be understood as manifestations or effluences of the One, the invisible Anthropos. As functions of consciousness, and particularly as imaginatio, speculatio, phantasia, and fides, they “intervene” and stimulate Melusina, the water-nixie, to change herself into human form. Dorn thinks of this as a “vision appearing in the mind” and not as a projection on a real woman. So far as our biographical knowledge extends, this latter possibility does not seem to have occurred to Paracelsus either. In Colonna’s Hypnerotomachia Poliphili the Lady Polia attains a high degree of reality (far more so than Dante’s ethereal Beatrice but still not as much as Helen in Faust II), yet even she dissolves into a lovely dream as the sun rises on the first day of May:
[215] 这段文本确实需要注释！斯卡约拉作为原人的四个部分、肢体或流溢，4 是他主动干预现象世界的器官，或借此与之相连的器官——正如不可见的第五精华（quinta essentia）或以太在这个世界中显现为四元素，或反过来由四元素组成。由于斯卡约拉如我们所见也是心理功能，它们必须被理解为太一——不可见的原人——的显现或流出。作为意识的功能，尤其是作为 imaginatio、speculatio、phantasia 和 fides，它们"介入"并激发美露辛——水妖——使之化为人形。多恩将此视为"出现在心智中的幻象"，而非对真实女人的投射。就我们的传记知识所及，后一种可能性似乎也没有出现在帕拉塞尔苏斯身上。在科洛纳的《波利菲洛的梦中爱的争斗》中，波利亚女郎达到了很高的实在程度（远甚于但丁缥缈的贝雅特丽齐，但仍不如《浮士德》第二部中的海伦），然而即使她也在五月一日的太阳升起时消融为一个美丽的梦：

… tears shone in her eyes like clear crystals, like round pearls, like the dew which Aurora strews on the clouds of dawn. Sighing like a heavenly image, like incense of musk and amber rising to give delight to the spirits of heaven, she dissolved into thin air, leaving nought behind her but a breath of heavenly fragrance. So, with my happy dream, she vanished from my sight, saying as she went: Poliphilo, most dear beloved, farewell!5
……泪珠在她眼中闪烁，如清澈的水晶，如圆润的珍珠，如黎明女神撒在朝霞云端的露珠。她如天上的形象般叹息，如麝香和琥珀的熏香升起以愉悦天上之灵，她消融于稀薄的空气中，身后只留下一缕天国的芬芳。于是，连同我幸福的梦，她从我的视线中消失，离去时说：波利菲洛，最亲爱的人，永别了！5

[216] Polia dissolves just before the long-desired union with her lover. Helen, on the other hand, vanishes only with the dissolution of her son Euphorion. Though Paracelsus gives clear indications of the nuptial mood with his “exaltation” in May and his allusion to the stinging nettle and the little flame, he disregards entirely the projection on a real person or a concretely visualized, personified image, but chooses instead the legendary figure of Melusina. Now this figure is certainly not an allegorical chimera or a mere metaphor: she has her particular psychic reality in the sense that she is a glamorous apparition who, by her very nature, is on one side a psychic vision but also, on account of the psyche’s capacity for imaginative realization (which Paracelsus calls Ares), is a distinct objective entity, like a dream which temporarily becomes reality. The figure of Melusina is eminently suited to this purpose. The anima belongs to those borderline phenomena which chiefly occur in special psychic situations. They are characterized by the more or less sudden collapse of a form or style of life which till then seemed the indispensable foundation of the individual’s whole career. When such a catastrophe occurs, not only are all bridges back into the past broken, but there seems to be no way forward into the future. One is confronted with a hopeless and impenetrable darkness, an abysmal void that is now suddenly filled with an alluring vision, the palpably real presence of a strange yet helpful being, in the same way that, when one lives for a long time in great solitude, the silence or the darkness becomes visibly, audibly, and tangibly alive, and the unknown in oneself steps up in an unknown guise.
[216] 波利亚在与情人长久渴望的结合即将实现之前消融了。而海伦则是在她的儿子欧福里翁消逝时才消失的。尽管帕拉塞尔苏斯以其"五月提升"和对刺荨麻与小火焰的暗示清楚地表明了婚礼的情绪，但他完全忽视了对一个真实的人或具体可视的拟人化形象的投射，而是选择了美露辛的传说形象。这一形象当然不是寓言式的怪物或单纯的隐喻：它有其特定的心理实在性——它是一个迷人的幻象，就其本性而言，一方面是心理愿景，但另一方面由于心理的想象实现能力（帕拉塞尔苏斯称之为阿瑞斯），它也是一个明确的客观实体——如同一个暂时变为现实的梦。美露辛的形象非常适合这一目的。阿尼玛属于那些主要在特殊心理情境中出现的边界现象。它们的特征是某种生活形式或风格突然崩溃——在此之前那似乎是个体整个事业不可或缺的基础。当这样的灾难发生时，不仅所有通向过去的桥梁都被断绝，而且似乎也没有通向未来的道路。人面对着一种绝望的、不可穿透的黑暗，一个深渊般的虚空——现在突然被一个诱人的幻象所填满——一个陌生却有帮助的存在之真切可感的临在——如同一个人长期独居时，寂静或黑暗变得可见、可闻、可触地活生生起来，自身中的未知者以未知的面貌走出来。

[217] This peculiarity of the anima is found also in the Melusina legend: Emmerich, Count of Poitiers, had adopted Raymond, the son of a poor kinsman. The relation between adoptive father and son was harmonious. But once, on the hunt, when pursuing a wild boar, they got separated from the rest and went astray in the forest. Night fell and they lit a fire to warm themselves. Suddenly the Count was attacked by the boar, and Raymond struck at it with his sword. But by an unlucky accident the blade rebounded and dealt the Count a mortal blow. Raymond was inconsolable, and in despair mounted his horse to flee he knew not where. After a time he came to a meadow with a bubbling spring. There he found three beautiful women. One of them was Melusina, who by her clever counsel saved him from dishonour and a homeless fate.
[217] 阿尼玛的这一特性也见于美露辛传说中：普瓦捷伯爵埃默里收养了贫穷亲戚的儿子雷蒙。养父与养子之间的关系是和谐的。但有一次狩猎时，追猎一头野猪，他们与众人走散，在森林中迷路了。夜幕降临，他们生火取暖。突然伯爵遭到野猪攻击，雷蒙挥剑砍去。但不幸剑刃弹回，给了伯爵致命一击。雷蒙悲痛欲绝，绝望地骑上马逃往不知何处。过了一阵他来到一片草地，有一汪冒泡的泉水。在那里他找到了三位美丽的女子。其中一位便是美露辛，她以聪明的建议拯救了他免于耻辱和流离失所的命运。

[218] According to the legend, Raymond found himself in the catastrophic situation we have described, when his whole way of life had collapsed and he faced ruin. That is the moment when the harbinger of fate, the anima, an archetype of the collective unconscious, appears. In the legend Melusina sometimes has the tail of a fish and sometimes that of a snake; she is half human, half animal. Occasionally she appears only in snake form. The legend apparently has Celtic roots,6 but the motif is found practically everywhere. It was not only extraordinarily popular in Europe during the Middle Ages, but occurs also in India, in the legend of Urvashi and Pururavas, which is mentioned in the Shatapatha-Brāhmana.7 It also occurs among the North American Indians.8 The motif of half-man, half-fish is universally disseminated. Special mention should be made of Conrad Vecerius,9 according to whom Melusina, or Melyssina, comes from an island in the sea where nine sirens dwell, who can change into any shape they want. This is of particular interest as Paracelsus mentions Melusina along with “Syrena.”10 The tradition probably goes back to Pomponius Mela,11 who calls the island “Sena” and the beings who dwell there “Senae.” They cause storms, can change their shape, cure incurable diseases, and know the future.12 Since the mercurial serpent of the alchemists is not infrequently called virgo and, even before Paracelsus, was represented in the form of a Melusina, the latter’s capacity to change her shape and to cure diseases is of importance in that these peculiarities were also predicated of Mercurius, and with special emphasis. On the other hand, Mercurius was also depicted as the grey-bearded Mercurius senex or Hermes Trismegistus, from which it is evident that two empirically very common archetypes, namely the anima and the Wise Old Man,13 flow together in the symbolic phenomenology of Mercurius. Both are daemons of revelation and, in the form of Mercurius, represent the panacea. Again and again Mercurius is called versatilis, versipellis, mutabilis, servus or cervus fugitivus, Proteus, etc.
[218] 根据传说，雷蒙发现自己处于我们所描述的灾难性情境中——他的整个生活方式已经崩溃，面临毁灭。这就是命运的先驱——阿尼玛，集体无意识的一个原型——出现的时刻。在传说中，美露辛有时有鱼尾，有时有蛇尾；她半人半兽。偶尔她仅以蛇形出现。这一传说显然有凯尔特根源，6 但这一母题几乎到处都有。它不仅在中世纪欧洲极为流行，也出现在印度——广延者与普鲁拉瓦斯的传说中，该传说见于《百道梵书》。7 它也见于北美印第安人。8 半人半鱼的母题普遍传播。特别应当提及康拉德·维切里乌斯，9 据他说美露辛或梅丽西娜来自海上的一座岛屿，那里住着九位海妖塞壬，她们可以随心所欲地变成任何形状。这一点特别有趣，因为帕拉塞尔苏斯将美露辛与"塞壬"（Syrena）并列提及。10 这一传统可能追溯到蓬波尼乌斯·梅拉，11 他称该岛为"塞纳"（Sena），称居住在那里的生物为"塞纳"（Senae）。她们引起风暴，能变形，治愈不治之症，知晓未来。12 由于炼金术士的水银蛇不乏被称为 virgo（童贞女），甚至在帕拉塞尔苏斯之前就以美露辛的形式被表现，后者的变形和治病能力就很重要——因为这些特性也被归于墨丘利乌斯，而且被特别强调。另一方面，墨丘利乌斯也被描绘为灰须的墨丘利乌斯老者（Mercurius senex）或赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯托斯，由此可见两个在经验上极为常见的原型——即阿尼玛和智慧老人13——在墨丘利乌斯的象征现象学中汇流。二者都是启示的精灵，在墨丘利乌斯的形式中代表万灵药。墨丘利乌斯一再被称为 versatilis（多变的）、versipellis（变皮的）、mutabilis（易变的）、servus 或 cervus fugitivus（逃亡的奴仆或鹿）、普罗透斯等。

[219] The alchemists, and Paracelsus too, were no doubt confronted often enough with the dark abyss of not-knowing, and, unable to go forward, were on their own admission dependent on revelation or illumination or a helpful dream. For this reason they needed a “ministering spirit,” a familiar or πάρεδρος, to whose invocation the Greek Magic Papyri bear witness. The snake form of the god of revelation, and of spirits in general, is a universal type.
[219] 炼金术士，以及帕拉塞尔苏斯，无疑经常面对不知的黑暗深渊，无法前行，据他们自己承认依赖启示或照明或有帮助的梦。正因如此他们需要一个"服侍之灵"，一个精灵或 πάρεδρος（护持灵）——希腊魔法纸草见证了对此的祈请。启示之神及一般精灵的蛇形是一个普遍的类型。

[220] Paracelsus seems to have known nothing of any psychological premises. He attributes the appearance and transformation of Melusina to the effect of the “intervening” Scaiolae, the driving spiritual forces emanating from the homo maximus. The opus was subordinated to them, for its aim was to raise man to the sphere of the Anthropos. There is no doubt that the goal of the philosophical alchemist was higher self-development, or the production of what Paracelsus calls the homo maior, or what I would call individuation. This goal confronts the alchemist at the start with the loneliness which all of them feared, when one has “only” oneself for company. The alchemist, on principle, worked alone. He formed no school. This rigorous solitude, together with his preoccupation with the endless obscurities of the work, was sufficient to activate the unconscious and, through the power of imagination, to bring into being things that apparently were not there before. Under these circumstances “enigmatical speculations” arise in which the unconscious is visually experienced as a “vision appearing in the mind.” Melusina emerges from the watery realm and assumes human form—sometimes quite concretely, as in Faust I, where Faust’s hopelessness leads him straight into the arms of Gretchen, in which form Melusina would doubtless remain were it not for the catastrophe which drives Faust still deeper into magic: Melusina changes into Helen. But she does not remain even there, for all attempts at concretization are shattered like the retort of the homunculus against the throne of Galatea. Another power takes over, “that difficult Adech,” who “at the end changes himself.” The greater man “hinders our purpose,” for Faust has to change himself at death into a boy, the puer aeternus, to whom the true world will be shown only after all desirousness has fallen away from him. “Miserable mortals, to whom Nature has denied her first and best treasure, the lumen naturae!”
[220] 帕拉塞尔苏斯似乎对任何心理学前提一无所知。他将美露辛的出现和转化归因于"介入的"斯卡约拉的效果——从至大之人流出的驱动性灵性力量。炼金术操作从属于它们，因为其目标是将人提升到原人的领域。毫无疑问，哲学炼金术士的目标是更高的自我发展，或生产帕拉塞尔苏斯所称的更大之人（homo maior），或我所说的个体化。这一目标在开始时就使炼金术士面对孤独——所有人都害怕的孤独——当一个人"只有"自己为伴时。炼金术士原则上独自工作。他不形成学派。这种严苛的孤独，加上他对工作无尽晦涩的专注，足以激活无意识，并通过想象之力使原本不在那里的事物出现。在这种情况下，"谜一般的思辨"产生——在其中无意识作为"出现在心智中的幻象"被视觉地体验到。美露辛从水之领域中浮现，假定人形——有时相当具体，如《浮士德》第一部中，浮士德的绝望直接将他送入格蕾琴的怀抱——若非灾难将浮士德更深层地推入魔法，美露辛无疑会以此形式留存：美露辛变为海伦。但她即使在那里也没有停留，因为一切具体化的尝试都如人造人的蒸馏瓶在伽拉忒亚的宝座前粉碎一样被击碎。另一种力量接管了——"那困难的阿德赫"——"在最终他改变了自身"。更大之人"阻碍了我们的意图"，因为浮士德在死亡时必须变为一个男孩——永恒少年（puer aeternus）——只有当一切欲望从他身上脱落之后，真正的世界才会向他展示。"可悲的必死之人，自然拒绝给予他们她最初和最好的宝藏——自然之光！"

[221] It is Adech, the inner man, who with his Scaiolae guides the purpose of the adept and causes him to behold fantasy images from which he will draw false conclusions, devising out of them situations of whose provisional and fragile nature he is unaware. Nor is he aware that by knocking on the door of the unknown he is obeying the law of the inner, future man, and that he is disobedient to this law whenever he seeks to secure a permanent advantage or possession from his work. Not his ego, that fragment of a personality, is meant; it is rather that a wholeness, of which he is a part, wants to be transformed from a latent state of unconsciousness into an approximate consciousness of itself.
[221] 正是阿德赫——内在之人——以其斯卡约拉引导修炼者的意图，使他观看到幻象图像，从中他得出错误的结论，从中设计出他未意识到其临时性和脆弱性的情境。他也没有意识到，通过敲击未知之门，他正在服从内在的、未来之人的法则，而每当他试图从工作中获取永久的利益或占有时，他就违背了这一法则。不是他的自我——那个人格的碎片——而是他作为其一部分的整体性，想要从无意识的潜在状态转化为对自身的近似意识。

[222] The “acts of Melusina” are deceptive phantasms compounded of supreme sense and the most pernicious nonsense, a veritable veil of Maya which lures and leads every mortal astray. From these phantasms the wise man will extract the “supermonic” elements, that is, the higher inspirations; he extracts everything meaningful and valuable as in a process of distillation,14 and catches the precious drops of the liquor Sophiae in the ready beaker of his soul, where they “open a window” for his understanding. Paracelsus is here alluding to a discriminative process of critical judgment which separates the chaff from the wheat—an indispensable part of any rapprochement with the unconscious. It requires no art to become stupid; the whole art lies in extracting wisdom from stupidity. Stupidity is the mother of the wise, but cleverness never. The “fixation” refers alchemically to the lapis but psychologically to the consolidation of feeling. The distillate must be fixed and held fast, must become a firm conviction and a permanent content.
[222] "美露辛的作为"是欺骗性的幻影——由最高的理智和最有害的胡说混合而成——一层真正的摩耶之幕，诱惑和引致每个凡人误入歧途。智者将从这些幻影中提取"超凡的"元素，即更高的灵感；他在蒸馏过程中14 提取一切有意义的和有价值的东西，将智慧之酒（liquor Sophiae）的珍贵滴液收入他灵魂准备好的烧杯中——在那里它们为他的理智"打开一扇窗"。帕拉塞尔苏斯在此暗示一种批判性判断的辨别过程——将糠秕与麦子分开——这是任何与无意识接近所不可或缺的部分。变得愚蠢不需要艺术；全部的艺术在于从愚蠢中提取智慧。愚蠢是智者之母，但聪明从不如此。"固定"在炼金术上指的是哲学家之石，但在心理学上指的是情感的巩固。馏出物必须被固定和牢牢把握，必须成为一种坚定的信念和持久的内容。





B. THE HIEROSGAMOS OF THE EVERLASTING MAN
B. 永恒之人的神圣婚礼


[223] Melusina, the deceptive Shakti, must return to the watery realm if the work is to reach its goal. She should no longer dance before the adept with alluring gestures, but must become what she was from the beginning: a part of his wholeness.15 As such she must be “conceived in the mind.” This leads to a union of conscious and unconscious that was always present unconsciously but was always denied by the one-sidedness of the conscious attitude. From this union arises that wholeness which the introspective philosophy of all times and climes has characterized with an inexhaustible variety of symbols, names, and concepts. The “mille nomina” disguise the fact that this coniunctio is not concerned with anything tangible or discursively apprehensible; it is an experience that simply cannot be reproduced in words, but whose very nature carries with it an unassailable feeling of eternity or timelessness.
[223] 美露辛——那欺骗性的沙克蒂——如果工作要达到目标，就必须回到水之领域。她不应再以诱人的姿态在修炼者面前跳舞，而必须成为她从一开始就是的东西：他整体性的一部分。15 作为这样的部分，她必须被"构想于心智中"。这导致了一种意识与无意识的结合——这种结合一直无意识地存在着，但一直被意识态度的片面性所否认。从这一结合中产生出整体性——一切时代和地域的内省哲学以无穷无尽的象征、名称和概念来表征它。"千名"掩盖了这样一个事实：这种结合不涉及任何有形的或可通过推理把握的东西；它是一种根本无法用语言再现的经验，但其本性本身带有一种不可动摇的永恒感或无时间感。

[224] I will not repeat here what I have said elsewhere on this subject. It makes no difference anyway what one says about it. Paracelsus does, however, give one more hint which I cannot pass over in silence: this concerns the “characters of Venus.”16
[224] 我不在这里重复我在别处对这一主题所说的话。无论如何，人们对它说什么都无关紧要。但帕拉塞尔苏斯确实给出了一个我不能略过的暗示：这涉及"维纳斯之符"。16

[225] Melusina, being a water-nixie, is closely connected with Morgana, the “sea-born,” whose classical counterpart is Aphrodite, the “foam-born.” Union with the feminine personification of the unconscious is, as we have seen, a well-nigh eschatological experience, a reflection of which is to be found in the Apocalyptic Marriage of the Lamb, the Christian form of the hierosgamos. The passage runs (Revelation 19 : 6–10):
[225] 美露辛作为水妖，与摩根娜——"海生者"——密切相关，其古典对应者是阿芙洛狄忒——"泡沫生者"。与无意识之女性人格化的结合，如我们所见，是一种近乎末世论的经验，其反映可见于羔羊婚宴——神圣婚礼的基督教形式。经文如下（《启示录》19:6–10）：

And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia; for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.
我听见好像群众的声音，众水的声音，大雷的声音，说：哈利路亚！因为主我们的神，全能者作王了。

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.
我们要欢喜快乐，将荣耀归给他。因为羔羊婚娶的时候到了，新妇也自己预备好了。

And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.
就蒙恩得穿光明洁白的细麻衣。这细麻衣就是圣徒所行的义。

And he saith unto me: Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.
天使吩咐我说：你要写上，凡被请赴羔羊之婚筵的有福了。又对我说：这是神真实的话。

And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren . . .
我就俯伏在他脚前要拜他。他说：千万不可！我和你并你的弟兄……同是作仆人的。

[226] The “he” of the text is the angel that speaks to John; in the language of Paracelsus, he is the homo maior, Adech. I need hardly point out that Venus is closely related to the love-goddess Astarte, whose sacred marriage-festivals were known to everyone. The experience of union underlying these festivals is, psychologically, the embrace and coming together again of two souls in the exaltation of spring, in the “true May”; it is the successful reuniting of an apparently hopelessly divided duality in the wholeness of a single being. This unity embraces the multiplicity of all beings. Hence Paracelsus says: “If you know yourselves one with others.” Adech is not my self, he is also that of my brothers: “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.” That is the specific definition of this experience of the coniunctio: the self which includes me includes many others also, for the unconscious that is “conceived in our mind” does not belong to me and is not peculiar to me, but is everywhere. It is the quintessence of the individual and at the same time the collective.
[226] 文本中的"他"是对约翰说话的天使；用帕拉塞尔苏斯的语言来说，他是更大之人——阿德赫。我无需指出维纳斯与爱神阿斯塔蒂密切相关——后者神圣的婚庆节庆是众所周知的。这些节庆所基于的结合经验，在心理学上是两个灵魂在春季的高扬中——在"真正的五月"中——的拥抱和重新聚首；它是一个显然无望地分裂的二元在单一存在的整体性中的成功重新统一。这一统一涵盖了众生的多样性。因此帕拉塞尔苏斯说："如果你们与他人一起认识自己。"阿德赫不是我的自性，他也是我兄弟的自性："我和你并你的弟兄同是作仆人的。"这就是这种结合经验的特定定义：包含我的自性也包含许多他人，因为"被构想于我们心智中"的无意识不属于我、不为我所特有，而是无处不在。它是个体的精华，同时也是集体的。

[227] The participants in the marriage of the Lamb enter into eternal blessedness; they are “virgins, which were not defiled with women” and are “redeemed from among men” (Rev. 14 : 4). In Paracelsus the goal of redemption is “the year Aniadin,” or time of perfection, when the One Man reigns for ever.
[227] 参与羔羊婚宴的人进入永恒的福乐；他们是"未曾沾染妇女的童贞男"，是"从人间买赎回来的"（《启示录》14:4）。在帕拉塞尔苏斯那里，救赎的目标是"阿尼亚丁之年"——即完美之时，届时太一人永远为王。





C. SPIRIT AND NATURE
C. 精神与自然


[228] Why did Paracelsus not avail himself of the Christian imagery, when it expresses the same thought so very clearly? Why does Venus appear in the place of Melusina, and why is it not the marriage of the Lamb, but a hierosgamos of Venus and Mars, as the text itself hints? The reason is probably the same as that which compelled Francesco Colonna to make Poliphilo seek his beloved Polia not with the Mother of God but with Venus. For the same reason the boy in Christian Rosencreutz’s Chymical Wedding17 led the hero down to an underground chamber, on the door of which was a secret inscription graven in copper characters. Copper (cuprum) is correlated with the Cyprian (Aphrodite, Venus). In the chamber they found a three-cornered tomb containing a copper cauldron, and in it was an angel holding a tree that dripped continually into the cauldron. The tomb was supported by three animals: an eagle, an ox, and a lion.18 The boy explained that in this tomb Venus lay buried, who had destroyed many an upright man. Continuing their descent, they came to the bedchamber of Venus and found the goddess asleep on a couch. Indiscreetly, the boy twitched the coverlet away and revealed her in all her naked beauty.19
[228] 帕拉塞尔苏斯为何不利用基督教意象——当后者如此清楚地表达了同样的思想？为何维纳斯出现在美露辛的位置上？为何不是羔羊的婚宴，而是维纳斯与马尔斯的神圣婚礼——如文本本身所暗示的？原因可能与迫使弗朗切斯科·科洛纳让波利菲洛不是在圣母的引导下而是在维纳斯的引导下去寻找他心爱的波利亚的原因相同。出于同样的原因，克里斯蒂安·罗森克鲁茨的《化学婚礼》中的男孩17 引领英雄下到一个地下室，门上用铜字刻着秘密铭文。铜（cuprum）与塞浦路斯的（阿芙洛狄忒、维纳斯）相关联。在地下室中他们发现了一座三角形的墓，里面有一个铜釜，釜中有一个天使，手持一棵不断向釜中滴水的树。墓由三只动物支撑：鹰、牛和狮。18 男孩解释说，这座墓中埋葬着维纳斯——她摧毁了许多正直的人。继续下行，他们来到维纳斯的卧室，发现女神正在榻上熟睡。男孩不慎地掀开了被单，展露了她全部的赤裸之美。19

[229] The ancient world contained a large slice of nature and a number of questionable things which Christianity was bound to overlook if the security of a spiritual standpoint was not to be hopelessly compromised. No penal code and no moral code, not even the sublimest casuistry, will ever be able to codify and pronounce just judgment upon the confusions, the conflicts of duty, and the invisible tragedies of the natural man in collision with the exigencies of culture. “Spirit” is one aspect, “Nature” another. “You may pitch Nature out with a fork, yet she’ll always come back again,” says the poet.20 Nature must not win the game, but she cannot lose. And whenever the conscious mind clings to hard and fast concepts and gets caught in its own rules and regulations—as is unavoidable and of the essence of civilized consciousness—nature pops up with her inescapable demands. Nature is not matter only, she is also spirit. Were that not so, the only source of spirit would be human reason. It is the great achievement of Paracelsus to have elevated the “light of nature” to a principle and to have emphasized it in a far more fundamental way than his predecessor Agrippa. The lumen naturae is the natural spirit, whose strange and significant workings we can observe in the manifestations of the unconscious now that psychological research has come to realize that the unconscious is not just a “subconscious” appendage or the dustbin of consciousness, but is a largely autonomous psychic system for compensating the biases and aberrations of the conscious attitude, for the most part functionally, though it sometimes corrects them by force. Consciousness can, as we know, be led astray by naturalness as easily as by spirituality, this being the logical consequence of its freedom of choice. The unconscious is not limited only to the instinctual and reflex processes of the cortical centres; it also extends beyond consciousness and, with its symbols, anticipates future conscious processes. It is therefore quite as much a “supra-consciousness.”
[229] 古代世界包含着自然的一大部分和一些可疑的事物——基督教不得不对此视而不见，如果不使精神立场的安全性无可奈何地受损的话。没有一部刑法典、没有一部道德法典，甚至最高明的决疑术，也永远无法将自然之人与文化需求碰撞时的混乱、义务冲突和看不见的悲剧编纂成法并做出公正判决。"精神"是一个方面，"自然"是另一方面。"你可以用叉子把自然赶出去，但她总会回来的，"诗人说。20 自然不应赢得这场游戏，但她不能输。每当意识心智执著于固定不变的概念、陷入自己的规则和条例时——正如文明意识不可避免的本质那样——自然就会以其不可逃避的要求突然出现。自然不仅是物质，她也是精神。如果不是如此，精神的唯一来源就将是人类的理性。帕拉塞尔苏斯的伟大成就在于将"自然之光"提升为一项原则，并以远比他的前辈阿格里帕更为根本的方式加以强调。自然之光是自然的精神——其奇特而重要的运作我们现在可以在无意识的显现中观察到——因为心理学研究已经认识到，无意识不仅仅是"潜意识的"附属物或意识的垃圾箱，而是一个很大程度上自主的心理系统，用于补偿意识态度的偏见和偏差——大部分情况下是功能性地补偿，尽管有时也以强力加以纠正。意识可以如我们所知的那样被自然性引入歧途，也容易被精神性引入歧途——这是其选择自由的逻辑后果。无意识不仅限于皮层中心的本能和反射过程；它也超越了意识，以其象征预示未来的意识过程。因此它同样是一种"超意识"。

[230] Convictions and moral values would have no meaning if they were not believed and did not possess exclusive validity. And yet they are man-made and time-conditioned assertions or explanations which we know very well are capable of all sorts of modifications, as has happened in the past and will happen again in the future. All that has happened during the last two thousand years shows that they are reliable signposts for certain stretches of the way, then comes a painful upheaval, which is felt as subversive and immoral, until a new conviction takes root. So far as the essential traits of human nature remain the same, certain moral values enjoy permanent validity. The most meticulous observance of the Ten Commandments, however, is no obstacle to the more refined forms of turpitude, and the far loftier principle of Christian love of one’s neighbour can lead to such tangled conflicts of duty that sometimes the Gordian knot can only be cut with a very unchristian sword.
[230] 信念和道德价值如果没有人信仰、不拥有排他性的有效性，就没有意义。然而它们是人造的、受时代制约的断言或解释——我们清楚地知道它们能够做出各种修改，正如过去已发生和将来会再次发生的那样。过去两千年所发生的一切表明，它们是某些路段上可靠的指路标，然后就会出现痛苦的剧变——被人们感受为颠覆性的和不道德的——直到一种新的信念扎根。就人性的本质特征保持不变而言，某些道德价值享有永久的有效性。然而，对十诫最一丝不苟的遵守并不能阻止更精致形式的堕落，而远为崇高的基督教爱邻原则可以导致如此纠结的义务冲突，以至于有时戈尔迪之结只能用一把非常不基督教的剑来斩断。





D. THE ECCLESIASTICAL SACRAMENT AND THE OPUS ALCHYMICUM
D. 教会圣事与炼金术操作


[231] Paracelsus, like many others, was unable to make use of the Christian symbolism because the Christian formula inevitably suggested the Christian solution and would thus have conduced to the very thing that had to be avoided. It was nature and her particular “light” that had to be acknowledged and lived with in the face of an attitude that assiduously overlooked them. This could only be done under the protective aegis of the arcanum. But one should not imagine Paracelsus or any other alchemist settling down to invent an arcane terminology that would make the new doctrine a kind of private code. Such an undertaking would presuppose the existence of definite views and clearly defined concepts. But there is no question of that: none of the alchemists ever had any clear idea of what his philosophy was really about. The best proof of this is the fact that everyone with any originality at all coined his own terminology, with the result that no one fully understood anybody else. For one alchemist, Lully was an obscurantist and a charlatan and Geber the great authority; while for another, Geber was a Sphinx and Lully the source of all enlightenment. So with Paracelsus: we have no reason to suppose that behind his neologisms there was a clear, consciously disguised concept. It is on the contrary probable that he was trying to grasp the ungraspable with his countless esotericisms, and snatched at any symbolic hint that the unconscious offered. The new world of scientific knowledge was still in a nascent dream-state, a mist heavy with the future, in which shadowy figures groped about for the right words. Paracelsus was not reaching back into the past; rather, for lack of anything suitable in the present, he was using the old remnants to give new form to a renewed archetypal experience. Had the alchemists felt any serious need to revive the past, their erudition would have enabled them to draw on the inexhaustible storehouse of the heresiologists. But except for the “Aquarium sapientum,”21 which likewise treats of heresies, I have found only one alchemist (of the sixteenth century) who shudderingly admits to having read the Panarium of Epiphanius. Nor are any secret traces of Gnostic usages to be found, despite the fact that the texts swarm with unconscious parallels.
[231] 帕拉塞尔苏斯如同许多其他人一样，无法利用基督教象征体系，因为基督教的程式不可避免地暗示基督教的解决方案，从而将导致恰恰需要避免的结果。必须被承认和与之共处的是自然及其特殊的"光"——面对一种勤勉地忽视它们的态度。这只能在秘术的保护伞下进行。但不应想象帕拉塞尔苏斯或任何其他炼金术士坐下来发明一套秘术语语，以使新教义成为一种私人密码。这样的企图需要以明确的观点和清晰界定的概念为前提。但根本谈不上这一点：没有一位炼金术士曾经清楚地知道自己的哲学到底是什么。最好的证明就是：每个有独创性的人都创造了自己的术语，结果是谁也不能完全理解别人。对一个炼金术士来说，拉蒙·略勒是一个蒙昧主义者和骗子，而贾比尔是伟大的权威；对另一个来说，贾比尔是一个斯芬克斯，而略勒是一切启蒙的源泉。帕拉塞尔苏斯也是如此：我们没有理由假定在他的新造词背后有清晰的、有意识地伪装的概念。相反，他很可能是在用无数秘语试图把握不可把握之物，抓住无意识提供的任何象征性暗示。科学知识的新世界仍处于初生的梦幻状态，一场弥漫着未来的迷雾，在其中模糊的身影摸索着寻找恰当的词语。帕拉塞尔苏斯不是在追溯过去；相反，由于当下没有合适的东西，他利用旧日的残余为一种重新体验的原型经验赋予新形式。如果炼金术士真的感到有严肃的复兴过去的需求，他们的博学会使他们能够从异端学家那取之不尽的宝库中汲取。但除了《智慧水族馆》21——它同样论述异端——之外，我只发现一位炼金术士（十六世纪的）战栗地承认读过埃皮法尼乌斯的《药箱》。也没有任何诺斯替教派用法的秘密痕迹被发现，尽管文献中充斥着无意识的平行。

[232] To return to our text: it is clear that it describes a procedure for attaining nothing less than immortality (“that we may arrive immortal at the year Aniadin”). There is, however, only one way to this goal, and that is through the sacraments of the Church. These are here replaced by the “sacrament” of the opus alchymicum, less by word than by deed, and without the least sign of any conflict with the orthodox Christian standpoint.
[232] 回到我们的文本：很明显，它描述的是一种获得不外乎永生的程序（"以便我们不朽地到达阿尼亚丁之年"）。然而，通往这一目标只有一条路，那就是通过教会的圣事。这些在这里被炼金术操作的"圣事"所取代——与其说是以言辞不如说是以行动，而且毫无与正统基督教立场冲突的迹象。

[233] Which way did Paracelsus hold to be the true one? Or were both of them true for him? Presumably the latter, and the rest he “leaves to the theoreticians to discuss.”
[233] 帕拉塞尔苏斯认为哪条路是正确的？还是两条路对他都是正确的？大概是后者，其余的他"留给理论家去讨论"。

[234] What is meant by the “characters of Venus” remains obscure. The “sapphire”22 which Paracelsus prized so much, the cheyri, ladanum, muscus, and ambra belong, according to Agrippa,23 to Venus. The goddess undoubtedly appears in our text on a higher level, in keeping with her classical cognomens: docta, sublimis, magistra rerum humanarum divinarumque, etc24 One of her characters is certainly love in the widest sense, so Dorn is not wrong when he interprets them as the “shield and buckler of love.” Shield and buckler are martial attributes, but there is also a Venus armata.25 Mythologically, the personified Amor is a son of Venus and Mars, whose cohabitation in alchemy is a typical coniunctio.26 Dorn, despite being a Paracelsist, had a decidedly polemical attitude towards certain fundamental tenets of alchemy,27 so that a Christian love of one’s neighbour, well armed against evil, suited him very well. But so far as Paracelsus is concerned this interpretation is doubtful. The word Venus points in quite another direction, and since the Christian gifts of grace were included in his Catholic faith he had in any case no need of a christianized Amor. On the contrary, a Venus Magistra or Aphrodite Urania, or even a Sophia, would have seemed to him more appropriate to the mystery of the lumen naturae. The words “minime tamen usurpatis” might also be a hint at discretion.28 Hence the Venus episode in the Chymical Wedding may have more bearing on the interpretation of this cryptic passage than Dorn’s well-meant circumlocution.
[234] "维纳斯之符"意味着什么仍然模糊。帕拉塞尔苏斯极为珍视的"蓝宝石"22，以及切伊里、劳丹姆、麝香和琥珀，据阿格里帕所说23 属于维纳斯。女神无疑在我们的文本中以更高的层次出现，与她的古典别号相称：docta（博学的）、sublimis（崇高的）、magistra rerum humanarum divinarumque（人事与神事之导师）等。24 她的符之一当然是广义的爱，所以多恩将它们解释为"爱之盾与胄"并非错误。盾和胄是战神的属性，但也有武装维纳斯（Venus armata）。25 在神话中，拟人化的爱神（Amor）是维纳斯与马尔斯之子，他们在炼金术中的同居是典型的结合（coniunctio）。26 多恩虽然是帕拉塞尔苏斯主义者，但对炼金术的某些基本信条持明确的论战态度，27 所以一种装备精良以抵御邪恶的基督教爱邻原则非常适合他。但就帕拉塞尔苏斯而言，这一解释是可疑的。维纳斯一词指向完全不同的方向，而且由于基督教恩赐已包含在他的天主教信仰中，他无论如何不需要一个基督教化的爱神。相反，维纳斯导师（Venus Magistra）或天王阿芙洛狄忒（Aphrodite Urania），甚至索菲亚（Sophia），在他看来更适合自然之光的奥秘。"minime tamen usurpatis"（却几乎没有使用）一语也可能是对谨慎的暗示。28 因此，《化学婚礼》中的维纳斯插曲可能比多恩善意的迂回说法更有助于解读这段晦涩的文字。

[235] The concluding reference to a “life without end” under the dominion of Aniadus is very reminiscent of Rev. 20 : 4: “… and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” The year Aniadin would thus correspond to the thousand-year reign in the Apocalypse.
[235] 结语中提到的在阿尼亚杜斯主宰下"无尽的生命"非常令人想起《启示录》20:4："……他们复活了，与基督一同作王一千年。"因此阿尼亚丁之年对应于《启示录》中的千年统治。

[236] In conclusion I would remark that the survey of the secret doctrine which I have attempted to sketch here makes it seem likely that besides the physician and Christian in Paracelsus there was also an alchemical philosopher at work who, pushing every analogy to the very limit, strove to penetrate the divine mysteries. The parallel with the mysteries of the Christian faith, which we can only feel as a most dangerous conflict, was no Gnostic heresy for him, despite the most disconcerting resemblances; for him as for every other alchemist, man had been entrusted with the task of bringing to perfection the divine will implanted in nature, and this was a truly sacramental work. To the question “Are you, as it would seem, an Hermetic?” he could have replied with Lazarello: “I am a Christian, O King, and it is no disgrace to be that and an Hermetic at the same time.”29
[236] 最后我要指出，我在这里尝试勾勒的秘术教义概览使以下说法显得可能：除了帕拉塞尔苏斯身上的医师和基督徒之外，还有一位炼金术哲学家在发挥作用，他将每一个类比推到极限，努力穿透神圣的奥秘。与基督教信仰奥秘的平行关系——我们只能感受为一种极其危险的冲突——对他来说不是诺斯替异端，尽管存在最令人困惑的相似之处；因为对他如同对所有其他炼金术士一样，人被委以使植入自然中的神圣意志达致完善的任务，而这是一项真正的圣事工作。对于"你似乎是一位赫尔墨斯主义者？"这一问题，他本可以像拉扎雷洛那样回答："我是基督徒，国王啊，作为基督徒和赫尔墨斯主义者并不矛盾。"29





5. EPILOGUE
5. 结语


[237] I had long been aware that alchemy is not only the mother of chemistry, but is also the forerunner of our modern psychology of the unconscious. Thus Paracelsus appears as a pioneer not only of chemical medicine but of empirical psychology and psychotherapy.
[237] 我早已意识到炼金术不仅是化学之母，也是我们现代无意识心理学的前驱。因此帕拉塞尔苏斯不仅是化学医学的先驱，也是经验心理学和心理治疗的先驱。

[238] It may seem that I have said too little about Paracelsus the self-sacrificing physician and Christian, and too much about his dark shadow, that other Paracelsus, whose soul was intermingled with a strange spiritual current which, issuing from immemorial sources, flowed beyond him into a distant future. But—ex tenebris lux—it was precisely because he was so fascinated by magic that he was able to open the door to the realities of nature for the benefit of succeeding centuries. The Christian and the primitive pagan lived together in him in a strange and marvellous way to form a conflicting whole, as in other great Renaissance figures. Although he had to endure the conflict, he was spared that agonizing split between knowledge and faith that has riven the later epochs. As a man he had one father, but as a spirit he had two mothers. His spirit was heroic, because creative, and as such was doomed to Promethean guilt. The secular conflict that broke out at the turn of the sixteenth century, and whose living image stands before our eyes in the figure of Paracelsus, is a prerequisite for higher consciousness; for analysis is always followed by synthesis, and what was divided on a lower level will reappear, united, on a higher one.
[238] 也许有人会说我对于作为自我牺牲之医师和基督徒的帕拉塞尔苏斯说得太少，而对于他黑暗的影子——那另一个帕拉塞尔苏斯——说得太多，后者的灵魂与一股奇异的精神潮流交织在一起，这股潮流源自远古，流经他而奔向遥远的未来。但是——ex tenebris lux（从黑暗中出光明）——正因为他如此着迷于魔法，他才能够为后世打开自然实在的大门。基督徒与原始异教徒以一种奇异而奇妙的方式在他身上共存，构成了一个冲突的整体，如同其他伟大的文艺复兴人物一样。虽然他不得不忍受这一冲突，但他被幸免于那撕裂了后来时代的知识与信仰之间痛苦的分裂。作为人他有一个父亲，但作为精神他有两个母亲。他的精神是英雄式的——因为它是创造性的——因此注定承受普罗米修斯式的罪愆。在十六世纪转折点爆发的世俗冲突——其活的形象在帕拉塞尔苏斯身上站在我们眼前——是更高意识的必要前提；因为分析之后总是跟随着综合，在较低层次上被分裂的将在较高层次上以统一的形态重新出现。

1. THE SPIRIT IN THE BOTTLE
1. 瓶中之灵


[239] In my contribution1 to the symposium on Hermes I will try to show that this many-hued and wily god did not by any means die with the decline of the classical era, but on the contrary has gone on living in strange guises through the centuries, even into recent times, and has kept the mind of man busy with his deceptive arts and healing gifts. Children are still told Grimm’s fairytale of “The Spirit in the Bottle,” which is ever-living like all fairytales, and moreover contains the quintessence and deepest meaning of the Hermetic mystery as it has come down to us today:
[239] 在我为赫尔墨斯研讨会所做的贡献1 中，我将试图表明：这位色彩斑斓、狡黠多端的神绝非随古典时代的衰落而死，相反，他以奇特的伪装在数个世纪中——甚至直到近代——继续存活着，以他欺骗的技艺和治愈的恩赐使人忙个不停。孩子们至今仍被讲述格林童话《瓶中之灵》，它如同所有童话一样长生不死，而且包含了流传至今的赫尔墨斯奥秘的精华与最深层意义：

Once upon a time there was a poor woodcutter. He had an only son, whom he wished to send to a high school. However, since he could give him only a little money to take with him, it was used up long before the time for the examinations. So the son went home and helped his father with the work in the forest. Once, during the midday rest, he roamed the woods and came to an immense old oak. There he heard a voice calling from the ground, “Let me out, let me out!” He dug down among the roots of the tree and found a well-sealed glass bottle from which, clearly, the voice had come. He opened it and instantly a spirit rushed out and soon became half as high as the tree. The spirit cried in an awful voice: “I have had my punishment and I will be revenged! I am the great and mighty spirit Mercurius, and now you shall have your reward. Who so releases me, him I must strangle.” This made the boy uneasy and, quickly thinking up a trick, he said, “First, I must be sure that you are the same spirit that was shut up in that little bottle.” To prove this, the spirit crept back into the bottle. Then the boy made haste to seal it and the spirit was caught again. But now the spirit promised to reward him richly if the boy would let him out. So he let him out and received as a reward a small piece of rag. Quoth the spirit: “If you spread one end of this over a wound it will heal, and if you rub steel or iron with the other end it will turn into silver.” Thereupon the boy rubbed his damaged axe with the rag, and the axe turned to silver and he was able to sell it for four hundred thaler. Thus father and son were freed from all worries. The young man could return to his studies, and later, thanks to his rag, he became a famous doctor.2
从前有一个贫穷的樵夫。他有一个独生子，想送他去上高中。然而，由于他只能给他很少的钱带在身上，这笔钱在考试之前很久就用完了。于是儿子回家帮父亲在森林中干活。有一次，在午休时，他在林中漫步，来到一棵巨大的老橡树前。他听到一个声音从地下传来："放我出去，放我出去！"他在树根间挖掘，发现一个密封良好的玻璃瓶，声音显然是从那里发出的。他打开瓶盖，一个精灵立刻冲出来，很快就变得有树的一半高。精灵用可怕的声音喊道："我受了惩罚，我要报复！我是伟大而强大的精灵墨丘利乌斯，现在你将得到你的报酬。谁释放了我，我就必须勒死谁。"这使男孩不安起来，他迅速想出一个计策，说："首先，我必须确定你就是被关在那个小瓶子里的精灵。"为了证明这一点，精灵爬回瓶中。然后男孩赶快封住瓶口，精灵又被抓住了。但现在精灵承诺如果男孩放他出去就重重报答他。于是他放了他，作为奖赏得到了一小块破布。精灵说："如果你把这布的一端覆盖在伤口上，伤口就会愈合；如果你用另一端擦拭钢铁或铁器，它就会变成银子。"于是男孩用那块布擦拭他损坏的斧头，斧头变成了银子，他得以以四百塔勒的价钱卖出。父子俩从此摆脱了一切烦恼。年轻人可以回去继续学业，后来，多亏了那块布，他成了一位著名的医生。2

[240] Now, what insight can we gain from this fairytale? As you know, we can treat fairytales as fantasy products, like dreams, conceiving them to be spontaneous statements of the unconscious about itself.
[240] 那么，我们能从这篇童话中获得什么洞见？如你们所知，我们可以将童话视为幻想产物，如同梦一样，将它们理解为无意识关于自身的自发陈述。

[241] As at the beginning of many dreams something is said about the scene of the dream action, so the fairytale mentions the forest as the place of the magic happening. The forest, dark and impenetrable to the eye, like deep water and the sea, is the container of the unknown and the mysterious. It is an appropriate synonym for the unconscious. Among the many trees—the living elements that make up the forest—one tree is especially conspicuous for its great size. Trees, like fishes in the water, represent the living contents of the unconscious. Among these contents one of special significance is characterized as an “oak.” Trees have individuality. A tree, therefore, is often a symbol of personality.3 Ludwig II of Bavaria is said to have honoured certain particularly impressive trees in his park by having them saluted. The mighty old oak is proverbially the king of the forest. Hence it represents a central figure among the contents of the unconscious, possessing personality in the most marked degree. It is the prototype of the self, a symbol of the source and goal of the individuation process. The oak stands for the still unconscious core of the personality, the plant symbolism indicating a state of deep unconsciousness. From this it may be concluded that the hero of the fairytale is profoundly unconscious of himself. He is one of the “sleepers,” the “blind” or “blindfolded,” whom we encounter in the illustrations of certain alchemical treatises.4 They are the unawakened who are still unconscious of themselves, who have not yet integrated their future, more extensive personality, their “wholeness,” or, in the language of the mystics, the ones who are not yet “enlightened.” For our hero, therefore, the tree conceals a great secret.5
[241] 如同许多梦的开头会交代梦境的场景一样，童话提到森林作为魔法事件发生之地。森林，暗沉而目不可透，如同深水和大海，是未知者和神秘之事的容器。它是无意识的恰当同义词。在众多树木——构成森林的活的元素——之中，有一棵树因其巨大的体型格外引人注目。树木如同水中的鱼，代表无意识的活的内含物。在这些内含物中，一个特别重要的被特征为"橡树"。树木有个体性。因此，一棵树常常是人格的象征。3 据说巴伐利亚的路德维希二世曾以鸣枪致敬的方式尊崇他公园中某些特别令人印象深刻的树木。巨大的老橡树俗语说是森林之王。因此它代表无意识内含物中的中心人物，在最显著的意义上具有人格。它是自性的原型，是个体化过程之源与目标的象征。橡树代表人格中仍然无意识的核心——植物象征暗示一种深度无意识的状态。由此可以推断，童话中的英雄对自身深度无意识。他是"沉睡者"之一，"盲者"或"被蒙眼者"——我们在某些炼金术论著的插图中遇到他们。4 他们是尚未觉醒、对自身仍无意识的人，尚未整合其未来的、更广阔的人格——他们的"整体性"——或者用神秘主义者的语言来说，是尚未"开悟"的人。因此，对我们的英雄来说，树隐藏着一个巨大的秘密。5

[242] The secret is hidden not in the top but in the roots of the tree;6 and since it is, or has, a personality it also possesses the most striking marks of personality—voice, speech, and conscious purpose, and it demands to be set free by the hero. It is caught and imprisoned against its will, down there in the earth among the roots of the tree. The roots extend into the inorganic realm, into the mineral kingdom. In psychological terms, this would mean that the self has its roots in the body, indeed in the body’s chemical elements. Whatever this remarkable statement of the fairytale may mean in itself, it is in no way stranger than the miracle of the living plant rooted in the inanimate earth. The alchemists described their four elements as radices, corresponding to the Empedoclean rhizomata, and in them they saw the constituents of the most significant and central symbol of alchemy, the lapis philosophorum, which represents the goal of the individuation process.
[242] 秘密不是隐藏在树顶而是树根中；6 由于它是或具有人格，它也拥有人格最显著的特征——声音、语言和有意识的目的，并要求被英雄释放。它违背己意被捕获和囚禁在那里，在地下树根之间。树根延伸到无机领域，即矿物界。用心理学术语来说，这意味着自性根植于身体，确实根植于身体的化学元素中。无论童话中这一奇特陈述本身可能意味着什么，它并不比有生命的植物扎根于无生命的大地这一奇术更为奇异。炼金术士将他们的四元素描述为 radices（根），对应于恩培多克勒的 rhizomata（根），他们在其中看到了炼金术最重大、最核心的象征——哲学家之石——的构成要素，而哲学家之石代表个体化过程的目标。

[243] The secret hidden in the roots is a spirit sealed inside a bottle. Naturally it was not hidden away among the roots to start with, but was first confined in a bottle, which was then hidden. Presumably a magician, that is, an alchemist, caught and imprisoned it. As we shall see later, this spirit is something like the numen of the tree, its spiritus vegetativus, which is one definition of Mercurius. As the life principle of the tree, it is a sort of spiritual quintessence abstracted from it, and could also be described as the principium individuationis. The tree would then be the outward and visible sign of the realization of the self. The alchemists appear to have held a similar view. Thus the “Aurelia occulta” says: “The philosophers have sought most eagerly for the centre of the tree which stands in the midst of the earthly paradise.”7 According to the same source, Christ himself is this tree.8 The tree comparison occurs as early as Eulogius of Alexandria (c. A.D. 600), who says: “Behold in the Father the root, in the Son the branch, and in the Spirit the fruit: for the substance [οὐσία] in the three is one.”9 Mercurius, too, is trinus et unus.
[243] 隐藏在根中的秘密是一个被封在瓶中的精灵。自然，它一开始并非被藏在树根间，而是先被囚在瓶中，然后被藏起来。大概是一位魔法师，即炼金术士，捕获并囚禁了它。如我们后将看到的，这个精灵有点像树的努门（numen），它的 spiritus vegetativus（生长之灵）——这是墨丘利乌斯的一个定义。作为树的生命原则，它是从树中抽象出来的一种灵性精华，也可以被描述为个体化原则（principium individuationis）。那么树就是自性之外在的、可见的标志。炼金术士似乎持有类似的看法。因此《奥雷利亚隐秘》说："哲学家们最热切地寻找的是那棵矗立在尘世乐园中央的树之中心。"7 据同一来源说，基督本身就是这棵树。8 树的比较早在亚历山大的欧洛吉乌斯（约公元600年）那里就出现了，他说："看哪，父是根，子是枝，灵是果：因为实体〔οὐσία〕在三者中是一。"9 墨丘利乌斯也是三位一体的（trinus et unus）。

[244] So if we translate it into psychological language, the fairytale tells us that the mercurial essence, the principium individuationis, would have developed freely under natural conditions, but was robbed of its freedom by deliberate intervention from outside, and was artfully confined and banished like an evil spirit. (Only evil spirits have to be confined, and the wickedness of this spirit was shown by its murderous intent.) Supposing the fairytale is right and the spirit was really as wicked as it relates, we would have to conclude that the Master who imprisoned the principium individuationis had a good end in view. But who is this well-intentioned Master who has the power to banish the principle of man’s individuation? Such power is given only to a ruler of souls in the spiritual realm. The idea that the principle of individuation is the source of all evil is found in Schopenhauer and still more in Buddhism. In Christianity, too, human nature is tainted with original sin and is redeemed from this stain by Christ’s self-sacrifice. Man in his “natural” condition is neither good nor pure, and if he should develop in the natural way the result would be a product not essentially different from an animal. Sheer instinctuality and naïve unconsciousness untroubled by a sense of guilt would prevail if the Master had not interrupted the free development of the natural being by introducing a distinction between good and evil and outlawing the evil. Since without guilt there is no moral consciousness and without awareness of differences no consciousness at all, we must concede that the strange intervention of the master of souls was absolutely necessary for the development of any kind of consciousness and in this sense was for the good. According to our religious beliefs, God himself is this Master—and the alchemist, in his small way, competes with the Creator in so far as he strives to do work analogous to the work of creation, and therefore he likens his microcosmic opus to the work of the world creator.10
[244] 如果我们将其翻译成心理学语言，童话告诉我们：墨丘利乌斯的本质，即个体化原则，本应在自然条件下自由发展，但被外部有意的干预剥夺了自由，被巧妙地囚禁和放逐，如同一个恶灵。（只有恶灵才需要被囚禁，而这个灵的恶意表现在它的杀人意图上。）假如童话是对的，灵真的如它所叙述的那样邪恶，那么我们就必须得出结论：囚禁个体化原则的大师有着善良的目的。但这位有权放逐人之个体化原则的善意大师是谁呢？这样的权力只赋予给灵性领域中的灵魂统治者。个体化原则是万恶之源这一观点见于叔本华，更见于佛教。在基督教中，人性也沾染了原罪，通过基督的自我牺牲从这一污点中被救赎。人在其"自然"状态中既非善也非纯洁，如果他以自然方式发展，结果将是一个与动物本质上无异的产物。如果大师没有通过引入善恶之辨并取缔恶来打断自然之 beings 的自由发展，那么纯粹的本能性和不被罪恶感所扰的朴素无意识将占上风。因为没有罪疚感就没有道德意识，没有差异意识就根本没有意识，我们必须承认灵魂之主这一奇特干预对于任何意识的发展都是绝对必要的，在这个意义上是善的。根据我们的宗教信念，上帝本人就是这位大师——而炼金术士以其微小的方式与造物主竞争，在他努力做类似于创世之功的工作时，因此他将自己的微宇宙操作比作世界创造者的工作。10

[245] In our fairytale the natural evil is banished to the “roots,” that is, to the earth, in other words the body. This statement agrees with the historical fact that Christian thought in general has held the body in contempt, without bothering much about the finer doctrinal distinctions.11 For, according to doctrine, neither the body nor nature in general is evil per se: as the work of God, or as the actual form in which he manifests himself, nature cannot be identical with evil. Correspondingly, the evil spirit in the fairytale is not simply banished to the earth and allowed to roam about at will, but is only hidden there in a safe and special container, so that he cannot call attention to himself anywhere except right under the oak. The bottle is an artificial human product and thus signifies the intellectual purposefulness and artificiality of the procedure, whose obvious aim is to isolate the spirit from the surrounding medium. As the vas Hermeticum of alchemy, it was “hermetically” sealed (i.e., sealed with the sign of Hermes);12 it had to be made of glass, and had also to be as round as possible, since it was meant to represent the cosmos in which the earth was created.13 Transparent glass is something like solidified water or air, both of which are synonyms for spirit. The alchemical retort is therefore equivalent to the anima mundi, which according to an old alchemical conception surrounds the cosmos. Caesarius of Heisterbach (thirteenth century) mentions a vision in which the soul appeared as a spherical glass vessel.14 Likewise the “spiritual” or “ethereal” (aethereus) philosophers’ stone is a precious vitrum (sometimes described as malleabile) which was often equated with the gold glass (aurum vitreum) of the heavenly Jerusalem (Rev. 21 : 21).
[245] 在我们的童话中，自然的恶被放逐到"根"中，即大地，换言之即身体。这一陈述与以下历史事实一致：基督教思想总体上蔑视身体，而不太在意更精细的教义区分。11 因为根据教义，身体或一般自然本身并非恶：作为上帝的造物，或作为他显现自身的实际形式，自然不可能等同于恶。相应地，童话中的恶灵不是简单地被放逐到地上任其游荡，而是被藏在一个安全的特殊容器中，使它除了在橡树下以外无处引人注目。瓶子是人造产品，因此标志着程序的知识目的性和人为性，其明显目的是将精灵从周围介质中隔离出来。作为炼金术的赫尔墨斯容器（vas Hermeticum），它被"赫尔墨斯式地"密封（即以赫尔墨斯的符号密封）；12 它必须由玻璃制成，还必须尽可能圆，因为它意在代表地球被创造于其中的宇宙。13 透明玻璃有点像凝固的水或空气，二者都是精神的同义词。因此炼金术的蒸馏瓶等同于世界灵魂（anima mundi），根据一种古老的炼金术观念，后者环绕着宇宙。海斯特巴赫的凯撒里乌斯（十三世纪）提到一个异象，其中灵魂显现为球形玻璃器皿。14 同样，"灵性的"或"以太的"（aethereus）哲学家之石是一种珍贵的玻璃（vitrum，有时被描述为可锻造的 malleabile），常被等同于天上的耶路撒冷的金玻璃（aurum vitreum）（《启示录》21:21）。

[246] It is worth noting that the German fairytale calls the spirit confined in the bottle by the name of the pagan god, Mercurius, who was considered identical with the German national god, Wotan. The mention of Mercurius stamps the fairytale as an alchemical folk legend, closely related on the one hand to the allegorical tales used in teaching alchemy, and on the other to the well-known group of folktales that cluster round the motif of the “spellbound spirit.” Our fairytale thus interprets the evil spirit as a pagan god, forced under the influence of Christianity to descend into the dark underworld and be morally disqualified. Hermes becomes the demon of the mysteries celebrated by all tenebriones (obscurantists), and Wotan the demon of forest and storm; Mercurius becomes the soul of the metals, the metallic man (homunculus), the dragon (serpens mercurialis), the roaring fiery lion, the night raven (nycticorax), and the black eagle—the last four being synonyms for the devil. In fact the spirit in the bottle behaves just as the devil does in many other fairytales: he bestows wealth by changing base metal into gold; and like the devil, he also gets tricked.
[246] 值得注意的是，这篇德国童话用异教神的名字墨丘利乌斯来称呼瓶中被囚的精灵——这位异教神被认为与日耳曼民族之神沃坦同一。墨丘利乌斯的出现使童话具有炼金术民间传说的特征，一方面与用于炼金术教学的寓言故事密切相关，另一方面与围绕"被迷法的灵"母题的著名民间故事群相关。因此我们的童话将恶灵解释为一个异教神——在基督教的影响下被迫坠入黑暗的地下世界并在道德上被剥夺资格。赫尔墨斯成为所有暗夜之徒（tenebriones，蒙昧主义者）所庆祝的奥秘之魔，沃坦成为森林和风暴之魔；墨丘利乌斯成为金属之灵、金属人（homunculus）、龙（serpens mercurialis）、咆哮的火狮、夜鸦（nycticorax）和黑鹰——后四者是魔鬼的同义词。事实上瓶中精灵的行为如同许多其他童话中的魔鬼：它通过将贱金属变为金子来赐予财富；如同魔鬼一样，它也被骗了。





2. THE CONNECTION BETWEEN SPIRIT AND TREE
2. 精灵与树的联系


[247] Before continuing our discussion of the spirit Mercurius, I should like to point out a not unimportant fact. The place where he lies confined is not just any place but a very essential one—namely, under the oak, the king of the forest. In psychological terms, this means that the evil spirit is imprisoned in the roots of the self, as the secret hidden in the principle of individuation. He is not identical with the tree, nor with its roots, but has been put there by artificial means. The fairytale gives us no reason to think that the oak, which represents the self, has grown out of the spirit in the bottle; we may rather conjecture that the oak presented a suitable place for concealing a secret. A treasure, for instance, is preferably buried near some kind of landmark, or else such a mark is put up afterwards. The tree of paradise serves as a prototype for this and similar tales: it, too, is not identical with the voice of the serpent which issued from it.1 However, it must not be forgotten that these mythical motifs have a significant connection with certain psychological phenomena observed among primitive peoples. In all such cases there is a notable analogy with primitive animism: certain trees are animated by souls—have the character of personality, we would say—and possess a voice that gives commands to human beings. Amaury Talbot2 reports one such case from Nigeria, where a native soldier heard an oji tree calling to him, and tried desperately to break out of the barracks and hasten to the tree. Under cross-examination he alleged that all those who bore the name of the tree now and then heard its voice. Here the voice is undoubtedly identical with the tree. These psychic phenomena suggest that originally the tree and the daemon were one and the same, and that their separation is a secondary phenomenon corresponding to a higher level of culture and consciousness. The original phenomenon was nothing less than a nature deity, a tremendum pure and simple, which is morally neutral. But the secondary phenomenon implies an act of discrimination which splits man off from nature and thus testifies to the existence of a more highly differentiated consciousness. To this is added, as a tertiary phenomenon testifying to a still higher level, the moral qualification which declares the voice to be an evil spirit under a ban. It goes without saying that this third level is marked by a belief in a “higher” and “good” God who, though he has not finally disposed of his adversary, has nevertheless rendered him harmless for some time to come by imprisonment (Rev. 20: 1–3).
[247] 在继续讨论墨丘利乌斯之灵之前，我想指出一个并非不重要的事实。他被囚禁的地方不是随便什么地方，而是一个非常关键的地点——即在森林之王橡树下。用心理学术语来说，这意味着恶灵被囚禁在自性的根中，作为隐藏在个体化原则中的秘密。它不与树同一，也不与树根同一，而是被人为地放在那里的。童话没有给我们任何理由认为代表自性的橡树是从瓶中灵长出来的；我们宁可推测橡树为隐藏秘密提供了一个合适的地点。例如，宝藏更愿意被埋在某个地标附近，或者事后设立这样的标记。乐园之树为这个和类似的故事提供了原型：它也不同于从中发出的蛇的声音。1 然而，不可忘记的是，这些神话母题与在原始民族中观察到的某些心理现象有着重要关联。在所有这类情况下，与原始泛灵论存在显著类比：某些树被灵魂赋予生命——我们会说具有人格特征——并拥有向人类发出命令的声音。阿莫里·塔尔博特2 从尼日利亚报告了一个这样的案例：一名土著士兵听到一棵 oji 树呼唤他，拼命试图冲出兵营奔赴那棵树。在盘问下他声称所有以该树为名的人都会不时听到它的声音。这里声音无疑与树同一。这些心理现象表明，最初树和精怪是同一的，它们的分离是一个次级现象，对应于更高的文化和意识水平。最初的现象不过是一位自然之神——纯粹的 tremendum（令人敬畏者）——在道德上是中立的。但次级现象暗示了一种区分行为，它将人与自然分离开来，从而证明了更高分化意识的存在。作为证明更高水平的第三级现象，是道德定性——宣布声音为受禁的恶灵。不言而喻，这第三个水平以信仰一位"更高的"和"善的"上帝为标志——他虽然尚未最终处置他的对手，但通过囚禁（《启示录》20:1–3）暂时使其无害。

[248] Since at the present level of consciousness we cannot suppose that tree daemons exist, we are forced to assert that the primitive suffers from hallucinations, that he hears his own unconscious which has projected itself into the tree. If this theory is correct—and I do not know how we could formulate it otherwise today—then the second level of consciousness has effected a differentiation between the object “tree” and the unconscious content projected into it, thereby achieving an act of enlightenment. The third level rises still higher and attributes “evil” to the psychic content which has been separated from the object. Finally a fourth level, the level reached by our consciousness today, carries the enlightenment a stage further by denying the objective existence of the “spirit” and declaring that the primitive has heard nothing at all, but merely had an auditory hallucination. Consequently the whole phenomenon vanishes into thin air—with the great advantage that the evil spirit becomes obviously non-existent and sinks into ridiculous insignificance. A fifth level, however, which is bound to take a quintessential view of the matter, wonders about this conjuring trick that turns what began as a miracle into a senseless self-deception—only to come full circle. Like the boy who told his father a made-up story about sixty stags in the forest, it asks: “But what, then, was all the rustling in the woods?” The fifth level is of the opinion that something did happen after all: even though the psychic content was not the tree, nor a spirit in the tree, nor indeed any spirit at all, it was nevertheless a phenomenon thrusting up from the unconscious, the existence of which cannot be denied if one is minded to grant the psyche any kind of reality. If one did not do that, one would have to extend God’s creatio ex nihilo—which seems so obnoxious to the modern intellect—very much further to include steam engines, automobiles, radios, and every library on earth, all of which would presumably have arisen from unimaginably fortuitous conglomerations of atoms. The only thing that would have happened is that the Creator would have been renamed Conglomeratio.
[248] 由于在当前的意识水平上，我们不能假定树精存在，我们被迫断言原始人患有幻觉，他听到的是自己投射到树中的无意识。如果这一理论是正确的——我不知道今天我们还能如何表述——那么第二个意识水平实现了"树"这一对象与投射其中的无意识内含物之间的分化，从而完成了一个启蒙行为。第三个水平更高，将"恶"归于已与对象分离的心理内含物。最后，第四个水平——我们今天的意识所达到的水平——将启蒙推进一步，否认"灵"的客观存在，宣布原始人什么也没听到，只是有了一个听觉幻觉。因此整个现象化为乌有——其巨大优势是恶灵明显不存在，沦于可笔的微不足道。然而，第五个水平——它必然会对事物采取一种精华式的看法——对这种将始于奇迹之物变为无意义自欺的魔术感到困惑——结果又回到原点。就像那个向父亲编造了一个关于林中有六十头雄鹿的故事的男孩一样，它问："那么，林中那些籁籁声到底是什么？"第五个水平认为毕竟有事情发生了：即使心理内含物不是树，不是树中的灵，实际上也根本不是任何灵，它仍然是从无意识中涌出的现象——如果有人愿意赋予心理以某种实在性的话，其存在不能被否认。如果不这样做，就得将上帝的 creatio ex nihilo（从虚无中创造）——对现代智识来说如此可憎——大大推广到包括蒸汽机、汽车、收音机和地球上每一座图书馆，所有这些大概都从难以想象的偶然原子聚合中产生。唯一发生的事情只是造物主被改名为 Conglomeratio（聚合体）。

[249] The fifth level assumes that the unconscious exists and has a reality just like any other existent. However odious it may be, this means that the “spirit” is also a reality, and the “evil” spirit at that. What is even worse, the distinction between “good” and “evil” is suddenly no longer obsolete, but highly topical and necessary. The crucial point is that so long as the evil spirit cannot be proved to be a subjective psychic experience, then even trees and other suitable objects would have, once again, to be seriously considered as its lodging places.
[249] 第五个水平假设无意识存在并像任何其他存在一样具有实在性。无论多么可憎，这意味着"灵"也是一种实在，而且是"恶"灵。更糟糕的是，"善"与"恶"之间的区别突然不再过时，而是高度现实和必要的。关键在于，只要恶灵不能被证明为主观的心理经验，那么树木和其他合适的物体就不得不再次被认真考虑为其栖居之所。





3. THE PROBLEM OF FREEING MERCURIUS
3. 释放墨丘利乌斯的问题


[250] We will not pursue the paradoxical reality of the unconscious any further now, but will return to the fairytale of the spirit in the bottle. As we have seen, the spirit Mercurius bears some resemblance to the “cheated devil.” The analogy, however, is only a superficial one, since, unlike the gifts of the devil, the gold of Mercurius does not turn to horse droppings but remains good metal, and the magic rag does not turn to ashes by morning but retains its healing power. Nor is Mercurius tricked out of a soul that he wanted to steal. He is only tricked into his own better nature, one might say, in that the boy succeeds in bottling him up again in order to cure his bad mood and make him tractable. Mercurius becomes polite, gives the young fellow a useful ransom and is accordingly set free. We now hear about the student’s good fortune and how he became a wonder-working doctor, but—strangely enough—nothing about the doings of the liberated spirit, though these might be of some interest in view of the web of meanings in which Mercurius, with his many-sided associations, entangles us. What happens when this pagan god, Hermes-Mercurius-Wotan, is let loose again? Being a god of magicians, a spiritus vegetativus, and a storm daemon, he will hardly have returned to captivity, and the fairytale gives us no reason to suppose that the episode of imprisonment has finally changed his nature to the pink of perfection. The bird of Hermes has escaped from the glass cage, and in consequence something has happened which the experienced alchemist wished at all costs to avoid. That is why he always sealed the stopper of his bottle with magic signs and set it for a very long time over the lowest fire, so that “he who is within may not fly out.” For if he escapes, the whole laborious opus comes to nothing and has to be started all over again. Our lad was a Sunday’s child and possibly one of the poor in spirit, on whom was bestowed a bit of the Kingdom of Heaven in the shape of the self-renewing tincture, with reference to which it was said that the opus needed to be performed only once.1 But if he had lost the magic rag he would certainly never have been able to produce it a second time, by himself. It looks as though some Master had succeeded in capturing the mercurial spirit and then hid him in a safe place, like a treasure—perhaps putting him aside for some future use. He may even have planned to tame the wild Mercurius to serve him as a willing “familiar,” like Mephisto—such trains of thought are not strange to alchemy. Perhaps he was disagreeably surprised when he returned to the oak tree and found that his bird had flown. At any rate, it might have been better not to have left the fate of the bottle to chance.
[250] 我们现在不进一步追索无意识的悖论实在性，而是回到瓶中灵的童话。如我们所见，墨丘利乌斯之灵与"被骗的魔鬼"有些相似。然而，这种类比只是表面的，因为与魔鬼的恩赐不同，墨丘利乌斯的金子不会变成马粪，而是保持为好金属，那块魔法破布也不会到早晨化为灰烬，而是保持其治愈之力。墨丘利乌斯也不是被骗走了他想偷取的灵魂。他只是被骗回了自身的更好的本性——可以这样说——因为男孩成功地将他重新装回瓶中，以治愈他的坏脾气并使他变得温顺。墨丘利乌斯变得礼貌了，给小伙子一件有用的赎金，因此被释放。我们现在听到那个学生的好运以及他如何成为了一位创造奇迹的医生，但——奇怪的是——对被释放精灵的行踪却只字未提，尽管鉴于墨丘利乌斯以其多方面的联想将我们缠入的意义之网，这些行踪可能颇有意思。当这个异教神——赫尔墨斯-墨丘利乌斯-沃坦——被重新释放后会怎样？作为魔法师之神、生长之灵（spiritus vegetativus）和风暴之魔，他不太可能回到囚禁中，童话也没有给我们任何理由认为囚禁事件已彻底改变了他的本性至尽善尽美。赫尔墨斯之鸟已从玻璃笼中逃脱，其后果是有经验的炼金术士不惜一切代价想要避免的。正因如此，他总是用魔法符号密封瓶口，并在最微小的火上放置很长时间，以便"里面的人不会飞出"。因为如果他逃了，整个费力的操作就付诸东流，必须从头开始。我们的少年是个幸运儿，也许是"灵之贫者"之一——天国的一角以自新酏剂的形态赐予了他——据说这种操作只需进行一次。1 但如果他丢了那块魔法布，他绝不可能靠自己第二次生产出来。看起来似乎有某位大师成功捕获了墨丘利乌斯之灵，然后像藏宝一样将其藏在一个安全的地方——也许留待将来使用。他甚至可能计划驯服野性的墨丘利乌斯，使其成为愿意效劳的"护卫灵"——如同梅菲斯特——这样的思路在炼金术中并不陌生。也许当他回到橡树旁发现他的鸟已飞走时感到不快。无论如何，把瓶子的命运交给偶然也许不是个好主意。

[251] Be that as it may, the behaviour of the boy—successfully as it worked out for him—must be described as alchemically incorrect. Apart from the fact that he may have infringed upon the legitimate claims of an unknown Master by setting Mercurius free, he was also totally unconscious of what might follow if this turbulent spirit were let loose upon the world. The golden age of alchemy was the sixteenth and the first half of the seventeenth century. At that time a storm bird did indeed escape from a spiritual vessel which the daemons must have felt was a prison. As I have said, the alchemists were all for not letting Mercurius escape. They wanted to keep him in the bottle in order to transform him: for they believed, like Petasios, that lead (another arcane substance) was “so bedevilled and shameless that all who wish to investigate it fall into madness through ignorance.”2 The same was said of the elusive Mercurius who evades every grasp—a real trickster who drove the alchemists to despair.3
[251] 不管怎样，男孩的行为——虽然对他来说成功了——必须被描述为在炼金术上是不正确的。除了他可能侵犯了某位未知大师的合法权利之外，他对自己释放这个暴躁精灵可能带来的后果完全无意识。炼金术的黄金时代是十六世纪和十七世纪上半叶。那时确实有一只风暴鸟从一个精神容器中逃脱——魔鬼们一定感到那容器是监狱。如我所说，炼金术士都主张不让墨丘利乌斯逃脱。他们想把他留在瓶中以便转化他：因为他们像佩塔西奥斯一样相信，铅（另一种秘术物质）"如此着魔和无耻，以至于所有想要研究它的人都因无知而陷入疯狂"。2 同样的说法也适用于难以捉摸的墨丘利乌斯——他躲避每一次抓取——一个真正的骗子，将炼金术士逼至绝望。3

1. INTRODUCTORY
1. 导论


[252] The interested reader will want, as I do, to find out more about this spirit—especially what our forefathers believed and said about him. I will therefore try with the aid of text citations to draw a picture of this versatile and shimmering god as he appeared to the masters of the royal art. For this purpose we must consult the abstruse literature of alchemy, which has not yet been properly understood. Naturally, in later times, the history of alchemy was mainly of interest to the chemist. The fact that it recorded the discovery of many chemical substances and drugs could not, however, reconcile him to the pitiful meagreness, so it seemed to him, of its scientific content. He was not in the position of the older authors, such as Schmieder, who could look on the possibility of goldmaking with hopeful esteem and sympathy; instead he was irritated by the futility of the recipes and the fraudulence of alchemical speculation in general. To him alchemy was bound to seem a gigantic aberration that lasted for more than two thousand years. Had he only asked himself whether the chemistry of alchemy was authentic or not, that is, whether the alchemists were really chemists or merely spoke a chemical jargon, then the texts themselves would have suggested a line of observation other than the purely chemical. The scientific equipment of the chemist does not, however, fit him to pursue this other line, since it leads straight into the history of religion. Thus it was a philologist, Reitzenstein, whom we have to thank for preliminary researches of the greatest value in this field. It was he who recognized the mythological and Gnostic ideas embedded in alchemy, thereby opening up the whole subject from an angle which promises to be most fruitful. For alchemy, as the earliest Greek and Chinese texts show, originally formed part of Gnostic philosophical speculations which also included a detailed knowledge of the techniques of the goldsmith and ironsmith, the faker of precious stones, the druggist and apothecary. In East and West alike, alchemy contains as its core the Gnostic doctrine of the Anthropos and by its very nature has the character of a peculiar doctrine of redemption. This fact necessarily escaped the chemist, although it is expressed clearly enough in the Greek and Latin texts as well as in the Chinese of about the same period.
[252] 有兴趣的读者会像我一样想进一步了解这位精灵——尤其是我们的祖辈对他信仰和说过什么。因此我将尝试借助文献引文，描绘这位多面而闪烁的神在皇家艺术大师面前的形象。为此我们必须查阅炼金术的深奥文献——这些文献至今尚未得到正确理解。自然，在后来的时代，炼金术的历史主要引起化学家的兴趣。它记录了许多化学物质和药物的发现这一事实，并不能使他调和于——在他看来——其科学内容可怜的贫乏。他不像施米德那样的早期作者，可以以充满希望的尊重和同情来看待制金的可能性；相反，他受到配方的徒劳和炼金术思辨总体上的欺诈性的刺激。对他来说，炼金术必然似乎是一场持续了两千多年的巨大迷误。如果他仅问自己炼金术的化学是否是真实的，即炼金术士是否真的是化学家或只是说化学行话，那么文献本身就会提示一种不同于纯化学的观察方向。然而化学家的科学装备并不适合追求这另一条路线，因为它直通宗教史。因此我们不得不感谢语言学家莱岑斯坦在这一领域中做了最有价值的初步研究。正是他认识到了嵌入炼金术中的神话和诺斯替思想，从而从最有希望的角度开启了整个主题。因为炼金术，如最早的希腊和中国文献所示，最初是诺斯替哲学思辨的一部分，也包含对金匠和铁匠、宝石伪造者、药剂师和药商技艺的详细了解。无论在东西方，炼金术都以诺斯替的原人教义为核心，并具有独特的救赎教义的特征。这一事实必然逃过了化学家，尽管它在希腊和拉丁文献以及大约同时期的中国文献中都有清楚表达。

[253] To begin with, of course, it is almost impossible for our scientifically trained minds to feel their way back into that primitive state of participation mystique in which subject and object are identical. Here the findings of modern psychology stood me in very good stead. Practical experience shows us again and again that any prolonged preoccupation with an unknown object acts as an almost irresistible bait for the unconscious to project itself into the unknown nature of the object and to accept the resultant perception, and the interpretation deduced from it, as objective. This phenomenon, a daily occurrence in practical psychology and more especially in psychotherapy, is without doubt a vestige of primitivity. On the primitive level, the whole of life is governed by animistic assumptions, that is, by projections of subjective contents into objective situations. For example, Karl von den Steinen says that the Bororos think of themselves as red cockatoos, although they readily admit that they have no feathers.1 On this level, the alchemists’ assumption that a certain substance possesses secret powers, or that there is a prima materia somewhere which works miracles, is self-evident. This is, however, not a fact that can be understood or even thought of in chemical terms, it is a psychological phenomenon. Psychology, therefore, can make an important contribution towards elucidating the alchemists’ mentality. What to the chemist seem to be the absurd fantasies of alchemy can be recognized by the psychologist without too much difficulty as psychic material contaminated with chemical substances. This material stems from the collective unconscious and is therefore identical with fantasy products that can still be found today among both sick and healthy people who have never heard of alchemy. On account of the primitive character of its projections, alchemy, so barren a field for the chemist, is for the psychologist a veritable gold-mine of materials which throw an exceedingly valuable light on the structure of the unconscious.
[253] 首先，当然，我们受过科学训练的心智几乎不可能回溯到那种原始的 participation mystique（神秘参与）状态——在那里主体与客体是同一的。在这里现代心理学的发现对我大有裨益。实践经验反复表明，任何对未知对象的长时间专注都会成为无意识几乎不可抗拒的诱饵，使其将自身投射到对象的未知本性中，并将由此产生的感知和从中推导的解释当作客观的来接受。这一现象在实践心理学中、尤其在心理治疗中每日发生，无疑是原始性的遗迹。在原始水平上，整个生活由泛灵论的假设所支配，即由主观内含物向客观情境的投射所支配。例如，卡尔·冯·登·施泰因说博罗罗人认为自己是红鹦鹉，尽管他们承认自己没有羽毛。1 在这一水平上，炼金术士关于某种物质具有隐秘力量的假设，或某处有一种创造奇迹的原初物质，是不言自明的。然而，这不是一个能在化学上被理解甚至被想到的事实，而是一个心理现象。因此，心理学可以对阐明炼金术士的心智做出重要贡献。对化学家来说似乎是炼金术荒谬幻想的东西，心理学家可以不太困难地识别为被化学物质所污染的心理材料。这些材料源自集体无意识，因此与今天在从未听说过炼金术的病人和健康人中都可见到的幻想产物是同一的。由于其投射的原始特征，炼金术——对化学家来说如此贫乏的领域——对心理学家来说却是一个真正的金矿，提供了对无意识结构极为宝贵的启发。

[254] Since in what follows I shall often refer to the original texts, it might be as well to say a few words about this literature, some of which is not easily accessible. I shall leave out of account the few Chinese texts that have been translated, and shall only mention that The Secret of the Golden Flower, published by Richard Wilhelm and myself, is representative of its class. Nor can I consider the Indian “Quicksilver System.”2 The Western literature I have used falls into four groups:
[254] 由于在下文中我将经常引用原始文献，也许有必要谈谈这些文献——其中一些不易获取。我将略去已翻译的少量中文文献，只提一下由理查德·威廉和我出版的《太乙金华宗旨》是其同类中的代表。我也无法涉及印度的"水银系统"。2 我所使用的西方文献分为四组：

1. Texts by ancient authors. This group comprises mainly Greek texts, which have been edited by Berthelot, and those transmitted by the Arabs, likewise edited by him. They date from the period between the first and eighth centuries.
1. 古代作者文献。这一组主要包括希腊文献，由贝特洛编辑，以及由阿拉伯人传佚的文献，同样由他编辑。它们的时代介于公元一世纪至八世纪之间。

2. Texts by the early Latinists. The most important of these are translations from the Arabic (or Hebrew?). Recent research shows that most of these texts derive from the Harranite school, which flourished until about 1050, and was also, probably, the source of the Corpus Hermeticum. To this group belong certain texts whose Arabic origin is doubtful but which at least show Arabic influence—for instance, the “Summa perfectionis” of Geber and the Aristotle and Avicenna treatises. This period extends from the ninth to the thirteenth century.
2. 早期拉丁作者文献。其中最重要的是从阿拉伯语（或希伯来语？）翻译的。最近的研究表明，这些文献大多源自哈兰学派——该学派繁盛至约1050年，也很可能是《赫尔墨斯文集》的来源。属于这一组的还有一些阿拉伯起源可疑但至少显示阿拉伯影响的文献——例如贾比尔的《完美总论》以及亚里士多德和阿维森纳的论著。这一时期从九世纪延伸至十三世纪。

3. Texts by the later Latinists. These comprise the principal group and range from the fourteenth to the seventeenth century.
3. 后期拉丁作者文献。这构成主要的一组，从十四世纪到十七世纪。

4. Texts in modern European languages. Sixteenth to seventeenth century. After that, alchemy fell into decline, which is why I have only occasionally used eighteenth-century texts.
4. 现代欧洲语言文献。十六至十七世纪。此后炼金术走向衰落，这就是为什么我仅偶尔使用十八世纪的文献。





2. MERCURIUS AS QUICKSILVER AND/OR WATER
2. 作为水银和/或水的墨丘利乌斯


[255] Mercurius was first understood pretty well everywhere as hydrargyrum1 (Hg), quicksilver or argentum vivum (Fr. vifargent or argent vive). As such, it was called vulgaris (common) and crudus. As a rule, mercurius philosophicus was specifically distinguished from this, as an avowedly arcane substance that was sometimes conceived to be present in mercurius crudus, and then, again, to differ from it completely. It was the true object of the alchemical procedure. Quicksilver, because of its fluidity and volatility, was also defined as water. A popular saying is: “Aqua manus non madefaciens” (the water that does not make the hands wet).2 Other designations are aqua vitae,3 aqua alba,4 aqua sicca.5 The last designation, dry water, is paradoxical, for which reason I should like to call special attention to it as characterizing the nature of the object described. Aqua septies distillata (seven times distilled water) and aqueum subtile6 point to the sublimated (“spiritual”) nature of the philosophic Mercurius. Many treatises simply speak of Mercurius as water.7 The doctrine of the humidum radicale (root-moisture or radical moisture) underlies such designations as humidum album,8 humiditas maxime permanens incombustibilis et unctuosa,9 and humiditas radicalis.10 Mercurius is also said to arise from the moisture like a vapour11 (which again points to his spiritual nature), or to rule the water.12 The “divine water” (ὕδωρ ϑεῑον) so often mentioned in the Greek texts is quicksilver.13 Mercurius as the arcane substance and golden tincture is indicated by the designation aqua aurea14 and by the description of the water as Mercurii caduceus.15
[255] 墨丘利乌斯最初在各地被普遍理解为 hydrargyrum1（Hg），即水银或 argentum vivum（活银，法文 vifargent 或 argent vive）。作为这种水银，它被称为 vulgaris（普通的）和 crudus（粗的）。通常，哲学墨丘利乌斯（mercurius philosophicus）与此有明确区别，是一种公开承认的秘术物质，有时被认为存在于粗水银之中，有时又被认为与之完全不同。它是炼金术程序的真正对象。水银因其流动性和挥发性也被定义为水。一句流行语说："Aqua manus non madefaciens"（不湿手的水）。2 其他名称还有 aqua vitae3、aqua alba4、aqua sicca5。最后这个名称——干水——是悖论的，因此我想特别提请注意它作为被描述对象本性的特征。Aqua septies distillata（七次蒸馏的水）和 aqueum subtile6 指向哲学墨丘利乌斯的升华（"灵性化"）本性。许多论著径直将墨丘利乌斯称为水。7 根本湿气（humidum radicale）学说构成了诸如 humidum album8、humiditas maxime permanens incombustibilis et unctuosa9 和 humiditas radicalis10 等名称的基础。据说墨丘利乌斯也如蒸气般从湿气中升起11（这再次指向其灵性本性），或统治水。12 希腊文献中常提到的"神圣之水"（ὕδωρ ϑεῑον）就是水银。13 作为秘术物质和金色酏剂的墨丘利乌斯由 aqua aurea14 这一名称以及将水描述为墨丘利乌斯的杖（Mercurii caduceus）15 来指示。





3. MERCURIUS AS FIRE
3. 作为火的墨丘利乌斯


[256] Many treatises define Mercurius simply as fire.1 He is ignis elementaris2 noster naturalis ignis certissimus,3 which again indicates his “philosophic” nature. The aqua mercurialis is even a divine fire.4 This fire is “highly vaporous” (vaporosus).5 Indeed, Mercurius is really the only fire in the whole procedure.6 He is an “invisible fire, working in secret.”7 One text says that the “heart” of Mercurius is at the North Pole and that he is like a fire (northern lights).8 He is, in fact, as another text says, “the universal and scintillating fire of the light of nature, which carries the heavenly spirit within it.”9 This passage is particularly important as it relates Mercurius to the lumen naturae, the source of mystical knowledge second only to the holy revelation of the Scriptures. Once more we catch a glimpse of the ancient role of Hermes as the god of revelation. Although the lumen naturae, as originally bestowed by God upon his creatures, is not by nature ungodly, its essence was nevertheless felt to be abysmal, since the ignis mercurialis was also connected with the fires of hell. It seems, however, that the alchemists did not understand hell, or its fire, as absolutely outside of God or opposed to him, but rather as an internal component of the deity, which must indeed be so if God is held to be a coincidentia oppositorum. The concept of an all-encompassing God must necessarily include his opposite. The coincidentia, of course, must not be too radical or too extreme, otherwise God would cancel himself out.10 The principle of the coincidence of opposites must therefore be completed by that of absolute opposition in order to attain full paradoxicality and hence psychological validity.
[256] 许多论著径直将墨丘利乌斯定义为火。1 它是 ignis elementaris2、noster naturalis ignis certissimus3，这再次指示其"哲学"本性。水银水（aqua mercurialis）甚至是神圣之火。4 这火"高度蒸气化"（vaporosus）。5 事实上，墨丘利乌斯是整个程序中唯一的火。6 它是"不可见的火，在暗中运作"。7 一篇文献说墨丘利乌斯的"心"在北极，它如火（北极光）。8 事实上，如另一篇文献所说，它是"自然之光的普遍而闪烁的火，其中携带着天上之灵"。9 这段话特别重要，因为它将墨丘利乌斯与自然之光联系起来——自然之光是仅次于圣经神圣启示的神秘知识之源。我们再次瞥见赫尔墨斯作为启示之神的古老角色。尽管自然之光作为上帝最初赐予其造物之物，本性上并非不虔的，但其本质却被感到是深不可测的，因为水银之火也与地狱之火相连。然而，炼金术士似乎并不将地狱或其火理解为绝对外在于上帝或与上帝对立的，而是理解为神性的内在组成部分——如果上帝被视为对立统一（coincidentia oppositorum）的话，这确实必然如此。一个无所不包的上帝概念必然包含其对立面。当然，统一不能太彻底或太极端，否则上帝就会自我取消。10 因此，对立统一原则必须由绝对对立原则来补充，以达到充分的悖论性并因此获得心理学有效性。

[257] The mercurial fire is found in the “centre of the earth,” or dragon’s belly, in fluid form. Benedictus Figulus writes: “Visit the centre of the earth, there you will find the global fire.”11 Another treatise says that this fire is the “secret, infernal fire, the wonder of the world, the system of the higher powers in the lower.”12 Mercurius, the revelatory light of nature, is also hell-fire, which in some miraculous way is none other than a rearrangement of the heavenly, spiritual powers in the lower, chthonic world of matter, thought already in St. Paul’s time to be ruled by the devil. Hell-fire, the true energic principle of evil, appears here as the manifest counterpart of the spiritual and the good, and as essentially identical with it in substance. After that, it can surely cause no offence when another treatise says that the mercurial fire is the “fire in which God himself burns in divine love.”13 We are not deceiving ourselves if we feel in scattered remarks of this kind the breath of true mysticism.
[257] 水银之火发现于"地之中心"或龙腹中，呈液态。本尼迪克图斯·菲古鲁斯写道："探访大地之中心，在那里你将找到全球之火。"11 另一篇文献说这火是"秘密的地狱之火，世界之奇，高能于低"。12 墨丘利乌斯，自然之启示之光，也是地狱之火——以某种奇妙的方式，它不过是天上灵性力量在低层的、冥界的物质世界中的重新安排——后者在圣保罗时代已被认为是受魔鬼统治的。地狱之火，恶的真正能量原则，在此显现为灵性和善的明显对应面，并在本质上与之同质。之后，当另一篇文献说水银之火是"上帝自身在其中以神圣之爱燃烧的火"时，13 肯定不会引起冒犯。如果我们在这类零散的言论中感受到真正神秘主义的气息，我们并没有自欺。

[258] Since Mercurius is himself of fiery nature, fire does not harm him: he remains unchanged within it, rejoicing like the salamander.14 It is unnecessary to point out that quicksilver does not behave like this but vaporizes under heat, as the alchemists themselves knew from very early times.
[258] 由于墨丘利乌斯本身具有火的性质，火不会伤害它：它在火中不变，如同火螄蜥般欢乐。14 无需指出水银并非如此表现——它在加热时挥发，炼金术士自己很早就知道这一点。





4. MERCURIUS AS SPIRIT AND SOUL
4. 作为精神与灵魂的墨丘利乌斯


[259] If Mercurius had been understood simply as quicksilver, there would obviously have been no need for any of the appellations I have listed. The fact that this need arose points to the conclusion that one simple and unmistakable term in no way sufficed to designate what the alchemists had in mind when they spoke of Mercurius. It was certainly quicksilver, but a very special quicksilver, “our” Mercurius, the essence, moisture, or principle behind or within the quicksilver—that indefinable, fascinating, irritating, and elusive thing which attracts an unconscious projection. The “philosophic” Mercurius, this servus fugitivus or cervus fugitivus (fugitive slave or stag), is a highly important unconscious content which, as may be gathered from the few hints we have given, threatens to ramify into a set of far-reaching psychological problems.
