The concept swells dangerously and we begin to perceive that the end is nowhere in sight. Therefore we would rather not tie this concept prematurely to any special meaning, but shall content ourselves with stating that the philosophic Mercurius, so dear to the alchemist as the transformative substance, is obviously a projection of the unconscious, such as always takes place when the inquiring mind lacks the necessary self-criticism in investigating an unknown quantity.
[259] 如果墨丘利乌斯仅仅被理解为水银，显然就没有必要列出我所列举的任何名称。这一需求的出现指向以下结论：一个简单而明确的术语绝不足以指称炼金术士谈论墨丘利乌斯时所想到的东西。它当然是水银，但是一种非常特殊的水银，"我们的"墨丘利乌斯——水银背后或其中的本质、湿气或原则——那个不可定义的、迷人的、恼人的和难以捉摸的东西，它吸引着无意识的投射。"哲学的"墨丘利乌斯——这个逃亡的奴仆或逃亡的鹿（servus fugitivus 或 cervus fugitivus）——是一个极为重要的无意识内含物，如从我们已给出的几条线索可以推知的，它威胁着分支为一系列深远的心理学问题。这一概念危险地膨胀，我们开始察觉终点遥不可及。因此我们不愿过早将这一概念绑定于任何特殊含义，而满足于以下陈述：炼金术士作为转化物质所钟爱的哲学墨丘利乌斯，显然是一种无意识的投射——每当探究的心智在调查未知量时缺乏必要的自我批评，这种投射就会发生。

[260] As has already been indicated, the psychic nature of the arcane substance did not escape the alchemists; indeed, they actually defined it as “spirit” and “soul.” But since these concepts—especially in earlier times—were always ambiguous, we must approach them with caution if we want to gain a moderately clear idea of what the terms spiritus and anima meant in alchemical usage.
[260] 如前所述，秘术物质的心理本性并未逃过炼金术士；他们实际上将其定义为"精神"和"灵魂"。但由于这些概念——特别是在早期——总是含糊的，如果我们想对 spiritus 和 anima 在炼金术用法中意味着什么获得一个适度清晰的概念，就必须谨慎对待它们。





A. MERCURIUS AS AN AERIAL SPIRIT
A. 作为气之灵的墨丘利乌斯


[261] Hermes, originally a wind god, and his counterpart the Egyptian Thoth, who “makes the souls to breathe,”1 are the forerunners of the alchemical Mercurius in his aerial aspect. The texts often use the terms pneuma and spiritus in the original concrete sense of “air in motion.” So when Mercurius is described in the Rosarium philosophorum (fifteenth century) as aereus and volans2 (winged), and in Hoghelande (sixteenth century) as totus aereus et spiritualis,3 what is meant is nothing more than a gaseous state of aggregation. Something similar is meant by the poetic expression serenitas aerea in the Ripley Scrowle,4 and by the same author’s statement that Mercurius is changed into wind.5 He is the lapis elevatus cum vento (the stone uplifted by the wind).6 The expressions spirituale corpus7 and spiritus visibilis, tamen impalpabilis8 (visible yet impalpable spirit) might also mean little more than “air” if one recalls the aforementioned vapour-like nature of Mercurius, and the same is probably true even of the spiritus prae cunctis valde purus9 (pre-eminently pure spirit). The designation incombustibilis10 is more doubtful, since this was often synonymous with incorruptibilis and then meant “eternal,” as we shall see later. Penotus (sixteenth century), a pupil of Paracelsus, stresses the corporeal aspect when he says that Mercurius is “nothing other than the spirit of the world become body within the earth.”11 This expression shows better than anything else the contamination—inconceivable to the modern mind—of two separate realms, spirit and matter; for to people in the Middle Ages the spiritus mundi was also the spirit which rules nature, and not just a pervasive gas. We find ourselves in the same dilemma when another author, Mylius, in his Philosophia reformata,12 describes Mercurius as an “intermediate substance” (media substantia), which is evidently synonymous with his concept of the anima media natura13 (soul as intermediate nature), for to him Mercurius was the “spirit and soul of the bodies.”14
[261] 赫尔墨斯——最初是风神——及其对应者埃及的托特——"使灵魂呼吸者"，1 是炼金术墨丘利乌斯在气态方面的前驱。文献常在"运动的空气"这一原始具体意义上使用 pneuma 和 spiritus 二词。因此当墨丘利乌斯在《哲学家玫瑰园》（十五世纪）中被描述为 aereus 和 volans2（有翼的），在霍赫兰德（十六世纪）中被描述为 totus aereus et spiritualis3 时，所意味的不过是一种气态的聚集状态。里普利卷轴中的诗意表达 serenitas aerea4 以及同一作者所说的墨丘利乌斯变为风5 也有类似含义。他是被风举起之石（lapis elevatus cum vento）。6 精神之体（spirituale corpus7）和可见却不可触之灵（spiritus visibilis, taman impalpabilis8）如果回忆前述墨丘利乌斯的蒸气般本性，也许也不过意味着"空气"，极纯之灵（spiritus prae cunctis valde purus9）大概也是如此。不可燃（incombustibilis10）一词则较为可疑，因为它常与不可腐朽（incorruptibilis）同义，那时意味着"永恒"——如我们后将看到的。帕拉塞尔苏斯的学生佩诺图斯（十六世纪）强调其身体面向说墨丘利乌斯"不外乎是世界之灵在大地中成为身体"。11 这一表达比任何其他都更好地展示了对现代心智不可想象的两个分离领域——精神和物质——的污染；因为对中世纪的人来说，世界之灵也是统治自然之灵，不仅仅是一种弥漫的气体。当另一位作者米利乌斯在其《改革哲学》12 中将墨丘利乌斯描述为"中间物质"（media substantia）时——这显然与他的作为中间自然之灵魂（anima media natura13）的概念同义——我们发现自己处于同样的困境，因为对他来说墨丘利乌斯是"身体的精神与灵魂"。14





B. MERCURIUS AS SOUL
B. 作为灵魂的墨丘利乌斯


[262] “Soul” represents a higher concept than “spirit” in the sense of air or gas. As the “subtle body” or “breath-soul” it means something non-material and finer than mere air. Its essential characteristic is to animate and be animated; it therefore represents the life principle. Mercurius is often designated as anima (hence, as a feminine being, he is also called foemina or virgo), or as nostra anima.15 The nostra here does not mean “our own” soul but, as in aqua nostra, Mercurius noster, corpus nostrum, refers to the arcane substance.
[262] "灵魂"在空气或气体的"精神"意义上代表一个更高的概念。作为"微细体"或"气息灵魂"，它意味着非物质的、比单纯空气更精细的东西。其本质特征是赋予生命和被赋予生命；因此它代表生命原则。墨丘利乌斯常被指定为 anima（因此，作为女性 beings，他也被称为 foemina 或 virgo），或 nostra anima。15 这里的 nostra 不是指"我们自己的"灵魂，而是如 aqua nostra、Mercurius noster、corpus nostrum 中一样，指秘术物质。

[263] However, anima often appears to be connected with spiritus, or is equated with it.16 For the spirit shares the living quality of the soul, and for this reason Mercurius is often called the spiritus vegetativus17 (spirit of life) or spiritus seminalis.18 A peculiar appellation is found in that seventeenth-century forgery which purports to be the secret book of Abraham le Juif, mentioned by Nicolas Flamel (fourteenth century). The epithet is spiritus Phytonis (from ϕὐω, ‘to procreate,’ ϕυτόν, ‘creature,’ ϕὐτωρ, ‘procreator,’ and Python, the Delphic serpent), and is accompanied by the serpent sign: Ω,19 Very much more material is the definition of Mercurius as a “life-giving power like a glue, holding the world together and standing in the middle between body and spirit.”20 This concept corresponds to Mylius’ definition of Mercurius as the anima media natura. From here it is but a step to the identification of Mercurius with the anima mundi,21 which is how Avicenna had defined him very much earlier (twelfth to thirteenth century). “He is the spirit of the Lord which fills the whole world and in the beginning swam upon the waters. They call him also the spirit of Truth, which is hidden from the world.”22 Another text says that Mercurius is the “supracelestial spirit which is conjoined with the light, and rightly could be called the anima mundi.”23 It is clear from a number of texts that the alchemists related their concept of the anima mundi on the one hand to the world soul in Plato’s Timaeus and on the other to the Holy Spirit, who was present at the Creation and played the role of procreator (ϕὐτωρ), impregnating the waters with the seed of life just as, later, he played a similar role in the obumbratio (overshadowing) of Mary.24 Elsewhere we read that a “life-force dwells in Mercurius non vulgaris, who flies like solid white snow. This is a spirit of the macrocosmic as of the microcosmic world, upon whom, after the anima rationalis, the motion and fluidity of human nature itself depends.”25 The snow represents the purified Mercurius in the state of albedo (= spirituality); here again matter and spirit are identical. Worth noting is the duality of soul caused by the presence of Mercurius: on the one hand the immortal anima rationalis given by God to man, which distinguishes him from animals; on the other hand the mercurial life-soul, which to all appearances is connected with the inflatio or inspiratio of the Holy Spirit. This fundamental duality forms the psychological basis of the two sources of illumination.
[263] 然而，anima 常与 spiritus 相连或被等同。16 因为精神分享灵魂的活性品质，正因如此墨丘利乌斯常被称为生命之灵（spiritus vegetativus17）或种子之灵（spiritus seminalis18）。一个特别的称谓见于那部据称是尼古拉·弗拉梅尔（十四世纪）所提到的犹太人亚伯拉罕秘书的十七世纪伪书中。该称谓是 spiritus Phytonis（源自 ϕὐω，'生殖'，ϕυτόν，'造物'，ϕὐτωρ，'生殖者'，以及 Python，德尔斐蛇），并伴有蛇的符号：Ω，19 更为物质化的是将墨丘利乌斯定义为"一种赋予生命的力量，如胶水般将世界粘合在一起，立于身体与精神之间"。20 这一概念对应于米利乌斯将墨丘利乌斯定义为作为中间自然之灵魂（anima media natura）。从这里到将墨丘利乌斯等同于世界灵魂（anima mundi）21 仅一步之遥——阿维森纳在更早的时候（十二至十三世纪）就是这样定义他的。22"他是主之灵，充满全世，在太初浮于水面之上。他们也称之为真理之灵，隐藏于世。"23 另一篇文献说墨丘利乌斯是"与光结合的超天体之灵，可以正当地称为世界灵魂"。24 从一些文献中可以清楚看到，炼金术士一方面将他们的世界灵魂概念与柏拉图《蒂迈欧篇》中的世界灵魂相联系，另一方面与圣灵相联系——圣灵在创世时在场并扮演生殖者（ϕὐτωρ）的角色，以生命之种使水受孕，正如后来他在玛利亚的遮蔽（obumbratio）中扮演类似角色。25 在别处我们读到"一种生命力寓于非凡的墨丘利乌斯（Mercurius non vulgaris）中，他如固态白雪般飞舞。这是大宇宙也是微宇宙之灵，人类的运动和流动性本身在理性灵魂（anima rationalis）之后依赖于他。"26 雪代表在白化状态（＝灵性化）下被净化的墨丘利乌斯；这里物质与精神再次同一。值得注意的是墨丘利乌斯的存在所导致的灵魂二重性：一方面是上帝赋予人的不朽的理性灵魂，它使人区别于动物；另一方面是水银生命之灵——它看起来与圣灵的吹入或默感相连。这一根本二重性构成了两种照明之源的心理学基础。





C. MERCURIUS AS SPIRIT IN THE INCORPOREAL, METAPHYSICAL SENSE
C. 作为非物质、形而上学之灵的墨丘利乌斯


[264] In many of the passages it remains doubtful whether spiritus means spirit in an abstract sense.20 It is moderately certain that this is so in Dorn, for he says that “Mercurius possesses the quality of an incorruptible spirit, which is like the soul, and because of its incorruptibility is called intellectual”27—i.e., pertaining to the mundus intelligibilis. One text expressly calls him “spiritual and hyperphysical,”28 and another says that the spirit of Mercurius comes from heaven.29 Laurentius Ventura (sixteenth century) may well have been associating himself with the “Platonis liber quartorum” and hence with the neo-Platonist ideas of the Harranite school when he defined the spirit of Mercurius as “completely and entirely like itself” (sibi omnino similis) and simplex,30 for this Harranite text defines the arcane substance as the res simplex and equates it with God.31
[264] 在许多段落中，spiritus 是否在抽象意义上指精神仍然可疑。20 可以适度确定的是多恩，因为他说"墨丘利乌斯具有不可腐朽之灵的品质，它如灵魂，因其不可腐朽性被称为理智的"27——即属于可知世界（mundus intelligibilis）。一篇文献明确称他为"灵性的和超物理的"，28 另一篇说墨丘利乌斯之灵来自天上。29 劳伦提乌斯·文图拉（十六世纪）很可能与《柏拉图第四书》并因此与哈兰学派的新柏拉图主义思想相关联，他将墨丘利乌斯之灵定义为"完全与自身相似"（sibi omnino similis）和单纯的（simplex），30 因为这部哈兰文献将秘术物质定义为单纯之物（res simplex）并将其等同于上帝。31

[265] The oldest reference to the mercurial pneuma occurs in an Ostanes quotation of considerable antiquity (possibly pre-Christian), which says: “Go to the streamings of the Nile, and there you will find a stone that has a spirit.”32 In Zosimos Mercurius is characterized as incorporeal (ἀσὠματον),33 and by another author as ethereal (αἰϑερῶδες πνεῡμα) and as having become rational or wise (σὠϕρων γενομἐνη).34 In the very old treatise “Isis to Horus” (first century) the divine water is brought by an angel and is clearly of celestial or possibly daemonic origin, since according to the text the angel Amnael who brings it is not a morally irreproachable figure.35 For the alchemists, as we know not only from the ancient but also from the later writers, Mercurius as the arcane substance had a more or less secret connection with the goddess of love. In the “Book of Krates,” which was transmitted by the Arabs and is possibly of Alexandrian origin, Aphrodite appears with a vessel from the mouth of which pours a ceaseless stream of quicksilver,36 and in the Chymical Wedding of Christian Rosencreutz the central mystery is his visit to the secret chamber of the sleeping Venus.
[265] 关于水银之灵的最古老参考见于一段相当古老（可能为前基督教时代）的奥斯塔内斯引文："去尼罗河的流泻处，在那里你会发现一块有灵的石头。"32 在佐西莫斯那里，墨丘利乌斯被特征为无形的（ἀσώματον），33 被另一位作者特征为以太的（αἰϑερῶδες πνεῡμα）和已成为理性的或智慧的（σώϕρων γενομένη）。34 在非常古老的论著《伊西斯致荷鲁斯》（一世纪）中，神圣之水由一位天使带来，显然具有天上或可能魔鬼的起源，因为根据文本，带来它的天使阿姆纳尔并非一个道德上无可指摘的人物。35 如我们从古代和后来的作者所知，对炼金术士来说，墨丘利乌斯作为秘术物质与爱神有着或多或少秘密的联系。在由阿拉伯人传佅、可能源自亚历山大城的《克拉特斯之书》中，阿芙洛狄忒手持一个器皿，从其口中不断流出水银，36 而在克里斯蒂安·罗森克鲁茨的《化学婚礼》中，核心奥秘是他探访沉睡的维纳斯的密室。

[266] The fact that Mercurius is interpreted as spirit and soul, in spite of the spirit-body dilemma which this involves, indicates that the alchemists themselves conceived of their arcane substance as something that we today would call a psychic phenomenon. Indeed, whatever else spirit and soul may be, from the phenomenological point of view they are psychic structures. The alchemists never tired of drawing attention to the psychic nature of Mercurius. So far we have concerned ourselves with, statistically, the commonest synonyms such as water and fire, spirit and soul, and it is now possible for us to conclude that these exemplify a psychological state of affairs best characterized by (or, indeed, actually demanding) an antinomian nomenclature. Water and fire are classic opposites and can be valid definitions of one and the same thing only if this thing unites in itself the contrary qualities of water and fire. The psychologem “Mercurius” must therefore possess an essentially antinomian dual nature.
[266] 墨丘利乌斯被解释为精神和灵魂这一事实——尽管这涉及精神-身体的二律背反——表明炼金术士自己将他们的秘术物质设想为我们今天称之为心理现象的东西。事实上，无论精神和灵魂还是什么，从现象学角度看，它们是心理结构。炼金术士不厌其烦地提请注意墨丘利乌斯的心理本性。到目前为止我们关注的是统计上最常见的同义词，如水和火、精神和灵魂，现在我们可以得出结论：这些例证了一种最好由二律背反的命名法来特征化的（或者实际上要求它的）心理状况。水和火是经典的对立面，只有在统一了水和火的相反品质的事物中才能成为同一事物的有效定义。因此，"墨丘利乌斯"这一心理学母题必然具有一种本质上的二律背反的双重本性。





5. THE DUAL NATURE OF MERCURIUS
5. 墨丘利乌斯的双重本性


[267] Mercurius, following the tradition of Hermes, is many-sided, changeable, and deceitful. Dorn speaks of “that inconstant Mercurius,”1 and another calls him versipellis (changing his skin, shifty).2 He is duplex3 and his main characteristic is duplicity. It is said of him that he “runs round the earth and enjoys equally the company of the good and the wicked.”4 He is “two dragons,”5 the “twin,”6 made of “two natures”7 or “two substances.”8 He is the “giant of twofold substance,” in explanation of which the text9 cites the twenty-sixth chapter of Matthew, where the sacrament of the Last Supper is instituted. The Christ analogy is thus made plain. The two substances of Mercurius are thought of as dissimilar, sometimes opposed; as the dragon he is “winged and wingless.”10 A parable says: “On this mountain lies an ever-waking dragon, who is called Pantophthalmos, for he is covered with eyes on both sides of his body, before and behind, and he sleeps with some open and some closed.”11 There is the “common and the philosophic” Mercurius;12 he consists of “the dry and earthy, the moist and viscous.”13 Two of his elements are passive, earth and water, and two active, air and fire.14 He is both good and evil.15 The “Aurelia occulta” gives a graphic description of him:16
[267] 墨丘利乌斯承袭赫尔墨斯的传统，是多面的、多变的、欺骗的。多恩谈到"那无常的墨丘利乌斯"，1 另一位称他为 versipellis（变皮的，狡猾的）。2 他是双重的（duplex）3，其主要特征是二重性。据说他"环绕大地奔跑，同样乐于与善人和恶人交往"。4 他是"两条龙"，5 是"孪生者"，6 由"两种本性"7 或"两种物质"8 组成。他是"双物质之巨人"——为解释这一点，文献9 引用了《马太福音》第二十六章，即设立圣餐圣事之处。基督类比由此变得明显。墨丘利乌斯的两种物质被认为是不相似的，有时是对立的；作为龙，他是"有翼和无翼的"。10 一个寓言说："在这座山上躺着一条永不沉睡的龙，他被称为 Pantophthalmos（全眼者），因为他身体前后两侧都布满了眼睛，他睡觉时一些睁开一些闭上。"11 有"普通的"和"哲学的"墨丘利乌斯；12 他由"干与土、湿与黏"组成。13 他的元素中两个是被动的——土和水，两个是主动的——气与火。14 他既是善的也是恶的。15《奥雷利亚隐秘》对他做了生动的描述：16

I am the poison-dripping dragon, who is everywhere and can be cheaply had. That upon which I rest, and that which rests upon me, will be found within me by those who pursue their investigations in accordance with the rules of the Art. My water and fire destroy and put together; from my body you may extract the green lion and the red. But if you do not have exact knowledge of me, you will destroy your five senses with my fire. From my snout there comes a spreading poison that has brought death to many. Therefore you should skilfully separate the coarse from the fine, if you do not wish to suffer utter poverty. I bestow on you the powers of the male and the female, and also those of heaven and of earth. The mysteries of my art must be handled with courage and greatness of mind if you would conquer me by the power17 of fire, for already very many have come to grief, their riches and labour lost. I am the egg of nature, known only to the wise, who in piety and modesty bring forth from me the microcosm, which was prepared for mankind by Almighty God, but given only to the few, while the many long for it in vain, that they may do good to the poor with my treasure and not fasten their souls to the perishable gold. By the philosophers I am named Mercurius; my spouse is the [philosophic] gold; I am the old dragon, found everywhere on the globe of the earth, father and mother, young and old, very strong and very weak, death and resurrection, visible and invisible, hard and soft; I descend into the earth and ascend to the heavens, I am the highest and the lowest, the lightest and the heaviest; often the order of nature is reversed in me, as regards colour, number, weight, and measure; I contain the light of nature; I am dark and light; I come forth from heaven and earth; I am known and yet do not exist at all;18 by virtue of the sun’s rays all colours shine in me, and all metals. I am the carbuncle of the sun, the most noble purified earth, through which you may change copper, iron, tin, and lead into gold.
我是那滴毒的龙，无处不在且廉价可得。我所依凭的以及依凭我的，将在那些按照艺术规则进行研究的人那里被发现于我之中。我的水和火毁灭又结合；从我的身体中你可以提取绿狮和红狮。但如果你对我的确切知识不够，你将用我的火毁掉你的五种感官。从我的吻中流出一种蔓延的毒物，已致多人死亡。因此你应巧妙地将粗的从细的中分离，如果你不想遭受赤贫。我赋予你男与女的力量，以及天与地的力量。我的艺术的奥秘必须以勇气和宏大之心来处理，如果你想以火之力17 征服我，因为已有许多人在此遭殃，失去了他们的财富和劳动。我是自然之卵，只有智者知道，他们以虔诚和谦逊从我身上产出微宇宙——这是全能上帝为人类准备的，但只赐予少数人，而多数人徒然渴望，以便他们可以用我的宝藏行善于贫者，而非将他们的灵魂绑在易腐的金上。哲学家们称我为墨丘利乌斯；我的配偶是〔哲学的〕金；我是老龙，在地球的各处被发现，父与母、幼与老、极强与极弱、死亡与复活、可见与不可见、硬与软；我降至大地又升上诸天，我是最高与最低、最轻与最重；颜色、数字、重量和度量之秩序在我中时常颠倒；我含自然之光；我是暗与明；我从天与地而出；我为人所知却全然不存在；18 凭太阳之光芒，一切颜色在我中闪耀，一切金属亦然。我是太阳之红宝石，最高贵的净化之土，通过它你可以将铜、铁、锡和铅变为金。

[268] Because of his united double nature Mercurius is described as hermaphroditic. Sometimes his body is said to be masculine and his soul feminine, sometimes the reverse. The Rosarium philosophorum, for example, has both versions.19 As vulgaris he is the dead masculine body, but as “our” Mercurius he is feminine, spiritual, alive and life-giving.20 He is also called husband and wife,21 bridegroom and bride, or lover and beloved.22 His contrary natures are often called Mercurius sensu strictiori and sulphur, the former being feminine, earth, and Eve, and the latter masculine, water, and Adam.23 In Dorn he is the “true hermaphroditic Adam,”24 and in Khunrath he is “begotten of the hermaphroditic seed of the Macrocosm” as “an immaculate birth from the hermaphroditic matter” (i.e., the prima materia).25 Mylius calls him the “hermaphroditic monster.”26 As Adam he is also the microcosm, or even “the heart of the microcosm,”27 or he has the microcosm “in himself, where are also the four elements and the quinta essentia which they call Heaven.”28 The term coelum for Mercurius does not, as one might think, derive from the firmamentum of Paracelsus, but occurs earlier in Johannes de Rupescissa (fourteenth century).29 The term homo is used as a synonym for “microcosm,” as when Mercurius is named the “Philosophic ambisexual Man.”30 In the very old “Dicta Belini” (Belinus or Balinus is a corruption of Apollonius of Tyana), he is the “man rising from the river,”31 probably a reference to the vision of Ezra.32 In Trismosin’s Splendor solis (sixteenth century) there is an illustration of this.33 The idea itself may go back to the Babylonian teacher of wisdom, Oannes. The designation of Mercurius as the “high man”34 does not fit in badly with such a pedigree. The terms Adam and microcosm occur frequently in the texts,35 but the Abraham le Juif forgery unblushingly calls Mercurius Adam Kadmon.36 As I have discussed this unmistakable continuation of the Gnostic doctrine of the Anthropos elsewhere,37 there is no need for me to go more closely now into this aspect of Mercurius.38 Nevertheless, I would like to emphasize once again that the Anthropos idea coincides with the psychological concept of the self. The atman and purusha doctrine as well as alchemy give clear proofs of this.
[268] 由于墨丘利乌斯统一的双重本性，他被描述为雌雄同体的。有时据说他的身体是男性的而他的灵魂是女性的，有时则相反。《哲学家玫瑰园》中两个版本都有。19 作为 vulgaris（普通的），他是死的男性身体；但作为"我们的"墨丘利乌斯，他是女性的、灵性的、活的、赋予生命的。20 他也被称为夫与妻，21 新郎与新娘，或爱者与被爱者。22 他的相反本性常被称为狭义的墨丘利乌斯（Mercurius sensu strictiori）和硫磺，前者是女性的、地、夏娃，后者是男性的、水、亚当。23 在多恩那里，他是"真正的雌雄同体的亚当"，24 在库恩拉特那里，他是"由大宇宙之雌雄同体的种子所生"，是"从雌雄同体的物质"（即原初物质）"中的无瑕出生"。25 米利乌斯称他为"雌雄同体的怪物"。26 作为亚当，他也是微宇宙，甚至是"微宇宙之心"，27 或者他"自身中包含微宇宙，其中也有四元素和他们称之为天的第五精华"。28 墨丘利乌斯的 coelum（天）一词并非如人们所想源自帕拉塞尔苏斯的 firmamentum，而是更早见于约翰内斯·德·鲁佩西萨（十四世纪）。29 homo（人）一词作为"微宇宙"的同义词使用，如墨丘利乌斯被称为"哲学的双性人"。30 在非常古老的《贝利努斯之言》（贝利努斯或巴利努斯是提亚纳的阿波罗尼乌斯之讹）中，他是"从河中升起之人"，31 可能暗指以斯拉的异象。32 在特里斯莫辛的《太阳之光》（十六世纪）中有一幅此图像的插图。33 这一思想本身可以追溯到巴比伦的智慧教师奥安内斯。将墨丘利乌斯称为"高人"34 与这样的谱系并非不配。亚当和微宇宙二词在文献中频繁出现，35 但《犹太人亚伯拉罕》伪书厚颜无耻地将墨丘利乌斯称为亚当·卡德蒙。36 由于我已在别处讨论过这一诺斯替原人教义的不言而喻的延续，37 现在无需更深入探讨墨丘利乌斯的这一方面。38 尽管如此，我想再次强调，原人思想与自性的心理学概念相吻合。阿特曼和普鲁沙教义以及炼金术都提供了明确的证据。

[269] Another aspect of the dual nature of Mercurius is his characterization as senex39 and puer.40 The figure of Hermes as an old man, attested by archaeology, brings him into direct relation with Saturn—a relationship which plays a considerable role in alchemy (see infra, pars. 274ff.). Mercurius truly consists of the most extreme opposites; on the one hand he is undoubtedly akin to the godhead, on the other he is found in sewers. Rosinus (Zosimos) even calls him the terminus ani.41 In the Bundahish,42 the anus of Garotman is “like hell on earth.”
[269] 墨丘利乌斯双重本性的另一面是他被特征为老者（senex）39 和少年（puer）。40 赫尔墨斯作为老人的形象——已由考古学证实——使他直接与土星相关——这一关系在炼金术中扮演着重要角色（见下文第274段以下）。墨丘利乌斯确实由最极端的对立面组成；一方面他无疑与神性亲近，另一方面他在下水道中被发现。罗西努斯（佐西莫斯）甚至称他为 terminus ani（肛门之端）。41 在《班达希什》中，42 加罗特曼的肛门"如同地上的地狱"。





6. THE UNITY AND TRINITY OF MERCURIUS
6. 墨丘利乌斯的统一性与三元性


[270] In spite of his obvious duality the unity of Mercurius is also emphasized, especially in his form as the lapis. “In all the world he is One.”1 The unity of Mercurius is at the same time a trinity, with clear reference to the Holy Trinity, although his triadic nature does not derive from Christian dogma but is of earlier date. Triads occur as early as the treatise of Zosimos, περì ἀρετῆς (Concerning the Art).2 Martial calls Hermes omnia solus el ter unus (All and Thrice One).3 In Monakris (Arcadia), a three-headed Hermes was worshipped, and in Gaul there was a three-headed Mercurius.4 This Gallic god was also a psychopomp. The triadic character is an attribute of the gods of the underworld, as for instance the three-bodied Typhon, three-bodied and three-faced Hecate,5 and the “ancestors” (τριτοπάτορες) with their serpent bodies. According to Cicero,6 these latter are the three sons of Zeus the King, the rex antiquissimus.7 They are called the “forefathers” and are wind-gods;8 obviously by the same logic the Hopi Indians believe that snakes are at the same time flashes of lightning auguring rain. Khunrath calls Mercurius triunus9 and ternarius.10 Mylius represents him as a three-headed snake.11 The “Aquarium sapientum” says that he is a “triune, universal essence which is named Jehova.12 He is divine and at the same time human.”13
[270] 尽管墨丘利乌斯有明显的二元性，他的统一性也被强调，尤其是在他作为石头的形态中。"在整个世界中他是一。"1 墨丘利乌斯的统一性同时是三元性，明确指向神圣三一，尽管他的三重本性并非源自基督教教义，而是更早。三元组合早在佐西莫斯的论著 περì ἀρετῆς（《论技艺》）中就出现了。2 马尔提亚利斯称赫尔墨斯为 omnia solus et ter unus（万有与三一者）。3 在莫纳克里斯（阿卡迪亚），一尊三头赫尔墨斯被崇拜，在高卢有一尊三头墨丘利乌斯。4 这位高卢神也是引魂者。三重性是冥界之神的属性，例如三体堤丰、三体三面赫卡忒，5 以及蛇身的"先祖"（τριτοπάτορες）。据西塞罗，6 后者是宙斯王——最古老之王（rex antiquissimus）7——的三个儿子。他们被称为"先祖"，是风之神；8 显然出于同样的逻辑，霍皮印第安人相信蛇同时也是预告雨水的闪电。库恩拉特称墨丘利乌斯为三位一体（triunus）9 和三重的（ternarius）。10 米利乌斯将他表现为三头蛇。11《智慧水族馆》说他是"名为耶和华的三重普遍本质。12 他是神圣的同时也是人的。"13

[271] From all this one must conclude that Mercurius corresponds not only to Christ, but to the triune divinity in general. The “Aurelia occulta” calls him “Azoth,” and explains the term as follows: “For he is the A and O that is everywhere present. The philosophers have adorned [him] with the name Azoth, which is compounded of the A and Z of the Latins, the alpha and omega of the Greeks, and the aleph and tau of the Hebrews:
[271] 从这一切必须得出结论：墨丘利乌斯不仅对应于基督，而且对应于一般的三一神性。《奥雷利亚隐秘》称他为"Azoth"，并解释如下："因为他是处处临在的 A 和 O。哲学家们以 Azoth 之名装饰他，该名由拉丁人的 A 和 Z、希腊人的 alpha 和 omega、希伯来人的 aleph 和 tau 组成：



The parallel with the Trinity could not be more clearly indicated. The anonymous commentator of the “Tractatus aureus” puts the parallel with Christ as Logos just as unmistakably. All things proceed from the “philosophic heaven adorned with an infinite multitude of stars,”15 from the creative Word incarnate, the Johannine Logos, without which “was not any thing made that was made.” The commentator says: “Thus the Word of renewal is invisibly inherent in all things, but it is not evident in elementary solid bodies unless they have been brought back to the fifth, or heavenly and astral essence. Hence this Word of renewal is the seed of promise, or the philosophic heaven refulgent with the infinite lights of the stars.”16 Mercurius is the Logos become world. The description given here may point to his basic identity with the collective unconscious, for as I tried to show in my essay “On the Nature of the Psyche,”17 the image of the starry heaven seems to be a visualization of the peculiar nature of the unconscious. Since Mercurius is often called filius, his sonship is beyond question.18 He is therefore like a brother to Christ and a second son of God, though in point of time he must be accounted the elder and the first-born. This idea goes back to the conceptions of the Euchites reported in Michael Psellus,19 who believed that God’s first son was Satanaël20 and that Christ was the second.21 However, Mercurius is not only the counterpart of Christ in so far as he is the “son”; he is also the counterpart of the Trinity as a whole in so far as he is conceived to be a chthonic triad. According to this view he would be equal to one half of the Christian Godhead. He is indeed the dark chthonic half, but he is not simply evil as such, for he is called “good and evil,” or a “system of the higher powers in the lower.” He calls to mind that double figure which seems to stand behind both Christ and the devil—that enigmatic Lucifer whose attributes are shared by both. In Rev. 22 : 16 Christ says of himself: “I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright and the morning star.”
与三一的平行关系不可能更清楚地被指示了。《金色论著》的匿名注释者同样明确地提出了与基督作为逻各斯的平行关系。万物从"点缀着无限星群的哲学之天"15，从创世之道的道成肉身——约翰逻各斯——而出，"没有它就没有任何被造之物被造"。注释者说："因此更新之道不可见地内在于万物，但在元素性的坚固之体中并不显现，除非它们被带回第五精华，即天上的和星辰的本质。因此这更新之道是应许之种，或闪烁着无限星光的哲学之天。"16 墨丘利乌斯是成为世界的逻各斯。这里给出的描述可能指向他与集体无意识的基本同一性，因为如我在《论心灵的本性》一文中所试图表明的，17 星空的形象似乎是无意识特有本性的可视化。由于墨丘利乌斯常被称为子，他的子性是无疑的。18 因此他如同基督的兄弟，是上帝的第二个儿子——尽管从时间上看他应被视为长子。这一思想追溯到迈克尔·普塞洛斯所记载的犹各派的概念，19 他们相信上帝的长子是撒坦那伊尔（Satanaël）20，而基督是第二个。21 然而，墨丘利乌斯不仅是作为"子"的基督的对应面；他作为冥界三元也被构想为整个三一的对应面。根据这一观点，他将等于基督教神格的一半。他确实是黑暗的冥界一半，但他并非简单地就是恶的，因为他被称为"善与恶"，或"高能于低"。他让人想起那个似乎站在基督和魔鬼背后的双重形象——那神秘的卢奇菲尔，其属性为二者所共有。在《启示录》22:16中基督说到自己："我是大卫的根和后裔，是明亮的晨星。"

[272] One peculiarity of Mercurius which undoubtedly relates him to the Godhead and to the primitive creator god is his ability to beget himself. In the “Allegoriae super librum Turbae” he says: “The mother bore me and is herself begotten of me.”22 As the uroboros dragon, he impregnates, begets, bears, devours, and slays himself, and “himself lifts himself on high,” as the Rosarium says,23 so paraphrasing the mystery of God’s sacrificial death. Here, as in many similar instances, it would be rash to assume that the alchemists were as conscious of their reasoning processes as perhaps we are. But man, and through him the unconscious, expresses a great deal that is not necessarily conscious in all its implications. Nevertheless I should like to avoid giving the impression that the alchemists were absolutely unconscious of their thought-processes. How little this was so is proved by the above quotations. But although Mercurius, in many texts, is stated to be trinus et unus, this does not prevent him from sharing very strongly the quaternity of the lapis, with which he is essentially identical. He thus exemplifies that strange dilemma which is posed by the problem of three and four—the well-known axiom of Maria Prophetissa. There is a classical Hermes tetracephalus as well as the Hermes tricephalus.24 The ground-plan of the Sabaean temple of Mercurius was a triangle inside a square.25 In the scholia to the “Tractatus aureus” the sign for Mercurius is a square inside a triangle surrounded by a circle (symbol of totality).26
[272] 墨丘利乌斯的一个特性——无疑将他关联于神性和原始创世之神——是他自我生育的能力。在《集会之寓言》中他说："母亲生了我，她自己又由我所生。"22 作为衔尾蛇龙，他使自己受孕、生育、孕育、吞噬、杀死自己，并"自己将自己举起"——如《玫瑰园》所说，23 以此诠释上帝牺牲之死的奥秘。在这里，如同在许多类似的情况下，假定炼金术士对其推理过程如同我们一样有意识将是草率的。但人——以及通过人，无意识——表达了许多在其一切含义上并不必然是有意识的东西。然而，我不想给人留下炼金术士对其思维过程完全无意识的印象。上述引文证明了这远非如此。但尽管墨丘利乌斯在许多文献中被表述为三位一体（trinus et unus），这并不妨碍他强烈地分享与之本质上同一的哲学家之石的四元性。因此，他例证了三与四的问题——著名的玛丽亚先知公理——所提出的奇特困境。有四头赫尔墨斯也有三头赫尔墨斯。24 萨巴ean墨丘利乌斯神庙的平面图是一个正方形中的三角形。25 在《金色论著》的注释中，墨丘利乌斯的符号是一个三角形内的正方形，外被圆圈（整体性的象征）所环绕。26





7. THE RELATION OF MERCURIUS TO ASTROLOGY AND THE DOCTRINE OF THE ARCHONS
7. 墨丘利乌斯与星象学及执政官教义的关系


[273] One of the roots of the peculiar philosophy relating to Mercurius lies in ancient astrology and in the Gnostic doctrine of the archons and aeons, which is derived from it. Between Mercurius and the planet there is a relation of mystical identity due either to contamination or to an actual spiritual identity. In the first case quicksilver is simply the planet Mercury as it appears in the earth (just as gold is simply the sun in the earth);1 in the second, the “spirit” of quicksilver is identical with the planetary spirit. Both spirits individually, or the two as one spirit, were personified and called upon for aid or magically conjured into service as a paredros or “familiar.” Within the alchemical tradition we find directions for such procedures in the Harranite treatise “Clavis maioris sapientiae” of Artefius,2 which agree with descriptions of the invocations mentioned by Dozy and de Goeje.3 There are also references to procedures of this kind in the “Liber Platonis quartorum.”4 Parallel with this is the account according to which Democritus received the secret of the hieroglyphs from the genius of the planet Mercury.5 The spirit Mercurius appears here in the role of a mystagogue, as in the Corpus Hermeticum or the visions of Zosimos. He plays the same role in the remarkable dream-vision recorded in “Aurelia occulta,” where he appears as the Anthropos with a crown of stars.6 As the little star near the sun, he is the child of sun and moon.7 But contrariwise he is also the begetter of his parents;8 or, as the treatise of Wei Po-yang (c. A.D. 142) remarks, the gold (sun) gets its qualities from Mercurius.9 (Owing to the contamination, the astrological myth is always thought of in chemical terms as well.) Because of his half-feminine nature, Mercurius is often identified with the moon10 and Venus.11 As his own divine consort he easily turns into the goddess of love, just as in his role of Hermes he is ithyphallic. But he is also called the “most chaste virgin.”12 The relation of quicksilver to the moon (silver) is obvious enough. Mercurius as the shining and shimmering planet, appearing like Venus close to the sun in the morning or evening sky, is like her a Lucifer, a light-bringer (ϕωσϕóροζ). He heralds, as the morning star does, only much more directly, the coming of the light.
[273] 与墨丘利乌斯相关的奇特哲学的根源之一在于古代星象学和源出于它的诺斯替执政官与永世教义。墨丘利乌斯与行星之间存在着神秘同一性的关系——这是由于混淆或实际的精神同一性。在前一种情况下，水银就是行星水星在大地中的显现（正如金就是太阳在大地中的显现）；1 在后一种情况下，水银的"灵"与行星之灵同一。两个灵各自独立，或二者作为一个灵，被拟人化并被祈求帮助或被魔法咒为护持灵（paredros）或"护卫灵"。在炼金术传统中，我们在哈兰学派的阿尔特菲乌斯论著《大智慧之钥》中发现了此类程序的指引，2 与多齐和德·古耶所记载的祈请描述一致。3《柏拉图第四书》中也有对此类程序的提及。4 与此平行的是德谟克利特从水星精灵那里获得象形文字秘密的记载。5 墨丘利乌斯之灵在此以秘仪引导者的角色出现，如同在《赫尔墨斯文集》中或佐西莫斯的异象中。他在《奥雷利亚隐秘》所记录的非凡梦境异象中扮演同样的角色——他以戴着星辰王冠的原人之身出现。6 作为太阳旁边的小星，他是太阳与月亮之子。7 但反过来他也是其父母的生育者；8 或者如魏伯阳的论著（约公元142年）所说，金（太阳）的品质来自墨丘利乌斯。9（由于混淆，星象神话总是也以化学术语来思考。）由于其半女性的本性，墨丘利乌斯常被认同于月亮10 和维纳斯。11 作为他自己的神圣配偶，他容易变为爱神——正如他在赫尔墨斯的角色中是勃起的。但他也被称为"最贞洁的童贞女"。12 水银与月亮（银）的关系足够明显。墨丘利乌斯作为闪耀闪烁的行星——如同维纳斯般在晨昏天空出现在太阳附近——与她一样是一个卢奇菲尔，一个携光者（ϕωσϕόρος）。他如同晨星一般——但更为直接地——预告光的到来。

[274] But the most important of all for an interpretation of Mercurius is his relation to Saturn. Mercurius senex is identical with Saturn, and to the earlier alchemists especially, it is not quicksilver, but the lead associated with Saturn, which usually represents the prima materia. In the Arabic text of the Turba13 quicksilver is identical with the “water of the moon and of Saturn.” In the “Dicta Belini” Saturn says: “My spirit is the water that loosens the rigid limbs of my brothers.”14 This refers to the “eternal water” which is just what Mercurius is. Raymund Lully remarks that “a certain oil of a golden colour is extracted from the philosophic lead.”15 In Khunrath Mercurius is the “salt of Saturn,”16 or Saturn is simply Mercurius. Saturn “draws the eternal water.”17 Like Mercurius, Saturn is hermaphroditic.18 Saturn is “an old man on a mountain, and in him the natures are bound with their complement [i.e., the four elements], and all this is in Saturn.”19 The same is said of Mercurius. Saturn is the father and origin of Mercurius, therefore the latter is called “Saturn’s child.”20 Quicksilver comes “from the heart of Saturn or is Saturn,”21 and a “bright water” is extracted from the plant Saturnia, “the most perfect water and flower in the world.”22 This statement of Sir George Ripley, Canon of Bridlington, is a most remarkable parallel to the Gnostic teaching that Kronos (Saturn) is a “power of the colour of water” (ύδατóχρους) which destroys everything, since “water is destruction.”23
[274] 但对于诠释墨丘利乌斯而言最重要的，是他与土星的关系。墨丘利乌斯老者（Mercurius senex）与土星同一，对早期炼金术士来说尤其如此——通常代表原初物质的不是水银，而是与土星相关联的铅。在《集会》的阿拉伯文本中，13 水银与"月亮和土星之水"同一。在《贝利努斯之言》中土星说："我的灵是水，它松弛我兄弟们僵硬的肢体。"14 这指的是"永恒之水"——正是墨丘利乌斯。拉蒙·略勒说从哲学铅中提取出"一种金色的油"。15 在库恩拉特那里，墨丘利乌斯是"土星之盐"，16 或者土星就是墨丘利乌斯。土星"吸引永恒之水"。17 如同墨丘利乌斯，土星是雌雄同体的。18 土星是"山上的一位老人，在他之中各本性与其补充〔即四元素〕相绑定，这一切都在土星之中"。19 同样的说法也见于墨丘利乌斯。土星是墨丘利乌斯之父和起源，因此后者被称为"土星之子"。20 水银"来自土星之心或就是土星"，21 从土星植物中提取出"明亮之水"，"世界上最完美之水与花"。22 布里德灵顿座堂修士乔治·里普利的这一陈述，是诺斯替教义——克罗诺斯（土星）是一种"水色之力"（ύδατόχρους），它毁灭一切，因为"水即毁灭"23——的最非凡的平行。

[275] Like the planetary spirit of Mercurius, the spirit of Saturn is “very suited to this work.”24 One of the manifestations of Mercurius in the alchemical process of transformation is the lion, now green and now red. Khunrath calls this transformation “luring the lion out of Saturn’s mountain cave.” From ancient times the lion was associated with Saturn.25 Khunrath calls him “the lion of the Catholic tribe,”20 paraphrasing the “lion of the tribe of Judah”—an allegory of Christ.27 He calls Saturn “the lion green and red.”28 In Gnosticism Saturn is the highest archon, the lion-headed Ialdabaoth,29 meaning “child of chaos.” But in alchemy the child of chaos is Mercurius.30
[275] 如同墨丘利乌斯的行星之灵，土星之灵"非常适合这项工作"。24 墨丘利乌斯在炼金术转化过程中的显现之一是狮子——时而绿时而红。库恩拉特称这种转化为"将狮子从土星的山洞中引出"。自古以来狮子就与土星相关。25 库恩拉特称他为"天主教支派之狮"，26 诠释了"犹大支派之狮"——基督的寓言。27 他称土星为"绿与红的狮子"。28 在诺斯替教中，土星是最高的执政官——狮头伊阿尔达鲍斯，29 意为"混沌之子"。但在炼金术中，混沌之子是墨丘利乌斯。30

[276] The relation to and identity with Saturn is important because Saturn is not only a maleficus but actually the dwelling-place of the devil himself. Even as the highest archon and demiurge his Gnostic reputation was not the best. According to one Cabalistic source, Beelzebub was associated with him.31 Mylius says that if Mercurius were to be purified, then Lucifer would fall from heaven.32 A contemporary marginal note in a seventeenth-century treatise in my possession explains the term sulphur, the masculine principle of Mercurius,33 as diabolus. If Mercurius is not exactly the Evil One himself, he at least contains him—that is, he is morally neutral, good and evil, or as Khunrath says: “Good with the good, evil with the evil.”34 His nature is more exactly defined, however, if one conceives him as a process that begins with evil and ends with good. A rather deplorable but picturesque poem in Verus Hermes (1620) summarizes the process as follows:
[276] 与土星的关系和同一性很重要，因为土星不仅是一颗凶星，实际上是魔鬼本身的居所。即使作为最高的执政官和造物者，他在诺斯替教派中的名声也不是最好的。据一个卡巴拉来源说，别西卜与他相关。31 米利乌斯说如果墨丘利乌斯被净化，卢奇菲尔就会从天上坠落。32 我所收藏的一部十七世纪论著中一条同时代的页边注将硫磺——墨丘利乌斯的男性原则33——解释为 diabolus（魔鬼）。如果墨丘利乌斯不完全是恶者本身，他至少包含恶者——也就是说，他在道德上是中立的、善与恶兼有的，或者如库恩拉特所说："与善人善，与恶人恶。"34 然而，如果将他构想为一个始于恶终于善的过程，他的本性就被更确切地定义了。《真赫尔墨斯》（1620年）中一首相当拙劣但生动的诗总结了这一过程如下：



A weakling babe, a greybeard old,
弱婴一个，白髯老叟，

Surnamed the Dragon: me they hold
人称我为龙：

In darkest dungeon languishing
困于最深的地牢中

That I may be reborn a king.
以便重生为王。



A fiery sword makes me to smart,
火剑令我灼痛，

Death gnaws my flesh and bones apart.
死亡噬我骨肉。

My soul and spirit fast are sinking,
灵魂与精神沉沦，

And leave a poison, black and stinking.
留下黑臭毒物。



To a black crow am I akin,
我与黑鸦同族，

Such be the wages of all sin.
此即一切罪之报。

In deepest dust I lie alone,
独卧最深尘土，

O that the Three would make the One!
愿三者合为一！



O soul, O spirit with me stay,
灵魂啊，精神啊，与我同留，

That I may greet the light of day.
使我得见天光。

Hero of peace, come forth from me,
和平之英雄，从我而出，

Whom the whole world would like to see!
全世界都愿相见！

[277] In this poem Mercurius is describing his own transformation, which at the same time signifies the mystic transformation of the artifex; for not only Mercurius but also what happens to him is a projection of the collective unconscious. This, as can easily be seen from what has gone before, is the projection of the individuation process, which, being a natural psychic occurrence, goes on even without the participation of consciousness. But if consciousness participates with some measure of understanding, then the process is accompanied by all the emotions of a religious experience or revelation. As a result of this, Mercurius was identified with Sapientia and the Holy Ghost. It is therefore very probable that those heresies which began with the Euchites, Paulicians, Bogomils, and Cathars, and which developed the concept of the Paraclete very much in the spirit of the founder of Christianity, were continued in alchemy, partly unconsciously and partly under a deliberate disguise.35
[277] 在这首诗中，墨丘利乌斯描述的是自身的转化，这同时也意味着工匠的神秘转化；因为不仅是墨丘利乌斯，而且发生在他身上的事情也是集体无意识的投射。如从前文可以容易看出的，这是个体化过程的投射——作为一种自然心理事件，它即使没有意识的参与也在进行。但如果意识以一定程度的理解参与其中，那么这个过程就伴随着宗教经验或启示的一切情感。正因如此，墨丘利乌斯被认同于智慧（Sapientia）和圣灵。因此，那些始于犹各派、保罗派、鲍格米勒派和清洁派的异端——他们以基督教创始人的精神大大发展了保惠师的概念——很可能在炼金术中得到了延续，部分是无意识的，部分是有意伪装的。35





8. MERCURIUS AND HERMES
8. 墨丘利乌斯与赫尔墨斯


[278] We have already met with a number of alchemical statements which show plainly that the character of the classical Hermes was faithfully reproduced later in the figure of Mercurius. This is in part an unconscious repetition, in part a spontaneous re-experience, and finally also a conscious reference to the pagan god. There can be no doubt that Michael Maier was consciously alluding to Hermes as pointer of the way (óδηγóϛ) when he said that he found on his mystic peregrination a statue of Mercurius pointing the way to paradise,1 and that he was referring to Hermes the mystagogue when he made the Erythraean Sibyl say of Mercurius: “He will make you a witness of the mysteries of God and the secrets of nature.”2 Again, as the divinus ternarius, Mercurius is the revealer of divine secrets,3 or in the form of gold is conceived to be the soul of the arcane substance (magnesia),4 or the fructifier of the philosophical tree.5 In the “Epigramma Mercurio philosophico dicatum”6 he is called the messenger of the gods, the hermeneut (interpreter), and the Egyptian “Theutius” (Thoth). Maier even goes so far as to relate him to Hermes Kyllenios when he calls him “this faithless and all too elusive Arcadian youth,”7 for in Arcadia was the sanctuary of Kyllenios, the ithyphallic Hermes. In the scholia to the “Tractatus aureus” Mercurius is named outright the “Kyllenian hero.”8 Maier’s words might also be a reference to Eros. And in fact, in Rosencreutz’s Chymical Wedding, Mercurius does appear in the form of Cupid,9 and punishes the adept for his curiosity in visiting the Lady Venus by wounding him in the hand with an arrow. The arrow is the “dart of passion” (telum passionis), which is also an attribute of Mercurius.10 He is an “archer,” and indeed one who “shoots without a bowstring” and is “nowhere to be found on earth,”11 so is obviously a daemon. In the Table of Symbols in Penotus12 he is associated with nymphs, which reminds one of the pastoral god, Pan. His lasciviousness is borne out by an illustration in the Tripus chimicus of Sendivogius,13 where he appears on a triumphal chariot drawn by a cock and a hen, and behind him is a naked pair of embracing lovers. In this connection may also be mentioned the numerous somewhat obscene pictures of the coniunctio in old prints, often preserved merely as pornographica. Pictures in old manuscripts of excretory acts, including vomiting, likewise belong to this sphere of the “underworldly Hermes.”14 Again, Mercurius represents the “continuous cohabitation”15 which is found in unalloyed form in the Tantric Shiva-Shakti concept. Connections between Greek and Arabic alchemy and India are not unlikely. Reitzenstein16 reports the story of Padmanaba from a Turkish book of folklore17 about the forty viziers, which may date back to the time of the Moguls. Already in the first centuries of our era, Indian religious influences were at work in southern Mesopotamia, and in the second century B.C. there were Buddhist monasteries in Persia. In the royal temple of Padmanabhapura in Travancore (c. fifteenth century) I found two reliefs representing an entirely non-Indian senex ithyphallicus with wings. In one of them he stands up to his waist in the bowl of the moon. One is reminded of the winged ithyphallic old man who pursues the “blue” or “doglike”18 woman in Hippolytus. Kyllenios does in fact appear in Hippolytus19 as identical on the one hand with the Logos and on the other with the wicked Korybas, the phallus, and the demiurgic principle in general.20 Another aspect of this dark Mercurius is the mother-son incest, which may be traceable to Mandaean influences: there Nabu (Mercurius) and Istar (Astarte) form a syzygy. Astarte is the mother and love goddess throughout the whole Near East, where she is also tainted with the incest motif. Nabu is the “Messiah of the Lie,” who because of his malice is punished and kept in prison by the sun.21 The texts remind us again and again that Mercurius is “found in the dung-heaps,” but they add ironically that “many have grubbed in the dung-heaps, but extracted nothing thereby.”22
[278] 我们已经遇到了一些炼金术陈述，清楚地表明古典赫尔墨斯的性格后来忠实地重现于墨丘利乌斯的形象中。这一定程度上是无意识的重复，一定程度上是自发的再体验，最后也是有意识地对异教神的引用。毫无疑问，迈克尔·迈尔有意识地暗指赫尔墨斯作为引路者（ὁδηγός）——当他说他在神秘的漫游中发现了一座指路的墨丘利乌斯雕像，指向乐园之路1——以及他指赫尔墨斯这位秘仪引导者——当他让厄利特里亚女巫说到墨丘利乌斯："他将使你成为上帝之奥秘与自然之秘密的见证者。"2 同样，作为神圣的三元（divinus ternarius），墨丘利乌斯是神圣秘密的启示者，3 或者以金的形态被构想为秘术物质（magnesia）之灵，4 或哲学之树的丰育者。5 在《献给哲学墨丘利乌斯的题辞》中6 他被称为诸神的信使、诠释者和埃及的"特乌提乌斯"（托特）。迈尔甚至在他称墨丘利乌斯为"这位不忠且太过难捉摸的阿卡迪亚少年"7 时将他关联于基勒涅奥斯的赫尔墨斯，因为阿卡迪亚正是基勒涅奥斯——勃起的赫尔墨斯——的圣所所在。在《金色论著》的注释中，墨丘利乌斯被直呼为"基勒涅英雄"。8 迈尔的话也可能是指厄洛斯。事实上，在罗森克鲁茨的《化学婚礼》中，墨丘利乌斯确实以丘比特的形象出现，9 并以箭伤手惩罚工匠好奇探访维纳斯女士。箭是"激情之矢"（telum passionis），它也是墨丘利乌斯的属性。10 他是一位"射手"，而且是一位"不用弓弦射箭"且"在地球上无处可寻"的射手，11 显然是一位精灵。在佩诺图斯的符号表12 中，他与宁芙相关，令人想起牧神潘。他的淫荡由森迪沃吉乌斯的《化学三足》13 中的一幅插图所证实——在那里他出现在一辆由公鸡和母鸡拉着的凯旋车上，身后是一对裸体拥抱的恋人。与此相关还可以提及旧版画中大量颇为猥亵的结合图——它们常仅以色情品的形式被保存。旧手稿中的排泄行为图像，包括呕吐，同样属于这个"冥界赫尔墨斯"的领域。14 此外，墨丘利乌斯代表"持续的同居"15——这在坦特罗的湿婆-沙克蒂概念中找到纯粹的形式。希腊和阿拉伯炼金术与印度之间的联系并非不可能。莱岑斯坦16 报告了从一本关于四十位维齐尔的土耳其民间故事书17 中帕德玛纳巴的故事，该书可能追溯到莫卧儿时代。在我们纪元的最初几个世纪，印度宗教影响已在美索不达米亚南部发挥作用，公元前二世纪波斯已有佛教寺院。在特拉凡科的帕德玛纳巴普拉王室神庙（约十五世纪）中，我发现两幅浮雕，表现了一个完全非印度的有翼勃起老人。在其中一幅上，他站在月亮之碗的齐腰处。人们想起希波吕托斯中追击"蓝色"或"犬样"18 女人的有翼勃起老人。基勒涅奥斯确实在希波吕托斯19 中出现——一方面与逻各斯同一，另一方面与邪恶的科里巴斯（Korybas）、阳具以及一般的造物者原则同一。20 这个黑暗墨丘利乌斯的另一面是母-子乱伦，可能可追溯到曼达派影响：在那里纳布（墨丘利乌斯）和伊什塔尔（阿斯塔蒂）构成一个配对。阿斯塔蒂是整个近东的母亲和爱神，在那里她也沾染了乱伦母题。纳布是"谎言的弥赛亚"，因他的恶意被太阳惩罚并囚禁。21 文献一再提醒我们墨丘利乌斯"在粪堆中被发现"，但讽刺地补充说"许多人在粪堆中刨掘，却什么也没提取出来"。22

[279] This dark Mercurius must once again be understood as representing the initial nigredo state, the lowest being a symbol of the highest and vice versa:
[279] 这一黑暗的墨丘利乌斯必须再次被理解为代表初始的黑化（nigredo）状态——最低者是最高者的象征，反之亦然：

Anfang und Ende
始与终

Reichen sich die Hände.23
彼此伸手相握。23

He is the uroboros, the One and All, the union of opposites accomplished during the alchemical process, of which Penotus says:24
他是衔尾蛇，太一与万有，在炼金术过程中完成的对立统一——佩诺图斯说：24

Mercurius is begotten by nature as the son of nature and the fruit of the liquid element. But even as the Son of Man is begotten by the philosopher and created as the fruit of the Virgin, so must he [Mercurius] be raised from the earth and cleansed of all earthiness, then he ascends entire into the air, and is changed into spirit. Thus is fulfilled the word of the philosopher: He ascends from earth to heaven and receives the power of Above and Below, and puts off his earthy and impure nature and clothes himself in the heavenly nature.
墨丘利乌斯由自然所生，作为自然之子和液体元素之果。但正如人之子由哲学家所生、作为童贞女之果被创造一样，他〔墨丘利乌斯〕必须从大地中被举起，洗去一切土性，然后整个升入空中，变为灵。如此先哲之言得以应验：他从地升到天，接受上下之力，脱去土性不洁之体，穿上天之本性。

[280] Since Penotus is here referring to the “Tabula smaragdina,” it must be emphasized that he departs from the spirit of the “Tabula” in one essential point. In the version of Penotus, the ascent of Mercurius is in entire accord with the Christian transformation of the hylic into the pneumatic man. The “Tabula,” on the other hand, says: “He ascends from earth to heaven and descends again to earth, and receives the power of Above and Below. His power is complete when he has returned to earth.” So it is not a question of a one-way ascent to heaven, but, in contrast to the route followed by the Christian Redeemer, who comes from above to below and from there returns to the above, the filius macrocosmi starts from below, ascends on high, and, with the powers of Above and Below united in himself, returns to earth again. He carries out the reverse movement and thereby manifests a nature contrary to that of Christ and the Gnostic Redeemers, while on the other hand he displays a certain affinity with the Basilidian concept of the third sonship. Mercurius has the circular nature of the uroboros, hence he is symbolized by the circulus simplex of which he is at the same time the centre.25 He can therefore say of himself: “I am One and at the same time Many in myself.”26 This same treatise says that the centre of the circle in man is the earth, and calls it the “salt” to which Christ referred when he said: “Ye are the salt of the earth.”27
[280] 由于佩诺图斯在此引用的是《翡翠石板》，必须强调他在一个要点上偏离了《石板》的精神。在佩诺图斯的版本中，墨丘利乌斯的升天完全符合基督教的从属体人到属灵人的转化。而《石板》则说："他从地升到天，又从天降于地，接受上下之力。当他回归大地时，他的力量是完整的。"因此，这不是单向上天的问题，而是——与基督教救赎者从上到下、再从下回到上面的路线相反——大宇宙之子从下出发，升上高处，将上下之力统合于自身后再次回归大地。他执行反向运动，从而展现了一种与基督和诺斯替救赎者相反的本性，而另一方面他显示了一种与巴西利德派的第三子性概念的某种亲和。墨丘利乌斯具有衔尾蛇的循环本性，因此他被象征为单一之圆——他同时是圆心。25 因此他可以说自己："我是一，同时自身中是多。"26 同一文献说圆在人之中的中心是大地，称之为"盐"——基督所说的"你们是世上的盐"之盐。27

[281] Hermes is a god of thieves and cheats, but also a god of revelation who gave his name to a whole philosophy. Seen in historical retrospect, it was a moment of the utmost significance when the humanist Patrizi proposed to Pope Gregory XIV that Hermetic philosophy should take the place of Aristotle in ecclesiastical doctrine. At that moment two worlds came into contact, which—after heaven knows what happenings!—must yet be united in the future. At that time it was obviously impossible. A psychological differentiation of religious as well as scientific views is still needed before a union can begin to be brought about.28
[281] 赫尔墨斯是小偷和骗子之神，但也是启示之神——一整部哲学以他命名。从历史的回顾来看，当人文主义者帕特里齐向教皇格里高利十四世提议以赫尔墨斯哲学取代亚里士多德在教会教义中的地位时，那是一个意义重大的时刻。在那一刻，两个世界发生了接触——在——天知道发生了什么之后！——必须在未来实现统一。当时显然不可能。宗教以及科学观点的心理分化仍然需要，然后才能开始实现统一。28





9. MERCURIUS AS THE ARCANE SUBSTANCE
9. 作为秘术物质的墨丘利乌斯


[282] Mercurius, it is generally affirmed, is the arcanum,1 the prima materia,2 the “father of all metals,”3 the primeval chaos, the earth of paradise, the “material upon which nature worked a little, but nevertheless left imperfect.”4 He is also the ultima materia, the goal of his own transformation, the stone,5 the tincture, the philosophic gold, the carbuncle, the philosophic man, the second Adam, the analogue of Christ, the king, the light of lights, the deus terrestris, indeed the divinity itself or its perfect counterpart. Since I have already discussed the synonyms and meanings of the stone elsewhere there is no need for me to go into further details now.
[282] 一般认为，墨丘利乌斯就是秘术（arcanum），1 是原初物质（prima materia），2 是"万金之父"，3 是原初混沌，是乐园之土，是"自然曾稍加作用但仍留下未完成的物质"。4 他也是终极物质（ultima materia），是他自身转化的目标，是石头，5 是染色剂，是哲学之金，是红宝石，是哲学之人，是第二亚当，是基督的类比物，是王，是众光之光，是地上之神（deus terrestris），实际上就是神性本身或其完美的对应面。由于我已在别处讨论过石头的同义词和含义，现在无需进一步展开。

[283] Besides being the prima materia of the lowly beginning as well as the lapis as the highest goal, Mercurius is also the process which lies between, and the means by which it is effected. He is the “beginning, middle, and end of the work.”6 Therefore he is called the Mediator,7 Servator, and Salvator. He is a mediator like Hermes. As the medicina catholica and alexipharmakon he is the “preserver [servator] of the world.” He is the “healer [salvator] of all imperfect bodies”8 and the “image of Christ’s incarnation,”9 the unigenitus “consubstantial with the parental hermaphrodite.”10 Altogether, in the macrocosm of nature he occupies the position which Christ holds in the mundus rationalis of divine revelation. But as the saying “My light surpasses all other lights”11 shows, the claim of Mercurius goes even further, which is why the alchemists endowed him with the attributes of the Trinity12 in order to make clear his complete correspondence to God. In Dante, Satan is three-headed and therefore three-in-one. He is the counterpart of God in the sense that he is God’s antithesis. The alchemists did not hold this view of Mercurius; on the contrary, they saw him as a divine emanation harmonious with God’s own being. The stress they laid on his capacity for self-generation, self-transformation, self-reproduction, and self-destruction contradicts the idea that he is a created being. It is therefore only logical when Paracelsus and Dorn state that the prima materia is an “increatum” and a principle coeternal with God. This denial of creatio ex nihilo is supported by the fact that in the beginning God found the Tehom already in existence, that same maternal world of Tiamat whose son we encounter in Mercurius.13
[283] 墨丘利乌斯既是卑微开端的原初物质，也是作为最高目标的石头，他同时还是介于两者之间的过程以及实现该过程的手段。他是"这项工作的开端、中间和终结"。6 因此他被称为中保（Mediator），7 保存者（Servator）和救主（Salvator）。如同赫尔墨斯一样，他是一位中保。作为普世良药（medicina catholica）和解毒剂（alexipharmakon），他是"世界的保存者"。他是"一切不完美之体的医治者〔救主〕"8 和"基督道成肉身的形象"，9 是"与父母雌雄同体同质"的独生子。10 总而言之，在自然的大宇宙中，他占据了基督在神圣启示的理性世界中所持的位置。但正如"我的光超越一切其他之光"11 这句话所示，墨丘利乌斯的诉求走得更远，这也是为什么炼金术士赋予他三一的属性，12 以表明他与上帝的完全对应。在但丁那里，撒旦是三头的，因此是三合一的。他是上帝的对应面，意义在于他是上帝的对立面。炼金术士并不这样看待墨丘利乌斯；相反，他们将之视为与上帝自身存在相和谐的神性流溢。他们对他自我生育、自我转化、自我繁殖和自我毁灭能力的强调，与他是被造之物的观念相矛盾。因此，当帕拉塞尔苏斯和多恩声称原初物质是一种"非被造之物"（increatum）且与上帝同永恒的原则时，这只是逻辑上的必然。这种对无中生有的否定得到以下事实的支持：在创世之初，上帝发现深渊（Tehom）已经存在——正是那个母性的提亚玛特世界，其子我们在墨丘利乌斯身上遇到。13





10. SUMMARY
10. 总结


[284] The multiple aspects of Mercurius may be summarized as follows:
[284] 墨丘利乌斯的众多方面可总结如下：

(1) Mercurius consists of all conceivable opposites. He is thus quite obviously a duality, but is named a unity in spite of the fact that his innumerable inner contradictions can dramatically fly apart into an equal number of disparate and apparently independent figures.
（1）墨丘利乌斯由一切可想象的对立面组成。因此他显然是一个二元体，但被称为统一体，尽管他无数的内在矛盾可以戏剧性地分裂为同等数量的各不相同且表面独立的形象。

(2) He is both material and spiritual.
（2）他既是物质的也是精神的。

(3) He is the process by which the lower and material is transformed into the higher and spiritual, and vice versa.
（3）他是低等的、物质的东西转化为高等的、精神的东西的过程，反之亦然。

(4) He is the devil, a redeeming psychopomp, an evasive trickster, and God’s reflection in physical nature.
（4）他是魔鬼，是救赎的引魂者，是狡猾的骗子，是上帝在物质自然中的映像。

(5) He is also the reflection of a mystical experience of the artifex that coincides with the opus alchymicum.
（5）他也是工匠的神秘经验之映像，该经验与炼金术之功（opus alchymicum）同时发生。

(6) As such, he represents on the one hand the self and on the other the individuation process and, because of the limitless number of his names, also the collective unconscious.1
（6）正因如此，他一方面代表自性，另一方面代表个体化过程，而且由于其名称之无限多，他也代表集体无意识。1

* * *

[285] Certainly goldmaking, as also chemical research in general, was of great concern to alchemy. But a still greater, more impassioned concern appears to have been—one cannot very well say the “investigation”—but rather the experience of the unconscious. That this side of alchemy—the μυστικά—was for so long misunderstood is due solely to the fact that nothing was known of psychology, let alone of the supra-personal, collective unconscious. So long as one knows nothing of psychic actuality, it will be projected, if it appears at all. Thus the first knowledge of psychic law and order was found in the stars, and was later extended by projections into unknown matter. These two realms of experience branched off into sciences: astrology became astronomy, and alchemy chemistry. On the other hand, the peculiar connection between character and the astronomical determination of time has only very recently begun to turn into something approaching an empirical science. The really important psychic facts can neither be measured, weighed, nor seen in a test tube or under a microscope. They are therefore supposedly indeterminable, in other words they must be left to people who have an inner sense for them, just as colours must be shown to the seeing and not to the blind.
[285] 诚然，制金术以及一般的化学研究对炼金术来说是极为重要的。但一个更大、更热烈的关切似乎是——人们不能很好地称之为"研究"——而是对无意识的经验。炼金术的这一面——那神秘之物（μυστικά）——之所以被误解了这么久，完全是因为人们对心理学一无所知，更不用说超个人的集体无意识了。只要人们对心理实在一无所知，它就会——如果它出现的话——被投射出去。因此，关于心理法则和秩序的最初知识是在星辰中发现的，后来通过投射扩展到了未知的物质中。这两个经验领域分化成了科学：星象学变成了天文学，炼金术变成了化学。另一方面，性格与天文时间测定之间的特殊联系直到最近才开始变成某种接近经验科学的东西。真正重要的心理事实既不能被测量、称重，也不能在试管或显微镜下被看到。因此它们被认为是不可确定的，换言之，它们必须留给那些对之有内在感觉的人，就像颜色必须展示给视觉正常的人而非盲人。

[286] The store of projections found in alchemy is, if possible, even less known, and there is a further drawback which makes closer investigation extremely difficult. For, unlike the astrological constituents of character which, if negative, are at most unpleasant for the individual, though amusing to his neighbour, the alchemical projections represent collective contents that stand in painful contrast—or rather, in compensatory relation—to our highest rational convictions and values. They give the strange answers of the natural psyche to the ultimate questions which reason has left untouched. Contrary to all progress and belief in a future that will deliver us from the sorrowful present, they point back to something primeval, to the apparently hopelessly static, eternal sway of matter that makes our fondly believed-in world look like a phantasmagoria of shifting scenes. They show us, as the redemptive goal of our active, desirous life, a symbol of the inorganic—the stone—something that does not live but merely exists or “becomes,” the passive subject of a limitless and unfathomable play of opposites. “Soul,” that bodiless abstraction of the rational intellect, and “spirit,” that two-dimensional metaphor of dry-as-dust philosophical dialectic, appear in alchemical projection in almost physical, plastic form, like tangible breath-bodies, and refuse to function as component parts of our rational consciousness. The hope for a psychology without the soul is brought to nothing, and the illusion that the unconscious has only just been discovered vanishes: in a somewhat peculiar form, admittedly, it has been known for close on two thousand years. Let us, however, not delude ourselves: no more than we can separate the constituents of character from the astronomical determinants of time are we able to separate that unruly and evasive Mercurius from the autonomy of matter. Something of the projection-carrier always clings to the projection, and even if we succeed to some degree in integrating into our consciousness the part we recognize as psychic, we shall integrate along with it something of the cosmos and its materiality; or rather, since the cosmos is infinitely greater than we are, we shall have been assimilated by the inorganic. “Transform yourselves into living philosophical stones!” cries an alchemist, but he did not know how infinitely slowly the stone “becomes.” Anyone who gives serious thought to the “natural light” that emanates from the projections of alchemy will certainly agree with the Master who spoke of the “wearisomeness of the interminable meditation” demanded by the work. In these projections we encounter the phenomenology of an “objective” spirit, a true matrix of psychic experience, the most appropriate symbol for which is matter. Nowhere and never has man controlled matter without closely observing its behaviour and paying heed to its laws, and only to the extent that he did so could he control it. The same is true of that objective spirit which today we call the unconscious: it is refractory like matter, mysterious and elusive, and obeys laws which are so non-human or suprahuman that they seem to us like a crimen laesae majestatis humanae. If a man puts his hand to the opus, he repeats, as the alchemists say, God’s work of creation. The struggle with the unformed, with the chaos of Tiamat, is in truth a primordial experience.
[286] 炼金术中发现的投射库存，如果可能的话，甚至更少为人所知，而且还有一个进一步的障碍使深入研究极为困难。因为，不同于性格的星象学成分——如果它们是消极的，对个人来说至多是不愉快的，虽然对他的邻居来说是有趣的——炼金术的投射代表着集体内容，它们与我们最高的理性信念和价值处于痛苦的对比——或者说补偿——关系之中。它们给出了自然心灵对理性未曾触及的终极问题的奇异回答。与一切进步和相信未来将把我们从悲伤的现在中拯救出来的信念相反，它们指向某种原初的东西，指向物质那表面上 hopeless 地静止的、永恒的统治——它使我们所深信不疑的世界看起来像一幅变幻场景的幻影。它们向我们展示了——作为我们积极的、充满欲望的生命的救赎目标——一个无机物的象征：石头——某种不活着而仅仅存在或"生成"的东西，一场无限而深不可测的对立游戏的被动主体。"灵魂"——理性智力的那种无形抽象——和"精神"——干枯的哲学辩证法的二维隐喻——在炼金术的投射中以几乎是物理的、立体的形式出现，如同可触摸的气息之体，拒绝作为我们理性意识的组成部分而发挥作用。没有灵魂的心理学的希望化为乌有，而无意识仅仅刚刚被发现的幻象也随之消失：以一种多少有些特殊的形态，它已经被知道了将近两千年。然而，让我们不要自欺欺人：正如我们无法将性格的成分与时间的天文决定因素分开一样，我们也无法将那桀骜不驯、难以捉摸的墨丘利乌斯与物质的自主性分开。投射载体总有某种东西附着在投射上，即使我们在某种程度上成功地将我们认定为心理的那部分整合进意识，我们也将随之整合某种宇宙及其物质性的东西；或者更确切地说，既然宇宙无限大于我们，我们将被无机物所同化。"将你们自己转化为活的哲学家之石！"一位炼金术士喊道，但他不知道石头"生成"得多么无限缓慢。任何认真思考从炼金术投射中散发出的"自然之光"的人，一定会同意那位谈到这项工作所要求的"无尽冥想的令人厌倦"的大师。在这些投射中，我们遇到了一种"客观"精神的现象学，一个心理经验的真正母体，其最恰当的象征就是物质。无论何时何地，人类都不曾不密切观察物质的行为和遵从其法则而控制物质，他也只有在这样做的程度上才能控制它。我们今天称为无意识的那种客观精神也是如此：它像物质一样难驾驭，神秘而难以捉摸，服从的法则如此非人乃至超人，以至于在我们看来就像对人类尊严的犯罪（crimen laesae majestatis humanae）。如果一个人着手此项大业（opus），如炼金术士所言，他就重复了上帝的创世之工。与未成形之物、与提亚玛特的混沌的斗争，确实是一种原初经验。

[287] Since the psyche, when directly experienced, confronts us in the “living” substance it has animated and appears to be one with it, Mercurius is called argentum vivum. Conscious discrimination, or consciousness itself, effects that world-shattering intervention which separates body from soul and divides the spirit Mercurius from the hydrargyrum, as if drawing off the spirit into the bottle, to speak in terms of our fairytale. But since body and soul, in spite of the artificial separation, are united in the mystery of life, the mercurial spirit, though imprisoned in the bottle, is yet found in the roots of the tree, as its quintessence and living numen. In the language of the Upanishads, he is the personal atman of the tree. Isolated in the bottle, he corresponds to the ego and the principle of individuation, which in the Indian view leads to the illusion of individual existence. Freed from his prison, Mercurius assumes the character of the supra-personal atman. He becomes the one animating principle of all created things, the hiranyagarbha (golden germ),2 the supra-personal self, represented by the filius macrocosmi, the one stone of the wise. “Rosinus ad Sarratantam” cites a saying of “Malus Philosophus”3 which attempts to formulate the psychological relation of the lapis to consciousness: “This stone is below thee, as to obedience; above thee, as to dominion; therefore from thee, as to knowledge; about thee, as to equals.”4 Applied to the self, this would mean: “The self is subordinate to you, yet on the other hand rules you. It is dependent on your own efforts and your knowledge, but transcends you and embraces all those who are of like mind.” This refers to the collective nature of the self, since the self epitomizes the wholeness of the personality. By definition, wholeness includes the collective unconscious, which as experience seems to show is everywhere identical.
[287] 由于心灵在被直接经验时，以它所赋予生气的"活的"物质呈现在我们面前，且似乎与之一体，墨丘利乌斯被称为银液（argentum vivum）。意识的辨别——或意识本身——实施了那场惊天动地的干预，将身体与灵魂分开，将灵性墨丘利乌斯与水银分开，仿佛——用我们童话的话说——将灵气抽入瓶中。但由于身体与灵魂在生命的奥秘中仍然结合在一起，尽管被人为地分离，水银之灵虽被囚于瓶中，却在树的根部被发现，作为其精华和活的灵力（numen）。用《奥义书》的语言来说，他是树的个人阿特曼。孤立于瓶中，他对应于自我（ego）和个体化原则——在印度思想中，后者导致了个体存在的幻觉。一旦从牢笼中解放，墨丘利乌斯便具有超个人阿特曼的特征。他成为一切被造之物的唯一赋灵原则，即金胎（hiranyagarbha），2 即超个人自性，由大宇宙之子（filius macrocosmi）——智者之一石——所代表。《罗西努斯致萨拉坦塔》引用了"恶哲学家"（Malus Philosophus）3 的一段话，试图表述石头与意识之间的心理学关系："此石在服从方面低于你；在统治方面高于你；因此在知识方面源自你；在同辈方面围绕你。"4 将此应用于自性，意味着："自性从属于你，但另一方面又统治你。它依赖于你自身的努力和知识，但又超越你并包容所有与你志同道合者。"这指的是自性的集体性质，因为自性是人格整体性的缩影。根据定义，整体性包含集体无意识，而经验似乎表明，集体无意识在所有地方都是同一的。

[288] The encounter of the poor student with the spirit in the bottle portrays the spiritual adventure of a blind and unawakened human being. The same motif underlies the tale of the swineherd who climbed the world-tree,5 and also forms the leitmotiv of alchemy. For what it signifies is the individuation process as it prepares itself in the unconscious and gradually enters consciousness. The commonest alchemical symbol for this is the tree, the arbor philosophica, which derives from the paradisal tree of knowledge. Here, as in our fairytale, a daemonic serpent, an evil spirit, prods and persuades to knowledge. In view of the Biblical precedent, it is not surprising that the spirit Mercurius has, to say the least, a great many connections with the dark side. One of his aspects is the female serpent-daemon, Lilith or Melusina, who lives in the philosophical tree. At the same time, he not only partakes of the Holy Spirit but, according to alchemy, is actually identical with it. We have no choice but to accept this shocking paradox after all we have learnt about the ambivalence of the spirit archetype. Our ambiguous Mercurius simply confirms the rule. In any case, the paradox is no worse than the Creator’s whimsical notion of enlivening his peaceful, innocent paradise with the presence of an obviously rather dangerous tree-snake, “accidentally” located on the very same tree as the forbidden apples.
[288] 贫穷学生与瓶中之灵的相遇，描绘了一个盲目而未觉醒的人的精神冒险。同样的动机也构成了猪倌攀登世界树5 的故事，并构成了炼金术的主导动机。因为它所意指的是在无意识中自行准备并逐渐进入意识的个体化过程。炼金术中对此最常见的象征是树——哲学之树（arbor philosophica）——它源于乐园的知识之树。在这里，如同在我们的童话中一样，一条精灵之蛇——一个恶灵——催促并引导人走向知识。鉴于《圣经》中的先例，灵性墨丘利乌斯有——至少可以说——大量与黑暗面的联系，这并不令人惊讶。他的一面是女性蛇灵——莉莉丝或美露辛——她住在哲学之树中。与此同时，他不仅分有圣灵，而且按照炼金术的说法，实际上与圣灵同一。在了解了精神原型的两面性之后，我们别无选择，只能接受这一令人震惊的悖论。我们含糊不清的墨丘利乌斯恰恰证实了这一规则。无论如何，这一悖论并不比造物主那古怪的念头更糟——他竟然用一条显然相当危险的树蛇来为他的和平无辜的乐园增添生气，这条蛇"碰巧"就位于那棵长着禁果的树上。

[289] It must be admitted that the fairytale and alchemy both show Mercurius in a predominantly unfavourable light, which is all the more striking because his positive aspect relates him not only to the Holy Spirit, but, in the form of the lapis, also to Christ and, as a triad, even to the Trinity. It looks as if it were precisely these relationships which led the alchemists to put particular stress on the dark and dubious quality of Mercurius, and this militates strongly against the assumption that by their lapis they really meant Christ. If this had been their meaning, why should they have renamed Christ the lapis philosophorum? The lapis is at most a counterpart or analogy of Christ in the physical world. Its symbolism, like that of Mercurius who constitutes its substance, points, psychologically speaking, to the self, as also does the symbolic figure of Christ.6 In comparison with the purity and unity of the Christ symbol, Mercurius-lapis is ambiguous, dark, paradoxical, and thoroughly pagan. It therefore represents a part of the psyche which was certainly not moulded by Christianity and can on no account be expressed by the symbol “Christ.” On the contrary, as we have seen, in many ways it points to the devil, who is known at times to disguise himself as an angel of light. The lapis formulates an aspect of the self which stands apart, bound to nature and at odds with the Christian spirit. It represents all those things which have been eliminated from the Christian model. But since they possess living reality, they cannot express themselves otherwise than in dark Hermetic symbols. The paradoxical nature of Mercurius reflects an important aspect of the self—the fact, namely, that it is essentially a complexio oppositorum, and indeed can be nothing else if it is to represent any kind of totality. Mercurius as deus terrestris has something of that deus absconditus (hidden god) which is an essential element of the psychological self, and the self cannot be distinguished from a God-image (except by incontestable and unprovable faith). Although I have stressed that the lapis is a symbol embracing the opposites, it should not be thought of as a—so to speak—more complete symbol of the self. That would be decidedly incorrect, for actually it is an image whose form and content are largely determined by the unconscious. For this reason it is never found in the texts in finished and well-defined form; we have to combine all the scattered references to the various arcane substances, to Mercurius, to the transformation process and the end product. Although the lapis in one aspect or another is almost always the subject discussed, there is no real consensus of opinion in regard to its actual form. Almost every author has his own special allegories, synonyms, and metaphors. This makes it clear that the stone, though indeed an object of general experiment, was to an even greater extent an outcropping of the unconscious, which only sporadically crossed the borderline of subjectivity and gave rise to the vague general concept of the lapis philosophorum.
[289] 必须承认，童话和炼金术都以一种主要是不利的光线展示墨丘利乌斯，这更加引人注目，因为他的积极方面不仅将他关联于圣灵，而且在石头的形态下也关联于基督，作为三元甚至关联于三一。看起来正是这些关系使炼金术士特别强调墨丘利乌斯的黑暗和可疑品质，这强烈反对了他们以石头真正意指基督的假设。如果这是他们的意思，他们为何要将基督改名为哲学家之石？石头至多是基督在物理世界中的对应面或类比物。它的象征——如同构成其物质的墨丘利乌斯的象征一样——从心理学角度讲指向自性，基督的象征形象也是如此。6 与基督象征的纯洁性和统一性相比，墨丘利乌斯-石头是含糊的、黑暗的、悖论性的、彻底异教的。因此，它代表了心灵中一个显然未被基督教塑造的部分，且绝不能以"基督"这一象征来表达。相反，如我们所见，它在许多方面指向魔鬼——众所周知，魔鬼有时会伪装成光明天使。石头表述了自性的一个方面——它独立于基督教精神之外，与自然绑定，与基督教精神相冲突。它代表了所有那些从基督教模式中被消除的东西。但由于它们具有活生生的实在性，它们只能以黑暗的赫尔墨斯式象征来表达自身。墨丘利乌斯的悖论本性反映了自性的一个重要方面——即它本质上是对立之合（complexio oppositorum），如果它要代表任何形式的整体性的话，它也确实只能是如此。作为地上之神（deus terrestris）的墨丘利乌斯具有某种隐藏之神（deus absconditus）的特质——这是心理自性的本质要素，而自性无法与上帝形象区分开来（除了通过无可争辩且无法证明的信仰）。虽然我强调石头是一个包容对立面的象征，但不应该认为它是一个——可以这么说——更完整的自性象征。那将完全是不正确的，因为实际上它是一个其形式和内容在很大程度上由无意识决定的形象。正因如此，它在文献中从未以完整而明确的形式出现；我们必须将所有散见于各种秘术物质、墨丘利乌斯、转化过程和最终产物的零星提及结合起来。虽然石头在这样或那样的方面几乎总是被讨论的主题，但对于它的实际形态并没有真正的共识。几乎每位作者都有自己的特殊寓言、同义词和隐喻。这清楚地表明，石头虽然确实是一般实验的对象，但在更大程度上是无意识的露头，只是零星地越过了主观性的边界，产生了模糊而一般的哲学家之石概念。

[290] Opposed to this figure veiled in the twilight of more or less secret doctrines there stands, sharply outlined by dogma, the Son of Man and Salvator Mundi, Christ the Sol Novus, before whom the lesser stars pale. He is the affirmation of the daylight of consciousness in trinitarian form. So clear and definite is the Christ figure that whatever differs from him must appear not only inferior but perverse and vile. This is not the result of Christ’s own teaching, but rather of what is taught about him, and especially of the crystal purity which dogma has bestowed upon his figure. As a result, a tension of opposites such as had never occurred before in the whole history of Christianity beginning with the Creation arose between Christ and the Antichrist, as Satan or the fallen angel. At the time of Job, Satan is still found among the sons of God. “Now there was a day,” it says in Job 1 : 6, “when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” This picture of a celestial family reunion gives no hint of the New Testament “Get thee hence, Satan” (Matthew 4 : 10), nor yet of the dragon chained in the underworld for a thousand years (Rev. 20 : 2). It looks as if the superabundance of light on one side had produced an all the blacker darkness on the other. One can also see that the uncommonly great diffusion of black substance makes a sinless being almost impossible. A loving belief in such a being naturally involves cleansing one’s own house of black filth. But the filth must be dumped somewhere, and no matter where the dump lies it will plague even the best of all possible worlds with a bad smell.
[290] 与这个笼罩在或多或少秘密学说的暮色中的形象相对立的，是被教义清晰勾勒的人子和救世主——基督，新太阳（Sol Novus），在他面前较小的星辰黯然失色。他是三一形态的意识白昼之光的肯定。基督的形象如此清晰明确，以至于一切与之不同者不仅显得低劣，而且显得扭曲和卑鄙。这不是基督本人教导的结果，而是关于他的教导的结果，尤其是教义赋予其形象的水晶般纯洁。由此，在基督与敌基督——即撒旦或堕落天使——之间产生了一种对立的张力，这种张力自创世以来在整个基督教历史上从未出现过。在约伯的时代，撒旦尚在众子之中。《约伯记》1:6说："有一天，神的众子来侍立在耶和华面前，撒但也来在其中。"这幅天上家庭聚会的画面毫不暗示新约中"撒旦退去吧"（《马太福音》4:10）的话，也不暗示被锁在地下千年之龙（《启示录》20:2）。看起来，一方的过剩之光在另一方产生了更深的黑暗。人们也可以看到，黑色物质的异常广泛扩散使得一个无罪之几乎不可能。对这样一个存在充满爱的信仰自然涉及清扫自己家中的黑色污秽。但污秽必须倒在某处，无论倾倒场在哪里，它都会用臭气使即使是最好的可能世界也受到困扰。

[291] The balance of the primordial world is upset. What I have said is not intended as a criticism, for I am deeply convinced not only of the relentless logic but of the expediency of this development. The emphatic differentiation of opposites is synonymous with sharper discrimination, and that is the sine qua non for any broadening or heightening of consciousness. The progressive differentiation of consciousness is the most important task of human biology and accordingly meets with the highest rewards—vastly increased chances of survival and the development of power technology. From the phylogenetic point of view, the effects of consciousness are as far-reaching as those of lung-breathing and warm-bloodedness. But clarification of consciousness necessarily entails an obscuration of those dimmer elements of the psyche which are less capable of becoming conscious, so that sooner or later a split occurs in the psychic system. Since it is not recognized as such it is projected, and appears in the form of a metaphysical split between the powers of light and the powers of darkness. The possibility of this projection is guaranteed by the presence of numerous archaic vestiges of the original daemons of light and darkness in any age. It seems likely, therefore, that the tension of opposites in Christianity is derived to a still unclarified degree from the dualism of ancient Persia, though the two are not identical.
[291] 原初世界的平衡被打破了。我所说的并非批评，因为我深信这一发展不仅有冷酷的逻辑，也有其合理性。对立面的强调性分化等同于更敏锐的辨别，而这是任何意识的扩展或提升的必要条件。意识的渐进分化是人类生物学最重要的任务，相应地获得了最高的回报——大大增加的生存机会和动力技术的发展。从系统发生学的角度看，意识的影响如同肺呼吸和温血一样深远。但意识的澄清必然导致心灵中那些较难成为意识的较暗元素的遮蔽，以至于迟早心理系统会发生分裂。由于这种分裂未被认出，它就被投射出去，以光之力量与暗之力量之间的形而上学分裂的形式出现。这种投射的可能性由任何时代都存在的大量光与暗的原初精灵的古老遗迹所保证。因此，基督教中的对立张力很可能在很大程度上——尽管尚未澄清——源自古波斯的二元论，尽管两者并非同一。

[292] There can be no doubt that the moral consequences of the Christian development represent a very considerable advance compared with the ancient Israelite religion of law. The Christianity of the synoptic gospels signifies little more than a coming to terms with issues inside Judaism, which may fairly be compared with the much earlier Buddhist reformation inside Hindu polytheism. Psychologically, both reformations resulted in a tremendous strengthening of consciousness. This is particularly evident in the maieutic method employed by Shakyamuni. But the sayings of Jesus manifest the same tendency, even if we discard as apocryphal the clearest formulation of this kind, the logion in Codex Bezae to Luke 6 : 4: “Man, if thou knowest what thou doest, thou art blessed. If thou knowest it not, thou art accursed and a transgressor of the law.” At all events, the parable of the unjust steward (Luke 16) has not found its way into the Apocrypha, where it would have fitted so well.
[292] 毫无疑问，基督教发展的道德后果代表了对古代以色列律法宗教的一个相当大的进步。对观福音书的基督教不过意味着犹太教内部问题的解决，可以公平地与更早在印度教多神教内部的佛教改革相比。在心理学上，两次改革都导致了意识的巨大增强。这在释迦牟尼所运用的助产术中尤为明显。但耶稣的话语也表现出同样的倾向，即使我们将此类最清晰的表述——即《贝扎抄本》中《路加福音》6:4的佚名语录："人啊，如果你知道你所做的事，你是有福的。如果你不知道，你是有祸的，是律法的违犯者"——视为伪经而排除在外。无论如何，不义管家的比喻（《路加福音》16章）并没有进入伪经，尽管它在那里会很合适。

[293] The rift in the metaphysical world has slowly risen into consciousness as a split in the human psyche, and the struggle between light and darkness moves to the battleground within. This shift of scene is not entirely self-evident, for which reason St. Ignatius Loyola considered it necessary to open our eyes to the conflict and impress it on our feelings by means of the most drastic spiritual exercises.7 These efforts, for obvious reasons, had only a very limited range of application. And so, strangely enough, it was the medical men who, at the turn of the nineteenth century, were forced to intervene and get the obstructed process of conscious realization going again. Approaching the problem from a scientific angle, and innocent of any religious aim, Freud uncovered the abysmal darkness of human nature which a would-be enlightened optimism had striven to conceal. Since then psychotherapy, in one form or another, has persistently explored the extensive area of darkness which I have called the shadow. This attempt of modern science opened the eyes of only a few. However, the historic events of our time have painted a picture of man’s psychic reality in indelible colours of blood and fire, and given him an object lesson which he will never be able to forget if—and this is the great question—he has today acquired enough consciousness to keep up with the furious pace of the devil within him. The only other hope is that he may learn to curb a creativity which is wasting itself in the exploitation of material power. Unfortunately, all attempts in that direction look like bloodless Utopias.
[293] 形而上学世界中的裂痕已经缓缓上升为意识，成为人类心灵的分裂，光与暗的斗争转移到了内部的战场。这一场景的转移并非完全不言自明，正因如此，圣依纳爵·罗耀拉认为有必要通过最剧烈的灵性操练来打开我们对冲突的眼睛，并将其铭刻于我们的感情。7 这些努力，出于明显的原因，只有非常有限的应用范围。因此，说来奇怪，正是医生们在十九世纪之交被迫介入，使受阻的意识化过程重新运转。从科学角度接近问题，且不带有任何宗教目的，弗洛伊德揭示了人性的深渊般的黑暗——一种自封的启蒙乐观主义一直竭力掩盖的黑暗。此后，心理治疗以这种或那种形式持续探索了我称之为阴影的广大黑暗领域。现代科学的这一尝试只睁开少数人的眼睛。然而，我们这个时代的历史事件以血与火的不可磨灭之色描绘了人类心理现实的画面，给他上了一堂实物课——如果——这是一个大问题——他今天是否已获得了足够的意识来跟上他内心魔鬼疯狂的步伐，他将永远无法忘记这一课。另一个唯一的希望是他可能学会遏制一种正在浪费于物质力量开发中的创造力。不幸的是，该方向上的一切尝试看起来都像毫无血色的乌托邦。

[294] The figure of Christ the Logos has raised the anima rationalis in man to a level of importance which remains unobjectionable so long as it knows itself to be below and subject to the κύριos, the Lord of Spirits. Reason, however, has set itself free and proclaimed itself the ruler. It has sat enthroned in Notre Dame as Déesse Raison and heralded events that were to come. Our consciousness is no longer confined within a sacred temenos of otherworldly, eschatological images. It was helped to break free by a force that did not stream down from above—like the lumen de lumine—but came up with tremendous pressure from below and increased in strength as consciousness detached itself from the darkness and climbed into the light. In accordance with the principle of compensation which runs through the whole of nature, every psychic development, whether individual or collective, possesses an optimum which, when exceeded, produces an enantiodromia, that is, turns into its opposite. Compensatory tendencies emanating from the unconscious may be noted even during the approach to the critical turning-point, though if consciousness persists in its course they are completely repressed. The stirrings in the darkness necessarily seem like a devilish betrayal of the ideal of spiritual development. Reason cannot help condemning as unreasonable everything that contradicts it or deviates from its laws, in spite of all evidence to the contrary. Morality can permit itself no capacity for change, for whatever it does not agree with is inevitably immoral and has therefore to be repressed. It is not difficult to imagine the multitude of energies which must flow off into the unconscious under such conscious domination.
[294] 基督作为逻各斯的形象将人身上的理性灵魂（anima rationalis）提升到一个重要水平——只要它知道自己处于灵之主（κύριος）之下并服从于他，这一水平就是无可非议的。然而，理性已经自我解放并宣布自己为统治者。它在巴黎圣母院登基为理性女神（Déesse Raison），预示了即将到来的事件。我们的意识不再被限制在一个由超世间的、末世论的形象构成的神圣围场（temenos）之内。帮助它挣脱的是一股力量——它并非从上方如光中之光（lumen de lumine）般流下，而是以巨大的压力从下方涌上，并随着意识从黑暗中脱离、攀升到光明中而增强力量。根据贯穿整个自然的补偿原则，每一次心理发展——无论是个体的还是集体的——都有一个最优点，一旦超越就产生突变（enantiodromia），即转化为其对立面。即使在接近临界转折点时，来自无意识的补偿倾向也可以被注意到，尽管如果意识坚持其方向，这些倾向就会被完全压抑。黑暗中的躁动必然看起来像对精神发展理想的魔鬼般背叛。理性不得不将一切与之矛盾或偏离其法则的东西斥为不合理的，尽管有所有反面的证据。道德不容许自身有任何改变的能力，因为它不同意的东西不可避免地是不道德的，因此必须被压抑。不难想象，在这样一种意识的主导下，有多少能量必须流入无意识。

[295] Hesitantly, as in a dream, the introspective brooding of the centuries gradually put together the figure of Mercurius and created a symbol which, according to all the psychological rules, stands in a compensatory relation to Christ. It is not meant to take his place, nor is it identical with him, for then indeed it could replace him. It owes its existence to the law of compensation, and its object is to throw a bridge across the abyss separating the two psychological worlds by presenting a subtle compensatory counterpoint to the Christ image. The fact that in Faust the compensatory figure is not, as one might almost have expected from the author’s classical predilections, the wily messenger of the gods, but, as the name “Mephistopheles”8 shows, a familiaris risen from the cesspits of medieval magic, proves, if anything, the ingrained Christian character of Goethe’s consciousness. To the Christian mentality, the dark antagonist is always the devil. As I have shown, Mercurius escapes this prejudice by only a hair’s breadth. But he escapes it, thanks to the fact that he scorns to carry on opposition at all costs. The magic of his name enables him, in spite of his ambiguity and duplicity, to keep outside the split, for as an ancient pagan god he possesses a natural undividedness which is impervious to logical and moral contradictions. This gives him invulnerability and incorruptibility, the very qualities we so urgently need to heal the split in ourselves.
[295] 犹豫不决地，如在梦中，几个世纪的内省沉思逐渐拼合出墨丘利乌斯的形象，创造了一个按照一切心理学规则与基督处于补偿关系的象征。它并非要取代他，也不与他同一，否则它确实可以取代他。它的存在归功于补偿法则，其目标是通过呈现基督形象的微妙补偿对应物，在分隔两个心理世界的深渊上架起一座桥梁。在《浮士德》中，补偿形象并非如人们从作者的古典偏好中几乎可以预期的那样，是狡猾的诸神信使，而是——如"墨菲斯托菲勒斯"8 之名所示——从中世纪魔法粪池中升起的家族精灵（familiaris），这证明了歌德意识的根深蒂固的基督教品格。在基督教心态中，黑暗的对立面总是魔鬼。如我所表明的，墨丘利乌斯仅以毫厘之差逃脱了这一偏见。但他逃脱了，多亏他藐视不惜一切代价地维持对立。他名字的魔力使他尽管含糊不清且具有二重性，仍能置身于分裂之外，因为作为一个古老的异教神，他拥有一种自然的未分裂性，对逻辑和道德矛盾不为所动。这赋予了他刀枪不入和不可腐蚀的品质——正是我们迫切需要用来医治自身分裂的品质。

[296] If one makes a synopsis of all the descriptions and alchemical pictures of Mercurius, they form a striking parallel to the symbols of the self derived from other sources. One can hardly escape the conclusion that Mercurius as the lapis is a symbolic expression for the psychological complex which I have defined as the self. Similarly, the Christ figure must be viewed as a self symbol, and for the same reasons. But this leads to an apparently insoluble contradiction, for it is not at first clear how the unconscious can shape two such different images from one and the same content, which moreover possesses the character of totality. Certainly the centuries have done their spiritual work upon these two figures, and one is inclined to assume that both have been in large measure anthropomorphized during the process of assimilation. For those who hold that both figures are inventions of the intellect, the contradiction is quickly resolved. It then merely reflects the subjective psychic situation: the two figures would stand for man and his shadow.
[296] 如果将墨丘利乌斯的所有描述和炼金术图像做一个总览，它们与从其他来源得出的自性象征形成了惊人的平行。人们几乎无法避免得出结论：作为石头的墨丘利乌斯是我所定义的自性这一心理情结的象征性表达。同样，基督的形象也必须被视为自性象征，理由相同。但这导致了一个表面上无法解决的矛盾，因为一开始并不清楚无意识如何能从同一个内容——一个具有整体性特征的内容——中塑造出两个如此不同的形象。诚然，几个世纪以来对这两个形象做了精神上的加工，人们倾向于认为两者在接纳过程中都在很大程度上被拟人化了。对于认为两个形象都是理智发明的人来说，矛盾很快就能解决。那它就仅仅反映了主观的心理状况：两个形象将代表人和他的阴影。

[297] This very simple and obvious solution is, unfortunately, founded on premises that do not stand up to criticism. The figures of Christ and the devil are both based on archetypal patterns, and were never invented but rather experienced. Their existence preceded all cognition of them,9 and the intellect had no hand in the matter, except to assimilate them and if possible give them a place in its philosophy. Only the most superficial intellectualism can overlook this fundamental fact. We are actually confronted with two different images of the self, which in all likelihood presented a duality even in their original form. This duality was not invented, but is an autonomous phenomenon.
[297] 这一非常简单而明显的解决方案，遗憾的是，建立在经不起批评的前提之上。基督和魔鬼的形象都基于原型模式，它们从未被发明而是被经验。它们的存在先于对它们的一切认知，9 理智在其中没有插手——除非是接纳它们并尽可能给它们一个哲学上的位置。只有最肤浅的智识主义才会忽视这一基本事实。我们实际上面对的是自性的两个不同形象，它们很可能在原始形态中就呈现了二元性。这一二元性不是被发明的，而是一个自主现象。
