[298] Since we naturally think from the standpoint of consciousness, we inevitably come to the conclusion that the split between consciousness and the unconscious is the sole cause of this duality. But experience has demonstrated the existence of a preconscious psychic functioning and of corresponding autonomous factors, the archetypes. Once we can accept the fact that the voices and delusions of the insane and the phobias and obsessions of the neurotic are beyond rational control, and that the ego cannot voluntarily fabricate dreams but simply dreams what it has to, then we can also understand that the gods came first and theology later. Indeed, we must go a step further and assume that in the beginning there were two figures, one bright and one shadowy, and only afterwards did the light of consciousness detach itself from the night and the uncertain shimmer of its stars.
[298] 由于我们自然而然地从意识的立场思考，我们不可避免地得出结论：意识与无意识之间的分裂是这一二元性的唯一原因。但经验证明了前意识心理运作和相应的自主因素——原型——的存在。一旦我们接受这样一个事实：疯子的声音和妄想以及神经症患者的恐惧和强迫症都是超越理性控制的，自我不能自愿地制造梦而只是梦它不得不梦的东西，那么我们也能理解神先于神学。事实上，我们还要更进一步，假设最初有两个形象，一明一暗，之后意识之光才从黑夜及其星辰不定的微光中脱离出来。

[299] So if Christ and the dark nature-deity are autonomous images that can be directly experienced, we are obliged to reverse our rationalistic causal sequence, and instead of deriving these figures from our psychic conditions, must derive our psychic conditions from these figures. This is expecting a good deal of the modern intellect but does not alter the logic of our hypothesis. From this standpoint Christ appears as the archetype of consciousness and Mercurius as the archetype of the unconscious. As Cupid and Kyllenios, he tempts us out into the world of sense; he is the benedicta viriditas and the multi flores of early spring, a god of illusion and delusion of whom it is rightly said: “Invenitur in vena / Sanguine plena” (He is found in the vein swollen with blood). He is at the same time a Hermes Chthonios and an Eros, yet it is from him that there issues the “light surpassing all lights,” the lux moderna, for the lapis is none other than the figure of light veiled in matter.10 It is in this sense that St. Augustine quotes I Thessalonians 5 : 5, “Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness,” and distinguishes two forms of knowledge, a cognitio vespertina and a cognitio matutina, the first corresponding to the scientia creaturae and the second to the scientia Creatoris.11 If we equate cognitio with consciousness, then Augustine’s thought would suggest that the merely human and natural consciousness gradually darkens, as at nightfall. But just as evening gives birth to morning, so from the darkness arises a new light, the stella matutina, which is at once the evening and the morning star—Lucifer, the light-bringer.
[299] 因此，如果基督和黑暗的自然之神是可直接经验的自主形象，我们就有义务颠倒我们的理性主义因果序列，不是从我们的心理条件推导这些形象，而是从这些形象推导我们的心理条件。这对现代理智要求甚多，但不改变我们假设的逻辑。从这个立场看，基督作为意识的原型出现，墨丘利乌斯作为无意识的原型出现。作为丘比特和基勒涅奥斯，他引诱我们进入感官世界；他是蒙福的绿意（benedicta viriditas）和早春的万紫千红（multi flores），是幻觉和迷惑之神——有谚语正确地说："在饱含血液的矿脉中被发现"（Invenitur in vena / Sanguine plena）。他同时是冥界赫尔墨斯（Hermes Chthonios）和厄洛斯，然而正是从他那里发出了"超越一切之光"——现代之光（lux moderna），因为石头无非是被物质遮蔽的光之形象。10 正是在这个意义上，圣奥古斯丁引用《帖撒罗尼迦前书》5:5："你们都是光明之子，都是白昼之子；我们不是属黑夜的，也不是属黑暗的"，并区分了两种知识形式——晚间之知（cognitio vespertina）和晨间之知（cognitio matutina），前者对应于被造物之知（scientia creaturae），后者对应于造物主之知（scientia Creatoris）。11 如果我们将 cognitio 等同于意识，那么奥古斯丁的思想将暗示：仅仅人类的和自然的意识逐渐变暗，如同日暮。但正如黄昏孕育黎明，从黑暗中升起一盏新光——晨星（stella matutina），它同时是黄昏之星和黎明之星——卢奇菲尔，携光者。

[300] Mercurius is by no means the Christian devil—the latter could rather be said to be a “diabolization” of Lucifer or of Mercurius. Mercurius is an adumbration of the primordial light-bringer, who is never himself the light, but a ϕωσϕóρος who brings the light of nature, the light of the moon and the stars which fades before the new morning light. Of this light St. Augustine says that it will never turn to darkness unless the Creator is abandoned by the love of his creatures. But this, too, belongs to the rhythm of day and night. As Hölderlin says in “Patmos”;
[300] 墨丘利乌斯绝非基督教的魔鬼——后者倒不如说是卢奇菲尔或墨丘利乌斯的"魔鬼化"。墨丘利乌斯是原初携光者的一个轮廓——他自身绝不是光，而是一个ϕωσϕόρος，带来自然之光，即在新晨光之前裉色的月亮和星辰之光。关于这光，圣奥古斯丁说，除非造物主被其造物的爱所抛弃，它永远不会转向黑暗。但这，也属于昼夜的节律。如荷尔德林在《帕特莫斯》中所说：

and shamefully
且可耻地

A power wrests away the heart from us;
一种力量夺走我们的心；

For the Heavenly each demand sacrifice,
因为天上的每者都要求牺牲，

But if it should be withheld,
但若被拒付，

Never has that led to good.
从未导致善果。

[301] When all visible lights are extinguished one finds, according to the words of the wise Yajñavalkya, the light of the self. “What then is the light of man? Self is his light. It is by the light of the self that a man rests, goes forth, does his work and returns.”12 Thus, with Augustine, the first day of creation begins with self-knowledge, cognitio sui ipsius,13 by which is meant a knowledge not of the ego but of the self, that objective phenomenon of which the ego is the subject.14 Then, following the order of the days of creation in Genesis, comes knowledge of the firmament, of the earth, the sea, the plants, the stars, the animals of the water and air, and finally, on the sixth day, knowledge of the land animals and of ipsius hominis, of man himself. The cognitio matutina is self-knowledge, but the cognitio vespertina is knowledge of man.15 As Augustine describes it, the cognitio matutina gradually grows old as it loses itself in the “ten thousand things” and finally comes to man, although one would expect this to have happened already with the onset of self-knowledge. But if this were true, Augustine’s parable would have lost its meaning by contradicting itself. Such an obvious lapse cannot be ascribed to so gifted a man. His real meaning is that self-knowledge is the scientia Creatoris,16 a morning light revealed after a night during which consciousness slumbered, wrapped in the darkness of the unconscious. But the knowledge arising with this first light finally and inevitably becomes the scientia hominis, the knowledge of man, who asks himself: “Who is it that knows and understands everything? Why, it is myself.” That marks the coming of darkness,17 out of which arises the seventh day, the day of rest: “But the rest of God signifies the rest of those who rest in God.”18 The Sabbath is therefore the day on which man returns to God and receives anew the light of the cognitio matutina. And this day has no evening.19 From the symbological standpoint it may not be without significance that Augustine had in mind the pagan names of the days of the week. The growing darkness reaches its greatest intensity on the day of Venus (Friday), and changes into Lucifer on Saturn’s day. Saturday heralds the light which appears in full strength on Sun-day. As I have shown, Mercurius is closely related not only to Venus but more especially to Saturn. As Mercurius he is juvenis, as Saturn senex.
[301] 当一切可见之光熄灭时，按照智者耶若那跋伽的话，人找到自性之光。"那么人的光是什么？自性是他的光。凭借自性之光，人安息、出行、工作、归来。"12 因此，与奥古斯丁一样，创世的第一日始于自知——cognitio sui ipsius，13 这里所指的不是自我的知识，而是自性的知识——自性是那个客观现象，而自我是其主体。14 然后，按照《创世记》中创世日的顺序，是对穹苍的知识，对地、海、植物、星辰、水生和气生动物的知识，最后在第六日，是对陆生动物和对人自身（ipsius hominis）的知识。晨间之知（cognitio matutina）是自知，而晚间之知（cognitio vespertina）是关于人的知识。15 如奥古斯丁所描述的，晨间之知在迷失于"万物"中时逐渐衰老，最终到达人——尽管人们会预期这在自知开始时就已发生。但如果真是如此，奥古斯丁的寓言就因自相矛盾而失去意义。如此明显的疏漏不能归于如此有天赋之人。他的真正意思是：自知是造物主之知（scientia Creatoris），16 是在意识沉睡于无意识黑暗中的一夜之后显现的晨光。但随这第一道光升起的知识，最终且不可避免地成为人学之知（scientia hominis），即关于人的知识——人自问："那个知一切懂一切的是谁？是我自己。"这标志着黑暗的来临，17 从黑暗中升起第七日——安息之日："但上帝的安息意味着那些在上帝中安息者的安息。"18 因此安息日是人回归上帝并重新接受晨间之知之光的日子。而这一日没有黄昏。19 从象征学角度看，奥古斯丁心中所想的异教星期名称可能并非无关紧要。渐深的黑暗在维纳斯之日（星期五）达到最大强度，并在土星之日变为卢奇菲尔。星期六预示着光，在太阳之日（星期日）完全展现。如我所表明的，墨丘利乌斯不仅与维纳斯密切相关，更与土星相关。作为墨丘利乌斯他是少年（juvenis），作为土星他是老者（senex）。

[302] It seems to me that Augustine apprehended a great truth, namely that every spiritual truth gradually turns into something material, becoming no more than a tool in the hand of man. In consequence, man can hardly avoid seeing himself as a knower, yes, even as a creator, with boundless possibilities at his command. The alchemist was basically this sort of person, but much less so than modern man. An alchemist could still pray: “Purge the horrible darknesses of our mind,” but modern man is already so darkened that nothing beyond the light of his own intellect illuminates his world. “Occasus Christi, passio Christi.”20 That surely is why such strange things are happening to our much lauded civilization, more like a Götterdämmerung than any normal twilight.
[302] 在我看来，奥古斯丁领悟了一个伟大的真理：每一个精神真理都会逐渐变成物质性的东西，沦为不过是在人手中的工具。结果是，人几乎不可避免地把自己视为一个知者，甚至是一个造物者，拥有无限的可能性供其支配。炼金术士基本上就是这样的人，但远不及现代人。炼金术士还能祈祷："涤除我们心灵的可怕黑暗"，但现代人已经如此昏暗，以至于除了他自己理智之光外，没有什么能照亮他的世界。"基督的没落，基督的受难。"20 这无疑就是为什么我们备受赞颂的文明正在发生如此奇异的事情——更像是一场诸神的黄昏（Götterdämmerung），而非任何寻常的薄暮。

[303] Mercurius, that two-faced god, comes as the lumen naturae, the Servator and Salvator, only to those whose reason strives towards the highest light ever received by man, and who do not trust exclusively to the cognitio vespertina. For those who are unmindful of this light, the lumen naturae turns into a perilous ignis fatuus, and the psychopomp into a diabolical seducer. Lucifer, who could have brought light, becomes the father of lies whose voice in our time, supported by press and radio, revels in orgies of propaganda and leads untold millions to ruin.
[303] 墨丘利乌斯，那双面之神，作为自然之光（lumen naturae）、保存者和救主，只降临于那些理性 striving 向人类所曾接受之最高光的人，以及那些不唯独信赖晚间之知的人。对于那些忘记这光的人，自然之光变成了危险的鬼火（ignis fatuus），引魂者变成了魔鬼般的诱惑者。卢奇菲尔本可以带来光明，却成了谎言之父——在我们这个时代，他的声音借助报刊和广播，沉醉于宣传的狂欢，将无数百万引入毁灭。

Ⅴ


THE PHILOSOPHICAL TREE
哲学之树

All theory, my friend, is grey,
一切理论，朋友，都是灰色的，

But green life’s golden tree.
而生命之金树却是绿的。

Faust I
《浮士德》第一部





I
Ⅰ



INDIVIDUAL REPRESENTATIONS OF THE TREE SYMBOL
树象征的个别表现


[304] An image which frequently appears among the archetypal configurations of the unconscious is that of the tree or the wonder-working plant. When these fantasy products are drawn or painted, they very often fall into symmetrical patterns that take the form of a mandala. If a mandala may be described as a symbol of the self seen in cross section, then the tree would represent a profile view of it: the self depicted as a process of growth. I shall not discuss here the conditions under which these pictures are produced, for I have already said all that is necessary in my essays “A Study in the Process of Individuation” and “Concerning Mandala Symbolism.” The examples I now propose to give all come from a series of pictures in which my patients tried to express their inner experiences.
[304] 在无意识的原型配置中经常出现的形象是树或奇草。当这些幻想产物被画出或绘出时，它们常常落入对称的图式，呈曼陀罗的形态。如果曼陀罗可以被描述为横截面的自性象征，那么树则代表它的侧视图：自性被描绘为一个成长过程。我不打算在此讨论这些图像产生的条件，因为我已在《个体化过程研究》和《论曼陀罗象征》两文中说过了所有必要的话。我现在要给出的例子都来自我的病人试图表达其内在经验的一系列画作。

[305] In spite of the diversity of the tree symbol, a number of basic features may be established. In the first part of my essay I shall comment on the pictures that have been reproduced and then, in the second part, give an account of the philosophical tree in alchemy and its historical background. My case material has not been influenced in any way, for none of the patients had any previous knowledge of alchemy or of shamanism. The pictures were spontaneous products of creative fantasy, and their only conscious purpose was to express what happens when unconscious contents are taken over into consciousness in such a way that it is not overwhelmed by them and the unconscious not subjected to any distortion. Most of the pictures were done by patients who were under treatment, but some by persons who were not, or were no longer, under any therapeutic influence. I must emphasize that I carefully avoided saying anything in advance that might have had a suggestive effect. Nineteen of the thirty-two pictures were done at a time when I myself knew nothing of alchemy, and the rest before my book Psychology and Alchemy was published.
[305] 尽管树象征多种多样，但仍可确立若干基本特征。在本文的第一部分，我将对所复制的图画加以评述，然后在第二部分论述炼金术中的哲学之树及其历史背景。我的案例材料未受任何方式的影响，因为没有任何病人事先了解炼金术或萨满教。这些画是创造性幻想的自发产物，其唯一的意识目的是表达当无意识内容被纳入意识时会发生什么——以这种方式使意识不被其淹没，无意识也不受到任何扭曲。大多数画是在治疗中的病人所作，但有些是在未受治疗影响或不再受治疗影响的人所作。我必须强调，我小心地避免预先说出任何可能产生暗示效果的话。三十二幅画中有十九幅是在我自己对炼金术一无所知时所作的，其余的则在我的《心理学与炼金术》出版之前所作。





Figure 1
图1


[306] The tree stands by itself on an island in the sea. Its great size is indicated by the fact that the upper part of it is cut off by the edge of the picture. The buds and the little white flowers suggest the coming of spring, when the great tree, whose age far exceeds the span of human existence, will awaken to new life. The solitariness of the tree and its axial position in the centre of the picture bring to mind the world-tree and the world-axis—attributes with which the tree symbol is almost universally endowed. These traits give expression to the inner process at work in the painter, and show that it has nothing to do with his personal psychology. Here the tree represents a symbol that is universal and alien to the personal consciousness. It is possible, however, that the painter was making conscious use of the Christmas tree in order to illustrate his inner state.
[306] 这棵树独立矗立于海中的一座岛上。它之巨大可以从其上部被画面边缘截去这一事实看出。芽苞和白色小花预示着春天的到来——届时这棵远超人类寿命的巨树将苏醒为新生命。树的孤独及其在画面中央的轴心位置让人联想到世界树和世界轴——这些属性几乎被普遍赋予树象征。这些特征表达了绘画者内在运作的过程，并表明它与个人心理无关。在这里，树代表一个普遍的、对个人意识陌生的象征。不过，也有可能绘画者有意识地利用了圣诞树来说明自己的内在状态。





Figure 2
图2


[307] The abstract stylization and the position of the tree on the globe of the earth illustrate the feeling of spiritual isolation. To make up for this, the perfect symmetry of the crown points to a union of opposites. This is the motivating force and the goal of the individuation process. If the painter of such a picture neither identifies with the tree nor is assimilated by it,1 he will not succumb to the danger of an auto-erotic isolation, but will only be intensely aware that his ego personality is confronted with a symbolical process he must come to terms with because it is just as real and undeniable as his ego. One can deny and nullify this process in all sorts of ways, but in doing so all the values represented by the symbol are lost. A naïvely curious mind will naturally cast round for a rational explanation, and if it does not find one at once it either makes do with a facile and completely inadequate hypothesis or else turns away in disappointment. It seems to be very hard for people to live with riddles or to let them live, although one would think that life is so full of riddles as it is that a few more things we cannot answer would make no difference. But perhaps it is just this that is so unendurable, that there are irrational things in our own psyche which upset the conscious mind in its illusory certainties by confronting it with the riddle of its existence.
[307] 抽象的风格化以及树在地球仪上的位置说明了精神孤立感。为弥补这一点，树冠的完美对称指向了对立面的统一。这是个体化过程的动力和目标。如果这样一幅画的绘画者既不与树认同也不被其同化，1 他就不会陷入自恋式孤立的危险，而只会强烈地意识到他的自我人格面对着一个象征性的过程——他必须与之达成和解，因为它和他的自我一样真实且不可否认。人们可以以各种方式否定和取消这个过程，但这样做就会失去象征所代表的一切价值。天真的好奇之心自然会寻找理性的解释，如果找不到，它要么满足于一个肤浅而完全不充分的假设，要么就失望地转身离去。对人们来说，与谜团共处或让谜团存在似乎非常困难，尽管人们会认为生活本身已经充满了谜团，再多几个无法回答的问题也不会有什么区别。但也许正是这一点如此不可忍受：在我们自己的心灵中有非理性的东西，它们以其存在的谜题来扰乱意识及其虚幻的确定性。





Figure 3
图3


[308] The picture shows a tree of light that is at the same time a candelabrum. The abstract form of the tree points to its spiritual nature. The ends of the branches are lighted candles illuminating the darkness of an enclosed space, perhaps a cave or vault. The secret and hidden nature of the process is thus emphasized and its function made clear: the illumination of consciousness.
[308] 画面显示一棵光之树，同时也是一个烛台。树的抽象形式指向其精神性质。枝端是点亮的蜡烛，照亮了一个封闭空间的黑暗——也许是一个洞穴或穹窿。因此，过程的隐秘和隐藏性质被强调，其功能也被阐明：照亮意识。





Figure 4
图4


[309] Although cut out of gold-foil, the tree is realistic. It is still in the wintry, leafless state of sleep. It rises up against a cosmic background and bears in its branches a large golden ball, probably the sun. The gold indicates that though the painter does not yet have a living, conscious relation to this content, she nevertheless has an emotional intuition of its great value.
[309] 这棵树虽用金箔剪出，却是写实的。它仍处于冬季无叶的休眠状态。它以宇宙背景为衬托升起，枝头抱有一个大金球，可能是太阳。金色表明，尽管绘画者尚未与此内容有活生生的意识关系，但她对此内容的巨大价值有一种情感上的直觉。





Figure 5
图5


[310] The tree is leafless but bears little red flowers, harbingers of spring. The branches are tipped with flames, and fire leaps up from the water out of which the tree is growing. So the tree is also something like the jet of a fountain. The symbol of the fountain, the fontina, is known in alchemy; in the alchemical pictures it is often shown as a medieval town fountain,2 and the upright part in the middle would correspond to the tree. The union of fire and water expresses the union of opposites. The picture bears out the alchemical saying: “Our water is fire.”
[310] 这棵树无叶但缀有小红花，是春天的先驱。枝端以火焰为尖，火从树所生长的水中跃出。因此这棵树也像喷泉的水柱。喷泉（fontina）的象征在炼金术中是已知的；在炼金术的图像中，它常以中世纪城镇喷泉的形态展示，2 而中间直立的部分就对应于树。火与水的结合表达了对立面的统一。这幅画印证了炼金术的格言："我们的水即是火。"





Figure 6
图6


[311] The tree is red and looks like a branch of coral. It is not reflected in the water, but grows simultaneously downwards and upwards. The four mountains in the lower half of the picture are not reflections either, for their opposites are five mountains. This suggests that the lower world is not a mere reflection of the upper world, but that each is a world in itself. The tree stands in the middle between two walls of rock, representing the opposites. The four mountains also appear in Figure 24.
[311] 这棵树是红色的，看起来像珊瑚枝。它不在水中倒映，而是同时向下和向上生长。画面下半部的四座山也不是倒映，因为它们的对应物是五座山。这暗示下界不是上界的单纯倒映，而各自都是一个独立的世界。树矗立在两堵岩壁之间的中央，代表着对立面。这四座山也出现在图24中。





Figure 7
图7


[312] The tree has broken with irresistible force through the earth’s crust, heaving up mountainous boulders on either side. The painter is expressing an analogous process in himself, which runs its course of necessity and cannot be checked by any amount of resistance. Since the boulders are snow-capped mountains, the tree has the cosmic character of the world-tree.
[312] 这棵树以不可阻挡的力量冲破了地壳，将巨石向两侧掀起。绘画者表达的是自身中一个类似的过程——它出于必然性而运行，任何程度的抵抗都无法阻止。由于这些巨石是覆雪山峰，树具有世界树的宇宙特征。

The stone is a dark blue sapphire, but its connection with the sapphire stone in Ezekiel, which played a great role in ecclesiastical allegory, was not known to the painter. They therefore called the sapphirine flower (i.e., the lapis) “Hermaphroditi flos saphyricus.” Constancy and permanence are expressed not only in the age of the tree but also in its fruit, the lapis. Like a fruit, the lapis is at the same time a seed, and although the alchemists constantly stressed that the “seed of corn” dies in the earth, the lapis despite its seedlike nature is incorruptible. It represents, just as man does, a being that is forever dying yet eternal.

Figure 18
图18


[323] The picture shows an initial state in which the tree is unable to raise itself from the earth in spite of its cosmic nature. It is a case of regressive development, probably due to the fact that while the tree has a natural tendency to grow away from the earth into a cosmic space filled with strange astronomical and meteorological phenomena, this would mean reaching up into an eerie unearthly world and making contact with otherworldly things which are terrifying to the earthbound rationality of the natural man. The upward growth of the tree would not only endanger the supposed security of his earthly existence but would be a threat to his moral and spiritual inertia, because it would carry him into a new time and a new dimension where he could not get along without making considerable efforts at readaptation. The patient in these cases is held back not by mere cowardice, but by a largely justifiable fear that warns him of the exacting demands of the future, without his being aware of what these demands are or knowing the dangers of not fulfilling them. His anxious resistance and aversion seem quite groundless, and it is only too easy for him to rationalize them away and, with a little assistance, brush them aside like a troublesome insect. The result is just the psychic situation shown by our picture: an inturned growth which throws the supposedly solid earth into increasing turmoil. Secondary fantasies then arise which, according to the patient’s disposition, revolve round sexuality or the power drive or both. This leads sooner or later to the formation of neurotic symptoms and to the almost unavoidable temptation for both patient and analyst to take these fantasies seriously as causative factors and thus to overlook the real task.
[323] 这幅画展示了一种初始状态——树尽管具有宇宙性质，却无法从大地中抬起。这是一种退行性发展，可能是因为：虽然树有远离大地、向充满奇异天文和气象现象的宇宙空间生长的自然趋势，但这将意味着伸入一个令人毛骨悚然的超世世界，与那些对大地束缚的自然人理性来说可怕的他世事物接触。树的向上生长不仅会危及其尘世存在的所谓安全感，而且会威胁其道德和精神的惰性，因为它将把他带入一个新的时间和一个新的维度，在那里不做出相当大的再适应努力就无法应对。在这些案例中，病人被阻遏并非仅出于懦弱，而是出于一种大体上有道理的恐惧——它警告他未来的苛刻要求，而他并不知道这些要求是什么，也不知道不满足它们的危险。他焦虑的抵抗和厌恶似乎完全没有根据，他很容易将它们理性化掉，并在些许帮助下像掸走一只烦人的虫子一样将它们抛开。结果正是我们这幅画所展示的心理状况：一种向内生长，将本应坚实的大地搅得越来越不安。然后次生幻想产生，根据病人的气质，围绕性或权力欲或两者旋转。这迟早导致神经症症状的形成，以及病人和分析师几乎不可避免的诱惑——将这些幻想当作因果因素认真对待，从而忽视真正的任务。

[325] The tree stands in isolation dominating the top of a mountain. It is thick with leaves and has in its trunk a doll swathed in multicoloured wrappings. She was conscious of having thought of Picasso, whose style was apparently suggested by the harlequin’s dress. The association probably has a deeper meaning and is not just a superficial combination of ideas. It was this same impression of irrationality that led to the regressive development in the two previous pictures. All three cases are concerned with a process which the modern mind finds extremely disturbing, and not a few of my patients have openly confessed their fear of any such autonomous development of their psychic contents. In these cases it is of the greatest therapeutic value if one can demonstrate to them the historicity of their apparently unique and unassimilable experiences. When a patient begins to feel the inescapable nature of his inner development, he may easily be overcome by a panic fear that he is slipping helplessly into some kind of madness he can no longer understand. More than once I have had to reach for a book on my shelves, bring down an old alchemist, and show my patient his terrifying fantasy in the form in which it appeared four hundred years ago. This has a calming effect, because the patient then sees that he is not alone in a strange world which nobody understands, but is part of the great stream of human history, which has experienced countless times the very things that he regards as a pathological proof of his craziness.

I will only mention in passing that, besides this, the number four possesses special mathematical properties. The quaternary elements in our picture, as well as accentuating the light-symbol, amplify it in such a way that it is not difficult to see what is meant: an acceptance of wholeness by the little female figure, an intuitive apprehension of the self.
[330] 数字四，如同化圆为方，并非偶然，这就是为什么——举一个连我的批评者都知道的例子——方向不是三个或五个，而恰恰是四个。我只想附带提一句，除此之外，数字四还具有特殊的数学性质。我们画中的四元元素，除了强调光之象征外，还以这样的方式扩展了它，使得不难看出其含义：小人形女性形象对整体性的接纳，对自性的直觉把握。

[331] A still later stage is shown here. The female figure is no longer just the recipient or bearer of the light-symbol but has been drawn into it. The personality is more powerfully affected than in the previous picture. This increases the danger of identification with the self—a danger not to be taken lightly. Anyone who has passed through such a development will feel tempted to see the goal of his experiences and efforts in union with the self. Indeed, there are suggestive precedents for this, and in the present case it is altogether possible. But there are certain factors in the picture which enable the painter to distinguish her ego from the self. She was an American woman who was influenced by the mythology of the Pueblo Indians: the corn-cobs characterize the female figure as a goddess. She is fastened to the tree by a snake, and thus forms an analogy to the crucified Christ, who, as the self, was sacrificed for earthly humanity, just as Prometheus was chained to the rock. Man’s efforts to achieve wholeness correspond, as the divine myth shows, to a voluntary sacrifice of the self to the bondage of earthly existence. Here I will only point out this correspondence without going into it further.
[331] 这里展示了一个更晚的阶段。女性形象不再仅仅是光之象征的接受者或承载者，而是被拉入了其中。人格比前一幅画受到更强有力的影响。这增加了与自性认同的危险——一个不可轻视的危险。任何经历过这样一种发展的人都会受到诱惑，将他的经验和努力的目标视为与自性的合一。确实，有暗示性的先例，在本案中完全有可能。但画中有某些因素使绘画者能够区分她的自我与自性。她是一位受普韦布洛印第安人神话影响的美国女性：玉米穗将女性形象特征为女神。她被一条蛇缚于树上，从而形成了与被钉十字架的基督的类比——基督作为自性为尘世人类而牺牲，正如普罗米修斯被锁在岩石上。人实现整体性的努力，如神圣神话所示，对应于自性对尘世存在束缚的自愿牺牲。在这里我只想指出这一对应，不再深入。

[332] In this picture, then, there are so many elements of the divine myth that unless the patient’s consciousness were utterly blinded (and there are no signs of this) she could easily discriminate between ego and self. At this stage it is important not to succumb to an inflation, such as would inevitably supervene with all its very unpleasant consequences if, at the moment when the self became recognizable, she identified with it and thus blinded herself to the insight she had attained. If the natural impulse to identify with the self is recognized, one then has a good chance of freeing oneself from a state of unconsciousness. But if this opportunity is overlooked or not used, the situation does not remain the same as before but gives rise to a repression coupled with dissociation of the personality. The development of consciousness which the realization of the self might have led to turns into a regression. I must emphasize that this realization is not just an intellectual act but is primarily a moral one, in comparison with which intellectual understanding is of secondary importance. For this reason, the symptoms I have described can also be observed in patients who, from inferior motives which they will not admit, refuse a task that has been laid upon them by fate.
[332] 因此，这幅画中有如此多的神圣神话元素，除非病人的意识完全盲目（没有迹象表明这一点），否则她可以轻易区分自我与自性。在这个阶段，重要的是不要屈服于膨胀——如果在自性变得可辨认的那一刻她与之认同，从而对已达成的洞见视而不见，这种膨胀就会不可避免地伴随其一切非常不愉快的后果而来。如果与自性认同的自然冲动被认识到，人就有很好的机会摆脱无意识状态。但如果这一机会被忽视或未被利用，情况不会保持原样，而是产生压抑并伴随人格的解离。自性的实现本可导致的意识发展转变为退行。我必须强调，这一实现不仅仅是理智行为，而首先是一种道德行为——与之相比，理智理解是次要的。正因如此，我所描述的症状也可以在那些出于不轨动机、不愿承认而拒绝命运赋予之任务的病人身上观察到。

[333] I would like to draw attention to a further peculiarity: the tree has no leaves, and its branches could just as well be roots. All its vitality is concentrated in the centre, in the human figure that represents its flower and fruit. A person whose roots are above as well as below is thus like a tree growing simultaneously downwards and upwards. The goal is neither height nor depth, but the centre.
[333] 我想提请注意一个进一步的特性：树没有叶子，它的枝条完全也可以是根。它的全部活力集中在中心——代表其花与果的人形上。一个根在上又在下的人，就像一棵同时向下和向上生长的树。目标既不是高度也不是深度，而是中心。

图26


[334] The idea developed in the previous picture reappears here in slightly variant form. This idea may truly be said to be in the process of delineating itself, for the conscious mind of the patient follows only a vague feeling which gradually takes shape in the act of drawing. She would have been quite unable to formulate beforehand, in a clear concept, what she wanted to express. The structure of the picture is a mandala divided into four, with the midpoint displaced downwards, beneath the feet of the figure. The figure stands in the upper section and thus belongs to the realm of light. This mandala is an inversion of the traditional Christian cross, whose long upright is below the cross-beam. We must conclude from the picture that the self was realized first of all as an ideal figure of light which nonetheless takes the form of an inverted Christian cross. Whereas the latter’s point of intersection is near the top, so that the goal of unconscious striving towards the centre is displaced upwards, the downward glance of the figure shows that her goal should lie below. The short upright beam of the cross of light rests on the black earth, and the figure holds in her left hand a black fish drawn from the dark sphere. The mudrā-like,7 hesitant gesture of the right hand, directed towards the fish coming from the left (i.e., from the unconscious), is characteristic of the patient, who had studied theosophy and was therefore under Indian influence. The fish has a soteriological significance whether conceived in Christian or in Indian terms (as the fish of Manu and as an avatar of Vishnu). There is reason to conjecture (see Figure 29) that the patient was acquainted with the Bhagavadgītā, which says (X, 31): “Among fishes I am Makara.” Makara is a dolphin or a species of Leviathan, and is one of the symbols of the svādhisthāna-chakra in Tantric yoga. This centre is localized in the bladder and is characterized as the water region by the fish and moon symbols. As the chakras are presumably equivalent to earlier localizations of consciousness (the anāhata-chakra, for instance, corresponding to the ϕρἑνες of the Greeks),8 svādhisthāna is probably the earliest localization of all. From this region comes the fish symbol with its age-old numen. We are reminded of the “days of Creation,” of the time when consciousness arose, when the primordial unity of being was barely disturbed by the twilight of reflection,9 and man swam like a fish in the ocean of the unconscious. In this sense the fish signifies a restoration of the pleromatic paradisal state or, in the language of Tibetan Tantrism, of the Bardo.10
[334] 前一幅画中发展的思想在这里以略微变异的形式重新出现。可以说这一思想确实正在自我勾勒，因为病人的意识只跟随一种模糊的感觉，它在绘画过程中逐渐成形。她完全无法事先以清晰的概念阐述她想表达的东西。画面的结构是一个四分的曼陀罗，中点下移到形象的脚下。形象矗立在上部，因此属于光的领域。这个曼陀罗是传统基督教十字架的倒置——后者长的竖梁在横梁之下。我们必须从画中得出结论：自性首先被实现为一个理想的光之形象，然而却以倒置的基督教十字架的形态出现。后者的交点靠近顶部，使无意识向中心追求的目标上移，而形象向下的目光表明她的目标应在下方。光之十字架短的竖梁立于黑色大地之上，形象左手持一条从黑暗领域中取出的黑鱼。右手那似手印（mudrā）般的、犹豫的手势，7 指向从左侧（即从无意识）而来的鱼——这是病人的特征，她研究过通灵术，因此受到印度影响。鱼具有救赎论意义，无论是以基督教还是印度术语来构想（作为摩奴之鱼和作为毗湿奴的化身）。有理由推测（见图29）病人熟悉《薄伽梵歌》，其中说（X, 31）："于鱼中我是摩伽罗。"摩伽罗是海豚或一种利维坦，是坦特罗瑜伽中 svādhisthāna-chakra 的象征之一。该中心定位于膀胱，以鱼和月的象征特征为水之领域。既然脉轮大概等同于较早的意识定位（例如 anāhata-chakra 对应于希腊人的ϕρένες），8 svādhisthāna 可能是最早的定位。鱼之象征及其古老灵力（numen）即来自这一区域。我们想起"创世之日"，意识升起之时，存在的原初一元性几乎未被反思的微光所干扰，9 人如同鱼一般在无意识的海洋中游泳。在这个意义上，鱼象征着丰饶乐园状态的恢复，或者用西藏坦特罗的语言说，中阴（Bardo）的恢复。10

[335] The plants at the foot of the figure are really rooted in the air. Tree, tree nymph, and plants are all lifted up from the earth or, more probably, are on the point of coming down to it. This is also suggested by the fish as emissary of the deep. The situation is in my experience an unusual one and may be due to theosophical influences. Filling the conscious mind with ideal conceptions is a characteristic feature of Western theosophy, but not the confrontation with the shadow and the world of darkness. One does not become enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making the darkness conscious. The latter procedure, however, is disagreeable and therefore not popular.
[335] 形象脚下的植物实际上是悬浮在空中的。树、树精和植物都从大地上升起，或者更可能即将降落。来自深渊的使者——鱼——也暗示了这一点。根据我的经验，这是一种不寻常的情况，可能是通灵术影响所致。用理想概念填充意识是西方通灵术的特征，但不是面对阴影和黑暗世界。人不是通过想象光之形象而开悟的，而是通过使黑暗变得有意识。然而后者是令人不快的，因此不受欢迎。

[336] Unlike the previous picture, this one is thoroughly Western, although it comes into the archetypal category of the god’s birth from the tree or lotus blossom. The archaic plant world of the carboniferous era illustrates the mood the painter was in when she intuitively apprehended the birth of the self. The human figure growing out of the archaic plant represents the union and quintessence of the four heads at its base, in agreement with the alchemical view that the lapis is composed of four elements. Awareness of the archetype imbues the experience with a primeval character. The division of the plant into six segments, like so much else in the realm of fantasy, may be purely accidental. Nevertheless, it should not be forgotten that the number six (the senarius) was considered in ancient times “aptissimus generationi” (most fit for generation).11

(The alchemical parallel to this is the “black sun.”)12 This means that the dark principle, or shadow, has been integrated and is now felt as a kind of centre in the body. As birds represent winged thoughts, we must conclude that the female figure progressively detached itself from the world of thought as the centre was displaced downwards, and that the thoughts have consequently returned to their natural element. She and her thoughts were identical before, with the result that she was raised above the earth as though she were an aerial being, while her thoughts lost their freedom of flight, since they had to support the whole weight of a human being in the air.
[338] 众多鸟绕树飞翔。由于鸟代表有翼的思想，我们必须得出结论：随着中心向下位移，女性形象逐渐脱离了思想世界，思想因此回到了它们的自然元素。她和她的思想此前是同一的，结果她被凌空托起如同空中存在，而她的思想失去了飞翔的自由，因为它们必须在空中支撑一个人的全部重量。

[339] The process of separation from the world of thought continues. A masculine daemon,14 who has obviously woken up all of a sudden, reveals himself with an air of triumph: he is the animus, the personification of masculine thinking in a woman (and of her masculine side in general). The patient’s previous state of suspension turns out to have been an animus possession, which is now sloughed off. Differentiation between her feminine consciousness and her animus means liberation for both. The sentence “I am the Game of the gambler” probably refers to Bhagavadgītā X, 36: “I am the game of dice.”10 Krishna says this of himself. The section in which it occurs begins with the words (X, 20-21): “I am the self, O Gudākesha! seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning and the middle and the end also of all beings. I am Vishnu among the Adityas;16 the beaming sun among the shining bodies.”
[339] 与思想世界分离的过程继续。一个男性精灵，14 显然是突然醒来的，以胜利的姿态现身：他是阿尼玛斯——女性身上男性思维的拟人化（也是她男性面的一般拟人化）。病人先前的悬浮状态原来是一种阿尼玛斯附身，现在被脱掉了。她的女性意识与阿尼玛斯的分化意味着两者的解放。"我是赌徒之戏"这句话可能指的是《薄伽梵歌》X, 36："我是赌骰之戏。"10 克里希纳如此说到自己。该段所在的部分以如下话语开始（X, 20-21）："我是自性，古塔凯沙啊！坐于一切众生心中。我是一切众生的始、中和终。于阿底提耶中我是毗湿奴；16 于发光体中我是灼耀之日。"

[340] Like Krishna, Agni is the game of dice in the Shatapatha-Brāhmana of the Yajur-Veda: “He (the Adhvaryu)17 throws down the dice, with ‘Hallowed by Svāhā,18 strive ye with Surya’s10 rays for the middlemost place among brethren!’ For that gaming ground is the same as ‘ample Agni,’ and those dice are his coals, thus it is him (Agni) he thereby pleases.”20
[340] 如同克里希纳，阿耆尼在《耶柔吠陀》的《百道梵书》中也是赌骰之戏："他（祭司）17 掷下骰子，念道：'以娑婆诃祝圣，18 尔等与苏利耶之 19 光争夺众兄弟中的中间位置！'因为那赌场即是'广阔的阿耆尼'，而那些骰子即是他的炭火，因此他由此取悦他（阿耆尼）。"20

[341] Both texts relate light, sun, and fire, as well as the god, to the game of dice. Similarly the Atharva-Veda speaks of the “brilliancy that is in the chariot, in the dice, in the strength of the bull, in the wind, Parjanya,21 and in the fire of Varuna.”22 The “brilliancy” corresponds to what is known in primitive psychology as “mana,” and in the psychology of the unconscious as “libido investment” or “emotional value” or “feeling tone.” In point of emotional intensity, which is a factor of decisive importance for the primitive consciousness, the most heterogeneous things—rain, storm, fire, the strength of the bull, and the passionate game of dice—can be identical. In emotional intensity, game and gambler coincide.
[341] 两部经文都将光、太阳和火以及神与赌骰之戏联系起来。同样，《阿闼婆吠陀》谈到"在战车中、在骰子中、在公牛的力量中、在风中、帕尔贾尼亚 21 中以及在伐楼拿之火中的光辉"。22 这种"光辉"对应于原始心理学中所谓的"玛那"（mana），在无意识心理学中称为"力比多投注"或"情感价值"或"感情色调"。就情感强度而言——这对原始意识是一个决定性因素——最异质的东西——雨、暴风、火、公牛的力量和热烈的赌骰游戏——可以是同一的。在情感强度上，游戏与赌者重合。

[342] This train of thought may help to explain the mood of the picture, which expresses liberation and relief. The patient evidently felt this moment as a breath of the divine numen. As the Bhagavadgītā text makes clear, Krishna is the self, with which the patient’s animus identifies. This identification is a regular occurrence when the shadow, the dark side, has not been sufficiently realized. Like every archetype, the animus has a Janus face, and besides this the limitation of being a merely masculine principle. He is therefore quite unfitted to represent totality, whether of God or the self. He must be content with an intermediate position. The generalizations characteristic of Indian theosophy, however, induced the patient, by a kind of psychological short-circuit, to identify the animus at least provisionally with wholeness, and to put him in the place of the self.
[342] 这一思路可能有助于解释画中的情绪——它表达了解放和释然。病人显然将这一时刻感受为神圣灵力的一丝气息。如《薄伽梵歌》经文所表明的，克里希纳是自性，病人的阿尼玛斯与之认同。当阴影——黑暗面——未被充分实现时，这种认同是经常发生的。如同每个原型，阿尼玛斯有一张雅努斯之面，此外还有仅作为男性原则的局限。因此他完全不适合代表整体性——无论是上帝的还是自性的。他必须满足于一个中间位置。然而，印度通灵术所特有的概括化倾向，通过一种心理短路，诱使病人至少暂时将阿尼玛斯与整体性认同，并将他置于自性的位置。

II



ON THE HISTORY AND INTERPRETATION OF THE TREE SYMBOL
树象征的历史与诠释



1. THE TREE AS AN ARCHETYPAL IMAGE
1. 树作为原型形象


[350] After having given some examples of spontaneously produced, modern tree symbols in the first part of this essay, I should like, in the second part, to say something about the historical background of the tree symbol in order to justify my title “The Philosophical Tree.” Although it will be obvious to anyone acquainted with the material that my examples are nothing more than special instances of a widely disseminated tree symbolism, it is nevertheless of importance, in interpreting the individual symbols, to know something about their historical antecedents. Like all archetypal symbols, the symbol of the tree has undergone a development of meaning in the course of the centuries. It is far removed from the original meaning of the shamanistic tree, even though certain basic features prove to be unalterable. The psychoid form underlying any archetypal image retains its character at all stages of development, though empirically it is capable of endless variations. The outward form of the tree may change in the course of time, but the richness and vitality of a symbol are expressed more in its change of meaning. The aspect of meaning is therefore essential to the phenomenology of the tree symbol. Taken on average, the commonest associations to its meaning are growth, life, unfolding of form in a physical and spiritual sense, development, growth from below upwards and from above downwards, the maternal aspect (protection, shade, shelter, nourishing fruits, source of life, solidity, permanence, firm-rootedness, but also being “rooted to the spot”), old age, personality,1 and finally death and rebirth.
[350] 在本文第一部分给出了一些自发产生的现代树象征的例子之后，我想在第二部分谈谈树象征的历史背景，以证明我"哲学之树"这一标题的合理性。虽然对于熟悉材料的人来说，我的例子不过是一种广泛传播的树象征主义的特例，但了解其历史前因对于诠释个别象征仍然是重要的。如同一切原型象征，树的象征在几个世纪的过程中经历了含义的发展。它已远离萨满树的原始含义，尽管某些基本特征被证明是不可改变的。任何原型形象底层的心理oid形式在一切发展阶段上都保持其特征，尽管在经验上它能够无限变化。树的外在形式可能随时间而改变，但象征的丰富性和活力更多地表现于其含义的变化。因此含义方面对于树象征的现象学是本质性的。总的来说，最常见的含义联想是：成长、生命、在物理和精神意义上的形态展开、发展、自下而上和自上而下的生长、母性方面（保护、遮蔽、庇护、滋养的果实、生命之源、稳固、持久、扎根——但也有"被钉在原地"）、年老、人格，1 以及最终死亡与重生。

Even the layman reading this essay will be struck by the amount of material from fairytale, myth, and poetry that appears in the illustrations. In this connection it is astonishing how relatively seldom the persons I interrogated were conscious of sources of this kind. The main reasons for this are: (1) In general, people think little, if at all, about the origins of dream images, and still less about myth motifs. (2) The sources have been forgotten. (3) The sources were never in any sense conscious; that is to say, the images are new, archetypal creations.
[351] 这一特征描述是多年来对个别病人陈述的研究积累。即使是阅读本文的外行人也会对插图中大量出现于童话、神话和诗歌中的材料感到震惊。在这方面，令人惊讶的是我所询问的人相对而言多么少地意识到此类来源。其主要原因是：（1）一般来说，人们很少思考——如果有的话——梦象的起源，更少思考神话主题的起源。（2）来源已被遗忘。（3）来源在任何意义上都从未是有意识的；也就是说，这些形象是新的、原型的创造。

[352] The third possibility is much less rare than one might suppose. On the contrary, it occurs so frequently that comparative research into symbols becomes unavoidable in elucidating the spontaneous products of the unconscious. The widely held view that mythologems or myth motifs2 are always connected with a tradition proves untenable, since they may reappear anywhere, at any time, and in any individual regardless of tradition. An image can be considered archetypal when it can be shown to exist in the records of human history, in identical form and with the same meaning. Two extremes must be distinguished here: (1) The image is clearly defined and is consciously connected with a tradition. (2) The image is without doubt autochthonous, there being no possibility let alone probability of a tradition.3 Every degree of mutual contamination may be found between these two extremes.
[352] 第三种可能性比人们想象的要少见得多。相反，它发生得如此频繁，以至于对符号的比较研究在阐释无意识的自发产物时变得不可避免。广泛流传的观点认为神话素或神话主题2 总是与传统相连，这被证明是站不住脚的，因为它们可以在任何地方、任何时间、任何个人身上重新出现，不论传统如何。当一个形象可以被证明以相同的形式和相同的含义存在于人类历史的记录中时，它就可以被认为是原型的。这里必须区分两个极端：（1）形象是明确定义的，并与传统有意识地相连。（2）形象毫无疑问是本土的，不存在传统的可能性，更不用说概率了。3 在这两个极端之间可以找到各种程度的相互渗透。

[353] In consequence of the collective nature of the image it is often impossible to establish its full range of meaning from the associative material of a single individual. But since it is of importance to do this for practical therapeutic purposes, the necessity of comparative research into symbols for medical psychology becomes evident on these grounds also.4 For this purpose the investigator must turn back to those periods in human history when symbol formation still went on unimpeded, that is, when there was still no epistemological criticism of the formation of images, and when, in consequence, facts that in themselves were unknown could be expressed in definite visual form. The period of this kind closest to us is that of medieval natural philosophy, which reached its zenith in the seventeenth century, and in the eighteenth century gradually left the field to science. It attained its most significant development in alchemy and Hermetic philosophy. Here, as in a reservoir, were collected the most enduring and the most important mythologems of the ancient world. It is significant that Hermetic philosophy was, in the main, practised by physicians.5
[353] 由于形象的集体性质，通常不可能仅从单一个体的联想材料中确立其全部含义范围。但由于出于实际治疗目的这样做很重要，因此医学心理学中进行符号比较研究的必要性也在此基礎上变得明显。4 为此目的，研究者必须回溯到人类历史上那些象征形成仍不受阻碍地进行的时期，即当时还没有对形象形成的认识论批判，因此那些本身未知的事实可以用确定的视觉形式表达。离我们最近的这种时期是中世纪自然哲学，它在十七世纪达到巅峰，在十八世纪逐渐将领域让给了科学。它在炼金术和赫尔墨斯哲学中获得了最重要的发展。在这里，如同在一个蓄水池中，收集了古代世界最持久和最重要的神话素。值得注意的是，赫尔墨斯哲学主要由医生所实践。5





2. THE TREE IN THE TREATISE OF JODOCUS GREVERUS
2. 约多库斯·格雷弗鲁斯论著中的树


[354] I would now like to show how the phenomenology of the tree is reflected in the medium of the epoch immediately preceding the one just mentioned. Holmberg,1 who wrote a comprehensive study of the tree of life, says that it is “mankind’s most magnificent legend,” thus confirming that the tree occupies a central position in mythology and is so widespread that its ramifications are to be found everywhere. The tree appears frequently in the medieval alchemical texts and in general represents the growth of the arcane substance and its transformation into the philosophical gold (or whatever the name of the goal may be). We read in the treatise of Pelagios that Zosimos had said the transformation process was like “a well-tended tree, a watered plant, which, beginning to ferment because of the plentiful water, and sprouting in the humidity and warmth of the air, puts forth blossoms and fruits by virtue of the great sweetness and special quality (ποιότητι) of nature.”2
[354] 我现在想展示树的现象学如何反映在刚刚所述时代的紧前一个时代的媒介中。霍尔姆贝格1 写了一部关于生命之树的全面研究，说它是"人类最壮丽的传说"，从而证实了树在神话学中占据中心地位，且其分布如此广泛，以至于其分支可以在任何地方找到。树在中世纪炼金术文献中频繁出现，一般代表秘术物质的生长及其向哲学之金的转化（或无论目标被称为什么）。我们在佩拉吉奥斯的论著中读到佐西莫斯曾说转化过程如同"一棵精心照料的树，一株浇过水的植物，它因丰沛的水分而开始发酵，在空气的湿度和温暖中萌芽，凭借自然的巨大甜美和特殊品质（ποιότητα）而开出花和果。"2

[355] A typical example of this process is to be found in the treatise of Jodocus Greverus, which was first printed in Leiden, 1588.3 The whole opus is depicted as the sowing and nurturing of the tree in a well-tended garden, into which nothing extraneous might enter. The soil consists of purified Mercurius; Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and Venus form the trunk (or trunks)4 of the tree, and the sun and moon supply their seeds. These planetary names refer partly to the corresponding metals, but we can see what they meant from the author’s qualifying remark: “For there enters into this work not the common gold, nor the common Mercurius, nor the common silver, nor anything else that is common, but [the metals] of the Philosophers.”5 The ingredients of the work might therefore be anything. At any rate they are imaginary ones, even though they were expressed outwardly by chemical substances. The planetary names refer ultimately not only to metals but, as every alchemist knew, to the (astrological) temperaments, that is, to psychic factors. These consist of instinctive dispositions which give rise to specific fantasies and desires and so reveal their character. Avarice as one of the original motives of the royal art is still apparent in the term aurum non vulgi, though it is just here that we discern the change of motivation and the displacement of the goal to another plane. In the parable that comes at the end of the treatise the wise old man says to the adept: “Son, lay aside the snares of worldly appetites.”6 Even when, as is often undoubtedly the case, the procedure given by an author has no other aim than the production of the common gold, the psychic meaning of the opus nevertheless comes through in the symbolic nomenclature he employs in spite of his conscious attitude. In the treatise of Greverus this stage has been overcome and it is openly admitted that the goal of the opus is “not of this world.” Accordingly, at the conclusion of his treatise on the “universal process of our work,”7 the author avows that it is a “gift of God, containing the secret of the undivided oneness of the Holy Trinity. O most excellent science, theatre of all nature and its anatomy, earthly astrology,8 proof of God’s omnipotence, testimony to the resurrection of the dead, example of the remission of sins, infallible proof of the judgment to come and mirror of eternal blessedness.”9
[355] 这一过程的一个典型例子见于约多库斯·格雷弗鲁斯的论著，该论著于1588年在莱顿首次印刷。3 整个大业被描绘为在一座精心照料的花园中播种和培育树，其中不得有任何外物进入。土壤由纯化的墨丘利乌斯组成；土星、木星、火星和金星构成树干（或多根树干）4，太阳和月亮提供它们的种子。这些行星名称部分指相应的金属，但我们可以从作者的限定性评论中看出它们的含义："因为进入这项工作的不是普通的金，不是普通的墨丘利乌斯，不是普通的银，也不是任何其他普通的东西，而是哲学家的〔金属〕。"5 因此这项工作的原料可以是任何东西。无论如何它们是想象性的，即使它们在外表上以化学物质来表达。行星名称最终不仅指金属，而且——如每位炼金术士所知——指（星象学的）气质，即心理因素。这些由本能倾向组成，它们产生特定的幻想和欲望，从而揭示其性格。贪婪作为王艺的原始动机之一仍可在 aurum non vulgi（非普通之金）一词中看出，但正是在这里我们辨别出动机的变化和目标向另一层面的转移。在论著结尾的寓言中，智慧老人对工匠说："孩子，放下世俗欲望的罗网。"6 即使当——如无疑经常是的那样——一位作者给出的程序除了制造普通金之外没有其他目的，大业的心理含义仍然通过他在象征性命名法中所用的符号而显露出来，尽管他有意识的态度如此。在格雷弗鲁斯的论著中，这一阶段已被克服，公开承认大业的目标是"不属这世界的"。因此，在他关于"我们工作的普遍过程"7 的论著的结尾，作者宣称它是"上帝的恩赐，包含神圣三一不可分割之统一的秘密。哦，最卓越的科学，一切自然及其解剖学的剧场，地上的星象学，8 上帝全能的证明，死者复活的见证，罪孽赦免的范例，未来审判的可靠证明，永恒福乐的镜子。"9

[356] A modern reader of this hymnlike paean of praise cannot help feeling that it is exaggerated and out of key, for one cannot imagine how the science of alchemy could, for instance, contain the Holy Trinity. Such enthusiastic comparisons with the mysteries of religion had already caused offence in the Middle Ages.10 Far from being rarities, they even became a leitmotiv of certain treatises in the seventeenth century, which however had their precursors in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. In my view they should not always be taken as spurious mystification, for the authors had something definite in mind. They obviously saw a parallel between the alchemical process and religious ideas—a parallel which is certainly not immediately perceptible to us. A bridge between two such very different realms of thought can be constructed only when we take into account the factor common to both: the tertium comparationis is the psychological element. Naturally an alchemist would have defended himself just as indignantly against the charge that his ideas about chemical substances were fantasies as would a metaphysician today, who still thinks that his statements amount to more than anthropomorphisms. Just as the alchemist was unable to distinguish between things as they are and the notions he had about them, so the modern metaphysician still believes that his views give valid expression to their metaphysical object. It obviously never occurred to either of them that a great diversity of views concerning their respective objects has been held since earliest times. But unlike metaphysicians, and unlike theologians in particular, the alchemists displayed no polemical tendencies; at most they lamented the obscurity of the authors whom they could not understand.
[356] 这首赞美诗般的颂词的现代读者不禁会觉得它是夸张的、不合拍的，因为人们无法想象炼金术科学如何能——比如说——包含神圣三一。这种与宗教奥秘的热情比较在中世纪就已经引起了反感。10 它们并非罕见，甚至在十七世纪的某些论著中成为主导动机，但其先驱可追溯到十三和十四世纪。在我看来，它们不应总被视为虚假的神秘化，因为作者们心中有确定的东西。他们显然看到了炼金术过程与宗教观念之间的平行——这种平行对我们来说当然不是立即可感知的。只有在考虑两者共同的因素时，才能在两个如此不同的思想领域之间架起桥梁：第三项比较物（tertium comparationis）是心理要素。自然，一位炼金术士会像今天的形而上学者一样愤慨地为自己辩护，反对他关于化学物质的想法是幻想的指控——后者仍然认为他的陈述不仅仅是拟人化。正如炼金术士无法区分事物本身和他对它们的观念一样，现代形而上学者仍然相信他的观点对其形而上学对象给出了有效的表达。他们两个显然都没有想到，自最早的时候起，关于各自对象的看法就一直存在着巨大的多样性。但与形而上学者——特别是神学家——不同，炼金术士没有表现出论战倾向；他们至多哀叹他们无法理解的作者的晦涩。

[357] It is clear to every reasonable person that in both cases we are concerned primarily with ideas born of fantasy—which is not to say that their unknown object does not exist. No matter what the ideas refer to, they are always organized by the same psychic laws, that is, by the archetypes. In their way the alchemists realized this when they insisted on the parallelism between their ideas and religious ones, as when Greverus compares his synthetic process with the Trinity. The common archetype in this case is the number three. As a Paracelsist, he must have been acquainted with the Paracelsan triad of sulphur, salt, and Mercurius. Sulphur belongs to the sun or represents it, and salt stands in the same relation to the moon. However, he says nothing about a synthesis of this kind.11 Sun and moon supply the seeds that are planted in the earth (= Mercurius), and presumably the four other planets form the trunk of the tree. The four that are to be united into one refer to the tetrasomia of Greek alchemy, where, corresponding to the planets, they stand for lead, tin, iron, and copper.12 Hence in his process of henosis (unification or synthesis), as Michael Maier correctly understood it,13 what Greverus had in mind was not the three basic Paracelsan substances but the ancient tetrasomia, which at the end of his treatise he compares with the “union of persons in the Holy Trinity.” For him the triad of sun, moon, and Mercurius was the starting point, the initial material as it were, in so far as it signified the seed of the tree and the earth in which it was sown. This is the so-called coniunctio triptativa. But here he is concerned with the coniunctio tetraptiva,14 whereby the four are joined in the “union of persons.” This is a characteristic example of the dilemma of three and four, which plays a great role in alchemy as the well-known axiom of Maria Prophetissa.15
[357] 每个理性的人都能清楚地看到，在这两种情况下我们主要关注的是幻想产生的观念——这并不是说它们未知的对象不存在。无论这些观念指向什么，它们总是由相同的心理法则——即原型——来组织的。炼金术士们以自己的方式意识到了这一点，当他们坚持他们的观念与宗教观念之间的平行主义时——如格雷弗鲁斯将他的合成过程与三一相比较。在这种情况下，共同的原型是数字三。作为帕拉塞尔苏斯主义者，他一定熟悉帕拉塞尔苏斯的硫磺、盐和墨丘利乌斯三合一。硫磺属于太阳或代表太阳，盐与月亮有同样的关系。然而，他没有提到这种合成的任何内容。11 太阳和月亮提供种子，播种在土中（=墨丘利乌斯），而其他四个行星大概构成树干。要合四为一的四个指的是希腊炼金术的四体（tetrasomia），在那里对应于行星，它们代表铅、锡、铁和铜。12 因此在他的合一过程（henosis）中——如迈克尔·迈尔正确理解的那样，13 格雷弗鲁斯心中的不是帕拉塞尔苏斯的三种基本物质，而是古代的四体——他在论著结尾将其与"圣三一中位格的统一"相比较。对他来说，太阳、月亮和墨丘利乌斯的三合一是起点，即初始材料——就它意指树的种子和播种它的土而言。这是所谓的三元结合（coniunctio triptativa）。但这里他关心的是四元结合（coniunctio tetraptativa），14 即四者在"位格的统一"中结合。这是三与四之困境的一个典型例子——作为著名的玛丽亚先知公理15 在炼金术中扮演着重要角色。





3. THE TETRASOMIA
3. 四体


[358] The aim of the tetrasomia is the reduction (or synthesis) of a quaternio of opposites to unity. The names of the planets themselves indicate two dyads, one benevolent (Jupiter and Venus), the other malefic (Saturn and Mars), and such dyads often constitute an alchemical quaternity.1 Zosimos gives the following description of the transformation process that is needed for the preparation of the tincture:
[358] 四体的目标是将一个对立四元体还原（或合成）为统一。行星的名称本身就指示了两个对偶，一个仁慈的（木星和金星），一个凶恶的（土星和火星），这样的对偶常常构成炼金术的四元体。1 佐西莫斯对制备染色剂所需的转化过程做了如下描述：

You have need of an earth formed from two bodies and a water formed from two natures to water it. When the water has been mingled with the earth . . . the sun must act on this clay and transform it into stone. This stone must be burnt, and that burning will bring out the secret of this matter, that is to say its spirit, which is the tincture2 sought by the philosophers.3
你需要一种由两种体形成的土和一种由两种性形成的水来浇灌它。当水与土混合后……太阳必须作用于这黏土并将其转化为石。这石必须被焚烧，那焚烧将带来这一物质的秘密，即它的灵，也就是哲学家们所寻的染色剂。2 3

As the text shows, the synthesis depends on the unification of a double dyad. This is expressed particularly clearly in another archetypal form of the same idea: in the structure of the royal marriage, which follows that of the cross-cousin marriage.4
如文本所示，合成依赖于一个双重对偶的统一。这在同一理念的另一个原型形式中表达得特别清楚：在王婚的结构中，它遵循交表婚的结构。4

[359] As a rule, the lapis is synthesized from the quaternity of the elements or from the ogdoad of elements plus qualities (cold/warm, moist/dry). Similarly Mercurius, known from ancient times as quadratus, is the arcane substance through whose transformation the lapis, or goal of the opus, is produced. Thus in the love-magic of Astrampsychos the invocation to Hermes says:
[359] 通常，石头是由元素的四元体或元素加性质（冷/暖、湿/干）的八元体合成的。同样，自古以来被称为 quadratus 的墨丘利乌斯是秘术物质，通过其转化产生石头——即大业的目标。因此在阿斯特兰普叙科斯的爱情魔法中，对赫尔墨斯的祈请说：

Your names . . . are in the four corners of the heavens. I know also your forms, which are: in the East you have the form of an ibis, in the West you have the form of a dog-headed baboon, in the North you have the form of a serpent, but in the South you have the form of a wolf. Your plant is the grape,5 which in that place is the olive.6 I know also your wood: it is ebony, etc.7
你的名……在天之四角。我也知你的形：在东方你有朱鹭之形，在西方你有犬头狒狒之形，在北方你有蛇之形，但在南方你有狼之形。你的植物是葡萄，5 在那地即为橄榄。6 我也知你的木：那是乌木，等等。7

[360] The fourfold Mercurius is also the tree or its spiritus vegetativus. The Hellenistic Hermes is on the one hand an all-encompassing deity, as the above attributes show, but on the other hand, as Hermes Trismegistus, he is the arch-authority of the alchemists. The four forms of Hermes in Egyptian Hellenism are clearly derived from the four sons of Horus. A god with four faces is mentioned as early as the Pyramid Texts of the fourth and fifth dynasties.8 The faces obviously refer to the four quarters of heaven—that is, the god is all-seeing. Budge points out that in chapter CXII of the Egyptian Book of the Dead the same god appears as the ram of Mendes with four heads.9 The original Horus, who represented the face of heaven, had long hair hanging down over his face, and these strands of hair were associated with the four pillars of Shu, the air god, which supported the four-cornered plate of the sky. Later the four pillars became associated with the four sons of Horus, who replaced the old gods of the four quarters of heaven. Hapi corresponded to the North, Tuamutef to the East, Amset to the South, and Qebhsennuf to the West. They played a large role in the cult of the dead, watching over the life of the dead man in the underworld. His two arms corresponded to Hapi and Tuamutef, his legs to Amset and Qebhsennuf. The Egyptian quaternity consisted of two dyads, as is evident from the text of the Book of the Dead: “Then said Horus to Re, Give me two divine brethren in the city of Pe and two divine brethren in the city of Nekhen, who [have sprung] from my body.”10 The quaternity is in fact a leitmotiv in the ritual for the dead: four men carry the coffin with the four Canopic jars, there are four sacrificial animals, all instruments and vessels are fourfold. Formulas and prayers are repeated four times, etc.11 It is evident from this that the quaternity was of special importance for the dead man: the four sons of Horus had to see to it that the four parts (i.e., the wholeness) of the body were preserved. Horus begot his sons with his mother Isis. The incest motif, which was continued in Christian tradition and extended into late medieval alchemy, thus begins far back in Egyptian antiquity. The four sons of Horus are often shown standing on a lotus before their grandfather Osiris, Mestha12 having a human head, Hapi the head of an ape, Tuamutef the head of a jackal, and Qebhsennuf the head of a hawk.
[360] 四重墨丘利乌斯也是树或其植物灵（spiritus vegetativus）。希腊化时期的赫尔墨斯一方面是一位无所不包的神——如上述属性所示——但另一方面，作为赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯，他是炼金术士的最高权威。埃及希腊化时期赫尔墨斯的四种形态明显源自荷鲁斯的四个儿子。一位四面的神早在第四和第五王朝的金字塔文中就被提及。8 这些面显然指的是天的四方——即这位神是全视的。巴奇指出，在埃及《亡灵书》第112章中，同一位神以门德斯的四头公羊的形态出现。9 最初的荷鲁斯代表天之面，他的长发垂在脸上，这些发绺与空气神舒的四柱——支撑四角天板——相关联。后来四柱与荷鲁斯的四个儿子相关联，后者取代了旧的四方之神。哈皮对应北方，图阿穆特夫对应东方，阿姆塞特对应南方，凯布塞努夫对应西方。他们在死者崇拜中扮演重要角色，守护死者在冥界的生命。他的两臂对应哈皮和图阿穆特夫，他的两腿对应阿姆塞特和凯布塞努夫。埃及的四元体由两个对偶组成，如《亡灵书》文本所示："荷鲁斯对拉说，在佩城给我两个神圣的兄弟，在涅亨城给我两个神圣的兄弟，他们〔生于〕我的身体。"10 四元体实际上是死者仪式中的主导动机：四个人抬棺和四个坎诺卜罐，有四只祭牲，一切器具和器皿都是四重的。公式和祈祷文重复四次，等等。11 由此可见四元体对死者具有特殊重要性：荷鲁斯的四个儿子必须确保身体的四个部分（即完整性）得到保存。荷鲁斯与他的母亲伊西斯生了儿子。乱伦主题——在基督教传统中延续并延伸到中世纪晚期炼金术——由此远溯至埃及古代。荷鲁斯的四个儿子常被展示站在其祖父奥西里斯面前的莲花上，梅斯萨12 有人头，哈皮有猿头，图阿穆特夫有豺头，凯布塞努夫有鹰头。

[361] The analogy with the vision of Ezekiel (chapters 1 and 10) is at once apparent. There the four cherubim had “the likeness of a man.” Each of them had four faces, a man’s, a lion’s, an ox’s, and an eagle’s, so that, as with the four sons of Horus, one quarter was human and three quarters animal. In the love-magic of Astrampsychos, on the other hand, all four forms are animal, probably because of the magic purport of the incantation.13
[361] 与以西结的异象（第1章和第10章）的类比立即可见。在那里四个基路伯有"人的模样"。每个有四张脸——人、狮、牛、鹰——因此与荷鲁斯的四个儿子一样，四分之一是人，四分之三是动物。另一方面，在阿斯特兰普叙科斯的爱情魔法中，四种形态全是动物，可能是因为咒语的魔法意图。13

[362] In keeping with the Egyptian predilection for multiples of four, there are 4 × 4 faces in the vision of Ezekiel.14 Moreover each of the cherubim has a wheel. In later commentaries the four wheels were interpreted as Merkabah, the chariot.15 Corresponding to the four pillars of Shu and the four sons of Horus as gods of the four quarters, who bear up the floor of the sky, there was “a firmament as the colour of terrible crystal, stretched forth over the heads” of the cherubim. On it stood the throne of him who had “the appearance of a man,” the counterpart of Osiris, who with the help of the older Horus and of Set had climbed up to heaven.
[362] 与埃及人对四的倍数的偏好一致，以西结的异象中有4×4张脸。14 此外每个基路伯有一个轮。在后来的注释中，四个轮被解释为梅尔卡瓦（Merkabah），即战车。15 与舒的四柱和荷鲁斯四子作为四方之神支撑天板相对应，基路伯的头上有"可畏水晶色的穹苍，展开在头上"。上面坐着那位有"人的样子"的——即奥西里斯的对应者，后者在老荷鲁斯和塞特的帮助下登上了天。

[363] The four wings of the cherubim recall the winged female genies who protect the coffin of Pharaoh. Each of the Horus sons had a female counterpart who fulfilled this same tutelary function. The cherubim, too, were protective genies, as is apparent from Ezekiel 28 : 14 and 16.16 The apotropaic significance of the quaternity is borne out by Ezekiel 9 : 4, where the prophet, at the behest of the Lord, sets a cross17 on the foreheads of the righteous to protect them from punishment. It is evidently the sign of God, who himself has the attribute of quaternity. The cross is the mark of his protégés. As attributes of God and also symbols in their own right, the quaternity and the cross signify wholeness. Thus Paulinus of Nola says:
[363] 基路伯的四翅让人想起保护法老棺椁的有翼女性守护神。荷鲁斯的每个儿子都有一个女性对应者，履行同样的守护功能。基路伯也是守护精灵，如《以西结书》28:14和16所示。16 四元体的驱邪意义由《以西结书》9:4证实，先知奉主之命在义人的额上画一个十字17 以保护他们免受惩罚。这显然是上帝的记号，而上帝自身具有四元体的属性。十字是他的保护者的标志。作为上帝的属性和独立的象征，四元体和十字都意味着整体性。如诺拉的保利努斯所说：

Extended on the four arms of the wood of the cross, he reached out to the four quarters of the world, that he might draw together unto life the peoples from every shore; and because Christ our God by the death of the cross shows himself all things to all men, that life may come into being and evil be destroyed, A and Ω stand beside the cross, each letter by its three strokes displaying a different figure in threefold wise, a single meaning perfected in triple form.18
伸展在十字木的四臂上，他伸向世界的四方，以便从每个海岸将万民引向生命；因为我们的上帝基督借十字之死向一切人显示自己为一切，使生命得以产生、恶被消灭，A 和 Ω 立于十字旁，每个字母以其三笔以三重方式显示不同的形状，一个意义以三重形式完成。18

[364] In the spontaneous symbolism of the unconscious the cross as quaternity refers to the self, to man’s wholeness.19 The sign of the cross is thus an indication of the healing effect of wholeness, or of becoming whole.
[364] 在无意识的自发象征中，十字作为四元体指向自性，指向人的完整性。19 十字记号因此是整体性或变得完整的治愈效果的标志。

[365] Four animals also appear in the vision of Daniel. The first was like a lion and was “made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man’s heart was given to it.” The second was like a bear, the third like a leopard, and the fourth was a beast “dreadful and terrible,” with “great iron teeth” and “ten horns.”20 Only the special treatment of the lion in any way recalls the human quarter of the tetramorph. All four of them are beasts of prey or, in psychological terms, functions that have succumbed to desire, lost their angelic character, and become daemonic in the worst sense. They represent the negative and destructive aspect of the four angels of God who, as the Book of Enoch shows, form his inner court. This regression has nothing to do with magic (see n. 13) but rather expresses the daemonization of man, or of certain powerful individuals. Accordingly Daniel interprets the four beasts as four kings which shall arise out of the earth (7 : 17, A.V.). The interpretation continues (7 : 18): “But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.” Like the lion with the human heart, this surprising interpretation is based on the positive aspect of the quaternity and refers to a blessed, protected state of things when four guardian angels reign in heaven and four just kings on earth, and the saints possess the kingdom. But this happy state is about to disappear, for the fourth beast in the quaternity has assumed monstrous form, has ten horns and represents “the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be diverse from all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth” (7 : 23). In other words, a monstrous lust for power will make the human quarter unconscious again. This is a psychological process which can be observed only too often both individually and collectively. It has recurred countless times in the history of mankind.
[365] 四只动物也出现在但以理的异象中。第一只像狮子，"被立起来用两脚站立，有人心给了它"。第二只像熊，第三只像豹，第四只是一只"令人恐惧、可怕"的兽，有"大铁牙"和"十角"。20 只有对狮子的特殊处理多少让人想起四联体的人的部分。它们全是猛兽，或者用心理学术语说，是屈服于欲望、失去了天使性质并在最恶劣意义上变为精灵的功能。它们代表上帝四天使的消极和破坏性方面——如《以诺书》所示，后者构成他的内廷。这种退行与魔法无关（见注13），而是表达了人或某些有权势之人的魔鬼化。因此但以理将四兽解释为将从地上兴起的四王（7:17，钦定本）。解释继续（7:18）："然而至高者的圣民必要得国享受，直到永永远远。"如同有人心的狮子一样，这一出人意料的解释基于四元体的积极方面，指的是一个蒙福的、受保护的状态——四个守护天使在天上统治，四个正义之王在地上统治，圣民拥有国度。但这幸福的状态即将消失，因为四元体中的第四只兽已采取怪物形态，有十角，代表"天上的第四国，必与一切国大不相同，必吞吃全地"（7:23）。换言之，一种怪异的权力欲将使人的那四分之一再次变得无意识。这是一个在个体和集体层面都屡见不鲜的心理过程。它在人类历史上已重演了无数次。

[366] Via Daniel and Enoch, the quaternity of God’s sons penetrated very early into Christian ideology. There are the three synoptic gospels and the one gospel of St. John, to which were assigned as emblems the symbols of the cherubim. The four gospels are as it were the pillars of Christ’s throne, and in the Middle Ages the tetramorph became the riding animal of the Church. But it was Gnostic speculation in particular that appropriated the quaternity. This theme is so far-reaching that it cannot be dealt with more closely here. I would only draw attention to the synonymity of Christ, Logos, and Hermes,21 and the derivation of Jesus from the so-called “second tetrad”22 among the Valentinians. “Thus our Lord in his fourfoldness preserves the form of the tetraktys and is composed of (1) the spiritual, which comes from Achamoth, (2) the psychic, which comes from the world-creator, (3) the body prepared with ineffable art, and (4) the divine, the saviour.”23
[366] 通过但以理和以诺，上帝之子的四元体很早就渗入了基督教意识形态。有三部对观福音书和一部约翰福音，它们被分配了基路伯的象征。四福音书如同基督宝座的四柱，在中世纪四联体成为教会的坐骑。但尤其是诺斯替思辨吸收了四元体。这一主题范围如此广泛，无法在此详述。我只想提请注意基督、逻各斯和赫尔墨斯的同一性，21 以及瓦伦廷派中耶稣从所谓"第二四元体"22 的派生。"因此我们的主以其四重性保持了四元体的形式，由（1）来自阿卡莫特的属灵者、（2）来自造物者的属魂者、（3）以不可言之艺所备之体、（4）属神性者即救主组成。"23

[367] The alchemical tetrasomia and its reduction to unity therefore have a long prehistory which reaches back far beyond the Pythagorean tetraktys into Egyptian antiquity. From all this we can see without difficulty that we are confronted with the archetype of a totality image divided into four. The resultant conceptions are always of a central nature, characterize divine figures, and carry over those qualities to the arcane substances of alchemy.
[367] 炼金术的四体及其向统一的还原因此有一段漫长的前史，远溯至毕达哥拉斯的四元体之上，直至埃及古代。从这一切我们可以不难看出，我们面对的是一个分为四的整体性形象的原型。由此产生的观念总是具有中心性质，特征化神性人物，并将这些品质传递到炼金术的秘术物质上。

[368] It is not the task of empirical psychology to speculate about the possible metaphysical significance of this archetype. We can only point out that in spontaneous psychic products such as dreams and fantasies the same archetype is at work and in principle produces over and over again the same figures, meanings, and values autochthonously. Anyone who studies impartially the above series of dream pictures will be able to convince himself of the validity of my conclusions.
[368] 经验心理学的任务不是推测这一原型可能的形而上学意义。我们只能指出，在梦和幻想等自发心理产物中，同一原型在起作用，并原则上自主地反复产生相同的形象、含义和价值。任何不偏不倚地研究上述梦画系列的人都能信服我结论的有效性。





4. THE IMAGE OF WHOLENESS
4. 整体性形象


[369] After this excursus into the history of the Hermetic quaternity, let us turn back to the image of wholeness in alchemy.
[369] 在这段赫尔墨斯四元体历史的离题之后，让我们回到炼金术中的整体性形象。

[370] One of the commonest and most important of the arcana is the aqua permanens, the ὔδωρ θεῑον of the Greeks. This, according to the unanimous testimony of both the ancient and the later alchemists, is an aspect of Mercurius, and of this divine water Zosimos says in his fragment περὶ τοῡ θείου ὕδατος:
[370] 最常见且最重要的秘术之一是永久水（aqua permanens），即希腊人的 ὔδωρ θεῑον。根据古代和后来的炼金术士的一致证词，这是墨丘利乌斯的一个方面，关于这种神性之水，佐西莫斯在其残篇 περὶ τοῡ θείου ὕδατος 中说：

This is the great and divine mystery which is sought, for it is the whole [τοῡτο γáρ ἐστι τὸ πᾱν]. And from it is the whole and through the same is the whole. Two natures, one substance [οὐσία]. But the one [substance] attracts the one, and the one rules the one. This is the silver water, male and female, which forever flees. . . . For it is not to be ruled. It is the whole in all things. And it has life and spirit and is destructive [ἀναιρετικόν].1
这就是所寻的伟大而神圣的奥秘，因为它即是整体〔τοῡτο γáρ ἐστι τὸ πᾱν〕。整体来自它，整体通过它而成。两种本性，一种实体〔οὐσία〕。但一〔实体〕吸引一，一统治一。这是银水，男与女，永远逃逸……因为它不可被统治。它是万有中的整体。它有生命和灵，并且是毁灭性的〔ἀναιρετικόν〕。1

[371] With regard to the central significance of the aqua permanens I must refer the reader to my earlier writings.2 The “water” is just as much the arcanum of alchemy as are Mercurius, the lapis, the filius philosophorum, etc. Like them it is a totality image, and as the above Zosimos quotation shows, this was so even in the Greek alchemy of the third century A.D. The text leaves no doubt in this respect: the water is wholeness. It is the “silver water” (= hydrargyrum), but not the ὕδωρ ἀεικίνητον, ‘ever-moving water,’ i.e., ordinary quicksilver which in Latin alchemy was called Mercurius crudus as distinct from Mercurius nonvulgi. In Zosimos the quicksilver is a πνεῦμα (spirit).3
[371] 关于永久水的中心意义，我必须请读者参阅我早先的著作。2"水"与墨丘利乌斯、石头、哲学家之子等一样是炼金术的秘术。如同它们一样，它是一个整体性形象，如上述佐西莫斯引文所示，这在公元三世纪的希腊炼金术中就已经如此。文本在这方面不留疑虑：水即整体性。它是"银水"（=水银），但不是 ὕδωρ ἀεικίνητον（"永远运动之水"），即普通水银——在拉丁炼金术中称为 Mercurius crudus 以区别于 Mercurius nonvulgi。在佐西莫斯那里，水银是一种 πνεῦμα（灵）。3

[372] Zosimos’s “whole” is a microcosm, a reflection of the universe in the smallest particle of matter, and is therefore found in everything organic and inorganic. Because the microcosm is identical with the macrocosm, it attracts the latter and thus brings about a kind of apocatastasis, a restoration of all individua to the original wholeness. Thus “every grain becomes wheat, and all metal gold,” as Meister Eckhart says; and the little, single individual becomes the “great man,” the homo maximus or Anthropos, i.e., the self. The moral equivalent of the physical transmutation into gold is self-knowledge, which is a re-remembering of the homo totus.4 Olympiodorus, citing Zosimos’s exhortation to Theosebeia, says:
[372] 佐西莫斯的"整体"是一个微宇宙，是宇宙在最微小的物质粒子中的映像，因此存在于一切有机物和无机物中。因为微宇宙与大宇宙同一，它吸引后者，从而带来一种万有复元（apocatastasis），即一切个体向原初整体性的恢复。因此"每一粒都变成麦，一切金属都变成金"——如迈斯特·埃克哈特所说；小小的、单一的个体变成了"大人"，homo maximus 或原人，即自性。物理上的转化为金的道德等价物是自知——那是对整全之人（homo totus）的重新记起。4 奥林匹奥多鲁斯引用佐西莫斯对提奥塞贝娅的劝勉说：

If thou wilt calmly humble thyself in relation to thy body, thou wilt calm thyself also in relation to the passions, and by acting thus, thou wilt summon the divine to thyself, and in truth the divine, which is everywhere5 will come to thee. But when thou knowest thyself, thou knowest also the God who is truly one.6
如果你能平静地在与你的身体的关系中谦卑自己，你也能在与激情的关系中平静自己，这样做你将召唤神性到你身边，而那无处不在的神性5 将真正来到你这里。当你认识自己时，你也就认识了那真正唯一的神。6

Hippolytus bears this out in his account of the Christian doctrine:
希波吕托斯在其关于基督教教义的叙述中证实了这一点：

But thou shalt speak with God and be joint heir with Christ. . . . For thou wilt have become God [γέγovας γὰρ θεός]. For whatever sufferings thou didst undergo as a man, thou hast shown that thou art a man; but whatever is appurtenant to a God, that God has promised to bestow, because thou hast been made divine [θεοποιηθῇς], since thou hast been begotten immortal [γεννηθείς]. That is the “Know thyself,” the knowing of the God who made thee. For to him who knoweth himself it is given to be known of Him by whom he is called.7
但你将与神交谈，并与基督同作后嗣……因为你将成为神〔γέγovας γὰρ θεός〕。因为你作为人所经受的一切苦难，你表明了你是人；但属于神的一切，神已应许赐予，因为你已被造为神〔θεοποιηθῇς〕，因为你已被生为不死者〔γεννηθείς〕。这就是"认识你自己"，认识那造你的神。因为认识自己的人，蒙呼召他的那位所认识。7

[373] The foregoing account of the associative background of the tree, prompted by the treatise of Jodocus Greverus, seemed to me a necessary prelude to a discussion of the significance of the tree in alchemy. A general survey of this kind may help the reader not to lose sight of the whole amid the unavoidable confusion of alchemical opinions and fantasies. Unfortunately my exposition will not be rendered any easier by my having to give numerous parallels from other fields of study. These, however, cannot be dispensed with, because the views of the alchemists were derived to a large extent from unconscious archetypal assumptions which also underlie other domains of human thought.
[373] 上述由约多库斯·格雷弗鲁斯论著引发的关于树的联想背景的叙述，在我看来是讨论树在炼金术中意义的必要前奏。这样的一般概述可以帮助读者在炼金术观点和幻想的不可避免混乱中不致迷失整体。不幸的是，我不得不给出来自其他研究领域的众多平行材料，这不会使我的阐述变得更容易。然而这些不能省略，因为炼金术士的观点在很大程度上来源于无意识的原型假设，这些假设也构成了人类思想其他领域的基础。





5. THE NATURE AND ORIGIN OF THE PHILOSOPHICAL TREE
5. 哲学之树的本性与起源


[374] In my book Psychology and Alchemy I devoted a special chapter1 to the projection of psychic contents (hallucinations, visions, etc.) and therefore need not dwell here on the spontaneous production of the tree symbol among the alchemists. Suffice to say that the adept saw branches and twigs2 in the retort, where his tree grew and blossomed.3 He was advised to contemplate its growth, that is, to reinforce it with active imagination. The vision was the thing to be sought (res quaerenda).4 The tree was “prepared” in the same way as salt.5 And just as the tree grew in the water, so also it was putrefied in it, “burnt” or “cooled” with the water.6 It was called oak,7 vine,8 myrtle.9 Djēbir ibn Hayyēn says of the myrtle: “Know that the myrtle is the leaf and the twig; it is a root yet no root. It is both a root and a branch. As a root, it is unquestionably a root if it be set over against the leaves and the fruits. It is separate from the trunk and forms part of the deep roots.” The myrtle, he says, is “what Maria10 calls the golden rungs, what Democritus calls the green bird. . . . It has been so called because of its green colour and because it is like the myrtle, in that it keeps its green colour for a long time despite the alternations of heat and cold.”11 It has seven branches.12
[374] 在我的《心理学与炼金术》一书中，我用了一章专门讨论心理内容的投射（幻觉、异象等），1 因此无需在此赘述树象征在炼金术士中的自发产生。只需说工匠在瓮中看到了枝和细枝，2 他的树在那里生长和开花。3 他被建议观想其生长，即用主动想象力来强化它。异象是应被追求的东西（res quaerenda）。4 树以与盐相同的方式"被制备"。5 正如树在水中生长，它也在水中腐化，被水"烧"或"冷"。6 它被称为橡树、7 葡萄藤、8 桃金娘。9 贾比尔·伊本·哈扬谈到桃金娘时说："要知道桃金娘是叶和细枝；它是根又不是根。它既是根又是枝。作为根，如果将其与叶和果对照，它无疑是根。它与树干分离并构成深根的一部分。"他说桃金娘是"玛丽亚10 所称的金阶，德谟克利特所称的绿鸟……它之所以如此得名是因为它的绿色，以及因为它像桃金娘一样，在冷热交替中长期保持绿色。"11 它有七根枝条。12

[375] Gerard Dorn says of the tree:
[375] 杰拉德·多恩谈到树时说：

After nature has planted the root of the metallic tree in the midst of her womb, viz., the stone which shall bring forth the metals, the gem, the salt, the alum, the vitriol, the salty spring, sweet, cold, or warm, the tree of coral or the Marcasita,13 and has set its trunk in the earth, this trunk is divided into different branches, whose substance is a liquid, not after the manner of water, nor of oil, nor of clay,14 nor of slime, but is not to be thought of otherwise than as the wood born of the earth, which is not earth although growing from it. The branches spread in such a way that the one is separated from the other by a space of two or three climates and as many regions: from Germany even as far as Hungary and beyond. In this way the branches of different trees spread through the whole globe of the earth, as in the human body the veins spread through the different limbs, which are separated from one another.
当自然将其金属之树的根植入其子宫中央——即那将产出金属、宝石、盐、明矾、矾、盐泉（甜的、冷的或暖的）、珊瑚树或马卡西塔的石头——并将树干设于土中之后，这树干分为不同的枝，其物质是液态的，不像水、不像油、不像黏土、14 不像泥，而只能被视为生于土的木，虽从土出却非土。这些枝以这样的方式展开：一根与另一根之间相隔两三个气候带和同样多的地区的空间——从德国一直到匈牙利及更远。这样不同树的枝条遍布整个地球，如同在人体中静脉伸展于不同的肢体，各肢体彼此分离。

The fruits of this tree drop off, and the tree itself dies and vanishes in the earth. “Afterwards, in accordance with natural conditions, another new [tree] is there.”15
这棵树的果实坠落，树本身死去并消逝于土中。"之后，按照自然条件，另一棵新的〔树〕就在那里了。"15

[376] In this text Dorn draws an impressive picture of the growth, expansion, death, and rebirth of the philosophical tree. Its branches are veins running through the earth, and although they spread to the most distant points of the earth’s surface they all belong to the same immense tree, which apparently renews itself. The tree is obviously thought of as a system of blood vessels. It consists of a liquid like blood, and when this comes out it coagulates into the fruit of the tree.16 Strangely enough, in ancient Persian tradition the metals are connected with the blood of Gayomart: his blood, soaking into the earth, turned into the seven metals.
[376] 在这段文本中，多恩描绘了哲学之树的生长、扩展、死亡和重生的生动画面。它的枝条是贯穿大地的静脉，虽然它们伸展到地球表面最遥远的点，但它们都属于同一棵巨树——它显然自我更新。树显然被构想为一个血管系统。它由一种像血的液体组成，当这液体出来时，它凝固为树的果实。16 奇怪的是，在古代波斯传统中，金属与盖约马特的血有关：他的血浸入大地，变成了七种金属。

[377] Dorn appends to his description of the tree a brief observation which I would not like to withhold from the reader since it affords an important insight into what is in its way the classic mode of alchemical thinking. He says:
[377] 多恩在他对树的描述之后附了一个简短的观察，我不想对读者隐瞒，因为它提供了对炼金术思维的——就其自身而言——经典模式的重要洞察。他说：

This and suchlike things proceed from the true physics and from the springs of the true philosophy, from which, by meditative contemplation of the wondrous works of God, the true knowledge of the supreme author and of his powers dawns upon the spiritual eyes of the philosophers, even as to the fleshly eyes the light is made visible. To those eyes the hidden is revealed. But that Greek Satan has implanted in the philosophic field of the true wisdom the tares17 and their false seeds, namely Aristotle, Albertus, Avicenna,18 Rasis,19 and men of that kidney, who are inimical to the light of God and the light of nature, and have perverted the whole physical truth from the time when they turned the name Sophia into Philosophia.20
这些及类似的事物来自真正的物理学和真正哲学的泉源，从中，通过对上帝奇妙工的冥想观想，最高创造者及其力量的真知在哲学家的灵性之眼前朗现，如同对肉眼之光可见一般。对那些眼睛，隐秘之事被启示。但那希腊的撒旦已在真正智慧之哲学领域中种下了櫟子17 及其伪种——即亚里士多德、大阿尔伯特、阿维森纳、18 拉齐斯19 以及同类之人——他们与上帝之光和自然之光为敌，自从他们将 Sophia 之名变为 Philosophia 以来，20 已歪曲了一切物理真理。

[378] Dorn was a Platonist and a fanatical opponent of Aristotle and, quite obviously, of the scientific empiricists as well. His attitude was essentially the same as that of Robert Fludd in respect of John Kepler.21 Basically, it was the old controversy about universals, the opposition between realism and nominalism, which in our scientific age has been decided in favour of a nominalistic tendency. Whereas the scientific attitude seeks, on the basis of careful empiricism, to explain nature in her own terms, Hermetic philosophy had for its goal an explanation that included the psyche in a total description of nature. The empiricist tries, more or less successfully, to forget his archetypal explanatory principles, that is, the psychic premises that are a sine qua non of the cognitive process, or to repress them in the interests of “scientific objectivity.” The Hermetic philosopher regarded these psychic premises, the archetypes, as inalienable components of the empirical world-picture. He was not yet so dominated by the object that he could ignore the palpable presence of psychic premises in the form of eternal ideas which he felt to be real. The empirical nominalist, on the other hand, already had the modern attitude towards the psyche, namely, that it had to be eliminated as something “subjective,” and that its contents were nothing but ideas formulated a posteriori, mere flatus vocis. His hope was to be able to produce a picture of the world that was entirely independent of the observer. This hope has been fulfilled only in part, as the findings of modern physics show: the observer cannot be finally eliminated, which means that the psychic premises remain operative.
[378] 多恩是一位柏拉图主义者，是亚里士多德——显然也是科学经验主义者——的狂热反对者。他的态度基本上与罗伯特·弗拉德对约翰内斯·开普勒的态度相同。21 根本上，这是关于共相的古老争论，是实在论与唯名论之间的对立——在我们科学时代，这一争论已决定性地有利于唯名论倾向。科学态度试图在谨慎的经验主义基础上用自然自身的术语来解释自然，而赫尔墨斯哲学的目标则是一种将心灵包含在对自然的总体描述中的解释。经验主义者或多或少成功地试图忘记他的原型解释原则——即认知过程不可或缺的心理前提——或为了"科学客观性"而压抑它们。赫尔墨斯哲学家则将这些心理前提——原型——视为经验世界图景的不可剥夺的组成部分。他尚未被对象所支配到可以忽视以永恒理念形式出现的心理前提的显著存在的地步——他感到这些理念是真实的。另一方面，经验主义的唯名论者已具有对待心灵的态度：心灵必须作为"主观的"东西被消除，其内容不过是从后天形成的理念、仅仅是 flatus vocis（声音之气）。他的希望是能够产生一幅完全独立于观察者的世界图景。这一希望只部分实现了——如现代物理学的发现所示：观察者不能被最终消除，这意味着心理前提仍在起作用。

[379] In the case of Dorn we can see how the archetypal tree, which consisted of the ramifications of the bronchi, blood vessels, and veins of ore, was projected upon the empirical world and gave rise to a totalistic view which embraced the whole of organic and inorganic nature and the “spiritual” world as well. The fanatical defence of his standpoint shows that Dorn was gnawed by inner doubt and was fighting a lost battle. Neither he nor Fludd could hold up the march of events, and today we see how the spokesmen of so-called objectivity are defending themselves with similar outbursts of affect against a psychology that demonstrates the necessity of psychic premises.
[379] 在多恩的案例中，我们可以看到由支气管、血管和矿脉的分枝组成的原型树如何被投射到经验世界上，产生了一种涵盖一切有机和无机自然以及"精神"世界的整体主义观点。多恩对其立场的狂热辩护表明他内心被疑虑折磨，正在打一场必败的仗。他或弗拉德都无法阻挡事件的进程，而今天我们看到所谓客观性的代言人们如何以类似的情感爆发来抵御一种展示心理前提之必要性的心理学。





6. DORN’S INTERPRETATION OF THE TREE
6. 多恩对树的诠释


[380] In his treatise “Congeries Paracelsicae chemicae de transmutatione metallorum” Dorn writes:1
[380] 多恩在其论著《帕拉塞尔苏斯化学集论金属转化》中写道：1

On account of likeness alone, and not substance, the Philosophers compare their material to a golden tree with seven branches, thinking that it encloses in its seed the seven metals, and that these are hidden in it, for which reason they call it a living thing. Again, even as natural trees bring forth divers blossoms in their season, so the material of the stone causes the most beautiful colours to appear2 when it puts forth its blossoms.3 Likewise they have said that the fruit of their tree strives up to heaven, because out of the philosophic earth there arises a certain substance, like to the branches of a loathsome sponge.4 Whence they have put forward the opinion that the point about which the whole art turns lies in the living things of nature [in vegetabilibus naturae] and not in the living things of matter; and also because their stone contains within it soul, body, and spirit, as do living things. From a likeness not altogether remote they have called this material virgin’s milk and blessed rose-coloured blood, although that belongs only to the prophets and sons of God. For this reason the Sophists have supposed that the philosophic matter consists of animal or human blood.
