So I want to explore the Moon with you in this light, to examine how it indicates what happens when we get close to someone, how it directly affects issues to do with merging and intimacy throughout our lives. The reason why the Moon is one of the prime significators for relationship isn't too hard to figure out. The Moon is a symbol for mother, and assessing its placement in a chart is a good indication of what that person's mother-child relationship was like. I've discussed this at length in the “Stages of Childhood” in The Development of the Personality.2 For instance, if you have the Moon natally in aspect to Saturn, then you would have met Saturn in some way through the mother; if you have the Moon in aspect to Jupiter, you would have met Jupiter through the mother, and so on. I won't go into detailed interpretations right now. But the point I want to make is that mother is not just mother. Besides being mother—the one who is meant to love, nurture and care for you—mother is also the first important relationship in your life. She is not just your mother, she is the first big love of your life. Your mother is your first big romance—for both men and women. Every child falls desperately and madly in love with his or her mother. It may be hard to believe this when you look at your mother now or consider what happened earlier on, but it's true. In the time we have, I want to analyse the Moon's placement in terms of how your first big romance went—how you “made out” in the first grand passion of your life. And I'm not doing this just to wallow in the past; I'm doing this because what happened back then has an undeniable influence on our later close relationships.
所以我想从这一角度与你们一起探索月亮，检视它如何预示我们靠近某人时会发生什么，如何直接影响我们一生中与融合和亲密有关的问题。月亮之所以是关系的主要征象星之一，原因不难理解。月亮是母亲的象征，评估它在星盘中的位置可以很好地指示那个人的母子关系是什么样的。我在《人格的发展》中的「童年阶段」中详细讨论了这个问题。² 例如，如果你的本命月亮与土星形成相位，那么你会通过母亲以某种方式遇见土星；如果你的月亮与木星形成相位，你会通过母亲遇见木星，以此类推。我现在不会做详细的解读。但我想提出的要点是，母亲不仅仅是母亲。除了作为母亲——那个本该爱你、养育和照顾你的人之外——母亲也是你生命中第一个重要的关系。她不仅仅是你的母亲，她是你生命中第一个大恋爱。你的母亲是你的初恋——对男性和女性都是如此。每个孩子都绝望地、疯狂地爱上了他或她的母亲。你现在看着你的母亲或回想之前发生的事时可能很难相信这一点，但这是真的。在我们有限的时间里，我想从你的初恋如何发展的角度分析月亮的位置——你如何在你生命中第一次伟大的激情中「表现」。我做这个不仅是为了沉溺于过去；我做这个是因为那时发生的事情对我们后来的亲密关系有着不可否认的影响。

I'm sure you're all pretty familiar with my thinking on this matter, and you know I believe that the past has a way of haunting us. We don't consciously remember what passed between mother and ourselves in the first year or so of our lives, but we never forget it. This is where I find the chart so useful. It's like an X-ray. If you know how to read a chart properly, you can learn a great deal about what went on in early childhood. You can make fairly safe conjectures about what happened between you and mother by looking at the natal placement of the Moon, and also by examining the early progressions and transits involving the Moon. To put it another way, the chart shows the “inner child of the past” in all of us. Our past, particularly our childhood, with all its hopes, fears and expectations, with all its joys and terrors, is stored and recorded in memory and shown by the chart. Your “inner child of the past” is still there in you right now. No matter how mature you become, no matter how sophisticated and learned you are, you still have an inner child inside you. I've seen even the most educated, mature people fall to pieces and start acting like frightened and angry children when a boyfriend or girlfriend doesn't ring them up as promised. Current relationships have a way of bringing to the surface deeper emotions which originally stem from early childhood bondings. Mother is our first important relationship, she is the first love of our life, and what happens in that relationship becomes a prototype for later close partnerships. What happens between you and mother sets up a pattern, template, or package of inner expectations which shape and influence what we meet and experience in later intimate unions. In her book Intimate Partners, Maggie Scarf comments on the link between mother and the eventual choice of a mate:
我相信你们对我在这方面的思考都很熟悉，你们知道我相信过去有办法纠缠我们。我们不会有意识地记得在生命的第一年左右母亲和我们之间发生了什么，但我们永远不会忘记它。这就是我发现星盘如此有用的地方。它就像一张X光片。如果你知道如何正确阅读星盘，你可以了解到很多关于早期童年发生了什么。你可以通过观察月亮的本命位置，以及检查涉及月亮的早期推运和过运，对母亲和你之间发生了什么做出相当可靠的推测。换言之，星盘展示了我们每个人内在「过去的内在小孩」。我们的过去，特别是我们的童年，带着所有的希望、恐惧和期望，所有的欢乐和恐惧，被存储和记录在记忆中并由星盘展示。你的「过去的内在小孩」现在仍在你的内在。无论你变得多么成熟，无论你多么世故和博学，你内在仍然有一个内在小孩。我曾见过最受过教育、最成熟的人在男朋友或女朋友没有如约打电话时崩溃并开始表现得像一个受惊和愤怒的孩子。当前关系有一种将更深层的情感带到表面的方式，这些情感最初源于早期的童年纽带。母亲是我们第一个重要的关系，她是我们生命中的初恋，在那段关系中发生的事情成为后来亲密伴侣关系的原型。你与母亲之间发生的事情设定了一种模式、模板或内在期望的包里，塑造和影响我们在后来的亲密结合中遇到和经验什么。

It is from this primitive psychological state—of total emotional symbiosis with a responsive, intuitively comprehending, need-satisfying other—that we slowly awaken to the human world. And it is in the context of this awakening that we begin to form assumptions about what the experience of intimate loving is like. For even as we come to know and recognize those who care for us—particularly mother—we develop feelings of attachment that are so intense that it would not be at all exaggerated to term them “the first grand passion of human life.” … What is “right” when it comes to the choosing of a mate, is to some degree what has been and what is familiar; it is what “works” on that inner template, or pattern of assumptions about what an intimate partnership is like.3
正是从这个原始的心理状态——与一个回应性的、直觉理解的、满足需求的他者完全的情感共生——我们慢慢觉醒到人类世界。也正是在这种觉醒的背景中，我们开始形成关于亲密之爱是什么体验的假设。因为即使我们开始认识并认出那些照顾我们的人——特别是母亲——我们也发展出如此强烈的依恋情感，称之为「人类生活的初恋」一点也不夸张。……在择偶方面什么是「对的」，在某种程度上就是过去已有的和熟悉的；就是那个在内在模板或关于亲密伙伴关系的假设模式上「有效」的东西。³

To underline the importance of the mother-child bond, I'd like to quickly review a study carried out in the 1940's by a Dr. Renee Spitz. Women prisoners who were pregnant had to give up their babies at birth. These babies were then put in a hospital where there was one nurse to every eight babies. The nurses kept changing; there were day nurses and night nurses, so the babies were unable to form a one-to-one bond with either a nurse or their natural mother. Imagine how confusing it must have been for the babies—eight of them needing attention, and only one caretaker around at a time, and not always the same one. The conclusions of the study are quite dramatic. When these babies reached the age of 1 year, they showed profound signs of physical and psychological retardation compared to babies who were reared on a one-to-one basis with mother or mother substitute. The babies in the Spitz study cried much more often than other babies. They smiled less. You could say they were depressed. They were slower to begin talking, they were more apathetic and less responsive than the infants raised normally. They caught infections more easily; in fact, they had a higher mortality rate than babies cared for by one mother. The study demonstrates with a frightening clarity that a loving partner in early life is a precondition for healthy development.4 You can die if you don't get this. So if we don't have a good, loving relationship there in the beginning, or if we have a lot of problems in bonding with mother—the first love of our life—we are left with what Judith Viorst in her book Necessary Losses refers to as “emotional scars on the brain,” deep emotional wounds.5 It is the mother-child bond which first teaches us about love, and first teaches us whether or not we are lovable.
为了强调母子纽带的重要性，我想快速回顾一项由 Renee Spitz 博士在1940年代进行的研究。怀孕的女囚犯必须在分娩时放弃她们的婴儿。这些婴儿随后被安置在一家医院里，每八个婴儿配一名护士。护士不断更换；有白班护士和夜班护士，所以婴儿无法与护士或亲生母亲形成一对一的纽带。想象一下这对婴儿来说有多么混乱——八个人需要关注，而同时只有一位看护者在场，而且不总是同一位。研究的结果相当惊人。当这些婴儿达到一岁时，与由母亲或母亲替代者一对一抚养的婴儿相比，他们表现出深刻的身心发育迟缓迹象。Spitz 研究中的婴儿比其他婴儿哭得更多。他们笑得更少。你可以说他们抑郁了。他们开始说话更慢，比正常抚养的婴儿更冷漠、反应更少。他们更容易感染；事实上，他们的死亡率比由一位母亲照顾的婴儿更高。这项研究以令人恐惧的清晰度表明，早期生活中有一个爱的伙伴是健康发展的前提。⁴ 得不到这个你可能会死。所以如果我们在一开始没有良好的、爱的关系，或者如果我们与母亲——我们生命中的初恋——的纽带有许多问题，我们就会留下 Judith Viorst 在她的书《必要的丧失》中所谓的「大脑上的情感伤疤」，深深的情感创伤。⁵ 正是母子纽带首先教会了我们关于爱，首先教会了我们是否被爱。

Later, I'll be discussing a study of children deprived of their fathers in their early years and the kinds of problems that this can give rise to. But now we're talking about the psychological significance of your relationship with mother. Speaking generally for a moment, if you have a number of difficult aspects to the Moon, then it usually means that your love affair with mother didn't go too well. If this is the case, you probably failed to develop a basic trust in life or in yourself, which can lead to a lot of fear and paranoia in partnership, to anxious feelings and deep uncertainty in close relationship. I believe that we all have the right to be loved, the right to a loving mother. And if you don't get that, you can be psychologically harmed and left not only with a distrust of life and a poor self-image, but you also may feel angry because you have not been given something which is a birthright. On the other hand, if the bonding with mother goes pretty well (which is normally shown by harmonious aspects to the Moon), then you feel safe, you feel cared for, you have your basic needs met, you feel understood. Obviously, this is going to be a blessing for you whenever you get close to someone later on in life. It's as if you already have a picture in your mind of closeness being okay, of love working for you.
稍后，我将讨论一项关于早期失去父亲的儿童以及这可能引起的问题的研究。但现在我们在谈的是你与母亲的关系的心理意义。概括地说，如果你的月亮有许多困难相位，那通常意味着你与母亲的恋爱进行得不太好。如果是这种情况，你可能未能发展出对生活或对自己的基本信任，这可能导致伴侣关系中的很多恐惧和偏执，亲密关系中的焦虑和深深的不确定。我相信我们都有被爱的权利，拥有一个爱你的母亲的权利。如果你没有得到这些，你可能在心理上受到伤害，不仅留下对生活的不信任和糟糕的自我形象，你也可能感到愤怒，因为你没有被给予某种与生俱来的东西。另一方面，如果与母亲的纽带进行得相当顺利（这通常由与月亮的和谐相位显示），那么你感到安全，你感到被照顾，你的基本需求得到满足，你感到被理解。显然，这将在你后来生活中靠近某人时对你是一种祝福。就好像你脑海中已经有一幅画面：亲密是可以的，爱对你有效。

Fortunately, all is not lost if our bonding with mother went awry. We can work through many of these issues, and part of this process involves getting to know the “inner child of the past” which is still alive in us right now. It is important to form a relationship to the child inside you, to befriend it, to recognise its needs and moods. In this way, we can begin to heal or make peace with the wounding or scarring that might have taken place. Many of us still need to mourn the loss of that blissful state of unity we once shared with mother. Many of us still need to grieve for the ideal mothering we never experienced; if we don't grieve and let go of the past, we are compelled to keep looking for that lost ideal mothering from mates and partners later in life—a search that is destined to fail because, no matter how much someone loves and adores us, no one can meet such impossible expectations. Soon we'll be examining all this in terms of astrological aspects to the Moon. But before I do so, I'd like to give you a short exercise which may help you reconnect to the child inside you.
幸运的是，如果我们与母亲的纽带出了问题，并非一切都已失去。我们可以处理许多这些问题，而这个过程的一部分涉及去认识那个现在仍活在内在的「过去的内在小孩」。与内在小孩建立关系，与之交友，认识它的需求和情绪是很重要的。这样，我们就可以开始疗愈或与可能发生的创伤或伤疤和解。我们中许多人仍然需要哀悼曾经与母亲共享的幸福的合一状态。我们中许多人仍然需要为从未经历过的理想母爱而悲伤；如果我们不悲伤、不放下过去，我们就会被迫在后来的生活中不断从伴侣和配偶那里寻找那种失去的、理想的母爱——这种寻找注定失败，因为无论一个人多么爱和崇拜我们，没有人能满足这样的不可能期望。很快我们将从月亮的占星相位角度来检视这一切。但在那之前，我想给你们一个小练习，可能有助于你重新连接内在的小孩。

Start by closing your eyes.
首先闭上眼睛。

(If this exercise becomes difficult for you at any time, just open your eyes and write about what you are experiencing.)
（如果这个练习在任何时候让你感到困难，只需睁开眼睛，写下你正在经历的感受。）

Take a minute to relax, a few deep breaths to help let go of tensions, and then let your mind and your heart recall the feelings you have about your mother.
花一分钟放松，几次深呼吸帮助释放紧张，然后让你的心和你的思想回忆你对母亲的感受。

When you think about her, do you feel warm and safe, or do you feel anxious and uncomfortable?
当你想到她时，你感到温暖和安全，还是感到焦虑和不安？

Now, let an actual memory come to your mind, some event or situation that happened between you and your mother.
现在，让一个实际的记忆浮现在你的脑海中，某个发生在你和你母亲之间的事件或情境。

Just let it arise spontaneously.
让它自然浮现。

Spend a minute reliving this memory.
花一分钟重新体验这段记忆。

Now, let go of that memory and bring to mind another event or situation concerning you and your mother.
现在，放下那段记忆，回想另一个关于你和你母亲的事件或情境。

Take another minute to reflect on this.
再花一分钟反思这段记忆。

See if you can come up with an overall image, symbol or feeling which sums up or describes your feelings around mother.
看看你是否能找到一个总体的意象、象征或感受，来概括或描述你对母亲的感受。

When I've done this exercise with various groups, it's been interesting to see the range of emotions people feel and connect with. Some feel terror and dread at the thought of mother; others feel safe and warm. The Moon's placement by sign and aspect, along with the parental house you assign to the mother, will in some way reflect the kinds of feelings you have toward her.
当我在不同群体中做这个练习时，有趣的是看到人们感受到并联系上的情绪范围。有些人一想到母亲就感到恐惧和可怕；另一些人感到安全和温暖。月亮按星座和相位的配置，以及你分配给母亲的家长宫位，会以某种方式反映你对她拥有的感受类型。

I always manage to get around to talking about the womb in whatever lecture I give. Most of you are familiar with my thinking and ideas about the womb experience and how it can affect us later in life, so today I'm not going to talk about it at length, but draw you a picture instead (see figure 2, page 59). In the womb, and for the first six months or so after birth, our identity is totally fused with the mother. In figure 2, Mother is the big egg, and your identity is a little egg within that big egg. You can see at a glance that your whole being is immersed in her. By the time you reach six months after birth the developmental task is to somehow get the little egg (which is you) separated from that big egg (which is your mother); then you have a little egg and a big egg which can relate with one another because the little egg is no longer enmeshed in the big egg.
我总能在任何讲座中设法谈到子宫。你们大多数人熟悉我关于子宫经验及其如何影响我们后来生活的思考和想法，所以今天我不打算长篇大论地谈它，而是给你们画一幅图（见第59页图2）。在子宫中，以及出生后的大约前六个月，我们的身份与母亲完全融合。在图2中，母亲是大蛋，你的身份是大蛋中的一个小蛋。你可以一目了然地看到你的整个存在都沉浸在她之中。到你出生后六个月时，发展任务是以某种方式让小蛋（即你）从大蛋（即你的母亲）中分离出来；然后你就有一个小蛋和一个大蛋可以彼此建立关系，因为小蛋不再嵌入大蛋中。

Figure 2. The need to differentiate your “I” or ego from that of mother.
图2. 将你的「我」或自我与母亲的自我区分开来的需要。

Let me explain this further. For the first few months or so after birth, you really don't have a relationship with a specific or personal mother; instead you are fused with the Great Mother, someone who is the whole world to you. But by six months, you gradually begin to differentiate or distinguish an “I” that is not your mother. This is shown by the little egg which is now separated out from the big egg. Once your identity is no longer immersed in the Great Mother, you then have a specific, personal or “circumstantial” mother with whom to relate. You are beginning to recognise yourself as a separate person, and therefore you are forced to recognise your mother's separateness from you. So by six months we form what is called a specific mother attachment. It is only then that you can actually begin to make a one-to-one relationship with her—if you are the same as something else, you can't have a relationship with it because there is no duality. When you separate your “I” from your mother's “I,” then you have to face the issue of how these two “I's” (yours and your mother's) are going to get along with one another. What do you think happens when it dawns on you that mother is not you, when you begin to distinguish her as a person separate and distinct from yourself? If you're dealing with someone who is not you, one of the first things you might feel is terror, fear or dread. Where there is other, there is fear. If mother is not me, what if she doesn't like me, what if she doesn't understand my needs, what if she decides to go away and abandon me? The key issue in the first few years of life is survival. We are born unfinished, we are banished from the womb without certain essentials, such as our own flat, our own car, and without any of our own credit cards. We need mother to be on our side to survive.
让我进一步解释这一点。在出生后大约前几个月，你实际上并没有与某个具体的或个人的母亲的关系；相反，你与大母神融合了——对你来说她是整个世界。但到六个月时，你逐渐开始分化或区分一个不是母亲的「我」。这由现在从大蛋中分离出来的小蛋来表示。一旦你的身份不再沉浸在大母神中，你就拥有了一个可以与之建立关系的具体的、个人的或「情境性的」母亲。你开始将自己作为一个独立的人来认识，因此你被迫认识到母亲与你是分离的。所以到六个月时我们形成了所谓的特定母亲依恋。只有到那时你才能真正开始与她建立一对一的关系——如果你与某物是同一的，你就无法与之建立关系，因为没有二元性。当你将你的「我」与母亲的「我」分开时，你就必须面对这两个「我」（你和母亲的）将如何相处的问题。你认为当意识到母亲不是你时会发生什么，当你开始将她区分为一个与你分离和不同的人时？如果你在与一个不是你的人打交道，你可能首先感到的东西之一就是恐惧、害怕或可怕。有他者的地方就有恐惧。如果母亲不是我，如果她不喜欢我怎么办，如果她不理解我的需求怎么办，如果她决定离开抛弃我怎么办？生命最初几年的关键议题是生存。我们出生时未完成，被逐出子宫时没有某些必需品，比如自己的公寓、自己的汽车，也没有任何自己的信用卡。我们需要母亲站在我们这一边才能生存。

According to many schools of psychological thought, when we first differentiate our identity from that of our mother, we attempt to ease the ensuing fear and terror by trying to get her to fall in love with us, by wooing her and winning her love and therefore her loyalty and special attention. If she loves us, she will want to keep us alive and well. This is what I mean by having a romance with your mother; you try to impress her, you try to win her over like you would do if you were going on a date with someone you really liked and with whom you thought there could be a good future. Now remember, all this occurs around six months after birth. In terms of the transiting Sun in the chart, what happens to everybody at six months old? Yes, there is the first opposition of the transiting Sun to one's own Sun. I think this is an apt symbol of the fact that, for the first time, two separate selves are encountering one another. If we consider the Sun to be a symbol of the developing ego, the fact that it forms an opposition (an aspect long associated with relationship) indicates that your emerging ego is coming face to face with somebody else's ego or self. Of course, differentiating identity from mother doesn't happen overnight; it's a gradual process and usually takes about three years to complete. And it helps immensely if there is a father around or another key figure on the scene to draw us away from mother. I'll be going more deeply into how this works when we look at ways the father can help break the early mother-child symbiosis by being an attractive outsider who draws us away from a too-intense bond with the mother.
根据许多心理学流派，当我们首次将我们的身份与母亲的区分开来时，我们试图通过让她爱上我们、追求她并赢得她的爱进而她的忠诚和特殊关注来缓解随之而来的恐惧和害怕。如果她爱我们，她会想让我们活着和健康。这就是我所说的与你的母亲有一段浪漫；你试图打动她，试图赢得她的心，就像你要与你真心喜欢并且觉得可能有美好未来的人约会时那样做。现在请记住，所有这些大约发生在出生后六个月。就星盘中过运太阳而言，每个人在六个月大时会发生什么？没错，过运太阳与本命太阳形成第一次对冲。我认为这是一个恰当的象征，标志着两个独立的自我首次相遇。如果我们把太阳视为发展中的自我的象征，它形成对冲（一个长久与关系相关的相位）的事实表明，你正在浮现的自我正在面对面地遭遇另一个人的自我或自性。当然，将身份与母亲区分开来不是一夜之间发生的；它是一个渐进的过程，通常需要大约三年才能完成。而且如果在场有一位父亲或其他关键人物，将我们从母亲身边引开，那将大有裨益。当我们审视父亲如何作为一个有吸引力的外来者，将我们从与母亲的过于强烈的纽带中引开从而打破早期母子共生时，我将更深入地探讨这是如何运作的。

I've been emphasising how this differentiation stage gets into swing at six months old. We can learn something about what happened then by looking at the chart. For starters, I would examine the natal aspects to the Moon to glean a general overview of how your love affair with mother went. But I would also look at the transits and progressions involving the Moon from six months to three years old. The progressed Moon moves approximately one degree a month. Look to see what it was doing when you were six months old. Let's say your progressed Moon moved into an exact applying opposition to Pluto at this time, a time when you were beginning to view your mother as distinct from yourself. If this is the case, then you will have met Pluto just as you were entering the relationship arena, and therefore relationships will become associated in your mind with the kinds of qualities or issues to do with Pluto. If your progressed Moon at six months comes to conjunct or trine your Venus, then Venus will have bearing on what you will expect to meet in later relationships.
我一直在强调这种分化阶段如何在六个月大时开始。我们可以通过看星盘来了解那时发生了什么。首先，我会检查月亮的本命相位以窥见你与母亲的恋爱总体概况。但我也会看从六个月到三岁之间涉及月亮的过运和推运。推运月亮每月大约移动一度。看看你六个月大时它在做什么。比方说你的推运月亮在此时移入了一个精确的入相位对冲冥王星——一个你开始将母亲视为与自己不同的人的时期。如果是这样，那么你就在进入关系舞台时遇见了冥王星，因此关系在你心中将与冥王星相关的品质或议题联系在一起。如果你的推运月亮在六个月时合相或三分你的金星，那么金星将影响你在后来关系中期望遇到的东西。

I would also look at transits to the Moon. Within six months after birth, most transits to the Moon from Saturn and the outer planets will be natal aspects as well. But if we consider the fact that differentiation can take up to three years to complete, then we should also examine any important transits to the Moon right up to age three in light of our later expectations in relationship. You may be born with Saturn at 1 degree Leo and the Moon at 29 degrees Leo. This is not a conjunction, but when you are 2½ or so Saturn will pass over your Moon. You're still very impressionable at this age, and therefore Saturn is going to influence your feelings about what it is like to be close to someone in a supposedly caring relationship.
我也会看过运对月亮的影响。出生后六个月内，来自土星和外行星的大多数对月亮的过运也将是本命相位。但如果我们考虑到分化可能需要长达三年才能完成这一事实，那么我们也应该检查直到三岁的任何重要对月亮过运，并从我们后来在关系中的期望的角度来审视它们。你可能出生时土星在狮子座1度，月亮在狮子座29度。这不是合相，但当你大约两岁半时，土星将经过你的月亮。你在这个年龄仍然非常易受影响，因此土星将影响你对在所谓的关怀关系中靠近某人是什么感觉的感受。

Let's look more closely at a few natal aspects to the Moon to see what they might mean in terms of the link between mother and later partnerships. We won't have time to cover all the possible aspects to the Moon in depth. I also want to consider the Moon in another way—as a significator not just of one-to-one relationships, but as a measure of how you relate to society in general and how you behave in social situations.
让我们更仔细地看几个月亮的本命相位，看看它们在母亲与后来伴侣关系之间的联系方面可能意味着什么。我们没有时间深入覆盖所有可能的月亮相位。我也想以另一种方式考虑月亮——不仅作为一对一关系的征象星，而且作为你如何与一般社会建立关系以及你在社交场合如何行为的衡量标准。

We'll start now with Moon-Mercury aspects, examining these in terms of what your love affair with mother was like, how your first big romance went. I'll focus in on the hard angles and the inconjunct, because these are the trickier and more interesting ones. I don't want to do all the work, so please add your own comments and ideas. If you are born with the Moon in hard angle to Mercury, what kinds of problems could you have encountered with mother?
现在我们从月-水相位开始，从你与母亲的恋爱是什么样的、你的初恋如何发展的角度来审视这些。我将聚焦于硬相位和梅花相位，因为这些是更棘手也更有趣的。我不想做所有的工作，所以请补充你们的评论和想法。如果你出生时月亮与水星形成硬相位，你可能与母亲遇到了什么样的问题？

Audience: Problems in communication.
听众：交流方面的问题。

Howard: Yes, problems understanding one another, problems communicating with one another. It's pretty obvious why this is the case. The Moon is associated with your safety and security needs, your need to be held and fed and comforted. Mercury is associated with the transferring of information. Therefore when you have the Moon, the significator for mother, in trouble with Mercury, you may find that the two of you have difficulty understanding one another. To put it simply, she may not read you right—you get your wires crossed. This can happen if your mother has a very different temperament from you; for instance, if your mother is quite fiery and you're more earthy or watery. You may be trying to communicate that you need to be held or fed in a certain way, but she doesn't get the message, she doesn't pick up on what you are asking for or require. As an infant this could make you feel that you're stupid, that there must be something lacking in you. This becomes part of your personal mythology, an early impression you form about life and about yourself which might haunt you later on. In other words, Moon-Mercury problems can manifest as an insecurity about your intelligence or your ability to communicate and be understood. But we shouldn't just examine the past and early childhood in order to moan about what happened. We want to go into the past and into the unconscious in order to understand the present better, to see the connection between your later life or current relationship problems and what happened between you and mother as a child. So if you had trouble making yourself understood and you experienced communication difficulties with mother, what are the possible consequences in later relationships? What will you be sensitive or touchy about? I often hear people who have these aspects complaining “My partner doesn't understand me. We can't express our needs or feelings to each other.” You see how this is the same problem which was there with mother in first few years of life.
Howard：对，互相理解的问题，互相沟通的问题。原因很明显。月亮与你的安全和安全感需求有关，你被抱住、被喂食和被安慰的需求。水星与信息传递有关。因此当你的月亮——母亲的征象星——与水星有困难时，你可能会发现你们两个之间难以互相理解。简单说，她可能读不懂你——你们的线路搭错了。如果你的母亲与你气质差异很大时就会发生这种情况；比如，你的母亲很火爆而你偏土象或水象。你可能试图传达你需要以某种方式被抱住或喂食，但她没有收到信息，她没有理解你在要求或需要什么。作为婴儿，这可能让你觉得自己很笨，觉得自己一定有什么缺陷。这成为你个人神话的一部分，你对生活和自己形成的早期印象，后来可能会纠缠你。换言之，月-水问题可能表现为对你智力或沟通能力和被理解能力的不安全感。但我们不应仅仅为了抱怨过去发生的事而检视过去和早期童年。我们想要进入过去和潜意识，是为了更好地理解现在，看到你后来的生活或当前关系问题与你小时候和母亲之间发生的事情之间的联系。如果你在让母亲理解你方面遇到了困难，在与母亲的沟通中经历了困难，那么在后来的关系中可能会有什么后果？你会对什么敏感或容易触怒？我经常听到有这些相位的人抱怨「我的伴侣不理解我。我们无法向对方表达我们的需求或感受。」你看，这与生命最初几年与母亲之间的问题是一样的。

Let's consider the hard angles of the Moon to Venus. What kinds of problems can these aspects signify in terms of your love affair with mother?
让我们考虑月亮与金星的硬相位。就你与母亲的恋爱而言，这些相位可能意味着什么样的问题？

Audience: I have Moon square Venus and I can remember finding my mother ugly and coarse. I didn't like the way she moved or touched me.
听众：我的月亮四分金星，我记得觉得母亲丑陋粗俗。我不喜欢她移动或触碰我的方式。

Howard: Yes, I've heard other people report similar things. Even though the Moon and Venus are personal planets and you might not think that the hard angles between them would be as problematic as Moon in trouble with Saturn or an outer planet, difficult Moon-Venus aspects can create quite a lot of tension in relationship later on. Here we have your need for security and what you require to feel safe and included (the Moon and mother) at odds with what you find attractive or beautiful (Venus). Later in life, this conflict could repeat itself in a variety of ways. You may marry or get involved with someone who offers you security or who makes you feel safe, but this person somehow isn't the one who really turns you on erotically or excites you in a Venusian way. In other words, because these two planets are in conflict with one another, you may marry for safety at the expense of Venus. Or it could be the converse situation: the people you're attracted to (Venus) are not the ones who can offer you the kind of safety or security you need.
Howard：是的，我听过其他人也报告了类似的事情。尽管月亮和金星都是个人行星，你可能不认为它们之间的硬相位会像月亮与土星或外行星的困难相位那样问题严重，但困难的月-金相位在后来的关系中可以制造相当多的紧张。这里你有你的安全感需求和你需要感到安全和被接纳的东西（月亮和母亲）与你觉得有吸引力的或美丽的东西（金星）之间的冲突。在后来的生活中，这种冲突可能以各种方式重复。你可能与一个提供你安全感或让你感到安全的人结婚或交往，但这个人在某种意义上并不是真正在情欲上吸引你或以金星的方式让你兴奋的人。换言之，因为这两颗行星彼此冲突，你可能为了安全而以牺牲金星为代价结婚。或者情况可能相反：你被吸引的人（金星）不是能提供你需要的那种安全感的人。

I've also seen Moon-Venus problems manifest in quite another way. When you have these two planets in square or hard angle, it signifies a tension or probable incompatibility between what these planets represent archetypically. We've looked briefly at the case of not finding the mother beautiful. But the reverse could be true—we might find her too exciting or too enticing. In other words, there is a mix-up between the maternal principle and the sexual or erotic principle. So mother may be feeding or holding you in the course of fulfilling your basic Moon/survival needs, but it actually feels sexual to you. Perhaps mother is not getting her Venusian needs met through her partner, and unconsciously turns to her child for that kind of excitement or pleasure. What we have here is the “seductive mother.” This can create problems for the male child later in life because there is a taboo against sex with mother. So he starts getting close to a woman but as soon as she becomes too familiar or maternal with him, he feels funny about being sexual with her.
我也见过月-金问题以另一种方式表现。当这两颗行星四分或形成硬相位时，它象征着这两颗行星在原型层面所代表的东西之间的紧张或可能的不兼容。我们已经简要看过觉得母亲不美的情况。但反过来也可能是——我们可能觉得她太令人兴奋或太诱人了。换言之，母性原则与性或情欲原则之间有混淆。所以母亲可能在满足你的基本月亮/生存需求的过程中喂食或抱住你，但对你来说它实际上感觉是性的。也许母亲没有从她的伴侣那里满足她的金星需求，于是无意识地转向她的孩子寻求那种兴奋或愉悦。我们这里看到的是「诱惑型母亲」。这可能在后来给男性孩子制造问题，因为与母亲发生性关系是禁忌。所以他开始接近一个女人，但一旦她变得太熟悉或太像母亲，他就对与她发生性关系感到不舒服。

Moon-Venus aspects can give a slightly different problem in the chart of a female child. Mother may be seen as the one with a monopoly on beauty, style or taste, thereby leaving the child feeling inadequate by comparison. A kind of competitiveness can arise: “Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the fairest of them all?” This sense of not being as beautiful as the mother can stay with the female child right through life, manifesting in difficulties and rivalries with other women later on.
月-金相位在女性孩子的星盘中可能给出稍微不同的问题。母亲可能被视为垄断了美丽、风格或品味的人，因此让孩子在比较中感到不足。一种竞争性可能产生：「魔镜魔镜，谁是最美的人？」这种不如母亲美的感觉可能伴随女性孩子一生，在后来与其他女性的困难和和对立中表现出来。

Audience: Is it possible with these aspects that the mother feels the child is unattractive and the child picks up on those feelings?
听众：这些相位是否可能意味着母亲觉得孩子没有吸引力，而孩子感受到了这些情绪？

Howard: Yes, in some cases I think that the child may feel that he or she is not what the mother values or appreciates. Moon-Venus problems can also be seen as a tension or incompatibility between two different faces of the feminine principle, between the maternal and the erotic. Some women with these aspects experience a conflict as they get older between these two faces of the feminine. They might align themselves with being maternal and forfeit their Venusian side by letting their looks go or not really caring about their attractiveness, or they are puella or hetaira types who are happy being a flirt, a girlfriend or an inspiration to a partner, but are uncertain about committment, marriage or maternity. The challenge is to make room in marriage or relationship for both the Moon and Venus—for instance, every once in a while leaving the kids with your mother for a week so that you and your spouse can go off alone on a romantic holiday for two. We've already mentioned how men with hard Moon-Venus angles may split their anima figures into the whore and the madonna. If they live with someone for a while, the partner is seen as mother and this gives rise to sexual problems because it's not on to have sex with mother. Some men attempt to “resolve” this tension by having an affair or something on the side to satisfy their Venusian needs, although I'm sure there are ways to have both the Moon and Venus in a marriage or long-standing relationship.
Howard：是的，在某些情况下我认为孩子可能感到他或她不是母亲所重视或欣赏的。月-金问题也可以被视为女性原则两个面向之间的紧张或不兼容——母性的面向与情欲的面向之间。一些有这些相位的女性随着年龄增长会在这两个面向之间经历冲突。她们可能与母性认同而放弃她们的金星面——放任外表或不在意自己的吸引力；或者她们是少女型或女伴型，乐意做个调情者、女友或伴侣的灵感源泉，但对承诺、婚姻或母性感到不确定。挑战在于在婚姻或关系中为月亮和金星都留出空间——比如，偶尔把孩子交给你的母亲一周，这样你和配偶可以单独去度一个浪漫的假期。我们已经提到过月-金硬相位的男性如何将他们的阿尼玛意象分裂为妓女和圣母。如果他们与某人生活一段时间，伴侣被视为母亲，这会引起性问题，因为与母亲发生性关系是不可以的。一些男性试图通过有外遇或找外遇来「解决」这种紧张，以满足他们的金星需求，尽管我相信在婚姻或长期关系中是有办法同时拥有月亮和金星的。

How about the Moon in difficult angle to Mars? What could these aspects indicate in terms of how your love affair with mother went?
月亮与火星的硬相位如何？就你与母亲的恋爱而言，这些相位可能暗示什么？

Audience: There may have been battles.
听众：可能有斗争。

Howard: Yes, I immediately think of a battle between two strongwilled individuals: you want it one way, she wants it another; you want it now, she wants it later; she wants you to behave in a certain way, and you're not in the mood to comply. You don't have the verbal capacity to quarrel or argue with your mother when you are six months old, but these aspects can manifest in fierce arguments and plate-throwing in later relationships. You'll very often have territorial or space problems in your early love affair with mother. The feeling is that mother is too intrusive, bossy or domineering. It's not hard to see why this could be the case with these two particular planets interconnected—the Moon is mother and it is linked with Mars, the god of war and assertion. I also have an image of an infant wanting to venture out and explore the immediate environment or the outside world, but mother comes along and intrudes. You start to “do” your Mars and assert your independence or sense of adventure, but if it is in hard angle to the Moon then mother is somehow dragging along after you or interfering, barging in with her view of what you should be doing or how you should be doing it. So if you have these kinds of experiences in your first major relationship, there might then be a tendency to attract or be sensitive to similar issues in later partnerships. Again and again I hear people with Moon-Mars angles complain about being invaded or not have enough space. In actual fact I believe that a hard Moon-Mars angle is an inner conflict, an inner dilemma between that part of you which wants to be adventurous and independent and another part of you which craves closeness, safety and security. The ego, however, hates ambivalence, so you may identify with and live out the Mars side and project the Moon—that is, see others as trying to cling to you or hold you back.
Howard：对，我立刻想到两个意志坚强的个体之间的战斗：你想这样，她想那样；你想现在，她想等会儿；她希望你以某种方式行事，而你没心情顺从。你六个月大时还没有与母亲争吵或辩论的语言能力，但这些相位在后来的关系中可以表现为激烈的争吵和摔盘子。你在早期与母亲的恋爱中经常会有领地或空间问题。感觉是母亲太侵入、太专横或太控制。不难看出为什么这两颗特定的行星连接在一起会如此——月亮是母亲，它与火星——战神和主张之神——联系在一起。我还有一个意象是婴儿想要出去探索周围环境或外部世界，但母亲过来介入。你开始「做」你的火星并主张你的独立或冒险感，但如果它与月亮形成硬相位，那么母亲就以某种方式拖在你后面或干涉，带着她对你应该做什么或应该怎么做的看法闯入。所以如果你在第一段主要关系中有这些经历，那么后来在伴侣关系中就可能倾向于吸引或对类似的问题敏感。我一次又一次听到有月-火相位的人抱怨被侵入或没有足够的空间。实际上我相信月-火硬相位是一种内在冲突，是你想要冒险和独立的那部分与你渴望亲密、安全和安全的另一部分之间的内在困境。然而，自我讨厌矛盾，所以你可能认同并活出火星面而投射月亮——即，看到别人试图依附于你或拖后腿。

Audience: Is this also the case with the conjunction?
听众：合相也是如此吗？

Howard: Yes, very often. But whenever you're assessing how a conjunction will work, you also have to examine any other aspects in the chart to the conjunction. If you have Moon conjunct Mars trine Venus it will be less of a problem than Moon conjunct Mars square Venus. Nonetheless, the conjunction of these two planets inevitably links your image of mother with the god of war. You'll usually view her as strong, powerful or angry. She may not show that anger, frustration or power: it may be simmering, it may be seething or hiding underneath, but it is there. Originally mother is the whole world to you, so what passes between you and your mother is a pretty good indication of how you will see or relate to the world in general later on. If we felt safe with mother, then the world feels safe; if mother didn't seem too steady or reliable a container, then later on the world feels more dangerous. If you have to fight with mother to establish your space or independence, then later on you may find yourself repeatedly in situations where you are fighting with close friends, partners or loved ones for more freedom and room to move.
Howard：对，通常如此。但每当你评估一个合相如何运作时，你还必须检查星盘中对合相的任何其他相位。如果你有月亮合火星三分金星，那将比月亮合火星四分金星问题少些。尽管如此，这两颗行星的合相不可避免地将你的母亲意象与战神联系在一起。你通常会认为她是强壮的、有力的或愤怒的。她可能不显示那种愤怒、挫折感或力量：它可能在翻滚，可能在沸腾或隐藏在下面，但它在。最初母亲对你来说是整个世界，所以你与母亲之间发生的事情很好地预示了你后来将如何看待或与整个世界建立关系。如果我们与母亲在一起感到安全，那么世界感觉安全；如果母亲似乎不太稳定或不太可靠作为容器，那么后来世界感觉更危险。如果你必须与母亲争斗来确立你的空间或独立，那么后来你可能发现自己反复在与亲密朋友、伴侣或爱人争夺更多自由和活动空间。

Let's take Moon-Jupiter aspects. With the hard angles, the relationship with mother may go through noticeable—often quite dramatic—mood swings, from love and bliss to pain and despair, all wonderful one day and then all terrible the next. We love her and think she is the greatest thing on earth, and then for whatever reason the situation reverses, leaving us feeling betrayed and let down. Can you see why this is? The Moon is associated with emotions and feelings, while Jupiter is a planet associated with expansiveness and the tendency to over-do or go to extremes. People with Moon in aspect to Jupiter often have manic, rollercoasterlike relationships.
让我们看月-木相位。在硬相位中，与母亲的关系可能经历明显的——通常是相当戏剧性的——情绪波动，从爱与幸福到痛苦与绝望，一天一切都美好然后第二天一切都糟糕。我们爱她并认为她是世界上最伟大的，然后出于什么原因情况逆转了，让我们感到被背叛和失望。你能看出为什么吗？月亮与情绪和感受有关，而木星是一颗与扩张性和过度或走极端倾向有关的行星。月亮与木星有相位的人通常有躁狂的、过山车式的关系。

I'm reminded of a woman I know who has Moon conjunct Jupiter in Taurus square to Pluto in Leo. As a child, her feelings for her mother swung from worship and adoration to hate, fear and loathing—a pattern or prototype which she repeats in most of her adult involvements. The Pluto square serves to bring out the extremes of her Moon-Jupiter conjunction. After telling me about her wonderful and kind mother, she then added that there were times when her mother beat her badly or locked her up in a cupboard for a relatively minor misdemeanour. As a consequence of these early experiences, she came to associate relationships with dramatic ups and downs. She meets a man and rings me up to talk and rave about him: he is perfect, he is divine, he is Zeus incarnate. Her relationships usually get off the ground very quickly—two days after getting together, she and her new lover are planning their future life together, and this usually involves starting up a business or project which magically will bring money and fulfilment to them. I mean this woman functions like clockwork. Whenever she calls and tells me these things, I look at my watch and check the date. I know that in approximately two weeks I'll be hearing from her again, and shell be moaning about what a bastard and disappointment he is. I've been observing this pattern in her for years and years. So just by assessing the Moon in her chart, you have a good idea of what her relationships are like. This is the point I'm making, that the Moon is as much of a significator for relationship as is Venus.
我想起我认识的一位女性，月亮合金星在金牛座，四分狮子座冥王星。作为孩子，她对母亲的感情从崇拜和爱慕摆动到仇恨、恐惧和厌恶——她在大多数成年关系中重复这一模式或原型。冥王星的四分有助于将她月-木合相的极端性带出来。在告诉我她那位美妙善良的母亲之后，她补充说有时候母亲因为一个相对轻微的过错就狠打她或把她锁在橱柜里。由于这些早期经验，她开始将关系与戏剧性的起伏联系在一起。她遇到一个男人并打电话给我谈论和狂热地称赞他：他完美，他神圣，他是宙斯转世。她的关系通常很快起飞——在一起两天后，她和她的新恋人就在规划他们的未来生活，这通常涉及创立一个神奇地为他们带来金钱和满足感的生意或项目。我是说这个女人像钟表一样运作。每当她打电话告诉我这些事，我就看表查日期。我知道大约两周后我会再收到她的消息，然后她就会抱怨他是个多么混蛋和令人失望。我观察她的这种模式已经很多年了。所以仅仅通过评估她星盘中的月亮，你就能对她的关系有一个好的了解。这就是我要强调的：月亮与金星一样是关系的征象星。

If you have a Moon-Jupiter aspect in your natal chart, it could also mean that your mother had a conflict between mothering and wanting to be out in the world doing something she considered more adventurous or exciting. She may literally be foreign or travel a great deal, or have a penchant for religion, philosophy or sport, anything expansive. So the image of your loved one is linked with qualities of Jupiter. In a man's chart, he may later seek a partner who somehow embodies Jupiter, someone who is exciting, inspirational, adventurous. This is fine so long as it's not at odds with another side of him that wants a more sedate or settled woman for a mate.
如果你的本命图中有月-木相位，这也可能意味着你的母亲在母性与想要出去到世界上做她认为更有冒险性或更令人兴奋的事情之间有冲突。她可能确实是外国人或经常旅行，或者热爱宗教、哲学或体育，任何扩张性的事物。所以你的爱人意象与木星的品质联系在一起。在男性星盘中，他后来可能寻找一个以某种方式体现木星的伴侣，一个令人兴奋的、鼓舞人心的、冒险的人。只要这与他想要一个更安稳的伴侣的另一面不冲突就没问题。

Let's briefly consider some possible manifestations of the hard aspects of the Moon to Saturn. What could these aspects indicate in terms of your urge to love and relate with mother?
让我们简要考虑月亮与土星硬相位的一些可能表现。就你爱与母亲建立联系的冲动而言，这些相位可能暗示什么？

Audience: You might meet some form of coldness.
听众：你可能遇到某种形式的冷漠。

Howard: Yes, you could encounter someone who is uptight in some way, who seems to be burdened with difficulties, or who simply has problems responding to your needs in a fashion which makes you feel at ease. In some cases, mother may be trying her hardest to be attentive to your comfort and satisfaction, but she might be so nervous about doing her job right that what you ultimately pick up on is her insecurity and doubts. We could also look at it in another way. Picture yourself at six months or so wanting to be fed or held but for whatever reasons, your mother fails or is unable to meet these needs. You run into a brick wall; maybe she's busy with other responsibilities or has read in a book that babies should be fed according to a timetable and not just when they express a desire to be fed. So you have real emotional or physiological requirements, but they're not being met. What might this do to you? How is this going to affect you inside?
Howard：对，你可能遇到一个在某种意义上紧张的人，一个似乎被困难所困扰的人，或者一个单纯以让你感到自在的方式回应你的需求有困难的人。在某些情况下，母亲可能在尽力关注你的舒适和满足，但她可能对做好工作太紧张了，以至于你最终感受到的是她的不安全感和疑虑。我们也可以从另一个角度看。想象你六个月大想要被喂食或被抱住，但出于什么原因，你的母亲未能或无法满足这些需求。你碰了一堵砖墙；也许她忙于其他责任，或者她在一本书上读到婴儿应该按时间表喂食而不是仅仅在他们表达喂食欲望时。所以你有真实的情感或生理需求，但它们没有被满足。这会对你做什么？这会怎样在内在影响你？

Audience: You then feel frustrated and insecure.
听众：你然后会感到沮丧和不安。

Howard: Yes, that is very likely. It's also likely that you'll feel you're to blame, that there's something wrong with you: “She doesn't give me what I need, therefore I must be bad and unlovable.” This is called “introjecting” the bad mother, or identifying with the bad breast. Early impressions cut deeply, so if you think you're bad, no good, or unworthy of love, then what kinds of feelings are you going to bring into relationships with you later in life? Even if someone truly loves you, on some deep level you are unable to believe it. People with Moon in hard angle to Saturn often lack selfconfidence and carry the conviction that others will fail to meet their needs. They form touchy, nervous attachments; they find it hard to relax in a relationship, and their anxieties and insecurities may, in the end, drive the other person away. In this way, they manage to turn their worst fears and expectations into a selffulfilling prophecy. Or (according to the doctrine of repetition compulsion), you may go for those people who, by nature, have difficulty showing love or meeting your particular needs. There may be suitors around who truly desire you and want to make you happy, but they're not the ones who interest you. Instead you're drawn to the difficult people who can't quite respond to you in the way you need, as if some part of your psyche is still trying to turn a “bad” mother into a good one.
Howard：对，这很有可能。你也很可能会感到自己应受责备，觉得自己有什么问题：「她不给我需要的东西，因此我一定是坏的、不可爱的。」这叫做「内摄」坏母亲，或认同坏乳房。早期印象切得很深，所以如果你觉得自己坏、不好或不配被爱，那么你会在后来的关系中带来什么样的感受？即使有人真心爱你，在某个深层你无法相信。月-土硬相位的人通常缺乏自信，并带着别人将无法满足他们需求的信念。他们形成敏感的、紧张的关系；他们在关系中难以放松，他们的焦虑和不安最终可能把另一个人赶走。这样，他们成功地把自己最大的恐惧和期望变成了自我实现的预言。或者（根据强迫性重复的学说），你可能会选择那些本质上难以表达爱或满足你特定需求的人。可能有追求者真心想要你并想让你幸福，但他们不是让你感兴趣的人。相反你被那些无法完全以你需要的方式回应你的困难的人吸引，好像你心理的某部分仍在试图将一个「坏」母亲变成好母亲。

Moon-Saturn aspects also can give rise to someone who doesn't feel okay about even having needs or wants. If as a child you had difficulties getting your needs fulfilled, it may be easier for you to stop needing, rather than going through the pain of not getting what you seek. If you needed mother to be there in a certain way, and over and over again you were let down, you begin to feel that loving and needing hurt too much. Emotional detachment becomes a strategy or defence against the pain of unfulfilled needs—it is better not to acknowledge or show your needs because it hurts too much when these are not met. So you cut off from what you really want, you deny your feelings. In doing so you become seemingly self-sufficient. A rock feels no pain: you appear tough and strong, but underneath is someone who is hurting, someone who is fearful and who doesn't feel worthy of love and fulfilment.6
月-土相位也可能产生一个甚至对有需求或想要都感到不自在的人。如果你作为孩子就难以满足需求，那么停止需要可能比经历得不到所求的痛苦更容易。如果你需要母亲以某种方式在场，而一次又一次地被失望，你开始觉得爱和需要太痛苦了。情感疏离成为一种策略或防御，用来对抗未被满足的需求的痛苦——最好不要承认或展示你的需求，因为当它们不被满足时太痛苦了。所以你切断了你真正想要的东西，你否认你的感受。这样做你变得看似自给自足。岩石没有痛感：你显得坚强和强壮，但下面是一个受伤的人，一个恐惧的人，一个不觉得自己配得到爱和满足的人。⁶

Compensation also may come into play here. If you had a Moon-Saturn type relationship with your mother and you ended up feeling unlovable or unworthy, you may then try to make up for this by being superproductive and by doing things to prove your value to the world. But there is a compulsion or complex underlying this kind of compensatory behaviour. If you're not being productive or doing what you consider are worthwhile things, then you don't feel you deserve love. You have to keep proving yourself; you can never really fully relax. In order to feel worthy or safe, you have to be responsible, successful and achieving in a Saturntype way. All this is a means of making up for your deeper underlying sense of inadequacy. I'm sure some of you can identify with what I'm talking about, or know others who behave in this way. It is especially important for Moon-Saturn people to grieve for the ideal mothering they never received, to work through the pain, guilt and anger engendered when the bonding with mother has failed, or was too weak, or tenuous.
补偿也可能在这里起作用。如果你与母亲有月-土型关系，最终感到自己不可爱或不配，你可能试图通过过度产出和做事来弥补，向世界证明你的价值。但这种补偿行为的背后有一种强迫或情结。如果你不产出或做你认为有价值的事情，你就不觉得自己配被爱。你必须不断证明自己；你永远无法真正放松。为了感到有价值或安全，你必须以土星式的方式负责、成功和有成就。所有这些都是弥补你更深层的不配感的一种手段。我相信你们中有些人能认同我所说的，或者认识以这种方式行事的人。对月-土人来说，哀悼从未得到的理想母爱，处理当与母亲的纽带失败时——太弱或太脆弱时——所产生的痛苦、内疚和愤怒，尤为重要。

Now, let's briefly examine difficult Moon-Uranus contacts in terms of our early romance with mother. Try to picture the consequences of these two planets at odds with one another. You're attempting to bond with mother and then you run into Uranus; in other words, you run into some kind of disruption, something erratic, uncertain or unconventional—any of those qualities we normally associate with Uranus. Mother may be felt as a shaky or unstable container; she may be there physically but for some reasons you don't feel sure about her. Something in you senses she's restless and might get up and leave at any moment. She can be holding or feeding you, and yet she doesn't feel solid and fully attentive—her mind may be somewhere else, thinking about other things she would like to be doing or contemplating abstract theories and philosophies rather than being totally present for you. If you have these kinds of aspects, you may feel that your safety and security could be disrupted at any moment, things could change in a minute.
现在，让我们从早期与母亲的恋爱角度简要检视月-天困难接触。试着想象这两颗行星彼此冲突的后果。你试图与母亲建立纽带然后遇到了天王星；换言之，你遇到了某种中断、某种不稳定的、不确定的或非传统的东西——任何我们通常与天王星联系的品质。母亲可能被感觉为一个不稳或不稳定的容器；她可能在身体上在场，但出于什么原因你对她不确定。你内在的某种东西感觉到她不安分，可能随时起身离开。她可以正在抱住或喂你，然而她感觉不坚实和不完全专注——她的心可能在别处，想着她想做的其他事情或沉思抽象理论和哲学，而不是完全为你临在。如果你有这些相位，你可能觉得你的安全和安全感可能随时被中断，事情可能在一瞬间改变。

If you meet these kinds of situations with mother in your first big romance, it's likely that similar apprehensions or expectations will consciously or unconsciously remain with you into adult life. Later on you find yourself in a relationship, but you have a nagging sense that it could all change or end suddenly. Conversely, because you have not had the experience of a solid and safe container, you don't know how to be one yourself; therefore you may be the one who feels restless in partnership, who is easily bored or distracted. Or you grow into the kind of person who appears totally autonomous and self-sufficient, when, in actual fact, your self-sufficiency is a defence or armour concealing a frightened child living underneath, a child afraid to trust or rely on the love of others.
如果你在第一段大恋爱中与母亲遇到了这些情况，类似的忧虑或期望可能会有意或无意地伴随你进入成年生活。后来你发现自己处于一段关系中，但有一种挥之不去的感觉：一切都可能突然改变或结束。反过来，因为你没有体验过一个坚实和安全的容器，你不知道如何自己成为一个；因此你可能是那个在关系中感到不安分的人，那个容易无聊或分心的人。或者你成长为那种看起来完全自主和自给自足的人，而实际上你的自给自足是一种防御或盔甲，掩盖着一个活在下面的受惊的孩子，一个害怕信任或依赖他人的爱的孩子。

In a man's chart, it can indicate an almost compulsive attraction to women who are fairly independent or Uranian in nature, whether or not they show that side of themselves at first. In a woman's chart they indicate confusion about whether she really wants to mother at all or lead a conventional married life. Anyone with these aspects could have inner conflicts between wanting the type of partner who offers security and can make a settled home, and finding they are attracted to people who display a high degree of autonomy and independence.
在男性星盘中，它可能表明一种几乎强迫性的对相当独立或天王星本性女性的吸引力，无论她们最初是否表现出那一面。在女性星盘中，它表明她是否真的想要母性或过传统婚姻生活的困惑。有这些相位的人可能在内化在想要一个提供安全并能安家的伴侣与发现自己被吸引到展示高度自主和独立的人之间有内在冲突。

Because these two planets represent very different principles or archetypes, their hard aspects often produce a “closeness/ freedom” dilemma. The Moon craves closeness and inclusiveness, but Uranus likes its space and freedom. If you have Moon-Uranus aspects in your chart, you need to make room in your life for both sides of the polarity. If you just identify and side with your need for closeness, you're denying your need for greater autonomy and individuality. Should this be the case, your partner will likely be the one who acts out what you are suppressing in yourself. Your clingingness or your conventionality may drive away the partner in a search for someone more exciting, or in search of a freer and more expansive life. In other words, there is a split going on, what has been labelled by Maggie Scarf as an “emotional division of labour.”7 You carry the closeness needs, and the other person becomes the one who lives out your denied Uranian urges. Or the reverse is true: your partner is the one who provides the stability, and you're the one who is uncertain and variable. Either way, the situation is usually not very satisfying, and it doesn't make for relationships that last.
因为这两颗行星代表非常不同的原则或原型，它们的硬相位经常产生一种「亲密/自由」困境。月亮渴望亲密和包容，但天王星喜欢它的空间和自由。如果你的星盘中有月-天相位，你需要为两极在你的生活中留出空间。如果你只是认同并站在你渴望亲密的一边，你就否定了你对更大自主和个性的需求。如果是这种情况，你的伴侣可能是那个活出你所压抑的东西的人。你的依附性或你的传统性可能在寻找一个更令人兴奋的人或寻求更自由更广阔的生活中把伴侣赶走。换言之，这里有一个分裂，Maggie Scarf 称之为「情感分工」。⁷ 你带着亲密需求，另一个人成为那个活出你被否定的天王星冲动的人。或者反过来：你的伴侣是那个提供稳定性的人，而你是不确定和多变的。无论哪种方式，情况通常不是很令人满意，也不利于持久的关系。

I'll be discussing the freedom/closeness dilemma in greater depth in my lecture on Venus.8 For now, suffice it to say, that it's better for you to accept that you have both the desire for closeness and the desire for autonomy within yourself and work out some way to make room in your life and your relationships for both of these needs. The task at hand is how to be close and intimate and yet also leave some space for yourself. It's likely that your mother had a similar dilemma or tension inside her, and now it's in your life and can be seen in your relationship patterns.
我将在关于金星的讲座中更深入地讨论自由/亲密困境。⁸ 目前只需说，最好接受你在内在同时有对亲密和对自主的渴望，并想出某种方式在你的生活和你的关系中为这两种需求都留出空间。手头的任务是如何亲密和紧密但同时又为自己留一些空间。很可能你的母亲内在也有类似的困境或紧张，现在它出现在你的生活中并可以从你的关系模式中看到。

We will cover Moon-Neptune and Moon-Pluto aspects in the joint session on the Sun and Moon (in Part 3, pp. 197–201). Right now, I want to change gears slightly and broaden how we are looking at the Moon. We've been discussing it as one of the indicators of what we encounter or expect in intimate, one-to-one relationship based on our early love affair with mother. However, the Moon is activated anytime you seek to belong or be included. To put it another way, the Moon represents your inclusion needs. Just think about all the different kinds of situations you experience in life where you want to belong, where you want to be included: it can be a dinner party or other kinds of social gatherings, or even at the office where you work.
我们将在太阳与月亮的联合讲座中（第三部分，第197-201页）讨论月-海和月-冥相位。现在，我想稍微换一下话题，扩大我们看待月亮的视角。我们一直在讨论月亮作为基于早期与母亲的恋爱而在亲密的一对一关系中遇到或期望什么的指标之一。然而，每当你要寻求归属或被接纳时，月亮就被激活了。换言之，月亮代表你的归属需求。想想你在生活中经历的想要归属、想要被接纳的各种不同情境：可以是一场晚宴或其他社交聚会，甚至在你工作的办公室里。

I'm expanding the significance of the Moon to include what happens in group situations such as at a party, and to signify what you need to feel safe and secure in whatever environment you find yourself. I'd like you to observe yourself and see if you can get a sense of what you need to feel comfortable there, how you act or behave in order to feel safe and okay in a social setting. What makes you feel secure and included? What makes you feel unloved or unwanted, dislodged or the odd person out?
我在扩展月亮的含义，将其纳入在群体场合如聚会中发生的事情，并用以表示你在所发现的任何环境中需要什么才能感到安全和踏实。我希望你们观察自己，看看你能否感受到你在那里需要什么才能感到舒服，你如何行动或表现才能在社交场合感到安全和自在。什么让你感到安全和被接纳？什么让你感到不被爱或不需要、被排挤或是多余的人？

These are not original ideas. I'm borrowing from Stephen Arroyo, who in his book The Practice and Profession of Astrology, analyses the Moon as an indicator of how you interact with the environment in order to feel at home, in order to feel welcomed or included.9 In fact, we can play a kind of game with this. Project your mind onto an upcoming party and try to imagine what the different Moon signs will need or what they might do in order to feel comfortable at such an occasion. Arroyo suggests that a good way to do this is to use the phrase “Let us …” or “Let's do …” I'll illustrate what I mean by using the Moon in Aries as an example. Unless your Moon in Aries is severely restricted or impinged upon by more downbeat planets, you're likely to feel at your best if you can activate and arouse the environment in some way, so a phrase associated with the Moon in Aries may be something like “Let's get this thing going; let's energise the environment.” You might be impatient or easily bored, so you want to get the party moving. You may be the one who initiates speaking to someone you don't know, or you might be the first one to dance. For the majority of people with the Moon in Aries, doing anything is better than doing nothing: the way they feel comfortable and at home is by making things happen or getting things going.
这些并非原创想法。我借鉴了 Stephen Arroyo，他在他的著作《占星的实践与职业》中分析月亮作为你如何与环境互动以便感到自在、感到被欢迎或被接纳的指标。⁹ 事实上，我们可以用这个来玩一种游戏。将你的心投射到一个即将到来的聚会上，试着想象不同月亮星座的人会需要什么或会做什么才能在这种场合感到舒服。Arroyo 建议一个好的方法是使用短语「让我们……」或「让我们做……」我用月亮在白羊座为例来说明我的意思。除非你的月亮在白羊座受到更压抑的行星的严重限制或压迫，否则如果你能以某种方式激活和唤起环境，你很可能会处于最佳状态，所以与月亮在白羊座相关的短语可能是「让这件事动起来；让我们给环境注入活力」。你可能不耐烦或容易无聊，所以你想让聚会动起来。你可能是第一个主动跟不认识的人说话的人，或者你可能第一个跳舞。对于大多数月亮在白羊座的人来说，做任何事都比什么都不做好：他们感到自在和归属的方式是让事情发生或推动事情启动。

Contrast this with people who have Moon in Taurus. They usually need to feel physically comfortable or settled in order to feel safe. They'll look for a space to sit or stand that feels right. They may make themselves secure by heading straight for the food table—they may not feel safe until they have had something to eat. I'm joking to some extent. When I first read Arroyo on this, I was a little surprised when he wrote that the Moon in Taurus feels most safe if it has control over the environment. I had never really thought of Taurus in terms of control issues. But it is true. I have this placement and I know that I feel most at home or happiest when things aren't too hectic, chaotic or haphazard, when things are in order and I have a say about how they're going to be run. For instance, if I found out suddenly that we had to change our lecture room tomorrow, I'd probably have trouble sleeping tonight. Will the new room be adequate, will it have what I need? The more familiar I am with an environment, the more comfortable I feel.
将此与月亮在金牛座的人对比。他们通常需要感到身体上的舒适或安定才能感到安全。他们会找一个感觉合适的地方坐下或站。他们可能通过直奔餐台来让自己安心——他们可能直到吃了东西才感到安全。我在某种程度上是在开玩笑。当我第一次读到 Arroyo 写到月亮在金牛座如果能控制环境就感到最安全时，我有点惊讶。我从未真正从控制问题的角度想过金牛座。但这是真的。我有这个配置，我知道当事情不太忙乱、混乱或随意时，当事情井井有序而且我对它们如何运行有发言权时，我感到最自在或最快乐。例如，如果我突然发现明天我们不得不换讲座教室，我今晚可能睡不好。新教室够大吗，它有我需要的东西吗？我对环境越熟悉，我就越感到舒服。

What about Moon in Gemini? What might their “let us” statement be?
月亮在双子座呢？他们的「让我们」声明可能是什么？

Audience: Let's communicate and exchange information.
听众：让我们交流交换信息。

Howard: Exactly, they usually feel more comfortable and at home when they start talking with people and making connections with others. For instance, let's say a Moon in Gemini person meets someone at a party and discovers that they both know someone in common, or both have brothers who work in computers. Bingo! Now, they are off, now they fit in. They may want to impress you with their knowledge on a wide range of subjects. The Moon in Gemini also likes to observe, almost a voyeur who enjoys drawing conclusions or making deductions from what it sees. These are the sorts of things that instinctively make them feel secure or included. What about the Moon in Cancer? What would the most obvious need be?
Howard：没错，当他们开始与人交谈并与其他人建立联系时，他们通常感到更舒服和自在。比如，假设一个月亮在双子座的人在聚会上遇到某人，发现他们都认识某个共同的人，或者都有在计算机行业工作的兄弟。中了！现在他们开始了，现在他们融入了。他们可能想用他们在各种主题上的知识来打动你。月亮在双子座也喜欢观察，几乎像个窥探者，享受从所见事物中得出结论或推断。这些正是让他们本能地感到安全或被接纳的东西。月亮在巨蟹座呢？最明显的需求是什么？

Audience: To merge with the environment, or to be helpful and caring for those they are with.
听众：与环境融合，或对身边的人有帮助和关怀。

Howard: Yes, if they're not too threatened by their surroundings, their instinct is to merge and blend. So if they're in a room full of saintlike people, they will mirror back their saintly side. But if they are in a room full of criminals, people with the Moon in Cancer may try to blend and be included by displaying that they too can be bad. And what you say about their need to mother is often true. They may offer to go to the bar to get you a drink, or they are the ones to get the coffee for everyone. So by feeding others or being sensitive to other people's needs, the Moon in Cancer person feels more comfortable as well. But I've noticed something else: if those with the Moon in this sign really don't like the environment or are in one of their withdrawn moods, then their instinctive reaction is to retreat, to sit in the corner talking to no one, or even to leave the party or scene altogether. They just want to get back home into their shell, into what is familiar.
Howard：对，如果他们没有太被周围环境所威胁，他们的本能就是融合和融入。所以如果他们在一个满是圣徒般的人的房间里，他们会映射出他们圣徒般的一面。但如果他们在一个满是罪犯的房间里，月亮在巨蟹座的人可能试图通过展示他们也可以变坏来融入和被接纳。你说的关于他们母性的需求也往往是对的。他们可能主动去吧台给你拿饮料，或者他们是给大家泡咖啡的人。所以通过喂食他人或对别人的需求敏感，月亮在巨蟹座的人也感到更舒服。但我还注意到另一件事：如果月亮在这个星座的人真的不喜欢环境或正处于某种退缩情绪中，那么他们的本能反应就是退缩，坐在角落里不跟任何人说话，甚至完全离开聚会或场景。他们只想回到家回到他们的壳里，回到熟悉的地方。

What about the Moon in Leo; what does this fire sign Moon need to do in a social situation to feel safe or included?
月亮在狮子座呢？这个火象星座的月亮在社交场合需要做什么才能感到安全或被接纳？

Audience: They will probably need to make some sort of impact on the environment.
听众：他们可能需要对环境产生某种影响。

Howard: Yes, their statement might be, “Let's vitalise the environment, let's get noticed, let me do something which allows me to shine or stand out.” It's when people see that they are a little bit special or unique in some way that they feel okay. A karmic astrologer once remarked that if you have the Moon in Leo it probably means that you were royalty or someone famous in a past life, and now you come into this incarnation expecting to be treated special, expecting to be discovered or noticed. Some Moon in Leo people have come to me for readings and they look so shy and unobtrusive, but when I talk to them about these instinctive needs for recognition and admiration, they have to admit that such feelings are there strongly within them. Also, I've noticed that there can be quite a bit of one-upmanship going on in them. So if they're with a group of thieves or robbers, the Moon in Leo person would like to be able to say that “I've robbed more than you,” or, “I have the best idea of all for a bank job.” If they can do one better, then they feel good about themselves, then they feel worthy of inclusion and love. As children, the more special we are to mother, the safer we feel. This is especially true for the Moon in this sign. And this need for specialness in order to feel good about themselves stays throughout life, long after they have left mother's side.
Howard：对，他们的声明可能是：「让我们给环境注入活力，让我们引人注目，让我做点能让我闪耀或脱颖而出的事。」当人们看到他们在某种意义上有点特别或独特时，他们才感觉良好。一位业力占星师曾说，如果你有月亮在狮子座，这可能意味着你在前世是皇室或名人，现在你来到这一世期待被特殊对待，期待被发现或注意到。一些月亮在狮子座的人来找我做解读，他们看起来很害羞不引人注目，但当我跟他们谈到这些对认可和赞赏的本能需求时，他们不得不承认这样的感受在内心很强烈。另外，我注意到他们中可以有相当多的攀比心理。所以如果他们在一群小偷或强盗中间，月亮在狮子座的人会想能够说「我偷的比你们多」或「我有一个最好的抢银行方案」。如果他们能略胜一筹，他们就会对自己感觉良好，就会觉得自己配被接纳和爱。作为孩子，我们对母亲越特别，我们就越感到安全。这对这个星座的月亮尤其如此。这种为了对自己感觉良好而需要特别的需求，在他们离开母亲身边很久之后仍然贯穿一生。

How about the Moon in Virgo? This placement can be quite contradictory, but what do you think of first?
月亮在处女座呢？这个配置可能相当矛盾，但你首先想到的是什么？

Audience: Maybe they feel most at home and at ease if they are emptying ashtrays or clearing the table? Or if they can find someone with whom to discuss their health.
听众：也许他们在倒烟灰缸或收拾桌子时感到最自在？或者如果他们能找到一个可以讨论健康问题的人。

Howard: Yes, these fit with the textbook idea of the Moon in Virgo. I think they need to feel useful and productive in whatever environment they are in. So they may offer to do the washing up, or even before the party begins they ring up to see if you would like them to make the sandwiches or to bring anything along. Or, as you suggest, they'll feel as if they've arrived when they meet someone with whom they can compare cholesterol levels—that certainly would be in line with the typical Virgoan preoccupation with the body and physical well-being. More seriously, to feel safe, Moon in Virgo often needs to size up the environment, to analyse it, to “clock” it. So their statement might be, “Let's study the environment, let's figure out how it works and then I will feel more relaxed, at home, safe and comfortable.” After all, it is a Mercuryruled sign. If someone with the Moon in Virgo is supersensitive or very uptight, then what do you think they'll do to feel comfortable? Probably, they will instinctively start to criticise the environment, to dissect or tear others apart a little in order to feel all right about themselves. They might comment on how the room should be decorated differently, or remark on the low quality of some of the other people around. But this is usually only when they are extremely nervous or ill at ease.
Howard：对，这些符合月亮在处女座的教科书形象。我认为他们需要在所处的任何环境中感到有用和有产出。所以他们可能主动洗碗，甚至在聚会开始前就打电话问你需不需要他们做三明治或带什么东西来。或者如你建议的，当他们遇到一个可以比较胆固醇水平的人时，他们才觉得自己到了位——这确实符合处女座对身体和身心健康的典型关注。更严肃地说，为了感到安全，月亮在处女座通常需要评估环境，分析它，「打量」它。所以他们的声明可能是：「让我们研究环境，让我们搞清楚它是怎么回事，然后我就更放松、更自在、更安全、更舒服。」毕竟，这是一个水星守护的星座。如果月亮在处女座的人超敏感或非常紧张，那么你觉得他们会做什么来感到舒服？可能，他们会本能地开始批评环境，为了让自己感觉好些而稍微剖析或拆解他人。他们可能评论房间应该怎么不同地装饰，或者评论周围某些其他人的低品质。但这通常只有在他们极度紧张或不安时才会发生。

What is the most obvious way that a Moon in Libra would approach a social situation?
月亮在天秤座的人会用什么最明显的方式来接近社交场合？

Audience: Their statement might be, “Let's be pleasing.”
听众：他们的声明可能是：「让我们讨人喜欢。」

Howard: Yes, you often get the Moon in Libra with a strong desire to harmonise with the environment in order to feel safe and secure. Or they might want to beautify the surroundings in some way. But again, I think it is a misunderstanding to think that the Moon in Libra is just motivated to be nice or sweet. This sign is also equipped with an instinct to redress imbalances. So if they're in an environment where everyone is being sickly sweet to one another, some people with the Moon in Libra will instinctively want to act out the opposite, to be aggressive or a little rude, a little crude or pushy in order to balance out the phoniness or lopsidedness they see around them. So their statement could be, “Let's oppose the environment,” especially if they decide it's not worth the effort to be liked. There is something of the flavour of the Moon in Virgo in this regard; they too can be judgemental and critical, measuring the party or the people there against their own ideals or expectations. There is a theory that Virgo and Libra were once one sign in the distant past, and I've certainly observed some similarities between these two Moon sign placements. The shadow side of having high expectations is the tendency to be critical and judgmental when others don't live up to your ideals. This is very different from the stereotype of the sweet and charming Libra Moon type.
Howard：对，你经常看到月亮在天秤座有一种与环境和谐相处以感到安全和踏实的强烈愿望。或者他们可能想以某种方式美化周围环境。但再说一次，我认为认为月亮在天秤座只是被驱动着要友好或甜蜜是一种误解。这个星座也配备了一种纠正不平衡的本能。所以如果他们在一个每个人都在彼此恶心的甜腻的环境中，一些月亮在天秤座的人会本能地想表现出相反的一面，变得有攻击性或有点粗鲁，有点粗俗或强硬，以平衡他们周围看到的虚伪或失衡。所以他们的声明可能是「让我们与环境对抗」，特别是如果他们觉得不值得费力去被人喜欢的话。在这方面有月亮在处女座的味道；他们也可以是评判性的和批判性的，用自己的理想或期望来衡量聚会或那里的人。有一种理论认为处女座和天秤座在远古时曾经是一个星座，我确实观察到这两个月亮星座配置之间有一些相似之处。高期望的阴影面是当别人达不到你的理想时倾向于批评和评判。这与甜蜜迷人的天秤座月亮类型的刻板印象大不相同。

What about the Moon in Scorpio? How are they going to approach an environment or behave at a party to feel most safe or comfortable?
月亮在天蝎座呢？他们会怎样接近环境或在聚会上表现以感到最安全或舒服？

Audience: Maybe they'll have a “Let's wait and see” attitude.
听众：也许他们会有一种「让我们等等看」的态度。

Howard: Yes, that's an interesting way of putting it. Many people with the Moon in Scorpio will want to keep a close watch on what is going on around them, and that makes them feel less wary and more at home. So they might, at least at first, be on guard, not revealing too much. They are sharp-eyed like eagles. So their statement might be, “Let's understand the hidden workings going on in this environment; let's check out the undercurrents and subtle interactions between people.” They are not inclined to be satisfied just knowing what is happening on the surface, but they have a need to see the little games going on, who is chasing after whose date, and who is giving off what vibes and why. Then they start feeling more comfortable, more at home. And if the party is boring, they may resort to devising ways of stirring things up: “Who can I shock or upset in order to make all this more interesting?” I hate to say it, but people with the Moon in Scorpio often have something of the drama queen in them. If life or the environment is getting too dull or boring, there is nothing like a little crisis to liven things up.
Howard：对，这是一种有趣的说法。许多月亮在天蝎座的人会想要密切观察周围发生的事情，这让他们感到不那么警惕、更自在。所以他们可能，至少在起初，保持警惕，不透露太多。他们像鹰一样眼尖。所以他们的声明可能是：「让我们理解这个环境中正在发生的隐藏运作；让我们查看人与人之间的暗流和微妙互动。」他们不满足于仅仅知道表面上发生了什么，他们需要看到正在进行的小游戏，谁在追谁的约会对象，谁发出了什么样的气场以及为什么。然后他们开始感到更舒服、更自在。如果聚会无聊，他们可能诉诸想办法搅动局面：「我能震惊或冒犯谁来让这一切更有趣？」我不愿意说，但月亮在天蝎座的人通常有某种戏剧女王的味道。如果生活或环境变得太乏味或无聊，没有什么比一个小危机更能让事情活跃起来了。

What about the Moon in Sagittarius, what do you think their statement might be?
月亮在射手座呢，你觉得他们的声明可能是什么？

Audience: “Let's make the environment more lively.”
听众：「让我们让环境更活跃。」

Howard: Yes, “let's make things more interesting, let's stimulate or arouse the environment, let's be expansive or more adventurous.” It might even be “Let's move the party to somewhere bigger!” Unless the Sagittarian Moon is in serious trouble with Saturn or the outer planets, people with this placement are usually fairly gregarious. They feel good if they're learning from others, they feel at home if they're teaching or sharing their ideas and their enthusiasms, if they're meeting new and interesting people. But if they are insecure or uptight for some reason, then you may see an arrogant or slightly haughty side coming out: “These are not my people, this is not my scene, I'm above this, goodbye.”
Howard：对，「让事情更有趣，让我们刺激或唤起环境，让我们扩张或更冒险。」甚至可能是「让我们把聚会移到一个更大的地方！」除非射手座月亮与土星或外行星有严重困难，否则有这个配置的人通常相当合群。如果他们在向别人学习，他们感觉良好；如果他们在教导或分享他们的想法和热情，在遇到新和有趣的人时，他们感到自在。但如果他们出于某种原因感到不安全或紧张，那么你可能看到一个傲慢或有点高傲的一面出来：「这些人不是我的同类，这不是我的场景，我高于这些，再见。」

就月亮在摩羯座如何在社交聚会或社交场合中让自己舒服而言，你怎么看？这又是一个复杂的，但你首先想到的是什么？

听众：「让我们利用环境来在人生中出人头地。」

听众：也许他们希望重要人物在场，与高层人士交往会让他们感觉良好。

Howard: Yes, a fair number of people with the Moon in Capricorn have difficulty just relaxing, just letting go or playing. 月亮在水瓶座有几个不同面向。如果天王星在星盘中很强，他们的声明可能是：「让我们给环境充电，让我们在这里带来新能量和生命，或者让我们稍微搅动一下让事情更有趣或更活跃。」像月亮在双子座一样，这个配置通常对生活好奇，有兴趣观察别人如何运作和行事。有一种学习和发现东西的需求以便感到满足和自在，所以月亮在水瓶座的人可能会与各种各样的人交谈，了解他们来自哪里，他们信仰什么，他们如何经营自己的生活。某些月亮在这个星座的人在有机会表达自己的观点或与他人分享其政治或社会信念时最快乐。「既然你们都在这个聚会上，我想告诉你们关于动物权利的事。」

月亮在双鱼座在如何应对社交场合方面是一个有趣且多样的配置。一个明显的声明可能是：「让我们爱、关心和帮助环境。」当他们抓住某个需要安慰或同情的可怜人时，他们才觉得自己到了位。反过来也是。他们可能直到向另一个人倾诉了心事并找到一个理解他们、对他们有同情心的人才感到安全或自在，然后他们才能放松享受。他们通常喜欢融入或与环境融合。你看这与月亮在白羊座多么不同。月亮在白羊座不太在意融入或融合，但月亮在双鱼座如果这是可能的就感觉良好。所以你可能看到月亮在双鱼座以一种方式与一个群体或一种类型的人交往，而与另一种类型的人完全不同。或者他们花很多时间幻想和白日梦，想象这这那那正在进行。

Audience: I know a lot of people with the Moon in Pisces and their statement is “Let's drink!”
听众：我认识很多月亮在双鱼座的人，他们的声明是「让我们喝酒！」

Howard: Yes, I'll buy that. They feel good when they can let go, when their boundaries are loosened. There are certain similarities here with the Moon in Cancer: if they can't manage to feel comfortable where they are, they'll usually find some excuse to slip away, to do a disappearing act and escape the scene altogether.
Howard：对，我接受。当他们能放下、当他们的界限松动时感觉良好。这里与月亮在巨蟹座有某些相似之处：如果他们无法在所处的地方感到舒服，他们通常会找某个借口溜走，演一出消失戏，完全逃离场景。
