PART TWO
第二部分

THE SUN
太阳

THE HERO WITH A THOUSAND FACES
千面英雄

THE SUN AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF CONSCIOUSNESS
太阳与意识的发展

BY LIZ GREENE
LIZ GREENE 著

I would like to start this morning's session by talking about one of the oldest and most profound mythic representations of the Sun: the ancient symbol of kingship. Until the beginning of the present century, kingship was perceived as the earthly embodiment of the godhead, the mortal vessel through which the will of the divine made itself known in the world. Some of you may find this peculiar, especially since Switzerland is the oldest democracy in Europe and has never had a king. But there is an archaic layer in all of us which even today still responds to the magical symbol of kingship. In ancient times the king was also a priest, and the role of governing his people was combined with the role of the pontifex, the bridge-builder who mediated between heaven and earth. As we explore the mythology of the Sun this morning, it may help to keep the symbol of kingship in mind, because it binds together the various mythic solar figures.
我想以谈论太阳最古老、最深刻的神话象征之一来开始今天上午的讲座：古老的王权象征。直到本世纪初，王权被视为神格在尘世的体现，是神圣意志借此在世界中显现的凡人容器。你们中有些人可能觉得这很奇怪，特别是因为瑞士是欧洲最古老的民主国家且从未有过国王。但在我们所有人内在都有一个古老层面，即使今天仍会对王权这一魔法象征产生回应。在古代，国王也是祭司，治理子民的角色与祭司——即在天地之间调停的建桥者——的角色合而为一。在我们今天上午探索太阳的神话时，把王权的象征记在心里可能会有所帮助，因为它将各种神话中的太阳人物联系在一起。

Yesterday Howard and I talked about the Moon as an innate, instinctive dimension of the personality. Although we may need to work at expressing the Moon, our lunar nature does not consciously strive to develop goals in the world. Our self-nourishing capacity is intrinsic to us; we have only to listen to it. The Moon is also regressive in nature, always pulling us back toward the past and the mother-child bond, because our basic emotional and bodily needs do not change at core. But the Sun is progressive. It is an active, dynamic principle which unfolds during the course of a lifetime. We never really finish developing the Sun, for this aspect of the personality is always in a process of becoming, of moving toward some future vision or goal. Some of you may be familiar with what Joseph Campbell calls the “monomyth,” the story of the hero which recurs in every culture's mythology. The hero myth is a solar myth, for the hero is always on the way to becoming something. He is not automatically born a hero. He must earn his right to become hero and king and a fitting vessel for the god who parents him.
昨天 Howard 和我谈到了月亮作为人格中先天的、本能的维度。虽然我们可能需要努力表达月亮，但我们的月亮本性并不会有意识地在世界中追求发展目标。我们自给自足的能力是内在于我们的；我们只需倾听它。月亮在本质上也是回归性的，总是拉我们回到过去和母子纽带，因为我们的基本情感和身体需求在核心上不会改变。但太阳是前进性的。它是一个主动的、动态的原则，在一生中展开。我们永远不会真正完成太阳的发展，因为人格的这一面始终处于一个成为的过程、一个朝向某个未来愿景或目标移动的过程。你们中一些人可能熟悉 Joseph Campbell 所说的「单一神话」，即在每个文化的神话中反复出现的英雄故事。英雄神话是一个太阳神话，因为英雄始终在成为某种东西的路上。他不是天生就是英雄。他必须赢得成为英雄和国王的权利，成为孕育他的神的合适容器。

I should emphasise at this point that the hero, who is always masculine, is not the exclusive property of men, any more than the lunar mother is the property solely of women. We all possess a lunar and a solar dimension to our natures. The unfolding of the hero myth through the development of the Sun is just as relevant to women as the self-nourishing wisdom of the Moon is to men. The adjectives “masculine” and “feminine,” when used to describe a symbolic image, do not refer to one sex or the other. They refer to a quality of energy, receptive or dynamic, for which male or female deities in myth are the most appropriate images. In a similar fashion, as I hope you will see later in the week, the mythic conjunction or marriage between Sun and Moon describes a potential of inner relationship between these different aspects of the personality in either sex.
我应该在这里强调，始终是男性的英雄并非男性专属，正如月亮母亲并非女性专属。我们都拥有月亮和太阳两个维度。英雄神话通过太阳的发展而展开，对女性同样适用，正如月亮的自我滋养智慧对男性同样适用。「男性」和「女性」这些形容词用来描述象征意象时，并不指向某一性别。它们指向一种能量品质——接受的或动态的——在神话中男神或女神是最恰当的意象。类似地，正如我希望你们在本周稍后会看到的，太阳与月亮的神话联结或婚姻描述了这两种不同人格面向在任一性别中内在关系的潜力。

Now perhaps you can have a look at our diagram for the Sun (see figure 3 on page 83). Much of the material which I will be using to describe the myth of the solar hero comes from Joseph Campbell, whose book, The Hero with a Thousand Faces, is one of the best psychological explorations of myth.1 Before I link it up with astrological symbolism I would like to outline the basic stages of the hero's journey. First of all, the hero has a strange or portentous birth; he is usually fathered by a god on a mortal mother. In some cases, such as the Greek hero Achilles, this is reversed; his father was the mortal Peleus but his mother was the sea goddess Thetis. There is also the Roman hero Aeneas, fathered by the mortal Anchises on the goddess Venus. But whichever parent is the god, one of the characteristics of the hero is that he is a hybrid between human and divine, and is thus destined to be a pontifex.
现在也许你们可以看看我们的太阳图解（见第83页图3）。我用来描述太阳英雄神话的大部分材料来自 Joseph Campbell，他的著作《千面英雄》是对神话最好的心理学探索之一。¹ 在我将其与占星象征联系起来之前，我想概述英雄之旅的基本阶段。首先，英雄有一个奇特或预兆性的出生；他通常由一位神在一位凡人母亲身上所生。在某些情况下，如希腊英雄阿喀琉斯，这被反转了；他的父亲是凡人 Peleus 但母亲是海女神 Thetis。还有罗马英雄 Aeneas，由凡人 Anchises 与女神 Venus 所生。但无论哪位父母是神，英雄的特征之一是他是人与神的混血，因此注定要成为一座桥梁。

As a child the hero has no idea of his true parentage. He thinks he is just like everybody else, but he has a nagging feeling of being different and an intuition of a special destiny. One of the main themes of the hero's quest is the discovery of his true origin, which is both mortal and immortal. In this mythic image of hybrid birth we can perceive a deep sense of duality, a conviction that we are not merely made of earth and doomed to eat, reproduce and die. Each of us is special, unique, and has a personal destiny, an individual contribution to make to life. The Moon is our body life, parented by mortals and fated by our genetic inheritance. It is the Sun in us which senses that there is a quest to be pursued, a journey toward an unknown future, a profound mystery at the core of “me.”
作为孩子，英雄不知道自己真正的身世。他以为自己和其他人一样，但他有一种挥之不去的与众不同的感觉和对特殊命运的直觉。英雄探索的主题之一就是发现他真正的起源，既是凡人的也是不朽的。在这种混血出生的神话意象中，我们可以感知到一种深深的二元感，一种我们不仅仅由泥土构成、不仅仅注定吃饭、繁衍和死亡的信念。我们每个人都是特别的、独特的，都有一个个人命运，一个对生命的独特贡献。月亮是我们的身体生命，由凡人所生，受基因遗传命运的制约。正是我们内在的太阳感知到有一个探索要追求，一段朝向未知未来的旅程，一个「我」核心深处的深邃奥秘。

Figure 3. The mythology of the Sun.
图3. 太阳的神话。

Many children have a fantasy that they have been adopted. Those two ordinary people bumbling about the house could not possibly be our real parents. We were actually fathered or mothered by someone special and wonderful, a prince or a princess or a head of state, but this has been kept secret. This fantasy is so common amongst children that we can assume it is archetypal. It is one of the places where myth finds its way into ordinary human life, before “reality” stomps all over the imaginal world of childhood. The same motif also occurs regularly in fairy tales, where a stepmother or stepfather has replaced a missing parent. Although this missing parent may not be divine, he or she is shrouded in mystery. The stepparent is usually obnoxious and a comedown, and the child has a special destiny which involves escape from the oppressive environment and the discovery of his or her true birth.
许多孩子有一种被收养的幻想。那两个在屋子里笨拙走动的普通人不可能是我们的亲生父母。我们实际上是由某个特别而精彩的人——一位王子或公主或国家元首——所生或所育的，但这被保密了。这种幻想在孩子们中如此普遍，我们可以认为它是原型的。这是神话在「现实」践踏童年想象世界之前找到进入普通人生活的路径之一。同样的主题也经常出现在童话中，继母或继父替代了缺失的亲生父母。虽然这个缺失的父母可能不是神，但他或她被笼罩在神秘中。继父母通常令人讨厌且是一个降格，孩子有一个特殊命运，涉及逃离压迫性环境和发现自己的真正出生。

Our awareness of the Sun may first express itself in this early fantasy of a mysterious unknown parent, or of a “high” destiny awaiting us. The solar part of us does not feel subject to the same lunar cycles and laws of fate that our emotions and bodies are. It stubbornly refuses to be ordinary. Many people discover it in the middle of life, and I have often heard clients in their forties say, “I have this feeling there is some deeper purpose for my being alive. I am no longer satisfied by the old goals of money and emotional security and worldly achievement.” This awakening of the solar principle may coincide with the beginning of a period of inner exploration, and this in turn may be precipitated by a crisis of some kind which leaves depression and discontent in its wake. How many of you have experienced this feeling? Then you all know what I am talking about.
我们对太阳的觉察可能首先在这种对神秘的未知父母或等待我们的「崇高」命运的早期幻想中表达出来。我们内在的太阳部分不觉得自己受制于与我们的情绪和身体相同的月亮周期和命运法则。它固执地拒绝平凡。许多人在人生中期发现了它，我经常听到四十多岁的客户说：「我有一种感觉，我活着有某种更深的目的。我不再满足于金钱、情感安全和世俗成就这些旧目标。」这种太阳原则的觉醒可能恰逢一段内在探索的开始，而这反过来可能由某种危机引发，在它之后留下抑郁和不满。你们中有多少人经历过这种感觉？那么你们都知道我在说什么。

Audience. At first it's very difficult to articulate it in terms of concrete goals.
听众：一开始很难用具体目标来表达它。

Liz: Yes, it is, because the Sun is not really concerned with the concrete world as its final destination. Material reality is the domain of the Moon, and often what we think of as goals in the first half of life are really the lunar security needs translating themselves into mundane terms. Solar goals are inner, and are concerned with self-realisation and experiencing one's life as special and meaningful. These goals are very difficult to define, and they differ from one person to another in the kind of outer expression they need. Socrates called this mysterious inner driving force his daemon, the destiny that impels an individual toward becoming his or her own ideal. The Sun says, “But I am not just any old mouse or rabbit or cabbage. My life means something, I have potentials that I have not yet fulfilled.” You can see why we ignore this solar drive at our peril, for if we do not take the heroic leap and make a unique creative contribution in some way, however small, we are doomed to the nagging torment of an unlived self. Then we have every reason to fear death, for we have not truly lived.
Liz：是的，确实如此，因为太阳并不真正关注具体世界作为它的最终目的地。物质现实是月亮的领域，而我们在人生前半段所认为的目标往往是月亮的安全需求转化为世俗术语。太阳的目标是内在的，关乎自我实现和体验自己的生命为特别和有意义的。这些目标很难定义，而且它们所需的外在表达方式因人而异。苏格拉底称这种神秘的内在驱动力为他的「精灵」，即驱使个体走向成为他或她自己理想的天命。太阳说：「但我不是随便什么老鼠或兔子或卷心菜。我的生命有意义，我有尚未实现的潜能。」你可以看到为什么我们忽视这种太阳驱动是危险的，因为如果我们不迈出英雄的步伐、不以某种方式做出独特的创造性贡献，无论多么微小，我们就注定要遭受未活出自我的折磨。那样我们就有充分理由恐惧死亡，因为我们从未真正活过。

Another important element in the solar hero's childhood is that he is usually envied or persecuted without knowing why. Sometimes the enemy is his mother's husband, who is really his stepfather. Sometimes it is a usurping or wicked king who has had an omen or augury and fears that the hero, having reached manhood, will overthrow him. We can see this theme in the stories of Greek heroes such as Perseus as well as in the story of Jesus, who as an infant was persecuted by King Herod. The theme of envy, and the potential threat the hero holds for the ruling powers, is one which I will refer to many times as we explore the solar journey. The Sun is special, and the expression of specialness often invokes destructive envy in others. If the Sun remains unconscious, it may equally invoke destructive envy of others in oneself. Whenever we explore a myth, we can be sure we will find it everywhere in ordinary human life.
太阳英雄童年中的另一个重要元素是他通常在不知情的情况下被嫉妒或迫害。有时敌人是他母亲的丈夫，实际上是他的继父。有时是一个篡位或邪恶的国王，他得到了一个预兆或征兆，担心英雄成年后会推翻他。我们可以在希腊英雄如 Perseus 的故事以及耶稣的故事中看到这个主题，耶稣在婴儿时期就受到 King Herod 的迫害。嫉妒以及英雄对当权者构成的潜在威胁，是我们探索太阳之旅时会多次提到的主题。太阳是特别的，而特别性的表达常常在他人身上引发破坏性的嫉妒。如果太阳保持无意识，它同样可能在自身内在引发对他人的破坏性嫉妒。每当我们探索一个神话，我们可以确定会在普通人生活中到处找到它。

This archetypal problem of envy and persecution of nascent solar potentials, which may be seen enacted in a great many families, is one of the reasons why many people find it hard to express the Sun. They fear that, if they are truly themselves, then others will react with anger and attack them, verbally or emotionally. Often one's actual mother or father unconsciously did exactly that, because the parent's unlived solar life has turned sour and envious; and one has a direct experience of the mythic hero's persecuted childhood enacted in one's own formative years. The young hero-to-be may have his mortal mother's protection for a time, but sooner or later he must learn to cope on his own with the envious stepparent or ruler. He has to develop realism, since envy is a fact of life and an indelible part of human nature. He cannot always run home bleating when his specialness is attacked or called into question. And he must acquire toughness, self-sufficiency, insight, intelligence, and loyal friends in order to survive as an individual. Otherwise he might as well quench his solar light and crawl back into the womb again. This is in fact what many people do, for they find mother surrogates such as unfulfilling jobs or stifling relationships to protect them, and suppress their own individual potentials to avoid the competitive world outside.
这种嫉妒和迫害初生太阳潜能的原型问题，在许多家庭中都可以看到上演，是许多人发现难以表达太阳的原因之一。他们害怕如果真正做自己，别人会以愤怒回应并攻击他们，无论是言语上还是情感上。往往一个人实际的母亲或父亲无意识地正是这样做的，因为父母未活出的太阳生命已经变酸变嫉妒；于是一个人就直接体验了神话英雄被迫害的童年在自己的成长岁月中上演。年轻的准英雄可能暂时得到凡人母亲的保护，但迟早他必须学会自己应对嫉妒的继父母或统治者。他必须发展现实主义，因为嫉妒是生活事实和人性中不可磨灭的一部分。他不能总是在自己的特别性受到攻击或质疑时就跑回家哭诉。他必须获得韧性、自立、洞察力、智慧和忠诚的朋友才能作为个体生存。否则他倒不如熄灭自己的太阳光重新爬回子宫。这实际上是许多人所做的，因为他们找到母亲替代品——如不充实的工作或令人窒息的关系——来保护他们，并压抑自己的个人潜能以避开外面竞争的世界。

At some point in his growing-up process, the hero receives what Campbell refers to as “the call to adventure.” This can come in a number of forms. The divine parent may appear in a dream or vision, saying, “All right, son, pull your finger out, it's time to grow up and go after the treasure hard to attain.” In other words, the call may come from within us—a sudden intuition of meaning and destiny—which frequently occurs under major heavy planet cycles such as the Saturn return at 30, or in midlife coincident with the Uranus half-cycle or the second Saturn half-cycle. The hero's call in myth may also come through apparent external upheaval or disaster-the crops are failing, or a plague or invasion has struck, or the old king is dying and there is no known heir. Those of you who are familiar with the Arthurian legends will recognise that this last situation, when the Saxons are invading and King Uther Pen-dragon is dying, is the backdrop for the moment young Arthur is revealed as the rightful heir by drawing the magic sword Excalibur out of the stone. The mythic call to adventure can thus express itself in our lives as a major crisis which, unlike our usual everyday troubles, challenges us to plunge into the unknown and discover new resources that we did not know were there. I believe this is how the majority of people experience the solar call to adventure which, as well as being signalled by heavy planet cycles, is often reflected by a major transit or progression involving the Sun.
在成长过程的某个时刻，英雄会收到 Campbell 所说的「冒险的召唤」。这可以有多种形式。神圣父母可能出现在梦或幻象中说：「好了，儿子，振作起来，是时候长大了去追求难以获得的宝藏。」换言之，召唤可能来自我们内在——一种对意义和天命的突然直觉——这通常发生在大行星周期如30岁的回归或中年时期与天王星半周期或第二次土星半周期同时发生时。神话中英雄的召唤也可能通过表面的外部剧变或灾难而来——庄稼歉收、瘟疫或入侵、老国王垂死且没有已知继承人。熟悉亚瑟王传说的你们会认出最后这种情况——当 Saxons 入侵且 King Uther Pendragon 垂死时——正是年轻 Arthur 从石头中拔出魔法剑 Excalibur 而被揭示为合法继承人的背景。神话中的冒险召唤因此可以以重大危机的形式出现在我们生活中，这危机与我们日常的烦恼不同，它挑战我们投入未知并发现我们不知道存在的新资源。我相信大多数人就是这样体验太阳的冒险召唤的，它不仅由大行星周期标示，也经常反映为涉及太阳的重大过运或推运。

Not many of us get struck like Saul on the road to Damascus, where the god appears in a vision and announces one's unique destiny to save the world. When it does happen so floridly, especially in youth, there are often some questionable elements involved, such as deep-rooted feelings of inferiority which generate a compensatory messianic identification. There is a difference between the real adult emergence of the Sun in a relatively solid personality, and the global messianic fantasy which reflects a poorly developed ego structure. The Sun's uniqueness is not incompatible with realism and humility, and its sense of specialness does not need to look down on lesser mortals, unless it has become badly mixed up with unhealed childhood wounds.
我们中不多人像 Saul 在大马士革路上那样被击中——神在幻象中显现并宣布一个人拯救世界的独特天命。当它确实如此华丽地发生时，特别是在年轻时，往往涉及一些可疑因素，如根深蒂固的自卑感产生补偿性的救世主认同。在一个相对坚实的人格中太阳的真正成年浮现，与反映薄弱自我结构的全球性救世主幻想是不同的。太阳的独特性与现实主义和谦逊并不矛盾，它的特殊感不需要看不起凡夫俗子，除非它与未治愈的童年创伤严重混淆。

The timing of the hero's call to adventure has a strange preset quality in myths and folklore, rather like an alarm clock going off at a programmed time. It is inevitable, like the rising of the Sun. As Hamlet says:
英雄冒险召唤的时机在神话和民间传说中有一种奇怪的预设品质，就像闹钟在设定时间响起。它是不可避免的，就像太阳升起。正如 Hamlet 所说：

If it be now, 'tis not to come; if it be not to come, it will be now; if it be not now, yet it will come: the readiness is all.
若是现在，就不会将来；若非将来，就会是现在；若非现在，终将到来：准备就是一切。

The time is often specified at the hero's birth, right at the beginning of the story. This suggests the built-in timing of the astrological chart. Theseus, for example, discovers that his real father is the King of Athens when he lifts up the great stone under which the king's sword has been hidden. He is instructed by his mother to do this only when he has reached his seventeenth birthday, for that was his father's wish. There is a sense of unavoidable destiny about this timing, which is reflected in the feeling I have heard many people express, that the crisis which has awakened them was “meant” and happened “at the right time.” In myth the divine or royal parent may provide a test which must be passed before the hero's real identity and quest can be revealed to him. Thus he demonstrates that he is now fit to become himself.
时间往往在英雄出生时就被指定了，就在故事的一开始。这暗示了占星星盘中内置的时间感。例如，Theseus 发现他真正的父亲是雅典国王，是在他举起国王藏剑的大石时。他的母亲指示他只有在满十七岁时才能这样做，因为那是他父亲的意愿。这种时机有一种不可逃避的命运感，这反映在我听到许多人表达的感受中——唤醒他们的危机是「命中注定的」且发生在「正确的时间」。在神话中，神圣或皇室父母可能提供一个考验，必须在英雄的真正身份和探索被揭示之前通过。这样他证明了自己现在适合成为自己。

The timing of the call becomes very interesting to the astrological student when we consider transits and progressions involving the Sun. We all get many transits of heavy planets to the natal and progressed Sun, and many progressed planetary aspects to the natal Sun as well as progressed solar aspects to natal planets, during the course of a lifetime. Unlike the hero, we are given more than one chance to respond to the call, and it may come in separate segments, disguised as disparate life situations linked by a single meaningful thread. The hero's journey does not occur for us once and for all. It seems to operate on many levels, and repeats itself throughout life. Perhaps during this morning's session you might think about the ways in which the heroic call to adventure has arrived in your own life, and whether you recognised it at the time. But try to remember that the call may look like something entirely different, although the results are usually apparent later. Sometimes it occurs through an important encounter. Relationships can provide us with our awakening, especially if they begin or end under significant chart movements involving the Sun. The intervention of another person into our lives, whether this is a lover, a child, a teacher, or even an enemy or rival, can transform our consciousness and send the solar hero on his quest.
当我们考虑涉及太阳的过运和推运时，召唤的时机对占星学生来说变得非常有趣。我们一生中都会经历许多大行星对本命和推运太阳的过运，以及许多推运行星对本命太阳的相位和推运太阳对本命行星的相位。与英雄不同，我们有不止一次机会回应召唤，它可能分段到来，伪装成由一条有意义线索连接的分散生活情境。英雄之旅对我们来说并非一劳永逸地发生。它似乎在许多层面运作，并在一生中反复。也许在今天上午的讲座中，你们可以思考英雄的冒险召唤是如何在你自己的生活中到达的，以及你当时是否认出了它。但请记住召唤可能看起来完全像别的东西，尽管结果通常在后来才显现。有时它通过一次重要的相遇发生。关系可以为我们提供觉醒，特别是如果它们在涉及太阳的重大星图运动下开始或结束。另一个人介入我们的生活——无论是恋人、孩子、老师，甚至敌人或竞争对手——可以转化我们的意识，送太阳英雄上路。

Once the hero has been called, he usually acquires a helper, or receives assistance from divine or human or animal sources. Interestingly, he generally does not have to work for this initial assistance. It is provided by the divine parent, or by the mortal parent, or by other benign deities who are on his side for their own reasons. For example, when Theseus sets out to slay the Minotaur, Ariadne, who is in love with him, gives him the ball of thread which will enable him to find his way out of the Labyrinth. Jason, when he flees Colchis with the Golden Fleece, is aided by the priestess Medea, who deflects her father's pursuing ships by chopping up her brother and sprinkling the bloody pieces on the water. Perseus, when he goes forth to destroy the Medusa, is given a shield by Athena in which to see the monster's reflection. This help, sometimes morally questionable (as with Jason) but always exactly the right sort to ensure success, reflects the hero's divine right—he will be tested, but he is given every possible leeway, other than shirking, to help him achieve his goal.
英雄一旦被召唤，通常会获得一个帮助者，或从神圣、人类或动物来源获得援助。有趣的是，他通常不需要为这最初的援助而努力。它由神圣父母、或凡人父母、或出于各自原因站在他一边的其他善神提供。例如，当 Theseus 出发去消灭牛头怪时，爱上他的 Ariadne 给了他一团线球，让他能找到走出迷宫的路。Jason 带着金羊毛逃离 Colchis 时，得到了女祭司 Medea 的帮助，她通过砍碎弟弟并将血肉碎片撒在水中来转移父亲追来的船只。Perseus 出发去消灭 Medusa 时，Athena 给了他一面盾牌，可以在其中看到怪物的倒影。这种帮助，有时道德上有疑问（如 Jason），但总是恰好是确保成功的那种，反映了英雄的神圣权利——他将被考验，但他得到了一切可能的回旋余地，除了逃避，来帮助他实现目标。

The issue of shirking, or even of blowing it the first time around (as Parsifal did), may also be part of the hero's story. I am reminded of a very amusing television sketch 1 saw long ago, in which Bill Cosby played the part of Noah. God keeps calling him to warn him about the Flood, but Noah, far from being the righteous and humble figure of the Old Testament, keeps turning his back, making various excuses and offering the religious equivalent of “Not tonight, dear, I have a headache.” God eventually becomes so irritated and threatening that Noah gives in, but most gracelessly. It is extremely unheroic behaviour, but it faithfully reflects the way most of us feel when we are called upon by life to find heroic resources. In myth, the hero never whinges.2 In real life, it seems we all need to whinge a little in the face of the call. This is probably the voice of the Moon, which feels very aggrieved and sorry for itself because we are dragged away from our comforts by the demands of our own souls. It is a bit like the old Jewish joke—Thank you, Lord, for making me one of the Chosen, but couldn't you choose somebody else for a change?
逃避的问题，甚至第一次搞砸（如 Parsifal），也可能是英雄故事的一部分。我想起很久以前看过的一个非常有趣的电视小品，Bill Cosby 扮演 Noah。神不断呼唤他警告洪水的事，但 Noah 远非旧约中那个正义谦卑的人物，不断转身拒绝，找各种借口，提出宗教版的「今晚不行，亲爱的，我头痛。」神最终变得如此恼怒和威胁，Noah 才屈从，但极其不情愿。这是极不英雄的行为，但它忠实地反映了我们大多数人在被生活召唤去寻找英雄资源时的感受。在神话中，英雄从不抱怨。² 在现实生活中，似乎我们都需要在面对召唤时抱怨一番。这可能是月亮的声音，它感到非常委屈和自怜，因为我们被自身灵魂的要求从舒适中拖走。这有点像那个老犹太笑话——主啊，感谢你让我成为被选中的人之一，但你能不能换个选择别人？

It is of course possible to refuse the call absolutely, in which case it generally comes back again in a different form, with harder tests. The divine parent—who is a mythic image of something within ourselves—will not leave us alone simply because we don't feel up to it. I have met many people who have tried to escape the destiny which the Sun reflects during a time of important chart movements, and they have paid dearly on one level or another for their refusal to become themselves. Often the result is deep depression and a sense of failure and emptiness. Or the test may pass on to the next generation, and one's children and grandchildren may suffer by being the recipient of unfinished solar parental business, grown larger and more demanding with each generation's avoidance. More drastic forms of refusal may also be part of the constellation of breakdowns and serious physical illnesses. It is possible to refuse the call so violently that one retreats completely and self-destructively into the lunar world, which is perhaps connected with chronic “lunacy.” The world is full of lost people who have refused their solar call to adventure, not once but many times. Many of them seem “normal” in collective terms, except that there is nobody home, and I am reminded of T. S. Eliot's poem:
当然，绝对拒绝召唤是可能的，这种情况下它通常以不同形式回来，考验更难。神圣父母——是我们内在某种东西的神话意象——不会因为我们觉得自己不够格就放过我们。我遇到过许多试图在重要星图运动期间逃避太阳所反映的天命的人，他们因为拒绝成为自己而在某个层面或另一个层面付出了沉重代价。结果往往是深深的抑郁以及失败和空虚感。或者考验可能传到下一代，一个人的孩子和孙子可能因成为未完成的太阳父母事务的接收者而受苦，每代人的回避都让它变得更大、更多。更激烈的拒绝形式也可能是崩溃和严重身体疾病星群的一部分。有可能如此激烈地拒绝召唤，以至于完全且自我毁灭地退回到月亮世界，这也许与慢性「疯癫」有关。世界充满了拒绝了自己太阳冒险召唤的人——不是一次，而是很多次。他们在集体意义上似乎「正常」，只是内心无人居住，我想起 T.S. Eliot 的诗：

We are the hollow men
我们是空心人

We are the stuffed men
我们是填充的人

Leaning together
靠在一起

Headpiece filled with straw …
脑袋里塞满稻草……

Those who have crossed
那些已经渡过的人

With direct eyes, to death's other Kingdom
直視死亡之另一王國

Remember us—if at all—not as lost
