Now I would like to go back to the issue of the hero's assistance from outside sources, and consider it in astrological terms. This help comes from within us, although sometimes it is embodied by another person who miraculously provides support or a key of some kind at precisely the right moment. In myth it is often the mortal mother, or lunar goddesses such as Hera or Artemis, who offer the boon; and this might reflect the instinctual wisdom of the Moon, which can be depended upon in times of crisis because it shows us how to look after ourselves. Sometimes it is benign natal aspects which constitute our internal help—innate gifts or abilities which can be relied upon in a pinch. Where we have harmonious aspects, we often have what is called luck, because we are in harmony within ourselves and therefore intuitively approach life in the right way. For example, a Venus-Jupiter conjunction in the natal chart, ready at hand when the Sun is being triggered by a difficult transit or progression, might respond to this challenge with an innately optimistic and hopeful outlook which communicates itself to others, or a spontaneous generosity which makes people want to be generous in return. Mercury trine Saturn might respond with great shrewdness, realism, and a canny knowledge of the rules of the marketplace, so the person avoids the blunders which entrap more gullible souls. We all have “helpers” in our charts—planets in harmonious aspect, planets dignified or exalted by sign or house—which can form the psychic components of the hero's support team.
現在我想回到英雄從外界獲得幫助的問題，並從占星角度考慮它。這種幫助來自我們內在，雖然有時它由另一個人體現，在恰好正確的時刻奇蹟般地提供支持或某種關鍵。在神話中往往是凡人母親，或 Hera、Artemis 等月亮女神提供助力；這可能反映了月亮的本能智慧，在危機時刻可以依賴，因為它告訴我們如何照顧自己。有時是良性的本命相位構成了我們的內在幫助——先天的天賦或能力，在緊要關頭可以依賴。在我們有和諧相位的地方，我們往往擁有所謂的運氣，因為我們內在和諧，因此直覺地以正確方式接近生活。例如，本命盤中金星合木星，在太陽被困難過運或推運觸發時唾手可得，可能以天生的樂觀和充滿希望的態度回應這一挑戰，這種態度會傳達給他人，或以自發的慷慨使人們願意回報。水星三分土星可能以極大的精明、現實主義和對市場規則的精明知識來回應，因此此人避免了困擾更輕信者的錯誤。我們的星盤中都有「幫助者」——和諧相位的行星、得位或廟旺的行星——它們可以構成英雄支持團隊的心靈組成部分。

Help generally follows on the heels of the hero's acceptance of his call. It is as though something powerfully supportive within us is activated when we face and accept our own individual path in life. It is also quite revealing that other gods become involved who are not directly related to the hero. They have their own reasons for wanting him to succeed. For example, when Perseus goes after the Medusa, a whole crowd of deities joins in the fun. Perseus is the son of Zeus, but Athene offers a shield, Hades contributes a helmet which confers invisibility, and Hermes produces a pair of winged sandals out of his magician's hat. All these gods have an investment in the Medusa being destroyed, and I think this suggests, in mythic language, that the hero is really redeeming a problem which is bigger than his own personal quest.
幫助通常緊隨英雄接受召喚之後而來。似乎當我們面對並接受自己生活中的個體道路時，我們內在某種強大的支持力量就被激活了。同樣很說明問題的是，其他與英雄沒有直接關係的神也參與進來。他們有自己希望他成功的理由。例如，當 Perseus 去追殺 Medusa 時，一大群神祇加入了這場盛事。Perseus 是 Zeus 的兒子，但 Athena 提供了一面盾牌，Hades 貢獻了一頂能隱身的頭盔，Hermes 從他的魔術帽中變出一雙飛天涼鞋。所有這些神在 Medusa 被消滅一事中都有利益，我認為這以神話語言暗示，英雄實際上是在救贖一個比他個人探索更大的問題。

The solar hero is thus doing something for the collective, although he believes he is only doing it for himself. The Medusa in the Perseus myth symbolises more than a personal dilemma. She is a problem within the collective psyche, a universal human inheritance of resentment and poison which generates paralysing depression within families and social groups and even nations. The gods, it seems, cannot deal properly with their own business, and they need a hero to do the deed for them. Thus the collective unconscious depends upon each individual's authenticity to fulfil its greater design. We can glimpse the links between the solar hero, the priest who mediates the wisdom and intent of the gods, the artist who serves as society's prophetic voice, and the king who embodies the divine will through worldly authority. All these are mythic images for the deeper function of the Sun which, becoming the conduit for an individual's authentic self-expression, inevitably contributes something to the larger psyche from which the individual has come. But the hero must perform his task because he is driven to it from within. If he does it merely to please others, however humanitarian he might wish to sound, he will wind up in awful trouble, because he is not being true to himself. He must pursue his quest because he is pressed to do it by his own inner necessity, not because it will make other people love him. Yet in the act of becoming an individual, he contributes something to others by that act. You can see that the Sun is deeply paradoxical. By becoming ourselves, we have far more to offer than if we are rushing about trying to save the world in order to compensate for an empty place within.
因此太陽英雄正在為集體做某件事，儘管他以為自己只是為自己做。Perseus 神話中的 Medusa 象徵的不僅是個人困境。她是集體心靈中的一個問題，一種普遍的人類遺產——怨恨和毒液，在家庭、社會群體甚至國家內部產生癱瘓性的抑鬱。神祇似乎無法妥善處理自己的事務，他們需要一個英雄來替他們完成。因此集體無意識依賴每個個體的真實性來實現其更大的設計。我們可以窺見太陽英雄、調停神的智慧和意圖的祭司、作為社會預言之聲的藝術家、以及通過世俗權威體現神聖意志的國王之間的聯繫。所有這些都是太陽更深層功能的神話意象，成為個體真實自我表達的管道，不可避免地為個體所來自的更大心靈做出貢獻。但英雄必須完成他的任務，因為他被內在驅使去做。如果他只是為了取悅他人而做，無論他多麼希望聽起來人道，他最終都會陷入糟糕的麻煩，因為他沒有忠於自己。他必須追求他的探索，因為他被自己的內在必然性所驅使，而不是因為這會讓別人愛他。然而在成為個體的行為中，他通過這個行為為他人做出了貢獻。你可以看到太陽是深深矛盾的。通過成為自己，我們比忙著拯救世界以彌補內在空虛要有更多可貢獻的東西。

The hero eventually reaches what Campbell calls the Threshold Crossing. There is usually something rather nasty awaiting him here which attempts to block the goal of the quest. The dilemma of the Threshold Crossing reflects a basic life conflict within us. This may be described by many factors in the birth chart. Even the Sun sign portrays an innate conflict, since there are always weaknesses as well as strengths in every zodiacal sign. Difficult aspects to the Sun may suggest the obstacles which lie inside, albeit projected outside, that seem to stop us from growing. Saturn can also describe, by sign and house and aspect, the nature of the Threshold Crossing, since it portrays our defensiveness and fear and reluctance to reveal ourselves. When we look at an example chart later, we shall see how other planets might be linked up with the various characters in the solar hero's story.
英雄最終到達 Campbell 所說的門檻跨越。通常這裡有某種相當可怕的東西在等著他，試圖阻擋探索的目標。門檻跨越的困境反映了我們內在的基本生活衝突。這可以由出生星盤中的許多因素描述。即使是太陽星座也描繪了一種先天的衝突，因為每個黃道星座都有弱點也有優點。太陽的困難相位可能暗示著內在的障礙——雖然被投射到外面——似乎阻止我們成長。土星也可以通過星座、宮位和相位描述門檻跨越的性質，因為它描繪了我們的防禦、恐懼和不情願展現自己。當我們稍後看一個範例星盤時，我們將看到其他行星如何與太陽英雄故事中的各種角色聯繫起來。

Myth describes some typical forms for the enemy at the Threshold Crossing. Often the opponent is a dark brother, an embodiment of the shadowy, destructive or amoral side of the hero himself. Sometimes the enemy is female, a wicked stepmother or witch, and here we meet the lunar goddess in a most unmotherly guise. This reflects a situation where the instinctual needs, rooted in the family and the past, fight against the development of the independent individual. Sometimes the threat comes from a monster or a giant; and these are also images of the instincts, huge and blind and primeval. A good example of this is the hero Siegfried, who must first kill the giant Fafner, who has taken the form of a dragon, before he can pass through the ring of fire to find Br¨nnhilde. This giant embodies all the inertia and apathy and regressive conservatism of the instincts, which resist any kind of change or transformation; and he exists to a greater or lesser degree in us all.
神話描述了門檻跨越處敵人的幾種典型形式。對手通常是黑暗兄弟，是英雄自己陰暗、破壞性或不道德一面的化身。有時敵人是女性，一個邪惡的繼母或女巫，我們在這裡遇到了月亮女神最不母性的一面。這反映了一種情境：根植於家庭和過去的本能需求與獨立個體的發展對抗。有時威脅來自怪物或巨人；這些也是本能的意象，巨大而盲目而原始。一個好例子是英雄 Siegfried，他必須先殺死已化為龍的巨人 Fafner，然後才能穿過火環找到 Brünnhilde。這個巨人體現了本能的所有慣性、冷漠和回歸性保守主義，它們抵抗任何形式的變化或轉化；他在我們所有人內部或多或少地存在著。

The dragon may also be seen as a lunar image. It is a coldblooded, archaic creature, a portrait of the uroboric primal mother in the shape of a huge winged snake. This is what mother often feels like to a young child, for she is still the all-powerful life-giver and death-dealer. The dragon-snake at the threshold can personify what the Moon feels like to a hero who has not yet grown up. The Moon is mythically portrayed not only by goddesses; it is also the Hindu cosmic serpent Ananda, the Great Round of the womb, self-fertilising and world-generating. Our early perceptions of mother span a vast spectrum of experience, ranging from the benign Greek Demeter to the child-eating Babylonian Tiamat.
龍也可以被視為月亮意象。它是冷血的、古老的生物，是銜尾蛇式的原始母親以巨大有翼蛇形態出現的肖像。這就是母親對幼兒來說常常感覺到的樣子，因為她仍然是全能的賜予生命者和奪取生命者。門檻處的龍蛇可以人格化尚未長大的英雄所感受到的月亮面貌。月亮不僅由女神在神話中描繪；它也是印度宇宙巨蛇 Ananda、子宮的大圓、自我受精和世界生成。我們對母親的早期感知跨越了廣泛的經驗譜系，從仁慈的希臘 Demeter 到吃嬰兒的巴比倫 Tiamat。

So the solar hero must confront the mother-snake, as Osiris the Egyptian Sun god did every night when he descended into the underworld. If you are a child reaching the first Saturn square Saturn at 7 years, or a pubescent 14-year-old coming under the first Saturn opposition Saturn, there is great conflict between the longing to return to the womb and the urge to separate and become an individual. The whole process of adolescence reflects this conflict, and often the breakdowns and illnesses which afflict university students reflect that terrific collision between lunar and solar needs. When we are struggling to free ourselves from the grip of our need for mother, we may experience her as the dragon. Thus the Threshold Crossing is also a reflection of puberty and adolescence with its typical family conflicts. We are formed enough as solar entities to know that the backward pull is a kind of death; yet we are too unformed to feel we can face such regressive needs without a violent fight.
因此太陽英雄必須對抗母親蛇，就像埃及太陽神 Osiris 每晚降入冥界時所做的那樣。如果你是一個達到7歲第一次土星四分的孩子，或是一個正經歷第一次土星對沖的14歲青春期少年，回到子宮的渴望與分離成為個體的衝動之間存在巨大衝突。整個青春期的過程反映了這種衝突，困擾大學生的崩潰和疾病往往反映了月亮需求與太陽需求之間的可怕碰撞。當我們努力擺脫對母親需求的控制時，我們可能將她體驗為龍。因此門檻跨越也是青春期和青少年期及其典型家庭衝突的反映。我們已經形成足夠的太陽實體，知道向後拉是一種死亡；但我們又太未成形，覺得無法不經過激烈戰鬥就面對這種回歸性需求。

Erich Neumann, in The Origins and History of Consciousness,4 calls this stage of development that of the “Struggler.” Although it is an archetypal stage of youth and an inevitable stage of the solar hero's journey, it may also be a place to which we are compelled to return later in life if the Sun has remained undeveloped. For the Struggler, everything feels like a battle, and the feminine—whether the actual mother, the bonds of the family, the emotions, women, mother surrogates in the workplace, or one's own mortal flesh—is not viewed with kindness. We might understand certain adolescent battlegrounds such as anorexia in this light, for the violent rejection of food is the violent repudiation of mother. She is a dragon, and must be defeated. There is not yet the possibility of genuine relationship, because one is still too close. There is deep ambivalence in this early stage of the Sun's emergence, and many people become stuck there at the threshold, battling the mother-dragon all their lives. I think we are all familiar with the feeling of being caught between the need to be loved and wanted and the need to stand loyally for our own values. The dragon fight has many emotional levels, and can occur whenever we are confronted with this inner conflict. From the solar point of view, the Moon at these moments is only life-destroying, and must be vanquished. And no doubt there are times when it is appropriate to feel this way and act accordingly—even though the conquered dragon reappears later, secretly disguised as the hero's bride.
Erich Neumann 在《意識的起源與歷史》⁴ 中將這一發展階段稱為「奮鬥者」階段。雖然它是青年時期的原型階段和太陽英雄之旅的必然階段，但如果太陽一直未發展，我們也可能在後來的生活中被迫回到這裡。對奮鬥者來說，一切都像戰鬥，而女性——無論是實際的母親、家庭紐帶、情緒、女人、工作場所的母親替代者，還是自己的凡人身體——都不會被善意看待。我們可以從這個角度理解某些青少年戰場如厭食症，因為對食物的暴力拒絕就是對母親的暴力否定。她是一條龍，必須被打敗。這時還沒有真正關係的可能，因為彼此仍然太近。在太陽浮現的這個早期階段有深深的矛盾，許多人一生都卡在門檻處，一輩子與母親龍戰鬥。我想我們都熟悉被夾在需要被愛和需要忠於自己價值之間的感受。龍之戰有許多情感層面，可以在我們面臨這種內在衝突時的任何時候發生。從太陽的角度看，月亮在這些時刻只是毀滅生命的，必須被征服。毫無疑問，有時候以這種方式感受並相應行動是合適的——即使被征服的龍後來重新出現，秘密偽裝成英雄的新娘。

One of the most ancient myths describing this dragon fight is the Babylonian myth of creation, imaged as a battle between the Sun god Marduk and his mother, Tiamat. Tiamat, the saltwater ocean, is a personification of the primal world-creating mother in the form of a sea monster. She is both the lifegiver and the maw of death which devours all that it creates. This myth is an ancient portrayal of our earliest experiences of the womb and the life-threatening process of birth and separation. At the beginning of time, before any manifest cosmos has come into being, Tiamat and her consort, Apsu, the sweetwater ocean, contain within them all the lesser gods who are their children. Tiamat becomes bored and angry with her noisy offspring, and plots to annihilate them. But the children discover the plan, and Marduk the Sun god, the strongest and boldest of them, slays his father Apsu and challenges Tiamat to mortal combat. He shoots his flaming arrows into her throat and destroys her, and out of her body creates the vault of heaven and the earth beneath. Thus the manifest world is made.
描述這場龍之戰的最古老神話之一是巴比倫創世神話，被想像為太陽神 Marduk 與他的母親 Tiamat 之間的戰鬥。Tiamat，鹹水海洋，是原始創世母親以海怪形式出現的人格化。她既是賜予生命者，也是吞噬一切所造之物的死亡之口。這個神話是我們對子宮和出生與分離的威脅生命過程的最早經驗的古老描繪。在時間之初，在任何顯化的宇宙出現之前，Tiamat 和她的配偶 Apsu，淡水海洋，在他們體內包含了所有較小的神——他們的孩子。Tiamat 對她吵鬧的後代感到厭煩和憤怒，密謀消滅他們。但孩子們發現了計劃，太陽神 Marduk，他們中最強壯最勇敢的，殺死了父親 Apsu 並向 Tiamat 發起殊死戰鬥。他將燃燒的箭射入她的喉嚨並消滅了她，從她的身體創造了上天的穹頂和下方的大地。於是顯化的世界就這樣形成了。

This ancient tale is a stark portrait of the process of the solar individual emerging from the darkness of the womb and the collective unconscious. As with dreams, we may read all the characters in myth as unfolding their story inside us. Tiamat and Marduk are still alive and well within the child and the adult still grappling with the problem of separation from the mother. Marduk, the solar principle, must battle against the regressive pull of his own lunar hunger, and while this struggle continues, the needs of the instinctual nature are experienced as bitter (saltwater), monstrous and life-threatening. His victory results in the making of the world, which might be another way of describing the formation of individual reality. Myths are images of feelings as well as patterns of development, and some of you may recognise the stage of development which the Marduk-Taimat story describes. It is our ongoing battle against inertia, apathy, stagnation and addiction, and on a small scale we experience it in everyday skirmishes like sticking to a diet, or pursuing an exercise programme, or following through a difficult course of study. We may also see it in the struggle to leave an unsatisfactory but compulsive relationship or marriage, or a safe but stultifying job, or a reliable but devouring family. Marduk is the voice of “I am,” and although this unity with the oceanic mother is destroyed, this is replaced by the creation of individual reality and individual values.
這個古老的故事是太陽個體從子宮和集體無意識的黑暗中浮現的過程的鮮明肖像。如同夢境一樣，我們可以把神話中的所有角色解讀為在我們內在上演他們的故事。Tiamat 和 Marduk 仍然活得好好的，在仍在與從母親中分離的問題搏鬥的孩子和成人內在。Marduk，太陽原則，必須與他自身月亮渴望的回歸性拉力搏鬥，在這場搏鬥持續期間，本能性質的需求被體驗為苦澀的（鹹水）、怪異的和威脅生命的。他的勝利導致了世界的形成，這也許是描述個體現實形成的另一種方式。神話既是感受的意象也是發展的模式，你們中有些人可能認得出 Marduk-Tiamat 故事所描述的發展階段。這是我們與慣性、冷漠、停滯和成癮的持續戰鬥，在小規模上我們在日常的小衝突中經歷它——堅持節食、進行鍛鍊計劃或完成一門困難的學習課程。我們也可以在離開一段不滿意但強迫性的關係或婚姻、一份安全但令人窒息的工作、或一個可靠但吞噬性的家庭中看到它。Marduk 是「我是」的聲音，雖然與海洋性母親的合一被破壞了，但這被個體現實和個體價值的創造所取代。

In some myths, the Threshold Crossing is not a dragon fight, but involves the actual death of the hero, prior to transformation or resurrection. This is the case with Dionysos and Jesus, both of whom are destroyed but who can only assume their true form as divine redeemers through such ritual dismemberment. In these stories the hero is subjected to great suffering, which burns away his mortal aspect. This process is really the same as the dragon fight, but it is imaged from a different and more sophisticated perspective. In the archaic tale of Marduk and Tiamat, it is the mother-dragon who undergoes the suffering and dismemberment, while Marduk experiences only victory. In the Dionysian and Christian stories, the god experiences the suffering himself, for the mother-dragon is his own body which must be transformed or freed from the grip of instinctual bondage. We can see in this a kind of evolutionary process at work where, in the later myths, the deeper meaning of the dragon fight is revealed.
在某些神話中，門檻跨越不是一場龍之戰，而是涉及英雄的實際死亡，先於轉化或復活。Dionysos 和耶穌就是如此，他們都被摧毀了，但只有通過這種儀式性的肢解才能呈現他們作為神聖救贖者的真正形式。在這些故事中，英雄經受巨大的痛苦，這燒盡了他的凡人面。這個過程與龍之戰實際上相同，但它是從不同且更精緻的視角來想像的。在 Marduk 和 Tiamat 的古老故事中，是母親龍經受痛苦和肢解，而 Marduk 只經歷了勝利。在 Dionysian 和基督教故事中，是神自身經受痛苦，因為母親龍就是他自己的身體，必須被轉化或從本能束縛的控制中解放。我們可以在這裡看到一種進化過程在起作用：在後來的神話中，龍之戰更深層的含義被揭示了。

The dragon fight is a noble enactment, heroic on the grand scale. Its image still grips us and reappears perennially in the cinema in such films as Alien, not to mention the Hammer House of Horror epics where the hero battles the werewolves, vampires, ghouls and goblins of Hekate's underworld. Yet the internal experience is really a kind of dismemberment or crucifixion, because as we separate we suffer. There is always a problem of suffering—loneliness, isolation, guilt and the enmity of others—when the Sun begins to emerge. If we deny this process of suffering, we will always need to find a dragon outside upon whom to project our own pain.
龍之戰是一場崇高的展演，大規模的英雄之舉。它的意象仍然抓住我們，在電影中反覆出現如《異形》，更不用說 Hammer 恐怖史詩中英雄與 Hekate 冥界的狼人、吸血鬼、食屍鬼和哥布林的戰鬥。然而內在的經驗實際上是一種肢解或十字架刑，因為我們在分離時受苦。當太陽開始浮現時，總是有痛苦的問題——孤獨、隔離、內疚和他人的敵意。如果我們否認這個痛苦的過程，我們將總是需要在外面找到一條龍來投射我們自己的痛苦。

The mythic image of crucifixion is one of the most powerful symbols of our isolation and alienation on the Saturnian cross of matter. In this state we are unparented and forsaken. There is no home to return to, no comforting bosom to enfold us, no group or collective which can offer a palliative. This is the stark existential state of “I am,” which can tell us a lot about why the Sun only really emerges at midlife, when the person is sufficiently strong and formed enough to meet the challenge. The problem of alone-ness, which always accompanies any expression of the individual self, is the deepest meaning of the Threshold Crossing in the hero myth. It constellates our greatest anxieties about loss and separation, for there is always the risk that, if we emerge, no one may love us. So the battle with the dark twin, the dragon fight, and the dismemberment or crucifixion are all images of taking on the burden of one's separate self, which is the first important stage of the solar journey. The hero is then equipped to pursue the real object of his quest, because he has proven that he can stand alone.
十字架刑的神話意象是我們在物質的土星十字架上孤立和疏離的最強大象徵之一。在這種狀態中我們沒有父母、被遺棄。沒有家可以回去，沒有令人安慰的胸懷擁抱我們，沒有群體或集體可以提供慰藉。這是「我是」的赤裸存在狀態，它告訴我們很多關於為什麼太陽只在人生中期真正浮現——此時人足夠強壯和成形，能夠迎接挑戰。孤獨的問題——總是伴隨個體自我的任何表達——是英雄神話中門檻跨越的最深含義。它星座化了我們對失去和分離的最大焦慮，因為總有這樣的風險：如果我們浮現，可能沒有人愛我們。所以與黑暗雙生的戰鬥、龍之戰、以及肢解或十字架刑都是承擔個體分離自我重擔的意象，這是太陽之旅的第一個重要階段。英雄然後就裝備好了去追求他探索的真正目標，因為他已經證明他能獨自站立。

Now we need to explore this “real” quest, the prize or treasure which awaits the hero after his ordeals. The treasure is often literally a treasure—gold or jewels, or the water of life, or the rulership of a kingdom, or the gift of healing or prophecy. It is a highly individual goal, but it is always something of great value to the hero. The Sun, embodying the mythic hero, strives toward an ultimate reward, an indestructible nugget of identity which justifies and validates one's existence. The hero and his prize are really the same thing. The treasure is the essential core of the hero, his divine side which was always hidden in his mortal body. This may sound terribly abstract. But the sense of being a real, solid, indestructible “me” is a very precious and magical thing, and it is also hard won. Every life situation where we are called upon to separate ourselves and stand for our own values and goals forges a bit of this “me,” and we suffer for it each time, because the eternal mother-dragon must be fought again and again in different guises.
現在我們需要探索這個「真正的」探索——英雄在考驗之後等待著的獎品或寶藏。寶藏往往字面上就是寶藏——黃金或珠寶，或生命之水，或王國的統治權，或治療或預言的天賦。它是一個高度個體化的目標，但對英雄來說總是有巨大價值的東西。太陽，體現著神話英雄，追求一個最終的獎賞，一個不可毀滅的身份金塊，它證明和確認一個人的存在。英雄和他的獎品實際上是同一回事。寶藏是英雄的核心本質，他一直隱藏在凡人身體中的神聖一面。這可能聽起來非常抽象。但作為一個真實的、堅實的、不可毀滅的「我」的感覺是一件非常珍貴和神奇的東西，也是來之不易的。每一個我們被要求分離自己、為自己的價值和目標站起來的生活情境都鍛造了一點這個「我」，我們每次都為此受苦，因為永恆的母親龍必須以不同面貌一次又一次地被對抗。

Sometimes the hero's treasure is a bride, and the hierosgamos, the sacred marriage, is the end of the quest. The divine hero is fully united with his other half, his humanity, in the form of a woman. He then creates a dynasty, from whom are descended famous kings and queens, all of whom have a little bit of the blood of the immortals in them because of the hero's divine parentage. In pagan times, many rulers claimed they had some of this divine blood. Julius Caesar, for example, claimed descent from the goddess Venus through her son, the hero Aeneas, founder of Rome. If you have read The Holy Blood and the Holy Grail,5 you will know that there is a secret society in France who believe their proposed claimant to the French throne is descended from Jesus, who married Mary Magdalen. Because the theme of descent from the god through the semidivine hero is archetypal, it remains a potent symbol for us even today.
有時英雄的寶藏是一位新娘，而 hierosgamos，即神聖婚禮，是探索的終點。神聖英雄與他的另一半——他的人性——以女性形式完全合一。然後他創建一個王朝，從中產生了著名的國王和王后，他們都因英雄的神聖血統而帶著一點不朽者的血液。在異教時代，許多統治者聲稱他們有這種神聖血液。例如，Julius Caesar 聲稱通過女神 Venus 的兒子、羅馬建立者英雄 Aeneas 而是 Venus 的後裔。如果你讀過《聖血與聖杯》，⁵ 你會知道法國有一個秘密結社相信他們的法國王位候選人是耶穌的後裔——耶穌娶了 Mary Magdalen。因為通過半神聖英雄從神那裡傳下來的血統主題是原型的，即使對今天的我們來說它仍然是一個有力的象徵。

One aspect of the sacred marriage and the founding of the dynasty seems to be the anchoring of the divine seed in mortal life through the continuity of successive generations. There are descendants who carry the hero's blood down through time, which means he lives forever through his bloodline. What might this symbol mean for us psychologically? Perhaps it reflects the solar drive to create something which outlasts one's own life. The archetypal masculine longing for a son expresses the most basic, biological level of this drive. But there are inner levels as well. If we live the Sun as fully as we can, we may experience the feeling that we have secured our bit of eternity by offering something of lasting value to the collective. We have given something of our own lives to life. The 5th house of children is ruled by the Sun, which offers its essence to the future in order to experience the eternal realm. The Moon has its own instinctive need to bear children, but this reflects nature's continuity of life on earth. The Sun's longing for progeny reflects the quest for immortality.
神聖婚禮和王朝建立的一個面向似乎是通過連續世代將神聖種子錨定在凡人生活中。有後代在時間中傳承英雄的血脈，這意味著他通過血統永生。這個象徵對我們的心理學意味著什麼？也許它反映了太陽驅動去創造超越自己生命的東西。原型男性對兒子的渴望表達了這種驅力最基本的生物學層面。但也有內在的層面。如果我們盡可能充分地活出太陽，我們可能會體驗到一種感覺：我們通過向集體提供持久價值的東西而確保了自己的一點永恆。我們把自己的生命給予了生命。第五宮——子女宮——由太陽守護，它將自己的本質奉獻給未來以體驗永恆領域。月亮有自己的本能需求要生育子女，但這反映的是自然界在地球上的生命延續。太陽對後代的渴望反映的是對不朽的追求。

For many people, however, children are not the only channel through which the solar drive may need to express itself. Although this may be the most “natural” level, some individuals choose not to have children, or are unable to. Finding another dimension for the solar urge then becomes extremely important. The 5th house in the chart reflects the artist's longing to create something indestructible—an inner or imaginative child which will outlive its creator and contribute his or her essential being and vision to future generations. I have known people who fulfil this longing by planting trees. They know perfectly well that, by the time the tree reaches maturity, they will no longer be here. But this act gives them the feeling that they are transcending time. So the sacred marriage which generates a dynasty is a powerful symbol of the Sun's need to contribute a little piece of its divine essence to the future.
然而對許多人來說，子女不是太陽驅力可能需要表達的唯一管道。雖然這可能是最「自然」的層面，但有些人選擇不要孩子，或無法生育。找到太陽衝動的另一個維度就變得極為重要。星盤中的第五宮反映了藝術家渴望創造不可毀滅之物的願望——一個內在的或想像的孩子，它將比其創造者更長壽，並將其本質存在和視野貢獻給後代。我認識一些人通過種樹來實現這種渴望。他們完全清楚，等到樹成熟時，他們已不在人世。但這個行為給他們一種超越時間的感覺。因此產生王朝的神聖婚禮是太陽需要將其神聖本質的一小部分貢獻給未來的有力象徵。

Another image of the hero's goal is reunion with or redemption of the father. One of the stories which portrays this theme most vividly is that of Parsifal, the holy fool who sets off in quest of the Grail. The finding of the Grail is only one aspect of his journey; redemption of the suffering father, the sick Grail king, is the other. This brings us to the issue of the Sun as a symbol of the inheritance from the personal father. If we are to fully live the Sun, we must, in the words of the I Ching, “work on what has been spoiled by the father” by infusing it with new life. The sick or wounded father in myth is an image of spiritual decay and the loss of hope and faith. It is interesting in this context to consider Jung, who had the Sun in Leo and who was impelled to redeem his clergyman father's lost faith by restoring life to the Christian symbols in a new way. Jung's Answer to Job aroused considerable confusion and even hostility when it was published, but it is a brilliant analysis of this problem of redemption of the father, who in Job's case is God himself.6 Jung's thesis, put very simplistically, is that the necessity for Christ's incarnation arises from the fact that God the Father makes a bit of a mess of things with Job. The paternal deity's relationship to humankind is faulty and lacking in compassion, and God recognises that it needs to be redeemed through the suffering of Jesus, his only son. Just as the Moon represents an essential substance which we share with our mothers on the instinctual level, the Sun reflects an essential vision which we share with our fathers on the creative level, and which can only reach its proper fruition over many generations of solar striving.
英雄目標的另一個意象是與父親的重聚或救贖父親。最生動地描繪這個主題的故事之一是 Parsifal，這個神聖的傻瓜出發尋找聖杯。找到聖杯只是他旅途的一個面向；救贖受苦的父親——生病的聖杯國王——是另一個。這帶我們來到太陽作為來自個人父親的遺傳象徵的問題。如果我們要充分活出太陽，我們必須用易經的話說「治理被父親敗壞的東西」，用新的生命注入它。神話中生病的或受傷的父親是精神衰落和希望與信仰喪失的意象。在這個背景下考慮 Jung 是有趣的，他的太陽在獅子座，他被驅使去通過以新的方式恢復基督教象徵的生命力來救贖他牧師父親失去的信仰。Jung 的《答 Job》⁶ 在出版時引起了相當大的困惑甚至敵意，但它精彩地分析了這個救贖父親的問題——在 Job 的案例中父親就是上帝。Jung 的論點，簡化地說，是 Christ 化身的必要性源於上帝父親在 Job 的事情上弄糟了這一事實。父神的與人類的關係是有缺陷的、缺乏同情心的，上帝認識到這需要通過他唯一的兒子耶穌的受難來救贖。正如月亮代表我們在直覺層面與母親分享的基本實質，太陽反映了我們在創造層面與父親分享的基本視野，這只能通過多代太陽努力才能達到適當的成果。

The hero's prize is sometimes an elixir, which he must steal. This elixir may confer immortality or healing gifts or prophecy, or it may save the kingdom. The motif of the stolen elixir appears with great regularity in fairy tales as well as in myths such as that of the Babylonian Gilgamesh, who stole a branch of the Tree of Immortality, or Prometheus, who stole Zeus' sacred fire, or Jason, who stole the Golden Fleece. The magical substance is usually in the hands of a monster or dragon or sorcerer or witch, and the hero must nick it and bring it back into ordinary life. The illicit nature of the hero's task is a most interesting theme and we should look at it more carefully, for it can tell us yet more about the innate conflicts and dilemmas of expressing the Sun.
英雄的獎品有時是一種靈藥，他必須偷取。這種靈藥可以賦予不朽或治療天賦或預言，或者它可以拯救王國。偷來的靈藥這個主題在童話和神話中都以極大的規律性出現，如巴比倫的 Gilgamesh 偷了永生之樹的樹枝，或 Prometheus 偷了 Zeus 的聖火，或 Jason 偷了金羊毛。這種魔法物質通常在怪物或龍或巫師或女巫手中，英雄必須偷走它並帶回普通生活。英雄任務的非法性質是一個非常有趣的主題，我們應該更仔細地審視它，因為它可以告訴我們更多關於表達太陽的內在衝突和困境。

I have spoken about loneliness and the enmity of the collective as the emotional equivalents of the dangers the hero faces in his struggles. The issue of guilt (and the accompanying fear of reprisal) surrounding the theft of the elixir is also a fundamental aspect of the solar journey. There is something illicit about becoming oneself, because it involves stealing something from the mass psyche, something which was the common property of the collective unconscious. This dilemma can easily clothe itself in political garb, although the essence of all political ideologies is ultimately to be found in the individuals who formulate them. The more separate we feel, the more we experience an archetypal sense of guilt. The word guilt comes from an Anglo-Saxon root which means “debt.” And a profound sense of reneging on a debt—to mother, to the family and to the collective—is constellated by any act of individual creation which separates us from them.
我談到了孤獨和集體的敵意作為英雄在鬥爭中面臨的危險的情感等價物。圍繞偷取靈藥的內疚（以及伴隨的報復恐懼）問題也是太陽之旅的一個基本面。成為自己有一種非法的東西，因為它涉及從集體心靈中偷取某物，某物曾是集體無意識的共同財產。這種困境很容易披上政治外衣，儘管所有政治意識形態的本質最終都可以在制定它們的個體中找到。我們越感到分離，就越體驗到一種原型的內疚感。內疚這個詞來自一個盎格魯-撒克遜詞根，意思是「債務」。而一種深刻的拖欠債務——對母親、對家庭和對集體——的感覺，在任何將我們與他們分離的個體創造行為中都會被星座化。

I have worked with many people who are afraid to express the potentials they know are in them because on some level they fear the separation from the family psyche which such self-expression would entail. To be free enough to move beyond the family circle, especially if the parents themselves were blocked, repressed and stifled in their own lives, is tantamount to the dragon fight. It is better to stay where one is, however frustrated, and know that the magical umbilical cord remains unbroken. After all, the inner collective voice tells us, who do I think I am? What right do I have to become something my parents were never able to be, after all they sacrificed on my behalf? There is thus considerable guilt around expressing the Sun, because it means stealing an elixir which is the common property of all—albeit unused. The elixir can do nothing on a mass level until a hero comes along who knows what to do with it. But for an individual to possess it means that, at least initially, something is taken away from the mass. Of course it remains the hero's task at the end of the story to give something back to the collective. But this does not mitigate the initial sense of sin. In Wagner's Ring cycle, the dragon-giant who guards the gold and the ring of the Niebelungs does nothing with them. He lies asleep on top of his hoard, and would do so unto eternity. The solar gold is a human potential, common to us all, but if it is buried in the unconscious, it remains forever potential. It takes an individual to actualise the elixir. Yet in doing so, it is a theft, and the hero suffers for it. So the hero must return as a culture bringer, and make good his debt. I always find etymology interesting, because so often it gives us the key meaning of a word which we ordinarily take for granted. The word redeem comes from the same root as ransom, to buy back. Thus the hero must become a redeemer for his people, paying off the debt he incurred when he stole the elixir. He cannot use it for himself alone. He owes something to the mass psyche, and must create something original in return. Guilt is the shadow face of altruism, and we will always find it sitting side by side with the impulse to redeem which is so unconsciously powerful a motive in the helping professions.
我與許多人一起工作過，他們害怕表達自己知道在內的潛能，因為在某個層面上他們恐懼這種自我表達所必然帶來的與家庭心靈的分離。足夠自由地超越家庭圈子——特別是如果父母自己在生活中被阻礙、壓抑和窒息——等同於龍之戰。待在原地更好，無論多麼沮喪，知道魔法臍帶仍然未斷。畢竟，內在的集體聲音告訴我們，我以為自己是誰？我有什麼權利成為父母從未能夠成為的東西，畢竟他們為我犧牲了那麼多？因此圍繞表達太陽有相當大的內疚，因為它意味著偷取一種靈藥——一種所有人的共同財產——儘管是未使用的。靈藥在集體層面上做不了什麼，直到一個英雄出現並知道如何使用它。但對一個個體來說擁有它意味著，至少在起初，某種東西從集體中被拿走了。當然，在故事結束時英雄的任務是向集體回饋某種東西。但這不能減輕最初的罪惡感。在 Wagner 的《尼伯龍根指環》中，守衛黃金和指環的龍巨人什麼也不做。他躺在他的囤積物上面睡覺，會這樣做到永恆。太陽的黃金是人類的潛能，對我們所有人都是共同的，但如果它被埋在無意識中，它就永遠只是潛能。需要一個個體來實現這種靈藥。然而這樣做時，這是一種偷竊，英雄為此受苦。所以英雄必須作為文化傳播者回來，償還他的債務。我總覺得詞源學很有趣，因為它經常給我們一個我們通常視為理所當然的詞的關鍵含義。贖回這個詞與贖金的詞根相同，即買回。因此英雄必須成為他子民的救贖者，償還他偷取靈藥時所欠下的債務。他不能只為自己使用它。他欠集體心靈的，必須創造原創的東西來回報。內疚是利他主義的陰影面，我們總會發現它與救贖衝動並肩而坐，後者在助人專業中是一個無意識的強大動機。

We meet the same theme in the Biblical tale of Adam and Eve, for they, too, are embodiments of the solar hero. The apple which gives knowledge of good and evil is the fruit of consciousness, which inevitably separates us from fusion with mother and the collective. Adam and Eve have stolen something which previously belonged only to God, an elixir sitting unplucked and uneaten on the Tree, and for their sin they are expelled from Paradise. Nor are they allowed back in again until the solar hero-redeemer appears in the form of Christ to pay off their debt. Once the Sun has begun to shine we cannot enter the gates of Paradise again, unless we can also find within us the stuff of the redeemer who can buy back our debt. Unfortunately we usually try to find this redeemer outside.
我們在聖經中 Adam 和 Eve 的故事中遇到同樣的主題，因為他們也是太陽英雄的化身。那顆給予善惡知識的蘋果是意識之果，它不可避免地將我們與母親和集體的融合中分離出來。Adam 和 Eve 偷了以前只屬於上帝的東西，一種在樹上未摘未吃的靈藥，因為他們的罪他們被逐出天堂。他們也不被允許再回去，直到太陽英雄救贖者以基督的形式出現來償還他們的債務。一旦太陽開始照耀，我們就無法再進入天堂之門，除非我們也能在內在找到救贖者的材料來買回我們的債務。不幸的是我們通常試圖在外面尋找這個救贖者。

So the theft of the elixir is a profound rite of passage, and once it has been made, things cannot go back to where they were before the Fall. We can only move forward, and make something of the elixir which is really our own precious uniqueness. Even if we do a little backsliding and regressing now and then under heavy Neptune transits, we cannot undo what has been done, for with the light of the Sun the fantasy of fusion must cease. There is also the fear of reprisal, and the hero must usually run for his life once he has stolen the elixir, with all the legions of the angered guardian in hot pursuit. This threat of reprisal is not just paranoia, either, for the collective does indeed strike back, and we can see it most clearly in the operation of family dynamics when an individual breaks free of an enmeshed family unit. We can also see it in political, religious and professional groups when one of the members voices too original an opinion, or achieves more creatively or financially than the other members. Thus the ancient myth enacts itself outside us, until we recognise that all the characters lie within.
因此偷取靈藥是一個深刻的通過儀式，一旦完成，事物就無法回到 Fall 之前的狀態。我們只能前進，用真正是我們自己珍貴獨特性的靈藥做些什麼。即使我們在某些重大海王星過運下偶爾倒退和回歸，我們也無法撤銷已經做的事，因為有了太陽的光，融合的幻想必須停止。還有報復的恐懼，英雄偷了靈藥後通常必須逃命，身後是憤怒守護者的全部軍團緊追不捨。這種報復的威脅也不僅僅是偏執，因為集體確實會反擊，我們可以最清楚地看到它在家庭動力學中的運作——當一個個體從糾纏的家庭單位中掙脫時。我們也可以在政治、宗教和專業群體中看到它，當一個成員提出了太原創的意見，或在創造或財務上比其他成員取得更多時。因此古老的神話在我們外面上演，直到我們認識到所有角色都在內在。

The hero must eventually make his return, which is no more simple than the process of his setting out. He must pass the Threshold Crossing once again, with the elixir or the bride or both, and reenter ordinary life. Because the hero myth does not occur once in our lives, bur repeats itself over and over on many levels, this difficult process of return follows every act of creation and triumphant self-actualisation. Sometimes the return is reflected by a time of depression, because mundane reality contrasts painfully with the great inner tasks we have been engaged upon. Sometimes the hero must be rescued by his helpers at the very last stage of the quest. He may face yet another dragon or witch (which is of course the same one) barring the path of his return. And sometimes he doesn't really want to go back. The fiery temperament, which applies to Sun-ruled Leo as well as to Aries and Sagittarius, may find this return to ordinary life particularly difficult because it seems so boring, and the hero may already be planning his next quest before the old one is completed.
英雄最終必須回歸，這與他出發的過程一樣不簡單。他必須帶著靈藥或新娘或兩者兼有，再次通過門檻跨越，重新進入普通生活。因為英雄神話不是在我們生活中發生一次，而是在許多層面上一遍又一遍地重覆，這種困難的回歸過程伴隨著每一次創造和成功的自我實現。有時回歸反映為一段抑鬱時期，因為世俗現實與我們所從事的偉大內在任務痛苦地對比。有時英雄必須在探索的最後階段被他的幫助者營救。他可能面臨又一條龍或女巫（當然是同一個）阻擋他回歸的道路。有時他並不真正想回去。火象氣質——適用於太陽守護的獅子座以及白羊座和射手座——可能發現這種回歸普通生活特別困難，因為它看起來太無聊了，英雄可能還沒完成舊的探索就已在計劃下一個了。

We cannot simply look at a horoscope and say, “Ah, here is the story of Theseus and the Minotaur, that is your hero myth.” All the stages of the hero's journey are relevant to everyone at some point in their lives, although there may be more of a focus on a particular theme. For example, I have found that Gemini tends to repeatedly meet the dark twin in one form or another, while Scorpio favours confrontations with dragons. But these motifs may reflect other factors in the chart, such as Moon conjunct Pluto or a Gemini Ascendant, and they will interweave with the themes of the Sun's placement. We should also remember that sooner or later all the other planets will transit in aspect to the Sun, and the Sun will progress to aspect many planets during a lifetime. We all get a glimpse of what it might feel like to be somebody else, sooner or later. And as I have said, we enact the hero's journey many times in many different forms, some of them so small that they come to completion during the course of an ordinary week, or even a day. As soon as we have made any step in consciousness and self-unfoldment, another call to adventure comes, and off we go again. We never really finish the process of the Sun.
我們不能僅僅看一張星盤就說：「啊，這就是 Theseus 和牛頭怪的故事，那就是你的英雄神話。」英雄之旅的所有階段在某個時刻都與每個人相關，雖然可能有對某個特定主題更多的關注。例如，我發現雙子座傾向於反覆以一種或另一種形式遇到黑暗雙生，而天蠍座偏愛與龍的對峙。但這些主題可能反映星盤中的其他因素，如月亮合冥王星或雙子上升，它們將與太陽位置的主題交織。我們還應記住，遲早所有其他行星都會過運到與太陽形成相位，太陽也將在一生中推運到與許多行星形成相位。我們遲早都會瞥見做別人是什麼感覺。正如我所說，我們以許多不同形式多次上演英雄之旅，有些形式如此之小以至於在普通一週甚至一天內就完成了。一旦我們在意識和自我展開中邁出了任何一步，另一個冒險的召喚就來了，我們又出發了。我們永遠不會真正完成太陽的過程。

The sign in which the Sun is placed at birth is in theory the most basic of astrological factors, and is usually interpreted on the level of character. But it can also tell us a great deal about one of the main themes of the hero's journey. Each sign relates to a particular set of mythic figures, and each sign also has a planetary ruler or presiding deity with its own set of stories. The planetary ruler of the Sun sign can give us insight into the god who engenders the hero, for this planet, even more than the ruler of the Ascendant, describes the special potentials within us which we must work to find and develop. The chart ruler can give us information about what life will require of us and, in combination with the Ascendant itself, may describe the kinds of situations the hero will meet on his journey. But the Sun ruler is our presiding deity; and the hero and his prize are ultimately the same thing.
太陽所在的星座在理論上是最基本的占星因素，通常在性格層面上解讀。但它也可以告訴我們很多關於英雄之旅的主要主題之一。每個星座都與一組特定的神話人物相關，每個星座也有一個行星守護星或主管神祇，有自己的一套故事。太陽星座的守護星可以給我們洞察孕育英雄的神，因為這顆行星——甚至比上升的守護星更多地——描述了我們內在必須努力尋找和發展的特殊潛能。星盤守護星可以給我們關於生活將要求我們什麼的信息，與上升本身結合，可以描述英雄在旅途中將遇到的那種情境。但太陽守護星是我們的主管神祇；英雄和他的獎品最終是同一回事。

We can view the Sun sign from the perspective of what role we are called upon to play in life, and what unique contribution we can make by finding an individual channel for this archetypal energy. For example, if you are born under Gemini or Virgo, your Sun ruler is Mercury. On the level of character reading, you can say, “I am a Gemini, therefore I am communicative, intelligent, versatile and get bored easily.” But what happens if we think about Hermes? What is his domain? What spheres of life does he govern?
我們可以從我們被要求在生活中扮演什麼角色以及通過找到這種原型能量的個體化管道可以做出什麼獨特貢獻的角度來看太陽星座。例如，如果你出生在雙子座或處女座，你的太陽守護星是水星。在性格解讀的層面上，你可以說：「我是雙子座，因此我善於溝通、聰明、多才多藝且容易無聊。」但如果我們從 Hermes 的角度來思考呢？他的領域是什麼？他掌管哪些生活領域？

Hermes has many myths, from his theft of Apollo's cattle and his invention of the Iyre to his role as psychopomp, magus and messenger of the gods. You will hear a lot more about Hermes when Howard gives you a broader mythic background for the planet Mercury.7 But very briefly, Hermes is the god of the roads. He rules the ways in between, the linking routes between different domains or levels of the psyche. He presides over the wanderer and the merchant, for he belongs nowhere and travels everywhere, speaking every language and dealing in every currency. He is a negotiator and a messenger, without ambition of his own, serving the purposes of the other gods as well as his own mischievous whims. All his spheres of activity involve exchange or communication of one kind or another. It is possible to view this figure as the image of a particular daemon, a calling or destiny which needs individualised vehicles in ordinary life.
Hermes 有許多神話，從偷走 Apollo 的牛群到他發明豎琴，到他作為引魂者、術士和神的信使的角色。當 Howard 給你們一個更廣泛的水星神話背景時，你們會聽到更多關於 Hermes 的內容。⁷ 但簡要地說，Hermes 是道路之神。他掌管中間地帶，不同領域或心靈層面之間的連接路線。他主管流浪者和商人，因為他不屬於任何地方卻到處旅行，說每種語言、用每種貨幣交易。他是談判者和信使，沒有自己的野心，為其他神的目的服務，也為自己調皮的念頭服務。他所有的活動領域都涉及某種交換或溝通。可以將這個人物視為一個特定精靈的意象——一種召喚或天命，需要在普通生活中找到個體化的載體。

There are other myths which concern the sign of Gemini, and these too will be relevant in terms of the calling or destiny of the Gemini individual. The best-known Geminian myth is that of the Twins, Castor and Pollux (or Polydeuces), one of whom is divine (the son of Zeus) and the other mortal. One of the characteristic themes of the hero's Threshold Crossing, as we have seen, is the confrontation with the dark twin. This particular motif often enacts itself very literally in the Gemini person's childhood, through a competitive and difficult relationship with a sibling who may even be an actual twin. Or the theme may express itself through a particular pattern in friendships. The issue of sibling rivalry, whether literal or metaphoric, tends to occur over and over again in the lives of many Geminians. Yet all the while the Gemini may be heard to say, “Oh, but I'm not competitive, I haven't done anything to cause this problem, it's my brother/ sister/ friend who started all the trouble.” Yet the battle with the dark twin is the story of confrontation with the dark side of oneself, and those upon whom Gemini hooks this mythic image are really carriers for hidden aspects of oneself.
還有其他關於雙子座的神話，這些在雙子座個體的召喚或天命方面也同樣相關。最著名的雙子神話是雙胞胎 Castor 和 Pollux（或 Polydeuces），其中一個是神聖的（Zeus 的兒子），另一個是凡人。如我們所見，英雄門檻跨越的一個特徵主題是與黑暗雙生的對峙。這個特定主題經常在雙子座人的童年中非常字面地上演，通過與一個兄弟姐妹的競爭和困難的關係——甚至可能是實際的雙胞胎。或者這個主題可能通過友誼中的某種模式表達。兄弟姐妹競爭的問題——無論是字面的還是隱喻的——往往在許多雙子座人的生活中一次又一次地出現。然而雙子座的人可能一直被聽到說：「哦，但我不競爭，我沒有做任何引起這個問題的事，是我的兄弟/姐妹/朋友挑起了所有麻煩。」然而與黑暗雙生的戰鬥是與自己陰暗面對峙的故事，那些被雙子座投射這個神話意象的人實際上是隱藏的自我面向的載體。

The mythic themes which reflect the Sun sign and its ruler are extremely rich. They describe some of the main archetypal patterns behind the person's unfoldment as an individual. Now what would you say about the two Venus-ruled signs, Taurus and Libra? Can you try to approach these from a mythic rather than a character perspective?
反映太陽星座及其守護星的神話主題極其豐富。它們描述了個體作為個體展開的一些主要原型模式。那麼你會怎麼說兩個金星守護的星座——金牛座和天秤座？你能試著從神話而非性格的角度來接近它們嗎？

Audience: The mythic ruler is Aphrodite. She is the goddess of love.
聽眾：神話守護星是 Aphrodite。她是愛之神。

Liz: She is the goddess of a particular kind of love. All the feminine deities concern themselves with relationships of one kind or another. Aphrodite has a very precise domain over which she presides.
Liz：她是一種特殊類型的愛之神。所有女性神祇都關心這樣或那樣的關係。Aphrodite 有一個非常精確的領域。

Audience: Beauty.
聽眾：美。

Liz: That is part of her function; she embodies and presides over the creation of beauty, harmony and pleasure. Her love is erotic love, rooted in sensual pleasure and aesthetic delight. It is not concerned with marriage bonds or family ties. Plato once described love as passion aroused by beauty, which describes Aphrodite's love very nicely. Venusian love is not self-sacrificing like that of Neptune, nor is it concerned with fusion, empathy or security. Venus' principle is that of self-pleasuring, and you can take this on all possible levels. Through Libra, Venus pleasures the mind with its longing for a perfect, harmonious world; through Taurus, Venus pleasures the body with its longing for sensual satisfaction and beauty in concrete form. If you are a Libran or a Taurean, this capricious goddess is your presiding deity, and she will strive to be given creative expression in the world through vehicles which are appropriate for her nature.
Liz：那是她功能的一部分；她體現和掌管美、和諧和愉悅的創造。她的愛是情欲之愛，根植於感官愉悅和審美享受。它不涉及婚姻紐帶或家庭關係。Plato 曾將愛描述為由美激發的激情，這很好地描述了 Aphrodite 的愛。金星之愛不像海王星那樣自我犧牲，也不關心融合、共情或安全。金星的原則是自我愉悅，你可以在所有可能的層面上理解這一點。通過天秤座，金星以對完美和諧世界的渴望來愉悅心靈；通過金牛座，金星以對感官滿足和具體形式之美的渴望來愉悅身體。如果你是天秤座或金牛座，這位任性的女神就是你的主管神祇，她將努力通過適合她性質的載體在世界上獲得創造性表達。

The conventional listings of personality characteristics which are used to describe the Sun sign may fit some people up to a point; but often they do not fit at all, to the confusion of the layman who then assumes astrology does not work. I have heard many people rightly point out that they do not “behave” like the usual descriptions of their Sun sign. It is not sufficient for us to say, “Well, other chart factors are stronger.” The Sun is, after all, the Sun, the centre of the chart and the solar system. It must be hiding somewhere. But if we can understand that the Sun describes a process rather than a set of behaviour patterns, and can comprehend the core of each sign's inner drive (which is what myths portray), we can be far more helpful to a client struggling to express his or her individuality. We may not “behave” like our Sun signs, but we are them, in the deepest sense. The Sun ruler is our divine parent, and if this inner striving is thwarted or repressed, it is, in effect, tantamount to a refusal of the mythic call.
用來描述太陽星座的傳統性格特徵列表可能在某種程度上適合某些人；但往往完全不適合，讓外行困惑並因此假設占星學不起作用。我聽到許多人正確地指出他們不像太陽星座的通常描述那樣「行事」。對我們來說只說「嗯，其他星盤因素更強」是不夠的。太陽畢竟是太陽，星盤和太陽系的中心。它一定藏在哪里。但如果我們能理解太陽描述的是一個過程而非一組行為模式，並能理解每個星座內在驅力的核心（這正是神話所描繪的），我們就能對一個努力表達個性的客戶更有幫助。我們可能不「行事」像我們的太陽星座，但在最深層的意義上，我們就是它們。太陽守護星是我們的神聖父母，如果這種內在的努力被阻礙或壓抑，這實際上等同於拒絕神話的召喚。

If there is no expression of the Sun ruler, and no capacity to recognise the divine parenting, then the hero never grows. He refuses the call to adventure and remains a psychological child, unformed and uninitiated. In effect, nobody is home. Now perhaps you might think about the Saturn-ruled signs, Capricorn and Aquarius. What kind of presiding deity is this?
如果沒有太陽守護星的表達，也沒有認出神聖育的能力，那麼英雄永遠不會長大。他拒絕冒險的召喚，仍然是心理上的孩子，未成形、未啟蒙。實際上，無人在家。現在也許你們可以思考一下土星守護的星座——摩羯座和水瓶座。這是什麼樣的主管神祇？

Audience: Isn't Uranus the true ruler of Aquarius?
聽眾：天王星不是水瓶座的真正守護星嗎？

Liz: Both Saturn and Uranus rule Aquarius, and neither is more true than the other. One facet of Aquarius's complexity is that its two rulers have a certain mythic animosity toward each other. Uranus banishes Saturn (Kronos) to the underworld, and Saturn castrates his father and steals his throne in revenge. This is a psychological dynamic, a collision between ideal (Uranus) and reality (Saturn) which tends to repeat itself in various forms throughout the Aquarian's life. But if we focus on Saturn for the moment, who is this god? What is his function?
Liz：土星和天王星都守護水瓶座，兩者都不比另一個更真實。水瓶座複雜性的一個面向是它的兩個守護星之間有某種神話上的敵意。天王星放逐土星（Kronos）到冥界，土星閹割父親並偷走王位作為報復。這是一種心理動力，理想（天王星）與現實（土星）之間的碰撞，往往在水瓶座人的一生中以各種形式重覆。但如果我們暫時關注土星，這位神是誰？他的功能是什麼？

Audience: Working efficiently.
聽眾：高效工作。

Liz: That is one way of putting it. But efficient work is really a character trait, rather than the essence of the god. Saturn creates forms and structures. In myth he is a Titan, an earth god who presides over the productivity of the land. He embodies the laws governing the growing of crops—not the fecund receptivity of the soil, but the immutable structures which define the changing seasons and dictate the timing of seeding and harvesting. He teaches human beings how to obey the laws of nature in order to survive and flourish.
Liz：這是一種說法。但高效工作實際上是一種性格特徵，而不是神的本質。土星創造形式和結構。在神話中他是 Titan，一位掌管土地生產力的大地之神。他體現了管轄作物生長的法則——不是土壤的豐饒接受性，而是定義季節變化和決定播種和收穫時機的不可變結構。他教導人類如何服從自然法則以求生存和繁榮。

Audience: What about his destructiveness? What is the motif of castration, and swallowing his children?
聽眾：那他的破壞性呢？閹割和吞噬孩子的主題是什麼？

Liz: These are the inevitable concomitants of his function. If you take an unlimited idea (Uranus) and bind it in a formal structure, you are destroying its endless future possibilities. You have curtailed its fertility, and it is now limited by the choices you have made. A person may have the dream of a beautiful Edenlike garden with luxurious plants flowering all year long. In reality nothing flowers endlessly, and the gardener must contend not only with the immutable laws of the seasons and the climate but with slugs, aphids, black spot, mildew and the neighbour's cat. Have any of you ever written an essay or a story or a book? You begin with an idea, and it proliferates in your mind. You can do all kinds of things with it when it exists solely on the mental level. You can even fantasise receiving the Nobel Prize for Literature. But when you put your idea down in words on paper, and then finish your essay within the required number of pages, you have castrated it. That is the end of it. You might write another essay on a similar idea, but it will be different. Can you understand how incarnating something limits and castrates the original idea, as well as making it real and permanent? The swallowing of the children is a similar image. In myth Saturn does this because he has been warned that one of his sons will overthrow him. There is always the possibility that the unknown future will disrupt any present structure we build. Saturn swallows these dangerous future potentials (his children) because they are unknown and threatening to his law. The destructive feeling-tone of these images of castration and swallowing describes how the incarnating process looks from the Uranian or Jupiterian point of view. But Saturn was also the god of the Golden Age of humanity, when the earth was fertile and productive and everyone lived happily in accord with divine law. And if you are Saturn-ruled, it is important to understand things from his point of view.
Liz：這些是他的功能的必然伴隨物。如果你取一個無限的理念（天王星）並將它綁在正式結構中，你就破壞了它無盡的未來可能性。你削減了它的生育力，它現在受到你所做選擇的限制。一個人可能有夢想一個美麗的伊甸園般的花園，全年開滿繁盛的植物。在現實中沒有什麼是無限開花的，園丁必須不僅應對不可變的季節和氣候法則，還要應對蛞蝓、蚜蟲、黑斑病、黴菌和鄰居的貓。你們中有人寫過文章或故事或書嗎？你從一個想法開始，它在腦中繁衍。當它只存在於思維層面時，你可以做各種事情。你甚至可以幻想獲得諾貝爾文學獎。但當你把想法寫在紙上，然後在規定的頁數內完成文章，你就閹割了它。那就是它的終結。你可能會寫另一篇類似想法的文章，但它會不同。你能理解如何使某物具體化既限制和閹割了原始想法，同時也使它真實和永久嗎？吞噬孩子是類似的意象。在神話中土星這樣做是因為他被警告他的一個兒子會推翻他。總有未知未來將破壞我們建立的任何現有結構的可能性。土星吞噬這些危險的未來潛能（他的孩子）因為它們是未知的並威脅他的法則。閹割和吞噬這些意象的破壞性情感基調描述了從天王星或木星的角度來看具體化過程是什麼樣子。但土星也是人類黄金時代之神，那時土地肥沃豐產，每個人都幸福地遵循神聖法則生活。如果你是土星守護的，從他的角度理解事物很重要。

Audience: I understood that it was the Ascendant which described this kind of journey you're talking about.
聽眾：我理解的是上升描述了你正在談論的這種旅程。

Liz: Like you I also understand the Ascendant as a development pattern. But it doesn't seem to describe the essential core of character as the Sun does. The Ascendant is rather like a guide who accompanies us on our life's journey, and who requires us to learn certain lessons or attributes to help us become what is symbolised by the Sun. If I were to look for a mythic image to describe it, I would consider a hero such as Theseus, and understand his quest (the slaying of the Minotaur to redeem the kingdom) as the unfoldment of his essence (the Sun); but he must first develop certain skills and abilities in order to fulfil his task. If you read Mary Renault's wonderful novel about the Theseus myth, The King Must Die, you will see that he undergoes a kind of training before he achieves his goal.8 He must undergo the humiliation of slavery in order to learn control of his anger; he must learn the art of bull dancing in order to discipline his body; and he must develop diplomacy and strategy to become a fit leader of his people. In the novel he is very much an Aries type of hero; but his Ascendant is probably Capricorn. I believe the Ascendant reflects the particular training to which life subjects us.
Liz：和你一樣，我也把上升理解為一種發展模式。但它似乎不像太陽那樣描述性格的核心本質。上升更像是陪伴我們生命旅程的嚮導，要求我們學習某些課題或屬性以幫助我們成為太陽所象徵的東西。如果我要找一個神話意象來描述它，我會考慮像 Theseus 這樣的英雄，理解他的探索（消滅牛頭怪以救贖王國）為他的本質的展開（太陽）；但他必須首先發展某些技能和能力才能完成任務。如果你讀 Mary Renault 關於 Theseus 神話的精彩小說《國王必須死》，⁸ 你會看到他在實現目標之前經歷了一種訓練。他必須經歷奴隸的屈辱以學會控制憤怒；他必須學習鬥牛舞的技藝以訓練身體；他必須發展外交和策略才能成為合格的子民領袖。在小說中他非常白羊座類型的英雄；但他的上升可能是摩羯座。我相信上升反映了我們被生活施加的特定訓練。

One of the things I have noticed about the Ascendant is that on some profound level we seem to intuit that we will be required to develop its qualities and confront its archetypal situations. So we acquire a kind of beginners' version of it in the first half of life, an outer mask which often fits all the typical textbook descriptions. You know the sort of thing—Gemini rising is chatty, and Virgo rising is neat, and Aquarius rising is reasonable, and so on. But in fact the Ascendant presents us with an enormous dilemma, for it is very hard to internalise its meaning and take its values on board. Usually there is a lot of resistance to it, because it feels somehow alien, and is often projected out onto the immediate environment, so that we meet its positive and negative faces in the people close to us. But the Sun is not alien, unless it is severely repressed; and even in such cases, once the individual has discovered it within, there is usually a profound relief and sense of homecoming.
我注意到關於上升的一件事是，在某個深層面上我們似乎直覺到我們將被要求發展其品質並面對其原型情境。所以我們在人生前半段獲得了它的一種初學者版本——一副外在面具，往往符合所有典型的教科書描述。你知道那種東西——雙子上升愛聊天，處女上升愛整潔，水瓶上升很理性，等等。但實際上上升給我們帶來了一個巨大的困境，因為很難內化其含義並接受其價值。通常有很多抗拒，因為它感覺某種程度上是陌生的，並經常被投射到直接環境中，因此我們在身邊的人身上遇到它的正面和負面。但太陽並不陌生，除非它被嚴重壓抑；即使在這種情況下，一旦個體在內在發現了它，通常有一種深刻的如釋重負和回家的感覺。

When we express the Sun, we feel authentic and possess a quality of personal authority. Howard and I had a look at the etymological dictionary to find the roots of those words authenticity and authority, and of course the root is the same—the Greek word for “self.” All kinds of words spring from this root—automobile and automatic and autoerotic and autonomous and so on. The Sun gives us a feeling of personal potency and validity. Without this feeling, we are left feeling rather empty and awful, and desperate for reassurance from others. I think there are times when we all lose our connection to the Sun, and wander around in a fog seeking other people's affirmation to make us feel real again. The Sun says, “Whatever cockup I have made of my life, I am myself, and I don't wish to be anybody else.” But when we encounter the Ascendant, we often say, “Oh, there must be some mistake about my birth time. I couldn't possibly have a Pisces Ascendant, it must be Aquarius.”
當我們表達太陽時，我們感到真實並擁有一種個人權威的品質。Howard 和我查了詞源詞典來找 authenticity 和 authority 這些詞的詞根，當然詞根是相同的——希臘語中「自我」的意思。各種詞都從這個詞根產生——汽車、自動和自體情欲和自主等等。太陽給我們一種個人力量和有效性的感覺。沒有這種感覺，我們就感到相當空虛和糟糕，迫切需要他人的保證。我想我們都有失去與太陽聯繫的時候，在霧中徘徊尋求他人的肯定來讓我們重新感到真實。太陽說：「無論我把生活搞得多糟，我就是我自己，我不想成為任何別人。」但當我們遇到上升時，我們經常說：「哦，我的出生時間一定搞錯了。我不可能有雙魚上升，一定是水瓶座。」

Audience: How does the Sun show itself if it is not yet developed? Through its lower qualities?
聽眾：如果太陽還沒發展，它怎麼顯示自己？通過它的低等品質？

Liz: I am not very comfortable with distinctions such as “lower” and “higher.” These evaluations are highly subjective, and depend upon your personal frame of reference. What happens is that the Sun expresses itself unconsciously. Sometimes some of its qualities are projected, which can happen with any unconscious factor in the birth chart. Someone remarked before the session that there are still many cultures where women have little opportunity to express the Sun. What happens to it? It is projected onto their husbands and fathers, onto their male children, and onto authority figures in the outer world. It may also be projected onto other women, for women can also carry solar qualities. The sense of authority and meaning then lies outside, and the woman feels empty and bereft without the objects of her projection.
Liz：我不太舒服用「低等」和「高等」這樣的區分。這些評估是高度主觀的，取決於你的個人參考框架。實際發生的是太陽無意識地表達自己。有時它的一些品質被投射出去，這可以發生在出生星盤中的任何無意識因素上。有人在講座前說仍然有許多文化中女性很少有機會表達太陽。它怎麼了？它被投射到她們的丈夫和父親身上，投射到她們的兒子身上，投射到外在世界的權威人物身上。它也可能被投射到其他女性身上，因為女性也可以攜帶太陽品質。權威和意義感然後在外面，女性感到空虛和貧乏，沒有了她的投射對象。

Audience: But you cannot project everything belonging to a sign. You must surely retain some of its qualities.
聽眾但你不能投射屬於一個星座的所有東西。你一定保留了某些品質。

Liz: I think I said that some of its qualities are projected. I quite agree, it is not a clear black-and-white issue. We may live bits and give away other bits, and this changes as life progresses. Also, projection does not mean we don't behave in that way ourselves. It means we do not realise it, but prefer to think everybody else is doing it instead. One of the peculiar characteristics about the mechanism of projection is that the person can usually be spotted by others as having those particular attributes. Projection does not stop us acting things out, but it creates a kind of self-blindness. The qualities may indeed be what you are calling “lower” —the less attractive face of the sign. But they may also be “higher,” for we also project some of our best potentials onto those whom we feel have everything we lack.
Liz：我想我說的是它的一些品質被投射。我完全同意，這不是一個清晰的黑白問題。我們可能活出一些部分而放棄其他部分，這隨生活的進展而變化。而且，投射不意味著我們自己不以那種方式行事。它意味著我們不意識到它，但更願意認為是別人在這樣做。投射機制的一個奇特特徵是，通常別人可以看出這個人有那些特定的屬性。投射不阻止我們做出行為，但它製造了一種自我盲目。這些品質確實可能是你所說的「低等」——星座不太吸引人的面孔。但它們也可能是「高等」的，因為我們也把我們一些最好的潛能投射到我們覺得擁有我們所缺乏的一切的人身上。

The difference between conscious and unconscious expression is this quality of self-blindness, rather than a “good” or “bad” side of the Sun sign showing itself. Also, the more unaware we are of something within ourselves, the more likely it is to drive us compulsively, and take away our options for choice. Then we may set up situations where we feel it is all out of control, and we are the passive victims, when in fact it was really the unconscious Sun working relentlessly toward its goals from its headquarters in the basement. For example, some Sun in Aries people may be relatively unconnected with it because of childhood complexes, environmental pressures or other factors in the birth chart which mitigate against it (such as the Sun in the 12th opposite Saturn and a lot of planets in earth), they will have the normal Aries quota of aggression, competitiveness, fiery energy, imagination and hunger for challenge, but may not see themselves this way. There may be quite a lot of unconscious aggression and determination to have their own way, but it will all be very low-key and the anger may surface in manipulative ways; and these people will tell you they are really very compromising and indecisive and that others push them around. This might be superficially true, but the Aries qualities have fallen into the shadow, and will make themselves known sooner or later. There will usually be people about who provide a hook for the projection of these attributes, both positive and negative—a lover, perhaps, who is seen as incredibly potent and dashing and exciting, and a father or employer who is seen as domineering, selfish and insensitive.
有意識和無意識表達之間的區別是這種自我盲目的品質，而不是太陽星座的「好」或「壞」面的顯現。而且，我們越不意識到自己內在某物，它就越可能強迫地驅使我們，並剝奪我們選擇的餘地。然後我們可能設置情境，在其中我們覺得一切都失控了，我們是消極的受害者，而實際上真正是無意識的太陽從它在地下室的總部不懈地朝著目標工作。例如，某些太陽在白羊座的人可能因為童年情結、環境壓力或星盤中其他不利因素（如太陽在第十二宮對沖土星和大量行星在土象）而與之聯繫相對較少，他們會有正常的白羊座份額的攻擊性、競爭性、火爆能量、想像力和對挑戰的渴望，但可能不以這種方式看待自己。可能有相當多的無意識攻擊性和要按自己方式行事的決心，但這一切都非常低調，憤怒可能以操縱性方式出現；這些人會告訴你他們真的非常妥協和優柔寡斷，是別人在推他們。這在表面上也許是真的，但白羊座的品質已經落入陰影，遲早會讓自己被知道。通常會有人在周圍為這些屬性的投射提供掛鈎——包括正面和負面的——也許是一個戀人，被視為令人難以置信的有力和瀟灑和令人興奮的，還有一個父親或雇主被視為專橫、自私和不敏感的。

Anger in such a case may come back to the person via others, who are irritated by the unconscious assertiveness and impatience which are being expressed. I have heard quite a few Aries women complain that they could not understand why their friends turned against them; the Aries competitive spirit manifested unconsciously in trying to chat up all the friends' boyfriends but the woman was utterly unaware of it. So you can see that it is not as simple as just dumping the Sun sign and having none of it oneself. Projection is a fascinating and extremely subtle mechanism. We all have dimensions of the Sun which are unexpressed, for it reflects a process of becoming, and we never finish this process.
在這種情況下，憤怒可能通過他人回到這個人身上——他們被無意識表達的攻擊性和不耐煩所激怒。我聽到不少白羊座女性抱怨她們不理解為什麼朋友轉而反對她們；白羊座的競爭精神以無意識方式表現為試圖與所有朋友的男友調情，但這位女性完全沒有意識到。所以你可以看到這不像只是丟掉太陽星座而自己一無所有那樣簡單。投射是一種迷人且極其微妙的機制。我們都有未表達的太陽維度，因為它反映的是一個成為的過程，而我們永遠不會完成這個過程。

An undeveloped Sun may also be very envious. I have mentioned this problem already. Envy is one of the most basic of human emotions, and it can be turned into very creative fodder if we are honest enough to face it; for we envy in others what we value most highly, and usually this includes some of the untapped potentials of the Sun, which are projected onto suitable hooks. It can be very valuable to work with envy in this way, for we discover a great deal about ourselves. Venus may admire, but the Sun envies, and there is a high charge around the people upon whom we project this ideal of what we wish we could be.
未發展的太陽也可能非常嫉妒。我已經提到過這個問題。嫉妒是最基本的人類情感之一，如果我們足夠誠實面對它，它可以變成非常有創造性的養料；因為我們嫉妒的是我們最高度重視的東西，而這通常包括太陽一些未開發的潛能——被投射到合適的掛鈎上。以這種方式與嫉妒一起工作可以非常有價值，因為我們發現了很多關於自己的東西。金星可以仰慕，但太陽嫉妒，在我們投射這個我們希望自己能成為的理想的人身上有很高的電荷。

Now I would like to mention some of the functions of the Sun god in myth, because this might help to clarify the Sun's role in the chart. In some cultures the Sun is represented by a female deity, but in such cases the goddess's attributes are “masculine” in the sense of being dynamic. One example is the Egyptian solar goddess Sekhmet, daughter of the Sun god Ra, who was called the “Eye of Ra.” She was portrayed with a lion's head crowned by the disc of the Sun, and was a deity of battle and bloodshed. But Ra himself, one of the most ancient of solar gods, is more characteristic of the Sun's symbolism; he is the world creator and dispenser of justice, the All-Father who generates all the other gods from his own seed.
現在我想提一下太陽神在神話中的一些功能，因為這可能有助於澄清太陽在星盤中的角色。在某些文化中太陽由女性神祇代表，但在這種情況下女神的屬性是「男性」的——即動態的。一個例子是埃及太陽女神 Sekhmet，太陽神 Ra 的女兒，被稱為「Ra 之眼」。她被描繪為戴著太陽圓盤的獅頭，是一位戰爭和殺戮之神。但 Ra 本人，最古老的太陽神之一，更具太陽象徵性的特徵；他是世界創造者和正義的分配者，從自己的種子產生所有其他神的萬物之父。

Apollo, the Greek Sun god, is a much later and more humanised figure. He is the gentleman of Olympus, and we can learn a lot about the deeper meaning of the Sun from him. Perhaps most importantly, Apollo is the breaker of family curses. If you are in an awful mess like Orestes, and have inherited a seething mass of family complexes which are driving you mad, Apollo is the only deity who has the power to break the grip of the Erinyes (the Furies), the avengers of matriarchal law. Another myth about Apollo which carries a similar meaning is his conquest of the giant female snake Python. Having destroyed the snake, he sets up his shrine of Delphi over her former lair, and honours (or integrates) her by calling his oracular priestess the Pythia or Pythoness. The function of curse breaking is a most interesting one. What do you think this might mean?
Apollo，希臘太陽神，是一個晚得多也更人格化的人物。他是奧林匹斯的紳士，我們可以從他那裡學到很多關於太陽更深含義的東西。也許最重要的是，Apollo 是家庭詛咒的破除者。如果你像 Orestes 那樣陷入可怕的困境，繼承了一堆沸騰的家庭情結並快要發瘋，Apollo 是唯一有力量打破 Erinyes（復仇女神）——母權法則的報復者——控制的神。另一個帶有類似含義的 Apollo 神話是他征服了巨蛇 Python。消滅蛇後，他在她原來的巢穴上建立了 Delphi 神殿，並通過稱他的神諭女祭司為 Pythia 或 Pythoness 來致敬（或整合）她。破除詛咒的功能是非常有趣的一個。你覺得這可能意味著什麼？

Audience: The Sun helps us to work through unfinished family business.
聽眾：太陽幫助我們處理未完成的家庭事務。

Liz: Yes, that is how I would understand it also. The more we are able to feel separate and individual, the less we are at the mercy of the unconscious conflicts and compulsions of the family psyche. This does not mean that living the Sun makes one reject the family. On the contrary, the more one is oneself, the more one has to give others in a genuine, openhearted way. But it is the psychic skeletons in the cupboards which taint families—the power ploys to keep people close, the subtle undermining of talents and potentials, the envy and resentment and fear accruing over generations—and it is these which the light of the Sun has the power to dispel.
Liz：是的，這也是我理解的方式。我們越能感到分離和個體化，就越不受家庭心靈的無意識衝突和強迫的擺布。這不意味著活出太陽就會讓人拒絕家庭。相反，一個人越是自己，就越能以真誠的、開放的方式給予他人。但正是那些隱藏在家庭中的心靈骷髏——讓人靠近的權力手段、對才華和潛能的微妙破壞、世代累積的嫉妒和怨恨和恐懼——太陽的光有力量驅散這些。

In Greek myth, family curses are usually initiated by someone offending a god (through hubris or arrogance), who then casts a blight on successive generations. Because the deity is not offered the proper respect, the descendants must suffer until the curse is fulfilled or broken. Offence against a god is a way of describing offence against an archetypal principle, a fundamental life urge. Something is denied honour and value, and it strikes back through the psyche of the family, causing conflict and suffering which is psychologically passed down from parent to child. This happens in families all the time. It is the dark side of communal life, always hiding in the shadow of the warmth and support which a loving family can offer. Some families have a great deal of warmth and support and mutual respect to offer their members, and the dark side, which is perfectly human, causes those ordinary petty relationship problems we all encounter in life. Other families are truly blighted, carrying a vast reservoir of repression, manipulation and destructiveness, and all the members suffer. It is not always easy to spot this, since a tightly enmeshed family may present a united “loving” front to the outside world, while the problems are hidden or blamed on one individual's bad or sick behaviour. And sometimes all but one of the members seem perfectly satisfied to remain unconscious cells in the organism. It is the one who possesses a stronger need for individual expression who will often initially wind up as the “identified patient.”
在希臘神話中，家庭詛咒通常由某人冒犯了一位神（通過傲慢或驕傲）而引發，神然後在連續世代上施以災禍。因為神沒有被給予適當的尊重，後代必須受苦直到詛咒被履行或破除。冒犯神是描述冒犯原型原則——一種基本生命衝動——的一種方式。某物被否認了榮譽和價值，它通過家庭的心靈反擊，造成心理上從父母傳給孩子的衝突和痛苦。這種事一直在家庭中發生。它是共同體生活的陰暗面，總是隱藏在充滿愛的家庭所能提供的溫暖和支持的陰影中。有些家庭有大量的溫暖、支持和互相尊重可以提供給其成員，而陰暗面——完全人性的——造成我們在生活中都遇到的那種普通的關係問題。另一些家庭真正遭受災禍，攜帶著大量的壓抑、操縱和破壞性，所有成員都受苦。這並不總是容易發現的，因為一個緊密糾纏的家庭可能對外呈現團結的「有愛」面目，而問題被隱藏或歸咎於一個個體的不良或病態行為。有時除了一個成員之外所有人都似乎很滿意地保持為集體中的無意識細胞。正是那個擁有更強個體表達需求的人往往最初最終成為「被認定的病人」。

For example, certain emotions may not be permitted expression within the family circle. Perhaps affection is never openly displayed, or sexuality is never talked about, or no one ever gets angry, or everyone is expected to remain happily living in the same country town. There is a tribal feeling to such families, and members are warned by every possible covert means not to break the unspoken rules. If an individual attempts to challenge them, he or she may be made to feel bad, selfish, and unloved-or may even be labelled sick or evil. There is something about solar consciousness, the sense of “me,” which has the power to break the spell these unspoken family rules have over us. We are all vulnerable to loneliness, guilt and manipulation, since everyone has a Neptune and no one has a perfect childhood; and the threat of being outcast is painful to all human beings, although to some more than others. But if we can believe that we are what we are meant to be, and that challenging the unconscious system does not make us bad or worthless, then we can make efforts to retain positive relationships with family members while still preserving our own independent values and path in life.
例如，某些情緒可能不被允許在家庭圈子中表達。也許愛從不公開顯示，或性從不談論，或沒有人曾經發怒，或每個人都被期望留在同一個鄉鎮生活。這種家庭有一種部落感，成員被各種可能的隱蔽手段警告不要打破未說出口的規則。如果一個個體試圖挑戰它們，他或她可能被讓感覺不好、自私和不被愛——甚至可能被貼上病態或邪惡的標籤。太陽意識的某些東西——「我」的感覺——有力量打破這些未說出口的家庭規則對我們的控制。我們都容易受到孤獨、內疚和操縱的傷害，因為每個人都有一個海王星，沒有人有完美的童年；被放逐的威脅對所有人來說都是痛苦的，儘管對某些人比其他人更甚。但如果我們能相信我們就是我們注定要成為的，並且挑戰無意識的系統並不使我們變壞或無價值，那麼我們就可以努力與家庭成員保持積極的關係，同時仍保持自己獨立的價值和人生道路。

There is a lunar dimension to psychotherapy—containment, empathy and the building of a human relationship. There is also a solar dimension, which is related to Apollo's function of curse-breaking. The object of Apollonian analysis is not simply to dig up all the horrible traumas so that one can blame one's parents for all one's ills. It is consciousness of family patterns and the ways in which we still go on enacting them, which dispels the family curse. A curse is compulsive; we are trapped in behaviour which is destructive and self-defeating, yet we are blind to the source of the compulsion because there is not yet a sufficient sense of separateness from the collective, from the family psyche. The Furies which hunt the offending victim in Greek myth may be interpreted in many ways. I have found that for most people, they take the form of guilt, anxiety and resentment. Guilt tells us we do not deserve to be happy; anxiety makes us fearful of change and future potentials; and resentment makes us destructive toward others or ourselves. These are archetypal human feelings, and it is not possible to rid ourselves of them altogether. But the curse-breaking function of the Sun means that the more we value ourselves, the less we rush about trying to fulfil others' expectations, the less frightened we are of life overwhelming us, and the less resentful we feel about unlived potentials.
心理治療有一個月亮維度——包容、共情和建立人際關係。也有一個太陽維度，與 Apollo 破除詛咒的功能有關。Apollo 式分析的目的不僅僅是挖掘所有可怕的創傷以便一個人可以把自己的所有毛病歸咎於父母。是對家庭模式以及我們仍在如何上演它們的意識，驅散了家庭詛咒。詛咒是強迫性的；我們被困在破壞性和自敗的行為中，但我們對強迫的源頭盲目，因為還沒有足夠的與集體、與家庭心靈的分離感。希臘神話中追獵冒犯者的復仇女神可以有多種解讀。我發現對大多數人來說，它們以內疚、焦慮和怨恨的形式出現。內疚告訴我們我們不配幸福；焦慮使我們害怕變化和未來潛能；怨恨使我們對他人或自己有破壞性。這些是原型的人類感受，不可能完全擺脫。但太陽的破除詛咒功能意味著我們越重視自己，越少忙著試圖滿足他人的期望，越少害怕生活壓倒我們，越少對未活出的潛能感到怨恨。

Apollo is also a prophet. He is called Apollo Longsight, and his Delphic Oracle was consulted for many centuries as a sacred source of guidance and prescience. The idea that one might consult the god in order to find the right course of action or have a question answered, is a very ancient one; we can see the modern version in astrology as well as the I Ching. But Apollo's oracular nature is not what we would call “psychic.” Psychism is a kind of participation mystique, a capacity to lose one's own boundaries and fuse with the psyche of another. Solar prophecy is foresight, and there is no loss of self. It is intuitive rather than psychic, and bases its wisdom on a perception of the outcome of choices made in the present. The oracular side of Apollo was also called Double-Tongued, because one could never be quite sure about the meaning of the answer. Everything depended upon the level of interpretation. It was not predictive in the literal sense, but allowed choice to the querent in the same way that the images in a dream are multilevelled and may be interpreted or even acted upon in numerous ways.
Apollo 也是一位先知。他被稱為 Apollo Longsight，他的 Delphi 神諭被作為指導和預知的神聖來源諮詢了許多世紀。一個人可能向神諮詢以找到正確的行動方向或獲得問題的答案的想法非常古老；我們可以在占星學和易經中看到現代版本。但 Apollo 的神諭性質不是我們所說的「通靈」。通靈是一種參與神祕，一種失去自己界限並與另一個人的心靈融合的能力。太陽預言是前瞻，沒有自我的喪失。它是直覺的而非通靈的，其智慧基於對在現在做出的選擇的結果的感知。Apollo 的神諭面也被稱為雙舌，因為人們永遠無法確定答案的含義。一切取決於解讀的層面。它不是字面上的預測，而是允許求問者選擇，就像夢中的意象是多層次的，可以以多種方式解讀甚至付諸行動。

Oedipus, for example, consults the Delphic Oracle because he has begun to wonder whether the King and Queen of Corinth are really his parents. The Oracle tells him that he will be his father's slayer and his mother's husband. This is like a dream image; what might it really mean? Freud thought that we are all symbolically our parents' murderers and paramours; it is the essential truth of the child's world, and enacts itself throughout life whenever we overthrow some old authority structure, inner or outer, and strive toward union with a beloved ideal. Oedipus, however, takes this oracular statement literally, and runs away from Corinth to avoid his dreadful fate. But Apollo is double-tongued, and in running away Oedipus creates this fate. There is a great flaw in his nature—uncontrollable rage—and when he meets his father unknowingly on the road, he loses his temper and kills him. You know the rest. The outcome of the Oracle is strangely interwoven with the choice of the person to whom the Oracle is given. There is a pattern at work which cannot be changed; but it is up to the querent to understand the inner level of the pattern and act accordingly. By the way, Apollo is also the only god who succeeds in cheating the three Fates of a preordained death. He gets them drunk.
例如，Oedipus 諮詢 Delphi 神諭，因為他開始懷疑 Corinth 的國王和王后是否真的是他的父母。神諭告訴他他將成為父親的殺手和母親的丈夫。這像一個夢的意象；它真正意味著什麼？Freud 認為我們都是象徵性的父母的謀殺者和戀人；這是孩子世界的本質真理，每當我們推翻某個舊的權威結構——內在或外在的——並追求與心愛理想的結合時，它就在整個生活中上演。然而 Oedipus 字面理解了這個神諭陳述，逃離 Corinth 以避免他的可怕命運。但 Apollo 是雙舌的，在逃跑中 Oedipus 創造了這個命運。他的本性中有一個大缺陷——無法控制的憤怒——當他在路上不知不覺地遇到父親時，他發脾氣殺了他。你知道接下來的事。神諭的結果與被給予神諭的人的選擇奇特地交織在一起。有一個正在起作用的模式無法被改變；但由求問者來理解這個模式的內在層面並相應行動。順便說一句，Apollo 也是唯一成功欺騙三個命運女神關於預定死亡的神。他讓她們喝醉了。

So Apollo Longsight reflects a solar capacity to intuit a pattern at work in life and to foresee the consequences of our choices. We often make decisions blindly, out of emotional need or intellectual analysis or the desire to please. But we may fail to understand the broader picture—who we really are in relation to our environment, and what the deeper patterns of our own individual journey might be. Then we are astonished when the fruits of our past choices come ripe. Consulting the Oracle in myth is really a kind of turning inward, a meditative act which puts us in contact with a more prescient side of ourselves. Many people accomplish this with prayer or meditation, and it is a sacred act in the deepest sense, just as it was in ancient times when one approached the god. The more we know who we are, the more likely we are to act according to our own truth, or according to what is right for us—and even if the consequences are difficult or painful, we can retain our integrity and strength. This is why Apollo is a gentleman. Or, as Polonius says in Hamlet:
所以 Apollo Longsight 反映了太陽直覺一個正在起作用的生活模式並預見我們選擇的後果的能力。我們經常盲目地做決定——出於情感需求或理性分析或取悅的渴望。但我們可能無法理解更大的圖景——我們與環境的真正關係是什麼，以及我們自己個體之旅的更深層模式可能是什麼。然後當我們過去選擇的果實成熟時我們感到震驚。在神話中諮詢神諭實際上是一種內向的轉向，一種冥想的行為，它讓我們與自己更具先知的一面接觸。許多人通過祈禱或冥想來完成這一點，這是最深意義上的神聖行為，就像古代接近神時一樣。我們越了解自己是誰，就越可能按照自己的真理或按照對我們正確的東西行事——即使後果困難或痛苦，我們也能保持正直和力量。這就是為什麼 Apollo 是紳士。或者，如 Hamlet 中 Polonius 所說：

This above all: to thine own self be true,
最要緊的：忠於你自己，

And it must follow, as the night the day,
然後就像夜隨晝來一樣，

Thou canst not then be false to any man.
你便不能對任何人不忠。

Apollo's prophetic function is inside all of us. This dimension of the Sun reflects our vision and foresight, and our capacity to sense inner potentials which have not yet come ripe. The Sun is also associated with the image of the Divine Child, which is portrayed in some versions of the card of the Sun in the Tarot deck. The Divine Child embodies everything we have yet to become but which has not yet crystallised with time (Saturn). Experience, and the attitudes we acquire in response to experience, crystallise all those potentials and shape the adult. The Divine Child is our solar blueprint, which is present in us as a seed but takes a lifetime to unfold. The Sun gives us the feeling that we have a future, that it has meaning, that our lives follow an intelligent design. We are then able to retain trust in ourselves and can gamble a little with the unknown. Even if our gambling brings the roof down on our heads, we know we will survive to try again another time. From all this you should be able to work out what it is like to be disconnected from the solar principle. It is very dreary, because there is no vision of a future. There is only the past with all its mistakes and lost possibilities. That is the family curse. In the Tarot deck, I associate this feeling of hopelessness with the card of the Devil—the bondage which we cannot see but which casts a chain around our necks and stops us moving out into life.
Apollo 的預言功能在我們所有人內在。太陽的這個維度反映了我們的視野和前瞻，以及我們感知尚未成熟的內在潛能的能力。太陽也與神聖之子的意象有關，在塔羅牌太陽牌的某些版本中有描繪。神聖之子體現了我們尚未成為但尚未隨時間（土星）結晶的一切。經驗和我們對經驗的態度結晶了所有這些潛能並塑造了成人。神聖之子是我們的太陽藍圖，以種子形式存在於我們內在但需要一生來展開。太陽給我們一種感覺：我們有未來，它有意義，我們的生活遵循一個智慧的設計。然後我們能夠保持對自己的信任並可以與未知稍作賭博。即使我們的賭博讓屋頂塌在我們頭上，我們知道自己會活著下次再試。從所有這些中你應該能推斷出與太陽原則脫節是什麼感覺。非常沉悶，因為沒有未來的視野。只有過去及其所有錯誤和失去的可能性。那就是家庭詛咒。在塔羅牌中，我將這種絕望感與惡魔牌聯繫起來——我們看不見但卻套住我們脖子並阻止我們走出去進入生活的枷鎖。

Finally, Apollo is the god of music. He is also the father of the nine Muses, each of whom represents a different aspect of the arts. This rulership over the creative realm is different from Aphrodite's function as goddess of beauty and ornamentation, for Aphrodite takes what already exists in raw form and refines it. Apollo, on the other hand, creates something out of nothing; he symbolises the creative urge itself. Why music in particular?
最後，Apollo 是音樂之神。他也是九位繆斯的父親，每位繆斯代表藝術的不同面向。這種對創造領域的守護與 Aphrodite 作為美和裝飾女神的功能不同，因為 Aphrodite 是把已經以原始形式存在的東西加以精煉。而 Apollo 則是從無中創造某物；他象徵創造衝動本身。為什麼特別是音樂？

Audience: It comes from the heart.
聽眾：它來自內心。

Liz: Yes, but so do other forms of creative expression. Perhaps it has more to do with the immediate nature of music. I am thinking again of Mary Renault's novel, in which Theseus comments that if you go to Apollo with your grief and make it into a song, he will take the grief away. Music can embody any human emotion at the moment that the emotion is felt. This is not transcendence or transformation; it is distillation of an essence. Music does not convey feelings through images or words, both of which require interpretation and reflective distance. It is the most spontaneous of all the creative arts, and was probably the first—I should imagine people were rhythmically moving their bodies and beating sticks on rocks long before they worked out how to paint bisons on cave walls. Rhythm is basic to the body, rooted in the beating of the heart. In this sense music is the most primal art, preceding thought and perception, emerging from the very origins of life. And you need no implements to make music—all you need to do is tap your foot and open your mouth. Music somehow magically carries unbearable feelings and allows us to bear them. It is very difficult to be articulate about this function of the Sun, but I hope you can make some sense of what I am saying. I am not suggesting that everyone should become a musician or a music lover. But in expressing ourselves spontaneously, we are making music. This dimension of the solar principle fuses life and art.
Liz：是的，但其他形式的創造性表達也是如此。也許它更多與音樂的即時性有關。我又想到 Mary Renault 的小說，其中 Theseus 說如果你帶著悲傷去 Apollo 並把它變成一首歌，他會帶走悲傷。音樂可以在感受情緒的那一刻體現任何人類情緒。這不是超越或轉化；它是本質的蒸餾。音樂不通過意象或文字傳達感受——後兩者都需要解讀和反思性距離。它是最自發的所有創造藝術，可能是最早的——我想像人們在想出如何在洞穴壁上畫野牛之前很久就在有節奏地動身體和拿棍子敲石頭了。節奏是身體的基礎，根植於心跳。在這種意義上音樂是最原始的藝術，先於思考和感知，從生命的起源中浮現。而且你不需要任何工具來製造音樂——你只需要拍腳和張嘴。音樂以某種神奇的方式承載著無法承受的感受並讓我們能夠承受它們。很難有條理地闡述太陽的這個功能，但我希望你們能理解我所說的。我不是建議每個人都應該成為音樂家或音樂愛好者。但在自發地自我表達中，我們在製造音樂。太陽原則的這個維度融合了生活與藝術。
